query: Query: amino acid , peptide , or protein [SEP] Or protein peptide amino acid is amino acids and chains of amino acids connected by peptide linkages.

name: amino acids , acidic
query: Query: amino acids , acidic [SEP] Acidic amino acids is amino acids with side chains that are negatively charged at physiological pH.

name: amino acid transport system a
query: Query: amino acid transport system a [SEP] Amino acid transport system a is a sodium-dependent neutral amino acid transporter that accounts for most of the sodium-dependent neutral amino acid uptake by mammalian cells. The preferred substrates for this transporter system include [MASK]; serine; and [MASK].

name: amino acid transport system asc
query: Query: amino acid transport system asc [SEP] Amino acid transport system asc is a ubiquitous sodium-dependent neutral amino acid transporter. The preferred substrates for this transporter system include [MASK]; serine; and [MASK].

name: amino acid transport system l
query: Query: amino acid transport system l [SEP] Amino acid transport system l is a sodium-independent neutral amino acid transporter system with specificity for large amino acids. One of the functions of the transporter system is to supply large neutral amino acids to the brain.

name: amino acid transport systems , acidic
query: Query: amino acid transport systems , acidic [SEP] Acidic amino acid transport systems is amino acid transporter systems capable of transporting acidic amino acids (amino acids, acidic).

name: amino sugars
query: Query: amino sugars [SEP] Amino sugars is sugars containing an amino group. [MASK] of other compounds with these amino sugars results in aminoglycosides.

name: ammonium chloride
query: Query: ammonium chloride [SEP] Ammonium chloride is an acidifying agent that has expectorant and diuretic effects. Also used in etching and batteries and as a flux in electroplating.

name: ammonium hydroxide
query: Query: ammonium hydroxide [SEP] Ammonium hydroxide is the hydroxy [MASK] of ammonium ion. It is formed when [MASK] reacts with water molecules in solution.

name: ammonium sulfate
query: Query: ammonium sulfate [SEP] Ammonium sulfate is sulfuric acid diammonium [MASK]. It is used in chemical fractionation of proteins.

name: ampicillin
query: Query: ampicillin [SEP] Ampicillin is semi-synthetic derivative of penicillin that functions as an orally active broad-spectrum antibiotic.

name: ampicillin resistance
query: Query: ampicillin resistance [SEP] Ampicillin resistance is nonsusceptibility of a microbe to the action of ampicillin, a penicillin derivative that interferes with cell wall synthesis.

name: amplified fragment length polymorphism analysis
query: Query: amplified fragment length polymorphism analysis [SEP] Amplified fragment length polymorphism analysis is the detection of restriction fragment length polymorphisms by selective pcr amplification of restriction fragments derived from genomic dna followed by electrophoretic analysis of the amplified restriction fragments.

name: amplifiers , electronic
query: Query: amplifiers , electronic [SEP] Electronic amplifiers is electronic devices that increase the magnitude of a signal's power level or current.

name: amputation , traumatic
query: Query: amputation , traumatic [SEP] Traumatic [MASK] is loss of a limb or other bodily appendage by accidental injury.

name: amyloid
query: Query: amyloid [SEP] Amyloid is a fibrous protein complex that consists of proteins folded into a specific cross beta-pleated sheet structure. This fibrillar structure has been found as an alternative folding pattern for a variety of functional proteins. Deposits of amyloid in the form of amyloid plaques are associated with a variety of degenerative diseases. The amyloid structure has also been found in a number of functional proteins that are unrelated to disease.

name: anaerobic threshold
query: Query: anaerobic threshold [SEP] Anaerobic threshold is the oxygen consumption level above which aerobic energy production is supplemented by anaerobic mechanisms during exercise, resulting in a sustained increase in lactate concentration and metabolic acidosis. The anaerobic threshold is affected by factors that modify oxygen delivery to the tissues; it is low in patients with heart disease. Methods of measurement include direct measure of lactate concentration, direct measurement of bicarbonate concentration, and gas exchange measurements.

name: anal canal
query: Query: anal canal [SEP] Anal canal is the terminal segment of the large intestine, beginning from the ampulla of the rectum and ending at the anus.

name: analgesia , epidural
query: Query: analgesia , epidural [SEP] Epidural analgesia is the relief of pain without loss of consciousness through the introduction of an analgesic agent into the [MASK] of the vertebral canal. It is differentiated from anesthesia, epidural which refers to the state of insensitivity to sensation.

name: analytic sample preparation methods
query: Query: analytic sample preparation methods [SEP] Analytic sample preparation methods is use of various chemical separation and extraction methods, such as solid phase extraction; chromatography; and supercritical fluid extraction; to prepare samples for analytical measurement of components.

name: anatomic variation
query: Query: anatomic variation [SEP] Anatomic variation is peculiarities associated with the internal structure, form, topology, or architecture of organisms that distinguishes them from others of the same species or group.

name: anatomy , comparative
query: Query: anatomy , comparative [SEP] Comparative anatomy is the comparative study of animal structure with regard to homologous organs or parts. (Stedman, 25th ed)

name: anatomy , regional
query: Query: anatomy , regional [SEP] Regional anatomy is the anatomical study of specific regions or parts of organisms, emphasizing the relationship between the various structures (e.g. muscles, nerves, skeletal, cardiovascular, etc.).

name: anatomy , veterinary
query: Query: anatomy , veterinary [SEP] Veterinary anatomy is the study of the anatomical structures of animals.

name: andersen syndrome
query: Query: andersen syndrome [SEP] Andersen syndrome is a form of inherited long qt syndrome (or lqt7) that is characterized by a triad of potassium-sensitive periodic paralysis, ventricular ectopic beats, and abnormal features such as short stature, low-[MASK] ears, and scoliosis. It results from mutations of kcnj2 gene which encodes a channel protein (inward rectifier potassium channels) that regulates resting membrane potential.

name: anemia , neonatal
query: Query: anemia , neonatal [SEP] Neonatal anemia is the mildest form of erythroblastosis fetalis in which anemia is the chief manifestation.

name: anemia , refractory
query: Query: anemia , refractory [SEP] Refractory anemia is a severe sometimes chronic anemia, usually macrocytic in type, that does not respond to ordinary antianemic therapy.

name: anesthesia , cardiac procedures
query: Query: anesthesia , cardiac procedures [SEP] Cardiac procedures anesthesia is a range of methods used to induce unconsciousness; analgesia; and muscle relaxation during cardiac procedures.

name: anesthesia , caudal
query: Query: anesthesia , caudal [SEP] Caudal anesthesia is epidural anesthesia administered via the sacral canal.

name: anesthesia , inhalation
query: Query: anesthesia , inhalation [SEP] [MASK] anesthesia is anesthesia caused by the breathing of anesthetic gases or vapors or by insufflating anesthetic gases or vapors into the respiratory tract.

name: anesthesia , intravenous
query: Query: anesthesia , intravenous [SEP] Intravenous anesthesia is process of administering an anesthetic through injection directly into the bloodstream.

name: anesthesia , local
query: Query: anesthesia , local [SEP] Local anesthesia is a blocking of [MASK] to a specific area by an injection of an anesthetic agent.

name: anesthesia , rectal
query: Query: anesthesia , rectal [SEP] Rectal anesthesia is procedure involving the instillation of an anesthetic into the rectum.

name: anesthesia , spinal
query: Query: anesthesia , spinal [SEP] Spinal anesthesia is procedure in which an anesthetic is injected directly into the spinal cord.

name: anesthesia department , hospital
query: Query: anesthesia department , hospital [SEP] Hospital anesthesia department is hospital department responsible for the administration of functions and activities pertaining to the delivery of anesthetics.

name: aneurysm , infected
query: Query: aneurysm , infected [SEP] Infected aneurysm is aneurysm due to growth of microorganisms in the arterial wall, or infection arising within preexisting arteriosclerotic aneurysms.

name: anger
query: Query: anger [SEP] Anger is a strong emotional feeling of displeasure aroused by being interfered with, injured or threatened.

name: angiogenesis inducing agents
query: Query: angiogenesis inducing agents [SEP] Angiogenesis inducing agents is agents that induce or stimulate physiologic angiogenesis or pathologic angiogenesis.

name: angiography , digital subtraction
query: Query: angiography , digital subtraction [SEP] Digital subtraction angiography is a method of delineating blood vessels by subtracting a tissue background image from an image of tissue plus intravascular contrast material that attenuates the X-ray [MASK]. The background image is determined from a digitized image taken a few moments before injection of the contrast material. The resulting angiogram is a high-contrast image of the vessel. This subtraction technique allows extraction of a high-intensity signal from the superimposed background information. The image is thus the result of the differential absorption of X-rays by different tissues.

name: angioplasty , laser
query: Query: angioplasty , laser [SEP] Laser angioplasty is a technique utilizing a laser coupled to a catheter which is used in the dilatation of occluded blood vessels. This includes laser thermal angioplasty where the laser energy heats up a metal tip, and direct laser angioplasty where the laser energy directly ablates the occlusion. One form of the latter approach uses an excimer laser which creates microscopically precise cuts without thermal injury. When laser angioplasty is performed in combination with balloon angioplasty it is called laser-assisted balloon angioplasty (angioplasty, balloon, laser-assisted).

name: angiotensin ii type 2 receptor blockers
query: Query: angiotensin ii type 2 receptor blockers [SEP] Angiotensin ii type 2 receptor blockers is agents that antagonize the angiotensin ii type 2 receptor.

name: animal assisted therapy
query: Query: animal assisted therapy [SEP] Animal assisted therapy is the use of live animal as a means of therapy

name: animal care committees
query: Query: animal care committees [SEP] Animal care committees is institutional committees established to protect the welfare of animals used in research and education. The 1971 nih Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals introduced the policy that institutions using warm-blooded animals in projects supported by nih grants either be accredited by a recognized professional laboratory animal accrediting body or establish its own committee to evaluate animal care; the Public Health Service adopted a policy in 1979 requiring such committees; and the 1985 amendments to the Animal Welfare Act mandate review and approval of federally funded research with animals by a formally designated Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (iacuc).

name: animal communication
query: Query: animal communication [SEP] Animal communication is communication between animals involving the giving off by one individual of some chemical or physical signal, that, on being received by another, influences its behavior.

name: animal fur
query: Query: animal fur [SEP] Animal fur is usually densely-packed hairs on the skin of mammals.

name: animal nutritional physiological phenomena
query: Query: animal nutritional physiological phenomena [SEP] Animal nutritional physiological phenomena is nutritional physiology of animals.

name: animals , exotic
query: Query: animals , exotic [SEP] Exotic animals is animals native to a foreign country or of foreign origin or [MASK], that are not native to the United States.

name: animals , newborn
query: Query: animals , newborn [SEP] Newborn animals is refers to animals in the period of time just after birth.

name: animals , zoo
query: Query: animals , zoo [SEP] Zoo animals is animal population groups or individual animals that reside in captivity at a zoological park.

name: animal scales
query: Query: animal scales [SEP] Animal scales is tough, horny, brittle, smooth, striated or plate-like extensions of the stratum corneum or outer layer of the skin. It serves as a protective layer in fishes, reptiles, birds, and mammals.

name: animal shells
query: Query: animal shells [SEP] Animal shells is the hard rigid covering of animals including molluscs; turtles; insects; and crustaceans.

name: animal testing alternatives
query: Query: animal testing alternatives [SEP] Animal testing alternatives is procedures, such as tissue culture techniques; mathematical models; etc., when used or advocated for use in place of the use of animals in research or diagnostic laboratories.

name: animation
query: Query: animation [SEP] Animation is a film or video wholly or partially created by photographing drawings, sculptures, or other inanimate things in sequence to create the illusion of motion. Animations are also generated by computers. (From Moving Image Materials: Genre Terms, 1988)

name: anisotropy
query: Query: anisotropy [SEP] Anisotropy is a physical property showing different values in relation to the direction in or along which the measurement is made. The physical property may be with regard to thermal or electric conductivity or light refraction. In crystallography, it describes crystals whose index of refraction varies with the direction of the incident light. It is also called acolotropy and colotropy. The opposite of anisotropy is isotropy wherein the same values characterize the object when measured along axes in all directions.

name: ankle
query: Query: ankle [SEP] Ankle is the region of the lower limb between the [MASK] and the leg.

name: ankle brachial index
query: Query: ankle brachial index [SEP] Ankle brachial index is comparison of the blood pressure between the brachial artery and the [MASK]. It is a predictor of [MASK].

name: ankle fractures
query: Query: ankle fractures [SEP] Ankle fractures is fractures of any of the bones of the ankle.

name: ankle joint
query: Query: ankle joint [SEP] Ankle joint is the joint that is formed by the inferior articular and malleolar articular surfaces of the tibia; the malleolar articular surface of the fibula; and the medial malleolar, lateral malleolar, and superior surfaces of the talus.

name: annual report
query: Query: annual report [SEP] Annual report is annual statements concerning the administrative and operational functions of an institution or organization.

name: annual reports as topic
query: Query: annual reports as topic [SEP] Annual reports as topic is works on annual statements reviewing the status of the administrative and operational functions and accomplishments of an institution or organization.

name: anomalous left coronary artery
query: Query: anomalous left coronary artery [SEP] Anomalous left coronary artery is malformations of left coronary artery where it is connected to the [MASK] instead of the aorta.

name: answering services
query: Query: answering services [SEP] Answering services is communication services provided by a person or a machine to record and relay the message from the caller.

name: antarctic regions
query: Query: antarctic regions [SEP] Antarctic regions is the continent lying around the South Pole and the southern waters of the Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans. It includes the Falkland Islands Dependencies. (From Webster's New Geographical Dictionary, 1988, p55)

name: anterior cerebral artery
query: Query: anterior cerebral artery [SEP] Anterior cerebral artery is artery formed by the bifurcation of the internal carotid artery (carotid artery, internal). Branches of the anterior cerebral artery supply the caudate nucleus; internal capsule; putamen; septal nuclei; gyrus cinguli; and surfaces of the frontal lobe and parietal lobe.

name: anterior compartment syndrome
query: Query: anterior compartment syndrome [SEP] Anterior compartment syndrome is rapid swelling, increased tension, pain, and ischemic necrosis of the muscles of the anterior tibial compartment of the leg, often following excessive physical exertion.

name: anterior horn cells
query: Query: anterior horn cells [SEP] Anterior horn cells is motor neurons in the anterior (ventral) horn of the spinal cord which project to skeletal muscles.

name: anterior hypothalamic nucleus
query: Query: anterior hypothalamic nucleus [SEP] Anterior hypothalamic nucleus is loose heterogeneous collection of cells in the anterior hypothalamus, continuous rostrally with the medial and lateral preoptic areas and caudally with the tuber cinereum.

name: anterior spinal artery syndrome
query: Query: anterior spinal artery syndrome [SEP] Anterior spinal artery syndrome is ischemia or infarction of the spinal cord in the distribution of the anterior spinal artery, which supplies the ventral two-thirds of the spinal cord. This condition is usually associated with atherosclerosis of the aorta and may result from [MASK] of an aortic aneurysm or rarely [MASK] of the anterior spinal artery. Clinical features include weakness and loss of pain and temperature sensation below the level of injury, with relative sparing of position and vibratory sensation. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp1249-50)

name: anterior wall myocardial infarction
query: Query: anterior wall myocardial infarction [SEP] Anterior wall myocardial infarction is myocardial infarction in which the anterior wall of the heart is involved. Anterior wall myocardial infarction is often caused by occlusion of the left anterior descending coronary artery. It can be categorized as anteroseptal or anterolateral wall myocardial infarction.

name: antibiotic
query: Query: antibiotic [SEP] Antibiotic is substances that inhibit the growth or reproduction of bacteria.

name: antibodies , blocking
query: Query: antibodies , blocking [SEP] Blocking antibodies is antibodies that inhibit the reaction between antigen and other antibodies or sensitized t-lymphocytes (e.g., antibodies of the immunoglobulin g class that compete with ige antibodies for antigen, thereby blocking an allergic response). Blocking antibodies that bind tumors and prevent destruction of tumor cells by cytotoxic t-lymphocytes have also been called enhancing antibodies. (Rosen et al., Dictionary of [MASK], 1989)

name: antibodies , catalytic
query: Query: antibodies , catalytic [SEP] Catalytic antibodies is antibodies that can catalyze a wide variety of chemical reactions. They are characterized by high substrate specificity and share many mechanistic features with enzymes.

name: antibodies , fungal
query: Query: antibodies , fungal [SEP] Fungal antibodies is immunoglobulins produced in a response to fungal antigens.

name: antibodies , monoclonal
query: Query: antibodies , monoclonal [SEP] Monoclonal antibodies is antibodies produced by a single clone of cells.

name: antibodies , neoplasm
query: Query: antibodies , neoplasm [SEP] Neoplasm antibodies is immunoglobulins induced by antigens specific for tumors other than the normally occurring histocompatibility antigens.

name: antibody diversity
query: Query: antibody diversity [SEP] Antibody diversity is the phenomenon of immense variability characteristic of antibodies. It enables the immune system to react specifically against the essentially unlimited kinds of antigens it encounters. Antibody diversity is accounted for by three main theories: (1) the Germ Line Theory, which holds that each antibody-producing cell has genes coding for all possible antibody specificities, but expresses only the one stimulated by antigen; (2) the Somatic Mutation Theory, which holds that antibody-producing cells contain only a few genes, which produce antibody diversity by mutation; and (3) the Gene Rearrangement Theory, which holds that antibody diversity is generated by the rearrangement of immunoglobulin variable region gene segments during the differentiation of the antibody-producing cells.

name: antibody specificity
query: Query: antibody specificity [SEP] Antibody specificity is the property of antibodies which enables them to react with some antigenic determinants and not with others. Specificity is dependent on chemical composition, physical forces, and molecular structure at the binding site.

name: anticipation , genetic
query: Query: anticipation , genetic [SEP] Genetic anticipation is the apparent tendency of certain diseases to appear at earlier age of onset and with increasing severity in successive generations. (Rieger et al., Glossary of Genetics: Classical and Molecular, 5th ed)

name: anticipation , psychological
query: Query: anticipation , psychological [SEP] Psychological anticipation is the ability to foresee what is likely to happen on the basis of past experience. It is largely a frontal lobe function.

name: antigenic variation
query: Query: antigenic variation [SEP] Antigenic variation is change in the surface antigen of a microorganism. There are two different types. One is a phenomenon, especially associated with influenza viruses, where they undergo spontaneous variation both as slow antigenic drift and sudden emergence of new strains (antigenic shift). The second type is when certain parasites, especially trypanosomes, plasmodium, and borrelia, survive the immune response of the host by changing the surface coat (antigen switching). (From Herbert et al., The Dictionary of [MASK], 4th ed)

name: antigen presentation
query: Query: antigen presentation [SEP] Antigen presentation is the process by which antigen is presented to lymphocytes in a form they can recognize. This is performed by antigen presenting cells (APCs). Some antigens require processing before they can be recognized. Antigen processing consists of ingestion and partial [MASK] of the antigen by the apc, followed by presentation of fragments on the cell surface. (From Rosen et al., Dictionary of [MASK], 1989)

name: antigens , cd
query: Query: antigens , cd [SEP] Cd antigens is differentiation antigens residing on mammalian leukocytes. cd stands for cluster of differentiation, which refers to groups of monoclonal antibodies that show similar reactivity with certain subpopulations of antigens of a particular lineage or differentiation stage. The subpopulations of antigens are also known by the same cd designation.

name: antigens , ly
query: Query: antigens , ly [SEP] Ly antigens is a group of lymphocyte surface antigens located on mouse lymphocytes. Specific Ly antigens are useful markers for distinguishing subpopulations of lymphocytes.

name: antigens , plant
query: Query: antigens , plant [SEP] Plant antigens is substances found in plants that have antigenic activity.

name: antigens , viral , tumor
query: Query: antigens , viral , tumor [SEP] Tumor viral antigens is those proteins recognized by antibodies from serum of animals bearing tumors induced by viruses; these proteins are presumably coded for by the nucleic acids of the same viruses that caused the neoplastic transformation.

name: antimicrobial cationic peptides
query: Query: antimicrobial cationic peptides [SEP] Antimicrobial cationic peptides is small cationic peptides that are an important component, in most species, of early innate and induced defenses against invading microbes. In animals they are found on mucosal surfaces, within phagocytic granules, and on the surface of the body. They are also found in insects and plants. Among others, this group includes the defensins, protegrins, tachyplesins, and thionins. They displace divalent cations from phosphate groups of membrane lipids leading to disruption of the membrane.

name: antioxidants
query: Query: antioxidants [SEP] Antioxidants is naturally occurring or synthetic substances that inhibit or retard oxidation reactions. They counteract the damaging effects of oxidation in animal tissues.

name: antiretroviral therapy , highly active
query: Query: antiretroviral therapy , highly active [SEP] Highly active antiretroviral therapy is drug regimens, for patients with hiv infections, that aggressively suppress hiv replication. The regimens usually involve administration of three or more different drugs including a protease inhibitor.

name: anxiety , separation
query: Query: anxiety , separation [SEP] Separation anxiety is anxiety experienced by an individual upon separation from a person or object of particular significance to the individual.

name: aorta , abdominal
query: Query: aorta , abdominal [SEP] Abdominal aorta is the aorta from the diaphragm to the bifurcation into the right and left common iliac arteries.

name: aorta , thoracic
query: Query: aorta , thoracic [SEP] Thoracic aorta is the portion of the descending aorta proceeding from the arch of the aorta and extending to the diaphragm, eventually connecting to the abdominal aorta.

name: aortic aneurysm , abdominal
query: Query: aortic aneurysm , abdominal [SEP] Abdominal aortic aneurysm is an abnormal balloon- or sac-like dilatation in the wall of the abdominal aorta which gives rise to the visceral, the parietal, and the terminal (iliac) branches below the aortic hiatus at the diaphragm.

name: aortic aneurysm , thoracic
query: Query: aortic aneurysm , thoracic [SEP] Thoracic aortic aneurysm is an abnormal balloon- or sac-like dilatation in the wall of the thoracic aorta. This proximal descending portion of aorta gives rise to the visceral and the parietal branches above the aortic hiatus at the diaphragm.

name: aortic rupture
query: Query: aortic rupture [SEP] Aortic rupture is the tearing or bursting of the wall along any portion of the aorta, such as thoracic or abdominal. It may result from the rupture of an aneurysm or it may be due to trauma.

name: aortic valve
query: Query: aortic valve [SEP] Aortic valve is the valve between the left ventricle and the ascending aorta which prevents backflow into the left ventricle.

name: apache
query: Query: apache [SEP] Apache is an acronym for Acute Physiology and Chronic Health Evaluation, a scoring system using routinely collected data and providing an accurate, objective description for a broad range of intensive care unit admissions, measuring severity of illness in [MASK] patients.

name: apoptosis
query: Query: apoptosis [SEP] Apoptosis is a regulated cell death mechanism characterized by distinctive morphologic changes in the nucleus and cytoplasm, including the endonucleolytic cleavage of genomic dna, at regularly spaced, internucleosomal sites, i.e., [MASK].  It is genetically-programmed and serves as a balance to [MASK] in regulating the size of animal tissues and in mediating pathologic processes associated with tumor growth.

name: apoptosis inducing factor
query: Query: apoptosis inducing factor [SEP] Apoptosis inducing factor is a flavoprotein that functions as a powerful antioxidant in the mitochondria and promotes apoptosis when released from the mitochondria. In mammalian cells aif is released in response to pro-apoptotic protein members of the bcl-2 protein family. It translocates to the cell nucleus and binds dna to stimulate CASPASE-independent chromatin condensation.

name: appetite regulation
query: Query: appetite regulation [SEP] Appetite regulation is physiologic mechanisms which regulate or control the appetite and food intake.

name: applied behavior analysis
query: Query: applied behavior analysis [SEP] Applied behavior analysis is behavioral science applied with the aim of improving socially important issues such as behavior problems and learning. For individuals diagnosed with intellectual and developmental disabilities including autism, techniques can be categorized as comprehensive or focused.

name: arabia
query: Query: arabia [SEP] Arabia is the great peninsula of southwest Asia comprising most of the present countries of the Middle East. It has been known since the first millennium b.c. In early times it was divided into Arabia Petraea, the northwest part, the only part ever conquered, becoming a Roman province; Arabia Deserta, the northern part between Syria and Mesopotamia; and Arabia Felix, the main part of the peninsula but by some geographers restricted to modern Yemen. (From Webster's New Geographical Dictionary, 1988, p63)

name: arabidopsis proteins
query: Query: arabidopsis proteins [SEP] Arabidopsis proteins is proteins that originate from plants species belonging to the genus arabidopsis. The most intensely studied species of Arabidopsis, Arabidopsis thaliana, is commonly used in laboratory experiments.

name: architectural accessibility
query: Query: architectural accessibility [SEP] Architectural accessibility is designs for approaching areas inside or outside facilities.

name: architectural drawing
query: Query: architectural drawing [SEP] Architectural drawing is work consisting of drawings of architecture and architectural projects, whether the project was executed or not. (Art & Architecture Thesaurus, 1990, v.2)

name: archives
query: Query: archives [SEP] Archives is a collection of historical documents or records providing information about places, institutions, or groups of people; also the place where such records are kept.

name: arctic regions
query: Query: arctic regions [SEP] Arctic regions is the Arctic Ocean and the lands in it and adjacent to it. It includes Point Barrow, Alaska, most of the Franklin District in Canada, two thirds of Greenland, Svalbard, Franz Josef Land, Lapland, Novaya Zemlya, and Northern Siberia. (Webster's New Geographical Dictionary, 1988, p66)

name: area health education centers
query: Query: area health education centers [SEP] Area health education centers is education centers authorized by the Comprehensive Health Manpower Training Act, 1971, for the training of health personnel in areas where health needs are the greatest. May be used for centers other than those established by the United States act.

name: area under curve
query: Query: area under curve [SEP] Area under curve is a statistical means of summarizing information from a series of measurements on one individual. It is frequently used in clinical pharmacology where the auc from serum levels can be interpreted as the total uptake of whatever has been administered. As a plot of the concentration of a drug against time, after a single dose of medicine, producing a standard shape curve, it is a means of comparing the bioavailability of the same drug made by different companies. (From Winslade, Dictionary of Clinical Research, 1992)

name: argentina
query: Query: argentina [SEP] Argentina is country located in southern South America, bordering the South Atlantic Ocean, between [MASK] and Uruguay.

name: arsenic poisoning
query: Query: arsenic poisoning [SEP] Arsenic poisoning is disorders associated with acute or chronic exposure to compounds containing arsenic (arsenicals) which may be fatal. Acute oral ingestion is associated with gastrointestinal symptoms and an encephalopathy which may manifest as seizures, mental status changes, and coma. Chronic exposure is associated with mucosal irritation, desquamating rash, myalgias, peripheral neuropathy, and [MASK] transverse (Mees) lines in the fingernails. (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1212)

name: arterial pressure
query: Query: arterial pressure [SEP] Arterial pressure is the blood pressure in the arteries. It is commonly measured with a sphygmomanometer on the [MASK] which represents the arterial pressure in the brachial artery.

name: arterial switch operation
query: Query: arterial switch operation [SEP] Arterial switch operation is surgical procedure for anatomical correction of transposed great arteries (e.g., double outlet right ventricle).

name: arthritis , experimental
query: Query: arthritis , experimental [SEP] Experimental arthritis is arthritis that is induced in experimental animals. Immunological methods and infectious agents can be used to develop experimental arthritis models. These methods include injections of stimulators of the immune response, such as an adjuvant (adjuvants, immunologic) or collagen.

name: arthritis , juvenile
query: Query: arthritis , juvenile [SEP] Juvenile arthritis is arthritis in children, with onset before 16 years of age. The terms juvenile rheumatoid arthritis (jra) and juvenile idiopathic arthritis (jia) refer to classification systems for chronic arthritis in children. Only one subtype of juvenile arthritis (polyarticular-onset, rheumatoid factor-positive) clinically resembles adult rheumatoid arthritis and is considered its childhood equivalent.

name: arthritis , reactive
query: Query: arthritis , reactive [SEP] Reactive arthritis is an aseptic, inflammatory arthritis developing secondary to a primary extra-articular infection, most typically of the gastrointestinal tract or urogenital system. The initiating trigger pathogens are usually shigella; salmonella; yersinia; campylobacter; or chlamydia trachomatis. Reactive arthritis is strongly associated with hla-b27 antigen.

name: arthroplasty , replacement , elbow
query: Query: arthroplasty , replacement , elbow [SEP] Elbow replacement arthroplasty is replacement of the elbow joint.

name: arthroplasty , replacement , hip
query: Query: arthroplasty , replacement , hip [SEP] Hip replacement arthroplasty is replacement of the hip joint.

name: arthroplasty , replacement , knee
query: Query: arthroplasty , replacement , knee [SEP] [MASK] replacement arthroplasty is replacement of the [MASK].

name: articulation disorders
query: Query: articulation disorders [SEP] Articulation disorders is disorders of the quality of [MASK] characterized by the substitution, omission, distortion, and addition of phonemes.

name: artificial cells
query: Query: artificial cells [SEP] Artificial cells is chemically synthesized structures which functionally resemble natural cells.

name: art therapy
query: Query: art therapy [SEP] Art therapy is the use of art as an adjunctive therapy in the treatment of neurological, mental, or behavioral disorders.

name: ascites
query: Query: ascites [SEP] Ascites is accumulation or retention of free fluid within the peritoneal cavity.

name: ascorbic acid
query: Query: ascorbic acid [SEP] Ascorbic acid is a six carbon compound related to glucose. It is found naturally in citrus fruits and many vegetables. Ascorbic acid is an essential nutrient in human diets, and necessary to maintain connective tissue and bone. Its biologically active form, vitamin c, functions as a reducing agent and coenzyme in several metabolic pathways. Vitamin c is considered an antioxidant.

name: asia , central
query: Query: asia , central [SEP] Central asia is the geographical area of Asia comprising kazakhstan; kyrgyzstan; tajikistan; turkmenistan; and uzbekistan. The desert region of Kara Kum (Qara Qum) is largely in Turkmenistan and the desert region of Kyzyl Kum (Kizil Kum or Qizil Qum), is in Uzbekistan and Kazakhstan. (From Webster's New Geographical Dictionary, 1988, p233, 590, 636)

name: asian americans
query: Query: asian americans [SEP] Asian americans is persons living in the United States having origins in any of the original peoples of the Far East, Southeast Asia, or the Indian subcontinent.

name: assisted circulation
query: Query: assisted circulation [SEP] Assisted circulation is pumping that aids the natural activity of the heart. (Dorland, 27th ed)

name: assisted living facilities
query: Query: assisted living facilities [SEP] Assisted living facilities is a housing and health care alternative combining independence with personal care. It provides a combination of housing, personalized supportive services and health care designed to meet the needs, both scheduled and unscheduled, of those who need help with activities of daily living. (www.alfa.org)

name: association learning
query: Query: association learning [SEP] Association learning is the principle that items experienced together enter into a connection, so that one tends to reinstate the other.

name: asthma , occupational
query: Query: asthma , occupational [SEP] Occupational asthma is asthma attacks caused, triggered, or exacerbated by occupational exposure.

name: astronomy
query: Query: astronomy [SEP] Astronomy is the science concerned with celestial bodies and the [MASK] and interpretation of the radiation received in the vicinity of the earth from the component parts of the universe (McGraw Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 5th ed)

name: asymmetric cell division
query: Query: asymmetric cell division [SEP] Asymmetric cell division is unequal cell division that results in daughter cells of different sizes.

name: asymptomatic infections
query: Query: asymptomatic infections [SEP] Asymptomatic infections is infections that do not exhibit symptoms.

name: atlas
query: Query: atlas [SEP] Atlas is work consisting of collections of illustrative plates, charts, etc., usually with explanatory captions.

name: atomic bomb survivors
query: Query: atomic bomb survivors [SEP] Atomic bomb survivors is persons who survived exposure to radiation due to atomic bombs.

name: atp binding cassette transporter , subfamily a , member 4
query: Query: atp binding cassette transporter , subfamily a , member 4 [SEP] Member 4 subfamily a atp binding cassette transporter is an atp binding cassette sub-family a transporter that translocates 11-cis and all-trans isomers of N-retinylidene-phosphatidylethanolamine (retinoids) from the extracellular surface to the cytoplasmic membrane surface of retinal rod cells and [MASK]. Mutations in the abca4 gene are associated with Stargardt Disease 1, a hereditary juvenile form of macular degeneration.

name: atp binding cassette transporter , subfamily b , member 1
query: Query: atp binding cassette transporter , subfamily b , member 1 [SEP] Member 1 subfamily b atp binding cassette transporter is a 170-kDa transmembrane glycoprotein from the superfamily of atp-binding cassette transporters. It serves as an ATP-dependent efflux pump for a variety of chemicals, including many antineoplastic agents. Overexpression of this glycoprotein is associated with multidrug resistance (see drug resistance, multiple).

name: atp binding cassette transporter , subfamily b , member 11
query: Query: atp binding cassette transporter , subfamily b , member 11 [SEP] Member 11 subfamily b atp binding cassette transporter is aTP-binding cassette, subfamily b, protein (P-glycoproteins) that functions in the ATP-dependent secretion of [MASK] [MASK] into the [MASK] canaliculi of [MASK]. Mutations in the abcb11 gene are associated with progressive familial intrahepatic cholestasis 2 (see cholestasis, intrahepatic).

name: atp binding cassette transporter , subfamily b , member 2
query: Query: atp binding cassette transporter , subfamily b , member 2 [SEP] Member 2 subfamily b atp binding cassette transporter is an ATP-binding cassette, sub-family b protein (atp binding cassette transporter, subfamily b) that functions in the transport of antigens from the cytoplasm to the endoplasmic reticulum for association with histocompatibility antigens class i peptides. It also acts as a molecular scaffold for the final stage of mhc class i protein folding.

name: atp binding cassette transporter , subfamily b , member 3
query: Query: atp binding cassette transporter , subfamily b , member 3 [SEP] Member 3 subfamily b atp binding cassette transporter is aTP-binding cassette, subfamily b, protein that functions in the transport of antigens from the cytoplasm to the endoplasmic reticulum for association with histocompatibility antigens class i peptides. It functions as a heterodimer with atp binding cassette transporter, subfamily b, member 2.

name: atp binding cassette transporter , subfamily d , member 1
query: Query: atp binding cassette transporter , subfamily d , member 1 [SEP] Member 1 subfamily d atp binding cassette transporter is aTP-binding cassette transporter that functions in the import of long chain (13-21 carbons) and very long chain fatty acids (> 22 carbons), or their acyl-CoA-derivatives, into peroxisomes. Mutations in the abcd1 gene are associated with the X-linked form of adrenoleukodystrophy.

name: atp binding cassette transporter , subfamily g , member 2
query: Query: atp binding cassette transporter , subfamily g , member 2 [SEP] Member 2 subfamily g atp binding cassette transporter is aTP-binding cassette transporter, sub-family g protein that functions as a high capacity urea exporter, transporter of sterols, and in the absorption and efflux of many drugs. Its efflux activity for antineoplastic agents contributes to drug resistance. It functions as a homodimer and is expressed by cells in a variety of organs, as well as by neoplastic stem cells.

name: atp binding cassette transporter , subfamily g , member 5
query: Query: atp binding cassette transporter , subfamily g , member 5 [SEP] Member 5 subfamily g atp binding cassette transporter is atp binding cassette transporter, subfamily g protein that functions as a heterodimer with atp binding cassette transporter, subfamily g, member 8 in the selective transport of dietary cholesterol and phytosterols into and export out of enterocytes. It also functions in selective sterol excretion by the liver into [MASK].

name: atp binding cassette transporter , subfamily g , member 8
query: Query: atp binding cassette transporter , subfamily g , member 8 [SEP] Member 8 subfamily g atp binding cassette transporter is aTP-binding cassette transporter, sub-family g protein that functions as a heterodimer with atp binding cassette transporter, subfamily g, member 5 in the selective transport of dietary cholesterol and phytosterols into and export out of enterocytes. It also functions in selective sterol excretion by the liver into [MASK].

name: atp binding cassette transporter 1
query: Query: atp binding cassette transporter 1 [SEP] Atp binding cassette transporter 1 is a superfamily of integral ATP-binding cassette membrane proteins whose expression pattern is consistent with a role in lipid (cholesterol) efflux. It is implicated in tangier disease, characterized by accumulation of cholesteryl ester in various tissues.

name: atrial fibrillation
query: Query: atrial fibrillation [SEP] Atrial fibrillation is abnormal cardiac rhythm that is characterized by rapid, uncoordinated firing of electrical impulses in the upper chambers of the heart (heart atria). In such case, blood cannot be effectively pumped into the lower chambers of the heart (heart ventricles). It is caused by abnormal impulse generation.

name: atrial function , left
query: Query: atrial function , left [SEP] Left atrial function is the hemodynamic and electrophysiological action of the left atrium.

name: atrial function , right
query: Query: atrial function , right [SEP] Right atrial function is the hemodynamic and electrophysiological action of the right atrium.

name: atrial premature complexes
query: Query: atrial premature complexes [SEP] Atrial premature complexes is a type of cardiac arrhythmia with premature atrial contractions or beats caused by signals originating from ectopic atrial sites. The ectopic signals may or may not conduct to the heart ventricles. Atrial premature complexes are characterized by premature p waves on ecg which are different in configuration from the p waves generated by the normal pacemaker complex in the sinoatrial node.

name: atrial pressure
query: Query: atrial pressure [SEP] Atrial pressure is the pressure within the cardiac atrium. It can be measured directly by using a pressure catheter (see heart catheterization). It can be also estimated using various imaging techniques or other pressure readings such as [MASK] (an estimate of left atrial pressure) and [MASK] (an estimate of right atrial pressure).

name: atrial septum
query: Query: atrial septum [SEP] Atrial septum is the thin membrane-like muscular structure separating the right and the left upper chambers (heart atria) of a heart.

name: at rich sequence
query: Query: at rich sequence [SEP] At rich sequence is a nucleic acid sequence that contains an above average number of adenine and thymine bases.

name: attachment sites , microbiological
query: Query: attachment sites , microbiological [SEP] Microbiological attachment sites is specific loci on both the [MASK] (attB) and the phage dna (attP) which delineate the sites where recombination takes place between them, as the phage dna becomes integrated (inserted) into the [MASK] during lysogeny.

name: attentional bias
query: Query: attentional bias [SEP] Attentional bias is an increased focus or awareness of certain stimuli over others, which influence behavior.

name: attitude to computers
query: Query: attitude to computers [SEP] Attitude to computers is the attitude and behavior associated with an individual using the computer.

name: attitude to death
query: Query: attitude to death [SEP] Attitude to death is conceptual response of the person to the various aspects of death, which are based on individual psychosocial and cultural experience.

name: atypical squamous cells of the cervix
query: Query: atypical squamous cells of the cervix [SEP] Atypical squamous cells of the cervix is morphological abnormalities of the cervical epithelium, usually revealed in pap smear, which do not meet the criteria for squamous cervical intraepithelial neoplasia or squamous cell carcinomas of the cervix . It may be a sign of infection with certain types of human papillomavirus (HPV).or sign of a benign (not cancer) growth, such as a cyst or polyp or, in menopausal women, of low hormone levels. More testing, such as hpv test, may be needed.

name: auditory brain stem implantation
query: Query: auditory brain stem implantation [SEP] Auditory brain stem implantation is surgical insertion of an electronic hearing device (auditory brain stem implants) with electrodes to the cochlea nucleus in the brain stem rather than to the [MASK] as in cochlear implantation.

name: auditory brain stem implants
query: Query: auditory brain stem implants [SEP] Auditory brain stem implants is multi-channel hearing devices typically used for patients who have tumors on the cochlear nerve and are unable to benefit from [MASK] after tumor surgery that severs the cochlear nerve. The device electrically stimulates the nerves of cochlea nucleus in the brain stem rather than the [MASK] as in [MASK].

name: auditory cortex
query: Query: auditory cortex [SEP] Auditory cortex is the region of the cerebral cortex that receives the auditory radiation from the medial geniculate body.

name: auditory fatigue
query: Query: auditory fatigue [SEP] Auditory fatigue is loss of sensitivity to sounds as a result of [MASK], manifesting as a temporary shift in auditory threshold. The temporary threshold shift, tts, is expressed in decibels.

name: auditory perceptual disorders
query: Query: auditory perceptual disorders [SEP] Auditory perceptual disorders is acquired or developmental cognitive disorders of auditory perception characterized by a reduced ability to perceive information contained in auditory stimuli despite intact [MASK]. Affected individuals have difficulty with [MASK] perception, [MASK], and comprehending the meaning of inflections of [MASK].

name: augmented reality
query: Query: augmented reality [SEP] Augmented reality is technology in which images of virtual objects and/or other digital information are superimposed over the real time view of the physical objects providing a composite view with guides for carrying out a task with or on the physical objects.

name: austria
query: Query: austria [SEP] Austria is a country located in Central Europe, north of Italy and Slovenia. The capital is Vienna.

name: authorship
query: Query: authorship [SEP] Authorship is the profession of writing. Also the identity of the writer as the creator of a literary production.

name: autism spectrum disorder
query: Query: autism spectrum disorder [SEP] Autism spectrum disorder is wide continuum of associated cognitive and neurobehavioral disorders, including, but not limited to, three core-defining features: impairments in socialization, impairments in verbal and nonverbal communication, and restricted and repetitive patterns of behaviors. (from [MASK])

name: autoimmune pancreatitis
query: Query: autoimmune pancreatitis [SEP] Autoimmune pancreatitis is chronic pancreatitis associated with autoimmune diseases.

name: autoimmunity
query: Query: autoimmunity [SEP] Autoimmunity is process whereby the immune system reacts against the body's own tissues. Autoimmunity may produce or be caused by autoimmune diseases.

name: automation , laboratory
query: Query: automation , laboratory [SEP] Laboratory automation is controlled operations of analytic or diagnostic processes, or systems by mechanical or electronic devices.

name: autonomic agents
query: Query: autonomic agents [SEP] Autonomic agents is agents affecting the function of, or mimicking the actions of, the autonomic nervous system and thereby having an effect on such processes as respiration, circulation, [MASK], body temperature regulation, certain endocrine gland secretions, etc.

name: autonomic nerve block
query: Query: autonomic nerve block [SEP] Autonomic nerve block is interruption of sympathetic pathways, by local injection of an anesthetic agent, at any of four levels: peripheral nerve block, sympathetic ganglion block, extradural block, and subarachnoid block.

name: autopsy
query: Query: autopsy [SEP] Autopsy is postmortem examination of the body.

name: avoidance learning
query: Query: avoidance learning [SEP] Avoidance learning is a response to a cue that is instrumental in avoiding a noxious experience.

name: awareness
query: Query: awareness [SEP] Awareness is the act of "taking account" of an object or state of affairs. It does not imply assessment of, nor attention to the qualities or nature of the object.

name: axial length , eye
query: Query: axial length , eye [SEP] Eye axial length is the distance between the anterior and posterior poles of the eye, measured either by ultrasonography or by partial coherence interferometry.

name: axillary artery
query: Query: axillary artery [SEP] Axillary artery is the continuation of the subclavian artery; it distributes over the upper limb, axilla, chest and [MASK].

name: axonal transport
query: Query: axonal transport [SEP] Axonal transport is the directed transport of organelles and molecules along nerve cell axons. Transport can be anterograde (from the cell body) or retrograde (toward the cell body). (Alberts et al., Molecular Biology of the Cell, 3d ed, pG3)

name: axon guidance
query: Query: axon guidance [SEP] Axon guidance is the mechanism by which a neuronal process outgrows toward a target led by the growth cone. Local guidance cues are provided by cell surface proteins that act on the growing axon.

name: axon initial segment
query: Query: axon initial segment [SEP] Axon initial segment is first segment of axon that connects distal axon segments to the neuronal cell body at the axon hillock region. The axon initial segment is not protected by the myelin sheath and has properties critical for axonal growth. The axon initial segment and the axon hillock form an axonal trigger zone.

name: background radiation
query: Query: background radiation [SEP] Background radiation is radiation from sources other than the source of interest. It is due to cosmic rays and natural radioactivity in the environment.

name: bacteria , anaerobic
query: Query: bacteria , anaerobic [SEP] Anaerobic bacteria is bacteria that can survive and grow in the complete, or nearly complete absence of oxygen.

name: bacterial adhesion
query: Query: bacterial adhesion [SEP] Bacterial adhesion is physicochemical property of fimbriated (fimbriae, bacterial) and non-fimbriated bacteria of attaching to cells, tissue, and nonbiological surfaces. It is a factor in bacterial colonization and pathogenicity.

name: bacterial capsules
query: Query: bacterial capsules [SEP] Bacterial capsules is an envelope of loose gel surrounding a bacterial cell which is associated with the virulence of pathogenic bacteria. Some capsules have a well-defined border, whereas others form a slime layer that trails off into the medium. Most capsules consist of relatively simple polysaccharides but there are some bacteria whose capsules are made of polypeptides.

name: bacterial load
query: Query: bacterial load [SEP] Bacterial load is measurable quantity of bacteria in an object, organism, or organism compartment.

name: bacterial shedding
query: Query: bacterial shedding [SEP] Bacterial shedding is the expelling of bacteria from the body. Important routes include the respiratory tract, genital tract, and intestinal tract.

name: bacterial transferrin receptor complex
query: Query: bacterial transferrin receptor complex [SEP] Bacterial transferrin receptor complex is a complex of proteins that forms a receptor for transferrin in bacteria. Many pathogenic bacteria utilize the transferrin-binding complex to acquire their supply of iron from serum.

name: bacterium
query: Query: bacterium [SEP] Bacterium is single-celled microorganisms that can exist either as independent (free-living) organisms or as parasites (dependent on another organism for life)

name: balanced anesthesia
query: Query: balanced anesthesia [SEP] Balanced anesthesia is the use of several anesthetics together in small amounts, as opposed to a larger amount of one drug, to induce loss of sensation and loss of consciousness.

name: bangladesh
query: Query: bangladesh [SEP] Bangladesh is a country in Southern Asia, bordering the Bay of Bengal, between Burma and India. The capital is Dhaka.

name: banking , personal
query: Query: banking , personal [SEP] Personal banking is a financial account [MASK] up between a financial institution (such as a commercial bank) and a customer (individual, group, or business), whereby the latter may deposit and withdraw money, and where applicable, be paid interest.

name: barrett esophagus
query: Query: barrett esophagus [SEP] Barrett esophagus is a condition with damage to the lining of the lower esophagus resulting from chronic acid reflux (esophagitis, reflux). Through the process of metaplasia, the squamous cells are replaced by a columnar epithelium with cells resembling those of the intestine or the salmon-pink mucosa of the stomach. Barrett's columnar epithelium is a marker for severe reflux and precursor to adenocarcinoma of the esophagus.

name: basal ganglia hemorrhage
query: Query: basal ganglia hemorrhage [SEP] Basal ganglia hemorrhage is bleeding within the subcortical regions of cerebral hemispheres (basal ganglia). It is often associated with hypertension or arteriovenous malformations. Clinical manifestations may include headache; dyskinesias; and hemiparesis.

name: basal metabolism
query: Query: basal metabolism [SEP] Basal metabolism is metabolism (e.g., heat production) of an organism in an inactive, awake, fasting state. It may be determined directly by means of a calorimeter or indirectly by calculating the end products of oxidation within the organism or from the amount of oxygen utilized.

name: base composition
query: Query: base composition [SEP] Base composition is the relative amounts of the purines and pyrimidines in a nucleic acid.

name: basolateral nuclear complex
query: Query: basolateral nuclear complex [SEP] Basolateral nuclear complex is a [MASK] of amygdalar nuclei bordered laterally by the external capsule and medially by the central amygdaloid nucleus.

name: bed conversion
query: Query: bed conversion [SEP] Bed conversion is the reallocation of beds from one type of care service to another, as in converting acute care beds to long term care beds.

name: bed occupancy
query: Query: bed occupancy [SEP] Bed occupancy is a measure of inpatient health facility use based upon the average number or proportion of beds occupied for a given period of time.

name: bed rest
query: Query: bed rest [SEP] Bed rest is confinement of an individual to bed for therapeutic or experimental reasons.

name: beds
query: Query: beds [SEP] Beds is equipment on which one may lie and sleep, especially as used to care for the hospital patient.

name: beer
query: Query: beer [SEP] Beer is an alcoholic beverage usually made from malted cereal grain (as barley), flavored with hops, and brewed by slow fermentation.

name: beginning of human life
query: Query: beginning of human life [SEP] Beginning of human life is the point at which religious ensoulment or personhood is considered to begin.

name: behavioral medicine
query: Query: behavioral medicine [SEP] Behavioral medicine is the interdisciplinary field concerned with the development and integration of behavioral and biomedical science, knowledge, and techniques relevant to health and illness and the application of this knowledge and these techniques to prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and rehabilitation.

name: behavioral research
query: Query: behavioral research [SEP] Behavioral research is research that involves the application of the behavioral and social sciences to the study of the actions or reactions of persons or animals in response to external or internal stimuli. (from American Heritage Dictionary, 4th ed)

name: behavioral risk factor surveillance system
query: Query: behavioral risk factor surveillance system [SEP] Behavioral risk factor surveillance system is telephone surveys are conducted to monitor [MASK] of the major behavioral risks among adults associated with premature morbidity and mortality. The data collected is in regard to actual behaviors, rather than on attitudes or knowledge. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (cdc) established the Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System (brfss) in 1984.

name: behavior observation techniques
query: Query: behavior observation techniques [SEP] Behavior [MASK] techniques is a wide range of formal and informal techniques used to document behavior.

name: beijing
query: Query: beijing [SEP] Beijing is capital of china.

name: bell palsy
query: Query: bell palsy [SEP] Bell palsy is a syndrome characterized by the acute onset of unilateral [MASK] which progresses over a 2-5 day period. Weakness of the orbicularis oculi muscle and resulting incomplete eye closure may be associated with corneal injury. Pain behind the ear often precedes the onset of paralysis. This condition may be associated with herpesvirus 1, human infection of the facial nerve. (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1376)

name: benchmarking
query: Query: benchmarking [SEP] Benchmarking is method of measuring performance against established standards of [MASK].

name: benzene
query: Query: benzene [SEP] Benzene is toxic, volatile, flammable liquid hydrocarbon byproduct of coal distillation. It is used as an industrial solvent in paints, varnishes, lacquer thinners, gasoline, etc. Benzene causes central nervous system damage acutely and bone marrow damage chronically and is carcinogenic. It was formerly used as parasiticide.

name: berlin
query: Query: berlin [SEP] Berlin is the capital of Germany.

name: beta particles
query: Query: beta particles [SEP] Beta particles is high energy [MASK] or [MASK] ejected from a disintegrating atomic nucleus.

name: beta rhythm
query: Query: beta rhythm [SEP] Beta rhythm is brain waves with frequency between 15-30 Hz seen on eeg during wakefulness and mental activity.

name: bibliography
query: Query: bibliography [SEP] Bibliography is a work consisting of a list of books, articles, documents, publications, and other items, usually on a single subject or related subjects.

name: big data
query: Query: big data [SEP] Big data is extremely large amounts of data which require rapid and often complex computational analyses to reveal patterns, trends, and associations, relating to various facets of human and non-human entities.

name: bile acids and salts
query: Query: bile acids and salts [SEP] [MASK] acids and [MASK] is steroid acids and [MASK]. The primary [MASK] acids are derived from cholesterol in the liver and usually conjugated with glycine or taurine. The secondary [MASK] acids are further modified by bacteria in the intestine. They play an important role in the [MASK] and absorption of fat. They have also been used pharmacologically, especially in the treatment of gallstones.

name: bile reflux
query: Query: bile reflux [SEP] [MASK] reflux is retrograde [MASK] flow. Reflux of [MASK] can be from the duodenum to the stomach (duodenogastric reflux); to the esophagus (gastroesophageal reflux); or to the pancreas.

name: biliary tract surgical procedures
query: Query: biliary tract surgical procedures [SEP] Biliary tract surgical procedures is any surgical procedure performed on the biliary tract.

name: bilirubin
query: Query: bilirubin [SEP] Bilirubin is a [MASK] pigment that is a degradation product of heme.

name: binomial distribution
query: Query: binomial distribution [SEP] Binomial distribution is the probability distribution associated with two mutually exclusive outcomes; used to model cumulative incidence rates and [MASK] rates. The Bernoulli distribution is a special case of binomial distribution.

name: biological control agents
query: Query: biological control agents [SEP] Biological control agents is organisms, biological agents, or biologically-derived agents used strategically for their positive or adverse effect on the physiology and/or reproductive health of other organisms.

name: biological monitoring
query: Query: biological monitoring [SEP] Biological monitoring is monitoring of the level of toxins, chemical pollutants, microbial contaminants, or other harmful substances in the bodies of living organisms, by diagnostic imaging or by analyzing blood; urine; [MASK]; saliva, etc.

name: biological oxygen demand analysis
query: Query: biological oxygen demand analysis [SEP] Biological oxygen demand analysis is testing for the amount of biodegradable organic material in a water sample by measuring the quantity of oxygen consumed by biodegradation of those materials over a specific time period.

name: biological psychiatry
query: Query: biological psychiatry [SEP] Biological psychiatry is an interdisciplinary science concerned with studies of the biological bases of behavior - biochemical, genetic, physiological, and neurological - and applying these to the understanding and treatment of mental illness.

name: biological variation , individual
query: Query: biological variation , individual [SEP] Individual biological variation is differences in measurable biological values, characteristics, or traits, within one individual under different conditions for the individual such as fasting, season of the year, age, or state of wellness.

name: biomass
query: Query: biomass [SEP] Biomass is total mass of all the organisms of a given type and/or in a given area. (From Concise Dictionary of Biology, 1990) It includes the yield of vegetative mass produced from any given crop.

name: biomedical occupation or discipline
query: Query: biomedical occupation or discipline [SEP] Biomedical occupation or discipline is all of the divisions of the natural sciences dealing with the various aspects of the phenomena of life and vital processes.

name: biomedical or dental material
query: Query: biomedical or dental material [SEP] Biomedical or dental material is biomedical or dental material

name: biometric identification
query: Query: biometric identification [SEP] Biometric identification is a method of differentiating individuals based on the analysis of qualitative or quantitative biological traits or patterns. Biometric identification, which has applications in forensics and identity theft prevention, includes dna profiles or dna fingerprints; fingerprints; automated facial recognition; iris scan; retina scan; hand geometry; vascular patterns; automated voice pattern recognition; ultrasound of fingers; and x-rays.

name: biopsy , needle
query: Query: biopsy , needle [SEP] Needle biopsy is removal and examination of tissue obtained through a transdermal needle inserted into the specific region, organ, or tissue being analyzed.

name: biosynthetic pathways
query: Query: biosynthetic pathways [SEP] Biosynthetic pathways is sets of enzymatic reactions occurring in organisms and that form biochemicals by making new covalent bonds.

name: bird
query: Query: bird [SEP] Bird is warm-blooded vertebrates possessing feathres and belonging to the class Aves.

name: birth certificates
query: Query: birth certificates [SEP] Birth certificates is official certifications by a physician recording the individual's birth date, place of birth, parentage and other required identifying data which are filed with the local registrar of vital statistics.

name: birth intervals
query: Query: birth intervals [SEP] Birth intervals is the lengths of intervals between births to women in the population.

name: birth rate
query: Query: birth rate [SEP] Birth rate is the number of births in a given population per year or other unit of time.

name: birth weight
query: Query: birth weight [SEP] Birth weight is the mass or quantity of heaviness of an individual at birth. It is expressed by units of pounds or kilograms.

name: bleeding time
query: Query: bleeding time [SEP] Bleeding time is duration of blood flow after skin puncture. This test is used as a measure of capillary and platelet function.

name: blood alcohol content
query: Query: blood alcohol content [SEP] Blood alcohol content is mass of alcohol per unit of blood volume.

name: blood culture
query: Query: blood culture [SEP] Blood culture is test to determine the presence of blood infection (e.g. sepsis; bacteremia).

name: blood donors
query: Query: blood donors [SEP] Blood donors is a person who gives blood for use in transfusion.

name: blood flow velocity
query: Query: blood flow velocity [SEP] Blood flow velocity is a value equal to the total volume flow divided by the cross-sectional area of the vascular bed.

name: blood glucose
query: Query: blood glucose [SEP] Blood glucose is glucose in blood.

name: blood patch , epidural
query: Query: blood patch , epidural [SEP] Epidural blood patch is the injection of autologous blood into the [MASK] either as a prophylactic treatment immediately following an epidural puncture or for treatment of headache as a result of an epidural puncture.

name: blood platelets
query: Query: blood platelets [SEP] Blood platelets is non-nucleated disk-shaped cells formed in the megakaryocyte and found in the blood of all mammals. They are mainly involved in blood coagulation.

name: blood pressure monitoring , ambulatory
query: Query: blood pressure monitoring , ambulatory [SEP] Ambulatory blood pressure monitoring is method in which repeated blood pressure readings are made while the patient undergoes normal daily activities. It allows quantitative analysis of the high blood pressure load over time, can help distinguish between types of hypertension, and can assess the effectiveness of antihypertensive therapy.

name: blood safety
query: Query: blood safety [SEP] Blood safety is the degree to which the blood supply for blood transfusions is free of harmful substances or infectious agents, and properly typed and crossmatched (blood grouping and crossmatching) to insure serological compatibility between blood donors and recipients.

name: blood sedimentation
query: Query: blood sedimentation [SEP] Blood sedimentation is measurement of rate of settling of erythrocytes in anticoagulated blood.

name: blood specimen collection
query: Query: blood specimen collection [SEP] Blood specimen collection is the taking of a blood sample to determine its [MASK] as a whole, to identify levels of its component cells, chemicals, gases, or other constituents, to perform pathological examination, etc.

name: blood transfusion , autologous
query: Query: blood transfusion , autologous [SEP] Autologous blood transfusion is reinfusion of blood or blood products derived from the patient's own circulation. (Dorland, 27th ed)

name: blood transfusion , intrauterine
query: Query: blood transfusion , intrauterine [SEP] Intrauterine blood transfusion is in utero transfusion of blood into the fetus for the treatment of fetal diseases, such as fetal erythroblastosis (erythroblastosis, fetal).

name: blood urea nitrogen
query: Query: blood urea nitrogen [SEP] Blood urea nitrogen is the urea concentration of the blood stated in terms of nitrogen content. Serum (plasma) urea nitrogen is approximately 12% higher than blood urea nitrogen concentration because of the greater protein content of red blood cells. Increases in blood or serum urea nitrogen are referred to as azotemia and may have prerenal, renal, or postrenal causes. (From Saunders Dictionary & Encyclopedia of Laboratory Medicine and Technology, 1984)

name: blood vessel prosthesis implantation
query: Query: blood vessel prosthesis implantation [SEP] Blood vessel prosthesis implantation is surgical insertion of blood vessel prostheses to repair injured or diseased blood vessels.

name: blood volume determination
query: Query: blood volume determination [SEP] Blood volume determination is method for determining the circulating blood volume by introducing a known quantity of foreign substance into the blood and determining its concentration some minutes later when thorough mixing has occurred. From these two values the blood volume can be calculated by dividing the quantity of injected material by its concentration in the blood at the time of uniform mixing. Generally expressed as cubic centimeters or liters per kilogram of body weight.

name: bloom syndrome
query: Query: bloom syndrome [SEP] Bloom syndrome is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by telangiectatic erythema of the face, photosensitivity, dwarfism and other abnormalities, and a predisposition toward developing cancer. The Bloom syndrome gene (blm) encodes a RecQ-like dna helicase.

name: blotting , northern
query: Query: blotting , northern [SEP] Northern blotting is detection of rna that has been electrophoretically separated and immobilized by blotting on nitrocellulose or other type of [MASK] or nylon membrane followed by hybridization with labeled nucleic acid probes.

name: blotting , southern
query: Query: blotting , southern [SEP] Southern blotting is a method (first developed by e.m. Southern) for detection of dna that has been electrophoretically separated and immobilized by blotting on nitrocellulose or other type of [MASK] or nylon membrane followed by hybridization with labeled nucleic acid probes.

name: body height
query: Query: body height [SEP] Body height is the distance from the sole to the crown of the head with body standing on a flat surface and fully extended.

name: body location or region
query: Query: body location or region [SEP] Body location or region is anatomical areas of the body.

name: body mass index
query: Query: body mass index [SEP] Body mass index is an indicator of body density as determined by the relationship of body weight to body height. BMI=weight (kg)/height squared (m2). bmi correlates with body fat (adipose tissue). Their relationship varies with age and gender. For adults, bmi falls into these categories: below 18.5 (underweight); 18.5-24.9 (normal); 25.0-29.9 (overweight); 30.0 and above (obese). (National Center for Health Statistics, Centers for Disease Control and Prevention)

name: body part , organ , or organ component
query: Query: body part , organ , or organ component [SEP] Or organ component organ body part is body part , organ , or organ component

name: body remains
query: Query: body remains [SEP] Body remains is the physical entity of a deceased human or animal.

name: body space or junction
query: Query: body space or junction [SEP] Body space or junction is body space or junction

name: body substance
query: Query: body substance [SEP] Body substance is the substance of the body.

name: body surface area
query: Query: body surface area [SEP] Body surface area is the two dimensional measure of the outer layer of the body.

name: body system
query: Query: body system [SEP] Body system is groups of organs and tissues that work together to perform important jobs for the body.

name: body temperature regulation
query: Query: body temperature regulation [SEP] Body temperature regulation is the processes of [MASK] and cooling that an organism uses to control its temperature.

name: body water
query: Query: body water [SEP] Body water is fluids composed mainly of water found within the body.

name: bone banks
query: Query: bone banks [SEP] Bone banks is centers for acquiring, characterizing, and storing bones or bone tissue for future use.

name: bone density conservation agents
query: Query: bone density conservation agents [SEP] [MASK] conservation agents is agents that inhibit bone resorption and/or favor bone mineralization and bone regeneration. They are used to heal bone fractures and to treat metabolic bone diseases such as osteoporosis.

name: bone diseases , infectious
query: Query: bone diseases , infectious [SEP] Infectious bone diseases is bone diseases caused by pathogenic microorganisms.

name: bone marrow
query: Query: bone marrow [SEP] Bone marrow is the soft tissue filling the cavities of bones. Bone marrow exists in two types, yellow and red. Yellow marrow is found in the large cavities of large bones and consists mostly of fat cells and a few primitive blood cells. Red marrow is a hematopoietic tissue and is the site of production of erythrocytes and granular leukocytes. Bone marrow is made up of a framework of connective tissue containing branching fibers with the frame being filled with marrow cells.

name: bone marrow neoplasms
query: Query: bone marrow neoplasms [SEP] Bone marrow neoplasms is neoplasms located in the bone marrow. They are differentiated from neoplasms composed of bone marrow cells, such as multiple myeloma. Most bone marrow neoplasms are metastatic.

name: bone marrow transplantation
query: Query: bone marrow transplantation [SEP] Bone marrow transplantation is the transference of bone marrow from one human or animal to another for a variety of purposes including hematopoietic stem cell transplantation or mesenchymal stem cell transplantation.

name: bone matrix
query: Query: bone matrix [SEP] Bone matrix is extracellular substance of bone tissue consisting of collagen fibers, ground substance, and inorganic crystalline minerals and [MASK].

name: bone regeneration
query: Query: bone regeneration [SEP] Bone regeneration is renewal or repair of lost bone tissue. It excludes bony callus formed after bone fractures but not yet replaced by hard bone.

name: bony callus
query: Query: bony callus [SEP] Bony callus is the bony deposit formed between and around the broken ends of bone fractures during normal healing.

name: book collecting
query: Query: book collecting [SEP] Book collecting is seeking, locating, acquiring, organizing, cataloging, displaying, storing, and maintaining whatever books are of interest to a given individual collector.

name: book industry
query: Query: book industry [SEP] Book industry is the aggregate enterprise of manufacturing and technically producing books. (From Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

name: book review
query: Query: book review [SEP] Book review is work consisting of critical analyses of books or other monographic works.

name: books , illustrated
query: Query: books , illustrated [SEP] Illustrated books is books containing photographs, prints, drawings, portraits, plates, diagrams, facsimiles, maps, [MASK], or other representations or systematic arrangement of data designed to elucidate or decorate its contents. (From The ala Glossary of Library and Information Science, 1983, p114)

name: book selection
query: Query: book selection [SEP] Book selection is works about lists of books, articles, and other publications.

name: borderline personality disorder
query: Query: borderline personality disorder [SEP] Borderline personality disorder is a personality disorder marked by a pattern of instability of interpersonal relationships, self-image, and affects, and marked impulsivity beginning by early adulthood and present in a variety of contexts. ([MASK])

name: boston
query: Query: boston [SEP] Boston is city located in Massachusetts.

name: bottle feeding
query: Query: bottle feeding [SEP] Bottle feeding is use of nursing bottles for feeding. Applies to humans and animals.

name: brachial artery
query: Query: brachial artery [SEP] Brachial artery is the continuation of the axillary artery; it branches into the radial and ulnar arteries.

name: brachial plexus block
query: Query: brachial plexus block [SEP] Brachial plexus block is a blocking of [MASK] in the network of nerve fibers innervating the upper extremity.

name: brain abscess
query: Query: brain abscess [SEP] Brain abscess is a circumscribed collection of purulent exudate in the brain, due to bacterial and other infections. The majority are caused by spread of infected material from a focus of suppuration elsewhere in the body, notably the paranasal sinuses, [MASK] (see [MASK]); heart (see also endocarditis, bacterial), and lung. Penetrating craniocerebral trauma and neurosurgical procedures may also be associated with this condition. Clinical manifestations include headache; seizures; focal neurologic deficits; and alterations of consciousness. (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp712-6)

name: brain chemistry
query: Query: brain chemistry [SEP] Brain chemistry is changes in the amounts of various chemicals (neurotransmitters, receptors, enzymes, and other metabolites) specific to the area of the central nervous system contained within the head. These are monitored over time, during sensory stimulation, or under different disease states.

name: brain death
query: Query: brain death [SEP] Brain death is a state of prolonged irreversible cessation of all brain activity, including lower brain stem function with the complete absence of voluntary movements, responses to stimuli, brain stem reflexes, and spontaneous respirations. Reversible conditions which mimic this clinical state (e.g., sedative overdose, hypothermia, etc.) are excluded prior to making the determination of brain death. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp348-9)

name: brain edema
query: Query: brain edema [SEP] Brain edema is increased intracellular or extracellular fluid in brain tissue. Cytotoxic brain edema (swelling due to increased intracellular fluid) is indicative of a disturbance in cell metabolism, and is commonly associated with hypoxic or ischemic injuries (see hypoxia, brain). An increase in extracellular fluid may be caused by increased brain capillary permeability (vasogenic edema), an osmotic gradient, local blockages in interstitial fluid pathways, or by obstruction of csf flow (e.g., obstructive hydrocephalus). (From Childs Nerv Syst 1992 Sep; 8(6):301-6)

name: brain regeneration
query: Query: brain regeneration [SEP] Brain regeneration is endogenous repair and regeneration of the brain.
