name: brain stem
query: Query: brain stem [SEP] Brain stem is the part of the brain that connects the cerebral hemispheres with the spinal cord. It consists of the mesencephalon; pons; and medulla oblongata.

name: brain stem hemorrhage , traumatic
query: Query: brain stem hemorrhage , traumatic [SEP] Traumatic brain stem hemorrhage is bleeding into structures of brain stem, including the midbrain; pons; or medulla oblongata, as the result of craniocerebral trauma. diffuse axonal injury is commonly associated. Clinical manifestations may include ocular motility disorders; ataxia; paralysis; [MASK]; and coma.

name: brain tissue transplantation
query: Query: brain tissue transplantation [SEP] Brain tissue transplantation is transference of brain tissue, either from a fetus or from a born individual, between individuals of the same species or between individuals of different species.

name: branched dna signal amplification assay
query: Query: branched dna signal amplification assay [SEP] Branched dna signal amplification assay is a molecular probe technique that utilizes branched dna (bDNA) as a means to amplify the hybridization signal. One end of the bDNA molecule is designed to bind a specific target, while the other end of the bDNA molecule contains many branches of dna that are designed to bind a probe used for signal detection.

name: bread
query: Query: bread [SEP] Bread is baked food product made of flour or meal that is moistened, kneaded, and sometimes fermented. a major food since prehistoric times, it has been made in various forms using a variety of ingredients and methods.

name: breakthrough pain
query: Query: breakthrough pain [SEP] Breakthrough pain is acute pain that comes on rapidly despite the use of pain medication.

name: breast cyst
query: Query: breast cyst [SEP] Breast cyst is a fluid-filled closed cavity or sac that is lined by an epithelium and found in the breast. It may appear as a single large cyst in one breast, multifocal, or bilateral in fibrocystic breast disease.

name: breast implantation
query: Query: breast implantation [SEP] Breast implantation is surgical insertion of an inert sac filled with silicone or other material to augment the female form cosmetically.

name: breath holding
query: Query: breath holding [SEP] Breath holding is an involuntary or voluntary pause in breathing, sometimes accompanied by loss of consciousness.

name: breathing exercises
query: Query: breathing exercises [SEP] Breathing exercises is therapeutic exercises aimed to deepen inspiration or expiration or even to alter the rate and rhythm of respiration.

name: brief psychiatric rating scale
query: Query: brief psychiatric rating scale [SEP] Brief psychiatric rating scale is a scale comprising 18 symptom constructs chosen to represent relatively independent dimensions of manifest psychopathology. The initial intended use was to provide more efficient assessment of treatment response in clinical psychopharmacology research; however, the scale was readily adapted to other uses. (From Hersen, m. and Bellack, a.s., Dictionary of Behavioral Assessment Techniques, p. 87)

name: broadly neutralizing antibodies
query: Query: broadly neutralizing antibodies [SEP] Broadly neutralizing antibodies is neutralizing antibodies that reduce or abolish some biological activity of a soluble antigen or infectious agent (e.g., hiv) by targeting several epitopes.

name: bronchial fistula
query: Query: bronchial fistula [SEP] Bronchial fistula is an abnormal passage or communication between a bronchus and another part of the body.

name: bronchial neoplasms
query: Query: bronchial neoplasms [SEP] Bronchial neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the bronchi.

name: building codes
query: Query: building codes [SEP] Building codes is standards or regulations for construction which are designed to ensure safety against electrical hazards, fires, etc.

name: built environment
query: Query: built environment [SEP] Built environment is the man-made physical elements of the environment (e.g., homes, buildings, streets, open spaces, and infrastructure). The built environment influences a person's level of physical activity and may have other impacts on health in a community.

name: bundle of his
query: Query: bundle of his [SEP] Bundle of his is small band of specialized cardiac muscle fibers that originates in the atrioventricular node and extends into the membranous part of the interventricular septum. The bundle of His, consisting of the left and the right bundle branches, conducts the electrical impulses to the heart ventricles in generation of [MASK].

name: burns , chemical
query: Query: burns , chemical [SEP] Chemical burns is burns caused by contact with or exposure to caustics or strong acids.

name: burns , electric
query: Query: burns , electric [SEP] Electric burns is burns produced by contact with electric current or from a sudden discharge of electricity.

name: burn units
query: Query: burn units [SEP] Burn units is specialized hospital facilities which provide intensive care for burn patients.

name: butter
query: Query: butter [SEP] Butter is the fatty portion of milk, separated as a soft yellowish solid when milk or cream is churned. It is processed for cooking and [MASK] use. (Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

name: cadmium
query: Query: cadmium [SEP] Cadmium is an element with atomic symbol Cd, atomic number 48, and atomic weight 112.41. It is a metal and ingestion will lead to [MASK].

name: cadmium chloride
query: Query: cadmium chloride [SEP] Cadmium chloride is a cadmium halide in the form of colorless crystals, soluble in water, methanol, and ethanol. It is used in photography, in dyeing, and calico printing, and as a solution to precipitate sulfides. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 5th ed)

name: calcium , dietary
query: Query: calcium , dietary [SEP] Dietary calcium is calcium compounds used as food supplements or in food to supply the body with calcium. Dietary calcium is needed during growth for bone development and for maintenance of skeletal integrity later in life to prevent osteoporosis.

name: calcium carbonate
query: Query: calcium carbonate [SEP] Calcium carbonate is carbonic acid calcium [MASK] (CaCO3). An odorless, tasteless powder or crystal that occurs in nature. It is used therapeutically as a phosphate [MASK] in hemodialysis patients and as a calcium supplement.

name: calcium chloride
query: Query: calcium chloride [SEP] Calcium chloride is a [MASK] used to replenish calcium levels, as an acid-producing diuretic, and as an antidote for magnesium poisoning.

name: calcium citrate
query: Query: calcium citrate [SEP] Calcium citrate is a colorless crystalline or [MASK] powdery organic, tricarboxylic acid occurring in plants, especially citrus fruits, and used as a flavoring agent, as an antioxidant in foods, and as a sequestrating agent. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

name: calcium fluoride
query: Query: calcium fluoride [SEP] Calcium fluoride is calcium fluoride. Occurring in nature as the mineral fluorite or fluorspar. It is the primary source of fluorine and its compounds. Pure calcium fluoride is used as a catalyst in [MASK] and dehydrogenation and is used to fluoridate drinking water. (From Merck Index, 11th ed)

name: calcium isotopes
query: Query: calcium isotopes [SEP] Calcium isotopes is stable calcium atoms that have the same atomic number as the element calcium, but differ in atomic weight. Ca-42-44, 46, and 48 are stable calcium isotopes.

name: calcium metabolism disorders
query: Query: calcium metabolism disorders [SEP] Calcium metabolism disorders is disorders in the processing of calcium in the body: its absorption, transport, storage, and utilization.

name: calcium release activated calcium channels
query: Query: calcium release activated calcium channels [SEP] Calcium release activated calcium channels is specialized calcium channels that localize to the endoplamsic reticulum and plasma membrane. They contain the pore subunit orai1 protein which is activated by stromal interaction molecules upon intracellular calcium depletion.

name: calcium sulfate
query: Query: calcium sulfate [SEP] Calcium sulfate is a calcium [MASK] that is used for a variety of purposes including: building materials, as a desiccant, in dentistry as an impression material, cast, or die, and in medicine for immobilizing casts and as a tablet excipient. It exists in various forms and states of hydration. Plaster of Paris is a mixture of powdered and heat-treated gypsum.

name: calibration
query: Query: calibration [SEP] Calibration is determination, by measurement or comparison with a standard, of the correct value of each scale reading on a meter or other measuring instrument; or determination of the settings of a control device that correspond to particular values of voltage, current, frequency or other output.

name: call centers
query: Query: call centers [SEP] Call centers is a facility [MASK] up for the purpose of handling large volumes of telephone calls. Call Centers typically utilize some form of computer automation for receiving, dispatching, screening, logging and forwarding telephone calls.

name: cancer care facilities
query: Query: cancer care facilities [SEP] Cancer care facilities is institutions specializing in the care of cancer patients.

name: cannula
query: Query: cannula [SEP] Cannula is short, hollow cylinders or tubes for insertion into a canal, vessel, or body cavity.

name: capacity building
query: Query: capacity building [SEP] Capacity building is organizational development including enhancement of management structures, processes and procedures, within organizations and among different organizations and sectors to meet present and future needs.

name: capillary action
query: Query: capillary action [SEP] Capillary action is a phenomenon in which the surface of a liquid where it contacts a solid is elevated or depressed, because of the relative attraction of the molecules of the liquid for each other and for those of the solid. (from McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

name: capillary leak syndrome
query: Query: capillary leak syndrome [SEP] Capillary leak syndrome is a condition characterized by recurring episodes of fluid leaking from capillaries into extra-vascular compartments causing hematocrit to rise precipitously. If not treated, generalized vascular leak can lead to generalized edema; shock; cardiovascular collapse; and [MASK].

name: capillary permeability
query: Query: capillary permeability [SEP] Capillary permeability is the property of blood capillary endothelium that allows for the selective exchange of substances between the blood and surrounding tissues and through membranous barriers such as the blood-air barrier; blood-aqueous barrier; blood-brain barrier; blood-nerve barrier; blood-retinal barrier; and blood-testis barrier. Small lipid-soluble molecules such as carbon dioxide and oxygen move freely by diffusion. Water and water-soluble molecules cannot pass through the endothelial walls and are dependent on microscopic pores. These pores show narrow areas (tight junctions) which may limit large molecule movement.

name: capital expenditures
query: Query: capital expenditures [SEP] Capital expenditures is those funds disbursed for facilities and equipment, particularly those related to the delivery of health care.

name: capital financing
query: Query: capital financing [SEP] Capital financing is institutional funding for facilities and for equipment which becomes a part of the assets of the institution.

name: capsules
query: Query: capsules [SEP] Capsules is hard or soft soluble containers used for the oral administration of medicine.

name: carbohydrate biochemistry
query: Query: carbohydrate biochemistry [SEP] Carbohydrate biochemistry is the study of the structure, biosynthesis, and function of carbohydrates and [MASK].

name: carbon disulfide
query: Query: carbon disulfide [SEP] Carbon disulfide is a colorless, flammable, poisonous liquid, cs2. It is used as a solvent, and is a counterirritant and has local anesthetic properties but is not used as such. It is highly toxic with pronounced cns, hematologic, and dermatologic effects.

name: carbon footprint
query: Query: carbon footprint [SEP] Carbon footprint is a measure of the total greenhouse gas emissions produced by an individual, organization, event, or product. It is measured in units of equivalent kilograms of carbon dioxide generated in a given time frame.

name: carbon sequestration
query: Query: carbon sequestration [SEP] Carbon sequestration is any of several processes for the permanent or long-term artificial or natural capture or removal and storage of carbon dioxide and other forms of carbon, through biological, chemical or physical processes, in a manner that prevents it from being released into the atmosphere.

name: carcinoma , basal cell
query: Query: carcinoma , basal cell [SEP] Basal cell carcinoma is a malignant skin neoplasm that seldom metastasizes but has potentialities for local invasion and destruction. Clinically it is divided into types: nodular, cicatricial, morphaic, and erythematoid (pagetoid). They develop on hair-bearing skin, most commonly on sun-exposed areas. Approximately 85% are found on the head and [MASK] area and the remaining 15% on the trunk and limbs. (From DeVita Jr et al., Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 3d ed, p1471)

name: carcinoma , ductal , breast
query: Query: carcinoma , ductal , breast [SEP] Breast ductal carcinoma is an invasive (infiltrating) carcinoma of the mammary ductal system (mammary glands) in the human breast.

name: carcinoma , hepatocellular
query: Query: carcinoma , hepatocellular [SEP] Hepatocellular carcinoma is a primary malignant neoplasm of epithelial liver cells. It ranges from a well-differentiated tumor with epithelial cells indistinguishable from normal [MASK] to a poorly differentiated neoplasm. The cells may be uniform or markedly pleomorphic, or form giant cells. Several classification schemes have been suggested.

name: carcinoma , islet cell
query: Query: carcinoma , islet cell [SEP] Islet cell carcinoma is a primary malignant neoplasm of the pancreatic islet cells. Usually it involves the non-INSULIN-producing cell types, the pancreatic alpha cells and the pancreatic delta cells (somatostatin-secreting cells) in glucagonoma and somatostatinoma, respectively.

name: carcinoma , krebs 2
query: Query: carcinoma , krebs 2 [SEP] Krebs 2 carcinoma is a transplantable neoplasm of mice.

name: carcinoma , large cell
query: Query: carcinoma , large cell [SEP] Large cell carcinoma is a tumor of undifferentiated (anaplastic) cells of large size. It is usually bronchogenic. (From Dorland, 27th ed)

name: carcinoma , medullary
query: Query: carcinoma , medullary [SEP] Medullary carcinoma is a carcinoma composed mainly of epithelial elements with little or no stroma. Medullary carcinomas of the breast constitute 5%-7% of all mammary carcinomas; medullary carcinomas of the thyroid comprise 3%-10% of all thyroid malignancies. (From Dorland, 27th ed; DeVita Jr et al., Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 3d ed, p1141; Segen, Dictionary of Modern Medicine, 1992)

name: carcinoma , pancreatic ductal
query: Query: carcinoma , pancreatic ductal [SEP] Pancreatic ductal carcinoma is carcinoma that arises from the pancreatic ducts. It accounts for the majority of cancers derived from the pancreas.

name: carcinoma , papillary
query: Query: carcinoma , papillary [SEP] Papillary carcinoma is a malignant neoplasm characterized by the formation of numerous, irregular, finger-like projections of fibrous stroma that is covered with a surface layer of neoplastic epithelial cells. (Stedman, 25th ed)

name: carcinoma , papillary , follicular
query: Query: carcinoma , papillary , follicular [SEP] Follicular papillary carcinoma is a thyroid neoplasm of mixed papillary and follicular arrangement. Its biological behavior and prognosis is the same as that of a papillary adenocarcinoma of the thyroid. (From DeVita Jr et al., Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 3d ed, p1271)

name: carcinoma , small cell
query: Query: carcinoma , small cell [SEP] Small cell carcinoma is an anaplastic, highly malignant, and usually bronchogenic carcinoma composed of small ovoid cells with scanty neoplasm. It is characterized by a dominant, deeply basophilic nucleus, and absent or indistinct nucleoli. (From Stedman, 25th ed; [MASK] et al., Cancer Medicine, 3d ed, p1286-7)

name: carcinoma , transitional cell
query: Query: carcinoma , transitional cell [SEP] Transitional cell carcinoma is a malignant neoplasm derived from transitional epithelial cells, occurring chiefly in the [MASK]; ureters; or [MASK].

name: carcinoma 256 , walker
query: Query: carcinoma 256 , walker [SEP] Walker carcinoma 256 is a transplantable carcinoma of the rat that originally appeared spontaneously in the mammary gland of a pregnant albino rat, and which now resembles a carcinoma in young [MASK] and a sarcoma in older [MASK]. (Stedman, 25th ed)

name: cardiac care facilities
query: Query: cardiac care facilities [SEP] Cardiac care facilities is institutions specializing in the care of patients with heart disorders.

name: cardiac catheterization
query: Query: cardiac catheterization [SEP] Cardiac catheterization is procedures in which placement of cardiac catheters is performed for therapeutic or diagnostic procedures.

name: cardiac catheters
query: Query: cardiac catheters [SEP] Cardiac catheters is catheters inserted into various locations within the heart for diagnostic or therapeutic purposes.

name: cardiac output , high
query: Query: cardiac output , high [SEP] High cardiac output is a state of elevated cardiac output due to conditions of either increased hemodynamic demand or reduced cardiac oxygen output. These conditions may include anemia; arteriovenous fistula; thyrotoxicosis; pregnancy; exercise; fever; and hypoxia. In time, compensatory changes of the heart can lead to pathological form of high cardiac output and eventual heart failure.

name: cardiac output , low
query: Query: cardiac output , low [SEP] Low cardiac output is a state of subnormal or depressed cardiac output at rest or during stress. It is a characteristic of cardiovascular diseases, including congenital, valvular, rheumatic, hypertensive, coronary, and cardiomyopathic. The serious form of low cardiac output is characterized by marked reduction in [MASK], and systemic vasoconstriction resulting in cold, pale, and sometimes cyanotic extremities.

name: cardiac pacing , artificial
query: Query: cardiac pacing , artificial [SEP] Artificial cardiac pacing is regulation of the rate of contraction of the heart muscles by an artificial pacemaker.

name: cardiac rehabilitation
query: Query: cardiac rehabilitation [SEP] Cardiac rehabilitation is restoration of functions to the maximum degree possible in a person or persons suffering from a cardiovascular disease. It also includes cardiac conditioning and secondary prevention in patients with elevated cardiovascular risk profile.

name: cardiology
query: Query: cardiology [SEP] Cardiology is the study of the heart, its physiology, and its functions.

name: cardiovascular nursing
query: Query: cardiovascular nursing [SEP] Cardiovascular nursing is a specialty concerned with the nursing care of patients suffering from disorders of the cardiovascular system as well as those identified as at risk for adverse cardiac or vascular events.

name: career choice
query: Query: career choice [SEP] Career choice is selection of a type of occupation or profession.

name: caregivers
query: Query: caregivers [SEP] Caregivers is persons who provide care to those who need supervision or assistance in illness or disability. They may provide the care in the home, in a hospital, or in an institution. Although caregivers include trained medical, nursing, and other health personnel, the concept also refers to parents, spouses, or other family members, friends, members of the clergy, teachers, social workers, fellow patients.

name: caribbean netherlands
query: Query: caribbean netherlands [SEP] Caribbean [MASK] is a group Caribbean islands including Bonaire, Sint Eustatius, and Saba.

name: carotid artery , external
query: Query: carotid artery , external [SEP] External carotid artery is branch of the common carotid artery which supplies the exterior of the head, the face, and the greater part of the [MASK].

name: carotid artery , internal
query: Query: carotid artery , internal [SEP] Internal carotid artery is branch of the common carotid artery which supplies the anterior part of the brain, the eye and its appendages, the forehead and nose.

name: carotid artery , internal , dissection
query: Query: carotid artery , internal , dissection [SEP] [MASK] internal carotid artery is the splitting of the vessel wall in one or both (left and right) internal carotid arteries (carotid artery, internal). Interstitial hemorrhage into the media of the vessel wall can lead to occlusion of the internal carotid artery and aneurysm formation.

name: carotid sinus
query: Query: carotid sinus [SEP] Carotid sinus is the dilated portion of the common carotid artery at its bifurcation into external and internal carotids. It contains baroreceptors which, when stimulated, cause slowing of the heart, vasodilatation, and a fall in blood pressure.

name: carotid stenosis
query: Query: carotid stenosis [SEP] Carotid stenosis is narrowing or stricture of any part of the carotid arteries, most often due to [MASK] formation. Ulcerations may form in [MASK] and induce thrombus formation. Platelet or cholesterol emboli may arise from stenotic carotid lesions and induce a transient ischemic attack; cerebrovascular accident; or temporary blindness (amaurosis fugax). (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp 822-3)

name: carrier state
query: Query: carrier state [SEP] Carrier state is the condition of harboring an infective organism without manifesting symptoms of infection. The organism must be readily transmissible to another susceptible host.

name: cartilage , articular
query: Query: cartilage , articular [SEP] Articular cartilage is a protective layer of firm, flexible cartilage over the articulating ends of bones. It provides a smooth surface for joint movement, protecting the ends of long bones from wear at points of contact.

name: cartilage diseases
query: Query: cartilage diseases [SEP] Cartilage diseases is pathological processes involving the chondral tissue (cartilage).

name: casein kinase ii
query: Query: casein kinase ii [SEP] Casein kinase ii is a ubiquitous casein kinase that is comprised of two distinct [MASK] and dimeric regulatory subunit. Casein kinase ii has been shown to phosphorylate a large number of substrates, many of which are proteins involved in the regulation of gene expression.

name: case management
query: Query: case management [SEP] Case management is a traditional term for all the activities which a physician or other health care professional normally performs to insure the coordination of the medical services required by a patient. It also, when used in connection with managed care, covers all the activities of evaluating the patient, planning treatment, referral, and follow-up so that care is continuous and comprehensive and payment for the care is obtained. (From Slee & Slee, Health Care Terms, 2nd ed)

name: case managers
query: Query: case managers [SEP] Case managers is professionals who are in charge of assessment, planning, facilitation, care coordination, evaluation, and advocacy for options and services to meet a patient’s and family’s comprehensive health needs.

name: case reports
query: Query: case reports [SEP] Case reports is clinical presentations that may be followed by evaluative studies that eventually lead to a diagnosis.

name: caspase 8
query: Query: caspase 8 [SEP] Caspase 8 is a long pro-domain caspase that contains a [MASK] in its pro-domain region. Caspase 8 plays a role in apoptosis by cleaving and activating effector caspases. Activation of this enzyme can occur via the interaction of its N-terminal [MASK] with death domain receptor signaling adaptor proteins.

name: caspase 9
query: Query: caspase 9 [SEP] Caspase 9 is a long pro-domain caspase that contains a caspase recruitment domain in its pro-domain region. Caspase 9 is activated during cell stress by mitochondria-derived proapoptotic factors and by card signaling adaptor proteins such as apoptotic protease-activating factor 1. It activates apoptosis by cleaving and activating effector caspases.

name: caspase activation and recruitment domain
query: Query: caspase activation and recruitment domain [SEP] Caspase activation and recruitment domain is a homotypic protein interaction module of the death domain superfamily. It is composed of a bundle of six alpha-helices that is related in sequence and structure to the death domain and [MASK]. The Caspase Activation and Recruitment Domain (card domain) typically associates with other CARD-containing proteins, forming either dimers or trimers. card domains may occur in isolation, or in combination with other domains in card signaling adaptor proteins and initiator caspases that function in apoptosis.

name: caspase inhibitors
query: Query: caspase inhibitors [SEP] Caspase inhibitors is endogenous and exogenous compounds and that either inhibit caspases or prevent their activation.

name: catalog , drug
query: Query: catalog , drug [SEP] Drug catalog is lists of drugs for sale.

name: catalog , union
query: Query: catalog , union [SEP] Union catalog is lists of books and other information sources held among a cooperating group of libraries.

name: catalysis
query: Query: catalysis [SEP] Catalysis is the facilitation of a chemical reaction by material (catalyst) that is not consumed by the reaction.

name: cataract extraction
query: Query: cataract extraction [SEP] [MASK] extraction is the removal of a cataractous crystalline lens from the eye.

name: catastrophic illness
query: Query: catastrophic illness [SEP] Catastrophic illness is an acute or prolonged illness usually considered to be life-threatening or with the threat of serious residual disability. Treatment may be radical and is frequently costly.

name: catchment area , health
query: Query: catchment area , health [SEP] Health catchment area is a geographic area defined and served by a health program or institution.

name: cathepsin z
query: Query: cathepsin z [SEP] Cathepsin z is a ubiquitously-expressed [MASK] peptidase that exhibits carboxypeptidase activity. It is highly expressed in a variety of immune cell types and may play a role in inflammatory processes and immune responses.

name: catheterization , central venous
query: Query: catheterization , central venous [SEP] Central venous catheterization is placement of an intravenous catheter in the subclavian, jugular, or other central vein.

name: catheter obstruction
query: Query: catheter obstruction [SEP] Catheter obstruction is a hindrance to the passage of fluids through a catheter.

name: cathode ray tube
query: Query: cathode ray tube [SEP] Cathode ray tube is a vacuum tube equipped with an [MASK] emitting cathode and a fluorescent screen which emits visible light when excited by the cathode ray. Cathode ray tubes are used as imaging devises for televisions; computer terminals; text telecommunication devices; oscilloscopes; and other data display devices.

name: cations
query: Query: cations [SEP] Cations is positively charged atoms, radicals or groups of atoms which travel to the cathode or negative pole during electrolysis.

name: cell
query: Query: cell [SEP] Cell is the fundamental, structural, and functional units or subunits of living organisms. They are composed of cytoplasm containing various organelles and a cell membrane boundary.

name: cell adhesion
query: Query: cell adhesion [SEP] Cell adhesion is adherence of cells to surfaces or to other cells.

name: cell aggregation
query: Query: cell aggregation [SEP] Cell aggregation is the phenomenon by which dissociated cells intermixed in vitro tend to group themselves with cells of their own type.

name: cell biology
query: Query: cell biology [SEP] Cell biology is the study of the structure, behavior, growth, reproduction, and pathology of cells; and the function and chemistry of cellular components.

name: cell body
query: Query: cell body [SEP] Cell body is the portion of a cell that contains the nucleus and cytoplasm but not cell surface extensions such as flagella and neurites.

name: cell component
query: Query: cell component [SEP] Cell component is components of a cell.

name: cell enlargement
query: Query: cell enlargement [SEP] Cell enlargement is growth processes that result in an increase in cell size.

name: cell extracts
query: Query: cell extracts [SEP] Cell extracts is preparations of cell constituents or subcellular materials, isolates, or substances.

name: cell function
query: Query: cell function [SEP] Cell function is the function of cell.

name: cell fusion
query: Query: cell fusion [SEP] Cell fusion is fusion of somatic cells in vitro or in vivo, which results in somatic cell hybridization.

name: cell lineage
query: Query: cell lineage [SEP] Cell lineage is the developmental history of specific differentiated cell types as traced back to the original stem cells in the embryo.

name: cell line authentication
query: Query: cell line authentication [SEP] Cell line authentication is techniques used to characterize and confirm the identity of a cell line. Characterization involves authentication to verify that it matches the original description of the cells and ensures that they are not cross-contaminated with another cell line. This is done to avoid attributing data incorrectly to the wrong cell line.

name: cell membrane permeability
query: Query: cell membrane permeability [SEP] Cell membrane permeability is a quality of cell membranes which permits the passage of solvents and solutes into and out of cells.

name: cell migration assays , leukocyte
query: Query: cell migration assays , leukocyte [SEP] Leukocyte cell migration assays is assays that measure the rate of migration of leukocytes. They may involve a variety of techniques such as measuring the movement of leukocytes through substrates such as agarose gels or the rate of exit of cells from a glass capillary.

name: cell migration assays , macrophage
query: Query: cell migration assays , macrophage [SEP] Macrophage cell migration assays is assays that measure the rate of migration of macrophages. They may involve the use hollow plastic chamber, sealed at one end with a porous membrane and suspended over a larger well which may contain chemotactic factors. The migration of cell through the pores to the other side of the membrane is measured.

name: cell migration inhibition
query: Query: cell migration inhibition [SEP] Cell migration inhibition is phenomenon of cell-mediated immunity measured by in vitro inhibition of the migration or [MASK] of antigen-stimulated leukocytes or macrophages. Specific cell migration assays have been developed to estimate levels of migration inhibitory factors, immune reactivity against tumor-associated antigens, and immunosuppressive effects of infectious microorganisms.

name: cell or molecular dysfunction
query: Query: cell or molecular dysfunction [SEP] Cell or molecular dysfunction is cell or molecular dysfunction

name: cell phone use
query: Query: cell phone use [SEP] Cell phone use is utilization of wireless phones for communication.

name: cell polarity
query: Query: cell polarity [SEP] Cell polarity is orientation of intracellular structures especially with respect to the apical and basolateral domains of the plasma membrane. Polarized cells must direct proteins from the Golgi apparatus to the appropriate domain since tight junctions prevent proteins from diffusing between the two domains.

name: cells , immobilized
query: Query: cells , immobilized [SEP] Immobilized cells is microbial, plant, or animal cells which are immobilized by attachment to solid structures, usually a column matrix. a common use of immobilized cells is in biotechnology for the bioconversion of a substrate to a particular product. (From Singleton & Sainsbury, Dictionary of Microbiology and Molecular Biology, 2d ed)

name: cell self renewal
query: Query: cell self renewal [SEP] Cell self renewal is the ability of certain cell types, such as progenitor cells or tumor cells,  to go through numerous cycles of cell division while still maintaining an undifferentiated or partially differentiated state.

name: cell shape
query: Query: cell shape [SEP] Cell shape is the quality of surface form or [MASK] of cells.

name: cell surface display techniques
query: Query: cell surface display techniques [SEP] Cell surface display techniques is techniques utilizing cells that express recombinant fusion proteins engineered to translocate through the cell membrane and remain attached to the outside of the cell.

name: cell survival
query: Query: cell survival [SEP] Cell survival is the span of viability of a cell characterized by the capacity to perform certain functions such as metabolism, growth, reproduction, some form of responsiveness, and adaptability.

name: cell tracking
query: Query: cell tracking [SEP] Cell tracking is non-invasive imaging of cells that have been labeled non-destructively, such as with nanoemulsions or [MASK] that can be detected by molecular imaging, to monitor their location, viability, cell lineage expansion, response to drugs, movement, or other behaviors in vivo.

name: cell transformation , viral
query: Query: cell transformation , viral [SEP] Viral cell transformation is an inheritable change in cells manifested by changes in cell division and growth and alterations in cell surface properties. It is induced by infection with a transforming virus.

name: cellular reprogramming
query: Query: cellular reprogramming [SEP] Cellular reprogramming is a process where fully differentiated or specialized cells revert to pluripotency or a less differentiated cell type.

name: cellulose , oxidized
query: Query: cellulose , oxidized [SEP] Oxidized cellulose is a cellulose of varied carboxyl content retaining the fibrous structure. It is commonly used as a local hemostatic and as a matrix for normal blood coagulation.

name: central cord syndrome
query: Query: central cord syndrome [SEP] Central cord syndrome is a syndrome associated with traumatic injury to the cervical or upper thoracic regions of the spinal cord characterized by weakness in the [MASK] with relative sparing of the legs and variable sensory loss. This condition is associated with ischemia, hemorrhage, or necrosis involving the central portions of the spinal cord. Corticospinal fibers destined for the legs are spared due to their more external location in the spinal cord. This clinical pattern may emerge during recovery from spinal shock. Deficits may be transient or permanent.

name: centralized hospital services
query: Query: centralized hospital services [SEP] Centralized hospital services is the coordination of services in one area of a facility to improve efficiency.

name: central nervous system parasitic infections
query: Query: central nervous system parasitic infections [SEP] Central nervous system parasitic infections is infections of the brain, spinal cord, and meninges caused by parasites.

name: central nervous system sensitization
query: Query: central nervous system sensitization [SEP] Central nervous system sensitization is an increased response to stimulation that is mediated by amplification of signaling in the central nervous system (cns).

name: central nervous system vascular malformations
query: Query: central nervous system vascular malformations [SEP] Central nervous system vascular malformations is congenital, inherited, or acquired abnormalities involving arteries; veins; or venous sinuses in the brain; spinal cord; and meninges.

name: central pattern generators
query: Query: central pattern generators [SEP] Central pattern generators is networks of nerve cells that control the firing patterns of motor neurons to produce rhythmic movements such as mastication; walking; [MASK]; respiration; and peristalsis.

name: central tolerance
query: Query: central tolerance [SEP] Central tolerance is the mechanism, in central lymphoid organs (thymus; bone marrow), that prevents immature lymphocytes from reacting to self-antigens. This is accomplished by clonal anergy and clonal deletion.

name: central venous catheters
query: Query: central venous catheters [SEP] Central venous catheters is catheters that are inserted into a large central vein such as a subclavian vein or femoral vein.

name: cerebellar ataxia
query: Query: cerebellar ataxia [SEP] Cerebellar ataxia is incoordination of voluntary movements that occur as a manifestation of cerebellar diseases. Characteristic features include a tendency for limb movements to overshoot or undershoot a target (dysmetria), a tremor that occurs during attempted movements (intention tremor), impaired force and rhythm of diadochokinesis (rapidly alternating movements), and [MASK]. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p90)

name: cerebellar golgi cells
query: Query: cerebellar golgi cells [SEP] Cerebellar golgi cells is inhibitory interneurons embedded in the granular layer of the cerebellar cortex.

name: cerebellar neoplasms
query: Query: cerebellar neoplasms [SEP] Cerebellar neoplasms is primary or metastatic neoplasms of the cerebellum. Tumors in this location frequently present with ataxia or signs of intracranial hypertension due to obstruction of the fourth ventricle. Common primary cerebellar tumors include fibrillary astrocytoma and cerebellar hemangioblastoma. The cerebellum is a relatively common site for tumor metastases from the lung, breast, and other distant organs. (From Okazaki & Scheithauer, Atlas of Neuropathology, 1988, p86 and p141)

name: cerebellar nuclei
query: Query: cerebellar nuclei [SEP] Cerebellar nuclei is four clusters of neurons located deep within the [MASK] matter of the cerebellum, which are the nucleus dentatus, nucleus emboliformis, nucleus globosus, and nucleus fastigii.

name: cerebral angiography
query: Query: cerebral angiography [SEP] Cerebral angiography is radiography of the vascular system of the brain after injection of a contrast medium.

name: cerebral blood volume
query: Query: cerebral blood volume [SEP] Cerebral blood volume is volume of circulating blood in a region of the brain. It is a functional measure of the brain perfusion status which relates changes in this to changes in cerebrovasular circulation that are often seen in brain diseases.

name: cerebral hemorrhage , traumatic
query: Query: cerebral hemorrhage , traumatic [SEP] Traumatic cerebral hemorrhage is bleeding into one or both cerebral hemispheres due to trauma. Hemorrhage may involve any part of the cerebral cortex and the basal ganglia. Depending on the severity of bleeding, clinical features may include seizures; aphasia; vision disorders; movement disorders; paralysis; and coma.

name: cerebral palsy
query: Query: cerebral palsy [SEP] Cerebral palsy is a heterogeneous group of nonprogressive motor disorders caused by chronic brain injuries that originate in the prenatal period, perinatal period, or first few years of life. The four major subtypes are spastic, athetoid, ataxic, and mixed cerebral palsy, with spastic forms being the most common. The motor disorder may range from difficulties with fine motor control to severe spasticity (see muscle spasticity) in all limbs. Spastic diplegia (Little disease) is the most common subtype, and is characterized by spasticity that is more prominent in the legs than in the [MASK]. Pathologically, this condition may be associated with leukomalacia, periventricular. (From Dev Med Child Neurol 1998 Aug;40(8):520-7)

name: cerebral small vessel diseases
query: Query: cerebral small vessel diseases [SEP] Cerebral small vessel diseases is pathological processes or diseases where cerebral microvessels show abnormalities. They are often associated with aging, hypertension and risk factors for lacunar infarcts (see lacunar infarction); leukoaraiosis; and cerebral hemorrhage.

name: cerebral veins
query: Query: cerebral veins [SEP] Cerebral veins is veins draining the cerebrum.

name: cerebral ventricle neoplasms
query: Query: cerebral ventricle neoplasms [SEP] Cerebral ventricle neoplasms is neoplasms located in the brain ventricles, including the two lateral, the third, and the fourth ventricle. Ventricular tumors may be primary (e.g., choroid plexus neoplasms and glioma, subependymal), metastasize from distant organs, or occur as extensions of locally invasive tumors from adjacent brain structures.

name: cerebrospinal fluid
query: Query: cerebrospinal fluid [SEP] Cerebrospinal fluid is a watery fluid that is continuously produced in the choroid plexus and circulates around the surface of the brain; spinal cord; and in the cerebral ventricles.

name: cerebrospinal fluid leak
query: Query: cerebrospinal fluid leak [SEP] Cerebrospinal fluid leak is discharge of cerebrospinal fluid through a hole through the skull bone most commonly draining from the nose (cerebrospinal fluid rhinorrhea) or the ear (cerebrospinal fluid otorrhea).

name: cerebrospinal fluid proteins
query: Query: cerebrospinal fluid proteins [SEP] Cerebrospinal fluid proteins is proteins in the cerebrospinal fluid, normally albumin and globulin present in the ratio of 8 to 1. Increases in protein levels are of diagnostic value in neurological diseases. (Brain and Bannister's Clinical Neurology, 7th ed, p221)

name: certificate of need
query: Query: certificate of need [SEP] Certificate of need is a certificate issued by a governmental body to an individual or organization proposing to construct or modify a health facility, or to offer a new or different service. The process of issuing the certificate is also included.

name: cervical plexus
query: Query: cervical plexus [SEP] Cervical plexus is a network of nerve fibers originating in the upper four [MASK] segments. The cervical plexus distributes cutaneous nerves to parts of the [MASK], [MASK], and back of the head. It also distributes motor fibers to muscles of the cervical spinal column, infrahyoid muscles, and the diaphragm.

name: cervical plexus block
query: Query: cervical plexus block [SEP] Cervical plexus block is a blocking of [MASK] in the network of nerve fibers innervating the [MASK] and [MASK].

name: cervical rib syndrome
query: Query: cervical rib syndrome [SEP] Cervical rib syndrome is a condition associated with compression of the brachial plexus; subclavian artery; and subclavian vein at the thoracic outlet and caused by a complete or incomplete anomalous cervical rib or fascial band connecting the tip of a cervical rib with the first thoracic rib. Clinical manifestations may include pain in the [MASK] and [MASK] which radiates into the upper extremity, paresis or paralysis of brachial plexus innervated muscles; sensory loss; paresthesias; ischemia; and edema. (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p214)

name: cesarean section , repeat
query: Query: cesarean section , repeat [SEP] Repeat cesarean section is extraction of the fetus by abdominal hysterotomy anytime following a previous cesarean.

name: change management
query: Query: change management [SEP] Change management is processes, tools, and techniques involved in the management of organizational innovation, the purpose of which is to help individuals and work groups make successful personal transitions which ensure overall successful outcomes.

name: channel islands
query: Query: channel islands [SEP] Channel islands is a group of four British islands and several islets in the English Channel off the coast of France. They are known to have been occupied prehistorically. They were a part of Normandy in 933 but were united to the British crown at the time of the Norman Conquest in 1066. Guernsey and Jersey originated noted breeds of cattle. (From Webster's New Geographical Dictionary, 1988, p242)

name: charge syndrome
query: Query: charge syndrome [SEP] Charge syndrome is rare disease characterized by coloboma; choanal atresia; and abnormal semicircular canals. Mutations in chd7 protein resulting in disturbed neural crest development are associated with charge Syndrome.

name: chart
query: Query: chart [SEP] Chart is work consisting of information presented in graphic form, for example, graphs or diagrams.

name: cheese
query: Query: cheese [SEP] Cheese is a nutritious food consisting primarily of the curd or the semisolid substance formed when milk coagulates.

name: chemical and drug induced liver injury , chronic
query: Query: chemical and drug induced liver injury , chronic [SEP] Chronic chemical and drug induced liver injury is liver disease lasting six months or more, caused by an adverse effect of a drug or chemical. The adverse effect may be caused by drugs, drug metabolites, chemicals from the environment, or an idiosyncratic response.

name: chemical hazard release
query: Query: chemical hazard release [SEP] Chemical hazard release is uncontrolled release of a chemical from its containment that either threatens to or causes exposure to a chemical hazard. Such an incident may occur accidentally or deliberately.

name: chemical industry
query: Query: chemical industry [SEP] Chemical industry is the aggregate enterprise of manufacturing and technically producing chemicals. (From Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

name: chemical safety
query: Query: chemical safety [SEP] Chemical safety is risk or hazard associated with the handling and use of chemicals.

name: chemistry , clinical
query: Query: chemistry , clinical [SEP] Clinical chemistry is the specialty of [MASK] applied to assays of physiologically important substances found in blood, urine, tissues, and other biological fluids for the purpose of aiding the physician in making a diagnosis or following therapy.

name: chemistry , inorganic
query: Query: chemistry , inorganic [SEP] Inorganic chemistry is a field of chemistry which pertains to chemical compounds or ions that do not contain the element carbon (with the exception of carbon dioxide and compounds containing a carbonate radical, e.g., calcium carbonate).

name: chemistry , organic
query: Query: chemistry , organic [SEP] Organic chemistry is the study of the structure, preparation, properties, and reactions of carbon compounds. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

name: chemistry , physical
query: Query: chemistry , physical [SEP] Physical chemistry is the study of chemical phenomena and processes in terms of the underlying physical phenomena and processes.

name: chemokines , c
query: Query: chemokines , c [SEP] C chemokines is group of chemokines without adjacent cysteines that are chemoattractants for lymphocytes only.

name: chemotherapy , adjuvant
query: Query: chemotherapy , adjuvant [SEP] Adjuvant chemotherapy is drug therapy given to augment or stimulate some other form of treatment such as surgery or radiation therapy. Adjuvant chemotherapy is commonly used in the therapy of cancer and can be administered before or after the primary treatment.

name: chemotherapy , cancer , regional perfusion
query: Query: chemotherapy , cancer , regional perfusion [SEP] Regional perfusion cancer chemotherapy is neoplasm drug therapy involving an extracorporeal circuit with temporary exclusion of the tumor-bearing area from the general circulation during which high concentrations of the drug are perfused to the isolated part.

name: chest tubes
query: Query: chest tubes [SEP] Chest tubes is plastic tubes used for drainage of air or fluid from the pleural space. Their surgical insertion is called tube thoracostomy.

name: chest wall oscillation
query: Query: chest wall oscillation [SEP] Chest wall oscillation is a respiratory support system used to remove mucus and clear airway by oscillating pressure on the chest.

name: chief cells , gastric
query: Query: chief cells , gastric [SEP] Gastric chief cells is epithelial cells that line the basal half of the gastric glands. Chief cells synthesize and export an inactive enzyme pepsinogen which is converted into the highly proteolytic enzyme pepsin in the acid environment of the stomach.

name: chief executive officers , hospital
query: Query: chief executive officers , hospital [SEP] Hospital chief executive officers is individuals who have the formal authority to manage a hospital, including its programs and services, in accordance with the goals and objectives established by a governing body (governing board).

name: child , abandoned
query: Query: child , abandoned [SEP] Abandoned child is a child or adolescent who is deserted by parents or parent substitutes without regard for its future care.

name: child , exceptional
query: Query: child , exceptional [SEP] Exceptional child is a child whose needs, abilities, or other characteristics vary so much from the average in mental, physical, or social areas that a greater than usual level of services is needed to facilitate the child's maximum potential development.

name: child , foster
query: Query: child , foster [SEP] Foster child is individual who is unable to live safely with his or her family, usually due to abuse or neglect in the family home.

name: child , hospitalized
query: Query: child , hospitalized [SEP] Hospitalized child is child hospitalized for short term care.

name: child , preschool
query: Query: child , preschool [SEP] Preschool child is a child between the ages of 2 and 5.

name: child abuse , sexual
query: Query: child abuse , sexual [SEP] Sexual child abuse is sexual maltreatment of the child or minor.

name: child day care centers
query: Query: child day care centers [SEP] Child day care centers is facilities which provide care for pre-school and school-age children.

name: child guidance
query: Query: child guidance [SEP] Child guidance is the psychiatric, sociological and psychological study and treatment of the developing child with emphasis on preventive or prophylactic measures focused on the familial, educational and socio-environmental milieu of the child.

name: child guidance clinics
query: Query: child guidance clinics [SEP] Child guidance clinics is facilities which administer the delivery of mental health counseling services to children.

name: child health
query: Query: child health [SEP] Child health is the concept covering the physical and mental conditions of children.

name: child labor
query: Query: child labor [SEP] Child labor is employment of minors in work that deprives children of their childhood, potential, dignity, and is harmful to their physical and mental development. (International Labor Organization, un)

name: child language
query: Query: child language [SEP] Child language is the language and sounds expressed by a child at a particular maturational stage in development.

name: child nutrition disorders
query: Query: child nutrition disorders [SEP] Child nutrition disorders is disorders caused by nutritional imbalance, either overnutrition or undernutrition, occurring in children ages 2 to 12 years.

name: child nutrition sciences
query: Query: child nutrition sciences [SEP] Child nutrition sciences is the study of nutrition processes as well as the components of food, their actions, interaction, and balance in relation to health and disease of children, infants or adolescents.

name: child of impaired parents
query: Query: child of impaired parents [SEP] Child of impaired parents is child with one or more parents afflicted by a physical or mental disorder.

name: child protective services
query: Query: child protective services [SEP] Child protective services is local governmental offices which investigate reports of abuse and neglect of children, and act to assure a safe environment for minors.

name: child reactive disorders
query: Query: child reactive disorders [SEP] Child reactive disorders is reactions to an event or [MASK] of events which are considered to be of pathological degree, that have not developed into a neurosis, psychosis, or personality disorder with fixed patterns.

name: child rearing
query: Query: child rearing [SEP] Child rearing is the training or bringing-up of children by parents or parent-substitutes. It is used also for child rearing practices in different societies, at different economic levels, in different ethnic groups, etc. It differs from parenting in that in child rearing the emphasis is on the act of training or bringing up the child and the interaction between the parent and child, while parenting emphasizes the responsibility and qualities of exemplary behavior of the parent.

name: chitosan
query: Query: chitosan [SEP] Chitosan is deacetylated chitin, a linear polysaccharide of deacetylated beta-1,4-D-glucosamine. It is used in [MASK] and to treat wounds.

name: chlorine
query: Query: chlorine [SEP] Chlorine is an element with atomic symbol Cl, atomic number 17, and atomic weight 35, and member of the halogen family.

name: chloroplast proteins
query: Query: chloroplast proteins [SEP] Chloroplast proteins is proteins encoded by the chloroplast genome or proteins encoded by the nuclear genome that are imported to and resident in the choroplasts.

name: cho cells
query: Query: cho cells [SEP] Cho cells is cell line derived from the ovary of the Chinese hamster, Cricetulus griseus (cricetulus). The species is a favorite for cytogenetic studies because of its small chromosome number. The cell line has provided model systems for the study of genetic alterations in cultured mammalian cells.

name: cholera toxin
query: Query: cholera toxin [SEP] Cholera toxin is an enterotoxin from vibrio cholerae. It consists of two major protomers, the heavy (h) or a subunit and the b protomer which consists of 5 light (l) or b subunits. The catalytic a subunit is proteolytically cleaved into fragments a1 and a2. The a1 fragment is a mono(adp-ribose) transferase. The b protomer binds cholera toxin to intestinal epithelial cells, and facilitates the uptake of the a1 fragment. The a1 catalyzed transfer of adp-ribose to the alpha subunits of heterotrimeric g proteins activates the production of cyclic amp. Increased levels of cyclic amp are thought to modulate release of fluid and electrolytes from intestinal crypt cells.

name: cholera vaccines
query: Query: cholera vaccines [SEP] Cholera vaccines is vaccines or candidate vaccines used to prevent infection with vibrio cholerae. The original cholera vaccine consisted of killed bacteria, but other kinds of vaccines now exist.

name: cholesterol , dietary
query: Query: cholesterol , dietary [SEP] Dietary cholesterol is cholesterol present in food, especially in animal products.

name: cholesterol , ldl
query: Query: cholesterol , ldl [SEP] Ldl cholesterol is cholesterol which is contained in or bound to low density lipoproteins (ldl), including cholesterol esters and free cholesterol.

name: cholesterol esters
query: Query: cholesterol esters [SEP] Cholesterol esters is fatty acid esters of cholesterol which constitute about two-thirds of the cholesterol in the plasma. The accumulation of cholesterol esters in the arterial intima is a characteristic feature of atherosclerosis.

name: cholesterol ester storage disease
query: Query: cholesterol ester storage disease [SEP] Cholesterol ester storage disease is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutations in the gene for acid lipase (sterol esterase). It is characterized by the accumulation of neutral lipids, particularly cholesterol esters in leukocytes, fibroblasts, and [MASK].

name: cholinergic agonists
query: Query: cholinergic agonists [SEP] Cholinergic agonists is drugs that bind to and activate cholinergic receptors.

name: cholinergic antagonists
query: Query: cholinergic antagonists [SEP] Cholinergic antagonists is drugs that bind to but do not activate cholinergic receptors, thereby blocking the actions of acetylcholine or cholinergic agonists.

name: cholinergic fibers
query: Query: cholinergic fibers [SEP] Cholinergic fibers is nerve fibers liberating acetylcholine at the synapse after an impulse.

name: chondrocytes
query: Query: chondrocytes [SEP] Chondrocytes is polymorphic cells that form cartilage.

name: chromatin
query: Query: chromatin [SEP] Chromatin is the material of chromosomes. It is a complex of dna; histones; and nonhistone proteins (chromosomal proteins, non-histone) found within the nucleus of a cell.

name: chromatography , agarose
query: Query: chromatography , agarose [SEP] Agarose chromatography is a method of gel filtration chromatography using agarose, the non-ionic component of agar, for the separation of compounds with molecular weights up to several million.

name: chromatography , high pressure liquid
query: Query: chromatography , high pressure liquid [SEP] High pressure liquid chromatography is liquid chromatographic techniques which feature high inlet pressures, high sensitivity, and high speed.

name: chromatography , thin layer
query: Query: chromatography , thin layer [SEP] Thin layer chromatography is chromatography on thin layers of adsorbents rather than in columns. The adsorbent can be [MASK], [MASK], silicates, charcoals, or cellulose. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

name: chromium alloys
query: Query: chromium alloys [SEP] Chromium alloys is specific alloys not less than 85% chromium and nickel or cobalt, with traces of either nickel or cobalt, molybdenum, and other substances. They are used in partial dentures, orthopedic implants, etc.

name: chromium isotopes
query: Query: chromium isotopes [SEP] Chromium isotopes is stable chromium atoms that have the same atomic number as the element chromium, but differ in atomic weight. Cr-50, 53, and 54 are stable chromium isotopes.

name: chromosomal instability
query: Query: chromosomal instability [SEP] Chromosomal instability is an increased tendency to acquire chromosome aberrations when various processes involved in chromosome replication, repair, or segregation are dysfunctional.

name: chromosome deletion
query: Query: chromosome deletion [SEP] Chromosome deletion is actual loss of portion of a chromosome.

name: chromosome duplication
query: Query: chromosome duplication [SEP] Chromosome duplication is an aberration in which an extra chromosome or a chromosomal segment is made.

name: chromosome fragile sites
query: Query: chromosome fragile sites [SEP] Chromosome fragile sites is specific loci that show up during karyotyping as a gap (an uncondensed stretch in closer views) on a chromatid [MASK] after culturing cells under specific conditions. These sites are associated with an increase in chromosome fragility. They are classified as common or rare, and by the specific culture conditions under which they develop. Fragile site loci are named by the letters "fra" followed by a designation for the specific chromosome, and a letter which refers to which fragile site of that chromosome (e.g. fraxa refers to fragile site a on the x chromosome. It is a rare, folic acid-sensitive fragile site associated with fragile x syndrome.)

name: chromosome inversion
query: Query: chromosome inversion [SEP] Chromosome inversion is an aberration in which a chromosomal segment is deleted and reinserted in the same place but turned 180 degrees from its original orientation, so that the gene sequence for the segment is reversed with respect to that of the rest of the chromosome.

name: chromosome painting
query: Query: chromosome painting [SEP] Chromosome painting is a technique for visualizing chromosome aberrations using fluorescently labeled dna probes which are hybridized to chromosomal dna. Multiple fluorochromes may be attached to the probes. Upon hybridization, this produces a multicolored, or painted, effect with a unique [MASK] at each site of hybridization. This technique may also be used to identify cross-species homology by labeling probes from one species for hybridization with chromosomes from another species.

name: chromosomes , artificial , bacterial
query: Query: chromosomes , artificial , bacterial [SEP] Bacterial artificial chromosomes is dna constructs that are composed of, at least, a replication origin, for successful replication, propagation to and maintenance as an extra chromosome in bacteria. In addition, they can carry large amounts (about 200 kilobases) of other sequence for a variety of bioengineering purposes.

name: chromosomes , artificial , human
query: Query: chromosomes , artificial , human [SEP] Human artificial chromosomes is dna constructs that are composed of, at least, all elements, such as a replication origin; telomere; and centromere, required for successful replication, propagation to and maintainance in progeny human cells. In addition, they are constructed to carry other sequences for analysis or gene transfer.

name: chromosomes , artificial , yeast
query: Query: chromosomes , artificial , yeast [SEP] Yeast artificial chromosomes is chromosomes in which fragments of exogenous dna ranging in length up to several hundred kilobase pairs have been cloned into yeast through [MASK] to vector sequences. These artificial chromosomes are used extensively in molecular biology for the construction of comprehensive genomic libraries of higher organisms.

name: chromosomes , human , pair 3
query: Query: chromosomes , human , pair 3 [SEP] Pair 3 human chromosomes is a specific pair of human chromosomes in group a (chromosomes, human, 1-3) of the human chromosome classification.

name: chromosomes , insect
query: Query: chromosomes , insect [SEP] Insect chromosomes is structures within the cell nucleus of insect cells containing dna.

name: chromosomes , plant
query: Query: chromosomes , plant [SEP] Plant chromosomes is complex nucleoprotein structures which contain the genomic dna and are part of the cell nucleus of plants.

name: chromosome segregation
query: Query: chromosome segregation [SEP] Chromosome segregation is the orderly segregation of chromosomes during meiosis or [MASK].

name: chromosome walking
query: Query: chromosome walking [SEP] Chromosome walking is a technique with which an unknown region of a chromosome can be explored. It is generally used to isolate a locus of interest for which no probe is available but that is known to be linked to a gene which has been identified and cloned. a fragment containing a known gene is selected and used as a probe to identify other overlapping fragments which contain the same gene. The nucleotide sequences of these fragments can then be characterized. This process continues for the length of the chromosome.

name: chronic disease indicators
query: Query: chronic disease indicators [SEP] Chronic disease indicators is a [MASK] of surveillance indicators of disease developed by [MASK] among the cdc, the Council of State and Territorial Epidemiologists, and the National Association of Chronic Disease Directors. It enables public health professionals and policymakers to retrieve uniformly defined state and selected metropolitan-level data for chronic diseases and risk factors that impact public health.(https://www.cdc.gov/socialdeterminants/data/index.htm)

name: chronic pain
query: Query: chronic pain [SEP] Chronic pain is aching sensation that persists for more than a few months. It may or may not be associated with trauma or disease, and may persist after the initial injury has healed. Its localization, [MASK], and timing are more vague than with acute pain.

name: chronic traumatic encephalopathy
query: Query: chronic traumatic encephalopathy [SEP] Chronic traumatic encephalopathy is degenerative brain disease linked to repetitive brain trauma. Progressive symptoms may include memory loss; aggression; or depression.

name: cigarette smoking
query: Query: cigarette smoking [SEP] [MASK] smoking is the smoking of [MASK].

name: ciliary arteries
query: Query: ciliary arteries [SEP] Ciliary arteries is three groups of arteries found in the eye which supply the iris, pupil, sclera, conjunctiva, and the muscles of the iris.

name: ciliary neurotrophic factor
query: Query: ciliary neurotrophic factor [SEP] Ciliary neurotrophic factor is a neurotrophic factor that promotes the survival of various neuronal cell types and may play an important role in the injury response in the nervous system.

name: ciliary neurotrophic factor receptor alpha subunit
query: Query: ciliary neurotrophic factor receptor alpha subunit [SEP] Ciliary neurotrophic factor receptor alpha subunit is a ciliary neurotrophic factor receptor subunit. It is anchored to the cell surface via glycosylphosphatidylinositol linkage and has specificity for binding to ciliary neurotrophic factor. It lacks signal transducing domains which are found on the other two subunits of the receptor.

name: circadian clocks
query: Query: circadian clocks [SEP] Circadian clocks is biological mechanism that controls circadian rhythm. Circadian clocks exist in the simplest form in cyanobacteria and as more complex systems in fungi, plants, and animals. In humans the system includes photoresponsive [MASK] and the suprachiasmatic nucleus that acts as the central oscillator.

name: circadian rhythm
query: Query: circadian rhythm [SEP] Circadian rhythm is the regular recurrence, in cycles of about 24 hours, of biological processes or activities, such as sensitivity to drugs or environmental and physiological stimuli.

name: circulating tumor dna
query: Query: circulating tumor dna [SEP] Circulating tumor dna is dna released from tumor cells that is found circulating in plasma; serum; or other body fluids.

name: circulatory arrest , deep hypothermia induced
query: Query: circulatory arrest , deep hypothermia induced [SEP] Deep hypothermia induced circulatory arrest is a technique to arrest the flow of blood by lowering body temperature to about 20 degrees Centigrade, usually achieved by infusing chilled perfusate. The technique provides a bloodless surgical field for complex surgeries.

name: cisplatin
query: Query: cisplatin [SEP] Cisplatin is an inorganic and water-soluble [MASK] complex. After undergoing hydrolysis, it reacts with dna to produce both intra and interstrand crosslinks. These crosslinks appear to impair replication and transcription of dna. The cytotoxicity of cisplatin correlates with cellular arrest in the g2 phase of the cell cycle.

name: city planning
query: Query: city planning [SEP] City planning is comprehensive planning for the physical development of the city.

name: civil defense
query: Query: civil defense [SEP] Civil defense is preventive emergency measures and programs designed to protect the individual or community in times of hostile attack.

name: civil disorders
query: Query: civil disorders [SEP] Civil disorders is deliberate and planned acts of unlawful behavior engaged in by aggrieved segments of the population in seeking social change.

name: classical swine fever
query: Query: classical swine fever [SEP] Classical swine fever is an acute, highly contagious disease affecting swine of all ages and caused by the classical swine fever virus. It has a sudden onset with high morbidity and mortality.

name: clay
query: Query: clay [SEP] Clay is a naturally-occurring rock or soil constituent characterized by particles with a diameter of less than 0.005 mm. It is composed primarily of hydrous aluminum silicates, trace amounts of metal oxides, and organic matter.

name: cleft lip
query: Query: cleft lip [SEP] Cleft [MASK] is congenital defect in the upper [MASK] where the maxillary prominence fails to merge with the merged medial nasal prominences. It is thought to be caused by faulty migration of the mesoderm in the head region.

name: cleft palate
query: Query: cleft palate [SEP] Cleft palate is congenital fissure of the soft and/or [MASK], due to faulty fusion.

name: clinical attribute
query: Query: clinical attribute [SEP] Clinical attribute is clinical characteristics of disease or illness.

name: clinical coding
query: Query: clinical coding [SEP] Clinical coding is process of substituting a symbol or code for a term such as a diagnosis or procedure. (from Slee's Health Care Terms, 3d ed.)

name: clinical competence
query: Query: clinical competence [SEP] Clinical competence is the capability to perform acceptably those duties directly related to patient care.

name: clinical conference
query: Query: clinical conference [SEP] Clinical conference is work that consists of a conference of physicians on their observations of a patient at the bedside, regarding the physical state, laboratory and other diagnostic findings, clinical manifestations, results of current therapy, etc. a clinical conference usually ends with a confirmation or correction of clinical findings by a pathological diagnosis performed by a pathologist. "Clinical conference" is often referred to as a "clinico-pathological conference."

name: clinical decision rules
query: Query: clinical decision rules [SEP] Clinical decision rules is scores or algorithms that correlate with clinically significant findings and that are used to predict an outcome, or suggest a diagnostic or therapeutic action.

name: clinical deterioration
query: Query: clinical deterioration [SEP] Clinical deterioration is a critical disease progression, often measured by a [MASK] of clinical parameters, which activates hospital rapid response team.

name: clinical drug
query: Query: clinical drug [SEP] Clinical drug is a field of medicine that deals primarily with the practice and study of medicine based on the direct examination of the patient.

name: clinical enzyme tests
query: Query: clinical enzyme tests [SEP] Clinical enzyme tests is analyses for a specific enzyme activity, or of the level of a specific enzyme that is used to assess health and disease risk, for early detection of disease or disease prediction, diagnosis, and change in disease status.

name: clinical governance
query: Query: clinical governance [SEP] Clinical governance is a framework through which the United Kingdom's National Health Service organizations are accountable for continually improving the quality of their services and safeguarding high standards of care by creating an environment in which excellence in clinical care will flourish. (Scally and Donaldson, bmj (4 July 1998): 61-65)

name: clinical laboratory information systems
query: Query: clinical laboratory information systems [SEP] Clinical laboratory information systems is information systems, usually computer-assisted, designed to store, manipulate, and retrieve information for planning, organizing, directing, and controlling administrative and clinical activities associated with the provision and utilization of clinical laboratory services.

name: clinical laboratory services
query: Query: clinical laboratory services [SEP] Clinical laboratory services is organized services provided by medical laboratory personnel for the purpose of carrying out clinical laboratory techniques used for the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of disease.

name: clinical nursing research
query: Query: clinical nursing research [SEP] Clinical nursing research is research carried out by nurses in the clinical setting and designed to provide information that will help improve patient care. Other professional staff may also participate in the research.

name: clinical pharmacy information systems
query: Query: clinical pharmacy information systems [SEP] Clinical pharmacy information systems is information systems, usually computer-assisted, designed to store, manipulate, and retrieve information for planning, organizing, directing, and controlling administrative activities associated with the provision and utilization of [MASK].

name: clinical trial , phase i
query: Query: clinical trial , phase i [SEP] [MASK] is work that is the report of a pre-planned, usually controlled, clinical study of the safety and efficacy of diagnostic, therapeutic, or prophylactic drugs, devices, or techniques based on a small number of healthy persons and conducted over the period of about a year in either the United States or a foreign country.

name: clinical trial , phase ii
query: Query: clinical trial , phase ii [SEP] Phase ii clinical trial is work that is a report of a pre-planned, usually controlled, clinical study of the safety and efficacy of diagnostic, therapeutic, or prophylactic drugs, devices, or techniques based on several hundred volunteers, including a limited number of patients, and conducted over a period of about two years in either the United States or a foreign country.

name: clinical trial , phase iv
query: Query: clinical trial , phase iv [SEP] Phase iv clinical trial is work that is a report of a planned post-marketing study of diagnostic, therapeutic, or prophylactic drugs, devices, or techniques that have been approved for general sale after clinical trials, phases i, ii, and iii. These studies, conducted in the United States or a foreign country, often garner additional data about the safety and efficacy of a product.

name: clinical trial protocol
query: Query: clinical trial protocol [SEP] Clinical trial protocol is the written description of a clinical study. It contains the study's objectives, design, and methods including subject target and/or enrollment criteria. It may also present relevant scientific background and statistical information.

name: clinical trial protocols as topic
query: Query: clinical trial protocols as topic [SEP] Clinical trial protocols as topic is works about the written descriptions of a clinical study. It contains the study's objectives, design, and methods including subject target and/or enrollment criteria. It may also present relevant scientific background and statistical information.

name: clinical trials , phase ii as topic
query: Query: clinical trials , phase ii as topic [SEP] Phase ii as topic clinical trials is works about studies that are usually controlled to assess the effectiveness and dosage (if appropriate) of diagnostic, therapeutic, or prophylactic drugs, devices, or techniques. These studies are performed on several hundred volunteers, including a limited number of patients with the target disease or disorder, and last about two years. This concept includes phase ii studies conducted in both the u.s. and in other countries.

name: clinical trials , phase iii as topic
query: Query: clinical trials , phase iii as topic [SEP] Phase iii as topic clinical trials is works about comparative studies to verify the effectiveness of diagnostic, therapeutic, or prophylactic drugs, devices, or techniques determined in phase ii studies. During these trials, patients are monitored closely by physicians to identify any adverse reactions from long-term use. These studies are performed on groups of patients large enough to identify clinically significant responses and usually last about three years. This concept includes phase iii studies conducted in both the u.s. and in other countries.

name: clinical trials , phase iv as topic
query: Query: clinical trials , phase iv as topic [SEP] Phase iv as topic clinical trials is works about planned post-marketing studies of diagnostic, therapeutic, or prophylactic drugs, devices, or techniques that have been approved for general sale. These studies are often conducted to obtain additional data about the safety and efficacy of a product. This concept includes phase iv studies conducted in both the u.s. and in other countries.

name: clinical trials data monitoring committees
query: Query: clinical trials data monitoring committees [SEP] Clinical trials data monitoring committees is committees established to review interim data and efficacy outcomes in clinical trials. The findings of these committees are used in deciding whether a trial should be continued as designed, changed, or terminated. Government regulations regarding federally-funded research involving human subjects (the "Common Rule") require (45 cfr 46.111) that research ethics committees reviewing large-scale clinical trials monitor the data collected using a mechanism such as a data monitoring committee. fda regulations (21 cfr 50.24) require that such committees be established to monitor studies conducted in emergency settings.

name: clock proteins
query: Query: clock proteins [SEP] Clock proteins is basic helix-loop-helix (bHLH) domain-containing proteins that contain intrinsic histone acetyltransferase activity and play important roles in circadian rhythm regulation. Clock proteins combine with Arntl proteins to form heterodimeric transcription factors that are specific for e-box elements and stimulate the transcription of several E-box genes that are involved in cyclical regulation. This [MASK] also sets into motion a time-dependent [MASK] loop which in turn down-regulates the expression of clock proteins.

name: clonal deletion
query: Query: clonal deletion [SEP] Clonal deletion is removal, via cell death, of immature lymphocytes that interact with antigens during maturation. For T-lymphocytes this occurs in the thymus and ensures that mature T-lymphocytes are self tolerant. B-lymphocytes may also undergo clonal deletion.

name: clonal evolution
query: Query: clonal evolution [SEP] Clonal evolution is the process of accumulation of genetic and epigenetic changes over time in individual cells and the effect of the changes on cell proliferation.

name: clone cells
query: Query: clone cells [SEP] Clone cells is a group of genetically identical cells all descended from a single common ancestral cell by [MASK] in eukaryotes or by binary fission in prokaryotes. Clone cells also include populations of [MASK] molecules all carrying the same inserted sequence. (From King & Stansfield, Dictionary of Genetics, 4th ed)

name: cloning , organism
query: Query: cloning , organism [SEP] Organism cloning is the formation of one or more genetically identical organisms derived by vegetative reproduction from a single cell. The source nuclear material can be embryo-derived, fetus-derived, or taken from an adult somatic cell.

name: closed fracture reduction
query: Query: closed fracture reduction [SEP] [MASK] reduction is a procedure in which normal alignment of a fractured bone is restored by orthopedic manipulation without incision.

name: closing volume
query: Query: closing volume [SEP] Closing volume is the lung volume at which the dependent lung zones cease to ventilate presumably as a result of airway closure.

name: cloud computing
query: Query: cloud computing [SEP] Cloud computing is storing and processing data on multiple servers that can be accessed through the Internet.

name: coal
query: Query: coal [SEP] Coal is a natural fuel formed by partial decomposition of vegetable matter under certain environmental conditions.

name: coal ash
query: Query: coal ash [SEP] Coal ash is residue generated from combustion of coal or petroleum.

name: coal industry
query: Query: coal industry [SEP] Coal industry is enterprise associated with the mining, processing, marketing and distribution of coal.

name: coal mining
query: Query: coal mining [SEP] Coal mining is the practice of extracting coal from the earth.

name: coated vesicles
query: Query: coated vesicles [SEP] Coated vesicles is vesicles formed when cell-membrane coated pits (coated pits, cell-membrane) invaginate and pinch off.
