The outer surface of these vesicles are covered with a lattice-like network of coat proteins, such as clathrin, coat protein complex proteins, or caveolins.

name: coat protein complex i
query: Query: coat protein complex i [SEP] Coat protein complex i is a protein complex comprised of coatomer protein and adp ribosylation factor 1. It is involved in transport of vesicles between the endoplasmic reticulum and the golgi apparatus.

name: cobalt isotopes
query: Query: cobalt isotopes [SEP] Cobalt isotopes is stable cobalt atoms that have the same atomic number as the element cobalt, but differ in atomic weight. Co-59 is a stable cobalt isotope.

name: cochlear implantation
query: Query: cochlear implantation [SEP] Cochlear implantation is surgical insertion of an electronic hearing device ([MASK]) with electrodes to the cochlear nerve in the [MASK] to create sound sensation in patients with residual nerve fibers.

name: cod liver oil
query: Query: cod liver oil [SEP] Cod liver oil is oil obtained from fresh livers of the cod family, Gadidae. It is a source of vitamin a and vitamin d.

name: codon , initiator
query: Query: codon , initiator [SEP] Initiator codon is a codon that directs initiation of protein translation (translation, genetic) by stimulating the binding of initiator tRNA (rna, transfer, met). In prokaryotes, the codons aug or gug can act as initiators while in eukaryotes, aug is the only initiator codon.

name: coffee
query: Query: coffee [SEP] Coffee is a beverage made from ground coffea beans ([MASK]) infused in hot water. It generally contains caffeine and theophylline unless it is decaffeinated.

name: cognitive neuroscience
query: Query: cognitive neuroscience [SEP] Cognitive neuroscience is field of study concerning mental processes; learning; and the brain regions associated with them.

name: cognitive reserve
query: Query: cognitive reserve [SEP] Cognitive reserve is capacity that enables an individual to cope with and/or recover from the impact of a neural injury or a psychotic episode.

name: cold climate
query: Query: cold climate [SEP] Cold climate is a climate characterized by cold temperature for a majority of the time during the year.

name: cold injury
query: Query: cold injury [SEP] Cold injury is a physical injury caused by exposure of the body to extremely low ambient temperatures that may lead to loss of [MASK], or in extreme cases, death. Examples of cold injury are frostbite and chilblains.

name: cold ischemia
query: Query: cold ischemia [SEP] Cold ischemia is the chilling of a tissue or organ during decreased blood perfusion or in the absence of blood supply. Cold ischemia time during organ transplantation begins when the organ is cooled with a cold perfusion solution after organ procurement surgery, and ends after the tissue reaches physiological temperature during implantation procedures.

name: colitis , ischemic
query: Query: colitis , ischemic [SEP] Ischemic colitis is inflammation of the colon due to colonic ischemia resulting from alterations in systemic circulation or local vasculature.

name: colitis , lymphocytic
query: Query: colitis , lymphocytic [SEP] Lymphocytic colitis is a subtype of microscopic colitis, characterized by chronic watery [MASK] of unknown origin, a normal colonoscopy but abnormal histopathology on biopsy. Microscopic examination of biopsy samples taken from the colon show infiltration of lymphocytes in the superficial epithelium and the underlying connective tissue (lamina propria).

name: colitis , ulcerative
query: Query: colitis , ulcerative [SEP] Ulcerative colitis is inflammation of the colon that is predominantly confined to the mucosa. Its major symptoms include [MASK], rectal bleeding, the passage of mucus, and abdominal pain.

name: collagen
query: Query: collagen [SEP] Collagen is a polypeptide substance comprising about one third of the total protein in mammalian organisms. It is the main constituent of skin; connective tissue; and the organic substance of bones (bone and bones) and teeth (tooth).

name: collapse therapy
query: Query: collapse therapy [SEP] Collapse therapy is surgical treatment of pulmonary tuberculosis whereby the lung is totally or partially, temporarily or permanently, immobilized. The procedure was based on the popular concept that collapsing the affected portion of a tuberculous lung allowed the infected area to rest and thereby recover. At the beginning of the 20th century artificially induced pneumothorax (pneumothorax, artificial) was popular. Later a variety of other techniques was used to encourage collapse of the infected portion of the lung: unilateral phrenic nerve division, pneumonolysis, pneumoperitoneum (pneumoperitoneum, artificial), and thoracoplasty. Collapse therapy has declined since the advent of antitubercular chemotherapy. (Stedman, 25th ed; from Sabiston Jr, Textbook of Surgery, 14th ed, p1733-4)

name: collected correspondence
query: Query: collected correspondence [SEP] Collected correspondence is written communication between persons or between institutions or organizations.

name: collection
query: Query: collection [SEP] Collection is items gathered and assembled in some order to facilitate access or use.

name: collections as topic
query: Query: collections as topic [SEP] Collections as topic is works about items gathered and assembled in some order to facilitate access or use.

name: collective bargaining
query: Query: collective bargaining [SEP] Collective bargaining is the process of negotiation between representatives of an employee organization, association or union, and representatives of the employer.

name: colon , ascending
query: Query: colon , ascending [SEP] Ascending colon is the segment of large intestine between the cecum and the transverse colon. It passes cephalad from the cecum to the caudal surface of the right lobe of the liver where it bends sharply to the left, forming the right colic flexure.

name: colon , sigmoid
query: Query: colon , sigmoid [SEP] Sigmoid colon is a segment of the colon between the rectum and the [MASK].

name: colon , transverse
query: Query: colon , transverse [SEP] Transverse colon is the segment of large intestine between ascending colon and [MASK]. It passes from the right colic flexure across the abdomen, then turns sharply at the left colonic flexure into the [MASK].

name: colonic polyps
query: Query: colonic polyps [SEP] Colonic polyps is discrete tissue masses that protrude into the lumen of the colon. These polyps are connected to the wall of the colon either by a stalk, pedunculus, or by a broad base.

name: color perception
query: Query: color perception [SEP] [MASK] perception is mental processing of chromatic signals ([MASK] vision) from the eye by the visual cortex where they are converted into symbolic representations. [MASK] perception involves numerous neurons, and is influenced not only by the distribution of wavelengths from the viewed object, but also by its background [MASK] and brightness contrast at its boundary.

name: color perception tests
query: Query: color perception tests [SEP] [MASK] perception tests is type of vision test used to determine [MASK] vision defects.

name: color therapy
query: Query: color therapy [SEP] [MASK] therapy is a form of phototherapy using [MASK] to influence health and to treat various physical or mental disorders. The [MASK] rays may be in the visible or invisible spectrum and can be administered through colored lights or applied mentally through suggestion.

name: color vision
query: Query: color vision [SEP] [MASK] vision is function of the human eye that is used in bright [MASK] or in daylight (at photopic intensities). Photopic vision is performed by the three types of [MASK] with varied peak absorption wavelengths in the [MASK] spectrum (from violet to red, 400 - 700 nm).

name: color vision defects
query: Query: color vision defects [SEP] [MASK] vision defects is defects of [MASK] vision are mainly hereditary traits but can be secondary to acquired or developmental abnormalities in the [MASK]). Severity of hereditary defects of [MASK] vision depends on the degree of mutation of the rod opsins genes (on x chromosome and chromosome 3) that code the photopigments for red, green and blue.

name: combat disorders
query: Query: combat disorders [SEP] Combat disorders is neurotic reactions to unusual, severe, or overwhelming military stress.

name: comment
query: Query: comment [SEP] Comment is work consisting of a critical or explanatory note written to discuss, support, or dispute an article or other presentation previously published. It may take the form of an article, letter, [MASK], etc. It appears in publications under a variety of names: comment, commentary, [MASK] comment, viewpoint, etc.

name: commission on professional and hospital activities
query: Query: commission on professional and hospital activities [SEP] Commission on professional and hospital activities is the non-profit, non-governmental organization which collects, processes, and distributes data on hospital use. Two programs of the Commission are the Professional Activity Study and the Medical Audit Program.

name: commitment of mentally ill
query: Query: commitment of mentally ill [SEP] Commitment of [MASK] is legal process required for the institutionalization of a patient with severe mental problems.

name: committee membership
query: Query: committee membership [SEP] Committee membership is the composition of a committee; the state or status of being a member of a committee.

name: common cold
query: Query: common cold [SEP] Common cold is a catarrhal disorder of the upper respiratory tract, which may be viral or a mixed infection. It generally involves a runny nose, nasal congestion, and sneezing.

name: common data elements
query: Query: common data elements [SEP] Common data elements is data elements that are common to multiple data sets across different studies.

name: community dentistry
query: Query: community dentistry [SEP] Community dentistry is the practice of dentistry concerned with preventive as well as diagnostic and treatment programs in a circumscribed population.

name: community medicine
query: Query: community medicine [SEP] Community medicine is a branch of medicine concerned with the total health of the individual within the home environment and in the community, and with the application of comprehensive care to the prevention and treatment of illness in the entire community.

name: community mental health services
query: Query: community mental health services [SEP] Community mental health services is diagnostic, therapeutic and preventive mental health services provided for individuals in the community.

name: community pharmacy services
query: Query: community pharmacy services [SEP] Community pharmacy services is total pharmaceutical services provided to the public through community pharmacies.

name: comorbidity
query: Query: comorbidity [SEP] Comorbidity is the presence of co-existing or additional diseases with reference to an initial diagnosis or with reference to the index condition that is the subject of study. Comorbidity may affect the ability of affected individuals to function and also their survival; it may be used as a prognostic indicator for length of hospital stay, cost factors, and outcome or survival.

name: comparative effectiveness research
query: Query: comparative effectiveness research [SEP] Comparative effectiveness research is conduct and synthesis of systematic research comparing interventions and strategies to prevent, diagnose, treat, and monitor health conditions. The purpose of this research is to inform patients, providers, and decision-makers, responding to their expressed needs, about which interventions are most effective for which patients under specific circumstances. (hhs.gov/recovery/programs/cer/draftdefinition.html accessed 6/12/2009)

name: comparative study
query: Query: comparative study [SEP] Comparative study is comparison of outcomes, results, responses, etc for different techniques, therapeutic approaches or other inputs.

name: competitive bidding
query: Query: competitive bidding [SEP] Competitive bidding is pricing statements presented by more than one party for the purpose of securing a contract.

name: competitive medical plans
query: Query: competitive medical plans [SEP] Competitive medical plans is alternative health care delivery mechanisms, such as preferred provider organizations or other health insurance services or prepaid plans (other than health maintenance organizations), that meet Medicare qualifications for a risk-sharing contract. (From Facts on File Dictionary of Health Care Management, 1988)

name: complement factor b
query: Query: complement factor b [SEP] Complement factor b is a glycine-rich, heat-labile serum glycoprotein that contains a component of the c3 convertase alternate pathway (C3bBb). Bb, a serine protease, is generated when factor b is cleaved by complement factor d into Ba and Bb.

name: complement factor d
query: Query: complement factor d [SEP] Complement factor d is a serum protein which is important in the alternative complement activation pathway. This enzyme cleaves the complement C3B-bound complement factor b to form C3bBb which is alternative pathway c3 convertase.

name: complement membrane attack complex
query: Query: complement membrane attack complex [SEP] Complement membrane attack complex is a product of complement activation cascade, regardless of the pathways, that forms transmembrane channels causing disruption of the target cell membrane and cell lysis. It is formed by the sequential assembly of terminal complement components (complement c5b; complement c6; complement c7; complement c8; and complement c9) into the target membrane. The resultant C5b-8-poly-C9 is the "membrane attack complex" or mac.

name: complement pathway , alternative
query: Query: complement pathway , alternative [SEP] Alternative complement pathway is complement activation initiated by the interaction of microbial antigens with complement c3b. When complement factor b binds to the membrane-bound C3b, complement factor d cleaves it to form alternative c3 convertase (c3bbb) which, stabilized by complement factor p, is able to cleave multiple complement c3 to form alternative c5 convertase (c3bbb3b) leading to cleavage of complement c5 and the assembly of complement membrane attack complex.

name: compliance
query: Query: compliance [SEP] Compliance is distensibility measure of a chamber such as the lungs (lung compliance) or [MASK]. Compliance is expressed as a change in volume per unit change in pressure.

name: composite lymphoma
query: Query: composite lymphoma [SEP] Composite lymphoma is two or more distinct types of malignant lymphoid tumors occurring within a single organ or tissue at the same time. It may contain different types of non-Hodgkin lymphoma cells or both Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma cells.

name: comprehension
query: Query: comprehension [SEP] Comprehension is the act or fact of grasping the meaning, nature, or importance of; understanding. (American Heritage Dictionary, 4th ed) Includes understanding by a patient or research subject of information disclosed orally or in writing.

name: compressed air
query: Query: compressed air [SEP] Compressed air is air that is reduced in volume by pressure.

name: computed tomography angiography
query: Query: computed tomography angiography [SEP] Computed tomography angiography is a non-invasive method that uses a ct scanner for capturing images of blood vessels and tissues. a contrast material is injected, which helps produce detailed images that aid in diagnosing vascular diseases.

name: computers , analog
query: Query: computers , analog [SEP] Analog computers is computers in which quantities are represented by physical variables; problem parameters are translated into equivalent mechanical or electrical circuits as an analog for the physical phenomenon being investigated. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

name: computers , hybrid
query: Query: computers , hybrid [SEP] Hybrid computers is computers that combine the functions of analog and digital computers. (Sippl, Computer Dictionary, 4th ed)

name: computer user training
query: Query: computer user training [SEP] Computer user training is process of teaching a person to interact and communicate with a computer.

name: concept formation
query: Query: concept formation [SEP] Concept formation is a cognitive process involving the formation of ideas generalized from the knowledge of qualities, aspects, and relations of objects.

name: concurrent review
query: Query: concurrent review [SEP] Concurrent review is review of the medical necessity of hospital or other health facility admissions, upon or within a short time following an admission, and periodic review of services provided during the course of treatment.

name: conditioning , classical
query: Query: conditioning , classical [SEP] Classical conditioning is learning that takes place when a conditioned stimulus is paired with an unconditioned stimulus.

name: confidence intervals
query: Query: confidence intervals [SEP] Confidence intervals is a range of values for a variable of interest, e.g., a rate, constructed so that this range has a specified probability of including the true value of the variable.

name: confined spaces
query: Query: confined spaces [SEP] Confined spaces is a space which has limited openings for entry and exit combined with unfavorable natural ventilation such as caves, refrigerators, deep tunnels, pipelines, sewers, silos, tanks, vats, mines, deep trenches or pits, vaults, manholes, chimneys, etc.

name: conflict of interest
query: Query: conflict of interest [SEP] [MASK] of interest is a situation in which an individual might benefit personally from official or professional actions. It includes a [MASK] between a person's private interests and official responsibilities in a position of trust. The term is not restricted to government officials. The concept refers both to actual [MASK] of interest and the appearance or perception of [MASK].

name: congenital abnormality
query: Query: congenital abnormality [SEP] Congenital abnormality is malformations of organs or [MASK] during development in utero.

name: congenital hypothyroidism
query: Query: congenital hypothyroidism [SEP] Congenital hypothyroidism is a condition in infancy or early childhood due to an in-utero deficiency of thyroid hormones that can be caused by genetic or environmental factors, such as thyroid dysgenesis or hypothyroidism in infants of mothers treated with thiouracil during pregnancy. Endemic cretinism is the result of iodine deficiency. Clinical symptoms include severe mental retardation, impaired skeletal development, short stature, and myxedema.

name: consciousness
query: Query: consciousness [SEP] Consciousness is sense of awareness of self and of the environment.

name: consciousness monitors
query: Query: consciousness monitors [SEP] Consciousness monitors is devices used to assess the level of consciousness especially during anesthesia. They measure brain activity level based on the eeg.

name: conscious sedation
query: Query: conscious sedation [SEP] Conscious sedation is a drug-induced depression of consciousness during which patients respond purposefully to verbal commands, either alone or accompanied by light tactile stimulation. No interventions are required to maintain a patent airway. (From: American Society of Anesthesiologists Practice Guidelines)

name: consensus development conference , nih
query: Query: consensus development conference , nih [SEP] Nih [MASK] conference is official statements of the finding or recommendations expressing the outcome from a conference sponsored by nih.

name: consensus development conferences , nih as topic
query: Query: consensus development conferences , nih as topic [SEP] Nih as topic [MASK] conferences is articles on conferences sponsored by nih presenting summary statements representing the majority agreement of physicians, scientists, and other professionals convening for the purpose of reaching a [MASK] on a subject of interest. This heading is used for nih [MASK] conferences as a means of scientific communication. In indexing it is viewed as a type of review article and as a tag for any article appearing in any publication of the nih Office of Medical Applications of Research (omar).

name: consensus sequence
query: Query: consensus sequence [SEP] [MASK] sequence is a theoretical representative nucleotide or amino acid sequence in which each nucleotide or amino acid is the one which occurs most frequently at that site in the different sequences which occur in nature. The phrase also refers to an actual sequence which approximates the theoretical [MASK]. a known conserved sequence [MASK] is represented by a [MASK] sequence. Commonly observed supersecondary protein structures (amino acid motifs) are often formed by conserved sequences.

name: conservation of energy resources
query: Query: conservation of energy resources [SEP] Conservation of energy resources is planned management, use, and preservation of energy resources.

name: conservation of water resources
query: Query: conservation of water resources [SEP] Conservation of water resources is preservation and or management of water resources especially under conditions of scarce supply.

name: conservative treatment
query: Query: conservative treatment [SEP] Conservative treatment is therapeutic approaches that are limited, gradual, or well-established as opposed to radical methods.

name: constipation
query: Query: constipation [SEP] Constipation is infrequent or difficult evacuation of feces. These symptoms are associated with a variety of causes, including low dietary fiber intake, emotional or nervous disturbances, systemic and structural disorders, drug-induced aggravation, and infections.

name: constriction , pathologic
query: Query: constriction , pathologic [SEP] Pathologic constriction is the condition of an anatomical structure's being constricted beyond normal dimensions.

name: construction industry
query: Query: construction industry [SEP] Construction industry is the aggregate business enterprise of building.

name: consultants
query: Query: consultants [SEP] Consultants is individuals referred to for expert or professional advice or services.

name: consumer behavior
query: Query: consumer behavior [SEP] Consumer behavior is behavior associated with the procurement of goods, services, or experiences.

name: contact inhibition
query: Query: contact inhibition [SEP] Contact inhibition is arrest of cell locomotion or cell division when two cells come into contact.

name: contact lenses , hydrophilic
query: Query: contact lenses , hydrophilic [SEP] Hydrophilic contact lenses is soft, supple contact lenses made of plastic polymers which interact readily with water molecules. Many types are available, including continuous and extended-wear versions, which are gas-permeable and easily sterilized.

name: contact lens solutions
query: Query: contact lens solutions [SEP] Contact lens solutions is sterile solutions used to clean and disinfect contact lenses.

name: contingent negative variation
query: Query: contingent negative variation [SEP] Contingent negative variation is a negative shift of the cortical electrical potentials that increases over time. It is associated with an anticipated response to an expected stimulus and is an electrical event indicative of a state of readiness or expectancy.

name: continuous renal replacement therapy
query: Query: continuous renal replacement therapy [SEP] Continuous renal replacement therapy is procedures with continuous blood purification (e.g., dialysis, filtration or perfusion) via vascular access designed to mimic kidney function in kidney diseases (e.g., acute renal failure and poisoning).

name: contraception , barrier
query: Query: contraception , barrier [SEP] Barrier contraception is methods of contraception in which physical, chemical, or biological means are used to prevent the sperm from reaching the fertilizable ovum.

name: contraception behavior
query: Query: contraception behavior [SEP] Contraception behavior is behavior patterns of those practicing contraception.

name: contraceptive agents , female
query: Query: contraceptive agents , female [SEP] Female contraceptive agents is chemical substances or agents with contraceptive activity in females. Use for female contraceptive agents in general or for which there is no specific heading.

name: contraceptive agents , hormonal
query: Query: contraceptive agents , hormonal [SEP] Hormonal contraceptive agents is contraceptive agents that act on the endocrine system.

name: contraceptive effectiveness
query: Query: contraceptive effectiveness [SEP] Contraceptive effectiveness is the rate of success or failure of a method of contraception; contraceptive agents; or contraceptive devices.

name: contraceptive prevalence surveys
query: Query: contraceptive prevalence surveys [SEP] Contraceptive [MASK] surveys is collections of data, obtained from voluntary subjects, that measure the usage rate of methods of contraception; contraceptive devices; or contraceptive agents.

name: contrast media
query: Query: contrast media [SEP] Contrast media is substances used to allow enhanced visualization of tissues.

name: contrast sensitivity
query: Query: contrast sensitivity [SEP] Contrast sensitivity is the ability to detect sharp boundaries (stimuli) and to detect slight changes in luminance at regions without distinct contours. Psychophysical measurements of this visual function are used to evaluate visual acuity and to detect eye disease.

name: control groups
query: Query: control groups [SEP] Control groups is groups that serve as a standard for comparison in experimental studies. They are similar in relevant characteristics to the experimental group but do not receive the experimental intervention.

name: controlled substances
query: Query: controlled substances [SEP] Controlled substances is drugs or chemical agents whose manufacture, possession, or use are regulated by government. This may include narcotics and prescription medications.

name: convection
query: Query: convection [SEP] Convection is transmission of energy or mass by a medium involving movement of the medium itself. The circulatory movement that occurs in a fluid at a nonuniform temperature owing to the variation of its density and the action of gravity. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed; Webster, 10th ed)

name: conversion to open surgery
query: Query: conversion to open surgery [SEP] Conversion to open surgery is changing an operative procedure from an endoscopic surgical procedure to an open approach during the intraoperative period.

name: cooking
query: Query: cooking [SEP] Cooking is the art or practice of preparing food. It includes the preparation of special foods for diets in various diseases.

name: cooperative behavior
query: Query: cooperative behavior [SEP] Cooperative behavior is the interaction of two or more persons or organizations directed toward a common goal which is mutually beneficial. An act or instance of working or acting together for a common purpose or benefit, i.e., joint action. (From Random House Dictionary Unabridged, 2d ed)

name: coordination complexes
query: Query: coordination complexes [SEP] Coordination complexes is neutral or negatively charged ligands bonded to metal cations or neutral atoms. The number of ligand atoms to which the metal center is directly bonded is the metal cation's coordination number, and this number is always greater than the regular valence or oxidation number of the metal. a coordination complex can be negative, neutral, or positively charged.

name: copper transport proteins
query: Query: copper transport proteins [SEP] [MASK] transport proteins is membrane proteins that facilitate the transport of [MASK] cations across biological membranes.

name: cord factors
query: Query: cord factors [SEP] Cord factors is toxic glycolipids composed of trehalose dimycolate derivatives. They are produced by [MASK] and other species of mycobacterium. They induce cellular dysfunction in animals.

name: core binding factor alpha 1 subunit
query: Query: core binding factor alpha 1 subunit [SEP] Core binding factor alpha 1 subunit is a transcription factor that dimerizes with core binding factor beta subunit to form core binding factor. It contains a highly conserved DNA-binding domain known as the runt domain and is involved in genetic regulation of skeletal development and cell differentiation.

name: core binding factor beta subunit
query: Query: core binding factor beta subunit [SEP] Core binding factor beta subunit is a non-DNA binding transcription factor that is a subunit of core binding factor. It forms heterodimeric complexes with core binding factor alpha subunits, and regulates genetic transcription of a variety of genes involved primarily in cell differentiation and cell cycle progression.

name: corneal edema
query: Query: corneal edema [SEP] Corneal edema is an excessive amount of fluid in the cornea due to damage of the epithelium or endothelium causing decreased visual acuity.

name: corneal endothelial cell loss
query: Query: corneal endothelial cell loss [SEP] Corneal endothelial cell loss is loss of [MASK] usually following intraocular surgery (e.g., [MASK] surgery) or due to fuchs' endothelial dystrophy; angle-closure glaucoma; iritis; or aging.

name: corneal opacity
query: Query: corneal opacity [SEP] Corneal opacity is disorder occurring in the central or peripheral area of the cornea. The usual degree of transparency becomes relatively opaque.

name: corneal perforation
query: Query: corneal perforation [SEP] Corneal perforation is a puncture or hole through the corneal stroma resulting from various diseases or trauma.

name: corneal stroma
query: Query: corneal stroma [SEP] Corneal stroma is the lamellated connective tissue constituting the thickest layer of the cornea between the Bowman and Descemet membranes.

name: corneal transplantation
query: Query: corneal transplantation [SEP] Corneal transplantation is partial or total replacement of the cornea from one human or animal to another.

name: corneal ulcer
query: Query: corneal ulcer [SEP] Corneal [MASK] is loss of epithelial tissue from the surface of the cornea due to progressive erosion and necrosis of the tissue; usually caused by bacterial, fungal, or viral infection.

name: cornell medical index
query: Query: cornell medical index [SEP] Cornell medical index is self-administered health questionnaire developed to obtain details of the medical history as an adjunct to the medical interview. It consists of 195 questions divided into eighteen sections; the first twelve deal with somatic complaints and the last six with mood and feeling patterns. The Index is used also as a personality inventory or in epidemiologic studies.

name: corn oil
query: Query: corn oil [SEP] Corn oil is oil from zea mays or corn plant.

name: coronary aneurysm
query: Query: coronary aneurysm [SEP] Coronary aneurysm is abnormal balloon- or sac-like dilatation in the wall of coronary vessels. Most coronary aneurysms are due to coronary atherosclerosis, and the rest are due to inflammatory diseases, such as kawasaki disease.

name: coronary artery bypass
query: Query: coronary artery bypass [SEP] Coronary artery bypass is surgical therapy of ischemic coronary artery disease achieved by grafting a section of saphenous vein, internal mammary artery, or other substitute between the aorta and the obstructed coronary artery distal to the obstructive lesion.

name: coronary artery disease
query: Query: coronary artery disease [SEP] Coronary artery disease is pathological processes of coronary arteries that may derive from a congenital abnormality, atherosclerotic, or non-atherosclerotic cause.

name: coronary care units
query: Query: coronary care units [SEP] Coronary care units is the hospital unit in which patients with acute cardiac disorders receive intensive care.

name: coronary occlusion
query: Query: coronary occlusion [SEP] Coronary occlusion is complete blockage of blood flow through one of the coronary arteries, usually from coronary atherosclerosis.

name: coronary sinus
query: Query: coronary sinus [SEP] Coronary sinus is a short vein that collects about two thirds of the venous blood from the myocardium and drains into the right atrium. Coronary sinus, normally located between the left atrium and left ventricle on the posterior surface of the heart, can serve as an anatomical reference for cardiac procedures.

name: coronary stenosis
query: Query: coronary stenosis [SEP] Coronary stenosis is narrowing or constriction of a coronary artery.

name: coronary thrombosis
query: Query: coronary thrombosis [SEP] Coronary thrombosis is coagulation of blood in any of the coronary vessels. The presence of a blood clot (thrombus) often leads to myocardial infarction.

name: correlation of data
query: Query: correlation of data [SEP] Correlation of data is determination of whether or not two variables are correlated. This means to study whether an increase or decrease in one variable corresponds to an increase or decrease in the other variable.

name: corrosion
query: Query: corrosion [SEP] Corrosion is the gradual destruction of a metal or alloy due to oxidation or action of a chemical agent. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

name: corrosion casting
query: Query: corrosion casting [SEP] Corrosion casting is a tissue preparation technique that involves the injecting of plastic (acrylates) into blood vessels or other hollow viscera and treating the tissue with a caustic substance. This results in a negative copy or a solid replica of the enclosed space of the tissue that is ready for viewing under a scanning [MASK] microscope.

name: cortical bone
query: Query: cortical bone [SEP] Cortical bone is a type of osseous tissue which makes up the outer layer of bone. It is dense, rigid, strong, and forms concentric lamellar osteons.

name: cortical spreading depression
query: Query: cortical spreading depression [SEP] Cortical spreading depression is the decrease in neuronal activity (related to a decrease in metabolic demand) extending from the site of cortical stimulation. It is believed to be responsible for the decrease in [MASK] that accompanies the aura of [MASK] with aura. (Campbell's Psychiatric Dictionary, 8th ed.)

name: cosmic radiation
query: Query: cosmic radiation [SEP] Cosmic radiation is high-energy radiation or particles from extraterrestrial space that strike the earth, its atmosphere, or spacecraft and may create secondary radiation as a result of collisions with the atmosphere or spacecraft.

name: cost allocation
query: Query: cost allocation [SEP] Cost allocation is the assignment, to each of several particular cost-centers, of an equitable proportion of the costs of activities that serve all of them. Cost-center usually refers to institutional departments or services.

name: cost of illness
query: Query: cost of illness [SEP] Cost of illness is the personal cost of disease which may be economic, social, or psychological. The cost of illness may be reflected in absenteeism, productivity, response to treatment, peace of mind, or [MASK]. It differs from health care costs, the societal cost of providing services related to the delivery of health care.

name: cost savings
query: Query: cost savings [SEP] Cost savings is reductions in all or any portion of the costs of providing goods or services. Savings may be incurred by the provider or the consumer.

name: coup transcription factor i
query: Query: coup transcription factor i [SEP] Coup transcription factor i is a coup transcription factor that was originally identified as a homodimer that binds to a direct repeat regulatory element in the [MASK] albumin promoter. It is a transcription factor that plays an important role in embryonic development of the central nervous system.

name: coup transcription factor ii
query: Query: coup transcription factor ii [SEP] Coup transcription factor ii is a coup transcription factor that negatively regulates genetic transcription and competes with other hormone receptors for the common response element aggtca. It can also stimulate transcription of genes involved in the metabolism of glucose and cholesterol.

name: cpg islands
query: Query: cpg islands [SEP] Cpg islands is areas of increased density of the dinucleotide sequence cytosine--phosphate diester--guanine. They form stretches of dna several hundred to several thousand [MASK] long. In humans there are about 45,000 CpG islands, mostly found at the 5' ends of genes. They are unmethylated except for those on the inactive x chromosome and some associated with imprinted genes.

name: crack cocaine
query: Query: crack cocaine [SEP] Crack cocaine is the purified, alkaloidal, extra-potent form of cocaine. It is smoked (free-based), injected intravenously, and orally ingested. Use of crack results in alterations in function of the cardiovascular system, the autonomic nervous system, the central nervous system, and the gastrointestinal system. The slang term "crack" was derived from the crackling sound made upon igniting of this form of cocaine for smoking.

name: cranial fossa , anterior
query: Query: cranial fossa , anterior [SEP] Anterior cranial fossa is the compartment containing the inferior part and anterior extremities of the frontal lobes (frontal lobe) of the cerebral hemispheres. It is formed mainly by orbital parts of the [MASK] and the lesser wings of the sphenoid bone.

name: cranial fossa , middle
query: Query: cranial fossa , middle [SEP] Middle cranial fossa is the compartment containing the anterior extremities and half the inferior surface of the temporal lobes (temporal lobe) of the cerebral hemispheres. Lying posterior and inferior to the anterior cranial fossa (cranial fossa, anterior), it is formed by part of the [MASK] and sphenoid bone. It is separated from the posterior cranial fossa (cranial fossa, posterior) by crests formed by the superior borders of the petrous parts of the [MASK].

name: cranial fossa , posterior
query: Query: cranial fossa , posterior [SEP] Posterior cranial fossa is the infratentorial compartment that contains the cerebellum and brain stem. It is formed by the posterior third of the superior surface of the body of the sphenoid (sphenoid bone), by the occipital, the petrous, and mastoid portions of the [MASK], and the posterior inferior angle of the [MASK].

name: creatine
query: Query: creatine [SEP] Creatine is an amino acid that occurs in vertebrate tissues and in urine. In muscle tissue, creatine generally occurs as phosphocreatine. Creatine is excreted as creatinine in the urine.

name: creatine kinase , bb form
query: Query: creatine kinase , bb form [SEP] Bb form creatine kinase is a form of creatine kinase found in the brain.

name: creatine kinase , mb form
query: Query: creatine kinase , mb form [SEP] Mb form creatine kinase is an isoenzyme of creatine kinase found in the cardiac muscle.

name: creatine kinase , mitochondrial form
query: Query: creatine kinase , mitochondrial form [SEP] Mitochondrial form creatine kinase is a form of creatine kinase found in the mitochondria.

name: creatine kinase , mm form
query: Query: creatine kinase , mm form [SEP] Mm form creatine kinase is an isoenzyme of creatine kinase found in the muscle.

name: creativity
query: Query: creativity [SEP] Creativity is the ability to generate new ideas or images.

name: crisis intervention
query: Query: crisis intervention [SEP] Crisis intervention is brief therapeutic approach which is ameliorative rather than curative of acute psychiatric emergencies. Used in contexts such as emergency rooms of psychiatric or [MASK], or in the home or place of crisis occurrence, this treatment approach focuses on interpersonal and intrapsychic factors and environmental modification. (apa Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 7th ed)

name: critical care nursing
query: Query: critical care nursing [SEP] Critical care nursing is a nursing specialty that deals specifically with the care of patients who are [MASK].

name: critical period , psychological
query: Query: critical period , psychological [SEP] Psychological critical period is a specific stage in animal and human development during which certain types of behavior normally are shaped and molded for life.

name: crohn disease
query: Query: crohn disease [SEP] Crohn disease is a chronic transmural inflammation that may involve any part of the digestive tract from mouth to anus, mostly found in the ileum, the cecum, and the colon. In Crohn disease, the inflammation, extending through the intestinal wall from the mucosa to the serosa, is characteristically asymmetric and segmental. Epithelioid granulomas may be seen in some patients.

name: crop , avian
query: Query: crop , avian [SEP] Avian crop is a thin-walled distention of the alimentary tract protruding just outside the body cavity in the distal end of the [MASK] (esophagus), used for the temporary storage of food and water.

name: crop protection
query: Query: crop protection [SEP] Crop protection is the science and practice of preventing, minimizing, or eliminating damage to agricultural crops by pest organisms, weeds, and disease-causing agents.

name: cross infection
query: Query: cross infection [SEP] Cross infection is any infection which a patient contracts in a health-care institution.

name: crossing over , genetic
query: Query: crossing over , genetic [SEP] Genetic crossing over is the reciprocal exchange of segments at corresponding positions along pairs of homologous chromosomes by symmetrical breakage and crosswise rejoining forming cross-over sites (holliday junctions) that are resolved during chromosome segregation. Crossing-over typically occurs during meiosis but it may also occur in the absence of meiosis, for example, with bacterial chromosomes, organelle chromosomes, or somatic cell nuclear chromosomes.

name: cross protection
query: Query: cross protection [SEP] Cross protection is protection conferred on a host by inoculation with one strain or component of a microorganism that prevents infection when later challenged with a similar strain. Most commonly the microorganism is a virus.

name: cues
query: Query: cues [SEP] Cues is signals for an action; that specific portion of a perceptual field or pattern of stimuli to which a subject has learned to respond.

name: cultural competency
query: Query: cultural competency [SEP] Cultural competency is cultural and linguistic competence is a [MASK] of congruent behaviors, attitudes, and policies that come together in a system, agency, or among professionals that enables effective work in cross-cultural situations. Competence implies the capacity to function effectively as an individual and an organization within the context of the cultural beliefs, behaviors, and needs presented by consumers and their communities.

name: cultural diversity
query: Query: cultural diversity [SEP] Cultural diversity is coexistence of numerous distinct ethnic, racial, religious, or cultural groups within one social unit, organization, or population. (From American Heritage Dictionary, 2d college ed., 1982, p955)

name: cultural evolution
query: Query: cultural evolution [SEP] Cultural evolution is the continuous developmental process of a culture from simple to complex forms and from homogeneous to heterogeneous qualities. It is the change of cultures over time. Research in cultural evolution tries to understand the causal relationships that shape and change human culture in both the long and the short term.

name: culturally appropriate technology
query: Query: culturally appropriate technology [SEP] Culturally appropriate technology is a science or technology that promotes self-sufficiency and is suitable to the cultural, environmental, economic and social conditions of the geographic area in which it is applied.

name: culturally competent care
query: Query: culturally competent care [SEP] Culturally competent care is health care services that are respectful of and responsive to the health beliefs, practices and cultural and linguistic needs of diverse patients. The provider and the patient each bring their individual learned patterns of language and culture to the health care experience which must be transcended to achieve equal access and quality health care.

name: current procedural terminology
query: Query: current procedural terminology [SEP] Current procedural terminology is descriptive terms and identifying codes for reporting medical services and procedures performed by physicians. It is produced by the [MASK] and used in insurance claim reporting for medicare; medicaid; and private health insurance programs (From cpt 2002).

name: curriculum
query: Query: curriculum [SEP] Curriculum is a course of study offered by an educational institution.

name: cyanobacteria
query: Query: cyanobacteria [SEP] Cyanobacteria is a phylum of oxygenic photosynthetic bacteria comprised of unicellular to multicellular bacteria possessing [MASK] and carrying out oxygenic [MASK]. Cyanobacteria are the only known organisms capable of fixing both carbon dioxide (in the presence of light) and nitrogen. Cell morphology can include nitrogen-fixing heterocysts and/or resting cells called akinetes. Formerly called blue-green algae, cyanobacteria were traditionally treated as algae.

name: cyclic amp
query: Query: cyclic amp [SEP] Cyclic amp is an adenine nucleotide containing one phosphate group which is esterified to both the 3'- and 5'-positions of the sugar moiety. It is a second messenger and a key intracellular regulator, functioning as a mediator of activity for a number of hormones, including epinephrine, glucagon, and acth.

name: cyclic amp receptor protein
query: Query: cyclic amp receptor protein [SEP] Cyclic amp receptor protein is a transcriptional regulator in prokaryotes which, when activated by binding cyclic amp, acts at several promoters. Cyclic amp receptor protein was originally identified as a catabolite gene activator protein. It was subsequently shown to regulate several functions unrelated to catabolism, and to be both a negative and a positive regulator of transcription. Cell surface cyclic amp receptors are not included (cyclic amp receptors), nor are the eukaryotic cytoplasmic cyclic amp receptor proteins, which are the regulatory subunits of cyclic amp-dependent protein kinases.

name: cyclic imp
query: Query: cyclic imp [SEP] Cyclic imp is inosine cyclic 3',5'-(hydrogen phosphate). An inosine nucleotide which acts as a mild inhibitor of the hydrolysis of cyclic amp and cyclic gmp and as an inhibitor of cat heart cyclic amp phosphodiesterase.

name: cyclin c
query: Query: cyclin c [SEP] Cyclin c is a cyclin subtype that binds to the cyclin-dependent kinase 3 and cyclin-dependent kinase 8. Cyclin c plays a dual role as a transcriptional regulator and a g1 phase cell cycle regulator.

name: cyclin t
query: Query: cyclin t [SEP] Cyclin t is a cyclin subtype that is found associated with cyclin-dependent kinase 9. Unlike traditional cyclins, which regulate the cell cycle, type t cyclins appear to regulate transcription and are components of positive transcriptional elongation factor b.

name: cystic fibrosis
query: Query: cystic fibrosis [SEP] Cystic fibrosis is an autosomal recessive genetic disease of the exocrine glands. It is caused by mutations in the gene encoding the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator expressed in several organs including the lung, the pancreas, the biliary system, and the sweat glands. Cystic fibrosis is characterized by epithelial secretory dysfunction associated with ductal obstruction resulting in airway obstruction; chronic respiratory infections; pancreatic insufficiency; maldigestion; [MASK] depletion; and heat prostration.

name: cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator
query: Query: cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator [SEP] Cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator is a chloride channel that regulates secretion in many exocrine tissues. Abnormalities in the cftr gene have been shown to cause cystic fibrosis. (Hum Genet 1994;93(4):364-8)

name: cytokine release syndrome
query: Query: cytokine release syndrome [SEP] Cytokine release syndrome is a severe immune reaction characterized by excessive release of cytokines. Symptoms include dyspnea; fever; headache; hypotension; nausea; rash; tachycardia; hypoxia; hyperferritinemia, and [MASK]. It is associated with viral infections, sepsis, autoimmune diseases and a variety of factors used in immunotherapy.

name: cytoplasmic granules
query: Query: cytoplasmic granules [SEP] Cytoplasmic granules is condensed areas of cellular material that may be bounded by a membrane.

name: czech republic
query: Query: czech republic [SEP] Czech republic is created 1 January 1993 as a result of the division of Czechoslovakia into the Czech Republic and Slovakia.

name: daily or recreational activity
query: Query: daily or recreational activity [SEP] Daily or recreational activity is daily or recreational activity

name: dark adaptation
query: Query: dark adaptation [SEP] Dark adaptation is [MASK] of the eyes under conditions of low light. The sensitivity of the eye to light is increased during dark adaptation.

name: data aggregation
query: Query: data aggregation [SEP] Data aggregation is process of searching, gathering, and presenting data in a summarized format.

name: data analysis
query: Query: data analysis [SEP] Data analysis is process of systematically applying statistical and/or logical techniques to describe and illustrate, condense and recap, and evaluate data (https://ori.hhs.gov/education).

name: databases , nucleic acid
query: Query: databases , nucleic acid [SEP] Nucleic acid databases is databases containing information about nucleic acids such as base sequence; snps; nucleic acid conformation; and other properties. Information about the dna fragments kept in a gene library or genomic library is often maintained in dna databases.

name: databases , protein
query: Query: databases , protein [SEP] Protein databases is databases containing information about proteins such as amino acid sequence; protein conformation; and other properties.

name: databases as topic
query: Query: databases as topic [SEP] Databases as topic is works on organized collections of records, standardized in format and content, that are stored in any of a variety of computer-readable modes.

name: data compression
query: Query: data compression [SEP] Data compression is information application based on a variety of coding methods to minimize the amount of data to be stored, retrieved, or transmitted. Data compression can be applied to various forms of data, such as images and signals. It is used to reduce costs and increase efficiency in the maintenance of large volumes of data.

name: data interpretation , statistical
query: Query: data interpretation , statistical [SEP] Statistical data interpretation is application of statistical procedures to analyze specific observed or assumed facts from a particular study.

name: data management
query: Query: data management [SEP] Data management is processes that include acquiring, validating, storing, protecting, and processing data to ensure accessibility, reliability, and timeliness for users.

name: data mining
query: Query: data mining [SEP] Data mining is use of sophisticated analysis tools to sort through, organize, examine, and combine large sets of information.

name: dataset
query: Query: dataset [SEP] Dataset is works consisting of organized collections of data, which have been stored permanently in a formalized manner suitable for communication, interpretation, or processing.

name: datasets as topic
query: Query: datasets as topic [SEP] Datasets as topic is subject matter related to the curation of data from research projects, stored permanently in a formalized manner suitable for communication, interpretation, or processing.

name: data systems
query: Query: data systems [SEP] Data systems is organized collection of symbols and symbol-manipulating processes used to operate on such symbols.

name: data visualization
query: Query: data visualization [SEP] Data visualization is facilitating understanding of the significance of data by placing it in a visual context. Patterns, trends and correlations that might go undetected in text-based data may be exposed and recognized easier.

name: day care , medical
query: Query: day care , medical [SEP] Medical day care is institutional health care of patients during the day. The patients return home at night.

name: death certificates
query: Query: death certificates [SEP] Death certificates is official records of individual deaths including the [MASK] certified by a physician, and any other required identifying information.

name: death domain
query: Query: death domain [SEP] Death domain is a conserved protein interaction domain of the death domain superfamily that is structurally similar to the [MASK] and caspase recruitment domain. Death domains bind each other to form oligomers and occur on death domain receptors, where they are required for apoptosis signaling and non-apoptotic functions.

name: decision making , organizational
query: Query: decision making , organizational [SEP] Organizational decision making is the process by which decisions are made in an institution or other organization.

name: decision making , shared
query: Query: decision making , shared [SEP] Shared decision making is collaborative process of reaching a decision.

name: decision support systems , clinical
query: Query: decision support systems , clinical [SEP] Clinical decision support systems is computer-based information systems used to integrate clinical and patient information and provide support for decision-making in patient care.

name: decision support systems , management
query: Query: decision support systems , management [SEP] Management decision support systems is computer-based systems that enable management to interrogate the computer on an ad hoc basis for various kinds of information in the organization, which predict the effect of potential decisions.

name: decision trees
query: Query: decision trees [SEP] Decision trees is a graphic device used in decision analysis, series of decision options are represented as branches (hierarchical).

name: deep learning
query: Query: deep learning [SEP] Deep learning is supervised or unsupervised machine learning methods that use multiple layers of data representations generated by nonlinear transformations, instead of individual task-specific algorithms, to build and train neural network models.

name: deep sedation
query: Query: deep sedation [SEP] Deep sedation is drug-induced depression of consciousness during which patients cannot be easily aroused but respond purposely following repeated painful stimulation. The ability to independently maintain ventilatory function may be impaired. (From: American Society of Anesthesiologists Practice Guidelines)

name: delayed diagnosis
query: Query: delayed diagnosis [SEP] Delayed diagnosis is non-optimal interval of time between onset of symptoms, identification, and initiation of treatment.

name: delivery of health care , integrated
query: Query: delivery of health care , integrated [SEP] Integrated delivery of health care is a health care system which combines physicians, hospitals, and other medical services with a health plan to provide the complete spectrum of medical care for its customers. In a fully integrated system, the three key elements - physicians, hospital, and health plan membership - are in balance in terms of matching medical resources with the needs of purchasers and patients. (Coddington et al., Integrated Health Care: Reorganizing the Physician, Hospital and Health Plan Relationship, 1994, p7)

name: delta rhythm
query: Query: delta rhythm [SEP] Delta rhythm is brain waves seen on eeg characterized by a high amplitude and a frequency of 4 Hz and below. They are considered the "deep sleep waves" observed during sleep in dreamless states, infancy, and in some brain disorders.

name: democracy
query: Query: democracy [SEP] Democracy is a system of government in which there is free and equal participation by the people in the political decision-making process.

name: dendritic spines
query: Query: dendritic spines [SEP] Dendritic spines is spiny processes on dendrites, each of which receives excitatory input from one nerve ending (nerve endings). They are commonly found on purkinje cells and pyramidal cells.

name: dental anxiety
query: Query: dental anxiety [SEP] Dental anxiety is abnormal fear or dread of visiting the dentist for preventive care or therapy and unwarranted anxiety over dental procedures.

name: dental arch
query: Query: dental arch [SEP] Dental arch is the curve formed by the row of teeth in their normal position in the jaw. The inferior dental arch is formed by the mandibular teeth, and the superior dental arch by the maxillary teeth.

name: dental audit
query: Query: dental audit [SEP] Dental audit is a detailed review and evaluation of selected clinical records by qualified professional personnel for evaluating quality of dental care.

name: dental calculus
query: Query: dental calculus [SEP] Dental calculus is abnormal concretion or calcified deposit that forms around the teeth or dental prostheses.

name: dental care for children
query: Query: dental care for children [SEP] Dental care for children is the giving of attention to the special dental needs of children, including the prevention of tooth diseases and instruction in dental hygiene and dental health. The dental care may include the services provided by dental specialists.

name: dental care for chronically ill
query: Query: dental care for chronically ill [SEP] Dental care for chronically ill is dental care for patients with chronic diseases. These diseases include chronic cardiovascular, endocrinologic, hematologic, immunologic, neoplastic, and renal diseases. The concept does not include dental care for the mentally or physically disabled which is dental care for disabled.

name: dental care for disabled
query: Query: dental care for disabled [SEP] Dental care for disabled is dental care for the emotionally, mentally, or physically disabled patient. It does not include dental care for the chronically ill ( = dental care for chronically ill).

name: dental caries susceptibility
query: Query: dental caries susceptibility [SEP] Dental caries susceptibility is the predisposition to tooth decay (dental caries).

name: dental casting investment
query: Query: dental casting investment [SEP] Dental casting investment is material from which the casting mold is made in the fabrication of gold or cobalt-chromium castings. (Boucher's Clinical Dental Terminology, 4th ed, p168)

name: dental casting technique
query: Query: dental casting technique [SEP] Dental casting technique is the process of producing a form or impression made of metal or plaster using a mold.

name: dental clinics
query: Query: dental clinics [SEP] Dental clinics is facilities where dental care is provided to patients.

name: dental devices , home care
query: Query: dental devices , home care [SEP] Home care dental devices is devices used in the home by persons to maintain dental and periodontal health. The devices include toothbrushes, dental flosses, water irrigators, gingival stimulators, etc.

name: dental enamel
query: Query: dental enamel [SEP] Dental enamel is a hard thin translucent layer of calcified substance which envelops and protects the dentin of the crown of the tooth. It is the hardest substance in the body and is almost entirely composed of calcium [MASK]. Under the microscope, it is composed of thin rods (enamel prisms) held together by cementing substance, and surrounded by an enamel sheath. (From Jablonski, Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992, p286)

name: dental enamel permeability
query: Query: dental enamel permeability [SEP] Dental enamel permeability is the property of dental enamel to permit passage of light, heat, gases, liquids, metabolites, mineral ions and other substances. It does not include the penetration of the dental enamel by microorganisms.

name: dental implantation
query: Query: dental implantation [SEP] Dental implantation is the grafting or inserting of a prosthetic device of alloplastic material into the oral tissue beneath the mucosal or periosteal layer or within the bone. Its purpose is to provide support and retention to a partial or complete denture.

name: dental implants
query: Query: dental implants [SEP] Dental implants is biocompatible materials placed into (endosseous) or onto (subperiosteal) the jawbone to support a crown, bridge, or artificial tooth, or to stabilize a diseased tooth.

name: dental impression materials
query: Query: dental impression materials [SEP] Dental impression materials is substances used to create an impression, or negative reproduction, of the teeth and dental arches. These materials include dental plasters and cements, metallic oxide pastes, silicone base materials, or elastomeric materials.

name: dental impression technique
query: Query: dental impression technique [SEP] Dental impression technique is procedure of producing an imprint or negative likeness of the teeth and/or edentulous areas. Impressions are made in plastic material which becomes hardened or [MASK] while in contact with the tissue. They are later filled with plaster of Paris or artificial stone to produce a facsimile of the oral structures present. Impressions may be made of a full complement of teeth, of areas where some teeth have been removed, or in a mouth from which all teeth have been extracted. (Illustrated Dictionary of Dentistry, 1982)

name: dental leakage
query: Query: dental leakage [SEP] Dental leakage is the seepage of fluids, debris, and micro-organisms between the walls of a prepared dental cavity and the restoration.

name: dental marginal adaptation
query: Query: dental marginal adaptation [SEP] Dental marginal adaptation is the degree of approximation or fit of filling material or dental prosthetic to the tooth surface. a close marginal adaptation and seal at the interface is important for successful dental restorations.

name: dental occlusion , balanced
query: Query: dental occlusion , balanced [SEP] Balanced dental occlusion is dental occlusion in which the occlusal contact of the teeth on the working side of the jaw is accompanied by the harmonious contact of the teeth on the opposite (balancing) side. (From Jablonski, Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992, p556)

name: dental pins
query: Query: dental pins [SEP] Dental pins is small cylindrical pieces of metal used to enhance retention.

name: dental plaque
query: Query: dental plaque [SEP] Dental plaque is a film that attaches to teeth, often causing dental caries and gingivitis. It is composed of mucins, secreted from salivary glands, and microorganisms.

name: dental prosthesis design
query: Query: dental prosthesis design [SEP] Dental prosthesis design is the plan and delineation of dental prostheses in general or a specific dental prosthesis. It does not include denture design. The framework usually consists of metal.

name: dental prosthesis retention
query: Query: dental prosthesis retention [SEP] Dental prosthesis retention is holding a dental prosthesis in place by its design, or by the use of additional devices or adhesives.

name: dental pulp calcification
query: Query: dental pulp calcification [SEP] [MASK] calcification is calcinosis of the [MASK] or root canal.

name: dental pulp cavity
query: Query: dental pulp cavity [SEP] [MASK] cavity is the space in a tooth bounded by the dentin and containing the [MASK]. The portion of the cavity within the crown of the tooth is the pulp chamber; the portion within the root is the pulp canal or root canal.

name: dental pulp test
query: Query: dental pulp test [SEP] [MASK] test is investigations conducted on the physical health of teeth involving use of a tool that transmits hot or cold electric currents on a tooth's surface that can determine problems with that tooth based on reactions to the currents.

name: dental records
query: Query: dental records [SEP] Dental records is data collected during dental examination for the purpose of study, diagnosis, or treatment planning.

name: dental research
query: Query: dental research [SEP] Dental research is the study of laws, theories, and hypotheses through a systematic examination of pertinent facts and their interpretation in the field of dentistry. (From Jablonski, Illustrated Dictionary of Dentistry, 1982, p674)

name: dental restoration , temporary
query: Query: dental restoration , temporary [SEP] Temporary dental restoration is a prosthesis or restoration placed for a limited period, from several days to several months, which is designed to seal the tooth and maintain its position until a permanent restoration (dental restoration, permanent) will replace it. (From Jablonski, Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992)

name: dental restoration failure
query: Query: dental restoration failure [SEP] Dental restoration failure is inability or inadequacy of a dental restoration or prosthesis to perform as expected.

name: dental restoration repair
query: Query: dental restoration repair [SEP] Dental restoration repair is the process of repairing broken or worn parts of a permanent dental restoration.

name: dental restoration wear
query: Query: dental restoration wear [SEP] Dental restoration wear is occlusal wear of the surfaces of restorations and surface wear of dentures.

name: dental sac
query: Query: dental sac [SEP] Dental sac is dense fibrous layer formed from mesodermal tissue that surrounds the epithelial enamel organ. The cells eventually migrate to the external surface of the newly formed root dentin and give rise to the cementoblasts that deposit cementum on the developing root, fibroblasts of the developing periodontal ligament, and [MASK] of the developing alveolar bone.

name: dental scaling
query: Query: dental scaling [SEP] Dental scaling is removal of dental plaque and dental calculus from the surface of a tooth, from the surface of a tooth apical to the gingival margin accumulated in [MASK], or from the surface coronal to the gingival margin.

name: dental service , hospital
query: Query: dental service , hospital [SEP] Hospital dental service is hospital department providing dental care.

name: dental stress analysis
query: Query: dental stress analysis [SEP] Dental stress analysis is the description and measurement of the various factors that produce physical stress upon dental restorations, prostheses, or appliances, materials associated with them, or the natural oral structures.

name: dentate gyrus
query: Query: dentate gyrus [SEP] Dentate gyrus is gray matter situated above the gyrus hippocampi. It is composed of three layers. The molecular layer is continuous with the hippocampus in the hippocampal fissure. The granular layer consists of closely arranged spherical or oval neurons, called granule cells, whose axons pass through the polymorphic layer ending on the dendrites of pyramidal cells in the hippocampus.

name: dentin , secondary
query: Query: dentin , secondary [SEP] Secondary dentin is dentin formed by normal pulp after completion of root end formation.

name: dentin dysplasia
query: Query: dentin dysplasia [SEP] Dentin dysplasia is an apparently hereditary disorder of dentin formation, marked by a normal appearance of coronal dentin associated with pulpal obliteration, faulty root formation, and a tendency for peripheral lesions without obvious cause. (From Dorland, 27th ed)

name: dentin sensitivity
query: Query: dentin sensitivity [SEP] Dentin sensitivity is pain associated with exposed dentin surfaces of the teeth.

name: dentin solubility
query: Query: dentin solubility [SEP] Dentin solubility is the susceptibility of the dentin to dissolution.

name: deoxy sugars
query: Query: deoxy sugars [SEP] Deoxy sugars is sugars that in which one or more hydroxyl groups of the pyranose or furanose ring is substituted by hydrogen.

name: dependency , psychological
query: Query: dependency , psychological [SEP] Psychological dependency is the tendency of an individual or individuals to rely on others for advice, guidance, or support.

name: dependent personality disorder
query: Query: dependent personality disorder [SEP] Dependent personality disorder is a personality disorder characterized by a pervasive and excessive need to be taken care of that leads to submissive and clinging behavior and fears of separation, beginning by early adulthood and present in a variety of contexts. (From [MASK], 1994)

name: depression
query: Query: depression [SEP] Depression is depressive states usually of moderate intensity in contrast with major depression present in neurotic and psychotic disorders.

name: depression , postpartum
query: Query: depression , postpartum [SEP] Postpartum depression is depression in postpartum women, usually within four weeks after giving birth (parturition). The degree of depression ranges from mild transient depression to neurotic or psychotic depressive disorders. (From [MASK], p386)

name: depressive disorder , major
query: Query: depressive disorder , major [SEP] Major depressive disorder is disorder in which five (or more) of the following symptoms have been present during the same 2-week period and represent a change from previous functioning; at least one of the symptoms is either (1) depressed mood or (2) loss of interest or pleasure. Symptoms include: depressed mood most of the day, nearly every daily; markedly diminished interest or pleasure in activities most of the day, nearly every day; significant weight loss when not dieting or weight gain; Insomnia or hypersomnia nearly every day; psychomotor agitation or retardation nearly every day; fatigue or loss of energy nearly every day; feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt; diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness, nearly every day; or  recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation without a specific plan, or a suicide attempt. (dsm-5)

name: dermatitis , atopic
query: Query: dermatitis , atopic [SEP] Atopic dermatitis is a chronic inflammatory genetically determined disease of the skin marked by increased ability to form reagin (IgE), with increased susceptibility to allergic rhinitis and asthma, and hereditary disposition to a lowered threshold for pruritus. It is manifested by lichenification, excoriation, and crusting, mainly on the flexural surfaces of the elbow and [MASK]. In infants it is known as infantile eczema.

name: designer drugs
query: Query: designer drugs [SEP] Designer drugs is drugs designed and synthesized, often for illegal street use, by modification of existing drug structures (e.g., amphetamines). Of special interest are mptp (a reverse ester of meperidine), mda (3,4-methylenedioxyamphetamine), and mdma (3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine). Many drugs act on the aminergic system, the physiologically active biogenic amines.

name: developing countries
query: Query: developing countries [SEP] Developing countries is countries in the process of change with economic growth, that is, an increase in production, per capita consumption, and income. The process of economic growth involves better utilization of natural and human resources, which results in a change in the social, political, and economic structures.

name: device removal
query: Query: device removal [SEP] Device removal is removal of an implanted therapeutic or prosthetic device.

name: diabetes , gestational
query: Query: diabetes , gestational [SEP] Gestational diabetes is diabetes mellitus induced by pregnancy but resolved at the end of pregnancy. It does not include previously diagnosed diabetics who become pregnant (pregnancy in diabetics). Gestational diabetes usually develops in late pregnancy when insulin antagonistic hormones peaks leading to insulin resistance; glucose intolerance; and hyperglycemia.

name: diabetes mellitus , experimental
query: Query: diabetes mellitus , experimental [SEP] Experimental diabetes mellitus is diabetes mellitus induced experimentally by administration of various diabetogenic agents or by pancreatectomy.

name: diabetes mellitus , type 1
query: Query: diabetes mellitus , type 1 [SEP] Type 1 diabetes mellitus is a subtype of diabetes mellitus that is characterized by insulin deficiency. It is manifested by the sudden onset of severe hyperglycemia, rapid progression to diabetic ketoacidosis, and death unless treated with insulin. The disease may occur at any age, but is most common in childhood or adolescence.

name: diabetes mellitus , type 2
query: Query: diabetes mellitus , type 2 [SEP] Type 2 diabetes mellitus is a subclass of diabetes mellitus that is not INSULIN-responsive or dependent (niddm). It is characterized initially by insulin resistance and hyperinsulinemia; and eventually by glucose intolerance; hyperglycemia; and overt diabetes. Type ii diabetes mellitus is no longer considered a disease exclusively found in adults. Patients seldom develop ketosis but often exhibit obesity.

name: diabetic coma
query: Query: diabetic coma [SEP] Diabetic coma is a state of unconsciousness as a complication of diabetes mellitus. It occurs in cases of extreme hyperglycemia or extreme hypoglycemia as a complication of insulin therapy.

name: diabetic foot
query: Query: diabetic foot [SEP] Diabetic [MASK] is common [MASK] problems in persons with diabetes mellitus, caused by any combination of factors such as diabetic neuropathies; peripheral vascular diseases; and infection. With the loss of sensation and poor circulation, injuries and infections often lead to severe [MASK] ulceration, gangrene and [MASK].

name: diabetic retinopathy
query: Query: diabetic retinopathy [SEP] Diabetic retinopathy is disease of the retina as a complication of diabetes mellitus. It is characterized by the progressive microvascular complications, such as aneurysm, interretinal edema, and intraocular pathologic neovascularization.

name: diagnosis , dual ( psychiatry )
query: Query: diagnosis , dual ( psychiatry ) [SEP] Dual (psychiatry) diagnosis is the co-existence of a substance abuse disorder with a psychiatric disorder. The diagnostic principle is based on the fact that it has been found often that chemically dependent patients also have psychiatric problems of various degrees of severity.

name: diagnostic procedure
query: Query: diagnostic procedure [SEP] Diagnostic procedure is methods, procedures, and tests performed to diagnose disease, disordered function, or disability.

name: diagnostic screening programs
query: Query: diagnostic screening programs [SEP] Diagnostic screening programs is services for the presumptive identification of unrecognized disease in an apparently healthy, asymptomatic population by means of tests, examinations or other procedures that can be applied rapidly and easily to the target population. (from [MASK] Organization http://www.who.int/cancer/prevention/diagnosis-screening/screening/en/ Oct. 24,2017)

name: diagnostic test approval
query: Query: diagnostic test approval [SEP] [MASK] approval is the process of gaining approval by a government regulatory agency for diagnostic reagents and test kits. This includes any required preclinical or clinical testing, review, submission, and evaluation of the applications and test results, and post-marketing surveillance.

name: dialysis
query: Query: dialysis [SEP] Dialysis is a process of selective diffusion through a membrane. It is usually used to separate low-molecular-weight solutes which diffuse through the membrane from the colloidal and high-molecular-weight solutes which do not. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

name: diamond
query: Query: diamond [SEP] Diamond is diamond. a crystalline form of carbon that occurs as hard, colorless or tinted isomeric crystals. It is used as a precious stone, for cutting glass, and as bearings for delicate mechanisms. (From Grant & Hackh's Chemical Dictionary, 5th ed)

name: diaphragm
query: Query: diaphragm [SEP] Diaphragm is the musculofibrous partition that separates the thoracic cavity from the abdominal cavity. Contraction of the diaphragm increases the volume of the thoracic cavity aiding [MASK].

name: diary
query: Query: diary [SEP] Diary is work consisting of records, usually private, of writers' experiences, observations, feelings, attitudes, etc. They may also be works marked in [MASK] order in which to note appointments and the like. (From Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

name: dictionary , chemical
query: Query: dictionary , chemical [SEP] Chemical dictionary is a reference book containing a list of words related to chemistry-usually in alphabetic order-giving information about form, pronunciation, etymology, grammar, and meaning.

name: dictionary , classical
query: Query: dictionary , classical [SEP] Classical dictionary is a reference work containing a list of words related to the Greco-Roman World giving information about form, pronunciation, etymology, grammar, and meaning.

name: dictionary , dental
query: Query: dictionary , dental [SEP] Dental dictionary is a reference book containing a list of words related to dentistry-usually in alphabetic order-giving information about form, pronunciation, etymology, grammar, and meaning.

name: dictionary , medical
query: Query: dictionary , medical [SEP] Medical dictionary is a reference book containing a list of words related to medicine-usually in alphabetic order-giving information about form, pronunciation, etymology, grammar, and meaning.

name: dielectric spectroscopy
query: Query: dielectric spectroscopy [SEP] Dielectric spectroscopy is a technique of measuring the dielectric properties of materials, which vary over a range of frequencies depending on the physical properties of the material. The technique involves measuring, over a range of frequencies, electrical impedance and phase shift of an electric field as it passes through the material.

name: diet , carbohydrate loading
query: Query: diet , carbohydrate loading [SEP] Carbohydrate loading diet is a diet rich in dietary carbohydrates.

name: diet , healthy
query: Query: diet , healthy [SEP] Healthy diet is dietary patterns which have been found to be important in reducing disease risk.

name: diet , mediterranean
query: Query: diet , mediterranean [SEP] Mediterranean diet is a diet typical of the Mediterranean region characterized by a pattern high in fruits and vegetables, edible grain and bread, potatoes, poultry, beans, nuts, [MASK] and fish while low in red meat and dairy and moderate in alcohol consumption.

name: diet , reducing
query: Query: diet , reducing [SEP] Reducing diet is a diet designed to cause an individual to lose weight.

name: diet , western
query: Query: diet , western [SEP] Western diet is a pattern of food consumption adopted mainly by the people of North America and Western Europe. It is mainly characterized by high intake of meat, processed grains, dietary sugars, dairy products, and dietary fats.

name: dietary approaches to stop hypertension
