query: Query: dietary approaches to stop hypertension [SEP] Dietary approaches to stop hypertension is dietary recommendations that promote reduction in or prevention of high blood pressure. Recommendations include increasing intake of fruits and vegetables, and high-fiber, low-fat foods and reducing the intake of dietary sodium and high fat foods.

name: dietary fiber
query: Query: dietary fiber [SEP] Dietary fiber is the remnants of plant cell walls that are resistant to [MASK] by the alimentary enzymes of man. It comprises various polysaccharides and lignins.

name: dietary sucrose
query: Query: dietary sucrose [SEP] Dietary sucrose is sucrose present in the diet. It is added to food and drinks as a sweetener.

name: diet records
query: Query: diet records [SEP] Diet records is records of nutrient intake over a specific period of time, usually kept by the patient.

name: differential threshold
query: Query: differential threshold [SEP] Differential threshold is the smallest difference which can be discriminated between two stimuli or one which is barely above the threshold.

name: diffuse axonal injury
query: Query: diffuse axonal injury [SEP] Diffuse axonal injury is a relatively common sequela of blunt head injury, characterized by a global disruption of axons throughout the brain. Associated clinical features may include neurobehavioral manifestations; [MASK]; dementia; and other disorders.

name: diffusion chambers , culture
query: Query: diffusion chambers , culture [SEP] Culture diffusion chambers is devices used in a technique by which cells or tissues are grown in vitro or, by implantation, in vivo within chambers permeable to diffusion of solutes across the chamber walls. The chambers are used for studies of drug effects, osmotic responses, cytogenic and immunologic phenomena, metabolism, etc., and include tissue cages.

name: diffusion tensor imaging
query: Query: diffusion tensor imaging [SEP] Diffusion tensor imaging is the use of diffusion anisotropy data from diffusion magnetic resonance imaging results to construct images based on the direction of the faster diffusing molecules.

name: digestive system abnormalities
query: Query: digestive system abnormalities [SEP] Digestive system abnormalities is congenital structural abnormalities of the digestive system.

name: digital dermatitis
query: Query: digital dermatitis [SEP] Digital dermatitis is highly contagious infectious dermatitis with lesions near the interdigital spaces usually in cattle. It causes discomfort and often severe lameness (lameness, animal). Lesions can be either erosive or proliferative and wart-like with papillary growths and hypertrophied hairs. dichelobacter nodosus and treponema are the most commonly associated causative agents for this mixed bacterial infection disease.

name: digital divide
query: Query: digital divide [SEP] Digital divide is gap between individuals, households, businesses and geographic areas at different socioeconomic levels with regard to both their opportunities to access electronic  information and communication technologies (ICTs). Their use of the Internet for a wide variety of activities, reflects various differences among and within countries.

name: dilatation , pathologic
query: Query: dilatation , pathologic [SEP] Pathologic dilatation is the condition of an anatomical structure's being dilated beyond normal dimensions.

name: directed tissue donation
query: Query: directed tissue donation [SEP] Directed tissue donation is tissue, organ, or gamete donation intended for a designated recipient.

name: directive counseling
query: Query: directive counseling [SEP] Directive counseling is counseling during which a professional plays an active role in a client's or patient's decision making by offering advice, guidance, and/or recommendations.

name: directly observed therapy
query: Query: directly observed therapy [SEP] Directly observed therapy is a treatment method in which patients are under direct [MASK] when they take their medication or receive their treatment. This method is designed to reduce the risk of treatment interruption and to ensure patient compliance.

name: directory
query: Query: directory [SEP] Directory is work consisting of an alphabetical or classified list of names, organizations, subjects, etc., giving usually titles, addresses, affiliations, and other professional data.

name: direct service costs
query: Query: direct service costs [SEP] Direct service costs is costs which are directly identifiable with a particular service.

name: disaster medicine
query: Query: disaster medicine [SEP] Disaster medicine is branch of medicine involved with management and organization of public health response to disasters and major events including the special health and medical needs of a community in a disaster.

name: disaster planning
query: Query: disaster planning [SEP] Disaster planning is procedures outlined for the care of casualties and the maintenance of services in disasters.

name: disaster victims
query: Query: disaster victims [SEP] Disaster victims is persons adversely effected by disasters, occurrences that result in property damage, deaths, and/or injuries to a community.

name: discrimination learning
query: Query: discrimination learning [SEP] Discrimination learning is learning that is manifested in the ability to respond differentially to various stimuli.

name: disease notification
query: Query: disease notification [SEP] Disease notification is notification or reporting by a physician or other health care provider of the occurrence of specified contagious diseases such as tuberculosis and hiv infections to designated public health agencies. The United States system of reporting notifiable diseases evolved from the Quarantine Act of 1878, which authorized the us Public Health Service to collect morbidity data on cholera, smallpox, and yellow fever; each state in the us has its own list of notifiable diseases and depends largely on reporting by the individual health care provider. (From Segen, Dictionary of Modern Medicine, 1992)

name: disease reservoirs
query: Query: disease reservoirs [SEP] Disease reservoirs is animate or inanimate sources which normally harbor disease-causing organisms and thus serve as potential sources of [MASK]. Reservoirs are distinguished from vectors (disease vectors) and carriers, which are agents of disease transmission rather than continuing sources of potential [MASK]. Humans may serve both as disease reservoirs and carriers.

name: disease resistance
query: Query: disease resistance [SEP] Disease resistance is the capacity of an organism to defend itself against pathological processes or the agents of those processes. This most often involves innate immunity whereby the organism responds to pathogens in a generic way. The term disease resistance is used most frequently when referring to plants.

name: diseases in twins
query: Query: diseases in twins [SEP] Diseases in twins is disorders affecting twins, one or both, at any age.

name: disease vectors
query: Query: disease vectors [SEP] Disease vectors is invertebrates or non-human vertebrates which transmit infective organisms from one host to another.

name: disk diffusion antimicrobial tests
query: Query: disk diffusion antimicrobial tests [SEP] Disk diffusion antimicrobial tests is a method where a culturing surface inoculated with microbe is exposed to small disks containing known amounts of a chemical agent resulting in a zone of inhibition (usually in millimeters) of growth of the microbe corresponding to the susceptibility of the strain to the agent.

name: disks large homolog 4 protein
query: Query: disks large homolog 4 protein [SEP] Disks large homolog 4 protein is a neuronal protein consisting of three pdz domains, an sh3 domain, and a C-terminal guanylate kinase-like region (see maguk proteins). It localizes to the post-synaptic density and associates with the cytoplasmic tail of nmda receptors and shaker potassium channels, playing a critical role in nmda receptor-mediated synaptic plasticity.

name: disorder of sex development , 46 , xy
query: Query: disorder of sex development , 46 , xy [SEP] Xy 46 disorder of [MASK] development is disorder of [MASK] development , 46 , xy

name: displacement , psychological
query: Query: displacement , psychological [SEP] Psychological displacement is the process by which an emotional or behavioral response that is appropriate for one situation appears in another situation for which it is inappropriate.

name: disseminated intravascular coagulation
query: Query: disseminated intravascular coagulation [SEP] Disseminated intravascular coagulation is a disorder characterized by procoagulant substances entering the general circulation causing a systemic thrombotic process. The activation of the clotting mechanism may arise from any of a number of disorders. a majority of the patients manifest skin lesions, sometimes leading to purpura fulminans.

name: distance counseling
query: Query: distance counseling [SEP] Distance counseling is counseling conducted via electronic or other non-face-to-face interactions.

name: district of columbia
query: Query: district of columbia [SEP] District of columbia is a federal area located between Maryland and Virginia on the Potomac [MASK]; it is coextensive with [MASK], d.c., which is the capital of the United States.

name: dna , ancient
query: Query: dna , ancient [SEP] Ancient dna is dna isolated from fossils or other ancient specimens.

name: dna , antisense
query: Query: dna , antisense [SEP] Antisense dna is dna that is complementary to the sense strand. (The sense strand has the same sequence as the mRNA transcript. The antisense strand is the template for mRNA synthesis.) Synthetic antisense DNAs are used to hybridize to complementary sequences in target RNAs or DNAs to effect the functioning of specific genes for investigative or therapeutic purposes.

name: dna , chloroplast
query: Query: dna , chloroplast [SEP] Chloroplast dna is deoxyribonucleic acid that makes up the genetic material of chloroplasts.

name: dna , complementary
query: Query: dna , complementary [SEP] Complementary dna is single-stranded complementary dna synthesized from an rna template by the action of RNA-dependent dna polymerase. cDNA (i.e., complementary dna, not circular dna, not c-dna) is used in a variety of molecular cloning experiments as well as serving as a specific hybridization probe.

name: dna , mitochondrial
query: Query: dna , mitochondrial [SEP] Mitochondrial dna is double-stranded dna of mitochondria. In eukaryotes, the [MASK] is circular and codes for ribosomal RNAs, transfer RNAs, and about 10 proteins.

name: dna adducts
query: Query: dna adducts [SEP] Dna adducts is the products of chemical reactions that result in the addition of extraneous chemical groups to dna.

name: dna breaks
query: Query: dna breaks [SEP] Dna breaks is interruptions in the sugar-phosphate backbone of dna.

name: dna cleavage
query: Query: dna cleavage [SEP] Dna cleavage is a reaction that severs one of the covalent sugar-phosphate linkages between nucleotides that compose the sugar phosphate backbone of dna. It is catalyzed enzymatically, chemically or by radiation. Cleavage may be exonucleolytic - removing the end nucleotide, or endonucleolytic - splitting the strand in two.

name: dna contamination
query: Query: dna contamination [SEP] Dna contamination is the presence of dna from a source foreign to the sample being analysed.

name: dna copy number variations
query: Query: dna copy number variations [SEP] Dna copy number variations is stretches of genomic dna that exist in different multiples between individuals. Many copy number variations have been associated with susceptibility or resistance to disease.

name: dna degradation , necrotic
query: Query: dna degradation , necrotic [SEP] Necrotic dna degradation is the random catabolism of dna accompanying the irreversible damage to tissue which leads to the pathological death of one or more cells.

name: dna mismatch repair
query: Query: dna mismatch repair [SEP] Dna mismatch repair is a dna repair pathway involved in correction of errors introduced during dna replication when an incorrect base, which cannot form hydrogen bonds with the corresponding base in the parent strand, is incorporated into the daughter strand. Excinucleases recognize the [MASK] and cause a segment of polynucleotide chain to be excised from the daughter strand, thereby removing the mismatched base. (from Oxford Dictionary of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, 2001)

name: dna packaging
query: Query: dna packaging [SEP] Dna packaging is the folding of an organism's dna molecule into a compact, orderly structure that fits within the limited space of a cell or virus particle.

name: dna polymerase gamma
query: Query: dna polymerase gamma [SEP] Dna polymerase gamma is a DNA-directed dna polymerase that functions in the replication of mitochondrial dna. Mutations in the gene that encodes this enzyme (polg) are associated with some forms of ophthalmoplegia, chronic external progressive.

name: dna primers
query: Query: dna primers [SEP] Dna primers is short sequences (generally about 10 [MASK]) of dna that are complementary to sequences of messenger rna and allow reverse transcriptases to start copying the adjacent sequences of mRNA. Primers are used extensively in genetic and molecular biology techniques.

name: dna probes , hla
query: Query: dna probes , hla [SEP] Hla dna probes is dna probes specific for the human leukocyte antigen genes, which represent the major histocompatibility determinants in humans. The four known loci are designated as a, b, c, and d. Specific antigens are identified by a locus notation and number, e.g., hla-a11. The inheritance of certain hla alleles is associated with increased risk for certain diseases (e.g., insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus).

name: dna probes , hpv
query: Query: dna probes , hpv [SEP] Hpv dna probes is dna probes specific for the identification of human papilloma virus.

name: dna repair enzymes
query: Query: dna repair enzymes [SEP] Dna repair enzymes is enzymes that are involved in the reconstruction of a continuous two-stranded dna molecule without mismatch from a molecule, which contained damaged regions.

name: dna repeat expansion
query: Query: dna repeat expansion [SEP] Dna repeat expansion is an increase number of repeats of a genomic, tandemly repeated dna sequence from one generation to the next.

name: dna replication timing
query: Query: dna replication timing [SEP] Dna replication timing is the temporal order in which the dna of the genome is replicated.

name: dna transformation competence
query: Query: dna transformation competence [SEP] Dna transformation competence is the ability of bacterial cells to take up exogenous dna and be genetically transformed by it.

name: dominance , ocular
query: Query: dominance , ocular [SEP] Ocular dominance is the functional superiority and preferential use of one eye over the other. The term is usually applied to superiority in sighting (visual perception) or motor task but not difference in visual acuity or dysfunction of one of the eyes. Ocular dominance can be modified by visual input and neurotrophic factors.

name: donor conception
query: Query: donor conception [SEP] Donor conception is assisted reproductive techniques where eggs, sperm, both eggs and sperm (double donation), or embryos from donors are used.

name: donor selection
query: Query: donor selection [SEP] Donor selection is the procedure established to evaluate the health status and risk factors of the potential donors of biological materials. Donors are selected based on the principles that their health will not be compromised in the process, and the donated materials, such as tissues or organs, are safe for reuse in the recipients.

name: dopamine agonists
query: Query: dopamine agonists [SEP] Dopamine agonists is drugs that bind to and activate dopamine receptors.

name: dopamine uptake inhibitors
query: Query: dopamine uptake inhibitors [SEP] Dopamine uptake inhibitors is drugs that block the transport of dopamine into axon terminals or into storage vesicles within terminals. Most of the adrenergic uptake inhibitors also inhibit dopamine uptake.

name: doppler effect
query: Query: doppler effect [SEP] Doppler effect is changes in the observed frequency of waves (as sound, light, or radio waves) due to the relative motion of source and observer. The effect was named for the 19th century Austrian physicist Johann Christian Doppler.

name: double bind interaction
query: Query: double bind interaction [SEP] Double bind interaction is simultaneous communication of conflicting messages in which the response to either message evokes [MASK] or disapproval. (apa, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 8th ed.)

name: double effect principle
query: Query: double effect principle [SEP] Double effect principle is guideline for determining when it is morally permissible to perform an action to pursue a good end with knowledge that the action will also bring about bad results. It generally states that, in cases where a contemplated action has such double effect, the action is permissible only if: it is not wrong in itself; the bad result is not intended; the good result is not a direct causal result of the bad result; and the good result is "proportionate to" the bad result. (from Solomon, "Double Effect," in Becker, The Encyclopedia of Ethics, 1992)

name: double outlet right ventricle
query: Query: double outlet right ventricle [SEP] Double outlet right ventricle is incomplete transposition of the great vessels in which both the aorta and the [MASK] arise from the right ventricle. The only outlet of the left ventricle is a large ventricular septal defect (ventricular septal defects or vsd). The various subtypes are classified by the location of the septal defect, such as subaortic, subpulmonary, or noncommitted.

name: down syndrome
query: Query: down syndrome [SEP] Down syndrome is a chromosome disorder associated either with an extra chromosome 21 or an effective trisomy for chromosome 21. Clinical manifestations include hypotonia, short stature, brachycephaly, upslanting palpebral fissures, epicanthus, Brushfield spots on the iris, protruding tongue, small ears, short, broad hands, fifth finger clinodactyly, Simian crease, and moderate to severe intellectual disability. Cardiac and gastrointestinal malformations, a marked increase in the incidence of leukemia, and the early onset of alzheimer disease are also associated with this condition. Pathologic features include the development of neurofibrillary tangles in neurons and the deposition of amyloid beta-protein, similar to the pathology of alzheimer disease. (Menkes, Textbook of Child Neurology, 5th ed, p213)

name: drainage , postural
query: Query: drainage , postural [SEP] Postural drainage is a rehabilitation therapy for removal of copious mucus secretion from the lung of patients with diseases such as chronic bronchitis; bronchiectasis; pulmonary abscess; or cystic fibrosis. The patient's head is placed in a downward incline (so the [MASK] is inferior to the affected area) for 15- to 20-minute sessions.

name: drawing
query: Query: drawing [SEP] Drawing is work consisting of graphic representations of objects or ideas by lines.

name: drinking
query: Query: drinking [SEP] Drinking is the consumption of liquids.

name: drinking water
query: Query: drinking water [SEP] Drinking water is water that is intended to be ingested.

name: drive
query: Query: drive [SEP] Drive is a state of internal activity of an organism that is a necessary condition before a given stimulus will elicit a class of responses; e.g., a certain level of hunger (drive) must be present before food will elicit an eating response.

name: driving under the influence
query: Query: driving under the influence [SEP] Driving under the influence is operating a motor vehicle while impaired by alcohol or other drugs including those prescribed by physicians.

name: drosophila melanogaster
query: Query: drosophila melanogaster [SEP] Drosophila melanogaster is a species of fruit fly frequently used in genetics because of the large size of its chromosomes.

name: drug antagonism
query: Query: drug antagonism [SEP] Drug antagonism is phenomena and pharmaceutics of compounds that inhibit the function of agonists (drug agonism) and inverse agonists (drug inverse agonism) for a specific receptor. On their own, antagonists produce no effect by themselves to a receptor, and are said to have neither intrinsic activity nor efficacy.

name: drug approval
query: Query: drug approval [SEP] Drug approval is process that is gone through in order for a drug to receive approval by a government regulatory agency. This includes any required pre-clinical or clinical testing, review, submission, and evaluation of the applications and test results, and post-marketing surveillance of the drug.

name: drug collateral sensitivity
query: Query: drug collateral sensitivity [SEP] Drug collateral sensitivity is increase in sensitivity of an organism, disease, or tissue to one drug that develops following the loss of sensitivity (i.e. resistance) to another drug.

name: drug contamination
query: Query: drug contamination [SEP] Drug contamination is the presence of organisms, or any foreign material that makes a drug preparation impure.

name: drug costs
query: Query: drug costs [SEP] Drug costs is the amount that a health care institution or organization pays for its drugs. It is one component of the final price that is charged to the consumer (fees, pharmaceutical or [MASK]).

name: drug delivery device
query: Query: drug delivery device [SEP] Drug delivery device is engineered technologies for the targeted delivery and/or controlled release of therapeutic agents.

name: drug discovery
query: Query: drug discovery [SEP] Drug discovery is the process of finding chemicals for potential therapeutic use.

name: drug evaluation
query: Query: drug evaluation [SEP] Drug evaluation is any process by which toxicity, metabolism, absorption, elimination, preferred route of administration, safe dosage range, etc., for a drug or group of drugs is determined through clinical assessment in humans or veterinary animals.

name: drug labeling
query: Query: drug labeling [SEP] Drug labeling is use of written, printed, or graphic materials upon or accompanying a drug container or wrapper. It includes contents, indications, effects, dosages, routes, methods, frequency and duration of administration, warnings, hazards, contraindications, side effects, precautions, and other relevant information.

name: drug monitoring
query: Query: drug monitoring [SEP] Drug monitoring is the process of observing, recording, or detecting the effects of a chemical substance administered to an individual therapeutically or diagnostically.

name: drug resistance , multiple , bacterial
query: Query: drug resistance , multiple , bacterial [SEP] Bacterial multiple drug resistance is the ability of bacteria to resist or to become tolerant to several structurally and functionally distinct drugs simultaneously. This resistance may be acquired through gene mutation or foreign dna in transmissible plasmids (r factors).

name: drug resistance , multiple , fungal
query: Query: drug resistance , multiple , fungal [SEP] Fungal multiple drug resistance is the ability of fungi to resist or to become tolerant to several structurally and functionally distinct drugs simultaneously. This resistance phenotype may be attributed to multiple gene mutations.

name: drug resistance , neoplasm
query: Query: drug resistance , neoplasm [SEP] Neoplasm drug resistance is resistance or diminished response of a neoplasm to an antineoplastic agent in humans, animals, or cell or tissue cultures.

name: drug resistant epilepsy
query: Query: drug resistant epilepsy [SEP] Drug resistant epilepsy is epileptic condition in which adequate trials of two tolerated and appropriately chosen and used antiepileptic drugs schedules to achieve sustained seizure freedom failed.

name: drugs , generic
query: Query: drugs , generic [SEP] Generic drugs is drugs whose drug name is not protected by a trademark. They may be manufactured by several companies.

name: drug storage
query: Query: drug storage [SEP] Drug storage is the process of keeping pharmaceutical products in an appropriate location.

name: drug substitution
query: Query: drug substitution [SEP] Drug substitution is the practice of replacing one prescribed drug with another that is expected to have the same clinical or psychological effect.

name: drug users
query: Query: drug users [SEP] Drug users is people who take drugs for a non-therapeutic or non-medical effect. The drugs may be legal or illegal, but their use often results in adverse medical, legal, or social consequences for the users.

name: drug utilization review
query: Query: drug utilization review [SEP] Drug utilization review is formal programs for assessing drug prescription against some standard. Drug utilization review may consider clinical appropriateness, cost effectiveness, and, in some cases, outcomes. Review is usually retrospective, but some analysis may be done before drugs are dispensed (as in computer systems which advise physicians when prescriptions are entered). Drug utilization review is mandated for Medicaid programs beginning in 1993.

name: dry ice
query: Query: dry ice [SEP] Dry ice is a solid form of carbon dioxide used as a refrigerant.

name: dry socket
query: Query: dry socket [SEP] Dry socket is a condition sometimes occurring after tooth extraction, particularly after traumatic extraction, resulting in a dry appearance of the exposed bone in the socket, due to disintegration or loss of the blood clot. It is basically a focal osteomyelitis without suppuration and is accompanied by severe pain (alveolalgia) and foul odor. (Dorland, 28th ed)

name: dual medicaid medicare eligibility
query: Query: dual medicaid medicare eligibility [SEP] Dual medicaid medicare eligibility is coordination of coverage eligibility of those individuals who are entitled to medicaid and medicare.

name: duplicate publications as topic
query: Query: duplicate publications as topic [SEP] Duplicate publications as topic is work about simultaneous or successive publishing of identical or near- identical material in two or more different sources without acknowledgment. It differs from reprinted publication in that a reprint cites sources. It differs from plagiarism in that [MASK] is the product of the same authorship while plagiarism publishes a work or parts of a work of another as one's own.

name: duration of therapy
query: Query: duration of therapy [SEP] Duration of therapy is planned or actual duration of various treatments or preventive measures.

name: dye dilution technique
query: Query: dye dilution technique [SEP] Dye dilution technique is method for assessing flow through a system by injection of a known quantity of dye into the system and monitoring its concentration over time at a specific point in the system. (From Dorland, 28th ed)

name: dynamic light scattering
query: Query: dynamic light scattering [SEP] Dynamic light scattering is an analytical technique for measuring particle size of molecules that are less than a micron in diameter dispersed or dissolved in a liquid.

name: dyspnea
query: Query: dyspnea [SEP] Dyspnea is difficult or labored breathing.

name: ear cartilage
query: Query: ear cartilage [SEP] Ear cartilage is cartilage of the ear auricle and the [MASK].

name: early detection of cancer
query: Query: early detection of cancer [SEP] Early detection of cancer is methods to identify and characterize cancer in the early stages of disease and predict tumor behavior.

name: early growth response protein 2
query: Query: early growth response protein 2 [SEP] Early growth response protein 2 is an early growth response transcription factor that controls the formation of the myelin sheath around peripheral axons by schwann cells. Mutations in egr2 transcription factor have been associated with hereditary motor and sensory neuropathies such as charcot-marie-tooth disease.

name: early intervention , educational
query: Query: early intervention , educational [SEP] Educational early intervention is procedures and programs that facilitate the development or skill acquisition in infants and young children who have disabilities, who are at risk for developing disabilities, or who are gifted. It includes programs that are designed to prevent handicapping conditions in infants and young children and family-centered programs designed to affect the functioning of infants and children with special needs. (From Journal of Early Intervention, [MASK], 1989, vol. 13, no. 1, p. 3; a Discursive Dictionary of Health Care, prepared for the u.s. House of Representatives Committee on Interstate and Foreign Commerce, 1976)

name: early warning score
query: Query: early warning score [SEP] Early warning score is tool for bedside evaluation based on five physiological parameters: systolic pressure, pulse, respiratory rate, body temperature and avpu (alert, voice, pain, unresponsive) score.

name: ear neoplasms
query: Query: ear neoplasms [SEP] Ear neoplasms is tumors or cancer of any part of the hearing and equilibrium system of the body (the external ear, the [MASK], and the [MASK]).

name: ear protective devices
query: Query: ear protective devices [SEP] Ear protective devices is personal devices for protection of the ears from loud or high intensity noise, water, or cold. These include earmuffs and earplugs.

name: ecological systems , closed
query: Query: ecological systems , closed [SEP] Closed ecological systems is systems that provide for the maintenance of life in an isolated living chamber through reutilization of the material available, in particular, by means of a cycle wherein exhaled carbon dioxide, urine, and other waste matter are converted chemically or by [MASK] into oxygen, water, and food. (nasa Thesaurus, 1988)

name: economics , nursing
query: Query: economics , nursing [SEP] Nursing economics is economic aspects of the nursing profession.

name: economics , pharmaceutical
query: Query: economics , pharmaceutical [SEP] Pharmaceutical economics is economic aspects of the fields of pharmacy and pharmacology as they apply to the development and study of medical economics in rational drug therapy and the impact of pharmaceuticals on the cost of medical care. Pharmaceutical economics also includes the economic considerations of the pharmaceutical care delivery system and in drug prescribing, particularly of cost-benefit values. (From j Res Pharm Econ 1989;1(1); PharmacoEcon 1992;1(1))

name: economic status
query: Query: economic status [SEP] Economic status is personal or family variables such as household income, assets such as inherited wealth, savings, employment benefits, or ownership of homes or other property.

name: ectopic gene expression
query: Query: ectopic gene expression [SEP] Ectopic gene expression is the expression of a gene in an abnormal place,  or at an abnormal  time in an organism. Ectopic Gene  Expression is often induced artificially by genetic techniques.

name: edema , cardiac
query: Query: edema , cardiac [SEP] Cardiac edema is abnormal fluid retention by the body due to impaired cardiac function or heart failure. It is usually characterized by increase in venous and capillary pressure, and swollen legs when standing. It is different from the generalized edema caused by renal dysfunction (nephrotic syndrome).

name: edema disease of swine
query: Query: edema disease of swine [SEP] Edema disease of swine is an [MASK] of young pigs that is usually associated with weaning. It is characterized clinically by paresis and subcutaneous edema.

name: editorial policies
query: Query: editorial policies [SEP] [MASK] policies is the guidelines and policy statements [MASK] forth by the editor(s) or [MASK] board of a publication.

name: education , dental , continuing
query: Query: education , dental , continuing [SEP] Continuing dental education is educational programs designed to inform dentists of recent advances in their fields.

name: education , dental , graduate
query: Query: education , dental , graduate [SEP] Graduate dental education is educational programs for dental graduates entering a specialty. They include formal specialty training as well as academic work in the clinical and basic dental sciences, and may lead to board certification or an advanced dental degree.

name: education , distance
query: Query: education , distance [SEP] Distance education is education via communication media (correspondence, radio, television, computer networks) with little or no in-person face-to-face contact between students and teachers. (eric Thesaurus, 1997)

name: education , medical , continuing
query: Query: education , medical , continuing [SEP] Continuing medical education is educational programs designed to inform physicians of recent advances in their field.

name: education , medical , graduate
query: Query: education , medical , graduate [SEP] Graduate medical education is educational programs for medical graduates entering a specialty. They include formal specialty training as well as academic work in the clinical and basic medical sciences, and may lead to board certification or an advanced medical degree.

name: education , medical , undergraduate
query: Query: education , medical , undergraduate [SEP] Undergraduate medical education is the period of medical education in a medical school. In the United States it follows the baccalaureate degree and precedes the granting of the m.d.

name: education , nursing , associate
query: Query: education , nursing , associate [SEP] Associate nursing education is a two-year program in nursing education in a community or junior college leading to an a.d. (Associate Degree). Graduates of this program are eligible for state examination for licensure as rn (Registered Nurse).

name: education , nursing , continuing
query: Query: education , nursing , continuing [SEP] Continuing nursing education is educational programs designed to inform nurses of recent advances in their fields.

name: education , nursing , graduate
query: Query: education , nursing , graduate [SEP] Graduate nursing education is those educational activities engaged in by holders of a bachelor's degree in nursing, which are primarily designed to prepare them for entrance into a specific field of nursing, and may lead to board certification or a more advanced degree.

name: education , pharmacy , continuing
query: Query: education , pharmacy , continuing [SEP] Continuing pharmacy education is educational programs designed to inform graduate pharmacists of recent advances in their particular field.

name: education , pharmacy , graduate
query: Query: education , pharmacy , graduate [SEP] Graduate pharmacy education is educational programs for pharmacists who have a bachelor's degree or a Doctor of Pharmacy degree entering a specific field of pharmacy. They may lead to an advanced degree.

name: education , veterinary
query: Query: education , veterinary [SEP] Veterinary education is use for general articles concerning veterinary medical education.

name: educational activity
query: Query: educational activity [SEP] Educational activity is acquisition of knowledge as a result of instruction in a formal course of study.

name: educational technology
query: Query: educational technology [SEP] Educational technology is systematic identification, development, organization, or utilization of educational resources and the management of these processes. It is occasionally used also in a more limited sense to describe the use of equipment-oriented techniques or audiovisual aids in educational settings. (Thesaurus of eric Descriptors, December 1993, p132)

name: education department , hospital
query: Query: education department , hospital [SEP] Hospital education department is hospital department responsible for administering educational and training activities pertaining to health for patients and staff.

name: education of visually disabled
query: Query: education of visually disabled [SEP] Education of visually disabled is the teaching or training of those individuals with visual disability.

name: efficiency , organizational
query: Query: efficiency , organizational [SEP] Organizational efficiency is the capacity of an organization, institution, or business to produce desired results with a minimum expenditure of energy, time, money, personnel, material, etc.

name: egg shell
query: Query: egg shell [SEP] Egg shell is a hard or leathery calciferous exterior covering of an egg.

name: egg white
query: Query: egg white [SEP] Egg [MASK] is the [MASK] of an egg, especially a [MASK]'s egg, used in cooking. It contains albumin. (Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

name: egypt , ancient
query: Query: egypt , ancient [SEP] Ancient [MASK] is a civilization of ancient Northeastern Africa, concentrated along the lower reaches of the Nile [MASK] in the area of [MASK]. It was active from 3100 b.c. until its conquest by Alexander the Great in 332 b.c.

name: elastic tissue
query: Query: elastic tissue [SEP] Elastic tissue is connective tissue comprised chiefly of elastic fibers. Elastic fibers have two components: elastin and microfibrils.

name: elbow
query: Query: elbow [SEP] Elbow is region of the body immediately surrounding and including the elbow joint.

name: elbow joint
query: Query: elbow joint [SEP] Elbow joint is a hinge joint connecting the forearm to the [MASK].

name: elder nutritional physiological phenomena
query: Query: elder nutritional physiological phenomena [SEP] Elder nutritional physiological phenomena is nutritional physiology of adults aged 65 years of age and older.

name: electrical synapses
query: Query: electrical synapses [SEP] Electrical synapses is specialized junctions between neurons which connect the cytoplasm of one neuron to another allowing direct passage of an ion current.

name: electric impedance
query: Query: electric impedance [SEP] Electric impedance is the resistance to the flow of either alternating or direct electrical current.

name: electric power supplies
query: Query: electric power supplies [SEP] Electric power supplies is devices that control the supply of electric current for [MASK] electrical equipment.

name: electric stimulation
query: Query: electric stimulation [SEP] Electric stimulation is use of electric potential or currents to elicit biological responses.

name: electromagnetic fields
query: Query: electromagnetic fields [SEP] Electromagnetic fields is fields representing the joint interplay of electric and magnetic forces.

name: electronic data processing
query: Query: electronic data processing [SEP] Electronic data processing is applications that store and process large quantities of data.

name: electronic nicotine delivery systems
query: Query: electronic nicotine delivery systems [SEP] Electronic nicotine delivery systems is devices or objects designed to provide nicotine in the form of an inhaled aerosol.

name: electronic nose
query: Query: electronic nose [SEP] Electronic nose is a device used to detect airborne odors, gases, flavors, volatile substances or vapors.

name: electronic supplementary materials
query: Query: electronic supplementary materials [SEP] Electronic supplementary materials is supporting content or information, such as animation, datasets, multimedia files, video, movies, audio files, text files, or software, which is submitted for publication in an online journal or an online edition of a journal. This information may be referenced in the text of the article with a link to the supplementary data provided. catalog: do not use

name: electronic waste
query: Query: electronic waste [SEP] Electronic waste is discarded electronic devices containing valuable and sometimes hazardous materials such as lead, nickel, cadmium, and mercury. (from http://www.epa.gov/osw/conserve/materials/ecycling/faq.htm#impact accessed 4/25/2010)

name: electron microscope tomography
query: Query: electron microscope tomography [SEP] [MASK] microscope tomography is a tomographic technique for obtaining 3-dimensional images with transmission [MASK] microscopy.

name: electron transport
query: Query: electron transport [SEP] [MASK] transport is the process by which [MASK] are transported from a reduced substrate to molecular oxygen. (From Bennington, Saunders Dictionary and Encyclopedia of Laboratory Medicine and Technology, 1984, p270)

name: electron transport complex iii
query: Query: electron transport complex iii [SEP] [MASK] transport complex iii is a multisubunit enzyme complex that contains cytochrome b group; cytochrome c1; and iron-sulfur centers. It catalyzes the oxidation of ubiquinol to ubiquinone, and transfers the [MASK] to cytochrome c. In mitochondria the redox reaction is coupled to the transport of protons across the [MASK].

name: electrophoresis , capillary
query: Query: electrophoresis , capillary [SEP] Capillary electrophoresis is a highly-sensitive (in the picomolar range, which is 10,000-fold more sensitive than conventional electrophoresis) and efficient technique that allows separation of proteins; nucleic acids; and carbohydrates. (Segen, Dictionary of Modern Medicine, 1992)

name: electrophoresis , cellulose acetate
query: Query: electrophoresis , cellulose acetate [SEP] Cellulose acetate electrophoresis is electrophoresis in which cellulose acetate is the diffusion medium.

name: electrophoresis , disc
query: Query: electrophoresis , disc [SEP] Disc electrophoresis is electrophoresis in which discontinuities in both the voltage and pH gradients are introduced by using [MASK] of different composition and pH in the different parts of the gel column. The term 'disc' was originally used as an abbreviation for 'discontinuous' referring to the [MASK] employed, and does not have anything to do with the shape of the separated zones.

name: electrophoresis , starch gel
query: Query: electrophoresis , starch gel [SEP] [MASK] gel electrophoresis is electrophoresis in which a [MASK] gel (a mixture of amylose and amylopectin) is used as the diffusion medium.

name: element , ion , or isotope
query: Query: element , ion , or isotope [SEP] Or isotope ion element is element , ion , or isotope

name: eligibility determination
query: Query: eligibility determination [SEP] Eligibility determination is criteria to determine eligibility of patients for medical care programs and services.

name: embolism , air
query: Query: embolism , air [SEP] Air embolism is blocking of a blood vessel by air bubbles that enter the circulatory system, usually after trauma; surgical procedures, or changes in atmospheric pressure.

name: embryo , mammalian
query: Query: embryo , mammalian [SEP] Mammalian embryo is the entity of a developing mammal (mammals), generally from the cleavage of a zygote to the end of embryonic differentiation of basic structures. For the human embryo, this represents the first two months of intrauterine development preceding the stages of the fetus.

name: embryo culture techniques
query: Query: embryo culture techniques [SEP] Embryo culture techniques is the technique of maintaining or growing mammalian embryos in vitro. This method offers an opportunity to observe embryonic development; metabolism; and susceptibility to teratogens.

name: embryo loss
query: Query: embryo loss [SEP] Embryo loss is early pregnancy loss during the embryo, mammalian stage of development. In the human, this period comprises the second through eighth week after fertilization.

name: embryonic germ cells
query: Query: embryonic germ cells [SEP] Embryonic germ cells is pluripotent stem cells that are derived from early germ cells.

name: embryonic induction
query: Query: embryonic induction [SEP] Embryonic induction is the complex processes of initiating cell differentiation in the embryo. The precise regulation by cell interactions leads to diversity of cell types and specific pattern of organization (embryogenesis).

name: embryonic structure
query: Query: embryonic structure [SEP] Embryonic structure is the anatomical parts that make up an organism in the early stages of development.

name: emergency medical dispatch
query: Query: emergency medical dispatch [SEP] Emergency medical dispatch is the mobilization of emergency care to the locations and people that need them.

name: emergency medical service communication systems
query: Query: emergency medical service communication systems [SEP] Emergency medical service communication systems is the use of communication systems, such as telecommunication, to transmit emergency information to appropriate providers of health services.

name: emergency nursing
query: Query: emergency nursing [SEP] Emergency nursing is the specialty or practice of nursing in the care of patients admitted to the emergency department.

name: emergency services , psychiatric
query: Query: emergency services , psychiatric [SEP] Psychiatric emergency services is organized services to provide immediate psychiatric care to patients with acute psychological disturbances.

name: emotional adjustment
query: Query: emotional adjustment [SEP] Emotional [MASK] is psychological process that occurs when an individual adapts to a significant emotional event or stimulus.

name: emotional regulation
query: Query: emotional regulation [SEP] Emotional regulation is the manifestation of an emotional response by which individuals influence the intensity, duration, valence, or manifestation of their response. Emotion regulation either precedes (avoidance, interpretation) or follows an emotion (suppression, reappraisal). Emotion regulation is distinct from coping (focuses primarily on decreasing a negative emotional experience), and can include increasing or decreasing both positive and negative emotions consciously or unconsciously.

name: employee incentive plans
query: Query: employee incentive plans [SEP] Employee incentive plans is programs designed by management to motivate employees to work more efficiently with increased productivity, and greater employee [MASK].

name: employer health costs
query: Query: employer health costs [SEP] Employer health costs is that portion of total health care costs borne by an individual's or group's employing organization.

name: employment , supported
query: Query: employment , supported [SEP] Supported employment is paid work for mentally or physically disabled persons, taking place in regular or normal work settings. It may be competitive employment (work that pays minimum wage) or employment with subminimal wages in individualized or group placement situations. It is intended for persons with severe disabilities who require a range of support services to maintain employment. Supported employment differs from sheltered workshops in that work in the latter takes place in a controlled working environment. Federal regulations are authorized and administered by the u.s. Department of Education, Office of Special Education and Rehabilitative Services.

name: empowerment
query: Query: empowerment [SEP] Empowerment is process of increasing the capacity of individuals or groups to make choices and to transform those choices into desired actions as deigned by the individuals or groups.

name: enamel organ
query: Query: enamel organ [SEP] Enamel organ is epithelial cells surrounding the dental papilla and differentiated into three layers: the inner enamel epithelium, consisting of ameloblasts which eventually form the enamel, and the enamel pulp and external enamel epithelium, both of which atrophy and disappear before and upon eruption of the tooth, respectively.

name: encephalitis , herpes simplex
query: Query: encephalitis , herpes simplex [SEP] Herpes simplex encephalitis is an acute (or rarely chronic) inflammatory process of the brain caused by simplexvirus infections which may be fatal. The majority of infections are caused by human herpesvirus 1 (herpesvirus 1, human) and less often by human herpesvirus 2 (herpesvirus 2, human). Clinical manifestations include fever; headache; seizures; hallucinations; behavioral alterations; aphasia; hemiparesis; and coma. Pathologically, the condition is marked by a hemorrhagic necrosis involving the medial and inferior temporal lobe and orbital regions of the frontal lobe. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp751-4)

name: encephalitis virus , california
query: Query: encephalitis virus , california [SEP] California encephalitis virus is a species in the orthobunyavirus genus of the family bunyaviridae. Serotypes are found in temperate and arctic regions and each is closely associated with a single species of vector mosquito. The vertebrate hosts are usually small mammals but several serotypes infect humans.

name: encephalitis virus , japanese
query: Query: encephalitis virus , japanese [SEP] Japanese encephalitis virus is a species of flavivirus, one of the Japanese encephalitis virus group (encephalitis viruses, japanese), which is the etiological agent of Japanese encephalitis found in Asia, southeast Asia, and the Indian subcontinent.

name: encephalitis virus , murray valley
query: Query: encephalitis virus , murray valley [SEP] Murray valley encephalitis virus is a species of flavivirus, one of the Japanese encephalitis virus group (encephalitis viruses, japanese), found in Australia and [MASK]. It causes a fulminating viremia resembling Japanese encephalitis (encephalitis, japanese).

name: endometrial ablation techniques
query: Query: endometrial ablation techniques [SEP] Endometrial ablation techniques is procedures used for the targeted destruction of the mucous membrane lining of the uterine cavity.

name: endometrial hyperplasia
query: Query: endometrial hyperplasia [SEP] Endometrial hyperplasia is benign proliferation of the endometrium in the uterus. Endometrial hyperplasia is classified by its cytology and glandular tissue. There are simple, complex (adenomatous without atypia), and atypical hyperplasia representing also the ascending risk of becoming malignant.

name: endometriosis
query: Query: endometriosis [SEP] Endometriosis is a condition in which functional endometrial tissue is present outside the uterus. It is often confined to the pelvis involving the ovary, the ligaments, cul-de-sac, and the uterovesical peritoneum.

name: endoplasmic reticulum , rough
query: Query: endoplasmic reticulum , rough [SEP] Rough endoplasmic reticulum is a type of endoplasmic reticulum (er) where polyribosomes are present on the cytoplasmic surfaces of the er membranes. This form of er is prominent in cells specialized for protein secretion and its principal function is to segregate proteins destined for export or intracellular utilization.

name: endoplasmic reticulum , smooth
query: Query: endoplasmic reticulum , smooth [SEP] Smooth endoplasmic reticulum is a type of endoplasmic reticulum lacking associated ribosomes on the membrane surface. It exhibits a wide range of specialized metabolic functions including supplying enzymes for steroid synthesis, detoxification, and glycogen breakdown. In muscle cells, smooth endoplasmic reticulum is called sarcoplasmic reticulum.

name: endoplasmic reticulum stress
query: Query: endoplasmic reticulum stress [SEP] Endoplasmic reticulum stress is various physiological or molecular disturbances that impair endoplasmic reticulum function. It triggers many responses, including unfolded protein response, which may lead to apoptosis; and [MASK].

name: endoscopy , digestive system
query: Query: endoscopy , digestive system [SEP] Digestive system endoscopy is endoscopic examination, therapy or surgery of the digestive tract.

name: endothelial growth factors
query: Query: endothelial growth factors [SEP] Endothelial growth factors is these growth factors are soluble mitogens secreted by a variety of organs. The factors are a mixture of two single chain polypeptides which have affinity to heparin. Their molecular weight are organ and species dependent. They have mitogenic and chemotactic effects and can stimulate endothelial cells to grow and synthesize dna. The factors are related to both the basic and acidic fibroblast growth factors but have different amino acid sequences.

name: endothelial protein c receptor
query: Query: endothelial protein c receptor [SEP] Endothelial protein c receptor is a glycosylated transmembrane receptor for protein c that is highly expressed by endothelial cells on the surface of large blood vessels in the heart and lungs.  It facilitates protein c activation by the thrombin and thrombomodulin complex in blood coagulation.

name: endothelium , vascular
query: Query: endothelium , vascular [SEP] Vascular endothelium is single pavement layer of cells which line the luminal surface of the entire vascular system and regulate the transport of macromolecules and blood components.

name: endurance training
query: Query: endurance training [SEP] Endurance training is exercise programs of relatively long duration and moderate intensity, which enhance maximal oxygen uptake, increasing physical stamina.

name: energy drinks
query: Query: energy drinks [SEP] Energy drinks is beverages that contain stimulants such as a combination of caffeine with other substances such as vitamins; amino acids; and sugar or sugar derivatives.

name: energy intake
query: Query: energy intake [SEP] Energy intake is total number of calories taken in daily whether ingested or by parenteral routes.

name: english abstract
query: Query: english abstract [SEP] English [MASK] is identifier for English language [MASK] provided with non-English language works.

name: enhanced recovery after surgery
query: Query: enhanced recovery after surgery [SEP] Enhanced recovery after surgery is a protocol of components related to preadmission, preoperative, intraoperative, and postoperative care. The protocol is implemented with the goal of improving patient recovery, facilitating earlier discharge from the hospital, and potentially reducing health care costs without increasing complications or hospital readmissions. The protocol components may contribute to minimizing, and/or improving the response to, physiological stress associated with surgery.

name: enteric nervous system
query: Query: enteric nervous system [SEP] Enteric nervous system is two ganglionated neural plexuses in the gut wall which form one of the three major divisions of the autonomic nervous system. The enteric nervous system innervates the gastrointestinal tract, the pancreas, and the gallbladder. It contains sensory neurons, interneurons, and motor neurons. Thus the circuitry can autonomously sense the tension and the chemical environment in the gut and regulate blood vessel tone, motility, secretions, and fluid transport. The system is itself governed by the central nervous system and receives both parasympathetic and sympathetic innervation. (From Kandel, Schwartz, and Jessel, Principles of Neural Science, 3d ed, p766)

name: environmental biomarkers
query: Query: environmental biomarkers [SEP] Environmental biomarkers is a factor associated with the well-being of living organisms that is used as a measure of environmental change and or influence. For example, aldehyde dehydrogenase expression in earthworm tissue is used as an indication of heavy metal pollution in soils. Distinguish from biomarkers.

name: environmental dna
query: Query: environmental dna [SEP] Environmental dna is dna found in the environment that is from the residual biological materials of the organisms in the environment.

name: environmental indicators
query: Query: environmental indicators [SEP] Environmental indicators is data related to climate change, [MASK], eutrophication, acidification, toxic contamination, urban environmental quality, biodiversity, cultural landscapes, waste, water resources, forest resources, fish resources, and soil degradation including desertification and erosion. (from https://www.oecd.org/env/indicators-modelling-outlooks/37551205.pdfc).

name: environmental policy
query: Query: environmental policy [SEP] Environmental policy is a course of action or principle adopted or proposed by a government, party, business, or individual that concerns human interactions with nature and natural resources.

name: environmental psychology
query: Query: environmental psychology [SEP] Environmental psychology is the field that studies interactions between individuals and the built and natural environment. It includes investigating behaviors that inhibit or foster sustainable, climate-healthy, and nature-enhancing choices.

name: enzyme
query: Query: enzyme [SEP] Enzyme is biological molecules that possess catalytic activity. They may occur naturally or be synthetically created. Enzymes are usually proteins, however catalytic RNA and [MASK] molecules have also been identified.

name: enzyme activation
query: Query: enzyme activation [SEP] Enzyme activation is conversion of an inactive form of an enzyme to one possessing metabolic activity. It includes 1, activation by ions (activators); 2, activation by cofactors (coenzymes); and 3, conversion of an enzyme precursor (proenzyme or zymogen) to an active enzyme.

name: enzymes , immobilized
query: Query: enzymes , immobilized [SEP] Immobilized enzymes is enzymes which are immobilized on or in a variety of water-soluble or water-insoluble matrices with little or no loss of their catalytic activity. Since they can be reused continuously, immobilized enzymes have found wide application in the industrial, medical and research fields.

name: epidemiological monitoring
query: Query: epidemiological monitoring [SEP] Epidemiological monitoring is collection, analysis, and interpretation of data about the frequency, distribution, and consequences of disease or health conditions, for use in the planning, implementing, and evaluating public health programs.

name: epidermal growth factor
query: Query: epidermal growth factor [SEP] Epidermal growth factor is a 6-kDa polypeptide growth factor initially discovered in mouse submaxillary glands. Human epidermal growth factor was originally isolated from urine based on its ability to inhibit gastric secretion and called urogastrone. Epidermal growth factor exerts a wide variety of biological effects including the promotion of proliferation and differentiation of mesenchymal and epithelial cells. It is synthesized as a transmembrane protein which can be cleaved to release a soluble active form.

name: epidural abscess
query: Query: epidural abscess [SEP] Epidural abscess is circumscribed collections of suppurative material occurring in the spinal or intracranial [MASK]. The majority of epidural abscesses occur in the spinal canal and are associated with osteomyelitis of a vertebral body; analgesia, epidural; and other conditions. Clinical manifestations include local and radicular pain, weakness, sensory loss, urinary incontinence, and [MASK]. Cranial epidural abscesses are usually associated with osteomyelitis of a cranial bone, sinusitis, or otitis media. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p710 and pp1240-1; j Neurol Neurosurg Psychiatry 1998 Aug;65(2):209-12)

name: epidural neoplasms
query: Query: epidural neoplasms [SEP] Epidural neoplasms is neoplasms located in the space between the vertebral periosteum and dura mater surrounding the spinal cord. Tumors in this location are most often metastatic in origin and may cause neurologic deficits by mass effect on the spinal cord or nerve roots or by interfering with blood supply to the spinal cord.

name: epilepsy , absence
query: Query: epilepsy , absence [SEP] Absence epilepsy is a seizure disorder usually occurring in childhood characterized by rhythmic electrical brain discharges of generalized onset. Clinical features include a sudden cessation of ongoing activity usually without loss of postural tone. Rhythmic blinking of the eyelids or [MASK] smacking frequently accompanies the seizures. The usual duration is 5-10 seconds, and multiple episodes may occur daily. Juvenile absence epilepsy is characterized by the juvenile onset of absence seizures and an increased incidence of myoclonus and tonic-clonic seizures. (Menkes, Textbook of Child Neurology, 5th ed, p736)

name: epilepsy , benign neonatal
query: Query: epilepsy , benign neonatal [SEP] Benign neonatal epilepsy is a condition marked by recurrent seizures that occur during the first 4-6 weeks of life despite an otherwise benign neonatal course. Autosomal dominant familial and sporadic forms have been identified. Seizures generally consist of brief episodes of tonic posturing and other movements, apnea, eye deviations, and blood pressure fluctuations. These tend to remit after the 6th week of life. The risk of developing epilepsy at an older age is moderately increased in the familial form of this disorder. (Neurologia 1996 Feb;11(2):51-5)

name: epilepsy , frontal lobe
query: Query: epilepsy , frontal lobe [SEP] Frontal lobe epilepsy is a localization-related (focal) form of epilepsy characterized by seizures which arise in the frontal lobe.

name: epilepsy , reflex
query: Query: epilepsy , reflex [SEP] Reflex epilepsy is a subtype of epilepsy characterized by seizures that are consistently provoked by a certain specific stimulus. Auditory, visual, and somatosensory stimuli as well as the acts of writing, reading, eating, and decision making are examples of events or activities that may induce seizure activity in affected individuals. (From Neurol Clin 1994 Feb;12(1):57-8)

name: episode of care
query: Query: episode of care [SEP] Episode of care is an interval of care by a health care facility or provider for a specific medical problem or condition. It may be continuous or it may consist of a series of intervals marked by one or more brief separations from care, and can also identify the sequence of care (e.g., emergency, inpatient, outpatient), thus serving as one measure of health care provided.

name: epithelial cell adhesion molecule
query: Query: epithelial cell adhesion molecule [SEP] Epithelial cell adhesion molecule is a cell adhesion molecule that is expressed on the membranes of nearly all epithelial cells, especially at the junctions between intestinal epithelial cells and intraepithelial lymphocytes. It also is expressed on the surface of adenocarcinoma and epithelial tumor cells.  It may function in the mucosa through homophilic interactions to provide a barrier against infection. It also regulates the proliferation and differentiation of embryonic stem cells.

name: epithelial sodium channel blockers
query: Query: epithelial sodium channel blockers [SEP] [MASK] blockers is a subclass of sodium channel blockers that are specific for [MASK].

name: epithelium , corneal
query: Query: epithelium , corneal [SEP] Corneal epithelium is stratified squamous epithelium that covers the outer surface of the cornea. It is smooth and contains many free nerve endings.

name: epitopes
query: Query: epitopes [SEP] Epitopes is sites on an antigen that interact with specific antibodies.

name: equatorial guinea
query: Query: equatorial guinea [SEP] Equatorial [MASK] is a republic in central Africa, bordering the Bay of Biafra, cameroon is to the north and gabon to the south. Its capital is Malabo.

name: equipment reuse
query: Query: equipment reuse [SEP] Equipment reuse is further or repeated use of equipment, instruments, devices, or materials. It includes additional use regardless of the original intent of the producer as to disposability or durability. It does not include the repeated use of fluids or solutions.

name: equivalence trial
query: Query: equivalence trial [SEP] Equivalence trial is trial that aims to show a new treatment is no better and no worse than the standard treatment.

name: equivalence trials as topic
query: Query: equivalence trials as topic [SEP] Equivalence trials as topic is works about trials that aim to show a new treatment is no better and no worse than the standard treatment.

name: erythrocyte aggregation
query: Query: erythrocyte aggregation [SEP] Erythrocyte aggregation is the formation of clumps of red blood cells under low or non-flow conditions, resulting from the attraction forces between the red blood cells. The cells adhere to each other in rouleaux aggregates. Slight mechanical force, such as occurs in the circulation, is enough to disperse these aggregates. Stronger or weaker than normal aggregation may result from a variety of effects in the erythrocyte membrane or in blood plasma. The degree of aggregation is affected by erythrocyte deformability, erythrocyte membrane sialylation, masking of negative surface charge by plasma proteins, etc. blood [MASK] and the erythrocyte sedimentation rate are affected by the amount of erythrocyte aggregation and are parameters used to measure the aggregation.

name: erythrocyte aging
query: Query: erythrocyte aging [SEP] Erythrocyte aging is the senescence of red blood cells. Lacking the organelles that make protein synthesis possible, the mature erythrocyte is incapable of self-repair, reproduction, and carrying out certain functions performed by other cells. This limits the average life span of an erythrocyte to 120 days.

name: erythrocyte count
query: Query: erythrocyte count [SEP] Erythrocyte count is the number of red blood cells per unit volume in a sample of venous blood.

name: erythrocyte inclusions
query: Query: erythrocyte inclusions [SEP] Erythrocyte inclusions is pathologic inclusions occurring in erythrocytes.

name: erythrocyte indices
query: Query: erythrocyte indices [SEP] Erythrocyte indices is erythrocyte size and hemoglobin content or concentration, usually derived from erythrocyte count; blood hemoglobin concentration; and hematocrit. The indices include the mean corpuscular volume (mcv), the mean corpuscular hemoglobin (mch), and the mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration (mchc).

name: erythrocyte membrane
query: Query: erythrocyte membrane [SEP] Erythrocyte membrane is the semi-permeable outer structure of a red blood cell. It is known as a red cell 'ghost' after hemolysis.

name: erythrocyte volume
query: Query: erythrocyte volume [SEP] Erythrocyte volume is volume of circulating erythrocytes . It is usually measured by radioisotope dilution technique.

name: escape reaction
query: Query: escape reaction [SEP] Escape reaction is innate response elicited by sensory stimuli associated with a threatening situation, or actual confrontation with an enemy.

name: escherichia coli
query: Query: escherichia coli [SEP] Escherichia coli is a species of gram-negative, facultatively anaerobic, rod-shaped bacteria (gram-negative facultatively anaerobic rods) commonly found in the lower part of the intestine of warm-blooded animals. It is usually nonpathogenic, but some strains are known to produce [MASK] and pyogenic infections. Pathogenic strains (virotypes) are classified by their specific pathogenic mechanisms such as toxins (enterotoxigenic escherichia coli), etc.

name: escherichia coli proteins
query: Query: escherichia coli proteins [SEP] Escherichia coli proteins is proteins obtained from escherichia coli.

name: escherichia coli vaccines
query: Query: escherichia coli vaccines [SEP] Escherichia coli vaccines is vaccines or candidate vaccines used to prevent or treat both enterotoxigenic and enteropathogenic Escherichia coli infections.

name: esophageal cyst
query: Query: esophageal cyst [SEP] Esophageal cyst is any fluid-filled closed cavity or sac (cysts) that is lined by an epithelium and found in the esophagus region.

name: esophageal fistula
query: Query: esophageal fistula [SEP] Esophageal fistula is abnormal passage communicating with the esophagus. The most common type is tracheoesophageal fistula between the esophagus and the [MASK].

name: esophageal mucosa
query: Query: esophageal mucosa [SEP] Esophageal mucosa is circular innermost layer of the esophagus wall that mediates esophageal peristalsis which pushes ingested food bolus toward the stomach.

name: esophageal perforation
query: Query: esophageal perforation [SEP] Esophageal perforation is an opening or hole in the esophagus that is caused by trauma, injury, or pathological process.

name: esophageal ph monitoring
query: Query: esophageal ph monitoring [SEP] Esophageal ph monitoring is analysis of the hydrogen ion concentration in the lumen of the esophagus. It is used to record the pattern, frequency, and duration of gastroesophageal reflux.

name: esophageal sphincter , lower
query: Query: esophageal sphincter , lower [SEP] Lower esophageal sphincter is the physiologic or functional barrier to gastroesophageal reflux at the esophagogastric junction. Sphincteric muscles remain tonically contracted during the resting state and form the high-pressure zone separating the lumen of the esophagus from that of the stomach. (Haubrich et al, Bockus Gastroenterology, 5th ed., pp399, 415)

name: esophageal sphincter , upper
query: Query: esophageal sphincter , upper [SEP] Upper esophageal sphincter is the structure at the pharyngoesophageal junction consisting chiefly of the cricopharyngeus muscle. It normally occludes the lumen of the esophagus, except during swallowing.

name: esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
query: Query: esophageal squamous cell carcinoma [SEP] Esophageal squamous cell carcinoma is a carcinoma that originates usually from cells on the surface of the middle and lower third of the esophagus. Tumor cells exhibit typical squamous morphology and form large polypoid lesions. Mutations in rnf6, lzts1, tgfbr2, dec1, and wwox1 genes are associated with this cancer.

name: esophageal stenosis
query: Query: esophageal stenosis [SEP] Esophageal stenosis is a stricture of the esophagus. Most are acquired but can be congenital.

name: essay
query: Query: essay [SEP] Essay is short literary prose composition, usually dealing with a single theme.

name: essential tremor
query: Query: essential tremor [SEP] Essential tremor is a relatively common disorder characterized by a fairly specific pattern of tremors which are most prominent in the upper extremities and [MASK], inducing titubations of the head. The tremor is usually mild, but when severe may be disabling. An autosomal dominant pattern of inheritance may occur in some families (i.e., familial tremor). (Mov Disord 1988;13(1):5-10)

name: esters
query: Query: esters [SEP] Esters is compounds derived from organic or inorganic acids in which at least one hydroxyl group is replaced by an –O-alkyl or other organic group. They can be represented by the structure formula rcoor’ and are usually formed by the reaction between an acid and an alcohol with elimination of water.

name: estrogen replacement therapy
query: Query: estrogen replacement therapy [SEP] Estrogen replacement therapy is the use of hormonal agents with estrogen-like activity in postmenopausal or other estrogen-deficient women to alleviate effects of hormone deficiency, such as vasomotor symptoms, dyspareunia, and progressive development of osteoporosis. This may also include the use of progestational agents in combination therapy.

name: ethical theory
query: Query: ethical theory [SEP] Ethical theory is a philosophically coherent [MASK] of propositions (for example, utilitarianism) which attempts to provide general norms for the guidance and evaluation of moral conduct. (from Beauchamp and Childress, Principles of Biomedical Ethics, 4th ed)

name: ethics , business
query: Query: ethics , business [SEP] Business ethics is the moral obligations governing the conduct of commercial or industrial enterprises.

name: ethics , dental
query: Query: ethics , dental [SEP] Dental ethics is the principles of proper professional conduct concerning the rights and duties of the dentist, relations with patients and fellow practitioners, as well as actions of the dentist in patient care and interpersonal relations with patient families. (From Stedman, 25th ed)

name: ethics , medical
query: Query: ethics , medical [SEP] Medical ethics is the principles of professional conduct concerning the rights and duties of the physician, relations with patients and fellow practitioners, as well as actions of the physician in patient care and interpersonal relations with patient families.

name: ethics , nursing
query: Query: ethics , nursing [SEP] Nursing ethics is the principles of proper professional conduct concerning the rights and duties of nurses themselves, their patients, and their fellow practitioners, as well as their actions in the care of patients and in relations with their families.

name: ethics , pharmacy
query: Query: ethics , pharmacy [SEP] Pharmacy ethics is the principles of proper professional conduct concerning the rights and duties of the pharmacist, relations with patients and fellow practitioners, as well as actions of the pharmacist in health care and interpersonal relations with patient families. (From Stedman, 25th ed)

name: ethics committees , clinical
query: Query: ethics committees , clinical [SEP] Clinical ethics committees is hospital or other [MASK] committees established to consider the ethical dimensions of patient care. Distinguish from ethics committees, research, which are established to monitor the welfare of patients or [MASK] participating in research studies.

name: ethics committees , research
query: Query: ethics committees , research [SEP] Research ethics committees is hospital or other institutional committees established to protect the welfare of research subjects. Federal regulations (the "Common Rule" (45 cfr 46)) mandate the use of these committees to monitor federally-funded biomedical and behavioral research involving human subjects.

name: ethics consultation
query: Query: ethics consultation [SEP] Ethics consultation is services provided by an individual ethicist (ethicists) or an ethics team or committee (ethics committees, clinical) to address the ethical issues involved in a specific clinical case. The central purpose is to improve the process and outcomes of patients' care by helping to identify, analyze, and resolve ethical problems.

name: ethiopia
query: Query: ethiopia [SEP] Ethiopia is an independent state in eastern Africa. Ethiopia is located in the Horn of Africa and is bordered on the north and northeast by Eritrea, on the east by Djibouti and Somalia, on the south by Kenya, and on the west and southwest by Sudan. Its capital is Addis Ababa.

name: ethnic violence
query: Query: ethnic violence [SEP] Ethnic violence is violence or other hostile behavior arising when an ethnic group either feels itself under threat, or where it seeks to assert its superiority or dominance over other groups.

name: eukaryotic cells
query: Query: eukaryotic cells [SEP] Eukaryotic cells is cells of the higher organisms, containing a true nucleus bounded by a nuclear membrane.

name: eukaryotic initiation factors
query: Query: eukaryotic initiation factors [SEP] Eukaryotic initiation factors is peptide initiation factors from eukaryotic organisms. Over twelve factors are involved in peptide chain initiation, translational in eukaryotic cells. Many of these factors play a role in controlling the rate of mrna translation.

name: european union
query: Query: european union [SEP] European union is the collective designation of three organizations with common membership: the European Economic Community (Common Market), the European Coal and Steel Community, and the European Atomic Energy Community (Euratom). It was known as the European Community until 1994. It is primarily an economic union with the principal objectives of free movement of goods, capital, and labor. Professional services, social, medical and paramedical, are subsumed under labor. The constituent countries are Austria, [MASK], Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Greece, Ireland, Italy, Luxembourg, [MASK], Portugal, [MASK], Sweden, and the United Kingdom. (The World Almanac and Book of Facts 1997, p842)

name: evaluation study
query: Query: evaluation study [SEP] Evaluation study is works consisting of studies determining the effectiveness or utility of processes, personnel, and equipment.

name: evoked potentials , auditory , brain stem
query: Query: evoked potentials , auditory , brain stem [SEP] Brain stem auditory evoked potentials is electrical waves in the cerebral cortex generated by brain stem structures in response to auditory click stimuli. These are found to be abnormal in many patients with cerebellopontine angle lesions, multiple [MASK], or other demyelinating diseases.

name: evoked potentials , motor
query: Query: evoked potentials , motor [SEP] Motor evoked potentials is the electrical response evoked in a muscle or motor nerve by electrical or magnetic stimulation. Common methods of stimulation are by transcranial electrical and transcranial magnetic stimulation. It is often used for monitoring during neurosurgery.

name: evoked potentials , somatosensory
query: Query: evoked potentials , somatosensory [SEP] Somatosensory evoked potentials is the electric response evoked in the cerebral cortex by stimulation along afferent pathways from peripheral nerves to cerebrum.

name: evolution , chemical
query: Query: evolution , chemical [SEP] Chemical evolution is chemical and physical transformation of the biogenic elements from their nucleosynthesis in stars to their incorporation and subsequent modification in planetary bodies and terrestrial biochemistry. It includes the mechanism of incorporation of biogenic elements into complex molecules and molecular systems, leading up to the origin of life.

name: examination questions
query: Query: examination questions [SEP] Examination questions is work consisting of compilations of questions and answers pertaining to a particular subject, used for study and review.

name: examination tables
query: Query: examination tables [SEP] Examination [MASK] is a raised flat surface on which a patient is placed during a physical examination.

name: exchange transfusion , whole blood
query: Query: exchange transfusion , whole blood [SEP] Whole blood exchange transfusion is repetitive withdrawal of small amounts of blood and replacement with donor blood until a large proportion of the blood volume has been exchanged. Used in treatment of fetal erythroblastosis, hepatic coma, sickle cell anemia, disseminated intravascular coagulation, septicemia, burns, thrombotic thrombopenic purpura, and fulminant malaria.

name: excitation contraction coupling
query: Query: excitation contraction coupling [SEP] Excitation contraction coupling is a process fundamental to muscle physiology whereby an electrical stimulus or action potential triggers a myocyte to depolarize and contract. This mechanical muscle contraction response is regulated by entry of calcium ions into the cell.

name: excitatory amino acid agonists
query: Query: excitatory amino acid agonists [SEP] [MASK] agonists is drugs that bind to and activate [MASK].

name: excitatory amino acid transporter 1
query: Query: excitatory amino acid transporter 1 [SEP] [MASK] transporter 1 is a glial type glutamate plasma membrane transporter protein found predominately in astrocytes. It is also expressed in heart and skeletal muscle and in the placenta.

name: excitatory amino acid transporter 4
query: Query: excitatory amino acid transporter 4 [SEP] [MASK] transporter 4 is a glutamate plasma membrane transporter protein that is primarily expressed in cerebellar purkinje cells on postsynaptic dendritic spines.
