name: excitatory postsynaptic potentials
query: Query: excitatory postsynaptic potentials [SEP] Excitatory postsynaptic potentials is depolarization of membrane potentials at the synaptic membranes of target neurons during neurotransmission. Excitatory postsynaptic potentials can singly or in summation reach the trigger threshold for action potentials.

name: executive function
query: Query: executive function [SEP] Executive function is a [MASK] of cognitive functions that controls complex, goal-directed thought and behavior. Executive function involves multiple domains, such as concept formation, goal management, cognitive flexibility, inhibition control, and working memory. Impaired executive function is seen in a range of disorders, e.g., schizophrenia; and adhd.

name: exercise tolerance
query: Query: exercise tolerance [SEP] Exercise tolerance is the exercise capacity of an individual as measured by endurance (maximal exercise duration and/or maximal attained work load) during an exercise test.

name: exosomes
query: Query: exosomes [SEP] Exosomes is a type of extracellular vesicle, containing rna and proteins, that is secreted into the extracellular space by exocytosis when multivesicular bodies fuse with the plasma membrane.

name: experimental model of disease
query: Query: experimental model of disease [SEP] Experimental model of disease is experimental model of disease

name: expiratory reserve volume
query: Query: expiratory reserve volume [SEP] Expiratory reserve volume is the extra volume of air that can be expired with maximum effort beyond the level reached at the end of a normal, quiet expiration. Common abbreviation is erv.

name: exploratory behavior
query: Query: exploratory behavior [SEP] Exploratory behavior is the tendency to explore or investigate a novel environment. It is considered a motivation not clearly distinguishable from curiosity.

name: exposure to violence
query: Query: exposure to violence [SEP] Exposure to violence is experience of and exposure to violence.

name: expressed emotion
query: Query: expressed emotion [SEP] Expressed emotion is a measurement of collective behavior and attitudes that exist towards a specific person—a measurement of the social environment or social relationships of an individual.

name: expression of concern
query: Query: expression of concern [SEP] Expression of concern is a notification about the integrity of a published article that is typically written by an editor and should be labelled prominently in the item title. It is the responsibility of the editor to initiate appropriate investigative procedures, discover the outcome of the investigation, and notify readers of that outcome in a subsequent published item. The outcome may require the publication of a retraction notice.

name: external debt
query: Query: external debt [SEP] External debt is money owed to creditors outside of a country.

name: extinction , psychological
query: Query: extinction , psychological [SEP] Psychological extinction is the procedure of presenting the conditioned stimulus without reinforcement to an organism previously conditioned. It refers also to the diminution of a conditioned response resulting from this procedure.

name: extracellular polymeric substance matrix
query: Query: extracellular polymeric substance matrix [SEP] Extracellular polymeric substance matrix is extracellular matrix formed by secreted polymeric organic compounds by microorganisms. This secreted compound is mostly polysaccharides but may include proteins, lipids, and nucleic acids. The matrix facilitates attachment of microbes to form various biofilm communities.

name: extracellular traps
query: Query: extracellular traps [SEP] Extracellular traps is extracellular structure primarily composed of chromatin and associated proteases.

name: extreme heat
query: Query: extreme heat [SEP] Extreme heat is high temperature weather exceeding the average and of several weeks duration. Extreme heat is a dangerous situation that can bring on health emergencies in susceptible people.

name: extreme hot weather
query: Query: extreme hot weather [SEP] Extreme hot weather is a period of unusually high temperatures.

name: eye banks
query: Query: eye banks [SEP] Eye banks is centers for storing various parts of the eye for future use.

name: eye burns
query: Query: eye burns [SEP] Eye burns is injury to any part of the eye by extreme heat, chemical agents, or ultraviolet radiation.

name: eye foreign bodies
query: Query: eye foreign bodies [SEP] Eye foreign bodies is inanimate objects that become enclosed in the eye.

name: eye infections , fungal
query: Query: eye infections , fungal [SEP] Fungal eye infections is infection by a variety of fungi, usually through four possible mechanisms: superficial infection producing conjunctivitis, keratitis, or lacrimal obstruction; extension of infection from neighboring structures - skin, paranasal sinuses, nasopharynx; direct introduction during surgery or accidental penetrating trauma; or via the blood or lymphatic routes in patients with underlying mycoses.

name: eye infections , parasitic
query: Query: eye infections , parasitic [SEP] Parasitic eye infections is mild to severe infections of the eye and its adjacent structures (adnexa) by adult or larval protozoan or metazoan parasites.

name: eye injuries , penetrating
query: Query: eye injuries , penetrating [SEP] Penetrating eye injuries is deeply perforating or puncturing type intraocular injuries.

name: eye pain
query: Query: eye pain [SEP] Eye pain is a dull or sharp painful sensation associated with the outer or inner structures of the eyeball, having different causes.

name: eye protective devices
query: Query: eye protective devices [SEP] Eye protective devices is personal devices for protection of the eyes from impact, flying objects, glare, liquids, or injurious radiation.

name: eye proteins
query: Query: eye proteins [SEP] Eye proteins is proteins derived from tissues of the eye.

name: facial expression
query: Query: facial expression [SEP] Facial expression is observable changes of expression in the face in response to emotional stimuli.

name: facial neoplasms
query: Query: facial neoplasms [SEP] Facial neoplasms is new abnormal growth of tissue in the face.

name: facial nerve
query: Query: facial nerve [SEP] Facial nerve is the 7th cranial nerve. The facial nerve has two parts, the larger motor root which may be called the facial nerve proper, and the smaller intermediate or sensory root. Together they provide efferent innervation to the muscles of facial expression and to the lacrimal and salivary glands, and convey afferent information for taste from the anterior two-thirds of the tongue and for touch from the external ear.

name: facial nerve injuries
query: Query: facial nerve injuries [SEP] Facial nerve injuries is traumatic injuries to the facial nerve. This may result in [MASK], decreased lacrimation and salivation, and loss of taste sensation in the anterior tongue. The nerve may regenerate and reform its original pattern of innervation, or regenerate aberrantly, resulting in inappropriate lacrimation in response to gustatory stimuli (e.g., "crocodile tears") and other syndromes.

name: facial pain
query: Query: facial pain [SEP] Facial pain is pain in the facial region including orofacial pain and craniofacial pain. Associated conditions include local inflammatory and neoplastic disorders and neuralgic syndromes involving the trigeminal, facial, and glossopharyngeal nerves. Conditions which feature recurrent or persistent facial pain as the primary manifestation of disease are referred to as facial pain syndromes.

name: facial recognition
query: Query: facial recognition [SEP] Facial recognition is ability to identify an individual from their facial features.

name: facilitated diffusion
query: Query: facilitated diffusion [SEP] Facilitated diffusion is the passive movement of molecules exceeding the rate expected by simple diffusion. No energy is expended in the process. It is achieved by the introduction of passively diffusing molecules to an enviroment or path that is more favorable to the movement of those molecules. Examples of facilitated diffusion are passive transport of hydrophilic substances across a lipid membrane through hydrophilic pores that traverse the membrane, and the sliding of a dna binding protein along a strand of dna.

name: facilities and services utilization
query: Query: facilities and services utilization [SEP] Facilities and services utilization is extent of use of facilities or services. It includes overuse and underuse.

name: factor analysis , statistical
query: Query: factor analysis , statistical [SEP] Statistical factor analysis is a [MASK] of statistical methods for analyzing the correlations among several variables in order to estimate the number of fundamental dimensions that underlie the observed data and to describe and measure those dimensions. It is used frequently in the development of scoring systems for rating scales and questionnaires.

name: factor ix
query: Query: factor ix [SEP] Factor ix is storage-stable blood coagulation factor acting in the intrinsic pathway of blood coagulation. Its activated form, IXa, forms a complex with factor viii and calcium on platelet factor 3 to activate factor x to Xa. Deficiency of factor ix results in hemophilia b (Christmas Disease).

name: factor v deficiency
query: Query: factor v deficiency [SEP] Factor v deficiency is a deficiency of blood coagulation factor v (known as proaccelerin or accelerator globulin or labile factor) leading to a rare hemorrhagic tendency known as Owren's disease or parahemophilia. It varies greatly in severity. Factor v deficiency is an autosomal recessive trait. (Dorland, 27th ed)

name: factor vii deficiency
query: Query: factor vii deficiency [SEP] [MASK] deficiency is an autosomal recessive characteristic or a coagulation disorder acquired in association with vitamin k deficiency. [MASK] is a Vitamin k dependent glycoprotein essential to the extrinsic pathway of coagulation.

name: factor viii
query: Query: factor viii [SEP] Factor viii is factor viii of blood coagulation. Antihemophilic factor that is part of the factor VIII/von Willebrand factor complex. Factor viii is produced in the liver and acts in the intrinsic pathway of blood coagulation. It serves as a cofactor in factor x activation and this action is markedly enhanced by small amounts of thrombin.

name: factor xa
query: Query: factor xa [SEP] Factor xa is activated form of factor x that participates in both the intrinsic and extrinsic pathways of blood coagulation. It catalyzes the conversion of prothrombin to thrombin in conjunction with other cofactors.

name: factor x deficiency
query: Query: factor x deficiency [SEP] Factor x deficiency is blood coagulation disorder usually inherited as an autosomal recessive trait, though it can be acquired. It is characterized by defective activity in both the intrinsic and extrinsic pathways, impaired thromboplastin time, and impaired prothrombin consumption.

name: factor xia
query: Query: factor xia [SEP] Factor xia is activated form of factor xi. In the intrinsic pathway, Factor xi is activated to XIa by factor XIIa in the presence of cofactor hmwk; (high molecular weight kininogen). Factor XIa then activates factor ix to factor IXa in the presence of calcium.

name: factor xii
query: Query: factor xii [SEP] Factor xii is stable blood coagulation factor activated by contact with the subendothelial surface of an injured vessel. Along with prekallikrein, it serves as the contact factor that initiates the intrinsic pathway of blood coagulation. Kallikrein activates factor xii to XIIa. Deficiency of factor xii, also called the Hageman trait, leads to increased incidence of thromboembolic disease. Mutations in the gene for factor xii that appear to increase factor xii amidolytic activity are associated with hereditary angioedema type iii.

name: factor xii deficiency
query: Query: factor xii deficiency [SEP] Factor xii deficiency is an absence or reduced level of blood coagulation factor xii. It normally occurs in the absence of patient or family history of hemorrhagic disorders and is marked by prolonged clotting time.

name: faculty , dental
query: Query: faculty , dental [SEP] Dental faculty is the teaching staff and members of the administrative staff having academic rank in a dental school.

name: faculty , nursing
query: Query: faculty , nursing [SEP] Nursing faculty is the teaching staff and members of the administrative staff having academic rank in a [MASK].

name: faculty , pharmacy
query: Query: faculty , pharmacy [SEP] Pharmacy faculty is teaching and administrative staff having academic rank in a [MASK] or department.

name: failed back surgery syndrome
query: Query: failed back surgery syndrome [SEP] Failed back surgery syndrome is a condition of persistent pain and discomfort in the back and the leg following lumbar surgery, often seen in patients enrolled in [MASK].

name: failure to rescue , health care
query: Query: failure to rescue , health care [SEP] Health care failure to rescue is inability to prevent a clinical deterioration resulting from a complication of an underlying medical condition or a complication of medical care. It implies that common risk factors for such a complication were not recognized in a timely manner or treated appropriately.

name: faith healing
query: Query: faith healing [SEP] Faith healing is the use of faith and spirit to cure disease.

name: false negative reactions
query: Query: false negative reactions [SEP] False negative reactions is negative test results in subjects who possess the attribute for which the test is conducted. The labeling of diseased persons as healthy when screening in the detection of disease. (Last, a Dictionary of Epidemiology, 2d ed)

name: false positive reactions
query: Query: false positive reactions [SEP] False positive reactions is positive test results in subjects who do not possess the attribute for which the test is conducted. The labeling of healthy persons as diseased when screening in the detection of disease. (Last, a Dictionary of Epidemiology, 2d ed)

name: family conflict
query: Query: family conflict [SEP] Family [MASK] is struggle or disagreement between parents, parent and child or other members of a family.

name: family group
query: Query: family group [SEP] Family group is a group of family doctors who work together and in close collaboration with other health and social services professionals.

name: family nurse practitioners
query: Query: family nurse practitioners [SEP] Family nurse practitioners is registered nurses with graduate degrees in nursing who provide care to patients of all age levels, and who focus their efforts on the health care needs of the entire family.

name: family planning policy
query: Query: family planning policy [SEP] Family planning policy is a course or method of action selected, usually by a government, to guide and determine present and future decisions on population control by limiting the number of children or controlling fertility, notably through family planning and contraception within the nuclear family.

name: family planning services
query: Query: family planning services [SEP] Family planning services is health care programs or services designed to assist individuals in the planning of family size. Various methods of contraception can be used to control the number and timing of childbirths.

name: family practice
query: Query: family practice [SEP] Family practice is a medical specialty concerned with the provision of continuing, comprehensive primary health care for the entire family.

name: family separation
query: Query: family separation [SEP] Family separation is geographic separation of members of a family.

name: family therapy
query: Query: family therapy [SEP] Family therapy is a form of group psychotherapy. It involves treatment of more than one member of the family simultaneously in the same session.

name: famous persons
query: Query: famous persons [SEP] Famous persons is individuals widely known or recognized.

name: farms
query: Query: farms [SEP] Farms is areas of land [MASK] aside to grow crops or raise livestock.

name: fas ligand protein
query: Query: fas ligand protein [SEP] Fas ligand protein is a transmembrane protein belonging to the tumor necrosis factor superfamily that was originally discovered on cells of the lymphoid-myeloid lineage, including activated t-lymphocytes and natural killer cells. It plays an important role in immune homeostasis and cell-mediated toxicity by binding to the fas receptor and triggering apoptosis.

name: fas receptor
query: Query: fas receptor [SEP] Fas receptor is a tumor necrosis factor receptor subtype found in a variety of tissues and on activated lymphocytes. It has specificity for fas ligand and plays a role in regulation of peripheral immune responses and apoptosis. Multiple isoforms of the protein exist due to multiple [MASK]. The activated receptor signals via a conserved death domain that associates with specific tnf receptor-associated factors in the cytoplasm. Mutations in the cd95 gene are associated with cases of autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome.

name: fasting
query: Query: fasting [SEP] Fasting is abstaining from food.

name: fat body
query: Query: fat body [SEP] Fat body is a nutritional reservoir of fatty tissue found mainly in insects and amphibians.

name: fatigue syndrome , chronic
query: Query: fatigue syndrome , chronic [SEP] Chronic fatigue syndrome is a syndrome characterized by persistent or recurrent fatigue, diffuse [MASK], sleep disturbances, and subjective cognitive impairment of 6 months duration or longer. Symptoms are not caused by ongoing exertion; are not relieved by rest; and result in a substantial reduction of previous levels of occupational, educational, social, or personal activities. Minor alterations of immune, neuroendocrine, and autonomic function may be associated with this syndrome. There is also considerable overlap between this condition and fibromyalgia. (From Semin Neurol 1998;18(2):237-42; Ann Intern Med 1994 Dec 15;121(12): 953-9)

name: fat necrosis
query: Query: fat necrosis [SEP] Fat necrosis is a condition in which the death of adipose tissue results in neutral fats being split into fatty acids and glycerol.

name: fat substitutes
query: Query: fat substitutes [SEP] Fat substitutes is compounds used in food or in food preparation to replace dietary fats. They may be carbohydrate-, protein-, or fat-based. Fat substitutes are usually lower in calories but provide the same texture as fats.

name: fatty acids , volatile
query: Query: fatty acids , volatile [SEP] Volatile fatty acids is short-chain fatty acids of up to six carbon atoms in length. They are the major end products of microbial fermentation in the ruminant digestive tract and have also been implicated in the causation of neurological diseases in humans.

name: fatty acid synthase , type i
query: Query: fatty acid synthase , type i [SEP] Type i fatty acid synthase is animal form of fatty acid synthase which is encoded by a single gene and consists of seven [MASK] and is functional as a homodimer. It is overexpressed in some neoplasms and is a target in humans of some antineoplastic agents and some anti-obesity agents.

name: fatty alcohols
query: Query: fatty alcohols [SEP] Fatty alcohols is usually high-molecular-weight, straight-chain primary alcohols, but can also range from as few as 4 carbons, derived from natural fats and oils, including lauryl, stearyl, oleyl, and linoleyl alcohols. They are used in pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, detergents, plastics, and lube oils and in textile manufacture. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 5th ed)

name: fecal microbiota transplantation
query: Query: fecal microbiota transplantation [SEP] Fecal microbiota transplantation is transfer of gastrointestinal microbiota from one individual to another by infusion of donor feces to the upper or lower gastrointestinal tract of the recipient.

name: feces
query: Query: feces [SEP] Feces is excrement from the intestines, containing unabsorbed solids, waste products, secretions, and bacteria of the digestive system.

name: feedback , sensory
query: Query: feedback , sensory [SEP] Sensory [MASK] is a mechanism of communicating one's own sensory system information about a task, movement or skill.

name: feeder cells
query: Query: feeder cells [SEP] Feeder cells is cells used in coculture techniques which support the growth of the other cells in the culture. Feeder cells provide auxillary substances including attachment substrates, nutrients, or other factors that are needed for growth in culture.

name: feeding and eating disorders of childhood
query: Query: feeding and eating disorders of childhood [SEP] Feeding and eating disorders of childhood is mental disorders related to feeding and eating usually diagnosed in infancy or early childhood.

name: fees , dental
query: Query: fees , dental [SEP] Dental fees is amounts charged to the patient as payer for dental services.

name: femoral neck fractures
query: Query: femoral neck fractures [SEP] Femoral [MASK] fractures is fractures of the short, constricted portion of the [MASK] bone between the femur head and the trochanters. It excludes intertrochanteric fractures which are hip fractures.

name: femoral vein
query: Query: femoral vein [SEP] Femoral vein is the vein accompanying the [MASK] in the same sheath; it is a continuation of the popliteal vein and becomes the external [MASK].

name: femur head
query: Query: femur head [SEP] Femur head is the hemispheric articular surface at the upper extremity of the [MASK] bone. (Stedman, 26th ed)

name: femur neck
query: Query: femur neck [SEP] Femur [MASK] is the constricted portion of the [MASK] bone between the femur head and the trochanters.

name: ferm domains
query: Query: ferm domains [SEP] Ferm domains is widely occuring protein domains that function to link signaling and cytoskeletal proteins to the plasma membrane. They occur mostly at the N-terminal region of proteins that contain them.

name: fermentation
query: Query: fermentation [SEP] Fermentation is anaerobic degradation of glucose or other organic nutrients to gain energy in the form of atp. End products vary depending on organisms, substrates, and enzymatic pathways. Common fermentation products include ethanol and lactic acid.

name: fertility agents , female
query: Query: fertility agents , female [SEP] Female fertility agents is compounds which increase the capacity to conceive in females.

name: fertility agents , male
query: Query: fertility agents , male [SEP] Male fertility agents is compounds which increase the capacity of the male to induce conception.

name: fertility preservation
query: Query: fertility preservation [SEP] Fertility preservation is a method of providing future reproductive opportunities before a medical treatment with known risk of loss of fertility. Typically reproductive organs or tissues (e.g., sperm, egg, embryos and ovarian or testicular tissues) are cryopreserved for future use before the medical treatment (e.g., chemotherapy, radiation) begins.

name: fetal alcohol spectrum disorders
query: Query: fetal alcohol spectrum disorders [SEP] Fetal alcohol spectrum disorders is an umbrella term used to describe a pattern of disabilities and abnormalities that result from fetal exposure to ethanol during pregnancy. It encompasses a phenotypic range that can vary greatly between individuals, but reliably includes one or more of the following: characteristic facial dysmorphism, fetal growth retardation, central nervous system abnormalities, cognitive and/or behavioral dysfunction, birth defects. The level of maternal alcohol consumption does not necessarily correlate directly with disease severity.

name: fetal distress
query: Query: fetal distress [SEP] Fetal distress is a nonreassuring fetal status (nrfs) indicating that the fetus is compromised (American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists 1988). It can be identified by sub-optimal values in fetal heart rate; oxygenation of [MASK]; and other parameters.

name: fetal growth retardation
query: Query: fetal growth retardation [SEP] Fetal growth retardation is failure of a fetus to attain expected growth.

name: fetal heart
query: Query: fetal heart [SEP] Fetal heart is the heart of the fetus of any viviparous animal. It refers to the heart in the postembryonic period and is differentiated from the embryonic heart (HEART/embryology) only on the basis of time.

name: fetal hypoxia
query: Query: fetal hypoxia [SEP] Fetal hypoxia is deficient oxygenation of [MASK].

name: fetal membranes , premature rupture
query: Query: fetal membranes , premature rupture [SEP] Premature rupture fetal membranes is spontaneous tearing of the membranes surrounding the fetus any time before the onset of obstetric labor. Preterm prom is membrane rupture before 37 weeks of gestation.

name: fetal mortality
query: Query: fetal mortality [SEP] Fetal mortality is number of fetal deaths with stated or presumed gestation of 20 weeks or more in a given population. Late fetal mortality is death after of 28 weeks or more.

name: fetal movement
query: Query: fetal movement [SEP] Fetal movement is physical activity of the fetus in utero. Gross or fine fetal body movement can be monitored by the mother, palpation, or ultrasonography.

name: fetal organ maturity
query: Query: fetal organ maturity [SEP] Fetal organ maturity is functional competence of specific organs or body systems of the fetus in utero.

name: fetal proteins
query: Query: fetal proteins [SEP] Fetal proteins is proteins that are preferentially expressed or upregulated during fetal development.

name: fetal tissue transplantation
query: Query: fetal tissue transplantation [SEP] Fetal tissue transplantation is transference of fetal tissue between individuals of the same species or between individuals of different species.

name: fetal viability
query: Query: fetal viability [SEP] Fetal viability is the potential of the fetus to survive outside the uterus after birth, natural or induced. Fetal viability depends largely on the fetal organ maturity, and environmental conditions.

name: fetal weight
query: Query: fetal weight [SEP] Fetal weight is the weight of the fetus in utero. It is usually estimated by various formulas based on measurements made during prenatal ultrasonography.

name: fever of unknown origin
query: Query: fever of unknown origin [SEP] Fever of unknown origin is fever in which the etiology cannot be ascertained.

name: f factor
query: Query: f factor [SEP] F factor is a plasmid whose presence in the cell, either extrachromosomal or integrated into the bacterial chromosome, determines the "[MASK]" of the bacterium, host chromosome mobilization, transfer via conjugation ([MASK]) of genetic material, and the formation of [MASK] pili.

name: fibrin clot lysis time
query: Query: fibrin clot lysis time [SEP] Fibrin clot lysis time is a measurement of the time needed for fibrinolysis to occur.

name: fibrin fibrinogen degradation products
query: Query: fibrin fibrinogen degradation products [SEP] Fibrin fibrinogen degradation products is soluble protein fragments formed by the proteolytic action of plasmin on fibrin or fibrinogen. fdp and their complexes profoundly impair the hemostatic process and are a major cause of hemorrhage in intravascular coagulation and fibrinolysis.

name: fibrin foam
query: Query: fibrin foam [SEP] Fibrin foam is a dry artificial sterile sponge of fibrin prepared by clotting with thrombin a foam or solution of fibrinogen. It is used in conjunction with thrombin as a hemostatic in surgery at sites where bleeding cannot be controlled by more common methods. (From Martindale, The Extra Pharmacopoeia, 30th ed, p648)

name: fibrin modulating agents
query: Query: fibrin modulating agents [SEP] Fibrin modulating agents is agents that affect the function of fibrin in blood coagulation. They used as coagulants for hemorrhage or anticoagulants for thrombosis.

name: fibrin tissue adhesive
query: Query: fibrin tissue adhesive [SEP] Fibrin tissue adhesive is an autologous or commercial tissue adhesive containing fibrinogen and thrombin. The commercial product is a two component system from human plasma that contains more than fibrinogen and thrombin. The first component contains highly concentrated fibrinogen, factor viii, fibronectin, and traces of other plasma proteins. The second component contains thrombin, calcium chloride, and antifibrinolytic agents such as aprotinin. Mixing of the two components promotes blood clotting and the formation and cross-linking of fibrin. The tissue adhesive is used for tissue sealing, hemostasis, and wound healing.

name: fibroblast growth factor 1
query: Query: fibroblast growth factor 1 [SEP] Fibroblast growth factor 1 is a 17-kDa single-chain polypeptide growth factor that plays a significant role in the process of wound healing and is a potent inducer of physiologic angiogenesis. It binds to heparin, which potentiates its biological activity and protects it from proteolysis. The growth factor is an extremely potent inducer of dna synthesis in a variety of cell types from mesoderm and neuroectoderm lineages, and also has chemotactic and mitogenic activities. It was originally named acidic fibroblast growth factor based upon its chemical properties and to distinguish it from basic fibroblast growth factor (fibroblast growth factor 2).

name: fibroblast growth factor 2
query: Query: fibroblast growth factor 2 [SEP] Fibroblast growth factor 2 is a single-chain polypeptide growth factor that plays a significant role in the process of wound healing and is a potent inducer of physiologic angiogenesis. Several different forms of the human protein exist ranging from 18-24 kDa in size due to the use of alternative start sites within the fgf-2 gene. It has a 55 percent amino acid residue identity to fibroblast growth factor 1 and has potent heparin-binding activity. The growth factor is an extremely potent inducer of dna synthesis in a variety of cell types from mesoderm and neuroectoderm lineages. It was originally named basic fibroblast growth factor based upon its chemical properties and to distinguish it from acidic fibroblast growth factor (fibroblast growth factor 1).

name: fibroblast growth factor 3
query: Query: fibroblast growth factor 3 [SEP] Fibroblast growth factor 3 is a fibroblast growth factor that is expressed primarily during development.

name: fibroblast growth factor 4
query: Query: fibroblast growth factor 4 [SEP] Fibroblast growth factor 4 is a heparin binding fibroblast growth factor that may play a role in limb buds development.

name: fibroblast growth factor 6
query: Query: fibroblast growth factor 6 [SEP] Fibroblast growth factor 6 is a fibroblast growth factor that was initially identified based on its sequence similarity to fibroblast growth factor 4. It is found in myoblasts and plays an important role in muscle development.

name: fibroblast growth factor 7
query: Query: fibroblast growth factor 7 [SEP] Fibroblast growth [MASK] is a fibroblast growth factor that is a specific mitogen for epithelial cells. It binds a complex of heparan sulfate and fibroblast growth factor receptor 2b.

name: fibroblast growth factor 8
query: Query: fibroblast growth factor 8 [SEP] Fibroblast growth factor 8 is a fibroblast growth factor that preferentially activates [MASK]. It was initially identified as an androgen-induced growth factor and plays a role in regulating growth of human breast neoplasms and prostatic neoplasms.

name: fibroblast growth factor 9
query: Query: fibroblast growth factor 9 [SEP] Fibroblast growth factor 9 is a fibroblast growth factor that was originally identified as a mitogen for glial cells. It is expressed primarily in neurons.

name: financial audit
query: Query: financial audit [SEP] Financial audit is an examination, review and verification of all financial accounts.

name: finger injuries
query: Query: finger injuries [SEP] Finger injuries is general or unspecified injuries involving the fingers.

name: finger joint
query: Query: finger joint [SEP] Finger joint is the articulation between the head of one phalanx and the base of the one distal to it, in each finger.

name: fish
query: Query: fish [SEP] Fish is a group of cold-blooded, aquatic vertebrates having gills, fins, a cartilaginous or bony endoskeleton, and elongated bodies covered with scales.

name: fish diseases
query: Query: fish diseases [SEP] Fish diseases is diseases of freshwater, marine, hatchery or aquarium fish. This term includes diseases of both teleosts (true fish) and elasmobranchs (sharks, rays and skates).

name: fisheries
query: Query: fisheries [SEP] Fisheries is places for cultivation and harvesting of fish, particularly in sea waters. (from McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

name: fish flour
query: Query: fish flour [SEP] Fish flour is a flour made of pulverized, dried fish or fish parts.

name: fish proteins , dietary
query: Query: fish proteins , dietary [SEP] Dietary fish proteins is dietary protein from fish.

name: fitness centers
query: Query: fitness centers [SEP] Fitness centers is facilities having programs intended to promote and maintain a state of physical well-being for optimal performance and health.

name: flame ionization
query: Query: flame ionization [SEP] Flame ionization is pyrolysis of organic compounds at the temperature of a hydrogen-air flame to produce ionic intermediates which can be collected and the resulting ion current measured by gas chromatography.

name: flight , animal
query: Query: flight , animal [SEP] Animal flight is the use of wings or wing-like appendages to remain aloft and move through the air.

name: flour
query: Query: flour [SEP] Flour is ground up [MASK] of wheat.

name: flow cytometry
query: Query: flow cytometry [SEP] Flow cytometry is technique using an instrument system for making, processing, and displaying one or more measurements on individual cells obtained from a cell suspension. Cells are usually stained with one or more fluorescent dyes specific to cell components of interest, e.g., dna, and fluorescence of each cell is measured as it rapidly transverses the excitation beam (laser or mercury arc lamp). Fluorescence provides a quantitative measure of various biochemical and biophysical properties of the cell, as well as a basis for cell sorting. Other measurable optical parameters include light absorption and light scattering, the latter being applicable to the measurement of cell size, shape, density, granularity, and stain uptake.

name: flow injection analysis
query: Query: flow injection analysis [SEP] Flow injection analysis is the analysis of a chemical substance by inserting a sample into a carrier [MASK] of reagent using a sample injection valve that propels the sample downstream where mixing occurs in a coiled tube, then passes into a flow-through detector and a recorder or other data handling device.

name: fluid shifts
query: Query: fluid shifts [SEP] Fluid shifts is translocation of body fluids from one compartment to another, such as from the vascular to the interstitial compartments. Fluid shifts are associated with profound changes in vascular permeability and water-electrolyte imbalance. The shift can also be from the lower body to the upper body as in conditions of weightlessness.

name: fluid therapy
query: Query: fluid therapy [SEP] Fluid therapy is therapy whose basic objective is to restore the volume and composition of the body fluids to normal with respect to water-electrolyte balance. Fluids may be administered intravenously, orally, by intermittent gavage, or by hypodermoclysis.

name: fluorescein angiography
query: Query: fluorescein angiography [SEP] Fluorescein angiography is visualization of a vascular system after intravenous injection of a fluorescein solution. The images may be photographed or televised. It is used especially in studying the retinal and uveal vasculature.

name: fluorescence
query: Query: fluorescence [SEP] Fluorescence is the property of emitting radiation while being irradiated. The radiation emitted is usually of longer wavelength than that incident or absorbed, e.g., a substance can be irradiated with invisible radiation and emit visible light. X-ray fluorescence is used in diagnosis.

name: fluorescence polarization immunoassay
query: Query: fluorescence polarization immunoassay [SEP] Fluorescence polarization immunoassay is fluoroimmunoassay where detection of the hapten-antibody reaction is based on measurement of the increased polarization of fluorescence-labeled hapten when it is combined with antibody. The assay is very useful for the measurement of small haptenic antigens such as drugs at low concentrations.

name: fluorescence resonance energy transfer
query: Query: fluorescence resonance energy transfer [SEP] Fluorescence resonance energy transfer is a type of fluorescence spectroscopy using two fluorescent dyes with overlapping emission and absorption spectra, which is used to indicate proximity of labeled molecules. This technique is useful for studying interactions of molecules and protein folding.

name: fluorescent antibody technique , direct
query: Query: fluorescent antibody technique , direct [SEP] Direct fluorescent antibody technique is a form of fluorescent antibody technique utilizing a fluorochrome conjugated to an antibody, which is added directly to a tissue or cell suspension for the detection of a specific antigen. (Bennington, Saunders Dictionary & Encyclopedia of Laboratory Medicine and Technology, 1984)

name: fluorescent antibody technique , indirect
query: Query: fluorescent antibody technique , indirect [SEP] Indirect fluorescent antibody technique is a form of fluorescent antibody technique commonly used to detect serum antibodies and immune complexes in tissues and microorganisms in specimens from patients with infectious diseases. The technique involves formation of an antigen-antibody complex which is labeled with fluorescein-conjugated anti-immunoglobulin antibody. (From Bennington, Saunders Dictionary & Encyclopedia of Laboratory Medicine and Technology, 1984)

name: fluorescent dyes
query: Query: fluorescent dyes [SEP] Fluorescent dyes is chemicals that emit light after excitation by light. The wave length of the emitted light is usually longer than that of the incident light. Fluorochromes are substances that cause fluorescence in other substances, i.e., dyes used to mark or label other compounds with fluorescent tags.

name: foam cells
query: Query: foam cells [SEP] Foam cells is lipid-laden macrophages originating from monocytes or from smooth muscle cells.

name: focus groups
query: Query: focus groups [SEP] Focus groups is a method of data collection and a qualitative research tool in which a small group of individuals are brought together and allowed to interact in a discussion of their opinions about topics, issues, or questions.

name: folate receptor 1
query: Query: folate receptor 1 [SEP] Folate receptor 1 is a subtype of GPI-anchored folate receptors that is expressed in tissues of epithelial origin. This protein is also identified as an ovarian-tumor-specific antigen.

name: follicle stimulating hormone , beta subunit
query: Query: follicle stimulating hormone , beta subunit [SEP] Beta subunit follicle stimulating hormone is the beta subunit of follicle stimulating hormone. It is a 15-kDa glycopolypeptide. Full biological activity of fsh requires the non-covalently bound heterodimers of an alpha and a beta subunit. Mutation of the fshb gene causes delayed puberty, or infertility.

name: follicle stimulating hormone , human
query: Query: follicle stimulating hormone , human [SEP] Human follicle stimulating hormone is a major gonadotropin secreted by the human adenohypophysis (pituitary gland, anterior). Follicle-stimulating hormone stimulates gametogenesis and the supporting cells such as the ovarian granulosa cells, the testicular sertoli cells, and the leydig cells. fsh consists of two noncovalently linked subunits, alpha and beta. The alpha subunit is common in the three human pituitary glycoprotein hormones (tsh, lh, and fsh), but the beta subunit is unique and confers its biological specificity.

name: follicular cyst
query: Query: follicular cyst [SEP] Follicular cyst is cyst due to the occlusion of the duct of a follicle or small gland.

name: follicular fluid
query: Query: follicular fluid [SEP] Follicular fluid is the fluid surrounding the ovum and granulosa cells in the Graafian follicle (ovarian follicle). The follicular fluid contains [MASK] steroids, glycoprotein hormones, plasma proteins, mucopolysaccharides, and enzymes.

name: follicular phase
query: Query: follicular phase [SEP] Follicular phase is the period of the menstrual cycle representing follicular growth, increase in ovarian estrogen (estrogens) production, and epithelial proliferation of the endometrium. Follicular phase begins with the onset of menstruation and ends with ovulation.

name: food , genetically modified
query: Query: food , genetically modified [SEP] Genetically modified food is food derived from genetically modified organisms (organisms, genetically modified).

name: food addiction
query: Query: food addiction [SEP] Food addiction is a cluster of chemical dependencies to specific foods or food in general in which there develops a physical craving for these foods.

name: food analysis
query: Query: food analysis [SEP] Food analysis is measurement and evaluation of the components of substances to be taken as food.

name: food assistance
query: Query: food assistance [SEP] Food assistance is food or financial assistance for food given to those in need.

name: food chain
query: Query: food chain [SEP] Food chain is the sequence of transfers of matter and energy from organism to organism in the form of food. Food chains intertwine locally into a food web because most organisms consume more than one type of animal or plant. plants, which convert [MASK] to food by [MASK], are the primary food source. In a predator chain, a plant-eating animal is eaten by a larger animal. In a parasite chain, a smaller organism consumes part of a larger host and may itself be parasitized by smaller organisms. In a saprophytic chain, microorganisms live on dead organic matter.

name: food coloring agents
query: Query: food coloring agents [SEP] Food coloring agents is natural or synthetic dyes used as coloring agents in processed foods.

name: food contamination , radioactive
query: Query: food contamination , radioactive [SEP] Radioactive food contamination is exposure of food to radioactive substances, distinguishable from food irradiation, a food preservation technique.

name: food intolerance
query: Query: food intolerance [SEP] Food intolerance is digestive system disorder where a particular food irritates the digestive tract or cannot be properly digested (i.e., due to a lack of a digestive enzyme). It differs from food hypersensitivity which is an immune system disorder, usually due to specific proteins in food.  http://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/articles/problem-foods-is-it-an-allergy-or-intolerance.

name: food labeling
query: Query: food labeling [SEP] Food labeling is use of written, printed, or graphic materials upon or accompanying a food or its container or wrapper. The concept includes ingredients, nutritional value, directions, warnings, and other relevant information.

name: food microbiology
query: Query: food microbiology [SEP] Food microbiology is the presence of bacteria, viruses, and fungi in food and food products. This term is not restricted to pathogenic organisms: the presence of various non-pathogenic bacteria and fungi in cheeses and wines, for example, is included in this concept.

name: food preservation
query: Query: food preservation [SEP] Food preservation is procedures or techniques used to keep food from spoiling.

name: food supply
query: Query: food supply [SEP] Food supply is the production and movement of food items from point of origin to use or consumption.

name: foot bones
query: Query: foot bones [SEP] [MASK] bones is the tarsal bones; metatarsal bones; and phalanges of toes. The tarsal bones consists of seven bones: calcaneus; talus; cuboid; navicular; internal; middle; and external cuneiform bones. The five metatarsal bones are numbered one through five, [MASK] medial to lateral. There are 14 phalanges in each [MASK], the great toe has two while the other toes have three each.

name: foot injuries
query: Query: foot injuries [SEP] [MASK] injuries is general or unspecified injuries involving the [MASK].

name: forearm
query: Query: forearm [SEP] Forearm is part of the upper extremity in humans and primates extending from the elbow to the wrist.

name: foreign medical graduates
query: Query: foreign medical graduates [SEP] Foreign medical graduates is physicians who hold degrees from medical schools in countries other than the ones in which they practice.

name: forensic dentistry
query: Query: forensic dentistry [SEP] Forensic dentistry is the application of dental knowledge to questions of law.

name: forensic pathology
query: Query: forensic pathology [SEP] Forensic pathology is the application of pathology to questions of law.

name: forensic toxicology
query: Query: forensic toxicology [SEP] Forensic toxicology is the application of toxicology knowledge to questions of law.

name: forestry
query: Query: forestry [SEP] Forestry is the science of developing, [MASK] for, or cultivating forests.

name: forests
query: Query: forests [SEP] Forests is an ecosystem dominated by trees and other woody vegetation.

name: form
query: Query: form [SEP] Form is document used for acquiring particular information or for presenting particular information in a prescribed sequence and format, often with blank spaces or lines or other methods to prompt for insertion of the requested information.

name: forms as topic
query: Query: forms as topic [SEP] Forms as topic is works about documents used for acquiring particular information or for presenting particular information in a prescribed sequence and format, often with blank spaces or lines or other methods to prompt for insertion of the requested information.

name: fractional flow reserve , myocardial
query: Query: fractional flow reserve , myocardial [SEP] Myocardial fractional flow reserve is the ratio of maximum blood flow to the myocardium with coronary stenosis present, to the maximum equivalent blood flow without stenosis. The measurement is commonly used to verify borderline stenosis of coronary arteries.

name: fracture fixation , internal
query: Query: fracture fixation , internal [SEP] Internal fracture fixation is the use of internal devices (metal plates, nails, rods, etc.) to hold the position of a fracture in proper alignment.

name: fracture healing
query: Query: fracture healing [SEP] Fracture healing is the physiological restoration of bone tissue and function after a fracture. It includes bony callus formation and normal replacement of bone tissue.

name: fractures , cartilage
query: Query: fractures , cartilage [SEP] Cartilage fractures is breaks in cartilage.

name: fractures , multiple
query: Query: fractures , multiple [SEP] Multiple fractures is injuries involving the breaking of either several bones or one bone in two or more places.

name: fragile x syndrome
query: Query: fragile x syndrome [SEP] Fragile x syndrome is a condition characterized genotypically by mutation of the distal end of the long [MASK] of the x chromosome (at gene loci fraxa or fraxe) and phenotypically by cognitive impairment, hyperactivity, seizures, language delay, and enlargement of the ears, head, and testes. intellectual disability occurs in nearly all males and roughly 50% of females with the full mutation of fraxa. (From Menkes, Textbook of Child Neurology, 5th ed, p226)

name: freeze substitution
query: Query: freeze substitution [SEP] Freeze substitution is a modification of the freeze-drying method in which the ice within the frozen tissue is replaced by alcohol or other solvent at a very low temperature.

name: freezing
query: Query: freezing [SEP] Freezing is liquids transforming into solids by the removal of heat.

name: french revolution
query: Query: french revolution [SEP] French revolution is [MASK] during which traditional monarchy was ended and modern government functions were instituted.

name: friction
query: Query: friction [SEP] Friction is surface resistance to the relative motion of one body against the rubbing, sliding, rolling, or flowing of another with which it is in contact.

name: friend murine leukemia virus
query: Query: friend murine leukemia virus [SEP] Friend murine leukemia virus is a strain of Murine leukemia virus (leukemia virus, murine) producing leukemia of the reticulum-cell type with massive infiltration of liver, spleen, and bone marrow. It infects dba/2 and Swiss mice.

name: friends
query: Query: friends [SEP] Friends is persons whom one knows, likes, and trusts.

name: fuel oils
query: Query: fuel oils [SEP] Fuel oils is complex petroleum hydrocarbons consisting mainly of residues from crude oil distillation. These liquid products include [MASK] oils, stove oils, and furnace oils and are burned to generate energy.

name: fund raising
query: Query: fund raising [SEP] Fund raising is usually organized community efforts to raise money to promote financial programs of institutions. The funds may include individual [MASK].

name: fungal vaccines
query: Query: fungal vaccines [SEP] Fungal vaccines is suspensions of attenuated or killed fungi administered for the prevention or treatment of infectious fungal disease.

name: fungal viruses
query: Query: fungal viruses [SEP] Fungal viruses is viruses infecting species of fungi.

name: fused teeth
query: Query: fused teeth [SEP] Fused teeth is two teeth united during development by the union of their tooth germs; the teeth may be joined by the enamel of their crowns, by their root dentin, or by both.

name: gaba agonists
query: Query: gaba agonists [SEP] Gaba agonists is endogenous compounds and drugs that bind to and activate gamma-aminobutyric acid receptors (receptors, gaba).

name: gaba antagonists
query: Query: gaba antagonists [SEP] Gaba antagonists is drugs that bind to but do not activate gaba receptors, thereby blocking the actions of endogenous gamma-aminobutyric acid and gaba receptor agonists.

name: gabaergic neurons
query: Query: gabaergic neurons [SEP] Gabaergic neurons is neurons whose primary neurotransmitter is gamma-aminobutyric acid.

name: gaba modulators
query: Query: gaba modulators [SEP] Gaba modulators is substances that do not act as agonists or antagonists but do affect the gamma-aminobutyric acid receptor-ionophore complex. gaba-a receptors (receptors, gaba-a) appear to have at least three allosteric sites at which modulators act: a site at which benzodiazepines act by increasing the opening frequency of gamma-aminobutyric ACID-activated chloride channels; a site at which barbiturates act to prolong the duration of channel opening; and a site at which some steroids may act. general anesthetics probably act at least partly by potentiating GABAergic responses, but they are not included here.

name: gaba uptake inhibitors
query: Query: gaba uptake inhibitors [SEP] Gaba uptake inhibitors is compounds that suppress or block the plasma membrane transport of gamma-aminobutyric acid by gaba plasma membrane transport proteins.

name: gain of function mutation
query: Query: gain of function mutation [SEP] Gain of function mutation is a mutation that results in an increase in a gene's activity or in acquiring a new molecular function or a new pattern of gene expression.

name: gait analysis
query: Query: gait analysis [SEP] Gait analysis is determination of the level of functional limitation that may be due to pathology, and evaluating rehabilitative intervention of the way in which the body moves from one point to another. Most often, this is done by walking.

name: gallbladder
query: Query: gallbladder [SEP] Gallbladder is a storage reservoir for [MASK] secretion. Gallbladder allows the delivery of [MASK] acids at a high concentration and in a controlled manner, via the cystic duct to the duodenum, for degradation of dietary lipid.

name: gallbladder neoplasms
query: Query: gallbladder neoplasms [SEP] Gallbladder neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the gallbladder.

name: game theory
query: Query: game theory [SEP] Game theory is theoretical construct used in applied mathematics to analyze certain situations in which there is an interplay between parties that may have similar, opposed, or mixed interests. In a typical game, decision-making "players," who each have their own goals, try to gain advantage over the other parties by anticipating each other's decisions; the game is finally resolved as a consequence of the players' decisions.

name: gamma cameras
query: Query: gamma cameras [SEP] Gamma cameras is electronic instruments that produce photographs or cathode-ray tube images of the gamma-ray emissions from organs containing radionuclide tracers.

name: gamma rays
query: Query: gamma rays [SEP] Gamma rays is penetrating, high-energy electromagnetic radiation emitted from atomic nuclei during nuclear decay. The range of wavelengths of emitted radiation is between 0.1 - 100 pm which overlaps the shorter, more energetic hard x-rays wavelengths. The distinction between gamma rays and X-rays is based on their radiation source.

name: ganglia , spinal
query: Query: ganglia , spinal [SEP] Spinal ganglia is sensory ganglia located on the dorsal spinal roots within the vertebral column. The spinal ganglion cells are pseudounipolar. The single primary branch bifurcates sending a peripheral process to carry sensory information from the periphery and a central branch which relays that information to the spinal cord or brain.

name: ganglion cysts
query: Query: ganglion cysts [SEP] Ganglion cysts is nodular tumor-like lesions or mucoid flesh, arising from tendon sheaths, ligaments, or joint capsule, especially of the hands, wrists, or [MASK]. They are not true cysts as they lack epithelial wall. They are distinguished from synovial cysts by the lack of communication with a joint cavity or the synovial membrane.

name: gastric acid
query: Query: gastric acid [SEP] Gastric acid is hydrochloric acid present in gastric juice.

name: gastric artery
query: Query: gastric artery [SEP] Gastric artery is any of several branches of the splenic artery distributed to the greater curvature of the stomach.

name: gastric balloon
query: Query: gastric balloon [SEP] Gastric balloon is an inflatable device implanted in the stomach as an adjunct to therapy of morbid obesity. Specific types include the silicone Garren-Edwards Gastric Bubble (gegb), approved by the fda in 1985, and the Ballobes Balloon.

name: gastric dilatation
query: Query: gastric dilatation [SEP] Gastric dilatation is abnormal distention of the stomach due to accumulation of gastric contents that may reach 10 to 15 liters. Gastric dilatation may be the result of [MASK]; ileus; gastroparesis; or denervation.

name: gastric fistula
query: Query: gastric fistula [SEP] Gastric fistula is abnormal passage communicating with the stomach.

name: gastric fundus
query: Query: gastric fundus [SEP] Gastric fundus is the superior portion of the body of the stomach above the level of the cardiac notch.

name: gastric hypothermia
query: Query: gastric hypothermia [SEP] Gastric hypothermia is a method of lowering core body temperature by filling the stomach with chilled fluids.

name: gastric inhibitory polypeptide
query: Query: gastric inhibitory polypeptide [SEP] Gastric inhibitory polypeptide is a gastrointestinal peptide hormone of about 43-amino acids. It is found to be a potent stimulator of insulin secretion and a relatively poor inhibitor of gastric acid secretion.

name: gb virus b
query: Query: gb virus b [SEP] Gb virus b is a species of virus (tentatively placed in the genus hepacivirus) in the family flaviviridae, that was recovered from a tamarin monkey, but may have been of human origin. It causes hepatitis in several species of New World monkeys.

name: gender identity
query: Query: gender identity [SEP] Gender identity is a person's concept of self as being male and masculine or female and feminine, or ambivalent, based in part on physical characteristics, parental responses, and psychological and social pressures. It is the internal experience of gender role.

name: gene amplification
query: Query: gene amplification [SEP] Gene amplification is a selective increase in the number of copies of a gene coding for a specific protein without a proportional increase in other genes. It occurs naturally via the excision of a copy of the repeating sequence from the chromosome and its extrachromosomal replication in a plasmid, or via the production of an rna transcript of the entire repeating sequence of [MASK] followed by the reverse transcription of the molecule to produce an additional copy of the original dna sequence. Laboratory techniques have been introduced for inducing disproportional replication by unequal crossing over, uptake of dna from lysed cells, or generation of extrachromosomal sequences from rolling circle replication.

name: gene deletion
query: Query: gene deletion [SEP] Gene deletion is a genetic rearrangement through loss of segments of dna or rna, bringing sequences which are normally separated into close proximity. This deletion may be detected using cytogenetic techniques and can also be inferred from the phenotype, indicating a deletion at one specific locus.

name: gene dosage
query: Query: gene dosage [SEP] Gene dosage is the number of copies of a given gene present in the cell of an organism. An increase in gene dosage (by gene duplication for example) can result in higher levels of gene product formation. gene dosage compensation mechanisms result in [MASK] to the level gene expression when there are changes or differences in gene dosage.

name: gene duplication
query: Query: gene duplication [SEP] Gene duplication is processes occurring in various organisms by which new genes are copied. Gene duplication may result in a multigene family; supergenes or pseudogenes.

name: gene editing
query: Query: gene editing [SEP] Gene editing is genetic engineering or molecular biology techniques that involve dna repair mechanisms for incorporating site-specific modifications into a cell's genome.

name: gene expression profiling
query: Query: gene expression profiling [SEP] Gene expression profiling is the determination of the pattern of genes expressed at the level of genetic transcription, under specific circumstances or in a specific cell.

name: gene expression regulation , bacterial
query: Query: gene expression regulation , bacterial [SEP] Bacterial gene expression regulation is any of the processes by which cytoplasmic or intercellular factors influence the differential control of gene action in bacteria.

name: gene expression regulation , developmental
query: Query: gene expression regulation , developmental [SEP] [MASK] expression regulation is any of the processes by which nuclear, cytoplasmic, or intercellular factors influence the differential control of gene action during the developmental stages of an organism.

name: gene expression regulation , leukemic
query: Query: gene expression regulation , leukemic [SEP] Leukemic gene expression regulation is any of the processes by which nuclear, cytoplasmic, or intercellular factors influence the differential control of gene action in leukemia.

name: gene expression regulation , plant
query: Query: gene expression regulation , plant [SEP] Plant gene expression regulation is any of the processes by which nuclear, cytoplasmic, or intercellular factors influence the differential control of gene action in plants.

name: gene expression regulation , viral
query: Query: gene expression regulation , viral [SEP] Viral gene expression regulation is any of the processes by which cytoplasmic factors influence the differential control of gene action in viruses.

name: gene flow
query: Query: gene flow [SEP] Gene flow is the change in gene frequency in a population due to migration of gametes or individuals ([MASK]) across population barriers. In contrast, in [MASK] the cause of gene frequency changes are not a result of population or gamete movement.

name: gene knockdown techniques
query: Query: gene knockdown techniques [SEP] Gene knockdown techniques is the artificial induction of gene silencing by the use of rna interference to reduce the expression of a specific gene. It includes the use of double-stranded rna, such as small interfering rna and rna containing hairpin loop sequence, and anti-sense oligonucleotides.

name: gene knockout techniques
query: Query: gene knockout techniques [SEP] Gene knockout techniques is techniques to alter a gene sequence that result in an inactivated gene, or one in which the expression can be inactivated at a chosen time during development to study the loss of function of a gene.

name: gene ontology
query: Query: gene ontology [SEP] Gene ontology is sets of structured vocabularies used for describing and categorizing genes, and gene products by their molecular function, involvement in biological processes, and cellular location. These vocabularies and their associations to genes and gene products (Gene Ontology annotations) are generated and curated by the Gene Ontology Consortium.

name: gene order
query: Query: gene order [SEP] Gene order is the sequential location of genes on a chromosome.

name: gene or genome
query: Query: gene or genome [SEP] Gene or genome is a category of nucleic acid sequences that function as units of heredity and which code for the basic instructions for the development, reproduction, and maintenance of organisms.

name: gene pool
query: Query: gene pool [SEP] Gene pool is the total genetic information possessed by the reproductive members of a population of sexually reproducing organisms.

name: generalization , response
query: Query: generalization , response [SEP] Response generalization is the principle that after an organism learns to respond in a particular manner to a stimulus, that stimulus is effective in eliciting similar responses.

name: generalization , stimulus
query: Query: generalization , stimulus [SEP] Stimulus generalization is the tendency to react to stimuli that are different from, but somewhat similar to, the stimulus used as a conditioned stimulus.

name: general practitioners
query: Query: general practitioners [SEP] General practitioners is physicians whose practice is not restricted to a specific field of medicine.

name: gene regulatory networks
query: Query: gene regulatory networks [SEP] Gene regulatory networks is interacting DNA-encoded regulatory subsystems in the genome that coordinate input from activator and repressor transcription factors during development, cell differentiation, or in response to environmental cues. The networks function to ultimately specify expression of particular sets of genes for specific conditions, times, or locations.

name: genes , apc
query: Query: genes , apc [SEP] Apc genes is tumor suppressor genes located in the 5q21 region on the long [MASK] of human chromosome 5. The mutation of these genes is associated with familial adenomatous polyposis (adenomatous polyposis coli) and gardner syndrome, as well as some sporadic colorectal cancers.

name: genes , bacterial
query: Query: genes , bacterial [SEP] Bacterial genes is the functional hereditary units of bacteria.

name: genes , cdc
query: Query: genes , cdc [SEP] Cdc genes is genes that code for proteins that regulate the cell division cycle. These genes form a regulatory network that culminates in the onset of [MASK] by activating the p34cdc2 protein (protein p34cdc2).

name: genes , dominant
query: Query: genes , dominant [SEP] Dominant genes is genes that influence the phenotype both in the homozygous and the heterozygous state.

name: genes , duplicate
query: Query: genes , duplicate [SEP] Duplicate genes is two identical genes showing the same phenotypic action but localized in different regions of a chromosome or on different chromosomes. (From Rieger et al., Glossary of Genetics: Classical and Molecular, 5th ed)

name: genes , essential
query: Query: genes , essential [SEP] Essential genes is those genes found in an organism which are necessary for its viability and normal function.

name: genes , gag
query: Query: genes , gag [SEP] Gag genes is dna sequences that form the coding region for proteins associated with the viral core in retroviruses. gag is short for group-specific antigen.

name: genes , immunoglobulin light chain
query: Query: genes , immunoglobulin light chain [SEP] Immunoglobulin light chain genes is genes and gene segments encoding the immunoglobulin light chains. Gene segments of the light chain genes are designated as v (variable), j (joining), and c (constant).

name: genes , insect
query: Query: genes , insect [SEP] Insect genes is the functional hereditary units of insects.

name: genes , lethal
query: Query: genes , lethal [SEP] Lethal genes is genes whose loss of function or gain of function mutation leads to the death of the carrier prior to maturity. They may be essential genes (genes, essential) required for viability, or genes which cause a block of function of an essential gene at a time when the essential gene function is required for viability.

name: genes , mating type , fungal
query: Query: genes , mating type , fungal [SEP] Fungal mating type genes is fungal genes that mostly encode transcription factors. In some fungi they also encode pheromones and pheromone receptors. The transcription factors control expression of specific proteins that give a cell its mating identity. Opposite mating type identities are required for mating.

name: genes , mcc
query: Query: genes , mcc [SEP] Mcc genes is tumor suppressor genes located in the 5q21 region on the long [MASK] of human chromosome 5. The mutation of these genes is associated with the formation of colorectal cancer (mcc stands for mutated in colorectal cancer).

name: genes , mdr
query: Query: genes , mdr [SEP] Mdr genes is genes for membrane transport proteins that confer resistance to toxic compounds. Several superfamilies of these multidrug export proteins are known and found in both prokaryotes and eukaryotes.

name: genes , plant
query: Query: genes , plant [SEP] Plant genes is the functional hereditary units of plants.

name: genes , px
query: Query: genes , px [SEP] Px genes is dna sequences that form the coding region for at least three proteins which regulate the expression of human t-lymphotropic virus 1 and human t-lymphotropic virus 2. The proteins are p21(x), p27(rex), and p40(tax). The tax (trans-activator x) and rex (regulator x) genes are part of pX but are in overlapping reading frames. x was the original designation for the sequences or region (at that time of unknown function) in the long open reading frame (lor) which is now called pX.

name: genes , rev
query: Query: genes , rev [SEP] Rev genes is dna sequences that form the coding region for a protein that regulates the expression of the viral structural and regulatory proteins in human immunodeficiency virus (hiv). rev is short for regulator of virion.

name: genes , suppressor
query: Query: genes , suppressor [SEP] Suppressor genes is genes that have a suppressor allele or suppressor mutation (suppression, genetic) which cancels the effect of a previous mutation, enabling the wild-type phenotype to be maintained or partially restored. For example, amber suppressors cancel the effect of an amber nonsense mutation.

name: genes , synthetic
query: Query: genes , synthetic [SEP] Synthetic genes is biologically functional sequences of dna chemically synthesized in vitro.

name: genes , tat
query: Query: genes , tat [SEP] Tat genes is dna sequences that form the coding region for the protein responsible for trans-activation of transcription (tat) in human immunodeficiency virus (hiv).

name: genetic carrier screening
query: Query: genetic carrier screening [SEP] Genetic carrier screening is identification of individuals who are heterozygous at a genetic locus for a recessive phenotype.

name: genetic complementation test
query: Query: genetic complementation test [SEP] Genetic complementation test is a test used to determine whether or not complementation (compensation in the form of dominance) will occur in a cell with a given mutant phenotype when another mutant genome, encoding the same mutant phenotype, is introduced into that cell.

name: genetic counseling
query: Query: genetic counseling [SEP] Genetic counseling is an educational process that provides information and advice to individuals or families about a genetic condition that may affect them. The purpose is to help individuals make informed decisions about marriage, reproduction, and other health management issues based on information about the genetic disease, the available [MASK], and management programs. Psychosocial support is usually offered.

name: genetic enhancement
query: Query: genetic enhancement [SEP] Genetic enhancement is the use of genetic methodologies to improve functional capacities of an organism rather than to treat disease.

name: genetic fitness
query: Query: genetic fitness [SEP] Genetic fitness is the capability of an organism to survive and reproduce. The phenotypic expression of the genotype in a particular environment determines how genetically fit an organism will be.

name: genetic function
query: Query: genetic function [SEP] Genetic function is function of genes.

name: genetic markers
query: Query: genetic markers [SEP] Genetic markers is a phenotypically recognizable genetic trait which can be used to identify a genetic locus, a linkage group, or a recombination event.

name: genetic privacy
query: Query: genetic privacy [SEP] Genetic privacy is the protection of genetic information about an individual, family, or population group, from unauthorized disclosure.

name: genetic profile
query: Query: genetic profile [SEP] Genetic profile is a [MASK] of characteristics unique to the dna of an individual organism or population obtained by analyzing small samples of biological material such as body tissues or fluids, used especially in the context of predicting susceptibility to a particular disease. For example, some populations have identifiable genetic profiles which put them at higher risk for cancer. Distinguish from genetic background and genetic variation.

name: genetics , behavioral
query: Query: genetics , behavioral [SEP] Behavioral genetics is the experimental study of the relationship between the genotype of an organism and its behavior. The scope includes the effects of genes on simple sensory processes to complex organization of the nervous system.

name: genetics , microbial
query: Query: genetics , microbial [SEP] Microbial genetics is a subdiscipline of genetics which deals with the genetic mechanisms and processes of microorganisms.

name: genetics , population
query: Query: genetics , population [SEP] Population genetics is the discipline studying genetic composition of populations and effects of factors such as genetic selection, population size, mutation, migration, and [MASK] on the frequencies of various genotypes and phenotypes using a variety of genetic techniques.

name: gene transfer , horizontal
query: Query: gene transfer , horizontal [SEP] Horizontal gene transfer is the naturally occurring transmission of genetic information between organisms, related or unrelated, circumventing parent-to-offspring transmission. Horizontal gene transfer may occur via a variety of naturally occurring processes such as [MASK]; genetic transduction; and transfection. It may result in a change of the recipient organism's genetic composition (transformation, genetic).

name: genome , human
query: Query: genome , human [SEP] Human genome is the complete genetic complement contained in the dna of a [MASK] of chromosomes in a human. The length of the human genome is about 3 billion [MASK].

name: genomic library
query: Query: genomic library [SEP] Genomic library is a form of gene library containing the complete dna sequences present in the genome of a given organism. It contrasts with a cDNA library which contains only sequences utilized in protein coding (lacking introns).

name: genotyping techniques
query: Query: genotyping techniques [SEP] Genotyping techniques is methods used to determine individuals' specific alleles or snps (single nucleotide polymorphisms).

name: geographic area
query: Query: geographic area [SEP] Geographic area is The continents and countries situated on those continents; the United States and each of the constituent states arranged by region; Canada and each of its provinces; Australia and each of its states; the major bodies of water and major islands on both hemispheres; and selected major cities.

name: geographic atrophy
query: Query: geographic atrophy [SEP] Geographic atrophy is a form of macular degeneration also known as dry macular degeneration marked by occurrence of a well-defined progressive lesion or atrophy in the central part of the retina called the macula lutea. It is distinguishable from wet macular degeneration in that the latter involves neovascular exudates.

name: geographic information systems
query: Query: geographic information systems [SEP] Geographic information systems is computer systems capable of assembling, storing, manipulating, and displaying geographically referenced information, i.e. data identified according to their locations.

name: geographic mapping
query: Query: geographic mapping [SEP] Geographic mapping is creating a representation of areas of the earth or other celestial bodies, for the purpose of visualizing spatial distributions of various information.

name: geriatric assessment
query: Query: geriatric assessment [SEP] Geriatric assessment is evaluation of the level of physical, physiological, or mental functioning in the older population group.

name: geriatric dentistry
query: Query: geriatric dentistry [SEP] Geriatric dentistry is the branch of dentistry concerned with the dental problems of older people.

name: geriatric nursing
query: Query: geriatric nursing [SEP] Geriatric nursing is nursing care of the aged patient given in the home, the hospital, or special institutions such as nursing homes, psychiatric institutions, etc.

name: geriatric psychiatry
query: Query: geriatric psychiatry [SEP] Geriatric psychiatry is a subspecialty of psychiatry concerned with the mental health of the aged.

name: germany , east
query: Query: germany , east [SEP] East germany is the former German Democratic Republic which was reunified with the former Federal Republic of Germany in 1990.

name: germany , west
query: Query: germany , west [SEP] West germany is the former Federal Republic of Germany which was reunified with the former German Democratic Republic in 1990.

name: germination
query: Query: germination [SEP] Germination is the initial stages of the growth of [MASK] into a seedlings. The embryonic shoot (plumule) and embryonic plant roots (radicle) emerge and grow upwards and downwards respectively. Food reserves for germination come from endosperm tissue within the [MASK] and/or from the [MASK] leaves (cotyledon). (Concise Dictionary of Biology, 1990)

name: germ theory of disease
query: Query: germ theory of disease [SEP] Germ theory of disease is the fundamental tenet of modern medicine that certain diseases are caused by microorganisms. It was confirmed by the work of Pasteur, Lister, and Koch.

name: gestational age
query: Query: gestational age [SEP] Gestational age is the age of the conceptus, beginning from the time of fertilization. In clinical obstetrics, the gestational age is often estimated as the time from the last day of the last menstruation which is about 2 weeks before ovulation and fertilization.

name: ghana
query: Query: ghana [SEP] Ghana is a republic in western Africa, south of burkina faso and west of togo. Its capital is Accra.

name: ghrelin
query: Query: ghrelin [SEP] Ghrelin is a 28-amino acid, acylated, orexigenic peptide that is a ligand for growth hormone secretagogue receptors. Ghrelin is widely expressed but primarily in the stomach in the adults. Ghrelin acts centrally to stimulate growth hormone secretion and food intake, and peripherally to regulate energy homeostasis. Its large precursor protein, known as appetite-regulating hormone or motilin-related peptide, contains ghrelin and obestatin.

name: giant axonal neuropathy
query: Query: giant axonal neuropathy [SEP] Giant axonal neuropathy is rare autosomal recessive disorder of [MASK] proteins. The disease is caused by mutations in the gene that codes gigaxonin protein. The mutations result in disorganization of axonal [MASK] proteins, formation of the characteristic giant axons, and progressive neuropathy. The clinical features of the disease include early-onset progressive peripheral motor and sensory neuropathies often associated with central nervous system involvement (intellectual disability, seizures, dysmetria, and congenital nystagmus).

name: giant cells
query: Query: giant cells [SEP] Giant cells is multinucleated masses produced by the fusion of many cells; often associated with viral infections. In aids, they are induced when the envelope glycoprotein of the hiv virus binds to the cd4 antigen of uninfected neighboring t4 cells. The resulting syncytium leads to cell death and thus may account for the cytopathic effect of the virus.

name: giant cell tumor of bone
query: Query: giant cell tumor of bone [SEP] Giant cell tumor of bone is a bone tumor composed of cellular spindle-cell stroma containing scattered multinucleated giant cells resembling osteoclasts. The tumors range from benign to frankly malignant lesions. The tumor occurs most frequently in an end of a long tubular bone in young adults. (From Dorland, 27th ed; Stedman, 25th ed)

name: giant viruses
query: Query: giant viruses [SEP] Giant viruses is dna viruses that have genomes up to several megabases in length and infect primarily single-celled eukaryotes.

name: gingival hemorrhage
query: Query: gingival hemorrhage [SEP] Gingival hemorrhage is the flowing of blood from the marginal gingival area, particularly the sulcus, seen in such conditions as gingivitis, marginal periodontitis, injury, and ascorbic acid deficiency.

name: gingival neoplasms
query: Query: gingival neoplasms [SEP] Gingival neoplasms is new abnormal growth of tissue in the gingiva.

name: gingival recession
query: Query: gingival recession [SEP] Gingival recession is exposure of the root surface when the edge of the gum (gingiva) moves apically away from the crown of the tooth. This is common with advancing age, vigorous tooth brushing, diseases, or tissue loss of the gingiva, the periodontal ligament and the supporting bone (alveolar process).

name: gingival retraction techniques
query: Query: gingival retraction techniques [SEP] Gingival retraction techniques is techniques used to expose dental surface below the gingival margin in order to obtain better dental impression during periodental and peri-implant applications.
