The retraction of the gingival tissue can be achieved surgically (e.g., laser gingivectomy and rotary curettage) or chemically with a retraction cord.

name: glasgow coma scale
query: Query: glasgow coma scale [SEP] Glasgow coma scale is a scale that assesses the response to stimuli in patients with craniocerebral injuries. The parameters are eye opening, motor response, and verbal response.

name: glass
query: Query: glass [SEP] Glass is hard, amorphous, brittle, inorganic, usually transparent, polymerous silicate of basic oxides, usually potassium or sodium. It is used in the form of hard sheets, vessels, tubing, fibers, ceramics, beads, etc.

name: glaucoma , neovascular
query: Query: glaucoma , neovascular [SEP] Neovascular glaucoma is a form of secondary glaucoma which develops as a consequence of another ocular disease and is attributed to the forming of new vessels in the angle of the anterior chamber.

name: glia maturation factor
query: Query: glia maturation factor [SEP] Glia maturation factor is a factor identified in the brain that influences the growth and differentiation of neurons and neuroglia. Glia maturation factor beta is the 17-kDa polypeptide product of the gmfb gene and is the principal component of glia maturation factor.

name: global burden of disease
query: Query: global burden of disease [SEP] Global burden of disease is measure of the burden of disease using the disability-adjusted-life-year (daly). This time-based measure combines years of life lost due to premature mortality and years of life lost due to time lived in states of less than full health. The metric was developed to assess the burden of disease consistently across diseases, risk factors and regions.

name: global warming
query: Query: global warming [SEP] Global warming is increase in the temperature of the atmosphere near the Earth's surface and in the troposphere, which can contribute to changes in global climate patterns.

name: glucose clamp technique
query: Query: glucose clamp technique [SEP] Glucose clamp technique is maintenance of a constant blood glucose level by perfusion or infusion with glucose or insulin. It is used for the study of metabolic rates (e.g., in glucose, lipid, amino acid metabolism) at constant glucose concentration.

name: glucose intolerance
query: Query: glucose intolerance [SEP] Glucose intolerance is a pathological state in which blood glucose level is less than approximately 140 mg/100 ml of plasma at fasting, and above approximately 200 mg/100 ml plasma at 30-, 60-, or 90-minute during a glucose tolerance test. This condition is seen frequently in diabetes mellitus, but also occurs with other diseases and malnutrition.

name: glucose tolerance test
query: Query: glucose tolerance test [SEP] Glucose tolerance test is a test to determine the ability of an individual to maintain homeostasis of blood glucose. It includes measuring blood glucose levels in a fasting state, and at prescribed intervals before and after oral glucose intake (75 or 100 g) or [MASK] (0.5 g/kg).

name: glucose transporter type 3
query: Query: glucose transporter type 3 [SEP] Glucose transporter type 3 is a major glucose transporter found in neurons.

name: glycine
query: Query: glycine [SEP] Glycine is a non-essential amino acid. It is found primarily in gelatin and silk fibroin and used therapeutically as a nutrient. It is also a fast inhibitory neurotransmitter.

name: glycogen storage disease type i
query: Query: glycogen storage disease type i [SEP] Glycogen storage disease type i is an autosomal recessive disease in which gene expression of glucose-6-phosphatase is absent, resulting in hypoglycemia due to lack of glucose production. Accumulation of glycogen in liver and kidney leads to organomegaly, particularly massive hepatomegaly. Increased concentrations of lactic acid and hyperlipidemia appear in the plasma. Clinical gout often appears in early childhood.

name: glycogen storage disease type ii
query: Query: glycogen storage disease type ii [SEP] Glycogen storage disease type ii is an autosomal recessively inherited glycogen storage disease caused by glucan 1,4-alpha-glucosidase deficiency. Large amounts of glycogen accumulate in the lysosomes of skeletal muscle (muscle, skeletal); heart; liver; spinal cord; and brain. Three forms have been described: infantile, childhood, and adult. The infantile form is fatal in infancy and presents with hypotonia and a hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (cardiomyopathy, hypertrophic). The childhood form usually presents in the second year of life with proximal weakness and respiratory symptoms. The adult form consists of a slowly progressive proximal myopathy. (From Muscle Nerve 1995;3:s61-9; Menkes, Textbook of Child Neurology, 5th ed, pp73-4)

name: glycogen storage disease type iib
query: Query: glycogen storage disease type iib [SEP] Glycogen storage disease type iib is an X-linked dominant multisystem disorder resulting in cardiomyopathy, myopathy and intellectual disability. It is caused by mutation in the gene encoding lysosomal-associated membrane protein 2.

name: glycogen storage disease type iii
query: Query: glycogen storage disease type iii [SEP] Glycogen storage disease type iii is an autosomal recessive metabolic disorder due to deficient expression of amylo-1,6-glucosidase (one part of the glycogen debranching enzyme system). The clinical course of the disease is similar to that of glycogen storage disease type i, but milder. Massive hepatomegaly, which is present in young children, diminishes and occasionally disappears with age. Levels of glycogen with short outer branches are elevated in muscle, liver, and erythrocytes. Six subgroups have been identified, with subgroups Type IIIa and Type IIIb being the most prevalent.

name: glycogen storage disease type v
query: Query: glycogen storage disease type v [SEP] Glycogen storage disease type v is glycogenosis due to muscle phosphorylase deficiency. Characterized by painful cramps following sustained exercise.

name: glycogen storage disease type vi
query: Query: glycogen storage disease type vi [SEP] Glycogen storage disease type vi is a hepatic glycogen storage disease in which there is an apparent deficiency of hepatic phosphorylase (glycogen phosphorylase, liver form) activity.

name: glycogen storage disease type vii
query: Query: glycogen storage disease type vii [SEP] Glycogen storage disease type vii is an autosomal recessive glycogen storage disease in which there is deficient expression of 6-phosphofructose 1-kinase in muscle (phosphofructokinase-1, muscle type) resulting in abnormal deposition of glycogen in muscle tissue. These patients have severe congenital muscular dystrophy and are exercise intolerant.

name: glycolysis
query: Query: glycolysis [SEP] Glycolysis is a metabolic process that converts glucose into two molecules of pyruvic acid through a series of enzymatic reactions. Energy generated by this process is conserved in two molecules of atp. Glycolysis is the universal catabolic pathway for glucose, free glucose, or glucose derived from complex carbohydrates, such as glycogen and [MASK].

name: goals
query: Query: goals [SEP] Goals is the end-result or objective, which may be specified or required in advance.

name: goat diseases
query: Query: goat diseases [SEP] Goat diseases is diseases of the domestic or wild goat of the genus Capra.

name: gold alloys
query: Query: gold alloys [SEP] Gold alloys is alloys that contain a high percentage of gold. They are used in restorative or prosthetic dentistry.

name: gold colloid , radioactive
query: Query: gold colloid , radioactive [SEP] Radioactive gold colloid is a suspension of radioactive gold particles emitting negative beta particles and gamma irradiation. It was formerly used for liver scans and irradiation treatment of some metastatic malignancies.

name: golgi apparatus
query: Query: golgi apparatus [SEP] Golgi apparatus is a stack of flattened vesicles that functions in posttranslational processing and sorting of proteins, receiving them from the rough endoplasmic reticulum and directing them to [MASK], lysosomes, or the cell membrane. The movement of proteins takes place by transfer vesicles that bud off from the rough endoplasmic reticulum or Golgi apparatus and fuse with the Golgi, lysosomes or cell membrane. (From Glick, Glossary of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, 1990)

name: golgi matrix proteins
query: Query: golgi matrix proteins [SEP] Golgi matrix proteins is proteins on the cytoplasmic side of the golgi apparatus cisternae that tether the cisternae to each other or to the transport vesicles of the trans-golgi network to maintain the Golgi structure and function.

name: governing board
query: Query: governing board [SEP] Governing board is the group in which legal authority is vested for the control of health-related institutions and organizations.

name: governmental or regulatory activity
query: Query: governmental or regulatory activity [SEP] Governmental or regulatory activity is governmental or regulatory activity

name: government employees
query: Query: government employees [SEP] Government employees is persons employed by the government.

name: government publication
query: Query: government publication [SEP] Government publication is work consisting of publications issued by local, regional, or national governments or by their agencies or subdivisions.

name: government regulation
query: Query: government regulation [SEP] Government regulation is exercise of governmental authority to control conduct.

name: grade approach
query: Query: grade approach [SEP] Grade approach is a common, sensible, structured  and transparent approach to grading quality (or certainty) of evidence and strength of recommendations developed by the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (short grade) working group.

name: graft occlusion , vascular
query: Query: graft occlusion , vascular [SEP] Vascular [MASK] occlusion is obstruction of flow in biological or prosthetic vascular [MASK].

name: graft rejection
query: Query: graft rejection [SEP] [MASK] [MASK] is an immune response with both cellular and humoral components, directed against an allogeneic [MASK], whose tissue antigens are not compatible with those of the recipient.

name: graft survival
query: Query: graft survival [SEP] [MASK] survival is the survival of a [MASK] in a host, the factors responsible for the survival and the changes occurring within the [MASK] during growth in the host.

name: graft vs host disease
query: Query: graft vs host disease [SEP] [MASK] vs host disease is the clinical entity characterized by anorexia, [MASK], loss of hair, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, growth retardation, and eventual death brought about by the [MASK] vs host reaction.

name: graft vs leukemia effect
query: Query: graft vs leukemia effect [SEP] [MASK] vs leukemia effect is immunological [MASK] of leukemia cells following bone marrow transplantation.

name: grain proteins
query: Query: grain proteins [SEP] Grain proteins is dietary protein from edible grains.

name: granular cell tumor
query: Query: granular cell tumor [SEP] Granular cell tumor is unusual tumor affecting any site of the body, but most often encountered in the head and [MASK]. Considerable debate has surrounded the histogenesis of this neoplasm; however, it is considered to be a myoblastoma of, usually, a benign nature. It affects women more often than men. When it develops beneath the epidermis or mucous membrane, it can lead to proliferation of the squamous cells and mimic squamous cell carcinoma.

name: grape seed extract
query: Query: grape seed extract [SEP] Grape [MASK] extract is exudate from [MASK] of the grape plant Vitis vinifera, composed of oils and secondary plant metabolites (bioflavonoids and polyphenols) credited with important medicinal properties.

name: gray literature
query: Query: gray literature [SEP] Gray literature is works that include publications such as reports, theses, conference [MASK], translations and limited circulation government documents which are not normally available through commercial publication sources. (lcsh)

name: gray matter
query: Query: gray matter [SEP] Gray matter is region of central nervous system that appears darker in [MASK] than the other type, [MASK] matter. It is composed of neuronal cell bodies; neuropil; glial cells and capillaries but few myelinated nerve fibers.

name: greece
query: Query: greece [SEP] Greece is a country in southern Europe, bordering the Aegean Sea, Ionian Sea, and the Mediterranean Sea, between Albania and Turkey. The capital is Athens.

name: greece , ancient
query: Query: greece , ancient [SEP] Ancient greece is a civilization extant from about 1200 bc. to the death of Alexander the Great, in 323 b.c. It extended from the Greek city states to North Africa and eastward to the Indus [MASK].

name: greek world
query: Query: greek world [SEP] Greek world is a historical and cultural entity dispersed across a wide geographical area under the influence of Greek civilization, culture, and science. The Greek Empire extended from the Greek mainland and the Aegean islands from the 16th century b.c., to the Indus Valley in the 4th century under Alexander the Great, and to southern Italy and Sicily. Greek medicine began with Homeric and Aesculapian medicine and continued unbroken to Hippocrates (480-355 b.c.). The classic period of Greek medicine was 460-136 b.c. and the Graeco-Roman period, 156 b.c.-576 a.d. (From a. Castiglioni, a [MASK], 2d ed; from f. h. Garrison, An Introduction to the [MASK], 4th ed)

name: greenhouse gases
query: Query: greenhouse gases [SEP] Greenhouse gases is gaseous elements, chemicals that are in the atmosphere that may contribute to [MASK].

name: grid cells
query: Query: grid cells [SEP] Grid cells is neurons in the entorhinal cortex that project to the hippocampus. Grid cells and place cells play a role in cognitive representation of [MASK] and navigation.

name: gross domestic product
query: Query: gross domestic product [SEP] Gross domestic product is value of all final goods and services produced in a country in one year.

name: group attribute
query: Query: group attribute [SEP] Group attribute is values that reference groups to which this entry belongs.

name: group homes
query: Query: group homes [SEP] Group homes is housing for groups of patients, children, or others who need or desire emotional or physical support. They are usually established as planned, single housekeeping units in residential dwellings that provide care and supervision for small groups of residents, who, although unrelated, live together as a family.

name: group practice , dental
query: Query: group practice , dental [SEP] Dental group practice is any group of three or more full-time dentists, organized in a legally recognized entity for the provision of dental care, sharing space, equipment, personnel and records for both patient care and business management, and who have a predetermined arrangement for the distribution of income.

name: group purchasing
query: Query: group purchasing [SEP] Group purchasing is a shared service which combines the purchasing power of individual organizations or facilities in order to obtain lower prices for equipment and supplies. (From Health Care Terms, 2nd ed)

name: growth charts
query: Query: growth charts [SEP] Growth charts is graphic displays of height and weight showing development over time.

name: growth cones
query: Query: growth cones [SEP] Growth cones is bulbous enlargement of the growing tip of nerve axons and dendrites. They are crucial to neuronal development because of their pathfinding ability and their role in synaptogenesis.

name: growth differentiation factor 10
query: Query: growth differentiation factor 10 [SEP] Growth differentiation factor 10 is a growth differentiation factor that is closely-related in structure to bone morphogenetic protein 3. Growth differentiation factor 10 is found at high levels in bone, however it plays an additional roles in regulating embryonic development.

name: growth differentiation factor 15
query: Query: growth differentiation factor 15 [SEP] Growth differentiation factor 15 is a growth differentiation factor that is secreted in response to cell stress and in response to macrophage activation. In addition growth differentiation factor 15 demonstrates a diverse array of biological properties including the induction of cartilage formation, the inhibition of hematopoietic progenitor proliferation, and the induction of neuronal migration.

name: growth differentiation factor 2
query: Query: growth differentiation factor 2 [SEP] Growth differentiation factor 2 is a growth differentiation factor that plays a regulatory role as a paracrine factor for a diverse array of cell types during embryonic development and in the adult tissues. Growth differentiation factor 2 is also a potent regulator of chondrogenesis and was previously referred to as bone morphogenetic protein 9.

name: growth differentiation factor 3
query: Query: growth differentiation factor 3 [SEP] Growth differentiation factor 3 is a growth differentiation factor that may play a role in maintaining the undifferentiated state of pluripotent stem cells by inhibiting the actions of bone morphogenetic proteins. Differentiation factor 3 is also considered a nodal signaling ligand that influences the genesis of left-right asymmetry.

name: growth differentiation factor 5
query: Query: growth differentiation factor 5 [SEP] Growth differentiation factor 5 is a growth differentiation factor that plays a role in early chondrogenesis and joint formation.

name: growth differentiation factor 9
query: Query: growth differentiation factor 9 [SEP] Growth differentiation factor 9 is a bone morphogenetic protein that plays an essential role in the regulation of ovarian folliculogenesis.

name: guided tissue regeneration , periodontal
query: Query: guided tissue regeneration , periodontal [SEP] Periodontal guided tissue regeneration is techniques for enhancing and directing cell growth to repopulate specific parts of the periodontium that have been damaged by periodontal diseases; tooth diseases; or trauma, or to correct tooth abnormalities. Repopulation and repair is achieved by guiding the progenitor cells to reproduce in the desired location by blocking contact with surrounding tissue by use of membranes composed of synthetic or natural material that may include growth inducing factors as well.

name: guideline adherence
query: Query: guideline adherence [SEP] Guideline adherence is conformity in fulfilling or following official, recognized, or institutional requirements, guidelines, recommendations, protocols, pathways, or other standards.

name: hair analysis
query: Query: hair analysis [SEP] Hair analysis is examination of hair by chemical, physical, or microscopic means.

name: hair bleaching agents
query: Query: hair bleaching agents [SEP] Hair bleaching agents is chemicals that are used to oxidize pigments in hair.

name: hair cells , auditory , outer
query: Query: hair cells , auditory , outer [SEP] Outer auditory hair cells is sensory cells of organ of Corti. In mammals, they are usually arranged in three or four rows, and away from the core of spongy bone (the modiolus), lateral to the [MASK] and other supporting structures. Their cell bodies and stereocilia increase in length from the cochlear base toward the apex and laterally across the rows, allowing differential responses to various frequencies of sound.

name: hair dyes
query: Query: hair dyes [SEP] Hair dyes is dyes used as cosmetics to change hair [MASK] either permanently or temporarily.

name: hair follicle
query: Query: hair follicle [SEP] Hair follicle is a tube-like invagination of the epidermis from which the hair shaft develops and into which sebaceous glands open. The hair follicle is lined by a cellular inner and outer root sheath of epidermal origin and is invested with a fibrous sheath derived from the dermis. (Stedman, 26th ed) Follicles of very long hairs extend into the subcutaneous layer of tissue under the skin.

name: handbook
query: Query: handbook [SEP] Handbook is work consisting of concise reference works in which facts and information pertaining to a certain subject or field are arranged for ready reference and consultation rather than for continuous reading and study.

name: handling , psychological
query: Query: handling , psychological [SEP] Psychological handling is physical manipulation of animals and humans to induce a behavioral or other psychological reaction. In [MASK], the animal is handled to induce a stress situation or to study the effects of "gentling" or "mothering".

name: haplotypes
query: Query: haplotypes [SEP] Haplotypes is the genetic constitution of individuals with respect to one member of a pair of allelic genes, or sets of genes that are closely linked and tend to be inherited together such as those of the major histocompatibility complex.

name: happiness
query: Query: happiness [SEP] Happiness is highly pleasant emotion characterized by outward manifestations of gratification.

name: hardness tests
query: Query: hardness tests [SEP] Hardness tests is a test to determine the relative hardness of a metal, mineral, or other material according to one of several scales, such as Brinell, Mohs, Rockwell, Vickers, or Shore. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

name: harm reduction
query: Query: harm reduction [SEP] Harm reduction is the application of methods designed to reduce the risk of harm associated with certain behaviors without reduction in frequency of those behaviors. The risk-associated behaviors include ongoing and active addictive behaviors.

name: harvey murine sarcoma virus
query: Query: harvey murine sarcoma virus [SEP] Harvey murine sarcoma virus is a replication-defective mouse sarcoma virus (sarcoma viruses, murine) first described by j.j. Harvey in 1964.

name: hazardous waste sites
query: Query: hazardous waste sites [SEP] Hazardous waste sites is sites where hazardous substances are deposited. Some have facilities for safely storing, processing, and [MASK] these waste products.

name: head impulse test
query: Query: head impulse test [SEP] Head impulse test is identification of [MASK] during a rapid head [MASK] to assess vestibuloocular reflex.

name: head injuries , penetrating
query: Query: head injuries , penetrating [SEP] Penetrating head injuries is head injuries which feature compromise of the skull and dura mater. These may result from gunshot wounds (wounds, gunshot), stab wounds (wounds, stab), and other forms of trauma.

name: head kidney
query: Query: head kidney [SEP] Head kidney is a primitive form of vertebrate kidney that is found in adults of some primitive fishes and in the embryos of more advanced fishes. In some species of fishes it contains phagocytic cells and is also a major site of hematopoiesis, analogous to the mammalian bone marrow.

name: head movements
query: Query: head movements [SEP] Head movements is voluntary or involuntary motion of head that may be relative to or independent of body; includes animals and humans.

name: healthcare disparities
query: Query: healthcare disparities [SEP] Healthcare disparities is differences in access to or availability of medical facilities and services.

name: healthcare failure mode and effect analysis
query: Query: healthcare failure mode and effect analysis [SEP] Healthcare failure mode and effect analysis is prospective risk assessment tool aimed at identifying potential risks and their impact in healthcare settings.

name: healthcare financing
query: Query: healthcare financing [SEP] Healthcare financing is methods of generating, allocating, and using financial resources in healthcare systems.

name: health care reform
query: Query: health care reform [SEP] Health care reform is innovation and improvement of the health care system by reappraisal, amendment of services, and removal of faults and abuses in providing and distributing health services to patients. It includes a re-alignment of health services and health insurance to maximum demographic elements (the unemployed, indigent, uninsured, elderly, inner cities, rural areas) with reference to coverage, hospitalization, pricing and cost containment, insurers' and employers' costs, pre-existing medical conditions, prescribed drugs, equipment, and services.

name: health care related organization
query: Query: health care related organization [SEP] Health care related organization is health care related organization

name: health care sector
query: Query: health care sector [SEP] Health care sector is economic sector concerned with the provision, distribution, and consumption of health care services and related products.

name: health communication
query: Query: health communication [SEP] Health communication is the transfer of information from experts in the medical and public health fields to patients and the public. The study and use of communication strategies to inform and influence individual and community decisions that enhance health.

name: health education , dental
query: Query: health education , dental [SEP] Dental health education is education which increases the awareness and favorably influences the attitudes and knowledge relating to the improvement of dental health on a personal or community basis.

name: health equity
query: Query: health equity [SEP] Health equity is opportunity to attain full health potential and no one is disadvantaged from achieving this potential because of their social position or other socially determined circumstance.

name: health facility closure
query: Query: health facility closure [SEP] Health facility closure is the closing of any health facility, e.g., health centers, residential facilities, and hospitals.

name: health facility merger
query: Query: health facility merger [SEP] Health facility merger is the combining of administrative and organizational resources of two or more health care facilities.

name: health facility moving
query: Query: health facility moving [SEP] Health facility moving is the relocation of health care institutions or units thereof. The concept includes equipment relocation.

name: health impact assessment
query: Query: health impact assessment [SEP] Health impact assessment is combination of procedures, methods, and tools by which a policy, program, or project may be judged as to its potential effects on the health of a population, and the distribution of those effects within the population.

name: health information systems
query: Query: health information systems [SEP] Health information systems is a system for the collection and/or processing of data from various sources, and using the information for policy making and management of health services. It could be [MASK]-based or electronic. (From http://web.worldbank.org/WBSITE/EXTERNAL/TOPICS/EXTHEALTHNUTRITIONANDPOPULATION/EXTHSD/0,,contentMDK:22239824~menuPK:376799~pagePK:148956~piPK:216618~theSitePK:376793,00.html. http://www.who.int/healthinfo/systems/en/)

name: health insurance exchanges
query: Query: health insurance exchanges [SEP] Health insurance exchanges is state-provided health insurance marketplaces established under the patient protection and affordable care act.

name: health knowledge , attitudes , practice
query: Query: health knowledge , attitudes , practice [SEP] Practice attitudes health knowledge is knowledge, attitudes, and associated behaviors which pertain to health-related topics such as pathologic processes or diseases, their prevention, and treatment. This term refers to non-health workers and health workers (health personnel).

name: health maintenance organizations
query: Query: health maintenance organizations [SEP] Health maintenance organizations is organized systems for providing comprehensive prepaid health care that have five basic attributes: (1) provide care in a defined geographic area; (2) provide or ensure delivery of an agreed-upon [MASK] of basic and supplemental health maintenance and treatment services; (3) provide care to a voluntarily enrolled group of persons; (4) require their enrollees to use the services of designated providers; and (5) receive reimbursement through a predetermined, fixed, periodic prepayment made by the enrollee without regard to the degree of services provided. (From Facts on File Dictionary of Health Care Management, 1988)

name: health physics
query: Query: health physics [SEP] Health physics is the science concerned with problems of radiation protection relevant to reducing or preventing radiation exposure, and the effects of ionizing radiation on humans and their environment.

name: health priorities
query: Query: health priorities [SEP] Health priorities is preferentially rated health-related activities or functions to be used in establishing health planning goals. This may refer specifically to pl93-641.

name: health risk behaviors
query: Query: health risk behaviors [SEP] Health risk behaviors is pattern of behavior which predisposes certain individuals to increased risk for contracting disease or sustaining personal injury. These behaviors may cluster into a risky lifestyle.

name: health services for persons with disabilities
query: Query: health services for persons with disabilities [SEP] Health services for persons with disabilities is health services and access for disabled persons. Disabilities include impairments, activity limitations, or participation restrictions, and reflect the interaction between the individual with the disability and personal and environmental factors.

name: health services for the aged
query: Query: health services for the aged [SEP] Health services for the aged is services for the diagnosis and treatment of diseases in the aged and the maintenance of health in the elderly.

name: health smart cards
query: Query: health smart cards [SEP] Health smart cards is hand-sized cards with built-in computer chips used for accessing, storing, and protecting patients' medical information.

name: health status disparities
query: Query: health status disparities [SEP] Health status disparities is variation in rates of disease occurrence and disabilities between population groups defined by socioeconomic characteristics such as age, ethnicity, economic resources, or gender and populations identified geographically or similar measures.

name: health systems agencies
query: Query: health systems agencies [SEP] Health systems agencies is health planning and resources development agencies which function in each health service area of the United States (pl 93-641).

name: health workforce
query: Query: health workforce [SEP] Health workforce is the availability of health personnel. It includes the demand and recruitment of both professional and allied health personnel, their present and future supply and distribution, and their assignment and utilization.

name: healthy aging
query: Query: healthy aging [SEP] Healthy aging is the development and maintenance of optimal physical, mental, spiritual, and social well-being and function with advancing age.

name: healthy people programs
query: Query: healthy people programs [SEP] Healthy people programs is healthy People Programs are a [MASK] of health objectives to be used by governments, communities, professional organizations, and others to help develop programs to improve health. It builds on initiatives pursued over the past two decades beginning with the 1979 Surgeon General's Report, Healthy People, Healthy People 2000: National Health Promotion and Disease Prevention Objectives, and Healthy People 2010. These established national health objectives and served as the basis for the development of state and community plans. These are administered by the Office of Disease Prevention and Health Promotion (odphp). Similar programs are conducted by other national governments.

name: hearing loss , conductive
query: Query: hearing loss , conductive [SEP] Conductive hearing loss is hearing loss due to interference with the mechanical reception or amplification of sound to the cochlea. The interference is in the outer or [MASK] involving the [MASK]; tympanic membrane; or ear ossicles.

name: hearing loss , functional
query: Query: hearing loss , functional [SEP] Functional hearing loss is hearing loss without a physical basis. Often observed in patients with psychological or behavioral disorders.

name: hearing loss , unilateral
query: Query: hearing loss , unilateral [SEP] Unilateral hearing loss is partial or complete hearing loss in one ear.

name: heart , artificial
query: Query: heart , artificial [SEP] Artificial heart is a pumping mechanism that duplicates the output, rate, and blood pressure of the natural heart. It may replace the function of the entire heart or a portion of it, and may be an intracorporeal, extracorporeal, or paracorporeal heart. (Dorland, 28th ed)

name: heart bypass , right
query: Query: heart bypass , right [SEP] Right heart bypass is diversion of the flow of blood from the entrance to the right atrium directly to the [MASK], avoiding the right atrium and right ventricle (Dorland, 28th ed). This a permanent procedure often performed to bypass a congenitally deformed right atrium or right ventricle.

name: heart failure , diastolic
query: Query: heart failure , diastolic [SEP] Diastolic heart failure is heart failure caused by abnormal myocardial relaxation during diastole leading to defective cardiac filling.

name: heart failure , systolic
query: Query: heart failure , systolic [SEP] Systolic heart failure is heart failure caused by abnormal [MASK] during systole leading to defective cardiac emptying.

name: heart injuries
query: Query: heart injuries [SEP] Heart injuries is general or unspecified injuries to the heart.

name: heart rate , fetal
query: Query: heart rate , fetal [SEP] Fetal heart rate is the heart rate of the fetus. The normal range at term is between 120 and 160 beats per minute.

name: heart rate determination
query: Query: heart rate determination [SEP] Heart rate determination is methods, techniques, and processes by which heart rate is measured.

name: heart rupture
query: Query: heart rupture [SEP] Heart rupture is disease-related laceration or tearing of tissues of the heart, including the free-wall myocardium; heart septum; papillary muscles; chordae tendineae; and any of the heart valves. Pathological rupture usually results from myocardial infarction (heart rupture, post-infarction).

name: heart septal defects , atrial
query: Query: heart septal defects , atrial [SEP] Atrial heart septal defects is developmental abnormalities in any portion of the atrial septum resulting in abnormal communications between the two upper chambers of the heart. Classification of atrial septal defects is based on location of the communication and types of incomplete fusion of atrial septa with the endocardial cushions in the fetal heart. They include ostium primum, ostium secundum, sinus venosus, and coronary sinus defects.

name: heart septal defects , ventricular
query: Query: heart septal defects , ventricular [SEP] Ventricular heart septal defects is developmental abnormalities in any portion of the ventricular septum resulting in abnormal communications between the two lower chambers of the heart. Classification of ventricular septal defects is based on location of the communication, such as perimembranous, inlet, outlet (infundibular), central muscular, marginal muscular, or apical muscular defect.

name: heart transplantation
query: Query: heart transplantation [SEP] Heart transplantation is the transference of a heart from one human or animal to another.

name: heart valve prosthesis implantation
query: Query: heart valve prosthesis implantation [SEP] Heart valve prosthesis implantation is surgical insertion of synthetic material to repair injured or diseased heart valves.

name: heat exhaustion
query: Query: heat exhaustion [SEP] Heat exhaustion is a clinical syndrome caused by heat stress, such as over-exertion in a hot environment or excessive exposure to sun. It is characterized by sweating, water (volume) depletion, [MASK] depletion, cool clammy skin, nausea, and headache.

name: heat shock transcription factors
query: Query: heat shock transcription factors [SEP] Heat shock transcription factors is heat and cold stress-inducible, transcription factors that bind to inverted 5'-ngaan-3' pentamer dna sequences and are regulated by poly-adp-ribosylation. They play essential roles as transcriptional activators of the heat-shock response by inducing expression of large classes of molecular chaperones and heat-shock proteins. They also function in dna repair; transcriptional reactivation of latent hiv-1; and pre-mRNA processing and nuclear export of hsp70 heat-shock proteins during heat stress.

name: heavy ions
query: Query: heavy ions [SEP] Heavy ions is positively-charged atomic nuclei that have been stripped of their [MASK]. These particles have one or more units of electric charge and a mass exceeding that of the [MASK] nucleus ([MASK]).

name: helicobacter pylori
query: Query: helicobacter pylori [SEP] Helicobacter pylori is a spiral bacterium active as a human gastric pathogen. It is a gram-negative, urease-positive, curved or slightly spiral organism initially isolated in 1982 from patients with lesions of gastritis or peptic [MASK] in Western Australia. Helicobacter pylori was originally classified in the genus campylobacter, but rna sequencing, cellular fatty acid profiles, growth patterns, and other taxonomic characteristics indicate that the micro-organism should be included in the genus helicobacter. It has been officially transferred to Helicobacter gen. nov. (see Int j Syst Bacteriol 1989 Oct;39(4):297-405).

name: helper viruses
query: Query: helper viruses [SEP] Helper viruses is viruses which enable defective viruses to replicate or to form a protein coat by complementing the missing gene function of the defective (satellite) virus. Helper and satellite may be of the same or different genus.

name: helping behavior
query: Query: helping behavior [SEP] Helping behavior is behaviors associated with the giving of assistance or aid to individuals.

name: hematopoietic stem cell mobilization
query: Query: hematopoietic stem cell mobilization [SEP] Hematopoietic stem cell mobilization is the release of stem cells from the bone marrow into the peripheral blood circulation for the purpose of leukapheresis, prior to stem cell transplantation. Hematopoietic growth factors or chemotherapeutic agents often are used to stimulate the mobilization.

name: hemodialysis , home
query: Query: hemodialysis , home [SEP] Home hemodialysis is long-term maintenance hemodialysis in the home.

name: hemodialysis units , hospital
query: Query: hemodialysis units , hospital [SEP] Hospital hemodialysis units is hospital units in which care is provided the hemodialysis patient. This includes hemodialysis centers in hospitals.

name: hemodynamic monitoring
query: Query: hemodynamic monitoring [SEP] Hemodynamic monitoring is continuous measurement of the movement and forces of blood in the cardiovascular system.

name: hemorrhagic syndrome , bovine
query: Query: hemorrhagic syndrome , bovine [SEP] Bovine hemorrhagic syndrome is clinically severe [MASK] of cattle caused by noncytopathic forms of [MASK] ([MASK]). [MASK] are characterized by high morbidity and high mortality.

name: heparin antagonists
query: Query: heparin antagonists [SEP] Heparin antagonists is coagulant substances inhibiting the anticoagulant action of heparin.

name: hepatic artery
query: Query: hepatic artery [SEP] Hepatic artery is a branch of the celiac artery that distributes to the stomach, pancreas, duodenum, liver, gallbladder, and greater omentum.

name: hepatic encephalopathy
query: Query: hepatic encephalopathy [SEP] Hepatic encephalopathy is a syndrome characterized by central nervous system dysfunction in association with liver failure, including portal-systemic shunts. Clinical features include lethargy and confusion (frequently progressing to coma); asterixis; nystagmus, pathologic; brisk oculovestibular reflexes; decorticate and decerebrate posturing; muscle spasticity; and bilateral extensor plantar reflexes (see reflex, babinski). electroencephalography may demonstrate triphasic waves. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp1117-20; Plum & Posner, Diagnosis of Stupor and Coma, 3rd ed, p222-5)

name: hepatic veins
query: Query: hepatic veins [SEP] Hepatic veins is veins which drain the liver.

name: hepatitis , alcoholic
query: Query: hepatitis , alcoholic [SEP] Alcoholic hepatitis is inflammation of the liver due to alcohol abuse. It is characterized by necrosis of [MASK], infiltration by neutrophils, and deposit of mallory bodies. Depending on its severity, the inflammatory lesion may be reversible or progress to liver cirrhosis.

name: hepatitis , autoimmune
query: Query: hepatitis , autoimmune [SEP] Autoimmune hepatitis is a chronic self-perpetuating hepatocellular inflammation of unknown cause, usually with hypergammaglobulinemia and serum autoantibodies.

name: hepatitis , infectious canine
query: Query: hepatitis , infectious canine [SEP] Infectious canine hepatitis is a contagious disease caused by canine adenovirus (adenoviruses, canine) infecting the liver, the eye, the kidney, and other organs in dogs, other canids, and bears. Symptoms include fever; edema; vomiting; and [MASK].

name: hepatitis a
query: Query: hepatitis a [SEP] Hepatitis a is inflammation of the liver in humans caused by a member of the hepatovirus genus, human hepatitis a virus. It can be transmitted through fecal contamination of food or water.

name: hepatitis a vaccines
query: Query: hepatitis a vaccines [SEP] Hepatitis a vaccines is vaccines or candidate vaccines used to prevent infection with hepatitis a virus (hepatovirus).

name: hepatitis a virus , human
query: Query: hepatitis a virus , human [SEP] Human hepatitis a virus is a strain of hepatitis a virus which causes hepatitis in humans. The virus replicates in [MASK] and is presumed to reach the intestine via the [MASK]. Transmission occurs by the fecal-oral route.

name: hepatitis a virus cellular receptor 1
query: Query: hepatitis a virus cellular receptor 1 [SEP] Hepatitis a virus cellular receptor 1 is an Ig domain-containing membrane receptor for hepatitis a virus; ebola virus; marburg virus; and dengue virus. It may also function to modulate asthma and hypersensitivity.

name: hepatitis a virus cellular receptor 2
query: Query: hepatitis a virus cellular receptor 2 [SEP] Hepatitis a virus cellular receptor 2 is an Ig domain-containing membrane receptor that is expressed by th1 cells. It regulates the activation of macrophages and inhibits TH1-mediated auto- and alloimmune responses to promote immune tolerance.

name: hepatitis b , chronic
query: Query: hepatitis b , chronic [SEP] Chronic hepatitis b is inflammation of the liver in humans caused by hepatitis b virus lasting six months or more. It is primarily transmitted by parenteral exposure, such as transfusion of contaminated blood or blood products, but can also be transmitted via sexual or intimate personal contact.

name: hepatitis b e antigens
query: Query: hepatitis b e antigens [SEP] Hepatitis b e antigens is a closely related group of antigens found in the plasma only during the infective phase of hepatitis b or in virulent chronic hepatitis b, probably indicating active virus replication; there are three subtypes which may exist in a complex with immunoglobulins g.

name: hepatitis b surface antigens
query: Query: hepatitis b surface antigens [SEP] Hepatitis b surface antigens is those hepatitis b antigens found on the surface of the Dane particle and on the 20 nm spherical and tubular particles. Several subspecificities of the surface antigen are known. These were formerly called the Australia antigen.

name: hepatitis b vaccines
query: Query: hepatitis b vaccines [SEP] Hepatitis b vaccines is vaccines or candidate vaccines containing inactivated hepatitis b or some of its component antigens and designed to prevent hepatitis b. Some vaccines may be recombinantly produced.

name: hepatitis c , chronic
query: Query: hepatitis c , chronic [SEP] Chronic hepatitis c is inflammation of the liver in humans that is caused by hepatitis c virus lasting six months or more. Chronic hepatitis c can lead to liver cirrhosis.

name: hepatitis c antigens
query: Query: hepatitis c antigens [SEP] Hepatitis c antigens is antigens of the virions of hepacivirus, their surface, core, or other associated antigens.

name: hepatitis d , chronic
query: Query: hepatitis d , chronic [SEP] Chronic hepatitis d is inflammation of the liver in humans caused by [MASK] in conjunction with hepatitis b virus and lasting six months or more.

name: hepatitis e
query: Query: hepatitis e [SEP] Hepatitis e is acute inflammation of the liver in humans; caused by hepatitis e virus, a non-enveloped single-stranded rna virus. Similar to hepatitis a, its incubation period is 15-60 days and is enterically transmitted, usually by fecal-oral transmission.

name: hepatitis e virus
query: Query: hepatitis e virus [SEP] Hepatitis e virus is a positive-stranded rna virus species in the genus hepevirus, causing enterically-transmitted non-A, non-B hepatitis (hepatitis e).

name: hepatocyte nuclear factor 1
query: Query: hepatocyte nuclear factor 1 [SEP] [MASK] nuclear factor 1 is a transcription factor and homeodomain protein that regulates the expression of a large [MASK] of hepatic proteins including serum albumin; beta-fibrinogen; and alpha 1-antitrypsin. It is composed of hetero- or homo-dimers of [MASK] nuclear factor 1-alpha and [MASK] nuclear factor 1-beta.

name: hepatocyte nuclear factor 4
query: Query: hepatocyte nuclear factor 4 [SEP] [MASK] nuclear factor 4 is a subfamily of nuclear receptors that regulate genetic transcription of a diverse group of genes involved in the synthesis of blood coagulation factors; and in glucose; cholesterol; and fatty acids metabolism.

name: hernia , femoral
query: Query: hernia , femoral [SEP] Femoral hernia is a groin hernia occurring inferior to the inguinal ligament and medial to the femoral vein and [MASK]. The femoral hernia sac has a small [MASK] but may enlarge considerably when it enters the [MASK] of the [MASK]. It is caused by defects in the [MASK].

name: hernia , umbilical
query: Query: hernia , umbilical [SEP] Umbilical hernia is a hernia due to an imperfect closure or weakness of the umbilical ring. It appears as a skin-covered protrusion at the umbilicus during crying, coughing, or straining. The hernia generally consists of omentum or small intestine. The vast majority of umbilical hernias are congenital but can be acquired due to severe abdominal distention.

name: herpes simplex
query: Query: herpes simplex [SEP] Herpes simplex is a group of acute infections caused by herpes simplex virus type 1 or type 2 that is characterized by the development of one or more small fluid-filled vesicles with a raised erythematous base on the skin or mucous membrane. It occurs as a primary infection or recurs due to a reactivation of a latent infection. (Dorland, 27th ed.)

name: heuristics
query: Query: heuristics [SEP] Heuristics is experience-based techniques for problem-solving, learning, and discovery that find a solution which is not guaranteed to be optimal, but sufficient for a given [MASK] of goals.

name: higher nervous activity
query: Query: higher nervous activity [SEP] Higher nervous activity is a term used in Eastern European research literature on brain and behavior physiology for cortical functions. It refers to the highest level of integrative function of the brain, centered in the cerebral cortex, regulating language, thought, and behavior via sensory, motor, and cognitive processes.

name: high pressure neurological syndrome
query: Query: high pressure neurological syndrome [SEP] High pressure neurological syndrome is a syndrome related to increased atmospheric pressure and characterized by tremors, nausea, dizziness, decreased motor and mental performance, and seizures. This condition may occur in those who dive deeply (c. 1000 ft) usually while breathing a mixture of oxygen and [MASK]. The condition is associated with a neuroexcitatory effect of [MASK].

name: high vocal center
query: Query: high vocal center [SEP] High vocal center is nucleus in the neostriatum of bird brains that sends signals for song production and receives auditory input. In some adult songbirds, research has shown that the size of this nucleus changes seasonally and that it exhibits neurogenesis.

name: hinge exons
query: Query: hinge exons [SEP] Hinge exons is [MASK] gene exons coding for the hinge region of the heavy chains between the first constant region (on the fab fragments) and the second constant region (on the [MASK]).

name: hip
query: Query: hip [SEP] Hip is the projecting part on each side of the body, formed by the side of the pelvis and the top portion of the femur.

name: hip dislocation
query: Query: hip dislocation [SEP] Hip dislocation is displacement of the femur bone from its normal position at the hip joint.

name: hip dysplasia , canine
query: Query: hip dysplasia , canine [SEP] Canine hip dysplasia is a hereditary disease of the hip joints in dogs. Signs of the disease may be evident any time after 4 weeks of age.

name: hip prosthesis
query: Query: hip prosthesis [SEP] Hip prosthesis is replacement for a hip joint.

name: histamine antagonists
query: Query: histamine antagonists [SEP] Histamine antagonists is drugs that bind to but do not activate histamine receptors, thereby blocking the actions of histamine or [MASK]. Classical antihistaminics block the histamine h1 receptors only.

name: histidine
query: Query: histidine [SEP] Histidine is an essential amino acid that is required for the production of histamine.

name: histidine kinase
query: Query: histidine kinase [SEP] Histidine kinase is a member of the transferase superfamily of proteins. In the activated state, protein-histidine kinase autophosphorylates at a histidine residue, subsequently transferring high-energy phosphoryl groups to an aspartate residue of the response-regulator domain, which results in a conformational shift in the effector domain. Histidine kinases mediate signal transduction in a wide range of processes involving cellular adaptation to environmental stress.

name: histology , comparative
query: Query: histology , comparative [SEP] Comparative histology is the study of the similarities and differences in the structures of homologous tissues across various species.

name: histone code
query: Query: histone code [SEP] Histone code is the specific patterns of changes made to histones, that are involved in assembly, maintenance, and alteration of chromatin structural states (such as euchromatin and heterochromatin). The changes are made by various histone modification processes that include acetylation; methylation; phosphorylation; and ubiquitination.

name: historically controlled study
query: Query: historically controlled study [SEP] Historically controlled study is a study that compares a group of participants receiving an intervention with a similar group from the past who did not.

name: history , ancient
query: Query: history , ancient [SEP] Ancient history is the period of history before 500 of the common era.

name: history of dentistry
query: Query: history of dentistry [SEP] History of dentistry is study of past events and development in the field of dentistry.

name: hiv antigens
query: Query: hiv antigens [SEP] Hiv antigens is antigens associated with specific proteins of the human adult T-cell immunodeficiency virus (hiv); also called HTLV-III-associated and lymphadenopathy-associated virus (lav) antigens.

name: hiv enhancer
query: Query: hiv enhancer [SEP] Hiv enhancer is cis-acting regulatory sequences in the hiv long terminal repeat (ltr) which play a major role in induction or augmentation of hiv gene expression in response to environmental stimuli such as mitogens, phorbol esters, or other viruses. The hiv enhancer is the binding site for many cellular transcription factors including the nuclear factor NF-kappa b.

name: hiv fusion inhibitors
query: Query: hiv fusion inhibitors [SEP] Hiv fusion inhibitors is inhibitors of the fusion of hiv to host cells, preventing viral entry. This includes compounds that block attachment of hiv envelope protein gp120 to cd4 receptors.

name: hn protein
query: Query: hn protein [SEP] Hn protein is glycoprotein from Sendai, para-influenza, Newcastle Disease, and other viruses that participates in binding the virus to cell-surface receptors. The hn protein possesses both hemagglutinin and neuraminidase activity.

name: holistic nursing
query: Query: holistic nursing [SEP] Holistic nursing is a philosophy of nursing practice that takes into account total patient care, considering the physical, emotional, social, economic, and spiritual needs of patients, their response to their illnesses, and the effect of illness on patients' abilities to meet self-care needs. (From Mosby's Medical, Nursing, & Allied Health Dictionary, 4th ed, p745)

name: home infusion therapy
query: Query: home infusion therapy [SEP] Home infusion therapy is use of any infusion therapy on an ambulatory, outpatient, or other non-institutionalized basis.

name: home nursing
query: Query: home nursing [SEP] Home nursing is nursing care given to an individual in the home. The care may be provided by a family member or a friend. Home nursing as care by a non-professional is differentiated from home care services provided by professionals: [MASK], [MASK], hospital, or other organized community group.

name: homes for the aged
query: Query: homes for the aged [SEP] Homes for the aged is geriatric long-term care facilities which provide supervision and assistance in activities of daily living with medical and nursing services when required.

name: honey
query: Query: honey [SEP] Honey is a sweet viscous liquid food, produced in the honey sacs of various bees from nectar collected from flowers. The nectar is ripened into honey by inversion of its sucrose sugar into fructose and glucose. It is somewhat acidic and has mild antiseptic properties, being sometimes used in the treatment of burns and lacerations.

name: hong kong
query: Query: hong kong [SEP] Hong kong is the former British crown colony located off the southeast coast of China, comprised of Hong Kong Island, Kowloon Peninsula, and New Territories. The three sites were ceded to the British by the Chinese respectively in 1841, 1860, and 1898. Hong Kong reverted to China in July 1997. The name represents the Cantonese pronunciation of the Chinese xianggang, fragrant port, from xiang, perfume and gang, port or harbor, with reference to its currents sweetened by fresh water from a [MASK] west of it.

name: hope
query: Query: hope [SEP] Hope is belief in a positive outcome.

name: hormone
query: Query: hormone [SEP] Hormone is chemical substances having a specific regulatory effect on the activity of a certain organ or organs. The term was originally applied to substances secreted by various endocrine glands and transported in the bloodstream to the target organs. It is sometimes extended to include those substances that are not produced by the endocrine glands but that have similar effects.

name: hormones , ectopic
query: Query: hormones , ectopic [SEP] Ectopic hormones is hormones released from neoplasms or from other cells that are not the usual sources of hormones.

name: hospital bed capacity , 100 to 299
query: Query: hospital bed capacity , 100 to 299 [SEP] 100 to 299 hospital bed capacity is hospital bed capacity , 100 to 299

name: hospital bed capacity , 500 and over
query: Query: hospital bed capacity , 500 and over [SEP] 500 and over hospital bed capacity is the number of beds 500 or more which a hospital has been designed and constructed to contain. It may also refer to the number of beds [MASK] up and staffed for use.

name: hospital bed capacity , under 100
query: Query: hospital bed capacity , under 100 [SEP] Under 100 hospital bed capacity is the number of beds under 100 which a hospital has been designed and constructed to contain. It may also refer to the number of beds [MASK] up and staffed for use.

name: hospital costs
query: Query: hospital costs [SEP] Hospital costs is the expenses incurred by a hospital in providing care. The hospital costs attributed to a particular patient care episode include the direct costs plus an appropriate proportion of the overhead for administration, personnel, building maintenance, equipment, etc. Hospital costs are one of the factors which determine [MASK] (the price the hospital sets for its services).

name: hospital distribution systems
query: Query: hospital distribution systems [SEP] Hospital distribution systems is systems for delivering hospital supplies, food, laundry, etc., to patient care areas.

name: hospital mortality
query: Query: hospital mortality [SEP] Hospital mortality is a vital statistic measuring or recording the rate of death from any cause in hospitalized populations.

name: hospital planning
query: Query: hospital planning [SEP] Hospital planning is areawide planning for hospitals or planning of a particular hospital unit on the basis of projected consumer need. This does not include [MASK] or architectural plans.

name: hospital rapid response team
query: Query: hospital rapid response team [SEP] Hospital rapid response team is multidisciplinary team most frequently consisting of intensive care unit trained personnel who are available 24 hours per day, 7 days per week for evaluation of patients who develop signs or symptoms of severe clinical deterioration.

name: hospital records
query: Query: hospital records [SEP] Hospital records is compilations of data on hospital activities and programs; excludes patient medical records.

name: hospital restructuring
query: Query: hospital restructuring [SEP] Hospital restructuring is reorganization of the hospital corporate structure.

name: hospitals , chronic disease
query: Query: hospitals , chronic disease [SEP] Chronic disease hospitals is hospitals which provide care to patients with long-term illnesses.

name: hospitals , county
query: Query: hospitals , county [SEP] County hospitals is hospitals controlled by the county government.

name: hospitals , district
query: Query: hospitals , district [SEP] District hospitals is government-controlled hospitals which represent the major health facility for a designated geographic area.

name: hospitals , group practice
query: Query: hospitals , group practice [SEP] Group practice hospitals is hospitals organized and controlled by a group of physicians who practice together and provide each other with mutual support.

name: hospitals , military
query: Query: hospitals , military [SEP] Military hospitals is hospitals which provide care for the military personnel and usually for their dependents.

name: hospitals , proprietary
query: Query: hospitals , proprietary [SEP] Proprietary hospitals is hospitals owned and operated by a corporation or an individual that operate on a for-profit basis, also referred to as investor-owned hospitals.

name: hospitals , psychiatric
query: Query: hospitals , psychiatric [SEP] Psychiatric hospitals is special hospitals which provide care to the [MASK] patient.

name: hospitals , rehabilitation
query: Query: hospitals , rehabilitation [SEP] Rehabilitation hospitals is free standing rehabilitation hospitals and rehabilitation units in acute care hospitals.  They provide an intensive inpatient rehabilitation program.

name: hospitals , religious
query: Query: hospitals , religious [SEP] Religious hospitals is private hospitals that are owned or sponsored by religious organizations.

name: hospitals , rural
query: Query: hospitals , rural [SEP] Rural hospitals is hospitals located in a rural area.

name: hospitals , state
query: Query: hospitals , state [SEP] State hospitals is hospitals controlled by agencies and departments of the [MASK].

name: hospitals , university
query: Query: hospitals , university [SEP] University hospitals is hospitals maintained by a university for the teaching of medical students, postgraduate training programs, and clinical research.

name: hospitals , veterans
query: Query: hospitals , veterans [SEP] Veterans hospitals is hospitals providing medical care to veterans of wars.

name: hospitals , voluntary
query: Query: hospitals , voluntary [SEP] Voluntary hospitals is private, not-for-profit hospitals that are autonomous, self-established, and self-supported.

name: hospital volunteers
query: Query: hospital volunteers [SEP] Hospital volunteers is individuals who donate their services to the hospital.

name: hot melt extrusion technology
query: Query: hot melt extrusion technology [SEP] Hot melt extrusion technology is solvent-free method for preparing numerous types of drug delivery systems and dosage forms for active pharmaceutical ingredients that have solubility issues. It involves pumping polymeric materials at temperatures above their glass transition temperature to mix in active pharmaceutical ingredients with or without binders thus forming an amorphous product with an  increase in the dissolution profile for the active pharmaceutical ingredients.

name: hot springs
query: Query: hot springs [SEP] Hot springs is habitat of hot water naturally heated by underlying geologic processes. Surface hot springs have been used for balneology. Underwater hot springs are called hydrothermal vents.

name: house calls
query: Query: house calls [SEP] House calls is visits to the patient's home by professional personnel for the purpose of diagnosis and/or treatment.

name: household articles
query: Query: household articles [SEP] Household articles is various material objects and items in the home. It includes temporary or permanent machinery and appliances. It does not include furniture or interior furnishings (furniture see interior design and furnishings; interior furnishings see interior design and furnishings).

name: household products
query: Query: household products [SEP] Household products is substances or materials used in the course of housekeeping or personal routine.

name: housing for the elderly
query: Query: housing for the elderly [SEP] Housing for the elderly is housing arrangements for the elderly or aged, intended to foster [MASK]. The housing may take the form of group homes or small apartments. It is available to the economically self-supporting but the concept includes housing for the elderly with some physical limitations. The concept should be differentiated from homes for the aged which is restricted to long-term geriatric facilities providing supervised medical and nursing services.

name: human characteristics
query: Query: human characteristics [SEP] Human characteristics is the fundamental dispositions and traits of humans. (Merriam-Webster's Collegiate Dictionary, 10th ed)

name: human embryonic stem cells
query: Query: human embryonic stem cells [SEP] Human embryonic stem cells is a type of pluripotent stem cells derived from early stage human embryos, up to and including the blastocyst stage.

name: human genome project
query: Query: human genome project [SEP] Human genome project is a coordinated effort of researchers to map (chromosome mapping) and sequence (sequence analysis, dna) the human genome.

name: human growth hormone
query: Query: human growth hormone [SEP] Human growth hormone is a 191-amino acid polypeptide hormone secreted by the human adenohypophysis (pituitary gland, anterior), also known as gh or somatotropin. Synthetic growth hormone, termed somatropin, has replaced the natural form in therapeutic usage such as treatment of dwarfism in children with growth hormone deficiency.

name: human umbilical vein endothelial cells
query: Query: human umbilical vein endothelial cells [SEP] Human umbilical vein endothelial cells is endothelial cells that line venous vessels of the umbilical cord.

name: humidity
query: Query: humidity [SEP] Humidity is a measure of the amount of water vapor in the air.

name: hungary
query: Query: hungary [SEP] Hungary is a country in Europe, northwest of Romania, south of Slovakia, and east of Austria. The capital is Budapest.

name: hybrid cells
query: Query: hybrid cells [SEP] Hybrid cells is any cell, other than a zygote, that contains elements (such as nuclei and cytoplasm) from two or more different cells, usually produced by artificial cell fusion.

name: hybridization , genetic
query: Query: hybridization , genetic [SEP] Genetic hybridization is the genetic process of crossbreeding between genetically dissimilar parents to produce a hybrid.

name: hydrogen bonding
query: Query: hydrogen bonding [SEP] Hydrogen bonding is a low-energy attractive force between hydrogen and another element. It plays a major role in determining the properties of water, proteins, and other compounds.

name: hydrolysis
query: Query: hydrolysis [SEP] Hydrolysis is the process of cleaving a chemical compound by the addition of a molecule of water.

name: hydrophobic and hydrophilic interactions
query: Query: hydrophobic and hydrophilic interactions [SEP] Hydrophobic and hydrophilic interactions is the thermodynamic interaction between a substance and water.

name: hydroxyl radical
query: Query: hydroxyl radical [SEP] Hydroxyl radical is the univalent radical oh. Hydroxyl radical is a potent oxidizing agent.

name: hygiene hypothesis
query: Query: hygiene hypothesis [SEP] Hygiene hypothesis is the theory that infectious agents, symbiotic microorganisms, and parasites are normal stimulants for the maturation of the immune system toward a balanced immune response. The theory predicts that lack of such stimulation leads to allergies and autoimmune diseases.

name: hyperplasia
query: Query: hyperplasia [SEP] Hyperplasia is an increase in the number of cells in a tissue or organ without tumor formation. It differs from hypertrophy, which is an increase in bulk without an increase in the number of cells.

name: hypertension , portal
query: Query: hypertension , portal [SEP] Portal hypertension is abnormal increase of resistance to blood flow within the hepatic portal system, frequently seen in liver cirrhosis and conditions with obstruction of the portal vein.

name: hypertension , renal
query: Query: hypertension , renal [SEP] Renal hypertension is persistent high blood pressure due to kidney diseases, such as those involving the renal parenchyma, the renal vasculature, or tumors that secrete renin.

name: hypertensive encephalopathy
query: Query: hypertensive encephalopathy [SEP] Hypertensive encephalopathy is brain dysfunction or damage resulting from sustained [MASK]. When blood pressure exceeds the limits of cerebral autoregulation, [MASK] is impaired (brain ischemia). Clinical manifestations include headache; nausea; vomiting; seizures; altered mental status (in some cases progressing to coma); papilledema; and retinal hemorrhage.

name: hypertrophy
query: Query: hypertrophy [SEP] Hypertrophy is general increase in bulk of a part or organ due to cell enlargement and accumulation of fluids and secretions, not due to tumor formation, nor to an increase in the number of cells (hyperplasia).

name: hypotension
query: Query: hypotension [SEP] Hypotension is abnormally low blood pressure that can result in inadequate blood flow to the brain and other vital organs. Common symptom is dizziness but greater negative impacts on the body occur when there is prolonged depravation of oxygen and nutrients.

name: hypothalamic area , lateral
query: Query: hypothalamic area , lateral [SEP] Lateral hypothalamic area is area in the hypothalamus bounded medially by the mammillothalamic tract and the anterior column of the fornix (brain). The medial edge of the internal capsule and the subthalamic region form its lateral boundary. It contains the lateral hypothalamic nucleus, tuberomammillary nucleus, lateral tuberal nuclei, and fibers of the medial forebrain bundle.

name: hypothermia
query: Query: hypothermia [SEP] Hypothermia is lower than normal body temperature, especially in warm-blooded animals.

name: hypoxia , brain
query: Query: hypoxia , brain [SEP] Brain hypoxia is a reduction in brain oxygen supply due to anoxemia (a reduced amount of oxygen being carried in the blood by hemoglobin), or to a restriction of the blood supply to the brain, or both. Severe hypoxia is referred to as anoxia, and is a relatively common cause of injury to the central nervous system. Prolonged brain anoxia may lead to brain death or a [MASK]. Histologically, this condition is characterized by neuronal loss which is most prominent in the hippocampus; globus pallidus; cerebellum; and inferior olives.

name: ice cover
query: Query: ice cover [SEP] Ice cover is a thick mass of ice formed over large regions of land; [MASK]; [MASK]; ponds; or seawater.

name: ice cream
query: Query: ice cream [SEP] Ice cream is a frozen dairy food made from cream or butterfat, milk, sugar, and flavorings. Frozen custard and French-type ice creams also contain eggs.

name: id
query: Query: id [SEP] Id is the part of the personality structure which harbors the [MASK] instinctive desires and strivings of the individual.

name: ideal body weight
query: Query: ideal body weight [SEP] Ideal body weight is expected weight of a healthy normal individual based on age, [MASK], and height. Thus, a malnourished person would weigh less than their ideal body weight.

name: identity crisis
query: Query: identity crisis [SEP] Identity crisis is chaotic concept of self wherein one's role in life appears to be an insoluble dilemma often expressed by isolation, withdrawal, rebellion and extremism.

name: idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
query: Query: idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis [SEP] Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis is a common interstitial lung disease of unknown etiology, usually occurring between 50-70 years of age. Clinically, it is characterized by an insidious onset of breathlessness with exertion and a nonproductive [MASK], leading to progressive dyspnea. Pathological features show scant interstitial inflammation, patchy collagen fibrosis, prominent fibroblast proliferation foci, and microscopic honeycomb change.

name: iliac artery
query: Query: iliac artery [SEP] Iliac artery is either of two large arteries originating from the abdominal aorta; they supply blood to the pelvis, [MASK] and legs.

name: immersion foot
query: Query: immersion foot [SEP] Immersion [MASK] is a condition of the [MASK] produced by prolonged exposure of the [MASK] to water. Exposure for 48 hours or more to warm water causes tropical immersion [MASK] or warm-water immersion [MASK] common in Vietnam where troops were exposed to prolonged or repeated wading in paddy fields or [MASK]. Trench [MASK] results from prolonged exposure to cold, without actual freezing. It was common in trench warfare during World War i, when soldiers stood, sometimes for hours, in trenches with a few inches of cold water in them. (Andrews' Diseases of the Skin, 8th ed, p27)

name: immobilized nucleic acids
query: Query: immobilized nucleic acids [SEP] Immobilized nucleic acids is dna or rna bound to a substrate thereby having fixed positions.

name: immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome
query: Query: immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome [SEP] [MASK] inflammatory syndrome is exuberant inflammatory response towards a previously acquired or undiagnosed [MASK]. It is frequently seen in aids patients following antiretroviral treatment.

name: immune sera
query: Query: immune sera [SEP] Immune sera is serum that contains antibodies. It is obtained from an animal that has been immunized either by antigen injection or infection with microorganisms containing the antigen.

name: immunity , herd
query: Query: immunity , herd [SEP] Herd immunity is the non-susceptibility to infection of a large group of individuals in a population. a variety of factors can be responsible for herd immunity and this gives rise to the different definitions used in the literature. Most commonly, herd immunity refers to the case when, if most of the population is immune, infection of a single individual will not cause an epidemic. Also, in such immunized populations, susceptible individuals are not likely to become infected. Herd immunity can also refer to the case when unprotected individuals fail to contract a disease because the infecting organism has been banished from the population.

name: immunity , humoral
query: Query: immunity , humoral [SEP] Humoral immunity is antibody-mediated immune response. Humoral immunity is brought about by antibody formation, resulting from th2 cells activating b-lymphocytes, followed by complement activation.

name: immunity , mucosal
query: Query: immunity , mucosal [SEP] Mucosal immunity is nonsusceptibility to the pathogenic effects of foreign microorganisms or antigenic substances as a result of antibody secretions of the mucous membranes. Mucosal epithelia in the gastrointestinal, respiratory, and reproductive tracts produce a form of IgA (immunoglobulin a, secretory) that serves to protect these ports of entry into the body.

name: immunization , passive
query: Query: immunization , passive [SEP] Passive immunization is transfer of immunity from immunized to non-immune host by administration of serum antibodies, or transplantation of lymphocytes (adoptive transfer).

name: immunoglobulin joining region
query: Query: immunoglobulin joining region [SEP] Immunoglobulin joining region is a segment of the [MASK], encoded by the [MASK] genes in the j segment where, during the maturation of b-lymphocytes; the gene segment for the variable region upstream is joined to a constant region gene segment downstream. The exact position of joining of the two gene segments is variable and contributes to antibody diversity. It is distinguished from the immunoglobulin j chains; a separate polypeptide that serves as a linkage piece in polymeric iga or igm.

name: immunoglobulin light chains , surrogate
query: Query: immunoglobulin light chains , surrogate [SEP] Surrogate immunoglobulin light chains is an immunolglobulin light chain-like protein composed of an immunoglobulin variable REGION-like peptide (such as light chain like lambda5 peptide) and an immunoglobulin constant REGION-like peptide (such as Vpreb1 peptide). Surrogate light chains associate with mu [MASK] in place of a conventional immunoglobulin light chains to form pre-B cell receptors.

name: immunosorbent techniques
query: Query: immunosorbent techniques [SEP] Immunosorbent techniques is techniques for removal by [MASK] and subsequent elution of a specific antibody or antigen using an immunosorbent containing the homologous antigen or antibody.

name: impulsive behavior
query: Query: impulsive behavior [SEP] Impulsive behavior is an act performed without delay, reflection, voluntary direction or obvious control in response to a stimulus.

name: inappropriate prescribing
query: Query: inappropriate prescribing [SEP] Inappropriate prescribing is the practice of administering medications in a manner that poses more risk than benefit, particularly where safer alternatives exist.

name: incidence
query: Query: incidence [SEP] Incidence is the number of new cases of a given disease during a given period in a specified population. It also is used for the rate at which new events occur in a defined population. It is differentiated from [MASK], which refers to all cases in the population at a given time.

name: incidental findings
query: Query: incidental findings [SEP] Incidental findings is unanticipated information discovered in the course of testing or medical care. Used in discussions of information that may have social or psychological consequences, such as when it is learned that a child's biological [MASK] is someone other than the putative [MASK], or that a person tested for one disease or disorder has, or is at risk for, something else.

name: income
query: Query: income [SEP] Income is revenues or receipts accruing from business enterprise, labor, or invested capital.

name: income tax
query: Query: income tax [SEP] Income tax is tax on the net income of an individual, organization, or business.

name: independent medical evaluation
query: Query: independent medical evaluation [SEP] Independent medical evaluation is an assessment of health status requested by third parties (e.g. insurers, adjudicating bodies, law enforcement, attorneys, etc) on a subject’s functional ability. Such information may be used in optimizing treatment or making informed decisions on compensation.

name: independent practice associations
query: Query: independent practice associations [SEP] Independent practice associations is a partnership, corporation, association, or other legal entity that enters into an arrangement for the provision of services with persons who are licensed to practice medicine, osteopathy, and dentistry, and with other care personnel. Under an ipa arrangement, licensed professional persons provide services through the entity in accordance with a mutually accepted compensation arrangement, while retaining their private practices. Services under the ipa are marketed through a prepaid health plan. (From Facts on File Dictionary of Health Care Management, 1988)

name: index
query: Query: index [SEP] Index is work providing an analytical subject approach to materials in a field of knowledge.

name: index of orthodontic treatment need
query: Query: index of orthodontic treatment need [SEP] Index of orthodontic treatment need is a dental health survey developed to evaluate a patient's orthodontic treatment need and priority for orthodontic care. The index is based on an assessment of degree of malocclusion and the potential aesthetic and dental [MASK] of the treatment under consideration.

name: india
query: Query: india [SEP] India is a country in southern Asia, bordering the Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal, between Burma and Pakistan. The capitol is New Delhi.

name: indiana
query: Query: indiana [SEP] Indiana is state bounded on the north by [MASK] Michigan and Michigan, on the east by Ohio, on the south by Kentucky, and on the west by Illinois.

name: indian ocean islands
query: Query: indian ocean islands [SEP] Indian ocean islands is numerous islands in the Indian Ocean situated east of Madagascar, north to the Arabian Sea and east to Sri Lanka. Included are comoros (republic), madagascar (republic), Maldives (republic), mauritius (parliamentary democracy), Pemba (administered by [MASK]), reunion (a department of France), and seychelles (republic).

name: indicator , reagent , or diagnostic aid
query: Query: indicator , reagent , or diagnostic aid [SEP] Or diagnostic aid reagent indicator is indicator , reagent , or diagnostic aid

name: individual behavior
query: Query: individual behavior [SEP] Individual behavior is the response of an individual to its environment.

name: indole alkaloids
query: Query: indole alkaloids [SEP] Indole alkaloids is group of alkaloids containing a benzylpyrrole group (derived from tryptophan).

name: induced pluripotent stem cells
query: Query: induced pluripotent stem cells [SEP] Induced pluripotent stem cells is cells from adult organisms that have been reprogrammed into a pluripotential state similar to that of embryonic stem cells.

name: induction chemotherapy
