query: Query: induction chemotherapy [SEP] Induction chemotherapy is initial drug treatment designed to bring about remission induction. It is typically a short-term and high-dose drug treatment that is followed by [MASK] and then [MASK].

name: industrial microbiology
query: Query: industrial microbiology [SEP] Industrial microbiology is the study, utilization, and manipulation of those microorganisms capable of economically producing desirable substances or changes in substances, and the control of undesirable microorganisms.

name: industrial waste
query: Query: industrial waste [SEP] Industrial waste is worthless, damaged, defective, superfluous or effluent material from industrial operations.

name: infant , extremely premature
query: Query: infant , extremely premature [SEP] Extremely premature infant is a human infant born before 28 weeks of gestation.

name: infant behavior
query: Query: infant behavior [SEP] Infant behavior is any observable response or action of a neonate or infant up through the age of 23 months.

name: infant formula
query: Query: infant formula [SEP] Infant formula is formulations for the nutrition of infants that are substituted for [MASK].

name: infant health
query: Query: infant health [SEP] Infant health is the concept covering the physical and mental conditions of infants.

name: infant welfare
query: Query: infant welfare [SEP] Infant welfare is organized efforts by communities or organizations to improve the health and well-being of infants.

name: infarction , anterior cerebral artery
query: Query: infarction , anterior cerebral artery [SEP] Anterior cerebral artery infarction is necrosis occurring in the anterior cerebral artery system, including branches such as Heubner's artery. These arteries supply blood to the medial and superior parts of the cerebral hemisphere, Infarction in the anterior cerebral artery usually results in sensory and motor impairment in the lower body.

name: infarction , middle cerebral artery
query: Query: infarction , middle cerebral artery [SEP] Middle cerebral artery infarction is necrosis occurring in the middle cerebral artery distribution system which brings blood to the entire lateral aspects of each cerebral hemisphere. Clinical signs include impaired cognition; aphasia; agraphia; weak and numbness in the face and [MASK], contralaterally or bilaterally depending on the infarction.

name: infarction , posterior cerebral artery
query: Query: infarction , posterior cerebral artery [SEP] Posterior cerebral artery infarction is necrosis induced by ischemia in the posterior cerebral artery distribution system which supplies portions of the brain stem; the thalamus; temporal lobe, and occipital lobe. Depending on the size and location of infarction, clinical features include olfaction disorders and visual problems (agnosia; alexia; hemianopsia).

name: infection control practitioners
query: Query: infection control practitioners [SEP] Infection control practitioners is physicians or other qualified individuals responsible for implementing and overseeing the policies and procedures followed by a health care facility to reduce the risk of infection to patients and staff.

name: infectious disease incubation period
query: Query: infectious disease incubation period [SEP] Infectious disease incubation period is the amount time between exposure to an infectious agent and becoming symptomatic.

name: infectious disease medicine
query: Query: infectious disease medicine [SEP] Infectious disease medicine is a branch of internal medicine concerned with the diagnosis and treatment of infectious diseases.

name: infectious disease transmission , vertical
query: Query: infectious disease transmission , vertical [SEP] Vertical infectious disease transmission is the transmission of infectious disease or pathogens from one generation to another. It includes transmission in utero or intrapartum by exposure to blood and secretions, and postpartum exposure via breastfeeding.

name: infertility , male
query: Query: infertility , male [SEP] Male infertility is the inability of the male to effect fertilization of an ovum after a specified period of unprotected intercourse. Male sterility is permanent infertility.

name: inflation , economic
query: Query: inflation , economic [SEP] Economic inflation is an increase in the volume of money and credit relative to available goods resulting in a substantial and continuing rise in the general price level.

name: influenza , human
query: Query: influenza , human [SEP] Human influenza is an acute viral infection in humans involving the respiratory tract. It is marked by inflammation of the nasal mucosa; the pharynx; and conjunctiva, and by headache and severe, often generalized, myalgia.

name: influenza in birds
query: Query: influenza in birds [SEP] Influenza in birds is infection of domestic and wild fowl and other birds with influenza a virus. Avian influenza usually does not sicken birds, but can be highly pathogenic and fatal in domestic poultry.

name: influenza vaccines
query: Query: influenza vaccines [SEP] Influenza vaccines is vaccines used to prevent infection by viruses in the family orthomyxoviridae. It includes both killed and attenuated vaccines. The composition of the vaccines is changed each year in response to antigenic shifts and changes in [MASK] of influenza virus strains. The flu vaccines may be mono- or multi-valent, which contains one or more influenzavirus a and influenzavirus b strains.

name: informal sector
query: Query: informal sector [SEP] Informal sector is a component of the private sector characterized by ease of entry; reliance on indigenous resources; family ownership; small scale operations;  skills acquired outside of the formal sector; and unregulated markets.

name: information seeking behavior
query: Query: information seeking behavior [SEP] Information seeking behavior is how information is gathered in personal, academic or work environments and the resources used.

name: infrared rays
query: Query: infrared rays [SEP] Infrared rays is that portion of the electromagnetic spectrum usually sensed as heat. Infrared wavelengths are longer than those of visible light, extending into the microwave frequencies. They are used therapeutically as heat, and also to warm food in restaurants.

name: infusions , spinal
query: Query: infusions , spinal [SEP] Spinal infusions is the administration of medication by insertion of a tiny needle or catheter into the spinal sac or epidural cavity.

name: infusions , subcutaneous
query: Query: infusions , subcutaneous [SEP] Subcutaneous infusions is the administration of liquid medication or nutrients under the skin, usually over minutes or hours.

name: inguinal canal
query: Query: inguinal canal [SEP] Inguinal canal is the tunnel in the lower anterior [MASK] through which the spermatic cord, in the male; round ligament, in the female; nerves; and vessels pass. Its internal end is at the deep inguinal ring and its external end is at the superficial inguinal ring.

name: inhibitory concentration 50
query: Query: inhibitory concentration 50 [SEP] Inhibitory concentration 50 is the concentration of a compound needed to reduce population growth of organisms, including eukaryotic cells, by 50% in vitro. Though often expressed to denote in vitro antibacterial activity, it is also used as a benchmark for cytotoxicity to eukaryotic cells in culture.

name: injections , intravenous
query: Query: injections , intravenous [SEP] Intravenous injections is injections made into a vein for therapeutic or experimental purposes.

name: injections , jet
query: Query: injections , jet [SEP] Jet injections is the injection of solutions into the skin by compressed air devices so that only the solution pierces the skin.

name: injury or poisoning
query: Query: injury or poisoning [SEP] Injury or poisoning is injury or poisoning

name: injury severity score
query: Query: injury severity score [SEP] Injury severity score is an anatomic severity scale based on the Abbreviated Injury Scale (ais) and developed specifically to score multiple traumatic injuries. It has been used as a predictor of mortality.

name: ink
query: Query: ink [SEP] Ink is pigmented or colored fluid used for writing, staining, painting, drawing, printing, or copying images.

name: inorganic chemical
query: Query: inorganic chemical [SEP] Inorganic chemical is compounds that do not contain both carbon and hydrogen.

name: inositol
query: Query: inositol [SEP] Inositol is an isomer of glucose that has traditionally been considered to be a b vitamin although it has an uncertain status as a vitamin and a deficiency syndrome has not been identified in man. (From Martindale, The Extra Pharmacopoeia, 30th ed, p1379) Inositol [MASK] are important in signal transduction.

name: insomnia , fatal familial
query: Query: insomnia , fatal familial [SEP] Fatal familial insomnia is an autosomal dominant disorder characterized by degeneration of the thalamus and progressive insomnia. It is caused by a mutation in the prion protein (prions).

name: institutional practice
query: Query: institutional practice [SEP] Institutional practice is professional practice as an employee or contractee of a health care institution.

name: instructional film and video
query: Query: instructional film and video [SEP] Instructional film and video is works consisting of nonfiction films and video designed to teach, instruct, or train. (From Moving Image Materials: Genre Terms, 1988)

name: insulator elements
query: Query: insulator elements [SEP] Insulator elements is nucleic acid regulatory sequences that limit or oppose the action of enhancer elements and define the boundary between differentially regulated gene loci.

name: insulin , regular , human
query: Query: insulin , regular , human [SEP] Human regular insulin is regular insulin preparations that contain the human insulin peptide sequence.

name: insulin antagonists
query: Query: insulin antagonists [SEP] Insulin antagonists is compounds which inhibit or antagonize the biosynthesis or action of insulin.

name: insulin coma
query: Query: insulin coma [SEP] Insulin coma is severe hypoglycemia induced by a large dose of exogenous insulin resulting in a coma or profound state of unconsciousness from which the individual cannot be aroused.

name: insulin secretion
query: Query: insulin secretion [SEP] Insulin secretion is production and release of insulin from pancreatic beta cells that primarily occurs in response to elevated blood glucose levels.

name: insurance , accident
query: Query: insurance , accident [SEP] Accident insurance is insurance providing coverage for physical injury suffered as a result of unavoidable circumstances.

name: insurance , hospitalization
query: Query: insurance , hospitalization [SEP] Hospitalization insurance is health insurance providing benefits to cover or partly cover hospital expenses.

name: insurance , liability
query: Query: insurance , liability [SEP] Liability insurance is insurance against loss resulting from liability for injury or damage to the persons or property of others.

name: insurance , life
query: Query: insurance , life [SEP] Life insurance is insurance providing for payment of a stipulated sum to a designated beneficiary upon death of the insured.

name: insurance , major medical
query: Query: insurance , major medical [SEP] Major medical insurance is insurance providing a broad range of medical services and supplies, when prescribed by a physician, whether or not the patient is hospitalized. It frequently is an extension of a basic policy and benefits will not begin until the basic policy is exhausted.

name: insurance , nursing services
query: Query: insurance , nursing services [SEP] Nursing services insurance is insurance providing benefits for the costs of care provided by nurses, especially nurse practitioners and [MASK].

name: insurance , surgical
query: Query: insurance , surgical [SEP] Surgical insurance is a specific type of health insurance which provides surgeons' fees for specified amounts according to the type of surgery listed in the policy.

name: insurance carriers
query: Query: insurance carriers [SEP] Insurance carriers is organizations which assume the financial responsibility for the risks of policyholders.

name: insurance claim reporting
query: Query: insurance claim reporting [SEP] Insurance claim reporting is the design, completion, and filing of forms with the insurer.

name: insurance claim review
query: Query: insurance claim review [SEP] Insurance claim review is review of claims by insurance companies to determine liability and amount of payment for various services. The review may also include determination of eligibility of the claimant or beneficiary or of the provider of the benefit; determination that the benefit is covered or not payable under another policy; or determination that the service was necessary and of reasonable cost and quality.

name: integrative medicine
query: Query: integrative medicine [SEP] Integrative medicine is the discipline concerned with using the combination of conventional allopathic medicine and alternative medicine to address the biological, psychological, social, and spiritual aspects of health and illness.

name: integrative oncology
query: Query: integrative oncology [SEP] Integrative oncology is these evidence-based therapies to reduce symptoms associated with treatment of cancer.

name: integrin beta chains
query: Query: integrin beta chains [SEP] Integrin beta chains is integrin beta chains combine with integrin alpha chains to form heterodimeric cell surface receptors. Integrins have traditionally been classified into functional groups based on the identity of one of three beta chains present in the heterodimer. The beta chain is necessary and sufficient for integrin-dependent signaling. Its short cytoplasmic tail contains sequences critical for inside-out signaling.

name: intensive care , neonatal
query: Query: intensive care , neonatal [SEP] Neonatal intensive care is continuous care and monitoring of newborn infants with life-threatening conditions, in any setting.

name: intensive care units , neonatal
query: Query: intensive care units , neonatal [SEP] Neonatal intensive care units is hospital units providing continuing surveillance and care to acutely ill newborn infants.

name: intention
query: Query: intention [SEP] Intention is what a person has in mind to do or bring about.

name: intention to treat analysis
query: Query: intention to treat analysis [SEP] Intention to treat analysis is strategy for the analysis of randomized controlled trials as topic that compares patients in the groups to which they were originally randomly assigned.

name: interleukin 1 receptor antagonist protein
query: Query: interleukin 1 receptor antagonist protein [SEP] Interleukin 1 receptor antagonist protein is a ligand that binds to but fails to activate the interleukin 1 receptor. It plays an inhibitory role in the regulation of inflammation and fever. Several isoforms of the protein exist due to multiple [MASK] of its mRNA.

name: intermediate back muscles
query: Query: intermediate back muscles [SEP] Intermediate back muscles is two muscles, the serratus posterior superior and serratus posterior inferior, located in between the deep and the [MASK] layers. Their function is to control thorax movement.

name: intermittent renal replacement therapy
query: Query: intermittent renal replacement therapy [SEP] Intermittent renal replacement therapy is procedures with non-continuous blood purification (e.g., dialysis, filtration and/or perfusion) via vascular access by increasing blood flow rate compared to continuous rrt.

name: intermittent urethral catheterization
query: Query: intermittent urethral catheterization [SEP] Intermittent urethral catheterization is insertion of a catheter into the urethra to drain the urine from the [MASK] at intervals as needed.

name: internal capsule
query: Query: internal capsule [SEP] Internal capsule is [MASK] matter pathway, flanked by nuclear masses, consisting of both afferent and efferent fibers projecting between the [MASK] matter and the brainstem. It consists of three distinct parts: an anterior limb, posterior limb, and genu.

name: international classification of diseases
query: Query: international classification of diseases [SEP] International classification of diseases is a system of categories to which morbid entries are assigned according to established criteria. Included is the entire range of conditions in a manageable number of categories, grouped to facilitate mortality reporting. It is produced by the [MASK] Organization (From icd-10, p1). The Clinical Modifications, produced by the united states dept. of health and human services, are larger extensions used for morbidity and general epidemiological purposes, primarily in the u.s.

name: international classification of functioning , disability and health
query: Query: international classification of functioning , disability and health [SEP] Disability and [MASK] classification of functioning is the [MASK] Organization's classification categories of health and health-related domains. The International Classification of Functioning, Disability and Health (icf) consists of two lists: a list of body functions and structure, and a list of domains of activity and participation. The icf also includes a list of environmental factors.

name: international educational exchange
query: Query: international educational exchange [SEP] International educational exchange is the exchange of students or professional personnel between countries done under the auspices of an organization for the purpose of further education.

name: international health regulations
query: Query: international health regulations [SEP] [MASK] regulations is regulations to prevent, protect against, control and provide a public health response to the international spread of disease in ways that are commensurate with and restricted to public health risks. (www.who.int/features/qa/39/en)

name: international normalized ratio
query: Query: international normalized ratio [SEP] International normalized ratio is system established by the [MASK] Organization and the International Committee on Thrombosis and Hemostasis for monitoring and reporting blood coagulation tests. Under this system, results are standardized using the International Sensitivity Index for the particular test reagent/instrument combination used.

name: international system of units
query: Query: international system of units [SEP] International system of units is a system of physical units in which the fundamental quantities are length, time, mass, electric current, temperature, luminous intensity, and amount of substance, and the corresponding units are the meter, second, kilogram, ampere, kelvin, candela, and mole. The system has been given official status and recommended for universal use by the General Conference on Weights and Measures.

name: internet access
query: Query: internet access [SEP] Internet access is ability to connect to access services available on the Internet.

name: internet of things
query: Query: internet of things [SEP] Internet of things is networking capability which facilitates information flow to and from objects and devices using the internet.

name: interpersonal psychotherapy
query: Query: interpersonal psychotherapy [SEP] Interpersonal psychotherapy is interpersonal modification of psychodynamic psychotherapy. Therapy is present-focused and seeks to resolve problems in interpersonal relations. Aspects of attachment theory are used to analyze how past relationships affect current relationships.

name: interrupted time series analysis
query: Query: interrupted time series analysis [SEP] Interrupted time series analysis is a study that uses observations at multiple time points before and after an intervention (the "interruption"), in an attempt to detect whether the intervention has had an effect significantly greater than any underlying trend over time.

name: interview , psychological
query: Query: interview , psychological [SEP] Psychological interview is a directed conversation aimed at eliciting information for psychiatric diagnosis, evaluation, treatment planning, etc. The interview may be conducted by a social worker or psychologist.

name: interviews as topic
query: Query: interviews as topic [SEP] Interviews as topic is works about conversations with an individual or individuals held in order to obtain information about their background and other personal biographical data, their attitudes and opinions, etc. It includes works about school admission or job interviews.

name: intestinal diseases , parasitic
query: Query: intestinal diseases , parasitic [SEP] Parasitic intestinal diseases is infections of the intestines with parasites, commonly involving parasitic worms. Infections with roundworms (nematode infections) and tapeworms (cestode infections) are also known as helminthiasis.

name: intestinal elimination
query: Query: intestinal elimination [SEP] Intestinal elimination is the discharge of substances from the blood supply into the intestinal lumen for excretion by defecation.

name: intestinal perforation
query: Query: intestinal perforation [SEP] Intestinal perforation is opening or penetration through the wall of the intestines.

name: intestinal secretions
query: Query: intestinal secretions [SEP] Intestinal secretions is fluids originating from the epithelial lining of the intestines, adjoining exocrine glands and from organs such as the liver, which empty into the cavity of the intestines.

name: intracranial hypotension
query: Query: intracranial hypotension [SEP] Intracranial hypotension is reduction of cerebrospinal fluid pressure characterized clinically by orthostatic headache and occasionally by an abducens nerve palsy; hearing loss; nausea; [MASK] stiffness, and other symptoms. This condition may be spontaneous or secondary to cerebrospinal fluid leak; [MASK]; neurosurgical procedures; [MASK]; uremia; trauma (see also craniocerebral trauma); and other processes. Chronic hypotension may be associated with subdural hematomas (see hematoma, subdural) or hygromas. (From Semin Neurol 1996 Mar;16(1):5-10; Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp637-8)

name: intramuscular absorption
query: Query: intramuscular absorption [SEP] Intramuscular absorption is uptake of substances via muscle tissue.

name: intraocular pressure
query: Query: intraocular pressure [SEP] Intraocular pressure is the pressure of the fluids in the eye.

name: intraoperative care
query: Query: intraoperative care [SEP] Intraoperative care is patient care procedures performed during the operation that are ancillary to the actual surgery. It includes monitoring, fluid therapy, medication, transfusion, anesthesia, radiography, and laboratory tests.

name: intrauterine device migration
query: Query: intrauterine device migration [SEP] [MASK] migration is the shifting in position or location of an [MASK] from its original placement.

name: intrinsically disordered proteins
query: Query: intrinsically disordered proteins [SEP] Intrinsically disordered proteins is functional proteins that do not have unique, stable, folded, three-dimensional native structures or that possess non-ordered regions under physiological conditions. They are characterized by extraordinary structural flexibility and plasticity, which enable them to adopt different conformations in response to different stimuli or different interactions.

name: introduced species
query: Query: introduced species [SEP] Introduced species is non-native organisms brought into a region, habitat, or ecosystem by human activity.

name: introns
query: Query: introns [SEP] Introns is sequences of dna in the genes that are located between the exons. They are transcribed along with the exons but are removed from the primary gene transcript by rna splicing to leave mature rna. Some introns code for separate genes.

name: intuition
query: Query: intuition [SEP] Intuition is knowing or understanding without conscious use of reasoning. (Thesaurus of eric Descriptors, 1994)

name: inverted repeat sequences
query: Query: inverted repeat sequences [SEP] Inverted repeat sequences is copies of nucleic acid sequence that are arranged in opposing orientation. They may lie adjacent to each other (tandem) or be separated by some sequence that is not part of the repeat (hyphenated). They may be true palindromic repeats, i.e. read the same backwards as forward, or complementary which reads as the base complement in the opposite orientation. Complementary inverted repeats have the potential to form hairpin loop or stem-loop structures which results in cruciform structures (such as cruciform dna) when the complementary inverted repeats occur in double stranded regions.

name: investments
query: Query: investments [SEP] Investments is use for articles on the investing of funds for income or profit.

name: in vitro oocyte maturation techniques
query: Query: in vitro oocyte maturation techniques [SEP] In vitro oocyte maturation techniques is methods used to induce premature oocytes, that are maintained in tissue culture, to progress through developmental stages including to a stage that is competent to undergo fertilization.

name: iodine isotopes
query: Query: iodine isotopes [SEP] Iodine isotopes is stable iodine atoms that have the same atomic number as the element iodine, but differ in atomic weight. i-127 is the only naturally occurring stable iodine isotope.

name: ion channel gating
query: Query: ion channel gating [SEP] Ion channel gating is the opening and closing of ion channels due to a stimulus. The stimulus can be a change in membrane potential (voltage-gated), drugs or chemical transmitters (ligand-gated), or a mechanical deformation. Gating is thought to involve conformational changes of the ion channel which alters selective permeability.

name: ion exchange
query: Query: ion exchange [SEP] Ion exchange is reversible chemical reaction between a solid, often one of the ion exchange resins, and a fluid whereby ions may be exchanged from one substance to another. This technique is used in [MASK], in research, and in industry.

name: ionic liquids
query: Query: ionic liquids [SEP] Ionic liquids is [MASK] that melt below 100 c. Their low volatilization can be an advantage over volatile organic solvents.

name: ion mobility spectrometry
query: Query: ion mobility spectrometry [SEP] Ion mobility spectrometry is techniques for separation and identification of ionized molecules based on their drift through a gas phase after being accelerated by an electric field. Their mobilities will be effected by their shape, size, and charge.

name: iran
query: Query: iran [SEP] Iran is a country bordering the Gulf of Oman, the Persian Gulf, and the Caspian Sea, between Iraq and Pakistan. The capital is Tehran.

name: ireland
query: Query: ireland [SEP] Ireland is a country in western Europe, occupying five-sixths of the island of Ireland in the North Atlantic Ocean, west of Great Britain. The capital is Dublin.

name: iris neoplasms
query: Query: iris neoplasms [SEP] Iris neoplasms is tumors of the iris characterized by increased pigmentation of melanocytes. Iris nevi are composed of proliferated melanocytes and are associated with neurofibromatosis and malignant melanoma of the choroid and [MASK]. Malignant melanoma of the iris often originates from preexisting nevi.

name: iron , dietary
query: Query: iron , dietary [SEP] Dietary iron is iron or iron compounds used in foods or as food. Dietary iron is important in oxygen transport and the synthesis of the iron-porphyrin proteins hemoglobin, myoglobin, cytochromes, and [MASK]. Insufficient amounts of dietary iron can lead to iron-deficiency anemia.

name: iron carbonyl compounds
query: Query: iron carbonyl compounds [SEP] Iron carbonyl compounds is complexes of iron atoms chelated with carbonyl ions.

name: iron overload
query: Query: iron overload [SEP] Iron overload is an excessive accumulation of iron in the body due to a greater than normal absorption of iron from the gastrointestinal tract or from parenteral injection. This may arise from idiopathic hemochromatosis, excessive iron intake, chronic alcoholism, certain types of refractory anemia, or transfusional hemosiderosis. (From Churchill's Illustrated Medical Dictionary, 1989)

name: ischemic attack , transient
query: Query: ischemic attack , transient [SEP] Transient ischemic attack is brief reversible episodes of focal, nonconvulsive ischemic dysfunction of the brain having a duration of less than 24 hours, and usually less than one hour, caused by transient thrombotic or embolic blood vessel occlusion or stenosis. Events may be classified by arterial distribution, temporal pattern, or etiology (e.g., embolic vs. thrombotic). (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp814-6)

name: ischemic preconditioning , myocardial
query: Query: ischemic preconditioning , myocardial [SEP] Myocardial ischemic preconditioning is exposure of myocardial tissue to brief, repeated periods of vascular occlusion in order to render the myocardium resistant to the deleterious effects of ischemia or reperfusion. The period of pre-exposure and the number of times the tissue is exposed to ischemia and reperfusion vary, the average being 3 to 5 minutes.

name: islam
query: Query: islam [SEP] Islam is a monotheistic religion promulgated by the Prophet Mohammed with Allah as the deity.

name: islet amyloid polypeptide
query: Query: islet amyloid polypeptide [SEP] Islet amyloid polypeptide is a pancreatic beta-cell hormone that is co-secreted with insulin. It displays an anorectic effect on nutrient metabolism by inhibiting gastric acid secretion, gastric emptying and postprandial glucagon secretion. Islet amyloid polypeptide can fold into amyloid fibrils that have been found as a major constituent of pancreatic amyloid deposits.

name: isolated heart preparation
query: Query: isolated heart preparation [SEP] Isolated heart preparation is method of isolation and maintenance of a working heart for various cardiac measurements. The model allows for the separation of cardiac and systemic variables in the denervated heart.

name: israel
query: Query: israel [SEP] Israel is a country in the Middle East, bordering the Mediterranean Sea, between [MASK] and Lebanon. The capital is Jerusalem.

name: japanese encephalitis vaccines
query: Query: japanese encephalitis vaccines [SEP] Japanese encephalitis vaccines is vaccines or candidate vaccines used to prevent infection with Japanese b encephalitis virus (encephalitis virus, japanese).

name: jaw relation record
query: Query: jaw relation record [SEP] Jaw relation record is a registration of any positional relationship of the mandible in reference to the maxillae. These records may be any of the many vertical, horizontal, or orientation relations. (Jablonski, Illustrated Dictionary of Dentistry)

name: jet lag syndrome
query: Query: jet lag syndrome [SEP] Jet lag syndrome is a chronobiologic disorder resulting from rapid travel across a number of time zones, characterized by insomnia or hypersomnolence, fatigue, behavioral symptoms, headaches, and gastrointestinal disturbances. (From Cooper, Sleep, 1994, pp593-8)

name: job application
query: Query: job application [SEP] Job application is process of applying for employment. It includes written application for employment or personal appearance.

name: job description
query: Query: job description [SEP] Job description is statement of the position requirements, qualifications for the position, wage range, and any special conditions expected of the employee.

name: job satisfaction
query: Query: job satisfaction [SEP] Job [MASK] is [MASK] relative to the work situation.

name: joint instability
query: Query: joint instability [SEP] Joint instability is lack of stability of a joint or joint prosthesis.

name: joint loose bodies
query: Query: joint loose bodies [SEP] Joint loose bodies is fibrous, bony, cartilaginous and osteocartilaginous fragments in a synovial joint. Major causes are osteochondritis dissecans, synovial chondromatosis, osteophytes, fractured articular surfaces and damaged menisci.

name: judgment
query: Query: judgment [SEP] Judgment is the process of discovering or asserting an objective or intrinsic relation between two objects or concepts; a faculty or power that enables a person to make judgments; the process of bringing to light and asserting the implicit meaning of a concept; a critical evaluation of a person or situation.

name: juvenile literature
query: Query: juvenile literature [SEP] Juvenile literature is works produced for children through age 15 or through the ninth grade.

name: kb cells
query: Query: kb cells [SEP] Kb cells is this line kb is now known to be a subline of the ubiquitous KERATIN-forming tumor cell line HeLa. It was originally thought to be derived from an epidermal carcinoma of the mouth, but was subsequently found, based on isoenzyme analysis, HeLa marker chromosomes, and dna fingerprinting, to have been established via contamination by hela cells. The cells are positive for keratin by immunoperoxidase staining. kb cells have been reported to contain human papillomavirus18 (hpv-18) sequences.

name: kenya
query: Query: kenya [SEP] Kenya is a republic in eastern Africa, south of ethiopia, west of somalia with [MASK] to its south, and coastline on the Indian Ocean. Its capital is Nairobi.

name: keratinocytes
query: Query: keratinocytes [SEP] Keratinocytes is epidermal cells which synthesize keratin and undergo characteristic changes as they move upward from the basal layers of the epidermis to the cornified (horny) layer of the skin. Successive stages of differentiation of the keratinocytes forming the epidermal layers are basal cell, spinous or prickle cell, and the granular cell.

name: kidney cortex
query: Query: kidney cortex [SEP] Kidney cortex is the outer zone of the kidney, beneath the capsule, consisting of kidney glomerulus; kidney tubules, distal; and kidney tubules, proximal.

name: kidney cortex necrosis
query: Query: kidney cortex necrosis [SEP] Kidney cortex necrosis is death of cells in the kidney cortex, a common final result of various renal injuries including hypoxia; ischemia; and drug toxicity.

name: kidney papillary necrosis
query: Query: kidney papillary necrosis [SEP] Kidney papillary necrosis is a complication of kidney diseases characterized by cell death involving [MASK] in the [MASK]. Damages to this area may hinder the kidney to concentrate urine resulting in polyuria. Sloughed off necrotic tissue may block [MASK] or ureter. Necrosis of multiple renal papillae can lead to kidney failure.

name: kidneys , artificial
query: Query: kidneys , artificial [SEP] Artificial kidneys is devices which can substitute for normally functioning kidneys in removing components from the blood by dialysis that are normally eliminated in the urine.

name: kidney transplantation
query: Query: kidney transplantation [SEP] Kidney transplantation is the transference of a kidney from one human or animal to another.

name: kidney tubules , collecting
query: Query: kidney tubules , collecting [SEP] Collecting kidney tubules is straight tubes commencing in the radiate part of the kidney cortex where they receive the curved ends of the distal convoluted tubules. In the medulla the collecting tubules of each pyramid converge to join a central tube (duct of Bellini) which opens on the summit of the papilla.

name: kidney tubules , distal
query: Query: kidney tubules , distal [SEP] Distal kidney tubules is the portion of renal tubule that begins from the enlarged segment of the ascending limb of the loop of henle. It reenters the kidney cortex and forms the convoluted segments of the distal tubule.

name: kidney tubules , proximal
query: Query: kidney tubules , proximal [SEP] Proximal kidney tubules is the renal tubule portion that extends from the bowman capsule in the kidney cortex into the [MASK]. The proximal tubule consists of a convoluted proximal segment in the cortex, and a distal straight segment descending into the medulla where it forms the U-shaped loop of henle.

name: killer cells , natural
query: Query: killer cells , natural [SEP] Natural killer cells is bone marrow-derived lymphocytes that possess cytotoxic properties, classically directed against transformed and virus-infected cells. Unlike t cells; and b cells; nk cells are not antigen specific. The cytotoxicity of natural killer cells is determined by the collective signaling of an array of inhibitory and stimulatory cell surface receptors. a subset of t-lymphocytes referred to as natural killer t cells shares some of the properties of this cell type.

name: killer factors , yeast
query: Query: killer factors , yeast [SEP] Yeast killer factors is protein factors released from one species of yeast that are selectively toxic to another species of yeast.

name: kinetics
query: Query: kinetics [SEP] Kinetics is the rate dynamics in chemical or physical systems.

name: knee dislocation
query: Query: knee dislocation [SEP] [MASK] dislocation is slippage of the femur off the tibia.

name: knee prosthesis
query: Query: knee prosthesis [SEP] [MASK] prosthesis is replacement for a [MASK].

name: knowledge discovery
query: Query: knowledge discovery [SEP] Knowledge discovery is a process that searches for hidden and important connections among information or results.

name: knowledge management
query: Query: knowledge management [SEP] Knowledge management is the leveraging of collective wisdom within an organization as a catalyst to increase responsiveness and innovation.

name: knowledge of results , psychological
query: Query: knowledge of results , psychological [SEP] Psychological knowledge of results is a principle that learning is facilitated when the learner receives immediate evaluation of learning performance. The concept also hypothesizes that learning is facilitated when the learner is promptly informed whether a response is correct, and, if incorrect, of the direction of error.

name: labor , induced
query: Query: labor , induced [SEP] Induced labor is artificially induced [MASK].

name: laboratories , dental
query: Query: laboratories , dental [SEP] Dental laboratories is facilities for the performance of services related to dental treatment but not done directly in the patient's mouth.

name: laboratories , hospital
query: Query: laboratories , hospital [SEP] Hospital laboratories is hospital facilities equipped to carry out investigative procedures.

name: laboratory animal science
query: Query: laboratory animal science [SEP] Laboratory animal science is the science and technology dealing with the procurement, breeding, care, health, and selection of animals used in biomedical research and testing.

name: laboratory critical values
query: Query: laboratory critical values [SEP] Laboratory critical values is test results which deviate substantially from normal ranges of reference values or other qualitative results. They trigger clinical laboratory services to place a special alert to ensure patient safety.

name: laboratory infection
query: Query: laboratory infection [SEP] Laboratory infection is accidentally acquired infection in laboratory workers.

name: laboratory or test result
query: Query: laboratory or test result [SEP] Laboratory or test result is the result that health care provider takes a sample of your blood, urine, other bodily fluid, or body tissue to get information about your health.

name: laboratory procedure
query: Query: laboratory procedure [SEP] Laboratory procedure is laboratory procedure

name: laboratory proficiency testing
query: Query: laboratory proficiency testing [SEP] Laboratory proficiency testing is assessments aimed at determining agreement in [MASK] results among laboratories. Identical survey samples are distributed to participating laboratories, with results stratified according to testing methodologies.

name: labor pain
query: Query: labor pain [SEP] Labor pain is pain associated with obstetric labor in childbirth. It is caused primarily by [MASK] as well as pressure on the cervix; [MASK]; and the gastrointestinal tract. Labor pain mostly occurs in the abdomen; the groin; and the back.

name: labor stage , first
query: Query: labor stage , first [SEP] First labor stage is period from the onset of true obstetric labor to the complete dilatation of the cervix uteri.

name: labor stage , second
query: Query: labor stage , second [SEP] Second labor stage is the period of obstetric labor that is from the complete dilatation of the cervix uteri to the expulsion of the fetus.

name: labor stage , third
query: Query: labor stage , third [SEP] Third labor stage is the final period of obstetric labor that is from the expulsion of the fetus to the expulsion of the placenta.

name: lac operon
query: Query: lac operon [SEP] Lac operon is the genetic unit consisting of three structural genes, an operator and a regulatory gene. The regulatory gene controls the synthesis of the three structural genes: beta-galactosidase and beta-galactoside permease (involved with the metabolism of lactose), and beta-thiogalactoside acetyltransferase.

name: lactation disorders
query: Query: lactation disorders [SEP] Lactation disorders is disturbances of milk secretion in either [MASK], not necessarily related to pregnancy.

name: lactose factors
query: Query: lactose factors [SEP] Lactose factors is plasmids which determine the ability of a bacterium to ferment lactose.

name: laminin
query: Query: laminin [SEP] Laminin is large, noncollagenous glycoprotein with antigenic properties. It is localized in the basement membrane lamina lucida and functions to bind epithelial cells to the basement membrane. Evidence suggests that the protein plays a role in tumor invasion.

name: language therapy
query: Query: language therapy [SEP] Language therapy is rehabilitation of persons with language disorders or training of children with language development disorders.

name: laryngeal edema
query: Query: laryngeal edema [SEP] Laryngeal edema is abnormal accumulation of fluid in tissues of any part of the larynx, commonly associated with laryngeal injuries and allergic reactions.

name: laryngeal neoplasms
query: Query: laryngeal neoplasms [SEP] Laryngeal neoplasms is cancers or tumors of the larynx or any of its parts: the glottis; epiglottis; laryngeal cartilages; [MASK]; and vocal cords.

name: laser coagulation
query: Query: laser coagulation [SEP] Laser coagulation is the use of green light-producing lasers to stop bleeding. The green light is selectively absorbed by hemoglobin, thus triggering blood coagulation.

name: lasers , dye
query: Query: lasers , dye [SEP] Dye lasers is tunable liquid lasers with organic compounds (i.e., dye) which have a strong absorption band, used as the active medium. During emission, the dye has to be optically excited by another light source (e.g., another laser or flash lamp). The range of the emission wavelength may be anywhere from the ultraviolet to the near infrared (i.e., from 180 to 1100nm). These lasers are operated in continuous wave and pulsed modes. (umdns, 2005)

name: lasers , semiconductor
query: Query: lasers , semiconductor [SEP] Semiconductor lasers is lasers with a semiconductor diode as the active medium. Diode lasers transform electric energy to light using the same principle as a light-emitting diode (led), but with internal reflection capability, thus forming a resonator where a stimulated light can reflect back and forth, allowing only a certain wavelength to be emitted. The emission of a given device is determined by the active compound used (e.g., gallium arsenide crystals doped with aluminum or indium). Typical wavelengths are 810, 1,060 and 1,300 nm. (From umdns, 2005)

name: laser scanning cytometry
query: Query: laser scanning cytometry [SEP] Laser scanning cytometry is a scanning microscope-based, cytofluorimetry technique for making fluorescence measurements and topographic analysis on individual cells. Lasers are used to excite fluorochromes in labeled cellular specimens. Fluorescence is detected in multiple discrete wavelengths and the locational data is processed to quantitatively assess apoptosis; ploidies; cell proliferation; gene expression; protein transport; and other cellular processes.

name: latent autoimmune diabetes in adults
query: Query: latent autoimmune diabetes in adults [SEP] Latent autoimmune diabetes in adults is autoimmune diabetes in adults with slowly progressive pancreatic beta cell failure and the presence of circulating autoantibodies to pancreatic islets cell antigens.

name: latent tuberculosis
query: Query: latent tuberculosis [SEP] Latent tuberculosis is the dormant form of tuberculosis where the person shows no obvious symptoms and no sign of the causative agent ([MASK]) in the sputum despite being positive for tuberculosis infection skin test.

name: late onset disorders
query: Query: late onset disorders [SEP] Late onset disorders is pathological conditions (Disorder, syndrome, or disease) whose signs and symptoms manifest late in the life of an individual.

name: lateral line system
query: Query: lateral line system [SEP] Lateral line system is aquatic vertebrate sensory system in fish and amphibians. It is composed of sense organs (canal organs and pit organs) containing neuromasts (mechanoreceptors) that detect water displacement caused by moving objects.

name: lateral sinus thrombosis
query: Query: lateral sinus thrombosis [SEP] Lateral sinus thrombosis is formation or presence of a blood clot (thrombus) in the lateral sinuses. This condition is often associated with ear infections (otitis media or mastoiditis) without antibiotic treatment. In [MASK], lateral sinus thrombosis can result from craniocerebral trauma; brain neoplasms; neurosurgical procedures; thrombophilia; and other conditions. Clinical features include headache; vertigo; and increased [MASK].

name: lateral thalamic nuclei
query: Query: lateral thalamic nuclei [SEP] Lateral thalamic nuclei is a narrow strip of cell groups on the dorsomedial surface of the thalamus. It includes the lateral dorsal nucleus, lateral posterior nucleus, and the pulvinar.

name: latex
query: Query: latex [SEP] Latex is a milky, product excreted from the latex canals of a variety of plant species that contain cauotchouc. Latex is composed of 25-35% caoutchouc, 60-75% water, 2% protein, 2% resin, 1.5% sugar & 1% ash. rubber is made by the removal of water from latex.(From Concise Encyclopedia Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, 3rd ed). Hevein proteins are responsible for latex hypersensitivity. Latexes are used as inert vehicles to carry antibodies or antigens in latex fixation tests.

name: law enforcement
query: Query: law enforcement [SEP] Law enforcement is organized efforts to insure obedience to the laws of a community.

name: lead
query: Query: lead [SEP] Lead is a soft, grayish metal with poisonous [MASK]; atomic number 82, atomic weight 207.2, symbol Pb.

name: lead poisoning , nervous system , adult
query: Query: lead poisoning , nervous system , adult [SEP] Adult nervous system lead poisoning is neurologic conditions in adults associated with acute or chronic exposure to lead or any of its [MASK]. The most common lead related neurologic syndrome in adults consists of a polyneuropathy involving motor fibers. This tends to affect distal nerves and may present as wrist drop due to radial neuropathy. Additional features of chronic lead exposure include anemia; constipation; colicky abdominal pain; a bluish lead line of the gums; interstitial nephritis (nephritis, interstitial); and saturnine gout. An encephalopathy may rarely occur. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1212)

name: lead poisoning , nervous system , childhood
query: Query: lead poisoning , nervous system , childhood [SEP] Childhood nervous system lead poisoning is neurologic disorders occurring in children following lead exposure. The most frequent manifestation of childhood lead toxicity is an encephalopathy associated with chronic ingestion of lead that usually presents between the ages of 1 and 3 years. Clinical manifestations include behavioral changes followed by lethargy; convulsions; hallucinations; delirium; ataxia; and vomiting. Elevated [MASK] (hypertension, intracranial) and cerebral edema may occur. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1210-2)

name: learning curve
query: Query: learning curve [SEP] Learning curve is the course of learning of an individual or a group. It is a measure of performance plotted over time.

name: learning health system
query: Query: learning health system [SEP] Learning health system is a system in which internal data and experience are systematically integrated with external evidence and that knowledge is put into practice. As a result, patients get higher quality, safer, more efficient care, and health care delivery organizations become better places to work. (https://healthit.ahrq.gov/health-care-theme/learning-health-system)

name: leg
query: Query: leg [SEP] Leg is the inferior part of the lower extremity between the [MASK] and the ankle.

name: legal epidemiology
query: Query: legal epidemiology [SEP] Legal epidemiology is scientific study of law as a factor in the cause, distribution, and prevention of disease and injury.  (From https://read.dukeupress.edu/jhppl/article/41/6/1151/40084/Policy-Surveillance-A-Vital-Public-Health-Practice).

name: legislation
query: Query: legislation [SEP] Legislation is works consisting of the text of proposed or enacted legislation that may be in the form of bills, laws, statutes, ordinances, or government regulations.

name: legislation , nursing
query: Query: legislation , nursing [SEP] Nursing legislation is laws and regulations, pertaining to the field of nursing, proposed for enactment by a legislative body.

name: legislation , pharmacy
query: Query: legislation , pharmacy [SEP] Pharmacy legislation is laws and regulations, pertaining to the field of pharmacy, proposed for enactment or enacted by a legislative body.

name: leg length inequality
query: Query: leg length inequality [SEP] Leg length inequality is a condition in which one of a pair of legs fails to grow as long as the other, which could result from injury or surgery.

name: length of stay
query: Query: length of stay [SEP] Length of stay is the period of confinement of a patient to a hospital or other health facility.

name: lens cortex , crystalline
query: Query: lens cortex , crystalline [SEP] Crystalline lens cortex is the portion of the crystalline lens surrounding the nucleus and bound anteriorly by the epithelium and posteriorly by the capsule. It contains lens fibers and amorphous, intercellular substance.

name: lenses , intraocular
query: Query: lenses , intraocular [SEP] Intraocular lenses is artificial implanted lenses.

name: lens implantation , intraocular
query: Query: lens implantation , intraocular [SEP] Intraocular lens implantation is insertion of an artificial lens to replace the natural crystalline lens after [MASK] extraction or to supplement the natural lens which is left in place.

name: lens nucleus , crystalline
query: Query: lens nucleus , crystalline [SEP] Crystalline lens nucleus is the core of the crystalline lens, surrounded by the cortex.

name: lesser pelvis
query: Query: lesser pelvis [SEP] Lesser pelvis is the part of the pelvis, inferior to the pelvic brim, that comprises both the pelvic cavity and the part of the perineum lying inferior to the [MASK].

name: letter
query: Query: letter [SEP] Letter is work consisting of written or printed communication between individuals or between persons and representatives of corporate bodies. The correspondence may be personal or professional. In medical and other scientific publications the letter is usually from one or more authors to the editor of the journal or book publishing the item being commented upon or discussed. letter is often accompanied by comment.

name: leukemia , lymphoid
query: Query: leukemia , lymphoid [SEP] Lymphoid leukemia is leukemia associated with hyperplasia of the lymphoid tissues and increased numbers of circulating malignant lymphocytes and lymphoblasts.

name: leukemia , plasma cell
query: Query: leukemia , plasma cell [SEP] Plasma cell leukemia is a rare, aggressive variant of multiple myeloma characterized by the circulation of excessive plasma cells in the peripheral blood. It can be a primary manifestation of multiple myeloma or develop as a terminal complication during the disease.

name: leukemia inhibitory factor
query: Query: leukemia inhibitory factor [SEP] Leukemia inhibitory factor is an interleukin-6 related cytokine that exhibits pleiotrophic effects on many physiological systems that involve cell proliferation, differentiation, and survival. Leukemia inhibitory factor binds to and acts through the lif receptor.

name: leukocyte disorders
query: Query: leukocyte disorders [SEP] Leukocyte disorders is disordered formation of various types of leukocytes or an abnormal accumulation or deficiency of these cells.

name: leukocyte reduction procedures
query: Query: leukocyte reduction procedures [SEP] Leukocyte reduction procedures is the removal of leukocytes from blood to reduce blood transfusion reactions and lower the chance of transmitting viruses. This may be performed by filtration or by cytapheresis.

name: lewis acids
query: Query: lewis acids [SEP] Lewis acids is any chemical species which accepts an [MASK]-pair from a [MASK] in a chemical bonding reaction.

name: l forms
query: Query: l forms [SEP] L forms is bacterial variants, unable to form a complete cell wall, which are formed in cultures by various bacteria; granules (l bodies) appear, unite, and grow into amorphous bodies which multiply and give rise to bacterial cells morphologically indistinguishable from the parent strain.

name: libraries , dental
query: Query: libraries , dental [SEP] Dental libraries is collections of [MASK] relevant to dentistry.

name: libraries , digital
query: Query: libraries , digital [SEP] Digital libraries is libraries in which a major proportion of the resources are available in machine-readable format, rather than on [MASK] or microform.

name: libraries , hospital
query: Query: libraries , hospital [SEP] Hospital libraries is information centers primarily serving the needs of [MASK] and sometimes also providing patient education and other services.

name: libraries , medical
query: Query: libraries , medical [SEP] Medical libraries is collection of [MASK] relevant to medicine.

name: libraries , nursing
query: Query: libraries , nursing [SEP] Nursing libraries is collections of [MASK] relevant to nursing.

name: library associations
query: Query: library associations [SEP] Library associations is organizations of persons and institutions associated with a type of library or region.

name: library collection development
query: Query: library collection development [SEP] Library collection development is development of a library collection, including the determination and coordination of selection policy, assessment of needs of users and potential users, collection use studies, collection evaluation, identification of collection needs, selection of materials, planning for resource sharing, collection maintenance and weeding, and budgeting.

name: library materials
query: Query: library materials [SEP] Library materials is print and non-print materials collected, processed, and stored by libraries. They comprise books, periodicals, pamphlets, reports, microforms, maps, manuscripts, motion pictures, and all other forms of audiovisual records. (Harrod, The Librarians' Glossary, 4th ed, p497)

name: library schools
query: Query: library schools [SEP] Library schools is educational institutions for individuals specializing in the field of library science or information.

name: library surveys
query: Query: library surveys [SEP] Library surveys is collection and analysis of data pertaining to operations of a particular library, library system, or group of independent libraries, with recommendations for improvement and/or ordered plans for further development.

name: library technical services
query: Query: library technical services [SEP] Library technical services is acquisition, organization, and preparation of library materials for use, including selection, weeding, cataloging, classification, and preservation.

name: lie detection
query: Query: lie detection [SEP] Lie detection is ascertaining of deception through detection of emotional disturbance as manifested by changes in physiologic processes usually using a polygraph.

name: life change events
query: Query: life change events [SEP] Life change events is those occurrences, including social, psychological, and environmental, which require an [MASK] or effect a change in an individual's pattern of living.

name: life support systems
query: Query: life support systems [SEP] Life support systems is systems that provide all or most of the items necessary for maintaining life and health. Provisions are made for the supplying of oxygen, food, water, temperature and pressure control, disposition of carbon dioxide and body waste. The milieu may be a spacecraft, a submarine, or the surface of the moon. In medical care, usually under hospital conditions, life support care is available. (From Webster's New Collegiate Dictionary)

name: lifting
query: Query: lifting [SEP] Lifting is moving or bringing something from a lower level to a higher one. The concept encompasses biomechanic stresses resulting from work done in transferring objects from one plane to another as well as the effects of varying techniques of patient handling and transfer.

name: ligands
query: Query: ligands [SEP] Ligands is a molecule that binds to another molecule, used especially to refer to a small molecule that binds specifically to a larger molecule, e.g., an antigen binding to an antibody, a hormone or neurotransmitter binding to a receptor, or a substrate or allosteric effector binding to an enzyme. Ligands are also molecules that donate or accept a pair of [MASK] to form a coordinate covalent bond with the central metal atom of a coordination complex. (From Dorland, 27th ed)

name: lightning
query: Query: lightning [SEP] Lightning is an abrupt high-current electric discharge that occurs in the atmosphere and that has a path length ranging from hundreds of [MASK] to tens of miles. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

name: lignin
query: Query: lignin [SEP] Lignin is the most abundant natural aromatic organic polymer found in all vascular plants. Lignin together with cellulose and hemicellulose are the major cell wall components of the fibers of all [MASK] and grass species. Lignin is composed of coniferyl, p-coumaryl, and sinapyl alcohols in varying ratios in different plant species. (From Merck Index, 11th ed)

name: limb buds
query: Query: limb buds [SEP] Limb buds is distinct regions of mesenchymal outgrowth at both flanks of an embryo during the somite period. Limb buds, covered by ectoderm, give rise to forelimb, hindlimb, and eventual functional limb structures. Limb bud cultures are used to study cell differentiation; organogenesis; and morphogenesis.

name: limb salvage
query: Query: limb salvage [SEP] Limb salvage is an alternative to [MASK] in patients with neoplasms, ischemia, fractures, and other limb-threatening conditions. Generally, sophisticated surgical procedures such as vascular surgery and reconstruction are used to salvage diseased limbs.

name: limited english proficiency
query: Query: limited english proficiency [SEP] Limited english proficiency is limited ability to communicate with or understand English.

name: limit of detection
query: Query: limit of detection [SEP] Limit of detection is concentration or quantity that is derived from the smallest measure that can be detected with reasonable certainty for a given analytical procedure.

name: lim kinases
query: Query: lim kinases [SEP] Lim kinases is serine protein kinases involved in the regulation of actin [MASK] and [MASK] disassembly. Their activity is regulated by phosphorylation of a threonine residue within the activation loop by intracellular signaling kinases such as p21-activated kinases and by rho kinase.

name: linear models
query: Query: linear models [SEP] Linear models is statistical models in which the value of a parameter for a given value of a factor is assumed to be equal to a + bx, where a and b are constants. The models predict a linear regression.

name: linkage disequilibrium
query: Query: linkage disequilibrium [SEP] Linkage disequilibrium is nonrandom association of linked genes. This is the tendency of the alleles of two separate but already linked loci to be found together more frequently than would be expected by chance alone.

name: lipid accumulation product
query: Query: lipid accumulation product [SEP] Lipid accumulation product is an index for monitoring the accumulation of lipids based on the waist circumference measurement and the level of triglycerides circulating in the blood.

name: lipid metabolism
query: Query: lipid metabolism [SEP] Lipid metabolism is physiological processes in biosynthesis (anabolism) and degradation (catabolism) of lipids.

name: lipid metabolism disorders
query: Query: lipid metabolism disorders [SEP] Lipid metabolism disorders is pathological conditions resulting from abnormal anabolism or catabolism of lipids in the body.

name: lipoprotein ( a )
query: Query: lipoprotein ( a ) [SEP] Lipoprotein (a) is a lipoprotein that resembles the low-density lipoproteins but with an extra protein moiety, aporoteinN (A) also known as apolipoprotein (A), linked to apolipoprotein B-100 on the LDL by one or two disulfide bonds. High plasma level of lipoprotein (a) is associated with increased risk of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease.

name: lipoprotein lipase activators
query: Query: lipoprotein lipase activators [SEP] Lipoprotein lipase activators is compounds that increase the enzymatic activity of lipoprotein lipase. Lipoprotein lipase activators have a potential role in the treatment of obesity by increasing lipid metabolism. Note that substances that increase the synthesis of lipoprotein lipase are not included here.

name: liposomes
query: Query: liposomes [SEP] Liposomes is artificial, single or multilaminar vesicles (made from lecithins or other lipids) that are used for the delivery of a variety of biological molecules or molecular complexes to cells, for example, drug delivery and gene transfer. They are also used to study membranes and membrane proteins.

name: liquid crystals
query: Query: liquid crystals [SEP] Liquid crystals is materials in intermediate state between solid and liquid.

name: liquid ventilation
query: Query: liquid ventilation [SEP] Liquid ventilation is artificial respiration (respiration, artificial) using an oxygenated fluid.

name: lithium carbonate
query: Query: lithium carbonate [SEP] [MASK] carbonate is a [MASK] [MASK], classified as a mood-stabilizing agent. [MASK] ion alters the metabolism of biogenic monoamines in the central nervous system, and affects multiple neurotransmission systems.

name: lithium chloride
query: Query: lithium chloride [SEP] [MASK] chloride is a [MASK] of [MASK] that has been used experimentally as an immunomodulator.

name: litter size
query: Query: litter size [SEP] Litter size is the number of offspring produced at one birth by a viviparous animal.

name: live birth
query: Query: live birth [SEP] Live birth is the event that a fetus is born alive with heartbeats or respiration regardless of gestational age. Such liveborn is called a newborn infant (infant, newborn).

name: liver cirrhosis , alcoholic
query: Query: liver cirrhosis , alcoholic [SEP] Alcoholic liver cirrhosis is fibrosis of the hepatic parenchyma due to chronic excess alcohol drinking.

name: liver cirrhosis , biliary
query: Query: liver cirrhosis , biliary [SEP] Biliary liver cirrhosis is fibrosis of the hepatic parenchyma due to obstruction of [MASK] flow (cholestasis) in the intrahepatic or extrahepatic [MASK] ([MASK], intrahepatic; [MASK], extrahepatic). Primary biliary cholangitis involves the destruction of small intra-hepatic [MASK] and decreased [MASK] secretion. Secondary biliary cholangitis is produced by prolonged obstruction of large intrahepatic or extrahepatic [MASK] from a variety of causes.

name: liver cirrhosis , experimental
query: Query: liver cirrhosis , experimental [SEP] Experimental liver cirrhosis is experimentally induced chronic injuries to the parenchymal cells in the liver to achieve a model for liver cirrhosis.

name: liver function tests
query: Query: liver function tests [SEP] Liver function tests is blood tests that are used to evaluate how well a patient's liver is working and also to help diagnose liver conditions.

name: liver glycogen
query: Query: liver glycogen [SEP] Liver glycogen is glycogen stored in the liver. (Dorland, 28th ed)

name: liver regeneration
query: Query: liver regeneration [SEP] Liver regeneration is repair or renewal of hepatic tissue.

name: liver transplantation
query: Query: liver transplantation [SEP] Liver transplantation is the transference of a part of or an entire liver from one human or animal to another.

name: liver x receptors
query: Query: liver x receptors [SEP] Liver x receptors is nuclear receptors that bind oxysterols and function as heterodimers with retinoid x receptors. They have important functions in regulating cholesterol homeostasis, energy metabolism; inflammation; and the immune response.

name: livestock
query: Query: livestock [SEP] Livestock is domesticated farm animals raised for home use or profit but excluding poultry. Typically livestock includes cattle; sheep; horses; swine; goats; and others.

name: living donors
query: Query: living donors [SEP] Living donors is non-cadaveric providers of organs for [MASK] to related or non-related recipients.

name: local government
query: Query: local government [SEP] Local government is smallest political subdivisions within a country at which general governmental functions are carried-out.

name: locus control region
query: Query: locus control region [SEP] Locus control region is a regulatory region first identified in the human beta-globin locus but subsequently found in other loci. The region is believed to regulate genetic transcription by opening and remodeling chromatin structure. It may also have enhancer activity.

name: lod score
query: Query: lod score [SEP] Lod score is the total relative probability, expressed on a logarithmic scale, that a linkage relationship exists among selected loci. Lod is an acronym for "logarithmic odds."

name: logical observation identifiers names and codes
query: Query: logical observation identifiers names and codes [SEP] Logical [MASK] identifiers names and codes is a vocabulary [MASK] of universal identifiers for laboratory and clinical test results. Its purpose is to facilitate the exchange and pooling of results for clinical care, outcomes management, and research. It is produced by the Regenstrief Institute. (loinc and relma [Internet]. Indianapolis: The Regenstrief Institute; c1995-2001 [cited 2002 Apr 2]. Available from http://www.regenstrief.org/loinc)

name: london
query: Query: london [SEP] London is the capital of the United Kingdom. It is located in England.

name: longevity
query: Query: longevity [SEP] Longevity is the normal length of time of an organism's life.

name: long term adverse effects
query: Query: long term adverse effects [SEP] Long term adverse effects is persistent detrimental effects from treatment for a condition. Included are effects from surgery such as postoperative complications, and from drug therapy, such as chemically induced disorders, or other therapeutics. Failure to attain a desired outcome from treatment for the condition is not considered an adverse effect.

name: los angeles
query: Query: los angeles [SEP] Los angeles is city in California.

name: lot quality assurance sampling
query: Query: lot quality assurance sampling [SEP] Lot quality assurance sampling is a sampling methodology using small sample sizes when conducting surveys in small geographical or population-based areas or lots.

name: love
query: Query: love [SEP] Love is affection; in psychiatry commonly refers to pleasure, particularly as it applies to gratifying experiences between individuals.

name: lower body negative pressure
query: Query: lower body negative pressure [SEP] Lower body negative pressure is external decompression applied to the lower body. It is used to study orthostatic intolerance and the effects of gravitation and [MASK], to produce simulated hemorrhage in physiologic research, to assess cardiovascular function, and to reduce abdominal stress during childbirth.

name: low tension glaucoma
query: Query: low tension glaucoma [SEP] Low tension glaucoma is a form of glaucoma in which chronic optic nerve damage and loss of vision normally attributable to buildup of intraocular pressure occurs despite prevailing conditions of normal intraocular pressure.

name: lung
query: Query: lung [SEP] Lung is either of the pair of organs occupying the cavity of the thorax that effect the aeration of the blood.

name: lung abscess
query: Query: lung abscess [SEP] Lung abscess is solitary or multiple collections of pus within the lung parenchyma as a result of infection by bacteria, protozoa, or other agents.

name: lung compliance
query: Query: lung compliance [SEP] Lung compliance is the capability of the lungs to distend under pressure as measured by pulmonary volume change per unit pressure change. While not a complete description of the pressure-volume properties of the lung, it is nevertheless useful in practice as a measure of the comparative stiffness of the lung. (From Best & Taylor's Physiological Basis of Medical Practice, 12th ed, p562)

name: lung diseases , fungal
query: Query: lung diseases , fungal [SEP] Fungal lung diseases is pulmonary diseases caused by fungal infections, usually through hematogenous spread.

name: lung diseases , interstitial
query: Query: lung diseases , interstitial [SEP] Interstitial lung diseases is a diverse group of lung diseases that affect the lung parenchyma. They are characterized by an initial inflammation of pulmonary alveoli that extends to the interstitium and beyond leading to diffuse pulmonary fibrosis. Interstitial lung diseases are classified by their etiology (known or unknown causes), and radiological-pathological features.

name: lung diseases , parasitic
query: Query: lung diseases , parasitic [SEP] Parasitic lung diseases is infections of the lungs with parasites, most commonly by parasitic worms (helminths).

name: lupus coagulation inhibitor
query: Query: lupus coagulation inhibitor [SEP] Lupus coagulation inhibitor is an antiphospholipid antibody found in association with [MASK] ([MASK];), antiphospholipid syndrome; and in a variety of other diseases as well as in healthy individuals. In vitro, the antibody interferes with the conversion of prothrombin to thrombin and prolongs the partial thromboplastin time. In vivo, it exerts a procoagulant effect resulting in thrombosis mainly in the larger veins and arteries. It further causes obstetrical complications, including fetal death and spontaneous abortion, as well as a variety of hematologic and neurologic complications.

name: lupus erythematosus , cutaneous
query: Query: lupus erythematosus , cutaneous [SEP] Cutaneous lupus erythematosus is a form of lupus erythematosus in which the skin may be the only organ involved or in which skin involvement precedes the spread into other body systems. It has been classified into three forms - acute (= [MASK] with skin lesions), subacute, and chronic (= lupus erythematosus, discoid).

name: lupus vulgaris
query: Query: lupus vulgaris [SEP] Lupus vulgaris is a form of cutaneous tuberculosis. It is seen predominantly in women and typically involves the nasal mucosa; [MASK]; and conjunctival mucosa.

name: lymphatic abnormalities
query: Query: lymphatic abnormalities [SEP] Lymphatic abnormalities is congenital or acquired structural abnormalities of the lymphatic system (lymphoid tissue) including the [MASK] vessels.

name: lymphatic irradiation
query: Query: lymphatic irradiation [SEP] Lymphatic irradiation is external or interstitial irradiation to treat lymphomas (e.g., Hodgkin's and non-Hodgkin's lymphomas) and [MASK] and also some autoimmune diseases, such as rheumatoid arthritis.

name: lymphatic vessel tumors
query: Query: lymphatic vessel tumors [SEP] Lymphatic vessel tumors is neoplasms composed of lymphoid tissue, a lattice work of reticular tissue the interspaces of which contain lymphocytes. The concept does not refer to neoplasms located in lymphatic vessels.

name: lymphocyte cooperation
query: Query: lymphocyte cooperation [SEP] Lymphocyte cooperation is t-cell enhancement of the B-cell response to thymic-dependent antigens.

name: lymphocyte count
query: Query: lymphocyte count [SEP] Lymphocyte count is the number of lymphocytes per unit volume of blood.

name: lymphocytes , null
query: Query: lymphocytes , null [SEP] Null lymphocytes is a class of lymphocytes characterized by the lack of surface markers specific for either t or b lymphocytes.

name: lymphocyte transfusion
query: Query: lymphocyte transfusion [SEP] Lymphocyte transfusion is the transfer of lymphocytes from a donor to a recipient or reinfusion to the donor.

name: lymphoid progenitor cells
query: Query: lymphoid progenitor cells [SEP] Lymphoid progenitor cells is stem cells from which b-lymphocytes; t-lymphocytes; natural killer cells; and some [MASK] derive.

name: lysine
query: Query: lysine [SEP] Lysine is an essential amino acid. It is often added to [MASK].

name: lysosomes
query: Query: lysosomes [SEP] Lysosomes is a class of morphologically heterogeneous cytoplasmic particles in animal and plant tissues characterized by their content of hydrolytic enzymes and the structure-linked latency of these enzymes. The intracellular functions of lysosomes depend on their lytic potential. The single unit membrane of the lysosome acts as a barrier between the enzymes enclosed in the lysosome and the external substrate. The activity of the enzymes contained in lysosomes is limited or nil unless the vesicle in which they are enclosed is ruptured or undergoes [MASK]. (From Rieger et al., Glossary of Genetics: Classical and Molecular, 5th ed)

name: machine activity
query: Query: machine activity [SEP] Machine activity is the activity of machines.

name: macrophage inflammatory proteins
query: Query: macrophage inflammatory proteins [SEP] Macrophage inflammatory proteins is heparin-binding proteins that exhibit a number of inflammatory and immunoregulatory activities. Originally identified as secretory products of macrophages, these chemokines are produced by a variety of cell types including neutrophils; fibroblasts; and epithelial cells. They likely play a significant role in respiratory tract defenses.

name: macrophages , alveolar
query: Query: macrophages , alveolar [SEP] Alveolar macrophages is round, granular, mononuclear phagocytes found in the alveoli of the lungs. They ingest small inhaled particles resulting in degradation and presentation of the antigen to immunocompetent cells.

name: magic
query: Query: magic [SEP] Magic is beliefs and practices concerned with producing desired results through supernatural forces or agents as with the manipulation of fetishes or rituals.

name: magnesium
query: Query: magnesium [SEP] Magnesium is a metallic element that has the atomic symbol Mg, atomic number 12, and atomic weight 24.31. It is important for the activity of many enzymes, especially those involved in oxidative phosphorylation.

name: magnesium chloride
query: Query: magnesium chloride [SEP] Magnesium chloride is magnesium chloride. An inorganic compound consisting of one magnesium and two chloride ions. The compound is used in medicine as a source of magnesium ions, which are essential for many cellular activities. It has also been used as a cathartic and in alloys.

name: magnesium deficiency
query: Query: magnesium deficiency [SEP] Magnesium deficiency is a nutritional condition produced by a deficiency of magnesium in the diet, characterized by anorexia, nausea, vomiting, lethargy, and weakness. Symptoms are paresthesias, muscle cramps, irritability, decreased attention span, and mental confusion, possibly requiring months to appear. Deficiency of body magnesium can exist even when serum values are normal. In addition, magnesium deficiency may be organ-selective, since certain tissues become deficient before others. (Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 12th ed, p1936)

name: magnesium hydroxide
query: Query: magnesium hydroxide [SEP] Magnesium hydroxide is an inorganic compound that occurs in nature as the mineral brucite. It acts as an antacid with cathartic effects.

name: magnesium oxide
query: Query: magnesium oxide [SEP] Magnesium oxide is magnesium oxide (MgO). An inorganic compound that occurs in nature as the mineral periclase. In aqueous media combines quickly with water to form magnesium hydroxide. It is used as an antacid and mild laxative and has many nonmedicinal uses.

name: magnetic field therapy
query: Query: magnetic field therapy [SEP] Magnetic field therapy is the magnetic stimulation of specific target tissues or areas of the body for therapeutic purposes via the application of magnetic fields generated by [MASK] or [MASK].

name: magnetic resonance angiography
query: Query: magnetic resonance angiography [SEP] Magnetic resonance angiography is non-invasive method of vascular imaging and determination of internal anatomy without injection of contrast media or radiation exposure. The technique is used especially in cerebral angiography as well as for studies of other vascular structures.

name: magnetic resonance imaging , cine
query: Query: magnetic resonance imaging , cine [SEP] Cine magnetic resonance imaging is a type of imaging technique used primarily in the field of cardiology. By coordinating the fast gradient-echo mri sequence with retrospective ECG-gating, numerous short time frames evenly spaced in the cardiac cycle are produced. These images are laced together in a cinematic display so that wall motion of the ventricles, valve motion, and blood flow patterns in the heart and great vessels can be visualized.

name: malaria , avian
query: Query: malaria , avian [SEP] Avian malaria is any of a group of infections of fowl caused by protozoa of the genera plasmodium, Leucocytozoon, and Haemoproteus. The [MASK] of these parasites and the disease produced bears strong resemblance to those observed in human malaria.

name: malaria , cerebral
query: Query: malaria , cerebral [SEP] Cerebral malaria is a condition characterized by somnolence or coma in the presence of an acute infection with plasmodium falciparum (and rarely other Plasmodium species). Initial clinical manifestations include headaches; seizures; and alterations of mentation followed by a rapid progression to coma. Pathologic features include cerebral capillaries filled with parasitized erythrocytes and multiple small foci of cortical and subcortical necrosis. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p136)

name: malaria , falciparum
