query: Query: malaria , falciparum [SEP] Falciparum malaria is malaria caused by plasmodium falciparum. This is the severest form of malaria and is associated with the highest levels of parasites in the blood. This disease is characterized by irregularly recurring febrile paroxysms that in extreme cases occur with acute cerebral, renal, or gastrointestinal manifestations.

name: malformations of cortical development , group i
query: Query: malformations of cortical development , group i [SEP] Group i malformations of cortical development is cortical malformations secondary to abnormal neuronal and glial cell proliferation or apoptosis in neurogenesis. This group includes congenital microcephalies; microlissencephalies, megalencephalies, hemimegalencephalies and cortical dysplasias with balloon cells.

name: malformations of cortical development , group ii
query: Query: malformations of cortical development , group ii [SEP] Group ii malformations of cortical development is cortical malformations secondary to abnormal neuronal cell migration in neurogenesis. This group includes cobblestone lissencephaly and periventricular nodular heterotopia.

name: malformations of cortical development , group iii
query: Query: malformations of cortical development , group iii [SEP] Group iii malformations of cortical development is cortical malformations secondary to abnormal cortical maturation after cell migration in neurogenesis. This group includes injury to the cortex during later stages of cortical development such as polymicrogyria and focal cortical dysplasias.

name: mammals
query: Query: mammals [SEP] Mammals is warm-blooded vertebrate animals belonging to the class Mammalia, including all that possess hair and suckle their young.

name: mammary analogue secretory carcinoma
query: Query: mammary analogue secretory carcinoma [SEP] Mammary analogue secretory carcinoma is a malignant neoplasm of epithelial cells of the salivary glands, with microcystic architecture, low-grade nuclei, and granular vacuolated cytoplasm.

name: mammary arteries
query: Query: mammary arteries [SEP] Mammary arteries is arteries originating from the subclavian or axillary arteries and distributing to the anterior thoracic wall, mediastinal structures, diaphragm, pectoral muscles and mammary gland.

name: mammary glands , animal
query: Query: mammary glands , animal [SEP] Animal mammary glands is mammary glands in the non-human mammals.

name: mammary glands , human
query: Query: mammary glands , human [SEP] Human mammary glands is glandular tissue in the breast of human that is under the influence of hormones such as estrogens; progestins; and prolactin. In women, after parturition, the mammary glands secrete milk ([MASK]) for the nourishment of the young.

name: mammary neoplasms , experimental
query: Query: mammary neoplasms , experimental [SEP] Experimental mammary neoplasms is experimentally induced mammary neoplasms in animals to provide a model for studying human breast neoplasms.

name: mammography
query: Query: mammography [SEP] Mammography is radiographic examination of the breast.

name: managed competition
query: Query: managed competition [SEP] Managed competition is a strategy for purchasing health care in a manner which will obtain maximum value for the price for the purchasers of the health care and the recipients. The concept was developed primarily by Alain Enthoven of Stanford University and promulgated by the Jackson Hole Group. The strategy depends on sponsors for groups of the population to be insured. The sponsor, in some cases a [MASK], acts as an intermediary between the group and competing provider groups (accountable health plans). The competition is price-based among annual premiums for a defined, standardized benefit package. (From Slee and Slee, Health Care Reform Terms, 1993)

name: management quality circles
query: Query: management quality circles [SEP] Management quality circles is participation of employees with management as a labor-management team, in decisions pertaining to the operational activities of the organization or industry.

name: management service organizations
query: Query: management service organizations [SEP] Management service organizations is voluntarily-formed groups of healthcare professionals who join for common management services and other benefits such as collective bargaining agreements with reimbursement agents. The physical assets of a practice are controlled by the mso which also provides billing, collections, and similar services. The practitioner retains control of patient records and management of patient care.

name: mandatory testing
query: Query: mandatory testing [SEP] Mandatory testing is testing or screening required by federal, state, or local law or other agencies for the diagnosis of specified conditions. It is usually limited to specific populations such as categories of health care providers, members of the military, and prisoners or to specific situations such as premarital examinations or donor screening.

name: mandibular fractures
query: Query: mandibular fractures [SEP] Mandibular fractures is fractures of the lower jaw.

name: mandibular neoplasms
query: Query: mandibular neoplasms [SEP] Mandibular neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the mandible.

name: manganese poisoning
query: Query: manganese poisoning [SEP] [MASK] poisoning is [MASK] poisoning is associated with chronic [MASK] of [MASK] particles by individuals who work with [MASK] ore. Clinical features include confusion; hallucinations; and an extrapyramidal syndrome (parkinson disease, secondary) that includes rigidity; dystonia; retropulsion; and tremor. (Adams, Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1213)

name: manifest anxiety scale
query: Query: manifest anxiety scale [SEP] Manifest anxiety scale is true-false questionnaire made up of items believed to indicate anxiety, in which the subject answers verbally the statement that describes him.

name: manipulation , orthopedic
query: Query: manipulation , orthopedic [SEP] Orthopedic manipulation is the planned and carefully managed manual movement of the musculoskeletal system, extremities, and spine to produce increased motion. The term is sometimes used to denote a precise sequence of movements of a joint to determine the presence of disease or to reduce a dislocation. In the case of fractures, orthopedic manipulation can produce better position and alignment of the fracture. (From Blauvelt & Nelson, a Manual of Orthopaedic Terminology, 5th ed, p264)

name: manipulation , spinal
query: Query: manipulation , spinal [SEP] Spinal manipulation is [MASK] and manipulation of the vertebral column.

name: manual lymphatic drainage
query: Query: manual lymphatic drainage [SEP] Manual lymphatic drainage is the application of massage to control edema and improve circulation by manually moving excess [MASK] out of a tissue.

name: manuscript , medical
query: Query: manuscript , medical [SEP] Medical manuscript is medical works prepared by hand including handwritten or typescript drafts of pre-publication [MASK] or works not otherwise reproduced in multiple copies.

name: manuscripts , medical as topic
query: Query: manuscripts , medical as topic [SEP] Medical as topic manuscripts is works about unpublished medical works.

name: map
query: Query: map [SEP] Map is works consisting of representations, normally to scale and on a flat medium, of a selection of material or [MASK] features on the surface of the earth. They may be used also in delineating the heavens and celestial bodies. (From Anglo-American Cataloguing Rules, 2d ed, p619)

name: map kinase kinase kinase 1
query: Query: map kinase kinase kinase 1 [SEP] Map kinase kinase kinase 1 is a 195-kDa zinc finger motif-containing map kinase kinase kinase with broad specificity for map kinase kinases. It localizes to the cytoskeleton and can activate a variety of map kinase-dependent pathways.

name: map kinase kinase kinase 2
query: Query: map kinase kinase kinase 2 [SEP] Map kinase kinase kinase 2 is a 70-kDa map kinase kinase kinase with specificity for map kinase kinase 5. It is activated during the cellular response to growth factors, oxidative stress, and hyperosmotic conditions.

name: map kinase kinase kinase 3
query: Query: map kinase kinase kinase 3 [SEP] Map kinase kinase kinase 3 is a 70-kDa mapk kinase kinase with specificity for map kinase kinase 5.

name: map kinase kinase kinase 5
query: Query: map kinase kinase kinase 5 [SEP] Map kinase kinase kinase 5 is a 150-kDa map kinase kinase kinase that may play a role in the induction of apoptosis. It has specificity for map kinase kinase 3; map kinase kinase 4; and map kinase kinase 6.

name: margins of excision
query: Query: margins of excision [SEP] Margins of excision is the edges of tissue removed in a surgery for assessment of the effectiveness of a surgical procedure in achieving the local control of a neoplasm and the adequacy of tumor removal. When the margin is negative or not involved by tumor (e.g., cancer) it suggests all of the tumor has been removed by the surgery.

name: markov chains
query: Query: markov chains [SEP] Markov chains is a stochastic process such that the conditional probability distribution for a state at any future instant, given the present state, is unaffected by any additional knowledge of the past history of the system.

name: marriage
query: Query: marriage [SEP] Marriage is the social institution involving legal and/or religious sanction whereby individuals are joined together.

name: mars
query: Query: mars [SEP] Mars is the fourth planet in order from the sun. Its two natural satellites are Deimos and Phobos. It is one of the four inner or terrestrial planets of the solar system.

name: mass drug administration
query: Query: mass drug administration [SEP] Mass drug administration is administration of a medication to at-risk individuals in a population without individual diagnosis. It is often used in order to treat, control, and/or prevent spread of often [MASK] [MASK] such as neglected diseases in high disease burden areas.

name: material safety data sheets
query: Query: material safety data sheets [SEP] Material safety data sheets is information or data used to ensure the safe handling and disposal of substances in the workplace. Such information includes physical properties (i.e. melting, boiling, flashing points), as well as data on toxicity, health effects, reactivity, storage, disposal, [MASK], protective equipment, and spill-handling procedures.

name: materials science
query: Query: materials science [SEP] Materials science is an interdisciplinary study of the microstructure and composition of various materials such as metals, semiconductors, ceramics, and polymers, in relation to their macromolecular physical and chemical properties. Materials science enables the custom creation of new materials with specific properties and uses.

name: maternal behavior
query: Query: maternal behavior [SEP] Maternal behavior is the behavior patterns associated with or characteristic of a mother.

name: maternal death
query: Query: maternal death [SEP] Maternal death is the death of the female parent.

name: maternal deprivation
query: Query: maternal deprivation [SEP] Maternal deprivation is prolonged separation of the offspring from the mother.

name: maternal exposure
query: Query: maternal exposure [SEP] Maternal exposure is exposure of the female parent, human or animal, to potentially harmful chemical, physical, or biological agents in the environment or to environmental factors that may include ionizing radiation, pathogenic organisms, or toxic chemicals that may affect offspring. It includes pre-conception maternal exposure.

name: maternal mortality
query: Query: maternal mortality [SEP] Maternal mortality is maternal deaths resulting from complications of pregnancy and childbirth in a given population.

name: maternal serum screening tests
query: Query: maternal serum screening tests [SEP] Maternal serum screening tests is analysis of the level of specific biomarkers in a pregnant woman's sera to identify those at risk for pregnancy complications or birth defects.

name: maternal welfare
query: Query: maternal welfare [SEP] Maternal welfare is organized efforts by communities or organizations to improve the health and well-being of the mother.

name: mating factor
query: Query: mating factor [SEP] Mating factor is a protein also known as pheromone mating factor that occurs on the surfaces of organisms such as yeast and fungi.

name: mating preference , animal
query: Query: mating preference , animal [SEP] Animal mating preference is the selection or choice of [MASK] in animals. Often this reproductive preference is based on traits in the potential mate, such as coloration, size, or behavioral boldness. If the chosen ones are genetically different from the rejected ones, then natural selection is occurring.

name: matrix bands
query: Query: matrix bands [SEP] Matrix bands is devices which provide an artificial temporary wall, or matrix, used in filling a prepared cavity.

name: maxillary artery
query: Query: maxillary artery [SEP] Maxillary artery is a branch of the external carotid artery which distributes to the deep structures of the face (internal maxillary) and to the side of the face and nose (external maxillary).

name: maximal respiratory pressures
query: Query: maximal respiratory pressures [SEP] Maximal respiratory pressures is a respiratory function test that includes the maximal inspiratory pressure and maximal expiratory pressure. It is determined by spirometry that measures the patient's residual volume and total lung capacity and assesses the strength of respiratory muscles.

name: maximum allowable concentration
query: Query: maximum allowable concentration [SEP] Maximum allowable concentration is the maximum exposure to a biologically active physical or chemical agent that is allowed during an 8-hour period (a workday) in a population of workers, or during a 24-hour period in the general population, which does not appear to cause appreciable harm, whether immediate or delayed for any period, in the target population. (From Lewis Dictionary of Toxicology, 1st ed)

name: maze procedure
query: Query: maze procedure [SEP] Maze procedure is a surgical treatment in which heart tissue is scarred (cut-and-sew method), excised or otherwise destroyed in an open chest approach to direct electrical signals through a more controlled path via the atrioventricular node. It is often used to restore normal rhythms in atrial fibrillation.

name: meals
query: Query: meals [SEP] Meals is a portion of the food eaten for the day, usually at regular occasions during the day.

name: meaningful use
query: Query: meaningful use [SEP] Meaningful use is using certified electronic health records technology to improve quality, safety, efficiency, and reduce healthcare disparities; engage patients and families in their health care; improve care coordination; improve population and public health; while maintaining privacy and security.

name: mean platelet volume
query: Query: mean platelet volume [SEP] Mean platelet volume is a measure of the size of platelets.

name: meat products
query: Query: meat products [SEP] Meat products is articles of food which are derived by a process of manufacture from any portion of carcasses of any animal used for food (e.g., head cheese, sausage, scrapple).

name: mechanics
query: Query: mechanics [SEP] Mechanics is the branch of physics which deals with the motions of material bodies, including kinematics, dynamics, and statics. When the laws of mechanics are applied to living structures, as to the locomotor system, it is referred to as biomechanical phenomena. (From Dorland, 28th ed)

name: medial forebrain bundle
query: Query: medial forebrain bundle [SEP] Medial forebrain bundle is a complex group of fibers arising from the basal olfactory regions, the periamygdaloid region, and the septal nuclei, and passing to the lateral hypothalamus. Some fibers continue into the tegmentum.

name: medial tibial stress syndrome
query: Query: medial tibial stress syndrome [SEP] Medial tibial stress syndrome is skeletal muscle pain and tenderness along the posteromedial tibia resulting from exercise such as [MASK] and other physical activity.

name: median nerve
query: Query: median nerve [SEP] Median nerve is a major nerve of the upper extremity. In humans, the fibers of the median nerve originate in the lower cervical and upper thoracic spinal cord (usually c6 to t1), travel via the brachial plexus, and supply sensory and motor innervation to parts of the forearm and hand.

name: mediator complex subunit 1
query: Query: mediator complex subunit 1 [SEP] Mediator complex subunit 1 is a mediator complex subunit that is believed to play a key role in the coactivation of nuclear receptor-activated transcription by the mediator complex. It interacts with a variety of nuclear receptors including retinoic acid receptors; thyroid hormone receptors; vitamin d receptors; peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors; estrogen receptors; and [MASK].

name: medicaid
query: Query: medicaid [SEP] Medicaid is federal program, created by Public Law 89-97, Title xix, a 1965 amendment to the Social Security Act, administered by the states, that provides health care benefits to indigent and medically indigent persons.

name: medical informatics computing
query: Query: medical informatics computing [SEP] Medical informatics computing is precise procedural mathematical and logical operations utilized in the study of medical information pertaining to health care.

name: medical laboratory personnel
query: Query: medical laboratory personnel [SEP] Medical laboratory personnel is health care professionals, technicians, and assistants staffing laboratories in research or health care facilities.

name: medical laboratory science
query: Query: medical laboratory science [SEP] Medical laboratory science is the specialty related to the performance of techniques in clinical pathology such as those in hematology, microbiology, and other general clinical laboratory applications.

name: medically unexplained symptoms
query: Query: medically unexplained symptoms [SEP] Medically unexplained symptoms is persistent health symptoms which remain unexplained after a complete medical evaluation. a cluster of symptoms that consistently appear together but without a known cause are referred to as a medically unexplained syndrome (mus).

name: medical office buildings
query: Query: medical office buildings [SEP] Medical office buildings is office and laboratory facilities constructed for the use of physicians and other health personnel.

name: medical order entry systems
query: Query: medical order entry systems [SEP] Medical order entry systems is information systems, usually computer-assisted, that enable providers to initiate medical procedures, prescribe medications, etc. These systems support medical decision-making and error-reduction during patient care.

name: medical record linkage
query: Query: medical record linkage [SEP] Medical record linkage is the creation and maintenance of medical and vital records in multiple institutions in a manner that will facilitate the combined use of the records of identified individuals.

name: medical records department , hospital
query: Query: medical records department , hospital [SEP] Hospital medical records department is hospital department responsible for the creating, care, storage and retrieval of medical records. It also provides statistical information for the medical and administrative staff.

name: medical waste disposal
query: Query: medical waste disposal [SEP] Medical waste disposal is management, removal, and elimination of biologic, infectious, pathologic, and [MASK]. The concept includes blood, mucus, tissue removed at surgery or autopsy, soiled surgical dressings, and other materials requiring special control and handling. Disposal may take place where the waste is generated or elsewhere.

name: medical writing
query: Query: medical writing [SEP] Medical writing is the practice of writing usually by a skilled or specialized writer focused on the reporting or dissemination of medical information for a target audience.

name: medicare part a
query: Query: medicare part a [SEP] Medicare part a is the compulsory portion of Medicare that is known as the Hospital Insurance Program. All persons 65 years and older who are entitled to benefits under the Old Age, Survivors, Disability and Health Insurance Program or railroad [MASK], persons under the age of 65 who have been eligible for disability for more than two years, and insured workers (and their dependents) requiring renal dialysis or kidney transplantation are automatically enrolled in Medicare Part a.

name: medicare part c
query: Query: medicare part c [SEP] Medicare part c is the Balanced Budget Act (bba) of 1997 establishes a Medicare+Choice program under part c of Title xviii, Section 4001, of the Social Security Act. Under this program, an eligible individual may elect to receive Medicare benefits through enrollment in a Medicare+Choice plan. Beneficiaries may choose to use private pay options, establish [MASK], use managed care plans, or join provider-sponsored plans.

name: medicare payment advisory commission
query: Query: medicare payment advisory commission [SEP] Medicare payment advisory commission is the Commission was created by the Balanced Budget Act of 1997 under Title xviii. It is specifically charged to review the effect of Medicare+Choice under Medicare Part c and to review payment policies under Parts a and b. It is also generally charged to evaluate the effect of prospective payment policies and their impact on health care delivery in the us. The former Prospective Payment Assessment Commission (ProPAC) and the [MASK] (pprc) were merged to form medpac.

name: medication adherence
query: Query: medication adherence [SEP] Medication adherence is voluntary cooperation of the patient in taking drugs or medicine as prescribed. This includes timing, dosage, and frequency.

name: medication therapy management
query: Query: medication therapy management [SEP] Medication therapy management is assistance in managing and monitoring drug therapy for patients receiving treatment for cancer or chronic conditions such as asthma and diabetes, consulting with patients and their families on the proper use of medication; conducting wellness and disease prevention programs to improve public health; overseeing medication use in a variety of settings.

name: medicine , african traditional
query: Query: medicine , african traditional [SEP] African traditional medicine is a system of traditional medicine which is based on the beliefs and practices of the African peoples. It includes treatment by [MASK] and other materia medica as well as by the ministrations of diviners, medicine men, witch doctors, and sorcerers.

name: medicine , arabic
query: Query: medicine , arabic [SEP] Arabic medicine is traditional concepts of medicine and associated methods reflected in medicine in the arab world.

name: medicine in the arts
query: Query: medicine in the arts [SEP] Medicine in the arts is depiction of medical issues or themes via the arts including visual, oral, or written forms of expression.

name: mediterranean islands
query: Query: mediterranean islands [SEP] Mediterranean islands is islands in the Mediterranean Sea. The chief islands are the [MASK], Corsica, Crete, Cyprus, the Cyclades, Dodecanese and Ionian Islands, Malta, Sardinia and Sicily.

name: medline
query: Query: medline [SEP] Medline is the premier bibliographic [MASK] of the national library of medicine. medline® (medlars Online) is the primary subset of pubmed and can be searched on NLM's Web site in PubMed or the nlm Gateway. medline references are indexed with medical subject headings (MeSH).

name: medullary sponge kidney
query: Query: medullary sponge kidney [SEP] Medullary sponge kidney is a non-hereditary kidney disorder characterized by the abnormally dilated (ectasia) medullary and inner papillary portions of the collecting ducts. These collecting ducts usually contain cysts or diverticula filled with jelly-like material or small calculi (kidney stones) leading to infections or obstruction. It should be distinguished from congenital or hereditary polycystic kidney diseases.

name: meiosis
query: Query: meiosis [SEP] Meiosis is a type of cell nucleus division, occurring during maturation of the germ cells. Two successive cell nucleus divisions following a single chromosome duplication (s phase) result in daughter cells with half the number of chromosomes as the parent cells.

name: melatonin
query: Query: melatonin [SEP] Melatonin is a biogenic amine that is found in animals and plants. In mammals, melatonin is produced by the pineal gland. Its secretion increases in darkness and decreases during exposure to light. Melatonin is implicated in the regulation of sleep, mood, and reproduction. Melatonin is also an effective antioxidant.

name: membrane cofactor protein
query: Query: membrane cofactor protein [SEP] Membrane cofactor protein is a ubiquitously expressed complement receptor that binds complement c3b and complement c4b and serves as a co-factor for their inactivation by complement factor i. It also interacts with a wide variety of pathogens and mediates the immune response.

name: memory , episodic
query: Query: memory , episodic [SEP] Episodic memory is type of declarative memory, consisting of personal memory in contrast to general knowledge.

name: meningitis , fungal
query: Query: meningitis , fungal [SEP] Fungal meningitis is meningitis caused by fungal agents which may occur as [MASK] or arise in immunocompetent hosts.

name: meningitis , pneumococcal
query: Query: meningitis , pneumococcal [SEP] Pneumococcal meningitis is an acute purulent infection of the meninges and subarachnoid space caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae, most prevalent in children and adults over the age of 60. This illness may be associated with otitis media; mastoiditis; sinusitis; respiratory tract infections; sickle cell disease (anemia, sickle cell); skull fractures; and other disorders. Clinical manifestations include fever; headache; [MASK] stiffness; and somnolence followed by seizures; focal neurologic deficits (notably deafness); and coma. (From Miller et al., Merritt's Textbook of Neurology, 9th ed, p111)

name: meningitis , viral
query: Query: meningitis , viral [SEP] Viral meningitis is viral infections of the leptomeninges and subarachnoid space. togaviridae infections; flaviviridae infections; rubella; bunyaviridae infections; orbivirus infections; picornaviridae infections; orthomyxoviridae infections; rhabdoviridae infections; arenaviridae infections; herpesviridae infections; adenoviridae infections; jc virus infections; and retroviridae infections may cause this form of meningitis. Clinical manifestations include fever, headache, [MASK] pain, vomiting, photophobia, and signs of meningeal irritation. (From Joynt, Clinical Neurology, 1996, Ch26, pp1-3)

name: menopause , premature
query: Query: menopause , premature [SEP] Premature menopause is the premature cessation of menses (menstruation) when the last menstrual period occurs in a woman under the age of 40. It is due to the depletion of ovarian follicles. Premature menopause can be caused by diseases; ovariectomy; radiation; chemicals; and chromosomal abnormalities.

name: mental competency
query: Query: mental competency [SEP] Mental competency is the ability to understand the nature and effect of the act in which the individual is engaged. (From Black's Law Dictionary, 6th ed).

name: mental health
query: Query: mental health [SEP] Mental health is emotional, psychological, and social well-being of an individual or group.

name: mentally disabled persons
query: Query: mentally disabled persons [SEP] Mentally disabled persons is mentally disabled persons

name: mental or behavioral dysfunction
query: Query: mental or behavioral dysfunction [SEP] Mental or behavioral dysfunction is troublesome or disruptive behavioral displays.

name: mental process
query: Query: mental process [SEP] Mental process is conceptual functions or thinking in all its forms.

name: mental recall
query: Query: mental recall [SEP] Mental recall is the process whereby a representation of past experience is elicited.

name: mercury , planet
query: Query: mercury , planet [SEP] Planet mercury is the first planet in order from the sun. It has no known natural satellites. It is one of the four inner or terrestrial planets of the solar system.

name: mercury compounds
query: Query: mercury compounds [SEP] Mercury compounds is inorganic compounds that contain mercury as an integral part of the molecule.

name: mercury isotopes
query: Query: mercury isotopes [SEP] Mercury isotopes is stable mercury atoms that have the same atomic number as the element mercury, but differ in atomic weight. Hg-196, 198-201, and 204 are stable mercury isotopes.

name: mesenchymal stem cells
query: Query: mesenchymal stem cells [SEP] Mesenchymal stem cells is mesenchymal stem cells, also referred to as multipotent stromal cells or mesenchymal stromal cells are multipotent, non-hematopoietic adult stem cells that are present in multiple tissues, including bone marrow; adipose tissue; and wharton jelly. Mesenchymal stem cells can differentiate into mesodermal lineages, such as adipocytic, osteocytic and chondrocytic.

name: mesenchymal stem cell transplantation
query: Query: mesenchymal stem cell transplantation [SEP] Mesenchymal stem cell transplantation is transfer of mesenchymal stem cells between individuals within the same species (transplantation, homologous) or transfer within the same individual (transplantation, autologous).

name: mesenteric cyst
query: Query: mesenteric cyst [SEP] Mesenteric cyst is a rare intra-abdominal tumor in the mesentery. Mesenteric cysts are usually benign and can be very large fluid-filled (2000 mL) lesions.

name: mesenteric ischemia
query: Query: mesenteric ischemia [SEP] Mesenteric ischemia is ischemic tissue injury produced by insufficient perfusion of intestinal tissue by the mesenteric circulation (i.e., celiac [MASK] artery; infererior mesenteric artery; and mesenteric veins). It can progress from ischemia; edema; and gangrene of the bowel wall to peritonitis and cardiovascular collapse.

name: mesenteric vascular occlusion
query: Query: mesenteric vascular occlusion [SEP] Mesenteric vascular occlusion is obstruction of the flow in the splanchnic circulation by atherosclerosis; embolism; thrombosis; stenosis; trauma; and compression or intrinsic pressure from adjacent tumors. Rare causes are drugs, intestinal parasites, and vascular immunoinflammatory diseases such as periarteritis nodosa and thromboangiitis obliterans. (From Juergens et al., Peripheral Vascular Diseases, 5th ed, pp295-6)

name: mesenteric veins
query: Query: mesenteric veins [SEP] Mesenteric veins is veins which return blood from the intestines; the inferior mesenteric vein empties into the splenic vein, the superior mesenteric vein joins the splenic vein to form the portal vein.

name: mesoderm
query: Query: mesoderm [SEP] Mesoderm is the middle germ layer of an embryo derived from three paired mesenchymal aggregates along the neural tube.

name: metabolic clearance rate
query: Query: metabolic clearance rate [SEP] Metabolic clearance rate is volume of biological fluid completely cleared of drug metabolites as measured in unit time. Elimination occurs as a result of metabolic processes in the kidney, liver, saliva, sweat, intestine, heart, brain, or other site.

name: metabolic equivalent
query: Query: metabolic equivalent [SEP] Metabolic equivalent is a measurement of oxygen uptake in a sitting, resting person (resting oxygen consumption), varying with age, [MASK], race, and other factors. In normal adult men, one met is approximately 3.5 ml O2/kg/min of body weight. Oxygen uptake during activities or work can be measured in METs which can be use to determine health status and exercise prescription.

name: metabolic syndrome
query: Query: metabolic syndrome [SEP] Metabolic syndrome is a cluster of symptoms that are risk factors for cardiovascular diseases and type 2 diabetes mellitus. The major components of metabolic syndrome include [MASK]; atherogenic dyslipidemia; hypertension; hyperglycemia; insulin resistance; a proinflammatory state; and a prothrombotic (thrombosis) state.

name: metadata
query: Query: metadata [SEP] Metadata is structured data elements used to describe other data.

name: metal ceramic alloys
query: Query: metal ceramic alloys [SEP] Metal ceramic alloys is the fusion of ceramics (porcelain) to an alloy of two or more metals for use in restorative and prosthodontic dentistry. Examples of metal alloys employed include cobalt-chromium, gold-palladium, gold-[MASK]-palladium, and nickel-based alloys.

name: metals , rare earth
query: Query: metals , rare earth [SEP] Rare earth metals is a group of elements that include scandium; yttrium; and the lanthanoid series elements. Historically, the rare earth metals got their name from the fact that they were never found in their pure elemental form, but as an oxide. In addition they were very difficult to purify. They are not truly rare and comprise about 25% of the metals in the earth's crust.

name: methanol
query: Query: methanol [SEP] Methanol is a colorless, flammable liquid used in the manufacture of formaldehyde and acetic acid, in chemical synthesis, antifreeze, and as a solvent. Ingestion of methanol is toxic and may cause blindness.

name: methyl cpg binding domain
query: Query: methyl cpg binding domain [SEP] Methyl cpg binding domain is a protein domain of about 70 amino acids in length that folds into a sandwich structure consisting of a beta sheet, alpha helix, and C-terminal hairpin loop which forms a hydrophobic methylated-DNA binding patch. It binds to methylated cpg islands in eukaryotes and occurs with other dna and chromatin binding domains such as at-hook motifs in eukaryotic dna binding proteins.

name: metric system
query: Query: metric system [SEP] Metric system is a system of units used in scientific work throughout the world and employed in general commercial transactions and engineering applications. Its units of length, time, and mass are the meter, second, and kilogram respectively, or decimal multiples and submultiples thereof. ( McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

name: mice , 129 strain
query: Query: mice , 129 strain [SEP] 129 strain mice is strains of mice arising from a parental inbred stock that was subsequently used to produce substrains of knockout and other mutant mice with targeted mutations.

name: mice , inbred a
query: Query: mice , inbred a [SEP] Inbred a mice is an inbred strain of mouse that is widely used in [MASK] studies and cancer research.

name: mice , inbred balb c
query: Query: mice , inbred balb c [SEP] Inbred balb c mice is an inbred strain of mouse that is widely used in [MASK] studies and cancer research.

name: mice , inbred cftr
query: Query: mice , inbred cftr [SEP] Inbred cftr mice is a strain of mice widely studied as a model for cystic fibrosis. These mice are generated from embryonic stem cells in which the cftr (cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator) gene is inactivated by gene targeting. As a result, all mice have one copy of this altered gene in all their tissues. Mice homozygous for the disrupted gene exhibit many features common to young cystic fibrosis patients, including failure to thrive, meconium ileus, and alteration of mucous and serous glands.

name: mice , inbred nod
query: Query: mice , inbred nod [SEP] Inbred nod mice is a strain of non-obese diabetic mice developed in Japan that has been widely studied as a model for T-cell-dependent autoimmune insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus in which insulitis is a major histopathologic feature, and in which genetic susceptibility is strongly MHC-linked.

name: mice , knockout , apoe
query: Query: mice , knockout , apoe [SEP] Apoe knockout mice is strains of mice that contain genetic disruptions (knockout) of apolipoproteins e genes. They are used as models for atherosclerosis research.

name: mice , neurologic mutants
query: Query: mice , neurologic mutants [SEP] Neurologic mutants mice is mice which carry mutant genes for neurologic defects or abnormalities.

name: michigan
query: Query: michigan [SEP] Michigan is state bounded on the north by the Great [MASK], on the east by Canada, on the south by Wisconsin, Indiana, and Ohio, and on the west by [MASK] Michigan and Wisconsin.

name: microbial interactions
query: Query: microbial interactions [SEP] Microbial interactions is the inter- and intra-relationships between various microorganisms. This can include both positive (like symbiosis) and negative (like antibiosis) interactions. Examples include virus - bacteria and bacteria - bacteria.

name: microbial viability
query: Query: microbial viability [SEP] Microbial viability is ability of a microbe to survive under given conditions. This can also be related to a colony's ability to replicate.

name: microbiota
query: Query: microbiota [SEP] Microbiota is the full collection of microbes (bacteria, fungi, virus, etc.) that naturally exist within a particular biological niche such as an organism, soil, a body of water, etc.

name: microsatellite repeats
query: Query: microsatellite repeats [SEP] Microsatellite repeats is a variety of simple repeat sequences that are distributed throughout the genome. They are characterized by a short repeat unit of 2-8 basepairs that is repeated up to 100 times. They are also known as short tandem repeats (STRs).

name: microscopy , acoustic
query: Query: microscopy , acoustic [SEP] Acoustic microscopy is a scientific tool based on ultrasonography and used not only for the [MASK] of microstructure in metalwork but also in living tissue. In biomedical application, the acoustic propagation speed in normal and abnormal tissues can be quantified to distinguish their tissue elasticity and other properties.

name: microscopy , electrochemical , scanning
query: Query: microscopy , electrochemical , scanning [SEP] Scanning electrochemical microscopy is a scanning probe microscopy technique that uses an ultramicroelectrode as the scanning probe that simultaneously records changes in electrochemical potential as it scans thereby creating topographical images with localized electrochemical information.

name: microscopy , electron , scanning
query: Query: microscopy , electron , scanning [SEP] Scanning [MASK] microscopy is microscopy in which the object is examined directly by an [MASK] beam scanning the specimen point-by-point. The image is constructed by detecting the products of specimen interactions that are projected above the plane of the sample, such as backscattered [MASK]. Although scanning transmission [MASK] microscopy also scans the specimen point by point with the [MASK] beam, the image is constructed by detecting the [MASK], or their interaction products that are transmitted through the sample plane, so that is a form of transmission [MASK] microscopy.

name: microscopy , electron , scanning transmission
query: Query: microscopy , electron , scanning transmission [SEP] Scanning transmission [MASK] microscopy is a type of transmission [MASK] microscopy in which the object is examined directly by an extremely narrow [MASK] beam scanning the specimen point-by-point and using the reactions of the [MASK] that are transmitted through the specimen to create the image. It should not be confused with scanning [MASK] microscopy.

name: microscopy , fluorescence
query: Query: microscopy , fluorescence [SEP] Fluorescence microscopy is microscopy of specimens stained with fluorescent dye (usually fluorescein isothiocyanate) or of naturally fluorescent materials, which emit light when exposed to ultraviolet or blue light. Immunofluorescence microscopy utilizes antibodies that are labeled with fluorescent dye.

name: microscopy , polarization
query: Query: microscopy , polarization [SEP] Polarization microscopy is microscopy using polarized light in which phenomena due to the preferential orientation of optical properties with respect to the vibration plane of the polarized light are made visible and correlated parameters are made measurable.

name: microsomes , liver
query: Query: microsomes , liver [SEP] Liver microsomes is closed vesicles of fragmented endoplasmic reticulum created when liver cells or tissue are disrupted by homogenization. They may be smooth or rough.

name: microspheres
query: Query: microspheres [SEP] Microspheres is small uniformly-sized spherical particles, of micrometer dimensions, frequently labeled with radioisotopes or various reagents acting as tags or markers.

name: microvascular decompression surgery
query: Query: microvascular decompression surgery [SEP] Microvascular decompression surgery is surgery performed to relieve pressure from microvessels that are located around nerves and are causing nerve compression syndromes.

name: microwave imaging
query: Query: microwave imaging [SEP] Microwave imaging is use of microwaves as a diagnostic tool.

name: middle aged
query: Query: middle aged [SEP] Middle aged is an adult aged 45 - 64 years.

name: middle cerebral artery
query: Query: middle cerebral artery [SEP] Middle cerebral artery is the largest of the cerebral arteries. It trifurcates into temporal, frontal, and parietal branches supplying blood to most of the parenchyma of these lobes in the cerebral cortex. These are the areas involved in motor, sensory, and [MASK] activities.

name: midline thalamic nuclei
query: Query: midline thalamic nuclei [SEP] Midline thalamic nuclei is small, nonspecific nerve cells scattered in the periventricular gray matter, separating the medial part of the thalamus from the ependyma of the third ventricle. The group includes the paraventricular nucleus, paratenial nucleus, reuniens nucleus, rhomboidal nucleus, and subfascular nucleus.

name: military dentistry
query: Query: military dentistry [SEP] Military dentistry is the practice of dentistry as applied to special circumstances associated with military operations.

name: military facilities
query: Query: military facilities [SEP] Military facilities is areas designated for use by the armed forces personnel.

name: military family
query: Query: military family [SEP] Military family is men and women serving on active duty in the military, or in a reserve military force, and their immediate family including spouses, children, and parents.

name: military health
query: Query: military health [SEP] Military health is the physical and mental conditions of military personnel, active duty and retired u.s. Military personnel and their dependents.

name: military health services
query: Query: military health services [SEP] Military health services is services organized for the diagnosis and treatment of disease and the maintenance of health primarily of military personnel.

name: military hygiene
query: Query: military hygiene [SEP] Military hygiene is science dealing with the maintenance of health in servicemen.

name: military medicine
query: Query: military medicine [SEP] Military medicine is the practice of medicine as applied to special circumstances associated with military operations.

name: military personnel
query: Query: military personnel [SEP] Military personnel is persons including soldiers involved with the armed forces.

name: milk ejection
query: Query: milk ejection [SEP] Milk ejection is expulsion of milk from the mammary alveolar lumen, which is surrounded by a layer of milk-secreting epithelial cells and a network of myoepithelial cells. Contraction of the myoepithelial cells is regulated by neuroendocrine signals.

name: milk proteins
query: Query: milk proteins [SEP] Milk proteins is the major protein constituents of milk are caseins and whey proteins such as lactalbumin and lactoglobulins. immunoglobulins occur in high concentrations in colostrum and in relatively lower concentrations in milk. (Singleton and Sainsbury, Dictionary of Microbiology and Molecular Biology, 2d ed, p554)

name: miller fisher syndrome
query: Query: miller fisher syndrome [SEP] Miller fisher syndrome is a variant of the guillain-barre syndrome characterized by the acute onset of oculomotor dysfunction, ataxia, and loss of deep tendon reflexes with relative sparing of strength in the extremities and trunk. The ataxia is produced by peripheral sensory nerve dysfunction and not by cerebellar injury. Facial weakness and sensory loss may also occur. The process is mediated by autoantibodies directed against a component of myelin found in peripheral nerves. (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1313; Neurology 1987 Sep;37(9):1493-8)

name: mineral fibers
query: Query: mineral fibers [SEP] Mineral fibers is long, pliable, cohesive natural or manufactured filaments of various lengths. They form the structure of some minerals. The medical significance lies in their potential ability to cause various types of pneumoconiosis (e.g., asbestosis) after occupational or environmental exposure. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed, p708)

name: minimal clinically important difference
query: Query: minimal clinically important difference [SEP] Minimal clinically important difference is a statistically significant minimum [MASK] of clinical outcomes that demonstrates a clinical benefit of an intervention or treatment.

name: minority health
query: Query: minority health [SEP] Minority health is the concept covering the physical and mental conditions of members of minority groups.

name: minor lymphocyte stimulatory antigens
query: Query: minor lymphocyte stimulatory antigens [SEP] Minor lymphocyte stimulatory antigens is endogenous superantigens responsible for inducing strong proliferative responses in T-cells in mixed lymphocyte reactions (see lymphocyte culture test, mixed). They are encoded by mouse mammary tumor viruses that have integrated into the germ line as dna proviruses (minor lymphocyte stimulatory loci).

name: minor lymphocyte stimulatory loci
query: Query: minor lymphocyte stimulatory loci [SEP] Minor lymphocyte stimulatory loci is genetic loci responsible for the encoding of minor lymphocyte stimulatory antigens. There are at least two unlinked loci (in the mouse) and they appear to be separate from the major histocompatibility complex and minor histocompatibility loci. The mouse mammary tumor virus (see mammary tumor virus, mouse) has the ability to integrate into these loci. The antigens induce strong T-cell proliferative responses in mixed lymphocyte reactions.

name: minor planets
query: Query: minor planets [SEP] Minor planets is small solar system planetary bodies including asteroids. Most asteroids are found within the gap lying between the [MASK] of Mars and Jupiter.

name: mirror neurons
query: Query: mirror neurons [SEP] Mirror neurons is neurons that fire when an animal acts or observes the same action of another thus coding the motor response. They were originally discovered in the premotor and parietal cortex of the monkey and studies have shown that neurons that have a similar mechanism are present in humans. Mirror neurons are theorized to be related to social cognition.

name: missed diagnosis
query: Query: missed diagnosis [SEP] Missed diagnosis is failure to identify or diagnose a medical condition at the time a health professional is acquainted with the symptoms.

name: mitochondria , heart
query: Query: mitochondria , heart [SEP] Heart mitochondria is the mitochondria of the myocardium.

name: mitochondrial membrane transport proteins
query: Query: mitochondrial membrane transport proteins [SEP] [MASK] transport proteins is proteins involved in the transport of specific substances across the membranes of the mitochondria.

name: mitochondrial swelling
query: Query: mitochondrial swelling [SEP] Mitochondrial swelling is an increase in mitochondrial volume due to an influx of fluid; it occurs in hypotonic solutions due to osmotic pressure and in isotonic solutions as a result of altered permeability of the membranes of respiring mitochondria.

name: mitosis modulators
query: Query: mitosis modulators [SEP] [MASK] modulators is agents that affect [MASK] of cells.

name: mitral valve
query: Query: mitral valve [SEP] Mitral valve is the valve between the left atrium and left ventricle of the heart.

name: mitral valve stenosis
query: Query: mitral valve stenosis [SEP] Mitral valve stenosis is narrowing of the passage through the mitral valve due to fibrosis, and calcinosis in the leaflets and chordal areas. This elevates the left atrial pressure which, in turn, raises pulmonary venous and capillary pressure leading to bouts of dyspnea and tachycardia during physical exertion. rheumatic fever is its primary cause.

name: mixed connective tissue disease
query: Query: mixed connective tissue disease [SEP] Mixed connective tissue disease is a syndrome with overlapping clinical features of [MASK], scleroderma, polymyositis, and Raynaud's phenomenon. The disease is differentially characterized by high serum titers of antibodies to ribonuclease-sensitive extractable (saline soluble) nuclear antigen and a "speckled" epidermal nuclear staining pattern on direct immunofluorescence.

name: mixed tumor , malignant
query: Query: mixed tumor , malignant [SEP] Malignant mixed tumor is a malignant tumor composed of more than one type of neoplastic tissue. (Dorland, 27th ed)

name: mobile applications
query: Query: mobile applications [SEP] Mobile applications is computer programs or software installed on mobile electronic devices which support a wide range of functions and uses which include television, telephone, video, music, word processing, and Internet service.

name: mobile health units
query: Query: mobile health units [SEP] Mobile health units is movable or portable facilities in which diagnostic and therapeutic services are provided to the community.

name: mobility limitation
query: Query: mobility limitation [SEP] Mobility limitation is difficulty in walking from place to place.

name: models , cardiovascular
query: Query: models , cardiovascular [SEP] Cardiovascular models is theoretical representations that simulate the behavior or activity of the cardiovascular system, processes, or phenomena; includes the use of mathematical equations, computers and other electronic equipment.

name: models , genetic
query: Query: models , genetic [SEP] Genetic models is theoretical representations that simulate the behavior or activity of genetic processes or phenomena. They include the use of mathematical equations, computers, and other electronic equipment.

name: models , immunological
query: Query: models , immunological [SEP] Immunological models is theoretical representations that simulate the behavior or activity of immune system, processes, or phenomena. They include the use of mathematical equations, computers, and other electrical equipment.

name: models , neurological
query: Query: models , neurological [SEP] Neurological models is theoretical representations that simulate the behavior or activity of the neurological system, processes or phenomena; includes the use of mathematical equations, computers, and other electronic equipment.

name: models , organizational
query: Query: models , organizational [SEP] Organizational models is theoretical representations and constructs that describe or explain the structure and hierarchy of relationships and interactions within or between formal organizational entities or informal social groups.

name: molar , third
query: Query: molar , third [SEP] Third molar is the aftermost permanent tooth on each side in the maxilla and mandible.

name: molecular biology research technique
query: Query: molecular biology research technique [SEP] Molecular biology research technique is molecular biology research technique

name: molecular docking simulation
query: Query: molecular docking simulation [SEP] Molecular docking simulation is a computer simulation technique that is used to model the interaction between two molecules. Typically the docking simulation measures the interactions of a small molecule or ligand with a part of a larger molecule such as a protein.

name: molecular epidemiology
query: Query: molecular epidemiology [SEP] Molecular epidemiology is the application of molecular biology to the answering of epidemiological questions. The examination of patterns of changes in dna to implicate particular carcinogens and the use of molecular markers to predict which individuals are at highest risk for a disease are common examples.

name: molecular farming
query: Query: molecular farming [SEP] Molecular farming is the large scale production of pharmaceutically important and commercially valuable recombinant proteins.

name: molecular targeted therapy
query: Query: molecular targeted therapy [SEP] Molecular targeted therapy is treatments with drugs which interact with or block synthesis of specific cellular components characteristic of the individual's disease in order to stop or interrupt the specific biochemical dysfunction involved in progression of the disease.

name: molecular typing
query: Query: molecular typing [SEP] Molecular typing is using molecular biology techniques, such as dna sequence analysis; pulsed-field gel electrophoresis; and dna fingerprinting, to identify, classify, and compare organisms and their subtypes.

name: molecular weight
query: Query: molecular weight [SEP] Molecular weight is the sum of the weight of all the atoms in a molecule.

name: monitoring , intraoperative
query: Query: monitoring , intraoperative [SEP] Intraoperative monitoring is the constant checking on the state or condition of a patient during the course of a surgical operation (e.g., checking of vital signs).

name: monkey diseases
query: Query: monkey diseases [SEP] Monkey diseases is diseases of Old World and New World monkeys. This term includes diseases of baboons but not of chimpanzees or gorillas (= ape diseases).

name: moon
query: Query: moon [SEP] Moon is the natural satellite of the planet Earth. It includes the lunar cycles or phases, the lunar month, lunar landscapes, geography, and soil.

name: moral development
query: Query: moral development [SEP] Moral development is the process by which individuals internalize standards of right and wrong conduct.

name: moral obligations
query: Query: moral obligations [SEP] Moral obligations is duties that are based in ethics, rather than in law.

name: morning sickness
query: Query: morning sickness [SEP] Morning sickness is symptoms of nausea and vomiting in pregnant women that usually occur in the morning during the first 2 to 3 months of pregnancy. Severe persistent vomiting during pregnancy is called hyperemesis gravidarum.

name: mortality , premature
query: Query: mortality , premature [SEP] Premature mortality is deaths that occur before [MASK] is reached within a given population.

name: mosaic viruses
query: Query: mosaic viruses [SEP] Mosaic viruses is viruses which produce a mottled appearance of the leaves of plants.

name: mosquito vectors
query: Query: mosquito vectors [SEP] Mosquito vectors is mosquitoes (members of the family culicidae) that transmit pathogens or their intermediate forms from one host to another.

name: mothers
query: Query: mothers [SEP] Mothers is female parents, human or animal.

name: motion perception
query: Query: motion perception [SEP] Motion perception is the real or apparent movement of objects through the [MASK].

name: motion pictures
query: Query: motion pictures [SEP] Motion pictures is the art, technique, or business of producing motion pictures for entertainment, propaganda, or instruction.

name: motor cortex
query: Query: motor cortex [SEP] Motor cortex is area of the frontal lobe concerned with primary motor control located in the dorsal precentral gyrus immediately anterior to the central sulcus. It is comprised of three areas: the primary motor cortex located on the anterior paracentral lobule on the medial surface of the brain; the premotor cortex located anterior to the primary motor cortex; and the supplementary motor area located on the midline surface of the hemisphere anterior to the primary motor cortex.

name: motor disorders
query: Query: motor disorders [SEP] Motor disorders is motor skills deficits that significantly and persistently interfere with activities of daily living appropriate to chronological age.  (from dsm-5)

name: motor neurons , gamma
query: Query: motor neurons , gamma [SEP] Gamma motor neurons is motor neurons which activate the contractile regions of intrafusal skeletal muscle fibers, thus adjusting the sensitivity of the muscle spindles to stretch. Gamma motor neurons may be "static" or "dynamic" according to which aspect of responsiveness (or which fiber types) they regulate. The alpha and gamma motor neurons are often activated together (alpha gamma coactivation) which allows the spindles to contribute to the control of movement trajectories despite changes in muscle length.

name: motor vehicles
query: Query: motor vehicles [SEP] Motor vehicles is automobiles, trucks, buses, or similar engine-driven conveyances. (From Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

name: mouse embryonic stem cells
query: Query: mouse embryonic stem cells [SEP] Mouse embryonic stem cells is pluripotent stem cells derived from the blastocyst inner cell mass of day 3.5 mouse embryos.

name: mouth breathing
query: Query: mouth breathing [SEP] Mouth breathing is abnormal breathing through the mouth, usually associated with obstructive disorders of the nasal passages.

name: mouth floor
query: Query: mouth floor [SEP] Mouth floor is the area of the mouth beneath the tongue.

name: mouth rehabilitation
query: Query: mouth rehabilitation [SEP] Mouth rehabilitation is process of restoring damaged or decayed teeth using various restorative and non-cosmetic materials so that [MASK] is improved.

name: moving and lifting patients
query: Query: moving and lifting patients [SEP] Moving and lifting patients is moving or repositioning patients within their beds, from bed to bed, bed to chair, or otherwise from one posture or surface to another.

name: multicenter studies as topic
query: Query: multicenter studies as topic [SEP] Multicenter studies as topic is works about controlled studies which are planned and carried out by several cooperating institutions to assess certain variables and outcomes in specific patient populations, for example, a multicenter study of congenital anomalies in children.

name: multicenter study
query: Query: multicenter study [SEP] Multicenter study is a work that reports on a study executed by several cooperating institutions.

name: multifunctional nanoparticles
query: Query: multifunctional nanoparticles [SEP] Multifunctional nanoparticles is nanoparticles that are engineered to have two or more physical properties.

name: multilevel analysis
query: Query: multilevel analysis [SEP] Multilevel analysis is the statistical manipulation of hierarchically and non-hierarchically nested data. It includes clustered data, such as a sample of subjects within a group of schools. Prevalent in the social, behavioral sciences, and biomedical sciences, both linear and nonlinear regression models are applied.

name: multiple chemical sensitivity
query: Query: multiple chemical sensitivity [SEP] Multiple chemical sensitivity is an acquired disorder characterized by recurrent symptoms, referable to multiple organ systems, occurring in response to demonstrable exposure to many chemically unrelated compounds at doses below those established in the general population to cause harmful effects. (Cullen mr. The worker with multiple chemical sensitivities: an overview. Occup Med 1987;2(4):655-61)

name: multiple chronic conditions
query: Query: multiple chronic conditions [SEP] Multiple chronic conditions is two or more concurrent chronic physical, mental, or behavioral health problems in an individual.

name: multiple pulmonary nodules
query: Query: multiple pulmonary nodules [SEP] Multiple pulmonary nodules is a number of small lung lesions characterized by small round masses of 2- to 3-mm in diameter. They are usually detected by chest ct scans (computed tomography, x-ray). Such nodules can be associated with metastases of malignancies inside or outside the lung, benign granulomas, or other lesions.

name: multiplex polymerase chain reaction
query: Query: multiplex polymerase chain reaction [SEP] Multiplex polymerase chain reaction is methods for using more than one primer [MASK] in a polymerase chain reaction to amplify more than one segment of the target dna sequence in a single reaction.

name: multivariate analysis
query: Query: multivariate analysis [SEP] Multivariate analysis is a [MASK] of techniques used when variation in several variables has to be studied simultaneously. In statistics, multivariate analysis is interpreted as any analytic method that allows simultaneous study of two or more dependent variables.

name: murine hepatitis virus
query: Query: murine hepatitis virus [SEP] Murine hepatitis virus is a species of the coronavirus genus causing hepatitis in mice. Four strains have been identified as mhv 1, mhv 2, mhv 3, and mhv 4 (also known as mhv-jhm, which is neurotropic and causes disseminated encephalomyelitis with demyelination as well as focal liver necrosis).

name: muscle , smooth , vascular
query: Query: muscle , smooth , vascular [SEP] Vascular smooth muscle is the nonstriated involuntary muscle tissue of blood vessels.

name: muscle development
query: Query: muscle development [SEP] Muscle development is developmental events leading to the formation of adult muscular system, which includes differentiation of the various types of muscle cell precursors, migration of myoblasts, activation of myogenesis and development of muscle anchorage.

name: muscle fatigue
query: Query: muscle fatigue [SEP] Muscle fatigue is a state arrived at through prolonged and strong contraction of a muscle. Studies in [MASK] during prolonged submaximal exercise have shown that muscle fatigue increases in almost direct proportion to the rate of muscle glycogen depletion. Muscle fatigue in short-term maximal exercise is associated with oxygen lack and an increased level of blood and muscle lactic acid, and an accompanying increase in hydrogen-ion concentration in the exercised muscle.

name: muscle fibers , skeletal
query: Query: muscle fibers , skeletal [SEP] Skeletal muscle fibers is large, multinucleate single cells, either cylindrical or prismatic in shape, that form the basic unit of skeletal muscle. They consist of myofibrils enclosed within and attached to the sarcolemma. They are derived from the fusion of skeletal myoblasts (myoblasts, skeletal) into a syncytium, followed by differentiation.

name: muscle neoplasms
query: Query: muscle neoplasms [SEP] Muscle neoplasms is tumors or cancer located in muscle tissue or specific muscles. They are differentiated from neoplasms, muscle tissue which are neoplasms composed of skeletal, cardiac, or smooth muscle tissue, such as myosarcoma or leiomyoma.

name: muscle relaxation
query: Query: muscle relaxation [SEP] Muscle relaxation is that phase of a muscle twitch during which a muscle returns to a resting position.

name: muscle rigidity
query: Query: muscle rigidity [SEP] Muscle rigidity is continuous involuntary sustained muscle contraction which is often a manifestation of basal ganglia diseases. When an affected muscle is passively stretched, the degree of resistance remains constant regardless of the rate at which the muscle is stretched. This feature helps to distinguish rigidity from muscle spasticity. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p73)

name: muscle stretching exercises
query: Query: muscle stretching exercises [SEP] Muscle stretching exercises is exercises that stretch the muscle fibers with the aim to increase muscle-tendon flexibility, improve range of motion or musculoskeletal function, and prevent injuries. There are various types of stretching techniques including active, passive (relaxed), static, dynamic (gentle), ballistic (forced), isometric, and others.

name: muscle weakness
query: Query: muscle weakness [SEP] Muscle weakness is a vague complaint of debility, fatigue, or exhaustion attributable to weakness of various muscles. The weakness can be characterized as subacute or chronic, often progressive, and is a manifestation of many muscle and neuromuscular diseases. (From Wyngaarden et al., Cecil Textbook of Medicine, 19th ed, p2251)

name: muscular atrophy
query: Query: muscular atrophy [SEP] Muscular atrophy is derangement in size and number of muscle fibers occurring with aging, reduction in blood supply, or following immobilization, prolonged weightlessness, malnutrition, and particularly in denervation.

name: muscular atrophy , spinal
query: Query: muscular atrophy , spinal [SEP] Spinal muscular atrophy is a group of disorders marked by progressive degeneration of motor neurons in the spinal cord resulting in weakness and muscular atrophy, usually without evidence of injury to the corticospinal tracts. Diseases in this category include Werdnig-Hoffmann disease and later onset spinal muscular atrophies of childhood, most of which are hereditary. (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1089)

name: music therapy
query: Query: music therapy [SEP] Music therapy is the use of music as an adjunctive therapy in the treatment of neurological, mental, or behavioral disorders.

name: mutation , missense
query: Query: mutation , missense [SEP] Missense mutation is a mutation in which a codon is mutated to one directing the incorporation of a different amino acid. This substitution may result in an inactive or unstable product. (From a Dictionary of Genetics, King & Stansfield, 5th ed)

name: mutation accumulation
query: Query: mutation accumulation [SEP] Mutation accumulation is concept which describes the incremental effects of mutation in living organisms.

name: mutation rate
query: Query: mutation rate [SEP] Mutation rate is the number of mutations that occur in a specific sequence, gene, or genome over a specified period of time such as years, cell divisions, or generations.

name: myelin basic protein
query: Query: myelin basic protein [SEP] Myelin basic protein is an abundant cytosolic protein that plays a critical role in the structure of multilamellar myelin. Myelin basic protein binds to the cytosolic sides of myelin cell membranes and causes a tight adhesion between opposing cell membranes.

name: myelin sheath
query: Query: myelin sheath [SEP] Myelin sheath is the lipid-rich sheath surrounding axons in both the central nervous systems and peripheral nervous system. The myelin sheath is an electrical insulator and allows faster and more energetically efficient conduction of impulses. The sheath is formed by the cell membranes of glial cells (schwann cells in the peripheral and oligodendroglia in the central nervous system). Deterioration of the sheath in demyelinating diseases is a serious clinical problem.

name: myeloid progenitor cells
query: Query: myeloid progenitor cells [SEP] Myeloid progenitor cells is stem cells derived from hematopoietic stem cells. Derived from these myeloid progenitor cells are the megakaryocytes; erythroid cells; myeloid cells; and some [MASK].

name: myeloma proteins
query: Query: myeloma proteins [SEP] Myeloma proteins is abnormal immunoglobulins characteristic of multiple myeloma.

name: myocardial bridging
query: Query: myocardial bridging [SEP] Myocardial bridging is a malformation that is characterized by a muscle bridge over a segment of the coronary arteries. Systolic contractions of the muscle bridge can lead to narrowing of coronary artery; coronary compression; myocardial ischemia; myocardial infarction; and [MASK].

name: myocardial reperfusion
query: Query: myocardial reperfusion [SEP] Myocardial reperfusion is generally, restoration of blood supply to heart tissue which is ischemic due to decrease in normal blood supply. The decrease may result from any source including atherosclerotic obstruction, narrowing of the artery, or surgical clamping. Reperfusion can be induced to treat ischemia. Methods include chemical dissolution of an occluding thrombus, administration of vasodilator drugs, angioplasty, catheterization, and artery bypass [MASK] surgery. However, it is thought that reperfusion can itself further damage the ischemic tissue, causing myocardial reperfusion injury.

name: myocardial reperfusion injury
query: Query: myocardial reperfusion injury [SEP] Myocardial reperfusion injury is damage to the myocardium resulting from myocardial reperfusion (restoration of blood flow to ischemic areas of the heart.) Reperfusion takes place when there is spontaneous thrombolysis, thrombolytic therapy, collateral flow from other coronary vascular beds, or reversal of vasospasm.

name: myocytes , smooth muscle
query: Query: myocytes , smooth muscle [SEP] Smooth muscle myocytes is non-striated, elongated, spindle-shaped cells found lining the digestive tract, uterus, and blood vessels. They are derived from specialized myoblasts (myoblasts, smooth muscle).

name: nad
query: Query: nad [SEP] Nad is a coenzyme composed of ribosylnicotinamide 5'-diphosphate coupled to adenosine 5'-phosphate by pyrophosphate linkage. It is found widely in nature and is involved in numerous enzymatic reactions in which it serves as an [MASK] carrier by being alternately oxidized (nad+) and reduced (nadh). (Dorland, 27th ed)

name: nadh dehydrogenase
query: Query: nadh dehydrogenase [SEP] Nadh dehydrogenase is a flavoprotein and iron sulfur-containing oxidoreductase that catalyzes the oxidation of nadh to nad. In eukaryotes the enzyme can be found as a component of mitochondrial [MASK] transport complex i. Under experimental conditions the enzyme can use cytochrome c group as the reducing cofactor. The enzyme was formerly listed as ec 1.6.2.1.

name: nanotubes , carbon
query: Query: nanotubes , carbon [SEP] Carbon nanotubes is nanometer-sized tubes composed mainly of carbon. Such nanotubes are used as probes for high-resolution structural and chemical imaging of biomolecules with [MASK].

name: nanotubes , peptide
query: Query: nanotubes , peptide [SEP] Peptide nanotubes is nanotubes formed from cyclic peptides (peptides, cyclic). Alternating d and l linkages create planar rings that self assemble by stacking into nanotubes. They can form pores through cell membrane causing damage to cells.

name: nanowires
query: Query: nanowires [SEP] Nanowires is nanometer-scale wires made of materials that conduct electricity. They can be coated with molecules such as antibodies that will bind to proteins and other substances.

name: narrative medicine
query: Query: narrative medicine [SEP] Narrative medicine is narration as a tool to collect and interpret information on a patient's experience of illness

name: narrative therapy
query: Query: narrative therapy [SEP] Narrative therapy is a form of psychotherapy that centers on the individuals as the experts in their own lives and views problems as separate from people. It is assumed that people have many skills, competencies, beliefs, values, commitments, and abilities that will assist them to reduce the influence of problems in their lives.

name: narrow band imaging
query: Query: narrow band imaging [SEP] Narrow band imaging is imaging techniques that use [MASK] created with several optical interference filters by which the frequency ranges are spectrally narrowed and light scatter is greatly reduced. Thus the reflected [MASK] reconstituting the images are from distinct depths (the surface and deeper layers) of the object being imaged.

name: nasal absorption
query: Query: nasal absorption [SEP] Nasal absorption is uptake of substances through the nasal mucosa.

name: nasal cavity
query: Query: nasal cavity [SEP] Nasal cavity is the proximal portion of the respiratory passages on either side of the [MASK]. Nasal cavities, extending from the nares to the nasopharynx, are lined with ciliated nasal mucosa.

name: nasal septal perforation
query: Query: nasal septal perforation [SEP] Nasal septal perforation is an opening or hole in the [MASK] that is caused by trauma, injury, drug use, or pathological process.

name: national health insurance , united states
query: Query: national health insurance , united states [SEP] United states national health insurance is federal system administering national health insurance in the United States.

name: national longitudinal study of adolescent health
query: Query: national longitudinal study of adolescent health [SEP] National longitudinal study of [MASK] is longitudinal study of a nationally representative sample of adolescents in grades 7-12 in the United States during the 1994-95 school year. The Add Health cohort has been followed into young adulthood. (from http://www.cpc.unc.edu/projects/addhealth accessed 08/2012)

name: natural cytotoxicity triggering receptor 3
query: Query: natural cytotoxicity triggering receptor 3 [SEP] Natural cytotoxicity triggering receptor 3 is a 30 kDa stimulatory receptor found on resting and activated natural killer cells.

name: natural family planning methods
query: Query: natural family planning methods [SEP] Natural family planning methods is a class of natural contraceptive methods in which [MASK] is practiced a few days before and after the estimated day of ovulation, during the fertile phase. Methods for determining the [MASK] or ovulation detection are based on various physiological indicators, such as circulating hormones, changes in [MASK] ([MASK]), and the basal body temperature.

name: natural gas
query: Query: natural gas [SEP] Natural gas is a combustible, gaseous mixture of low-molecular weight [MASK] hydrocarbons, generated below the surface of the earth. It contains mostly methane and ethane with small amounts of propane; butanes; and higher hydrocarbons, and sometimes nitrogen; carbon dioxide; [MASK]; and [MASK]. (from McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

name: natural history
query: Query: natural history [SEP] Natural history is a former branch of knowledge embracing the study, description, and classification of natural objects (as animals, plants, and minerals) and thus including the modern sciences of zoology, botany, and mineralogy insofar as they existed at that time. In the 17th, 18th, and 19th centuries it was much used for the generalized pursuit of certain areas of science. (Webster, 3d ed; from Dr. James h. Cassedy, nlm [MASK] Division)

name: near miss , healthcare
query: Query: near miss , healthcare [SEP] Healthcare near miss is event that presented a risk but did not result in a patient harm.

name: neck dissection
query: Query: neck dissection [SEP] [MASK] [MASK] is [MASK] in the [MASK] to remove all disease tissues including cervical [MASK] nodes and to leave an adequate margin of normal tissue. This type of surgery is usually used in tumors or cervical metastases in the head and [MASK]. The prototype of [MASK] [MASK] is the radical [MASK] [MASK] described by Crile in 1906.

name: neck injuries
query: Query: neck injuries [SEP] [MASK] injuries is general or unspecified injuries to the [MASK]. It includes injuries to the skin, muscles, and other soft tissues of the [MASK].

name: neck muscles
query: Query: neck muscles [SEP] [MASK] muscles is the [MASK] muscles consist of the platysma, splenius cervicis, sternocleidomastoid(eus), longus colli, the anterior, medius, and posterior scalenes, digastric(us), stylohyoid(eus), mylohyoid(eus), geniohyoid(eus), sternohyoid(eus), omohyoid(eus), sternothyroid(eus), and thyrohyoid(eus).

name: neck pain
query: Query: neck pain [SEP] [MASK] pain is discomfort or more intense forms of pain that are localized to the cervical region. This term generally refers to pain in the posterior or lateral regions of the [MASK].

name: needles
query: Query: needles [SEP] Needles is sharp instruments used for puncturing or suturing.

name: needle sharing
query: Query: needle sharing [SEP] Needle sharing is usage of a single needle among two or more people for injecting drugs. Needle sharing is a high-risk behavior for contracting infectious disease.

name: needs assessment
query: Query: needs assessment [SEP] Needs assessment is systematic identification of a population's needs or the assessment of individuals to determine the proper level of services needed.

name: negative results
query: Query: negative results [SEP] Negative results is subject matter related to research studies in which the data do not demonstrate any clear evidence of effect, especially if an effect was expected.

name: neglected diseases
query: Query: neglected diseases [SEP] Neglected diseases is diseases that are underfunded and have low name recognition but are major burdens in less [MASK]. The [MASK] Organization has designated six tropical infectious diseases as being neglected in [MASK] that are endemic in many developing countries (helminthiasis; leprosy; lymphatic filariasis; onchocerciasis; schistosomiasis; and trachoma).

name: neoadjuvant therapy
query: Query: neoadjuvant therapy [SEP] Neoadjuvant therapy is preliminary cancer therapy (chemotherapy, radiation therapy, hormone/endocrine therapy, immunotherapy, hyperthermia, etc.) that precedes a necessary second modality of treatment.

name: neonatal abstinence syndrome
query: Query: neonatal abstinence syndrome [SEP] Neonatal abstinence syndrome is fetal and neonatal addiction and withdrawal as a result of the mother's dependence on drugs during pregnancy. Withdrawal or abstinence symptoms develop shortly after birth. Symptoms exhibited are loud, high-pitched crying, sweating, yawning and gastrointestinal disturbances.

name: neonatal brachial plexus palsy
query: Query: neonatal brachial plexus palsy [SEP] Neonatal brachial plexus palsy is perinatal nerve injury involving the brachial plexus involving a weak or paralyzed upper extremity.

name: neonatal screening
query: Query: neonatal screening [SEP] Neonatal screening is the identification of selected parameters in newborn infants by various tests, examinations, or other procedures. Screening may be performed by clinical or laboratory measures. a screening test is designed to sort out healthy neonates (infant, newborn) from those not well, but the screening test is not intended as a diagnostic device, rather instead as epidemiologic.

name: neoplasm , residual
query: Query: neoplasm , residual [SEP] Residual neoplasm is remnant of a tumor or cancer after primary, potentially curative therapy.

name: neoplasm grading
query: Query: neoplasm grading [SEP] Neoplasm grading is methods which attempt to express in replicable terms the level of cell differentiation in neoplasms as increasing anaplasia correlates with the aggressiveness of the neoplasm.

name: neoplasm recurrence , local
query: Query: neoplasm recurrence , local [SEP] Local neoplasm recurrence is the local recurrence of a neoplasm following treatment. It arises from microscopic cells of the original neoplasm that have escaped therapeutic intervention and later become clinically visible at the original site.

name: neoplasm regression , spontaneous
