query: Query: neoplasm regression , spontaneous [SEP] Spontaneous neoplasm regression is disappearance of a neoplasm or neoplastic state without the intervention of therapy.

name: neoplasms , adipose tissue
query: Query: neoplasms , adipose tissue [SEP] Adipose tissue neoplasms is neoplasms composed of fatty tissue or connective tissue made up of fat cells in a meshwork of areolar tissue. The concept does not refer to neoplasms located in adipose tissue.

name: neoplasms , second primary
query: Query: neoplasms , second primary [SEP] Second primary neoplasms is abnormal growths of tissue that follow a previous neoplasm but are not metastases of the latter. The second neoplasm may have the same or different histological type and can occur in the same or different organs as the previous neoplasm but in all cases arises from an independent oncogenic event. The development of the second neoplasm may or may not be related to the treatment for the previous neoplasm since genetic risk or predisposing factors may actually be the cause.

name: neoplasms , unknown primary
query: Query: neoplasms , unknown primary [SEP] Unknown primary neoplasms is metastases in which the tissue of origin is unknown.

name: neoplasms , vascular tissue
query: Query: neoplasms , vascular tissue [SEP] Vascular tissue neoplasms is neoplasms composed of vascular tissue. This concept does not refer to neoplasms located in blood vessels.

name: neoplasm seeding
query: Query: neoplasm seeding [SEP] Neoplasm seeding is the local implantation of tumor cells by contamination of instruments and surgical equipment during and after surgical resection, resulting in local growth of the cells and tumor formation.

name: neoplastic cells , circulating
query: Query: neoplastic cells , circulating [SEP] Circulating neoplastic cells is exfoliate neoplastic cells circulating in the blood and associated with metastasizing tumors.

name: neoplastic process
query: Query: neoplastic process [SEP] Neoplastic process is the accumulation of somatic mutations in certain genes that thus give rise to tumor cells.

name: neoplastic stem cells
query: Query: neoplastic stem cells [SEP] Neoplastic stem cells is highly proliferative, self-renewing, and colony-forming stem cells which give rise to neoplasms.

name: nerve agents
query: Query: nerve agents [SEP] Nerve agents is a class of compounds that adversely affect the transmission of impulses through the nervous system.

name: nerve expansion
query: Query: nerve expansion [SEP] Nerve expansion is procedures that stimulate nerve elongation over a period of time. They are used in repairing nerve tissue.

name: nerve growth factor
query: Query: nerve growth factor [SEP] Nerve growth factor is nerve growth factor is the first of a series of neurotrophic factors that were found to influence the growth and differentiation of sympathetic and sensory neurons. It is comprised of alpha, beta, and gamma subunits. The beta subunit is responsible for its growth stimulating activity.

name: nerve sheath neoplasms
query: Query: nerve sheath neoplasms [SEP] Nerve sheath neoplasms is neoplasms which arise from nerve sheaths formed by schwann cells in the peripheral nervous system or by oligodendrocytes in the central nervous system. Malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors, neurofibroma, and neurilemmoma are relatively common tumors in this category.

name: neural cell adhesion molecules
query: Query: neural cell adhesion molecules [SEP] Neural cell adhesion molecules is cell adhesion molecule involved in a diverse range of contact-mediated interactions among neurons, astrocytes, oligodendrocytes, and myotubes. It is widely but transiently expressed in many tissues early in embryogenesis. Four main isoforms exist, including cd56; (cd56 antigen); but there are many other variants resulting from [MASK] and post-translational modifications. (From Pigott & Power, The Adhesion Molecule FactsBook, 1993, pp115-119)

name: neural crest
query: Query: neural crest [SEP] Neural crest is the two longitudinal ridges along the primitive streak appearing near the end of gastrulation during development of nervous system (neurulation). The ridges are formed by folding of neural plate. Between the ridges is a neural groove which deepens as the fold become elevated. When the folds meet at midline, the groove becomes a closed tube, the neural tube.

name: neural plate
query: Query: neural plate [SEP] Neural plate is the region in the dorsal ectoderm of a chordate embryo that gives rise to the future central nervous system. Tissue in the neural plate is called the neuroectoderm, often used as a synonym of neural plate.

name: neural stem cells
query: Query: neural stem cells [SEP] Neural stem cells is self-renewing cells that generate the main phenotypes of the nervous system in both the embryo and adult. Neural stem cells are precursors to both neurons and neuroglia.

name: neural tube
query: Query: neural tube [SEP] Neural tube is a tube of ectodermal tissue in an embryo that will give rise to the central nervous system, including the spinal cord and the brain. Lumen within the neural tube is called neural canal which gives rise to the central canal of the spinal cord and the ventricles of the brain. For malformation of the neural tube, see [MASK].

name: neuroendocrine cells
query: Query: neuroendocrine cells [SEP] Neuroendocrine cells is specialized neurons that produce hormones, such as neuropeptides or biogenic amines. They generally are in the nervous system, such as hypothalamus, but can be found in other organs or systems. These neurons contain dense neurosecretory granules and proprotein convertases allowing the rapidly release of neurohormones into the blood circulation upon stimulation.

name: neurology
query: Query: neurology [SEP] Neurology is a medical specialty concerned with the study of the structures, functions, and diseases of the nervous system.

name: neuromuscular blockade
query: Query: neuromuscular blockade [SEP] Neuromuscular blockade is the intentional interruption of transmission at the neuromuscular junction by external agents, usually [MASK]. It is distinguished from nerve block in which [MASK] ([MASK]) is interrupted rather than neuromuscular transmission. Neuromuscular blockade is commonly used to produce muscle relaxation as an adjunct to anesthesia during surgery and other medical procedures. It is also often used as an experimental manipulation in basic research. It is not strictly speaking anesthesia but is grouped here with anesthetic techniques. The failure of neuromuscular transmission as a result of pathological processes is not included here.

name: neuromuscular junction diseases
query: Query: neuromuscular junction diseases [SEP] Neuromuscular junction diseases is conditions characterized by impaired transmission of impulses at the neuromuscular junction. This may result from disorders that affect receptor function, pre- or postsynaptic membrane function, or acetylcholinesterase activity. The majority of diseases in this category are associated with autoimmune, toxic, or inherited conditions.

name: neuromuscular monitoring
query: Query: neuromuscular monitoring [SEP] Neuromuscular monitoring is the use of peripheral nerve stimulation to assess transmission at the neuromuscular junction, especially in the response to anesthetics, such as the intensity of neuromuscular blockade by [MASK].

name: neuronal plasticity
query: Query: neuronal plasticity [SEP] Neuronal plasticity is the capacity of the nervous system to change its reactivity as the result of successive activations.

name: neuroprotective agents
query: Query: neuroprotective agents [SEP] Neuroprotective agents is drugs intended to prevent damage to the brain or spinal cord from ischemia, stroke, convulsions, or trauma. Some must be administered before the event, but others may be effective for some time after. They act by a variety of mechanisms, but often directly or indirectly minimize the damage produced by endogenous [MASK].

name: neuroscience nursing
query: Query: neuroscience nursing [SEP] Neuroscience nursing is the nursing specialty focusing on the needs of patients with dysfunction of the nervous system.

name: neutrophil activation
query: Query: neutrophil activation [SEP] Neutrophil activation is the process in which the neutrophil is stimulated by diverse substances, resulting in degranulation and/or generation of reactive oxygen products, and culminating in the destruction of invading pathogens. The stimulatory substances, including opsonized particles, immune complexes, and chemotactic factors, bind to specific cell-surface receptors on the neutrophil.

name: neutrophil infiltration
query: Query: neutrophil infiltration [SEP] Neutrophil infiltration is the diffusion or accumulation of neutrophils in tissues or cells in response to a wide variety of substances released at the sites of inflammatory reactions.

name: news
query: Query: news [SEP] News is works consisting of an announcement or statement of recent or current events of new data and matters of interest in the field of medicine or science. In some publications, such as "Nature" or "Science," the news reports are substantively written and herald medical and scientific data of vital or controversial importance.

name: new south wales
query: Query: new south wales [SEP] New south wales is a state in southeastern Australia. Its capital is Sydney. It was discovered by Captain Cook in 1770 and first settled at Botany Bay by marines and convicts in 1788. It was named by Captain Cook who thought its coastline resembled that of South Wales. (From Webster's New Geographical Dictionary, 1988, p840 & Room, Brewer's Dictionary of Names, 1992, p377)

name: new york city
query: Query: new york city [SEP] New york city is city located at the mouth of the Hudson [MASK], in New York State.

name: nickel
query: Query: nickel [SEP] Nickel is a trace element with the atomic symbol Ni, atomic number 28, and atomic weight 58.69. It is a cofactor of the enzyme urease.

name: nigeria
query: Query: nigeria [SEP] Nigeria is a republic in western Africa, south of [MASK] between benin and cameroon. Its capital is Abuja.

name: nitric acid
query: Query: nitric acid [SEP] Nitric acid is nitric acid (hno3). a colorless liquid that is used in the manufacture of inorganic and organic nitrates and nitro compounds for fertilizers, dye intermediates, explosives, and many different organic chemicals. Continued exposure to vapor may cause chronic bronchitis; chemical pneumonitis may occur. (From Merck Index, 11th ed)

name: nitric oxide donors
query: Query: nitric oxide donors [SEP] [MASK] donors is a diverse group of agents, with unique chemical structures and biochemical requirements, which generate [MASK]. These compounds have been used in the treatment of cardiovascular diseases and the management of acute myocardial infarction, acute and chronic congestive heart failure, and surgical control of blood pressure. (Adv Pharmacol 1995;34:361-81)

name: nitric oxide synthase type i
query: Query: nitric oxide synthase type i [SEP] [MASK] synthase type i is a CALCIUM-dependent, constitutively-expressed form of [MASK] synthase found primarily in nerve tissue.

name: nitric oxide synthase type ii
query: Query: nitric oxide synthase type ii [SEP] [MASK] synthase type ii is a CALCIUM-independent subtype of [MASK] synthase that may play a role in immune function. It is an inducible enzyme whose expression is transcriptionally regulated by a variety of cytokines.

name: nitric oxide synthase type iii
query: Query: nitric oxide synthase type iii [SEP] [MASK] synthase type iii is a CALCIUM-dependent, constitutively-expressed form of [MASK] synthase found primarily in endothelial cells.

name: nitro compounds
query: Query: nitro compounds [SEP] Nitro compounds is compounds having the nitro group, -no2, attached to carbon. When attached to nitrogen they are nitramines and attached to oxygen they are nitrates.

name: nitrogen dioxide
query: Query: nitrogen dioxide [SEP] Nitrogen dioxide is nitrogen oxide (no2). a highly poisonous gas. Exposure produces inflammation of lungs that may only cause slight pain or pass unnoticed, but resulting edema several days later may cause death. (From Merck, 11th ed) It is a major atmospheric pollutant that is able to absorb uv light that does not reach the earth's surface.

name: nitrogen fixation
query: Query: nitrogen fixation [SEP] Nitrogen fixation is the process in certain bacteria; fungi; and cyanobacteria converting free atmospheric nitrogen to biologically usable forms of nitrogen, such as [MASK]; nitrates; and amino compounds.

name: nitrogen isotopes
query: Query: nitrogen isotopes [SEP] Nitrogen isotopes is stable nitrogen atoms that have the same atomic number as the element nitrogen, but differ in atomic weight. n-15 is a stable nitrogen isotope.

name: noise , occupational
query: Query: noise , occupational [SEP] Occupational noise is noise present in occupational, industrial, and factory situations.

name: noise , transportation
query: Query: noise , transportation [SEP] Transportation noise is noise associated with transportation, particularly aircraft and automobiles.

name: norepinephrine
query: Query: norepinephrine [SEP] Norepinephrine is precursor of epinephrine that is secreted by the adrenal medulla and is a widespread central and autonomic neurotransmitter. Norepinephrine is the principal transmitter of most postganglionic sympathetic fibers, and of the diffuse [MASK] system in the brain that arises from the locus ceruleus. It is also found in plants and is used pharmacologically as a sympathomimetic.

name: norepinephrine plasma membrane transport proteins
query: Query: norepinephrine plasma membrane transport proteins [SEP] Norepinephrine plasma membrane transport proteins is sodium chloride-dependent neurotransmitter symporters located primarily on the plasma membrane of noradrenergic neurons. They remove norepinephrine from the extracellular space by high affinity reuptake into presynaptic terminals. The norepinephrine transporter regulates signal amplitude and duration at noradrenergic synapses and is the target of adrenergic uptake inhibitors.

name: northwest territories
query: Query: northwest territories [SEP] Northwest territories is a federally administered division of Canada. Its capital is Yellowknife. The former northern and eastern-most parts of the Territory comprise the new territory of Nunavut, effective April 1, 1999.

name: nose neoplasms
query: Query: nose neoplasms [SEP] Nose neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the nose.

name: nuclear export signals
query: Query: nuclear export signals [SEP] Nuclear export signals is specific amino acid sequences present in the primary amino acid sequence of proteins which mediate their export from the cell nucleus. They are rich in hydrophobic residues, such as [MASK] and isoleucine.

name: nuclear factor 45 protein
query: Query: nuclear factor 45 protein [SEP] Nuclear factor 45 protein is a protein subunit that takes part in forming nuclear factor 90 protein complexes.

name: nuclear fusion
query: Query: nuclear fusion [SEP] Nuclear fusion is thermonuclear reaction in which the nuclei of an element of low atomic weight unite under extremely high temperature and pressure to form a nucleus of a heavier atom.

name: nuclear lamina
query: Query: nuclear lamina [SEP] Nuclear lamina is a lattice of fibrils which covers the entire inner surface of the nuclear envelope and interlinks nuclear pores (nuclear pore).

name: nuclear medicine
query: Query: nuclear medicine [SEP] Nuclear medicine is a specialty field of radiology concerned with diagnostic, therapeutic, and investigative use of radioactive compounds.

name: nuclear microscopy
query: Query: nuclear microscopy [SEP] Nuclear microscopy is a method of simultaneously imaging and measuring elements at the submicron level. Nuclear microscopy uses a focused high-energy ion beam of protons and [MASK] (a nuclear microprobe) to interact with the sample. The resulting emitted radiations are analyzed by a group of techniques simultaneously: particle induced x ray emission spectrometry for minor and trace element identification; Rutherford Backscattering Spectroscopy to assess sample thickness and bulk elements such as carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, and nitrogen; and Scanning Transmission Ion Microscopy to assess sample structure and density.

name: nuclear pore
query: Query: nuclear pore [SEP] Nuclear pore is an opening through the nuclear envelope formed by the nuclear pore complex which transports nuclear proteins or rna into or out of the cell nucleus and which, under some conditions, acts as an ion channel.

name: nuclear power plants
query: Query: nuclear power plants [SEP] Nuclear power plants is facilities that convert nuclear energy into electrical energy.

name: nuclear receptor subfamily 1 , group f , member 1
query: Query: nuclear receptor subfamily 1 , group f , member 1 [SEP] Member 1 group f nuclear receptor subfamily 1 is a DNA-binding orphan nuclear receptor that positively regulates expression of arntl transcription factors and is a regulatory component of the circadian clock system. The protein also has a role in neuron cell survival and differentiation in that loss of function mutations of its gene result in the mouse phenotype referred to as the staggerer mouse.

name: nuclear receptor subfamily 1 , group f , member 2
query: Query: nuclear receptor subfamily 1 , group f , member 2 [SEP] Member 2 group f nuclear receptor subfamily 1 is an orphan nuclear receptor that is expressed at high levels in neuronal tissues, the retina; epididymis; and vas deferens. The receptor is believed to play a role in regulating a variety of functions including the processing of sensory information, the differentiation of photoreceptor cells and the circadian rhythm.

name: nuclear transfer techniques
query: Query: nuclear transfer techniques [SEP] Nuclear transfer techniques is methods of implanting a cell nucleus from a donor cell into an enucleated acceptor cell.

name: nuclear weapons
query: Query: nuclear weapons [SEP] Nuclear weapons is a weapon that derives its destructive force from [MASK] and/or fusion.

name: nucleic acid denaturation
query: Query: nucleic acid denaturation [SEP] Nucleic acid denaturation is disruption of the secondary structure of nucleic acids by heat, extreme pH or chemical treatment. Double strand dna is "melted" by dissociation of the non-covalent hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions. Denatured dna appears to be a single-stranded flexible structure. The effects of denaturation on rna are similar though less pronounced and largely reversible.

name: nucleotide mapping
query: Query: nucleotide mapping [SEP] Nucleotide mapping is two-dimensional separation and analysis of nucleotides.

name: nucleotide motifs
query: Query: nucleotide motifs [SEP] Nucleotide motifs is commonly observed base sequence or nucleotide structural components which can be represented by a [MASK] sequence or a sequence logo.

name: nucleotide sequence

name: nurses , international

name: nurses , male
query: Query: nurses , male [SEP] Male nurses is nurses of the male [MASK].

name: nurses , neonatal
query: Query: nurses , neonatal [SEP] Neonatal nurses is qualified nursing professionals specializing in care of newborn infants.

name: nurses , public health

name: nurses instruction
query: Query: nurses instruction [SEP] Nurses instruction is work consisting of materials developed for a nursing audience.

name: nursing , private duty
query: Query: nursing , private duty [SEP] Private duty nursing is the practice of nursing by a registered or licensed nurse to care for a specific patient in a health facility or in the home.

name: nursing , team
query: Query: nursing , team [SEP] Team nursing is coordination of nursing services by various nursing care personnel under the [MASK] of a professional nurse. The team may consist of a professional nurse, nurses' aides, and the practical nurse.

name: nursing administration research
query: Query: nursing administration research [SEP] Nursing administration research is research concerned with establishing costs of nursing care, examining the relationships between nursing services and quality patient care, and viewing problems of nursing service delivery within the broader context of policy analysis and delivery of health services (from a national study, presented at the 1985 Council on Graduate Education for Administration in Nursing (cgean) meeting).

name: nursing audit
query: Query: nursing audit [SEP] Nursing audit is a detailed review and evaluation of selected clinical records by qualified professional personnel for evaluating quality of nursing care.

name: nursing diagnosis
query: Query: nursing diagnosis [SEP] Nursing diagnosis is conclusions derived from the nursing assessment that establish a health status profile for the patient and from which nursing interventions may be ordered.

name: nursing faculty practice
query: Query: nursing faculty practice [SEP] Nursing faculty practice is clinical practice by members of the nursing faculty in order to maintain a balance in their nursing activities--clinical, education, and research.

name: nursing methodology research
query: Query: nursing methodology research [SEP] Nursing methodology research is research carried out by nurses concerning techniques and methods to implement projects and to document information, including methods of interviewing patients, collecting data, and forming inferences. The concept includes exploration of methodological issues such as human subjectivity and human experience.

name: nursing records
query: Query: nursing records [SEP] Nursing records is data recorded by nurses concerning the nursing care given to the patient, including judgment of the patient's progress.

name: nursing service , hospital
query: Query: nursing service , hospital [SEP] Hospital nursing service is the hospital department which is responsible for the organization and administration of nursing activities.

name: nursing stations
query: Query: nursing stations [SEP] Nursing stations is an area in a clinic, unit, or ward in a health care facility that serves as the administrative center for nursing care. (from Mosby's Medical Dictionary, 8th ed)

name: nursing theory
query: Query: nursing theory [SEP] Nursing theory is concepts, definitions, and propositions applied to the study of various phenomena which pertain to nursing and nursing research.

name: nut proteins
query: Query: nut proteins [SEP] Nut proteins is proteins from nuts.

name: nutrients
query: Query: nutrients [SEP] Nutrients is various components of food that are required for nourishment.

name: nutrition assessment
query: Query: nutrition assessment [SEP] Nutrition assessment is evaluation and measurement of nutritional variables in order to assess the level of nutrition or the [MASK] of the individual. nutrition surveys may be used in making the assessment.

name: nutrition policy
query: Query: nutrition policy [SEP] Nutrition policy is guidelines and objectives pertaining to food supply and nutrition including recommendations for healthy diet.

name: obesity , morbid
query: Query: obesity , morbid [SEP] Morbid obesity is the condition of weighing two, three, or more times the ideal weight, so called because it is associated with many serious and life-threatening disorders. In the body mass index, morbid obesity is defined as having a bmi greater than 40.0 kg/m2.

name: obesity management
query: Query: obesity management [SEP] Obesity management is an integrated professional approach to screening, evaluation, control, and reduction of abnormal weight gain.

name: observational studies , veterinary as topic
query: Query: observational studies , veterinary as topic [SEP] Veterinary as topic observational studies is works about clinical studies in which animal subjects may receive diagnostic, therapeutic, or other types of interventions and where the investigator does not assign subjects  to specific interventions.

name: observational study
query: Query: observational study [SEP] Observational study is a work that reports on the results of a clinical study in which participants may receive diagnostic, therapeutic, or other types of interventions, but the investigator does not assign participants to specific interventions (as in an interventional study).

name: observer variation
query: Query: observer variation [SEP] Observer variation is the failure by the observer to measure or identify a phenomenon accurately, which results in an error. Sources for this may be due to the observer's missing an abnormality, or to faulty technique resulting in incorrect test measurement, or to misinterpretation of the data. Two varieties are inter-observer variation (the amount observers vary from one another when reporting on the same material) and intra-observer variation (the amount one observer varies between observations when reporting more than once on the same material).

name: obstetric nursing
query: Query: obstetric nursing [SEP] Obstetric nursing is a nursing specialty involving nursing care given to the pregnant patient before, after, or during childbirth.

name: occipital bone
query: Query: occipital bone [SEP] Occipital bone is part of the back and base of the cranium that encloses the foramen magnum.

name: occlusion body matrix proteins
query: Query: occlusion body matrix proteins [SEP] Occlusion body matrix proteins is proteins that assemble into a crystalline polyhedral or ovicylindrical shape around [MASK], including baculoviridae and cypovirus.

name: occupational health nursing
query: Query: occupational health nursing [SEP] [MASK] nursing is the practice of nursing in the work environment.

name: occupational health physicians
query: Query: occupational health physicians [SEP] [MASK] physicians is physicians employed in a company or corporate setting that is generally not in the health care industry.

name: occupational health services
query: Query: occupational health services [SEP] [MASK] services is health services for employees, usually provided by the employer at the place of work.

name: occupational injuries
query: Query: occupational injuries [SEP] Occupational injuries is injuries sustained from incidents in the course of work-related activities.

name: occupational medicine
query: Query: occupational medicine [SEP] Occupational medicine is medical specialty concerned with the promotion and maintenance of the physical and mental health of employees in occupational settings.

name: occupational therapists
query: Query: occupational therapists [SEP] Occupational therapists is professionals trained to help individuals develop or regain skills needed to achieve independence in their lives.

name: occupational therapy department , hospital
query: Query: occupational therapy department , hospital [SEP] Hospital [MASK] department is hospital department responsible for the administration and provision of any occupational or work activity for remedial purposes.

name: oceanic ancestry group
query: Query: oceanic ancestry group [SEP] Oceanic ancestry group is individuals whose ancestral origins are in the islands of the central and South Pacific, including Micronesia, Melanesia, Polynesia, traditionally Australasia including [MASK]..

name: ocular absorption
query: Query: ocular absorption [SEP] Ocular absorption is uptake of substances by tissues of the eye.

name: ocular hypotension
query: Query: ocular hypotension [SEP] Ocular hypotension is abnormally low intraocular pressure often related to chronic inflammation (uveitis).

name: office visits
query: Query: office visits [SEP] Office visits is visits made by patients to health service providers' offices for diagnosis, treatment, and follow-up.

name: ohio
query: Query: ohio [SEP] Ohio is state bounded on the north by Michigan and [MASK] Erie, on the east by Ohio [MASK] and Pennsylvania, on the south by Ohio [MASK], and on the west by Indiana.

name: oil and gas fields
query: Query: oil and gas fields [SEP] Oil and gas fields is areas of the earth where hydrocarbon deposits of petroleum and/or natural gas are located.

name: old age assistance
query: Query: old age assistance [SEP] Old age assistance is financial assistance for the impoverished elderly through public funding of programs, services, and individual income supplements.

name: olfactory marker protein
query: Query: olfactory marker protein [SEP] Olfactory marker protein is a ubiquitous, cytoplasmic protein found in mature [MASK] of all vertebrates. It is a modulator of the olfactory signal transduction pathway.

name: olfactory nerve
query: Query: olfactory nerve [SEP] Olfactory nerve is the 1st cranial nerve. The olfactory nerve conveys the sense of smell. It is formed by the axons of [MASK] which project from the olfactory epithelium (in the nasal epithelium) to the olfactory bulb.

name: olfactory nerve injuries
query: Query: olfactory nerve injuries [SEP] Olfactory nerve injuries is traumatic injuries to the olfactory nerve. It may result in various olfactory dysfunction including a complete loss of smell.

name: olfactory pathways
query: Query: olfactory pathways [SEP] Olfactory pathways is [MASK] of nerve fibers conducting impulses from olfactory receptors to the cerebral cortex. It includes the olfactory nerve; olfactory bulb; olfactory tract; olfactory tubercle; anterior perforated substance; and olfactory cortex.

name: olfactory perception
query: Query: olfactory perception [SEP] Olfactory perception is the process by which the nature and meaning of olfactory stimuli, such as odors, are recognized and interpreted by the brain.

name: oligonucleotide array sequence analysis
query: Query: oligonucleotide array sequence analysis [SEP] Oligonucleotide array sequence analysis is hybridization of a nucleic acid sample to a very large [MASK] of [MASK], which have been attached individually in columns and rows to a solid support, to determine a base sequence, or to detect variations in a gene sequence, gene expression, or for gene mapping.

name: oncogene fusion
query: Query: oncogene fusion [SEP] Oncogene fusion is the genetic recombination of the parts of two or more genes, including an oncogene as at least one of the fusion partners. Such gene fusions are often detected in neoplastic cells and are transcribed into [MASK].

name: oncology nursing
query: Query: oncology nursing [SEP] Oncology nursing is a nursing specialty concerned with the care provided to cancer patients. It includes aspects of family functioning through education of both patient and family.

name: online social networking
query: Query: online social networking [SEP] Online social networking is connectivity facilitated by computer-based communications among persons with family, work, or other common interests.

name: only child
query: Query: only child [SEP] Only child is child who has no siblings.

name: ontario
query: Query: ontario [SEP] Ontario is a province of Canada lying between the provinces of Manitoba and Quebec. Its capital is Toronto. It takes its name from [MASK] Ontario which is said to represent the Iroquois oniatariio, beautiful [MASK]. (From Webster's New Geographical Dictionary, 1988, p892 & Room, Brewer's Dictionary of Names, 1992, p391)

name: oocyte donation
query: Query: oocyte donation [SEP] Oocyte donation is transfer of preovulatory oocytes from donor to a suitable host. Oocytes are collected, fertilized in vitro, and transferred to a host that can be human or animal.

name: oocyte retrieval
query: Query: oocyte retrieval [SEP] Oocyte retrieval is procedures to obtain viable oocytes from the host. Oocytes most often are collected by needle aspiration from ovarian follicles before ovulation.

name: open abdomen techniques
query: Query: open abdomen techniques [SEP] Open abdomen techniques is abdominal wound closure techniques in which the opening from a laparoscopic abdominal incision is left open, but covered, to reduce or prevent intra-abdominal hypertension.

name: open access publishing
query: Query: open access publishing [SEP] Open access publishing is agreement in which author(s) and [MASK] holder(s) grant(s) to all users a free, irrevocable, worldwide, perpetual right of access to, and a license to copy, use, distribute, transmit and display the work publicly and to make and distribute derivative works, in any digital medium for any responsible purpose, subject to proper attribution of authorship, as well as the right to make small numbers of printed copies for their personal use. a complete version of the work and all supplemental materials, including a copy of the permission as stated above, in a suitable standard electronic format is deposited immediately upon initial publication in at least one online repository that is supported by an academic institution, scholarly society, government agency, or other well-established organization that seeks to enable open access, unrestricted distribution, interoperability, and long-term archiving. (from Bethesda Statement on Open Access Publishing)

name: open fracture reduction
query: Query: open fracture reduction [SEP] [MASK] reduction is restoration of normal alignment of a fractured bone via an operative surgical procedure.

name: open reading frames
query: Query: open reading frames [SEP] Open reading frames is a sequence of successive nucleotide triplets that are read as codons specifying amino acids and begin with an initiator codon and end with a stop codon (codon, terminator).

name: operating room nursing
query: Query: operating room nursing [SEP] Operating room nursing is the functions of the professional nurse in the operating room.

name: operating rooms
query: Query: operating rooms [SEP] Operating rooms is facilities equipped for performing surgery.

name: operating tables
query: Query: operating tables [SEP] Operating [MASK] is a raised flat surface on which a patient is placed during surgical procedures.

name: operative blood salvage
query: Query: operative blood salvage [SEP] Operative blood salvage is recovery of blood lost from surgical procedures for reuse by the same patient in autologous blood transfusions. It is collected during (intraoperatively) or after completion of (postoperatively) the surgical procedures.

name: operative time
query: Query: operative time [SEP] Operative time is the duration of a surgical procedure in hours and minutes.

name: operator regions , genetic
query: Query: operator regions , genetic [SEP] Genetic operator regions is the regulatory elements of an operon to which activators or repressors bind thereby effecting the transcription of genes in the operon.

name: ophthalmic solutions
query: Query: ophthalmic solutions [SEP] Ophthalmic solutions is sterile solutions that are intended for instillation into the eye. It does not include solutions for cleaning eyeglasses or contact lens solutions.

name: optical fibers
query: Query: optical fibers [SEP] Optical fibers is thin strands of transparent material, usually glass, that are used for transmitting light waves over long distances.

name: optical restriction mapping
query: Query: optical restriction mapping [SEP] Optical restriction mapping is a technique to generate restriction maps from single large dna molecules by spreading the dna onto a glass surface, digesting with dna restriction enzymes, staining with fluorescent dyes, and visualizing the dna cleavage sites by fluorescence microscopy.

name: optical storage devices
query: Query: optical storage devices [SEP] Optical storage devices is a computer disk read by a laser beam, containing data prerecorded by a vendor. The buyer cannot enter or modify data in any way but the advantages lie in the speed of accessibility, relative immunity to damage, and relatively low cost of purchase.

name: optic atrophy
query: Query: optic atrophy [SEP] Optic atrophy is atrophy of the [MASK] which may be congenital or acquired. This condition indicates a deficiency in the number of nerve fibers which arise in the retina and converge to form the [MASK]; optic nerve; optic chiasm; and optic tracts. glaucoma; ischemia; inflammation, a chronic elevation of [MASK], toxins, optic nerve compression, and inherited conditions (see optic atrophies, hereditary) are relatively common causes of this condition.

name: optic atrophy , hereditary , leber
query: Query: optic atrophy , hereditary , leber [SEP] Leber hereditary optic atrophy is a maternally linked genetic disorder that presents in mid-life as acute or subacute central vision loss leading to central scotoma and blindness. The disease has been associated with missense mutations in the mtDNA, in genes for Complex i, iii, and iv polypeptides, that can act autonomously or in association with each other to cause the disease. (from Online Mendelian Inheritance in Man, http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/Omim/, mim#535000 (April 17, 2001))

name: optic nerve glioma
query: Query: optic nerve glioma [SEP] Optic nerve glioma is glial cell derived tumors arising from the optic nerve, usually presenting in childhood.

name: optic neuropathy , ischemic
query: Query: optic neuropathy , ischemic [SEP] Ischemic optic neuropathy is ischemic injury to the optic nerve which usually affects the [MASK] (optic neuropathy, anterior ischemic) and less frequently the retrobulbar portion of the nerve (optic neuropathy, posterior ischemic). The disease primarily occurs in the sixth decade or later and presents with the sudden onset of painless and usually severe monocular visual loss. Anterior ischemic optic neuropathy also features [MASK] edema with microhemorrhages. The [MASK] appears normal in posterior ischemic optic neuropathy. (Glaser, Neuro-Ophthalmology, 2nd ed, p135)

name: oral hygiene index
query: Query: oral hygiene index [SEP] Oral hygiene index is a combination of the debris index and the dental calculus index to determine the status of oral hygiene.

It is the result of a variety of causes, e.g., denture irritation, aphthous stomatitis (stomatitis, aphthous); noma; necrotizing gingivitis (gingivitis, necrotizing ulcerative); toothbrushing; and various irritants. (From Jablonski, Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992, p842)

name: oregon

name: origin of life

name: ovarian reserve

name: overall

query: Query: ovulation induction [SEP] Ovulation induction is techniques for the artifical induction of ovulation, the rupture of the follicle and release of the ovum.

name: ovulation prediction
query: Query: ovulation prediction [SEP] Ovulation prediction is predicting the time of ovulation can be achieved by measuring the preovulatory elevation of estradiol; luteinizing hormone or other hormones in blood or urine. (From Dorland, 27th ed & Stedman, 25th ed)

query: Query: oxygen isotopes [SEP] Oxygen isotopes is stable oxygen atoms that have the same atomic number as the element oxygen, but differ in atomic weight. o-17 and 18 are stable oxygen isotopes.

name: pain , intractable

name: pain management
query: Query: pain management [SEP] Pain management is a form of therapy that employs a coordinated and interdisciplinary approach for easing the suffering and improving the [MASK] of those experiencing pain.

name: pain perception
query: Query: pain perception [SEP] Pain perception is the process by which pain is recognized and interpreted by the brain.

name: pain threshold

name: pair bond
query: Query: pair bond [SEP] Pair bond is in animals, the social relationship established between a male and female for reproduction. It may include raising of young.

name: pakistan

name: palate , soft

name: palliative care
query: Query: palliative care [SEP] Palliative care is care alleviating symptoms without curing the underlying disease. (Stedman, 25th ed)

name: palliative medicine
query: Query: palliative medicine [SEP] Palliative medicine is a branch of medicine concerned with preventing and relieving the suffering of patients in any stage of disease. Its focus is on comprehensive care and improving the quality of all areas of the patient's life.

name: pan american health organization
query: Query: pan american health organization [SEP] Pan american health organization is who regional office for the Americas acting as a coordinating agency for the improvement of health conditions in the hemisphere. The four main functions are: control or eradication of communicable diseases, strengthening of national and local health services, education and training, and research.

name: pancreas , artificial
query: Query: pancreas , artificial [SEP] Artificial pancreas is devices for simulating the activity of the pancreas. They can be either electromechanical, consisting of a glucose sensor, computer, and insulin pump or bioartificial, consisting of isolated islets of Langerhans in an artificial membrane.

name: pancreas transplantation
query: Query: pancreas transplantation [SEP] Pancreas transplantation is the transference of a pancreas from one human or animal to another.

name: pancreatic ducts
query: Query: pancreatic ducts [SEP] Pancreatic ducts is ducts that collect pancreatic juice from the pancreas and supply it to the duodenum.

name: pancreatic extracts
query: Query: pancreatic extracts [SEP] Pancreatic extracts is extracts prepared from pancreatic tissue that may contain the pancreatic enzymes or other specific uncharacterized factors or proteins with specific activities. pancreatin is a specific extract containing digestive enzymes and used to treat pancreatic insufficiency.

name: pancreatic fistula
query: Query: pancreatic fistula [SEP] Pancreatic fistula is abnormal passage communicating with the pancreas.

name: pancreatic juice
query: Query: pancreatic juice [SEP] Pancreatic juice is the fluid containing digestive enzymes secreted by the pancreas in response to food in the duodenum.

name: pancreatic polypeptide
query: Query: pancreatic polypeptide [SEP] Pancreatic polypeptide is a 36-amino acid pancreatic hormone that is secreted mainly by endocrine cells found at the periphery of the islets of langerhans and adjacent to cells containing somatostatin and glucagon. name: pancreatitis , alcoholic
query: Query: pancreatitis , alcoholic [SEP] Alcoholic pancreatitis is acute or chronic inflammation of the pancreas due to excessive alcohol drinking. Alcoholic pancreatitis usually presents as an acute episode but it is a chronic progressive disease in alcoholics.

name: pancreatitis , graft
query: Query: pancreatitis , graft [SEP] [MASK] pancreatitis is an inflammatory disease and serious complication of pancreas transplantation. It is caused by a premature activation of pancreatic proenzymes leading to autodigestion of the gland and can be attributed to immunological or nonimmunological causes.

name: panic

name: panic disorder
query: Query: panic disorder [SEP] Panic disorder is a type of anxiety disorder characterized by unexpected panic attacks that last minutes or, rarely, hours. Panic attacks begin with intense apprehension, fear or terror and, often, a feeling of impending doom. Symptoms experienced during a panic attack include dyspnea or sensations of being smothered; dizziness, loss of balance or faintness; choking sensations; palpitations or accelerated heart rate; shakiness; sweating; nausea or other form of abdominal distress; depersonalization or derealization; paresthesias; hot flashes or chills; chest discomfort or pain; fear of dying and fear of not being in control of oneself or going crazy. Agoraphobia may also develop. Similar to other anxiety disorders, it may be inherited as an autosomal dominant trait.

name: papillary muscles
query: Query: papillary muscles [SEP] Papillary muscles is conical muscular projections from the walls of the cardiac ventricles, attached to the cusps of the atrioventricular valves by the chordae tendineae.

name: paraffin embedding
query: Query: paraffin embedding [SEP] [MASK] embedding is the infiltrating of tissue specimens with [MASK], as a supporting substance, to prepare for sectioning with a microtome.

name: paralysis , obstetric

name: parasites
query: Query: parasites [SEP] Parasites is invertebrate organisms that live on or in another organism (the host), and benefit at the expense of the other. Traditionally excluded from definition of parasites are pathogenic bacteria; fungi; viruses; and plants; though they may live parasitically.

name: parasitic diseases , animal
query: Query: parasitic diseases , animal [SEP] Animal parasitic diseases is animal diseases caused by parasites.

name: parasitic sensitivity tests
query: Query: parasitic sensitivity tests [SEP] Parasitic sensitivity tests is tests that demonstrate the relative effectiveness of chemotherapeutic agents against specific parasites.

name: parathyroid hormone
query: Query: parathyroid hormone [SEP] Parathyroid hormone is a polypeptide hormone (84 amino acid residues) secreted by the [MASK] which performs the essential role of maintaining intracellular calcium levels in the body. Parathyroid hormone increases intracellular calcium by promoting the release of calcium from bone, increases the intestinal absorption of calcium, increases the renal tubular reabsorption of calcium, and increases the renal excretion of phosphates.

name: parathyroid neoplasms
query: Query: parathyroid neoplasms [SEP] Parathyroid neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the [MASK].

name: parenchymal tissue
query: Query: parenchymal tissue [SEP] Parenchymal tissue is the tissue that constitutes the essential or functional part of an organ (e.g., parenchyma of lung, parenchyma of liver, or parenchyma of kidney).

name: parental leave
query: Query: parental leave [SEP] Parental leave is the authorized absence from work of either parent prior to and after the birth of their child. It includes also absence because of the illness of a child or at the time of the adoption of a child. It does not include leave for care of siblings, parents, or other family members: for this family leave is available.

name: parenteral nutrition , home total
query: Query: parenteral nutrition , home total [SEP] Home total parenteral nutrition is the at-home administering of nutrients for assimilation and utilization by a patient whose sole source of nutrients is via solutions administered intravenously, subcutaneously or by some other non-alimentary route.

name: parenting
query: Query: parenting [SEP] Parenting is performing the role of a parent by care-giving, nurturance, and protection of the child by a natural or substitute parent. The parent supports the child by exercising authority and through consistent, empathic, appropriate behavior in response to the child's needs. parenting differs from child rearing in that in child rearing the emphasis is on the act of training or bringing up the children and the interaction between the parent and child, while parenting emphasizes the responsibility and qualities of exemplary behavior of the parent.

name: paris
query: Query: paris [SEP] Paris is the capital city of France.

name: parity
query: Query: parity [SEP] Parity is the number of offspring a female has borne. It is contrasted with gravidity, which refers to the number of pregnancies, regardless of outcome.

name: parking facilities
query: Query: parking facilities [SEP] Parking facilities is indoor or outdoor areas designated for the parking of vehicles.

name: parkinson disease associated proteins
query: Query: parkinson disease associated proteins [SEP] Parkinson disease associated proteins is proteins associated with sporadic or familial cases of parkinson disease.

name: parks , recreational
query: Query: parks , recreational [SEP] Recreational parks is an area of land open to the public for enjoyment.

name: particle size
query: Query: particle size [SEP] Particle size is relating to the size of solids.

name: patent
query: Query: patent [SEP] Patent is work consisting of documents granted by a government giving exclusive rights to an inventor or assignee to manufacture, use, or sell an invention for a certain number of years.

name: patents as topic
query: Query: patents as topic [SEP] Patents as topic is works about exclusive legal rights or privileges applied to inventions, plants, etc.

name: paternal age
query: Query: paternal age [SEP] Paternal age is age of the biological [MASK].

name: paternal behavior
query: Query: paternal behavior [SEP] Paternal behavior is the behavior patterns associated with or characteristic of a [MASK].

name: paternal exposure
query: Query: paternal exposure [SEP] Paternal exposure is exposure of the male parent, human or animal, to potentially harmful chemical, physical, or biological agents in the environment or to environmental factors that may include ionizing radiation, pathogenic organisms, or toxic chemicals that may affect offspring.

name: pathology , clinical
query: Query: pathology , clinical [SEP] Clinical pathology is a subspecialty of pathology applied to the solution of clinical problems, especially the use of laboratory methods in clinical diagnosis. (Dorland, 28th ed.)

name: pathology , molecular
query: Query: pathology , molecular [SEP] Molecular pathology is a subspecialty of pathology concerned with the molecular basis (e.g., mutations) of various diseases.

name: pathology department , hospital
query: Query: pathology department , hospital [SEP] Hospital pathology department is hospital department which administers and provides pathology services.

name: patient access to records
query: Query: patient access to records [SEP] Patient access to records is the freedom of patients to review their own medical, genetic, or other health-related records.

name: patient admission
query: Query: patient admission [SEP] Patient admission is the process of accepting patients. The concept includes patients accepted for medical and nursing care in a hospital or other health care institution.

name: patient care bundles
query: Query: patient care bundles [SEP] Patient care bundles is small sets of evidence-based interventions for a defined patient population and care setting.

name: patient comfort
query: Query: patient comfort [SEP] Patient comfort is patient care intended to prevent or relieve suffering in conditions that ensure optimal quality living.

name: patient credit and collection
query: Query: patient credit and collection [SEP] Patient credit and collection is accounting procedures for determining credit status and methods of obtaining payment.

name: patient discharge
query: Query: patient discharge [SEP] Patient discharge is the administrative process of discharging the patient, alive or dead, from hospitals or other health facilities.

name: patient discharge summaries
query: Query: patient discharge summaries [SEP] Patient discharge summaries is summaries that serve as the primary documents communicating a patient's care plan to the post-hospital care team.

name: patient generated health data
query: Query: patient generated health data [SEP] Patient generated health data is health-related data created, recorded, or gathered by patients, family members, or caregivers, to help address a health concern. Distinct from data generated in clinical settings and through encounters with providers.

name: patient harm
query: Query: patient harm [SEP] Patient harm is a measure of patient safety considering errors or mistakes which result in harm to the patient. They include errors in the administration of drugs and other medications (medication errors), errors in the performance of procedures or the use of other types of therapy, in the use of equipment, and in the interpretation of laboratory findings and preventable accidents involving patients.

name: patient health questionnaire
query: Query: patient health questionnaire [SEP] Patient health questionnaire is a self-administered version of the Primary Care Evaluation of Mental Disorders (prime-md), a diagnostic tool containing modules on multiple mental health disorders including anxiety, alcohol, eating, and somatoform modules. The Patient Health Questionnaire (phq-9) is designed specifically for mood/depression scoring each of the 9 [MASK] criteria based on the mood module from the original prime-md. The Generalized Anxiety Disorder scale (gad-7) scores 7 common anxiety symptoms.

name: patient isolation
query: Query: patient isolation [SEP] Patient isolation is the segregation of patients with communicable or other diseases for a specified time. Isolation may be strict, in which movement and social contacts are limited; modified, where an effort to control specified aspects of care is made in order to prevent cross infection; or reverse, where the patient is secluded in a controlled or germ-free environment in order to protect him or her from cross infection.

name: patient medication knowledge
query: Query: patient medication knowledge [SEP] Patient medication knowledge is patient health knowledge related to medications including what is being used and why as well as instructions and precautions.

name: patient or disabled group
query: Query: patient or disabled group [SEP] Patient or disabled group is patient or disabled group

name: patient participation
query: Query: patient participation [SEP] Patient participation is patient involvement in the decision-making process in matters pertaining to health.

name: patient positioning
query: Query: patient positioning [SEP] Patient positioning is moving a patient into a specific position or posture to facilitate examination, surgery, or for therapeutic purposes.

name: patient preference
query: Query: patient preference [SEP] Patient preference is individual's expression of desirability or value of one course of action, outcome, or selection in contrast to others.

name: patient safety
query: Query: patient safety [SEP] Patient safety is efforts to reduce risk, to address and reduce incidents and accidents that may negatively impact healthcare consumers.

name: patient simulation
query: Query: patient simulation [SEP] Patient simulation is the use of persons coached to feign symptoms or conditions of real diseases in a life-like manner in order to teach or evaluate medical personnel.

name: peak expiratory flow rate
query: Query: peak expiratory flow rate [SEP] Peak expiratory flow rate is measurement of the maximum rate of airflow attained during a forced vital capacity determination. Common abbreviations are pefr and pfr.

name: pea proteins
query: Query: pea proteins [SEP] Pea proteins is dietary proteins that are present in or isolated from the [MASK] of pisum sativum.

name: pediatric nurse practitioners
query: Query: pediatric nurse practitioners [SEP] Pediatric nurse practitioners is registered nurses with graduate degrees in nursing who provide care to pediatric patients who are acutely or [MASK].

name: pediatric obesity
query: Query: pediatric obesity [SEP] Pediatric obesity is body mass index in children (ages 2-12) and in adolescents (ages 13-18) that is grossly above the recommended cut-off for a specific age and [MASK]. For infants less than 2 years of age, obesity is determined based on standard weight-for-length percentile measures.

name: peer influence
query: Query: peer influence [SEP] Peer influence is the effect or sway that a peer group exerts on the beliefs, value systems and behavior of each member of a group. The social expectations for individuals to conform to peer group influence is known as peer pressure.

name: pelvic inflammatory disease
query: Query: pelvic inflammatory disease [SEP] Pelvic inflammatory disease is a spectrum of inflammation involving the female upper genital tract and the supporting tissues. It is usually caused by an ascending infection of organisms from the endocervix. Infection may be confined to the uterus (endometritis), the fallopian tubes; (salpingitis); the ovaries (oophoritis), the supporting ligaments (parametritis), or may involve several of the above uterine appendages. Such inflammation can lead to functional impairment and infertility.

name: pelvic neoplasms
query: Query: pelvic neoplasms [SEP] Pelvic neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the pelvic region.

name: peptide chain elongation , translational
query: Query: peptide chain elongation , translational [SEP] Translational peptide chain elongation is a process of genetic translation, when an amino acid is transferred from its cognate transfer rna to the lengthening chain of peptides.

name: peptide chain initiation , translational
query: Query: peptide chain initiation , translational [SEP] Translational peptide chain initiation is a process of genetic translation whereby the formation of a peptide chain is started. It includes assembly of the ribosome components, the messenger rna coding for the polypeptide to be made, initiator trna, and peptide initiation factors; and placement of the first amino acid in the peptide chain. The details and components of this process are unique for prokaryotic protein biosynthesis and eukaryotic protein biosynthesis.

name: peptide chain termination , translational
query: Query: peptide chain termination , translational [SEP] Translational peptide chain termination is a process of genetic translation whereby the terminal amino acid is added to a lengthening polypeptide. This termination process is signaled from the messenger rna, by one of three termination codons (codon, terminator) that immediately follows the last amino acid-specifying codon.

name: peptide elongation factors
query: Query: peptide elongation factors [SEP] Peptide elongation factors is protein factors uniquely required during the elongation phase of protein synthesis.

name: peptide mapping
query: Query: peptide mapping [SEP] Peptide mapping is analysis of peptides that are generated from the [MASK] or fragmentation of a protein or mixture of proteins, by electrophoresis; chromatography; or mass spectrometry. The resulting peptide fingerprints are analyzed for a variety of purposes including the identification of the proteins in a sample, genetic polymorphisms, patterns of gene expression, and patterns diagnostic for diseases.

name: peptide phi
query: Query: peptide phi [SEP] Peptide phi is a 27-amino acid peptide with histidine at the N-terminal and isoleucine amide at the C-terminal. The exact amino acid composition of the peptide is species dependent. The peptide is secreted in the intestine, but is found in the nervous system, many organs, and in the majority of peripheral tissues. It has a wide range of biological actions, affecting the cardiovascular, gastrointestinal, respiratory, and central nervous systems.

name: peptide termination factors
query: Query: peptide termination factors [SEP] Peptide termination factors is proteins that are involved in the peptide chain termination reaction (peptide chain termination, translational) on ribosomes. They include codon-specific class-I release factors, which recognize stop signals (terminator codon) in the messenger rna; and codon-nonspecific class-II release factors.

name: peptide transporter 1
query: Query: peptide transporter 1 [SEP] Peptide transporter 1 is a proton-coupled symporter that transports oligopeptides and dipeptides. It localizes to the brush-border membrane of the intestinal epithelium and plays a critical role in the assimilation of dietary proteins.

name: perceptual defense
query: Query: perceptual defense [SEP] Perceptual defense is selective perceiving such that the individual protects himself from becoming aware of something unpleasant or threatening, e.g., obscene words are not heard correctly, or violent acts are not seen accurately.

name: perfusion index
query: Query: perfusion index [SEP] Perfusion index is the ratio of arterial blood flow (pulsatile flow) to venous, capillary, and tissue blood flow  (non-pulsatile blood flow) - as measured regionally or peripherally.

name: perinatal death
query: Query: perinatal death [SEP] Perinatal death is the death of a fetus of gestational age 28 weeks or more, or the death of a live-born infant less than 28 days of age.

name: perinatal mortality
query: Query: perinatal mortality [SEP] Perinatal mortality is deaths occurring from the 28th week of gestation to the 28th day after birth in a given population.

name: period circadian proteins
query: Query: period circadian proteins [SEP] Period circadian proteins is circadian rhythm signaling proteins that influence circadian clock by interacting with other circadian regulatory proteins and transporting them into the cell nucleus.

name: periodical
query: Query: periodical [SEP] Periodical is publication intended to be issued on an ongoing basis, generally more frequently than annually, containing separate articles, stories, or writings.

name: periodontal cyst
query: Query: periodontal cyst [SEP] Periodontal cyst is an epithelium-lined sac containing fluid; usually found at the apex of a pulp-involved tooth. The lateral type occurs less frequently along the side of the root.

name: periodontal index
query: Query: periodontal index [SEP] Periodontal index is a numerical rating scale for classifying the periodontal status of a person or population with a single figure which takes into consideration [MASK] as well as severity of the condition. It is based upon probe measurement of [MASK] and on gingival tissue status.

name: periodontal prosthesis
query: Query: periodontal prosthesis [SEP] Periodontal prosthesis is any restorative and replacement device that is used as a therapeutic aid in the treatment of periodontal disease. It is an adjunct to other forms of periodontal therapy and does not cure periodontal disease by itself. (Boucher's Clinical Dental Terminology, 3d ed)

name: perioperative medicine
query: Query: perioperative medicine [SEP] Perioperative medicine is a medical specialty concerned with the patient before and after surgical procedures.

name: peripheral blood stem cell transplantation
query: Query: peripheral blood stem cell transplantation [SEP] [MASK] transplantation is transplantation of [MASK]. It is a less invasive alternative to direct marrow harvesting of hematopoietic stem cells. Enrichment of stem cells in peripheral blood can be achieved by inducing mobilization of stem cells from the bone marrow.

name: peripheral nerve injuries
query: Query: peripheral nerve injuries [SEP] Peripheral nerve injuries is injuries to the peripheral nerves.

name: peritoneal absorption
query: Query: peritoneal absorption [SEP] Peritoneal absorption is uptake of substances from the peritoneal cavity.

name: peritoneal dialysis , continuous ambulatory
query: Query: peritoneal dialysis , continuous ambulatory [SEP] Continuous ambulatory peritoneal dialysis is portable peritoneal dialysis using the continuous (24 hours a day, 7 days a week) presence of peritoneal dialysis solution in the peritoneal cavity except for periods of drainage and instillation of fresh solution.

name: peritoneal fibrosis
query: Query: peritoneal fibrosis [SEP] Peritoneal fibrosis is disorder characterized by a wide range of structural changes in peritoneum, resulting from fibrogenic or inflammatory processes. Peritoneal fibrosis is a common complication in patients receiving peritoneal dialysis and contributes to its gradual decrease in efficiency.

name: persistent fetal circulation syndrome
query: Query: persistent fetal circulation syndrome [SEP] Persistent fetal circulation syndrome is a syndrome of persistent pulmonary hypertension in the newborn infant (infant, newborn) without demonstrable heart diseases. This neonatal condition can be caused by severe pulmonary vasoconstriction (reactive type), hypertrophy of pulmonary arterial muscle (hypertrophic type), or abnormally developed pulmonary arterioles (hypoplastic type). The newborn patient exhibits cyanosis and acidosis due to the persistence of fetal circulatory pattern of right-to-left shunting of blood through a patent ductus arteriosus (ductus arteriosus, patent) and at times a patent foramen ovale (foramen ovale, patent).

name: personal construct theory
query: Query: personal construct theory [SEP] Personal construct theory is a psychological theory based on dimensions or categories used by a given person in describing or explaining the personality and behavior of others or of himself. The basic idea is that different people will use consistently different categories. The theory was formulated in the fifties by George Kelly. Two tests devised by him are the role construct repertory test and the repertory grid test. (From Stuart Sutherland, The International Dictionary of Psychology, 1989)

name: personal health services
query: Query: personal health services [SEP] Personal health services is health care provided to individuals.

name: personnel loyalty
query: Query: personnel loyalty [SEP] Personnel loyalty is dedication or commitment shown by employees to organizations or institutions where they work.

name: personnel turnover
query: Query: personnel turnover [SEP] Personnel turnover is a change or shift in personnel due to reorganization, resignation, or discharge.

name: pertussis vaccine
query: Query: pertussis vaccine [SEP] Pertussis vaccine is a suspension of killed Bordetella pertussis organisms, used for immunization against pertussis (whooping [MASK]). It is generally used in a mixture with diphtheria and tetanus toxoids (dtp). There is an acellular pertussis vaccine prepared from the purified antigenic components of Bordetella pertussis, which causes fewer adverse reactions than whole-cell vaccine and, like the whole-cell vaccine, is generally used in a mixture with diphtheria and tetanus toxoids. (From Dorland, 28th ed)

name: peru
query: Query: peru [SEP] Peru is a country in western South America, bordering the South Pacific Ocean, and located between [MASK] and Ecuador.

name: pesticide residues
query: Query: pesticide residues [SEP] Pesticide residues is pesticides or their breakdown products remaining in the environment following their normal use or accidental contamination.

name: petroleum pollution
query: Query: petroleum pollution [SEP] Petroleum pollution is release of oil into the environment usually due to human activity.

name: phage therapy
query: Query: phage therapy [SEP] Phage therapy is therapeutic use of bacteriophages to treat diseases.

name: pharmaceutical preparations , dental
query: Query: pharmaceutical preparations , dental [SEP] Dental pharmaceutical preparations is drugs intended for dentistry.

name: pharmaceutical research
query: Query: pharmaceutical research [SEP] Pharmaceutical research is research activity focused on pharmaceutical products and services.

name: pharmaceutical services , online
query: Query: pharmaceutical services , online [SEP] Online pharmaceutical services is pharmacy services accessed via electronic means.

name: pharmacists
query: Query: pharmacists [SEP] Pharmacists is those persons legally qualified by education and training to engage in the practice of pharmacy.

name: pharmacology , clinical
query: Query: pharmacology , clinical [SEP] Clinical pharmacology is the branch of pharmacology that deals directly with the effectiveness and safety of drugs in humans.

name: phd zinc fingers
query: Query: phd zinc fingers [SEP] Phd zinc fingers is zinc finger domains of approximately 50 to 80 amino acids in length that are characterized by a conserved [MASK](3)-Histidine-[MASK](4) amino acid motif which coordinates binding of two zinc ions. They are similar structurally to ring finger domains, with a globular fold topology of two beta-sheets and an alpha-helix. phd fingers occur in many proteins that function in chromatin-mediated gene expression and epigenetics such as polycomb-group proteins.

name: philadelphia chromosome
query: Query: philadelphia chromosome [SEP] [MASK] chromosome is an aberrant form of human chromosome 22 characterized by translocation of the distal end of chromosome 9 from 9q34, to the long [MASK] of chromosome 22 at 22q11. It is present in the bone marrow cells of 80 to 90 per cent of patients with chronic myelocytic leukemia (leukemia, myelogenous, chronic, bcr-abl positive).

name: phospholipid transfer proteins
query: Query: phospholipid transfer proteins [SEP] [MASK] transfer proteins is a ubiquitous family of proteins that transport [MASK] such as phosphatidylinositol and phosphatidylcholine between membranes. They play an important role in [MASK] metabolism during vesicular transport and signal transduction.

name: phosphorus , dietary
query: Query: phosphorus , dietary [SEP] Dietary phosphorus is phosphorus used in foods or obtained from food. This element is a major intracellular component which plays an important role in many biochemical pathways relating to normal physiological functions. High concentrations of dietary phosphorus can cause nephrocalcinosis which is associated with impaired kidney function. Low concentrations of dietary phosphorus cause an increase in calcitriol in the blood and osteoporosis.

name: phosphorus isotopes
query: Query: phosphorus isotopes [SEP] Phosphorus isotopes is stable phosphorus atoms that have the same atomic number as the element phosphorus, but differ in atomic weight. p-31 is a stable phosphorus isotope.

name: photograph
query: Query: photograph [SEP] Photograph is still image produced from radiation-sensitive materials (sensitive to light, [MASK] beams, or nuclear radiation), generally by means of the chemical action of light on a sensitive film, [MASK], glass, or metal. Photographs may be positive or negative, opaque or transparent.

name: photoperiod
query: Query: photoperiod [SEP] Photoperiod is the time period of daily exposure that an organism receives from daylight or artificial light. It is believed that photoperiodic responses may affect the control of energy balance and thermoregulation.

name: phrases
query: Query: phrases [SEP] Phrases is work consisting of common terms, phrases, idioms, and typical conversations, e.g., between health professional and patients. These are often intended for use by non-native speakers of a language.

name: physical abuse
query: Query: physical abuse [SEP] Physical abuse is violence inflicted on an individual through physical contact.

name: physical appearance , body
query: Query: physical appearance , body [SEP] Body physical appearance is the superficial physical looks, characteristics or qualities of an individual as distinguished from the underlying unseen nature or attributes.

name: physical therapists
query: Query: physical therapists [SEP] Physical therapists is persons trained in physical therapy specialty to make use of physical therapy modalities to prevent, correct, and alleviate movement dysfunction.

name: physical therapy department , hospital
query: Query: physical therapy department , hospital [SEP] Hospital physical therapy department is hospital department which is responsible for the administration and provision of diagnostic and medical rehabilitation services to restore or improve the functional capacity of the patient.

name: physician incentive plans
query: Query: physician incentive plans [SEP] Physician incentive plans is compensatory plans designed to motivate physicians in relation to patient referral, physician recruitment, and efficient use of the health facility.

name: physicians ' offices
query: Query: physicians ' offices [SEP] Physicians' offices is establishments of licensed physicians primarily engaged in the private or group practice of general or specialized medicine or surgery.

name: physicians , primary care
query: Query: physicians , primary care [SEP] Primary care physicians is providers of initial care for patients. These physicians refer patients when appropriate for secondary or specialist care.

name: physiology , comparative
query: Query: physiology , comparative [SEP] Comparative physiology is the biological science concerned with similarities or differences in the life-supporting functions and processes of different species.

name: pierre robin syndrome
query: Query: pierre robin syndrome [SEP] Pierre robin syndrome is congenital malformation characterized by micrognathia or retrognathia; glossoptosis and cleft palate. The mandibular abnormalities often result in difficulties in sucking and swallowing. The syndrome may be isolated or associated with other syndromes (e.g., andersen syndrome; campomelic dysplasia). Developmental mis-expression of sox9 transcription factor gene on chromosome 17q and its surrounding region is associated with the syndrome.

name: pilot projects
query: Query: pilot projects [SEP] Pilot projects is small-scale tests of methods and procedures to be used on a larger scale if the pilot study demonstrates that these methods and procedures can work.

name: pitch discrimination
query: Query: pitch discrimination [SEP] Pitch discrimination is the ability to differentiate sound frequency or pitch.

name: pituitary function tests
query: Query: pituitary function tests [SEP] Pituitary function tests is examinations that evaluate functions of the pituitary gland.

name: pituitary gland , anterior
query: Query: pituitary gland , anterior [SEP] Anterior pituitary gland is the anterior glandular lobe of the pituitary gland, also known as the adenohypophysis. It secretes the adenohypophyseal hormones that regulate vital functions such as growth; metabolism; and reproduction.

name: pituitary gland , intermediate
query: Query: pituitary gland , intermediate [SEP] Intermediate pituitary gland is the intermediate lobe of the pituitary gland. It shows considerable size variation among the species, small in humans, and large in amphibians and lower vertebrates. This lobe produces mainly melanocyte-stimulating hormones and other peptides from post-translational processing of pro-opiomelanocortin (pomc).

name: pituitary hormone release inhibiting hormones
query: Query: pituitary hormone release inhibiting hormones [SEP] Pituitary hormone release inhibiting hormones is polypeptide hormones produced in the hypothalamus which inhibit the release of pituitary hormones. Used for phrih in general or for which there is no specific heading.

name: pituitary neoplasms
query: Query: pituitary neoplasms [SEP] Pituitary neoplasms is neoplasms which arise from or metastasize to the pituitary gland. The majority of pituitary neoplasms are adenomas, which are divided into non-secreting and secreting forms. Hormone producing forms are further classified by the type of hormone they secrete. Pituitary adenomas may also be characterized by their staining properties (see adenoma, basophil; adenoma, acidophil; and adenoma, chromophobe). Pituitary tumors may compress adjacent structures, including the hypothalamus, several cranial nerves, and the optic chiasm. Chiasmal compression may result in bitemporal hemianopsia.

name: place cells
query: Query: place cells [SEP] Place cells is pyramidal neurons in the hippocampus that play a role in cognitive representation of a specific location within a space.

name: placenta
query: Query: placenta [SEP] Placenta is a highly vascularized mammalian fetal-maternal organ and major site of transport of oxygen, nutrients, and fetal waste products. It includes a fetal portion (chorionic villi) derived from trophoblasts and a maternal portion (decidua) derived from the uterine endometrium. The placenta produces an array of steroid, protein and peptide [MASK] hormones).

name: placenta , retained
query: Query: placenta , retained [SEP] Retained placenta is a placenta that fails to be expelled after birth of the fetus. a placenta is retained when the uterus fails to contract after the delivery of its content, or when the placenta is abnormally attached to the myometrium.

name: placental circulation
query: Query: placental circulation [SEP] Placental circulation is the circulation of blood, of both the mother and the fetus, through the placenta.

name: placental extracts
query: Query: placental extracts [SEP] Placental extracts is extracts prepared from placental tissue; they may contain specific but uncharacterized factors or proteins with specific activities.

name: placental insufficiency
query: Query: placental insufficiency [SEP] Placental insufficiency is failure of the placenta to deliver an adequate supply of nutrients and oxygen to the fetus.

name: plantar plate
query: Query: plantar plate [SEP] Plantar plate is fibrocartilaginous ligament at the metatarsophalangeal and the interphalangeal joint of the toe.

name: plant bark
query: Query: plant bark [SEP] Plant bark is the outer layer of the woody parts of plants.

name: plant cells
query: Query: plant cells [SEP] Plant cells is basic functional unit of plants.

name: plant growth regulators
query: Query: plant growth regulators [SEP] Plant growth regulators is any of the hormones produced naturally in plants and active in controlling growth and other functions. There are three primary classes: auxins, cytokinins, and gibberellins.

name: plant leaves
query: Query: plant leaves [SEP] Plant leaves is expanded structures, usually green, of vascular plants, characteristically consisting of a bladelike expansion attached to a stem, and functioning as the principal organ of [MASK] and transpiration. (American Heritage Dictionary, 2d ed)

name: plant pathology
query: Query: plant pathology [SEP] Plant pathology is the study of infectious diseases associated with plants.

name: plants , genetically modified
query: Query: plants , genetically modified [SEP] Genetically modified plants is plants, or their progeny, whose genome has been altered by genetic engineering.

name: plants , toxic
query: Query: plants , toxic [SEP] Toxic plants is plants or plant parts which are harmful to man or other animals.

name: plant shoots
query: Query: plant shoots [SEP] Plant shoots is new immature growth of a plant including stem, leaves, tips of branches, and seedlings.

name: plant stems
query: Query: plant stems [SEP] Plant stems is parts of plants that usually grow vertically upwards towards the light and support the leaves, buds, and reproductive structures. (From Concise Dictionary of Biology, 1990)

name: plant tumors
query: Query: plant tumors [SEP] Plant tumors is a localized proliferation of plant tissue forming a swelling or outgrowth, commonly with a characteristic shape and unlike any organ of the normal plant. Plant tumors or galls usually form in response to the action of a pathogen or a pest. (Holliday, p., a Dictionary of Plant Pathology, 1989, p330)

name: plant viral movement proteins
query: Query: plant viral movement proteins [SEP] Plant viral movement proteins is viral proteins that facilitate the movement of viruses between plant cells by means of plasmodesmata, channels that traverse the plant cell walls.

name: plaque , amyloid
query: Query: plaque , amyloid [SEP] Amyloid plaque is accumulations of extracellularly deposited amyloid fibrils within tissues.

name: plasma
query: Query: plasma [SEP] Plasma is the residual portion of blood that is left after removal of blood cells by centrifugation without prior blood coagulation.

name: plasma exchange
query: Query: plasma exchange [SEP] Plasma exchange is removal of plasma and replacement with various fluids, e.g., fresh frozen plasma, plasma protein fractions (ppf), albumin preparations, dextran solutions, saline. Used in treatment of autoimmune diseases, immune complex diseases, diseases of excess plasma factors, and other conditions.

name: plasma gases
query: Query: plasma gases [SEP] Plasma gases is ionized gases, consisting of free [MASK] and ionized atoms or molecules which collectively behave differently than gas, solid, or liquid.
