Plasma gases are used in biomedical fields in surface modification; biological decontamination; dentistry (e.g., [MASK]); and in other treatments (e.g., [MASK] plasma coagulation).

name: plasma skin regeneration
query: Query: plasma skin regeneration [SEP] Plasma skin regeneration is a cosmetic technique that uses plasma gases in therapeutic treatment to help achieve skin rejuvenation or regeneration and delay skin aging.

name: plasma volume
query: Query: plasma volume [SEP] Plasma volume is volume of plasma in the circulation. It is usually measured by indicator dilution techniques.

name: plasminogen
query: Query: plasminogen [SEP] Plasminogen is precursor of plasmin (fibrinolysin). It is a single-chain beta-globulin of molecular weight 80-90,000 found mostly in association with fibrinogen in plasma; plasminogen activators change it to fibrinolysin. It is used in wound debriding and has been investigated as a thrombolytic agent.

name: plasmodium falciparum
query: Query: plasmodium falciparum [SEP] Plasmodium falciparum is a species of protozoa that is the causal agent of falciparum malaria (malaria, falciparum). It is most prevalent in the tropics and subtropics.

name: platelet aggregation inhibitors
query: Query: platelet aggregation inhibitors [SEP] [MASK] inhibitors is drugs or agents which antagonize or impair any mechanism leading to blood [MASK], whether during the phases of activation and shape change or following the dense-granule release reaction and stimulation of the prostaglandin-thromboxane system.

name: platelet count
query: Query: platelet count [SEP] Platelet count is the number of platelets per unit volume in a sample of venous blood.

name: platelet factor 3
query: Query: platelet factor 3 [SEP] Platelet factor 3 is a [MASK] from the platelet membrane that contributes to the blood clotting cascade by forming a [MASK]-protein complex (thromboplastin) which serves as a cofactor with factor viia to activate factor x in the extrinsic pathway of blood coagulation.

name: platelet factor 4
query: Query: platelet factor 4 [SEP] Platelet factor 4 is a cxc chemokine that is found in the alpha granules of platelets. The protein has a molecular size of 7800 kDa and can occur as a monomer, a dimer or a tetramer depending upon its concentration in solution. Platelet factor 4 has a high affinity for heparin and is often found complexed with glycoproteins such as protein c.

name: platelet storage pool deficiency
query: Query: platelet storage pool deficiency [SEP] Platelet storage pool deficiency is disorder characterized by a decrease or lack of platelet dense bodies in which the releasable pool of adenine nucleotides and 5ht are normally stored.

name: play therapy
query: Query: play therapy [SEP] Play therapy is a treatment technique utilizing play as a medium for expression and communication between patient and therapist.

name: pleasure
query: Query: pleasure [SEP] Pleasure is sensation of enjoyment or gratification.

name: pleural cavity
query: Query: pleural cavity [SEP] Pleural cavity is paired but separate cavity within the thoracic cavity. It consists of the space between the parietal and visceral pleura and normally contains a capillary layer of serous fluid that lubricates the pleural surfaces.

name: pleural effusion , malignant
query: Query: pleural effusion , malignant [SEP] Malignant pleural effusion is presence of fluid in the pleural cavity as a complication of malignant disease. Malignant pleural effusions often contain actual malignant cells.

name: pneumonia , atypical interstitial , of cattle
query: Query: pneumonia , atypical interstitial , of cattle [SEP] Of cattle atypical interstitial pneumonia is a cattle disease of uncertain cause, probably an allergic reaction.

name: pneumonia , progressive interstitial , of sheep
query: Query: pneumonia , progressive interstitial , of sheep [SEP] Of sheep progressive interstitial pneumonia is chronic respiratory disease caused by the visna-maedi virus. It was formerly believed to be identical with jaagsiekte (pulmonary adenomatosis, ovine) but is now recognized as a separate entity.

name: pneumonia , viral
query: Query: pneumonia , viral [SEP] Viral pneumonia is inflammation of the lung parenchyma that is caused by a viral infection.

name: poison control centers
query: Query: poison control centers [SEP] Poison control centers is facilities which provide information concerning poisons and treatment of poisoning in emergencies.

name: poisson distribution
query: Query: poisson distribution [SEP] Poisson distribution is a distribution function used to describe the occurrence of rare events or to describe the sampling distribution of isolated counts in a continuum of time or space.

name: poland
query: Query: poland [SEP] Poland is a country in central Europe, east of Germany. The capital is Warsaw.

name: polar bodies
query: Query: polar bodies [SEP] Polar bodies is minute cells produced during development of an oocyte as it undergoes meiosis. a polar body contains one of the nuclei derived from the first or second meiotic cell division. Polar bodies have practically no cytoplasm. They are eventually discarded by the oocyte. (from King & Stansfield, a Dictionary of Genetics, 4th ed)

name: pollen tube
query: Query: pollen tube [SEP] Pollen tube is a growth from a pollen grain down into the flower style which allows two sperm to pass, one to the ovum within the ovule, and the other to the central cell of the ovule to produce endosperm of [MASK].

name: polymorphism , restriction fragment length
query: Query: polymorphism , restriction fragment length [SEP] Restriction fragment length polymorphism is variation occurring within a species in the presence or length of dna fragment generated by a specific endonuclease at a specific site in the genome. Such variations are generated by mutations that create or abolish recognition sites for these enzymes or change the length of the fragment.

name: polymorphism , single nucleotide
query: Query: polymorphism , single nucleotide [SEP] Single nucleotide polymorphism is a single nucleotide variation in a genetic sequence that occurs at appreciable frequency in the population.

name: polyvinyl alcohol
query: Query: polyvinyl alcohol [SEP] Polyvinyl alcohol is a polymer prepared from polyvinyl acetates by replacement of the acetate groups with hydroxyl groups. It is used as a pharmaceutic aid and ophthalmic lubricant as well as in the manufacture of surface coatings artificial sponges, cosmetics, and other products.

name: popular culture
query: Query: popular culture [SEP] Popular culture is choices and ways of doing things that predominate or are fashionable among ordinary people in a society during a point in time.

name: population control
query: Query: population control [SEP] Population control is includes mechanisms or programs which control the numbers of individuals in a population of humans or animals.

name: population forecast
query: Query: population forecast [SEP] Population forecast is estimates of projected population.

name: population group
query: Query: population group [SEP] Population group is individuals classified according to their [MASK], racial origin, religion, common place of living, financial or [MASK], or some other cultural or behavioral attribute.

name: population growth
query: Query: population growth [SEP] Population growth is increase, over a specific period of time, in the number of individuals living in a country or region.

name: porosity
query: Query: porosity [SEP] Porosity is condition of having pores or open spaces. This often refers to bones, bone implants, or bone cements, but can refer to the porous state of any solid substance.

name: portal pressure
query: Query: portal pressure [SEP] Portal pressure is the venous pressure measured in the portal vein.

name: portal vein
query: Query: portal vein [SEP] Portal vein is a short thick vein formed by union of the superior mesenteric vein and the splenic vein.

name: portion size
query: Query: portion size [SEP] Portion size is the amount of a particular food one chooses to eat at a single meal. It is different from [MASK], which is a reference amount of food as defined by an authoritative source, such as the Food Guide Pyramid devised by the united states department of agriculture.

name: portugal
query: Query: portugal [SEP] Portugal is a country in southwestern Europe, bordering the North Atlantic Ocean, west of [MASK]. The capital is Lisbon.

name: posterior cerebral artery
query: Query: posterior cerebral artery [SEP] Posterior cerebral artery is artery formed by the bifurcation of the basilar artery. Branches of the posterior cerebral artery supply portions of the occipital lobe; parietal lobe; inferior temporal gyrus, brainstem, and choroid plexus.

name: posterior cervical sympathetic syndrome
query: Query: posterior cervical sympathetic syndrome [SEP] Posterior cervical sympathetic syndrome is a pathological condition that is characterized by a host of cranial symptoms, such as headaches, abnormal functions of the eyes and the ears, and psychological and mental disorders. This syndrome usually appears after [MASK] injuries, inflammation, or neoplasm.

name: posterior horn cells
query: Query: posterior horn cells [SEP] Posterior horn cells is neurons in the spinal cord dorsal horn whose cell bodies and processes are confined entirely to the central nervous system. They receive collateral or direct terminations of dorsal root fibers. They send their axons either directly to anterior horn cells or to the [MASK] matter ascending and descending longitudinal fibers.

name: posterior thalamic nuclei
query: Query: posterior thalamic nuclei [SEP] Posterior thalamic nuclei is a transitional diencephalic zone of the thalamus consisting of complex and varied cells lying caudal to the [MASK], medial to the rostral part of the pulvinar, and dorsal to the medial geniculate body. It contains the limitans, posterior, suprageniculate, and submedial nuclei.

name: postnatal care
query: Query: postnatal care [SEP] Postnatal care is the care provided to women and their newborns for the first few months following childbirth.

name: postoperative care
query: Query: postoperative care [SEP] Postoperative care is the period of care beginning when the patient is removed from surgery and aimed at meeting the patient's psychological and physical needs directly after surgery. (From Dictionary of Health Services Management, 2d ed)

name: postoperative cognitive complications
query: Query: postoperative cognitive complications [SEP] Postoperative cognitive complications is cognitive impairment or functional decline after a surgical procedure.

name: postoperative hemorrhage
query: Query: postoperative hemorrhage [SEP] Postoperative hemorrhage is hemorrhage following any surgical procedure. It may be immediate or delayed and is not restricted to the [MASK].

name: postprandial period
query: Query: postprandial period [SEP] Postprandial period is the time frame after a meal or food intake.

name: potassium , dietary
query: Query: potassium , dietary [SEP] Dietary potassium is potassium or potassium compounds used in foods or as foods.

name: potassium acetate
query: Query: potassium acetate [SEP] Potassium acetate is a potassium [MASK] used to replenish electrolytes, for restoration of water-electrolyte balance, as well as a urinary and systemic alkalizer, which can be administered orally or by [MASK]. Formerly, it was used in diuretics and expectorants.

name: potassium channel blockers
query: Query: potassium channel blockers [SEP] Potassium channel blockers is a class of drugs that act by inhibition of potassium efflux through cell membranes. Blockade of potassium channels prolongs the duration of action potentials. They are used as anti-arrhythmia agents and vasodilator agents.

name: potassium channels , tandem pore domain
query: Query: potassium channels , tandem pore domain [SEP] Tandem pore domain potassium channels is potassium channels that contain two pores in tandem. They are responsible for baseline or leak currents and may be the most numerous of all k channels.

name: potentially inappropriate medication list
query: Query: potentially inappropriate medication list [SEP] Potentially inappropriate medication list is a list, criteria, or screening tool designed to improve patient safety by determining an individual's exposure to potentially inappropriate drugs. They are designed to prevent medication errors by inappropriate prescribing. Analysis for a list includes factors such as dose-response relationship, drug; drug-related side effects and adverse reactions; age factors; gender; and existing medical conditions.

name: poultry diseases
query: Query: poultry diseases [SEP] Poultry diseases is diseases of birds which are raised as a source of meat or eggs for human consumption and are usually found in barnyards, hatcheries, etc. The concept is differentiated from bird diseases which is for diseases of birds not considered poultry and usually found in zoos, parks, and the wild.

name: poultry products
query: Query: poultry products [SEP] Poultry products is food products manufactured from poultry.

name: poultry proteins
query: Query: poultry proteins [SEP] Poultry proteins is dietary proteins from poultry.

name: poverty areas
query: Query: poverty areas [SEP] Poverty areas is city, urban, rural, or suburban areas which are characterized by severe economic deprivation and by accompanying physical and social decay.

name: powders
query: Query: powders [SEP] Powders is substances made up of an aggregation of small particles, as that obtained by grinding or trituration of a solid drug. In pharmacy it is a form in which substances are administered. (From Dorland, 28th ed)

name: practice , psychological
query: Query: practice , psychological [SEP] Psychological practice is performance of an act one or more times, with a view to its fixation or improvement; any performance of an act or behavior that leads to learning.

name: practice guideline
query: Query: practice guideline [SEP] Practice guideline is work consisting of a [MASK] of directions or principles to assist the health care practitioner with patient care decisions about appropriate diagnostic, therapeutic, or other clinical procedures for specific clinical circumstances. Practice guidelines may be developed by government agencies at any level, institutions, organizations such as professional societies or governing boards, or by the convening of expert panels. They can provide a [MASK] for assessing and evaluating the quality and effectiveness of health care in terms of measuring improved health, reduction of variation in services or procedures performed, and reduction of variation in outcomes of health care delivered.

name: practice management , dental
query: Query: practice management , dental [SEP] Dental practice management is the organization and operation of the business aspects of a dental practice.

name: practice patterns , physicians '
query: Query: practice patterns , physicians ' [SEP] Physicians' practice patterns is practice patterns , physicians '

name: practice valuation and purchase
query: Query: practice valuation and purchase [SEP] Practice valuation and purchase is determination of economic value of an established health care provider practice including value of patient lists, equipment, and other assets, and process of buying or selling rights to said practice.

name: pragmatic clinical trial
query: Query: pragmatic clinical trial [SEP] Pragmatic clinical trial is randomized clinical trials that compare interventions in clinical settings and which look at a range of effectiveness outcomes and impacts.

name: pragmatic clinical trials as topic
query: Query: pragmatic clinical trials as topic [SEP] Pragmatic clinical trials as topic is works about randomized clinical trials that compare interventions in clinical settings and which look at a range of effectiveness outcomes and impacts.

name: precision medicine
query: Query: precision medicine [SEP] Precision medicine is clinical, therapeutic and diagnostic approaches to optimal disease management based on individual variations in a patient's genetic profile.

name: predictive value of tests
query: Query: predictive value of tests [SEP] Predictive value of tests is in screening and [MASK], the probability that a person with a positive test is a true positive (i.e., has the disease), is referred to as the predictive value of a positive test; whereas, the predictive value of a negative test is the probability that the person with a negative test does not have the disease. Predictive value is related to the sensitivity and specificity of the test.

name: preferred provider organizations
query: Query: preferred provider organizations [SEP] Preferred provider organizations is arrangements negotiated between a third-party payer (often a self-insured company or union trust fund) and a group of health-care providers (hospitals and physicians) who furnish services at lower than usual fees, and, in return, receive prompt payment and an expectation of an increased volume of patients.

name: prefrontal cortex
query: Query: prefrontal cortex [SEP] Prefrontal cortex is the rostral part of the frontal lobe, bounded by the inferior precentral fissure in humans, which receives [MASK] fibers from the mediodorsal nucleus of the thalamus. The prefrontal cortex receives afferent fibers from numerous structures of the diencephalon; mesencephalon; and limbic system as well as cortical afferents of visual, auditory, and somatic origin.

name: pregnancy , angular
query: Query: pregnancy , angular [SEP] Angular pregnancy is a rare type of abnormal pregnancy in which embryo implantation occurs at a lateral angle of the uterus, medial to the uterotubal junction and the round ligament of uterus.

name: pregnancy , ovarian
query: Query: pregnancy , ovarian [SEP] Ovarian pregnancy is a type of pregnancy in which embryo implantation occurs in an ovary instead of in the uterine cavity.

name: pregnancy , prolonged
query: Query: pregnancy , prolonged [SEP] Prolonged pregnancy is a term used to describe pregnancies that exceed the upper limit of a normal gestational period. In humans, a prolonged pregnancy is defined as one that extends beyond 42 weeks (294 days) after the first day of the last menstrual period (menstruation), or birth with gestational age of 41 weeks or more.

name: pregnancy , twin
query: Query: pregnancy , twin [SEP] Twin pregnancy is the condition of carrying twins simultaneously.

name: pregnancy complications , cardiovascular
query: Query: pregnancy complications , cardiovascular [SEP] Cardiovascular pregnancy complications is the co-occurrence of pregnancy and a cardiovascular disease. The disease may precede or follow fertilization and it may or may not have a deleterious effect on the pregnant woman or fetus.

name: pregnancy complications , hematologic
query: Query: pregnancy complications , hematologic [SEP] Hematologic pregnancy complications is the co-occurrence of pregnancy and a blood disease (hematologic diseases) which involves blood cells or coagulation factors. The hematologic disease may precede or follow fertilization and it may or may not have a deleterious effect on the pregnant woman or fetus.

name: pregnancy complications , neoplastic
query: Query: pregnancy complications , neoplastic [SEP] Neoplastic pregnancy complications is the co-occurrence of pregnancy and neoplasms. The neoplastic disease may precede or follow fertilization.

name: pregnancy complications , parasitic
query: Query: pregnancy complications , parasitic [SEP] Parasitic pregnancy complications is the co-occurrence of pregnancy and parasitic diseases. The parasitic infection may precede or follow fertilization.

name: pregnancy in adolescence
query: Query: pregnancy in adolescence [SEP] Pregnancy in adolescence is pregnancy in human adolescent females under the age of 19.

name: pregnant women
query: Query: pregnant women [SEP] Pregnant women is human females who are pregnant, as cultural, psychological, or sociological entities.

name: preliminary data
query: Query: preliminary data [SEP] Preliminary data is first-released version of study results in a series of data collection efforts used for the purpose of generating further interest in and or funding of a research study.

name: premature birth
query: Query: premature birth [SEP] Premature birth is childbirth before 37 weeks of pregnancy (259 days from the first day of the mother's last menstrual period, or 245 days after fertilization).

name: prenatal education
query: Query: prenatal education [SEP] Prenatal education is training for pregnant women and parents-to-be to prepare for childbirth; child care; and parenthood.

name: preoperative care
query: Query: preoperative care [SEP] Preoperative care is care given during the period prior to undergoing surgery when psychological and physical preparations are made according to the special needs of the individual patient. This period spans the time between admission to the hospital to the time the surgery begins. (From Dictionary of Health Services Management, 2d ed)

name: preoperative period
query: Query: preoperative period [SEP] Preoperative period is the period before a surgical operation.

name: prescription drug misuse
query: Query: prescription drug misuse [SEP] Prescription drug misuse is improper use of prescription drugs or medications outside the intended purpose, scope, or guidelines for use.

name: prescription drug monitoring programs
query: Query: prescription drug monitoring programs [SEP] Prescription drug monitoring programs is programs, usually run by [MASK], that require pharmacists to collect and distribute data on the prescription and dispensation of controlled substances. They are intended to prevent the abuse of such substances by the patient, or their transfer to recreational users and drug dealers.

name: prescription drugs
query: Query: prescription drugs [SEP] Prescription drugs is drugs that cannot be sold legally without a prescription.

name: pressure ulcer
query: Query: pressure ulcer [SEP] Pressure [MASK] is an ulceration caused by prolonged pressure on the skin and tissues when one stays in one position for a long period of time, such as lying in bed. The bony areas of the body are the most frequently affected sites which become ischemic (ischemia) under sustained and constant pressure.

name: presynaptic terminals
query: Query: presynaptic terminals [SEP] Presynaptic terminals is the distal terminations of axons which are specialized for the release of neurotransmitters. Also included are varicosities along the course of axons which have similar specializations and also release transmitters. Presynaptic terminals in both the central and peripheral nervous systems are included.

name: primary care nursing
query: Query: primary care nursing [SEP] Primary care nursing is techniques or methods of patient care used by nurses as primary careproviders.

name: primary cell culture
query: Query: primary cell culture [SEP] Primary cell culture is the initial culturing of cells derived directly from fresh tissues.

name: primary graft dysfunction
query: Query: primary graft dysfunction [SEP] Primary [MASK] dysfunction is a form of ischemia-reperfusion injury occurring in the early period following transplantation. Significant pathophysiological changes in mitochondria are the main cause of the dysfunction. It is most often seen in the transplanted lung, liver, or kidney and can lead to [MASK] [MASK].

name: primary nursing
query: Query: primary nursing [SEP] Primary nursing is the primary responsibility of one nurse for the planning, evaluation, and care of a patient throughout the course of illness, convalescence, and recovery.

name: primed in situ labeling
query: Query: primed in situ labeling [SEP] Primed in situ labeling is a technique that labels specific sequences in whole chromosomes by in situ dna chain elongation or pcr (polymerase chain reaction).

name: principal component analysis
query: Query: principal component analysis [SEP] Principal component analysis is mathematical procedure that transforms a number of possibly correlated variables into a smaller number of uncorrelated variables called principal components.

name: printing
query: Query: printing [SEP] Printing is process of reproducing words or images on a physical media.

name: prior authorization
query: Query: prior authorization [SEP] Prior authorization is a decision by a health insurer or plan that a health care service, treatment plan, prescription drug or [MASK] is medically necessary.

name: proactive inhibition
query: Query: proactive inhibition [SEP] Proactive inhibition is the state or process hypothesized to account for poorer learning rate for elements later in a series as compared to the learning rate for elements coming earlier in a series.

name: probability learning
query: Query: probability learning [SEP] Probability learning is usually refers to the use of mathematical models in the prediction of learning to perform tasks based on the theory of probability applied to responses; it may also refer to the frequency of occurrence of the responses observed in the particular study.

name: probability theory
query: Query: probability theory [SEP] Probability theory is the branch of mathematics dealing with the purely logical properties of probability. Its theorems underlie most statistical methods. (Last, a Dictionary of Epidemiology, 2d ed)

name: problems and exercises
query: Query: problems and exercises [SEP] Problems and exercises is works consisting of collections of practice questions and drills, generally for instructional or review use.

name: procedures and techniques utilization
query: Query: procedures and techniques utilization [SEP] Procedures and techniques utilization is extent of use of procedures or techniques. It includes overuse and underuse.

name: product labeling
query: Query: product labeling [SEP] Product labeling is use of written, printed, or graphic materials upon or accompanying a product or its container or wrapper. It includes purpose, effect, description, directions, hazards, warnings, and other relevant information.

name: product line management
query: Query: product line management [SEP] Product line management is management control systems for structuring health care delivery strategies around case types, as in DRGs, or specific clinical services.

name: professional autonomy
query: Query: professional autonomy [SEP] Professional autonomy is the quality or state of being independent and self-directing, especially in making decisions, enabling professionals to exercise judgment as they see fit during the performance of their jobs.

name: professional corporations
query: Query: professional corporations [SEP] Professional corporations is legally authorized corporations owned and managed by one or more professionals (medical, dental, legal) in which the income is ascribed primarily to the professional activities of the owners or stockholders.

name: professional or occupational group
query: Query: professional or occupational group [SEP] Professional or occupational group is professional or occupational group

name: professional practice gaps
query: Query: professional practice gaps [SEP] Professional practice gaps is difference between observed and ideal delivery of health care and healthcare outcomes that reflect the current state of knowledge.

name: professional practice location
query: Query: professional practice location [SEP] Professional practice location is geographic area in which a professional person practices; includes primarily physicians and dentists.

name: professional review organizations
query: Query: professional review organizations [SEP] Professional review organizations is organizations representing designated geographic areas which have contracts under the pro program to review the medical necessity, appropriateness, quality, and cost-effectiveness of care received by Medicare beneficiaries. Peer Review Improvement Act, pl 97-248, 1982.

name: professional society
query: Query: professional society [SEP] Professional society is organizations composed of members with common interests and whose professions may be similar.

name: programmed instruction
query: Query: programmed instruction [SEP] Programmed instruction is works consisting of sequenced self-correction texts.

name: programming , linear
query: Query: programming , linear [SEP] Linear programming is a technique of operations research for solving certain kinds of problems involving many variables where a best value or [MASK] of best values is to be found. It is most likely to be feasible when the quantity to be optimized, sometimes called the objective function, can be stated as a mathematical expression in terms of the various activities within the system, and when this expression is simply proportional to the measure of the activities, i.e., is linear, and when all the restrictions are also linear. It is different from computer programming, although problems using linear programming techniques may be programmed on a computer.

name: programming languages
query: Query: programming languages [SEP] Programming languages is specific languages used to prepare computer programs.

name: progressive patient care
query: Query: progressive patient care [SEP] Progressive patient care is organization of medical and nursing care according to the degree of illness and care requirements in the hospital. The elements are intensive care, intermediate care, self-care, long-term care, and organized home care.

name: prolactin
query: Query: prolactin [SEP] Prolactin is a lactogenic hormone secreted by the adenohypophysis (pituitary gland, anterior). It is a polypeptide of approximately 23 kD. Besides its major action on lactation, in some species prolactin exerts effects on reproduction, maternal behavior, fat metabolism, immunomodulation and osmoregulation. Prolactin receptors are present in the mammary gland, hypothalamus, liver, ovary, testis, and prostate.

name: proliferating cell nuclear antigen
query: Query: proliferating cell nuclear antigen [SEP] Proliferating cell nuclear antigen is nuclear antigen with a role in dna synthesis, dna repair, and cell cycle progression. pcna is required for the coordinated synthesis of both leading and lagging strands at the replication fork during dna replication. pcna expression correlates with the proliferation activity of several malignant and non-malignant cell types.

name: prone position
query: Query: prone position [SEP] Prone position is the posture of an individual lying face down.

name: proportional hazards models
query: Query: proportional hazards models [SEP] Proportional hazards models is statistical models used in survival analysis that assert that the effect of the study factors on the hazard rate in the study population is multiplicative and does not change over time.

name: prospective payment assessment commission
query: Query: prospective payment assessment commission [SEP] Prospective payment assessment commission is the commission charged with evaluating issues and factors which affect the implementation of the prospective payment system.

name: prospective studies
query: Query: prospective studies [SEP] Prospective studies is [MASK] of a population for a sufficient number of persons over a sufficient number of years to generate incidence or mortality rates subsequent to the selection of the study group.

name: prostatic hyperplasia
query: Query: prostatic hyperplasia [SEP] Prostatic hyperplasia is increase in constituent cells in the prostate, leading to enlargement of the organ (hypertrophy) and adverse impact on the lower urinary tract function. This can be caused by increased rate of cell proliferation, reduced rate of cell death, or both.

name: prostatic neoplasms
query: Query: prostatic neoplasms [SEP] Prostatic neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the prostate.

name: prosthesis coloring
query: Query: prosthesis coloring [SEP] Prosthesis coloring is coloring, shading, or tinting of prosthetic components, devices, and materials.

name: prosthesis failure
query: Query: prosthesis failure [SEP] Prosthesis failure is malfunction of implantation shunts, valves, etc., and prosthesis loosening, migration, and breaking.

name: prosthesis retention
query: Query: prosthesis retention [SEP] Prosthesis retention is holding a prosthesis in place.

name: proteasome inhibitors
query: Query: proteasome inhibitors [SEP] Proteasome inhibitors is compounds that inhibit the function or proteolytic action of the proteasome.

name: protein aggregation , pathological
query: Query: protein aggregation , pathological [SEP] Pathological protein aggregation is a biochemical phenomenon in which misfolded proteins aggregate either intra- or extracellularly. Triggered by factors such as mutation; post-translational modifications, and environmental stress, it is generally associated with alzheimer disease; parkinson disease; huntington disease; and type 2 diabetes mellitus.

name: protein array analysis
query: Query: protein array analysis [SEP] Protein array analysis is ligand-binding assays that measure protein-protein, protein-small molecule, or protein-nucleic acid interactions using a very large [MASK] of capturing molecules, i.e., those attached separately on a solid support, to measure the presence or interaction of target molecules in the sample.

name: proteinase inhibitory proteins , secretory
query: Query: proteinase inhibitory proteins , secretory [SEP] Secretory proteinase inhibitory proteins is peptides and proteins found in bodily secretions and body fluids that are protease inhibitors. They play a role in inflammation, tissue repair and innate immunity (immunity, innate) by inhibiting endogenous proteinases such as those produced by leukocytes and exogenous proteases such as those produced by invading microorganisms.

name: protein binding
query: Query: protein binding [SEP] Protein binding is the process in which substances, either endogenous or exogenous, bind to proteins, peptides, enzymes, protein precursors, or allied compounds. Specific protein-binding measures are often used as assays in diagnostic assessments.

name: protein c
query: Query: protein c [SEP] Protein c is a vitamin-K dependent zymogen present in the blood, which, upon activation by thrombin and thrombomodulin exerts anticoagulant properties by inactivating factors Va and VIIIa at the rate-limiting steps of thrombin formation.

name: protein c deficiency
query: Query: protein c deficiency [SEP] Protein c deficiency is an absence or deficiency in protein c which leads to impaired regulation of blood coagulation. It is associated with an increased risk of severe or premature thrombosis. (Stedman's Med. Dict., 26th ed.)

name: protein interaction maps
query: Query: protein interaction maps [SEP] Protein interaction maps is graphs representing sets of measurable, non-covalent physical contacts with specific proteins in living organisms or in cells.

name: protein isoforms
query: Query: protein isoforms [SEP] Protein isoforms is different forms of a protein that may be produced from different genes, or from the same gene by [MASK].

name: protein kinase c beta
query: Query: protein kinase c beta [SEP] Protein kinase c beta is pkc beta encodes two proteins (pkcb1 and pkcbii) generated by [MASK] of C-terminal exons. It is widely distributed with wide-ranging roles in processes such as B-cell receptor regulation, oxidative stress-induced apoptosis, androgen receptor-dependent transcriptional regulation, insulin signaling, and endothelial cell proliferation.

name: protein kinase inhibitors
query: Query: protein kinase inhibitors [SEP] Protein kinase inhibitors is agents that inhibit protein kinases.

name: protein modification , translational
query: Query: protein modification , translational [SEP] Translational protein modification is any of the enzymatically catalyzed modifications of the individual amino acids of proteins, and enzymatic cleavage or crosslinking of peptide chains that occur pre-translationally (on the amino acid component of [MASK]), co-translationally (during the process of genetic translation), or after translation is completed (post-translational protein processing).

name: protein phosphatase 2
query: Query: protein phosphatase 2 [SEP] Protein phosphatase 2 is a phosphoprotein phosphatase subtype that is comprised of a [MASK] and two different regulatory subunits. At least two genes encode isoforms of the protein phosphatase [MASK], while several isoforms of regulatory subunits exist due to the presence of multiple genes and the [MASK] of their mRNAs. Protein phosphatase 2 acts on a broad variety of cellular proteins and may play a role as a regulator of intracellular signaling processes.

name: protein s deficiency
query: Query: protein s deficiency [SEP] Protein s deficiency is an autosomal dominant disorder showing decreased levels of plasma protein s antigen or activity, associated with venous thrombosis and pulmonary embolism. protein s is a vitamin K-dependent plasma protein that inhibits blood clotting by serving as a cofactor for activated protein c (also a vitamin K-dependent protein), and the clinical manifestations of its deficiency are virtually identical to those of protein c deficiency. Treatment with heparin for acute thrombotic processes is usually followed by maintenance administration of coumarin drugs for the prevention of recurrent thrombosis. (From Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 12th ed, p1511; Wintrobe's Clinical Hematology, 9th ed, p1523)

name: protein structure , quaternary
query: Query: protein structure , quaternary [SEP] Quaternary protein structure is the characteristic 3-dimensional shape and arrangement of multimeric proteins (aggregates of more than one polypeptide chain).

name: protein subunits
query: Query: protein subunits [SEP] Protein subunits is single chains of amino acids that are the units of multimeric proteins. Multimeric proteins can be composed of identical or non-identical subunits. One or more monomeric subunits may compose a protomer which itself is a subunit structure of a larger assembly.

name: protein synthesis inhibitors
query: Query: protein synthesis inhibitors [SEP] Protein synthesis inhibitors is compounds which inhibit the synthesis of proteins. They are usually anti-bacterial agents or toxins. Mechanism of the action of inhibition includes the interruption of peptide-chain elongation, the blocking the a site of ribosomes, the misreading of the genetic code or the prevention of the attachment of oligosaccharide side chains to glycoproteins.

name: proteolysis
query: Query: proteolysis [SEP] Proteolysis is cleavage of proteins into smaller peptides or amino acids either by proteases or non-enzymatically (e.g., Hydrolysis). It does not include Protein Processing, Post-Translational.

name: proteome
query: Query: proteome [SEP] Proteome is the protein complement of an organism coded for by its genome.

name: proteomics
query: Query: proteomics [SEP] Proteomics is the systematic study of the complete complement of proteins (proteome) of organisms.

name: protons
query: Query: protons [SEP] Protons is stable elementary particles having the smallest known positive charge, found in the nuclei of all elements. The proton mass is less than that of a neutron. a proton is the nucleus of the light hydrogen atom, i.e., the hydrogen ion.

name: proton therapy
query: Query: proton therapy [SEP] Proton therapy is the use of an external beam of protons as radiotherapy.

name: pseudomonas vaccines
query: Query: pseudomonas vaccines [SEP] Pseudomonas vaccines is vaccines or candidate vaccines used to prevent or treat pseudomonas infections.

name: psychiatric department , hospital
query: Query: psychiatric department , hospital [SEP] Hospital psychiatric department is hospital department responsible for the organization and administration of psychiatric services.

name: psychiatric rehabilitation
query: Query: psychiatric rehabilitation [SEP] Psychiatric rehabilitation is specialty field that promotes recovery, community functioning, and increased well-being of individuals diagnosed with mental disorders that impair their ability to live meaningful lives.

name: psychiatric somatic therapies
query: Query: psychiatric somatic therapies [SEP] Psychiatric somatic therapies is the biologic treatment of mental disorders (e.g., electroconvulsive therapy), in contrast with psychotherapy. (Stone, American Psychiatric Glossary, 1988, p159)

name: psychiatry in literature
query: Query: psychiatry in literature [SEP] Psychiatry in literature is written or other literary works whose subject matter is related to mental disorders or psychiatry from the lay or practitioner perspective.

name: psychological distress
query: Query: psychological distress [SEP] Psychological distress is negative emotional state characterized by physical and/or emotional discomfort, pain, or anguish.

name: psychology , child
query: Query: psychology , child [SEP] Child psychology is branch of psychology involving the study of normal and abnormal behavior of children.

name: psychology , clinical
query: Query: psychology , clinical [SEP] Clinical psychology is the branch of psychology concerned with psychological methods of recognizing and treating behavior disorders.

name: psychology , medical
query: Query: psychology , medical [SEP] Medical psychology is a branch of psychology in which there is collaboration between psychologists and physicians in the management of medical problems. It differs from clinical psychology, which is concerned with the diagnosis and treatment of behavior disorders.

name: psychology , positive
query: Query: psychology , positive [SEP] Positive psychology is the scientific study of the strengths that enable individuals and communities to thrive. It is founded on the belief that people want to lead meaningful and fulfilling lives, to cultivate what is best within themselves, and to enhance their experiences of love, work, and play. (https://ppc.sas.upenn.edu/)

name: psychology , sports
query: Query: psychology , sports [SEP] Sports psychology is field of research that studies mental factors influencing the attainment of athletic skills and athletic performance.

name: psychopathology
query: Query: psychopathology [SEP] Psychopathology is the study of significant causes and processes in the development of mental illness.

name: psychosocial deprivation
query: Query: psychosocial deprivation [SEP] Psychosocial deprivation is the absence of appropriate stimuli in the physical or social environment which are necessary for the emotional, social, and intellectual development of the individual.

name: psychosocial support systems
query: Query: psychosocial support systems [SEP] Psychosocial support systems is organized efforts to address ongoing psychological and social problems of individuals, their partners, families and caregivers.

name: psychotic disorders
query: Query: psychotic disorders [SEP] Psychotic disorders is disorders in which there is a loss of ego boundaries or a gross impairment in reality testing with delusions or prominent hallucinations. (From [MASK], 1994)

name: puberty
query: Query: puberty [SEP] Puberty is a period in the human life in which the development of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal system takes place and reaches full maturity. The onset of synchronized endocrine events in puberty lead to the capacity for reproduction (fertility), development of secondary [MASK] characteristics, and other changes seen in adolescent development.

name: public expenditures
query: Query: public expenditures [SEP] Public expenditures is expenses of public funds incurred by government bodies:  state, regional and local.

name: public health informatics
query: Query: public health informatics [SEP] Public health informatics is the systematic application of information and computer sciences to public health practice, research, and learning.

name: public health surveillance
query: Query: public health surveillance [SEP] Public health surveillance is the ongoing, systematic collection, analysis, and interpretation of health-related data with the purpose of preventing or controlling disease or injury, or of identifying unusual events of public health importance, followed by the dissemination and use of information for public health action. (From Am j Prev Med 2011;41(6):636)

name: public housing
query: Query: public housing [SEP] Public housing is housing subsidized by tax funds, usually intended for low income persons or families.

name: public opinion
query: Query: public opinion [SEP] Public opinion is the attitude of a significant portion of a population toward any given proposition, based upon a measurable amount of factual evidence, and involving some degree of reflection, analysis, and reasoning.

name: public reporting of healthcare data
query: Query: public reporting of healthcare data [SEP] Public reporting of healthcare data is required public availability of quality indicators data from health facilities.

name: public service announcement
query: Query: public service announcement [SEP] Public service announcement is work consisting of announcements which promote programs, activities, or services of federal, state, or local governments or those of non-profit organizations and other announcements regarded as serving community interests.

name: pulmonary gas exchange
query: Query: pulmonary gas exchange [SEP] Pulmonary gas exchange is the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide between alveolar air and pulmonary capillary blood that occurs across the blood-air barrier.

name: pulmonary heart disease
query: Query: pulmonary heart disease [SEP] Pulmonary heart disease is hypertrophy and dilation of the right ventricle of the heart that is caused by pulmonary hypertension. This condition is often associated with pulmonary parenchymal or vascular diseases, such as [MASK] and pulmonary embolism.

name: pulmonary infarction
query: Query: pulmonary infarction [SEP] Pulmonary infarction is necrosis of lung tissue that is cause by the lack of oxygen or blood supply. The most common cause of pulmonary infarction is a blood clot in the lung.

name: pulmonary medicine
query: Query: pulmonary medicine [SEP] Pulmonary medicine is a subspecialty of internal medicine concerned with the study of the respiratory system. It is especially concerned with diagnosis and treatment of diseases and defects of the lungs and bronchial tree.

name: pulmonary surfactants
query: Query: pulmonary surfactants [SEP] Pulmonary surfactants is substances and drugs that lower the [MASK] of the mucoid layer lining the pulmonary alveoli.

name: pulmonary valve
query: Query: pulmonary valve [SEP] Pulmonary valve is a valve situated at the entrance to the pulmonary trunk from the right ventricle.

name: pulmonary valve insufficiency
query: Query: pulmonary valve insufficiency [SEP] Pulmonary valve insufficiency is backflow of blood from the [MASK] into the right ventricle due to imperfect closure of the pulmonary valve.

name: pulmonary valve stenosis
query: Query: pulmonary valve stenosis [SEP] Pulmonary valve stenosis is the pathologic narrowing of the orifice of the pulmonary valve. This lesion restricts blood outflow from the right ventricle to the [MASK]. When the trileaflet valve is fused into an imperforate membrane, the blockage is complete.

name: pulmonary veins
query: Query: pulmonary veins [SEP] Pulmonary veins is the veins that return the oxygenated blood from the lungs to the left atrium of the heart.

name: pulse
query: Query: pulse [SEP] Pulse is the rhythmical expansion and contraction of an artery produced by waves of pressure caused by the ejection of blood from the left ventricle of the heart as it contracts.

name: punishment
query: Query: punishment [SEP] Punishment is the application of an unpleasant stimulus or penalty for the purpose of eliminating or correcting undesirable behavior.

name: pupil
query: Query: pupil [SEP] Pupil is the aperture in the iris through which light passes.

name: purple membrane
query: Query: purple membrane [SEP] Purple membrane is functionally and structurally differentiated, purple-pigmented regions of the cytoplasmic membrane of some strains of Halobacterium halobium. The membrane develops under anaerobic conditions and is made almost entirely of the purple pigment bacteriorhodopsins. (From Singleton & Sainsbury Dictionary of Microbiology and Molecular Biology, 2d ed)

name: pyramidal tracts
query: Query: pyramidal tracts [SEP] Pyramidal tracts is fibers that arise from cells within the cerebral cortex, pass through the medullary pyramid, and descend in the spinal cord. Many authorities say the pyramidal tracts include both the corticospinal and corticobulbar tracts.

name: pyrolysis
query: Query: pyrolysis [SEP] Pyrolysis is high temperature decomposition without addition of extra air or oxygen. It yields syngas, bio-oil and bio-char.

name: pyruvate dehydrogenase complex deficiency disease
query: Query: pyruvate dehydrogenase complex deficiency disease [SEP] Pyruvate dehydrogenase complex deficiency disease is an inherited metabolic disorder caused by deficient enzyme activity in the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex, resulting in deficiency of acetyl CoA and reduced synthesis of acetylcholine. Two clinical forms are recognized: neonatal and juvenile. The neonatal form is a relatively common cause of [MASK] in the first weeks of life and may also feature an erythematous rash. The juvenile form presents with [MASK], alopecia, intermittent ataxia; seizures; and an erythematous rash. (From j Inherit Metab Dis 1996;19(4):452-62) Autosomal recessive and X-linked forms are caused by mutations in the genes for the three different enzyme components of this multisubunit pyruvate dehydrogenase complex. One of the mutations at Xp22.2-p22.1 in the gene for the e1 alpha component of the complex leads to leigh disease.

name: qualitative concept
query: Query: qualitative concept [SEP] Qualitative concept is works about studies that determine the effectiveness or value of processes, personnel, and equipment, or the material on conducting such studies.

name: qualitative research
query: Query: qualitative research [SEP] Qualitative research is any type of research that employs nonnumeric information to explore individual or group characteristics, producing findings not arrived at by statistical procedures or other quantitative means. (Qualitative Inquiry: a Dictionary of Terms Thousand Oaks, ca: Sage Publications, 1997)

name: quantitative concept
query: Query: quantitative concept [SEP] Quantitative concept is quantitative concept

name: quantum dots
query: Query: quantum dots [SEP] Quantum dots is nanometer sized fragments of semiconductor crystalline material which emit [MASK]. The wavelength is based on the quantum confinement size of the dot. They can be embedded in microbeads for high throughput analytical chemistry techniques.

name: quartz
query: Query: quartz [SEP] Quartz is quartz (SiO2). a glassy or crystalline form of silicon dioxide. Many colored varieties are semiprecious stones. (From Grant & Hackh's Chemical Dictionary, 5th ed)

name: quaternary prevention
query: Query: quaternary prevention [SEP] Quaternary prevention is actions taken to protect individuals (i.e. persons/patients) from unnecessary medical interventions that are likely to cause more harm than good.

name: queensland
query: Query: queensland [SEP] Queensland is a state in northeastern Australia. Its capital is Brisbane. Its coast was first visited by Captain Cook in 1770 and its first settlement (penal) was located on Moreton Bay in 1824. The name Cooksland was first proposed but honor to Queen Victoria prevailed. (From Webster's New Geographical Dictionary, 1988, p996 & Room, Brewer's Dictionary of Names, 1992, p441)

name: race factors
query: Query: race factors [SEP] Race factors is a constituent element or influence that could be used in studies for racial disparities as variables such as those related to risk factors and disease and or differential access to services.

name: race relations
query: Query: race relations [SEP] Race relations is cultural contacts between people of different races.

name: radial nerve
query: Query: radial nerve [SEP] Radial nerve is a major nerve of the upper extremity. In humans the fibers of the radial nerve originate in the lower cervical and upper thoracic spinal cord (usually c5 to t1), travel via the posterior cord of the brachial plexus, and supply motor innervation to extensor muscles of the [MASK] and cutaneous sensory fibers to extensor regions of the [MASK] and hand.

name: radiation genetics
query: Query: radiation genetics [SEP] Radiation genetics is a subdiscipline of genetics that studies radiation effects on the components and processes of biological inheritance.

name: radiation hybrid mapping
query: Query: radiation hybrid mapping [SEP] Radiation hybrid mapping is a method for ordering genetic loci along chromosomes. The method involves fusing irradiated donor cells with host cells from another species. Following cell fusion, fragments of dna from the irradiated cells become integrated into the chromosomes of the host cells. Molecular probing of dna obtained from the fused cells is used to determine if two or more genetic loci are located within the same fragment of donor cell dna.

name: radiation injuries , experimental
query: Query: radiation injuries , experimental [SEP] Experimental radiation injuries is experimentally produced harmful effects of ionizing or non-ionizing radiation in chordata animals.

name: radiation leukemia virus
query: Query: radiation leukemia virus [SEP] Radiation leukemia virus is a strain of Murine leukemia virus (leukemia virus, murine) isolated from radiation-induced lymphomas in c57bl mice. It is leukemogenic, thymotrophic, can be transmitted vertically, and replicates only in vivo.

name: radio
query: Query: radio [SEP] Radio is the transmission and reception of electric impulses or signals by means of electric waves without a connecting wire, or the use of these waves for the wireless transmission of electric impulses into which sound is converted. (From Webster's 3d)

name: radioactive hazard release
query: Query: radioactive hazard release [SEP] Radioactive hazard release is uncontrolled release of radioactive material from its containment. This either threatens to, or does, cause exposure to a radioactive hazard. Such an incident may occur accidentally or deliberately.

name: radioactivity
query: Query: radioactivity [SEP] Radioactivity is the spontaneous transformation of a nuclide into one or more different nuclides, accompanied by either the emission of particles from the nucleus, nuclear capture or ejection of orbital [MASK], or fission. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

name: radio frequency identification device
query: Query: radio frequency identification device [SEP] Radio frequency identification device is machine readable patient or equipment identification device using radio frequency from 125 kHz to 5.8 Ghz.

name: radiography , abdominal
query: Query: radiography , abdominal [SEP] Abdominal radiography is radiographic visualization of the body between the thorax and the pelvis, i.e., within the peritoneal cavity.

name: radiography , dental , digital
query: Query: radiography , dental , digital [SEP] Digital dental radiography is a rapid, low-dose, digital imaging system using a small intraoral sensor instead of radiographic film, an intensifying screen, and a charge-coupled device. It presents the possibility of reduced patient exposure and minimal distortion, although resolution and latitude are inferior to standard dental radiography. a receiver is placed in the mouth, routing signals to a computer which images the signals on a screen or in print. It includes digitizing from x-ray film or any other detector. (From medline [MASK]; personal communication from Dr. Charles Berthold, nidr)

name: radiography , interventional
query: Query: radiography , interventional [SEP] Interventional radiography is diagnostic and therapeutic procedures that are invasive or surgical in nature, and require the expertise of a specially trained radiologist. In general, they are more invasive than diagnostic imaging but less invasive than major surgery. They often involve catheterization, fluoroscopy, or computed tomography. Some examples include percutaneous transhepatic cholangiography, percutaneous transthoracic biopsy, balloon angioplasty, and arterial embolization.

name: radiography , thoracic
query: Query: radiography , thoracic [SEP] Thoracic radiography is x-ray visualization of the chest and organs of the thoracic cavity. It is not restricted to visualization of the lungs.

name: radiologists
query: Query: radiologists [SEP] Radiologists is physicians specializing in the use of x-ray and other forms of radiant energy to diagnose and treat disease.

name: radiology department , hospital
query: Query: radiology department , hospital [SEP] Hospital radiology department is hospital department which is responsible for the administration and provision of x-ray diagnostic and therapeutic services.

name: radiology information systems
query: Query: radiology information systems [SEP] Radiology information systems is information systems, usually computer-assisted, designed to store, manipulate, and retrieve information for planning, organizing, directing, and controlling administrative activities associated with the provision and utilization of radiology services and facilities.

name: radiotherapy , adjuvant
query: Query: radiotherapy , adjuvant [SEP] Adjuvant radiotherapy is radiotherapy given to augment some other form of treatment such as surgery or chemotherapy. Adjuvant radiotherapy is commonly used in the therapy of cancer and can be administered before or after the primary treatment.

name: radio waves
query: Query: radio waves [SEP] Radio waves is electromagnetic waves with frequencies between about 3 kilohertz (very low frequency - vlf) and 300,000 megahertz (extremely high frequency - ehf). They are used in television and radio broadcasting, land and satellite communications systems, radionavigation, radiolocation, and diathermy. The highest frequency radio waves are microwaves.

name: raf kinases
query: Query: raf kinases [SEP] Raf kinases is a family of closely-related serine-threonine kinases that were originally identified as the cellular homologs of the retrovirus-derived v-raf kinases. They are map kinase kinase kinases that play important roles in signal transduction.

name: ral guanine nucleotide exchange factor
query: Query: ral guanine nucleotide exchange factor [SEP] Ral guanine nucleotide exchange factor is a guanine nucleotide exchange factor that stimulates the dissociation of gdp from ral gtp-binding proteins. It also has gdp exchange activity towards other monomeric gtp-binding proteins.

name: random allocation
query: Query: random allocation [SEP] Random allocation is a process involving chance used in therapeutic trials or other research endeavor for allocating experimental subjects, human or animal, between treatment and control groups, or among treatment groups. It may also apply to experiments on inanimate objects.

name: random amplified polymorphic dna technique
query: Query: random amplified polymorphic dna technique [SEP] Random amplified polymorphic dna technique is technique that utilizes low-stringency polymerase chain reaction (pcr) amplification with single primers of arbitrary sequence to generate strain-specific arrays of anonymous dna fragments. rapd technique may be used to determine taxonomic identity, assess kinship relationships, analyze mixed genome samples, and create specific probes.

name: randomized controlled trial , veterinary
query: Query: randomized controlled trial , veterinary [SEP] Veterinary randomized controlled trial is a work that reports on a clinical trial with animal subjects that involves at least one test treatment and one control treatment, concurrent enrollment and follow-up of the test- and control-treated groups, and in which the treatments to be administered are selected by a random process, such as the use of a random-numbers [MASK].

name: range of motion , articular
query: Query: range of motion , articular [SEP] Articular range of motion is the distance and direction to which a bone joint can be extended. Range of motion is a function of the condition of the joints, muscles, and connective tissues involved. Joint flexibility can be improved through appropriate muscle stretching exercises.

name: rank ligand
query: Query: rank ligand [SEP] Rank ligand is a transmembrane protein belonging to the tumor necrosis factor superfamily that specifically binds receptor activator of nuclear factor-kappa b and osteoprotegerin. It plays an important role in regulating osteoclast differentiation and activation.

name: rape
query: Query: rape [SEP] Rape is sexual intercourse without consent of the victim.

name: rare books
query: Query: rare books [SEP] Rare books is books that are limited in availability, have early printing dates or special characteristics that increase the value of an individual copy, print run, or edition.

name: rare diseases
query: Query: rare diseases [SEP] Rare diseases is a large group of diseases which are characterized by a low [MASK] in the population. They frequently are associated with problems in diagnosis and treatment.

name: ras guanine nucleotide exchange factors
query: Query: ras guanine nucleotide exchange factors [SEP] Ras guanine nucleotide exchange factors is a family of guanine nucleotide exchange factors that are specific for ras proteins.

name: rate setting and review
query: Query: rate setting and review [SEP] Rate setting and review is a method of examining and setting levels of payments.

name: rats , inbred bn
query: Query: rats , inbred bn [SEP] Inbred bn rats is an inbred strain of rat that is widely used in a variety of research areas such as the study of asthma; carcinogenesis; aging; and leukemia.

name: rats , inbred lec
query: Query: rats , inbred lec [SEP] Inbred lec rats is a cinnamon-colored strain of Long-Evans rats which carries a mutation causing [MASK] and jaundice, with an associated gross accumulation of [MASK] in the liver. This strain is a model for Wilson's Disease (see hepatolenticular degeneration).

name: rats , inbred shr
query: Query: rats , inbred shr [SEP] Inbred shr rats is a strain of Rattus norvegicus with elevated blood pressure used as a model for studying hypertension and stroke.

name: rats , inbred wf
query: Query: rats , inbred wf [SEP] Inbred wf rats is an inbred strain of rat that is used in biomedical research.

name: rats , nude
query: Query: rats , nude [SEP] Nude rats is a mutant strain of Rattus norvegicus without a thymus and with depressed or absent T-cell function. This strain of rats may have a small amount of hair at times, but then lose it.

name: rats , wistar
query: Query: rats , wistar [SEP] Wistar rats is a strain of albino rat developed at the Wistar Institute that has spread widely at other institutions. This has markedly diluted the original strain.

name: raw foods
query: Query: raw foods [SEP] Raw foods is food prepared for consumption without exposure to heat.

name: reactive inhibition
query: Query: reactive inhibition [SEP] Reactive inhibition is tendency toward a lessened strength of response due to practice or activity. It is independent of the effect of reward and is a direct function of time interval since the last response and the number of preceding responses.

name: reading
query: Query: reading [SEP] Reading is acquiring information from text.

name: reagent strips
query: Query: reagent strips [SEP] Reagent strips is narrow pieces of material impregnated or covered with a substance used to produce a chemical reaction. The strips are used in detecting, measuring, producing, etc., other substances. (From Dorland, 28th ed)

name: reality testing
query: Query: reality testing [SEP] Reality testing is the individual's objective evaluation of the external world and the ability to differentiate adequately between it and the internal world; considered to be a primary ego function.

name: receptor
query: Query: receptor [SEP] Receptor is a molecule inside or on the surface of a cell that binds to a specific substance and causes a specific effect in the cell.

name: receptor , angiotensin , type 1
query: Query: receptor , angiotensin , type 1 [SEP] Type 1 angiotensin receptor is an angiotensin receptor subtype that is expressed at high levels in a variety of adult tissues including the cardiovascular system, the kidney, the endocrine system and the nervous system. Activation of the type 1 angiotensin receptor causes vasoconstriction and sodium retention.

name: receptor , angiotensin , type 2
query: Query: receptor , angiotensin , type 2 [SEP] Type 2 angiotensin receptor is an angiotensin receptor subtype that is expressed at high levels in fetal tissues. Many effects of the angiotensin type 2 receptor such as vasodilation and sodium loss are the opposite of that of the angiotensin type 1 receptor.

name: receptor , fibroblast growth factor , type 1
query: Query: receptor , fibroblast growth factor , type 1 [SEP] Type 1 fibroblast growth factor receptor is a fibroblast growth factor receptor with specificity for fibroblast growth factors; heparan sulfate proteoglycan; and neuronal cell adhesion molecules. Several variants of the receptor exist due to multiple [MASK] of its mRNA. Fibroblast growth factor receptor 1 contains three extracellular immunoglobulin c2-[MASK] domains and is a tyrosine kinase that transmits signals through the [MASK].

name: receptor , fibroblast growth factor , type 2
query: Query: receptor , fibroblast growth factor , type 2 [SEP] Type 2 fibroblast growth factor receptor is a fibroblast growth factor receptor which contains three extracellular immunoglobulin i-[MASK] domains and is expressed as two isoforms. One receptor isoform is expressed in the mesenchyme and is activated by fibroblast growth factor 2. a second isoform is expressed mainly by epithelial cells and is activated by fibroblast growth [MASK] and [MASK]. Mutation of the gene for fibroblast growth factor receptor 2 can result in craniosynostotic syndromes (e.g., apert syndrome; and crouzon syndrome).

name: receptor , fibroblast growth factor , type 3
query: Query: receptor , fibroblast growth factor , type 3 [SEP] Type 3 fibroblast growth factor receptor is a fibroblast growth factor receptor that regulates chondrocyte growth and cell differentiation. Mutations in the gene for fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 have been associated with achondroplasia; thanatophoric dysplasia and neoplastic cell transformation.

name: receptor , fibroblast growth factor , type 5
query: Query: receptor , fibroblast growth factor , type 5 [SEP] Type 5 fibroblast growth factor receptor is the most divergent of the known fibroblast growth factor receptors. It does not contain an intracellular tyrosine kinase domain and has been shown to interact with fibroblast growth factor 2. Fibroblast growth factor receptor 5 is found primarily in skeletal tissue.

name: receptor , insulin
query: Query: receptor , insulin [SEP] Insulin receptor is a cell surface receptor for insulin. It comprises a tetramer of two alpha and two beta subunits which are derived from cleavage of a single precursor protein. The receptor contains an intrinsic tyrosine kinase domain that is located within the beta subunit. Activation of the receptor by insulin results in numerous metabolic changes including increased uptake of glucose into the liver, muscle, and adipose tissue.

name: receptor , parathyroid hormone , type 1
query: Query: receptor , parathyroid hormone , type 1 [SEP] Type 1 parathyroid hormone receptor is a parathyroid hormone receptor subtype that recognizes both parathyroid hormone and parathyroid hormone-related protein. It is a G-protein-coupled receptor that is expressed at high levels in bone and in kidney.

name: receptor , parathyroid hormone , type 2
query: Query: receptor , parathyroid hormone , type 2 [SEP] Type 2 parathyroid hormone receptor is a parathyroid hormone receptor subtype found in the brain and the pancreas. It is a G-protein-coupled receptor with a ligand specificity that varies between homologs from different species.

name: receptor aggregation
query: Query: receptor aggregation [SEP] Receptor aggregation is chemically stimulated aggregation of cell surface receptors, which potentiates the action of the effector cell.

name: receptors , androgen
query: Query: receptors , androgen [SEP] Androgen receptors is proteins, generally found in the cytoplasm, that specifically bind androgens and mediate their cellular actions. The complex of the androgen and receptor migrates to the cell nucleus where it induces transcription of specific segments of dna.

name: receptors , aryl hydrocarbon
query: Query: receptors , aryl hydrocarbon [SEP] Aryl hydrocarbon receptors is cytoplasmic proteins that bind certain aryl hydrocarbons, translocate to the nucleus, and activate transcription of particular dna segments. ah receptors are identified by their high-affinity binding to several carcinogenic or teratogenic environmental chemicals including polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons found in [MASK] smoke and smog, heterocyclic amines found in cooked foods, and halogenated hydrocarbons including dioxins and polychlorinated biphenyls. No endogenous ligand has been identified, but an unknown natural messenger with a role in cell differentiation and development is suspected.

name: receptors , ccr
query: Query: receptors , ccr [SEP] Ccr receptors is chemokine receptors that are specific for [MASK].

name: receptors , chimeric antigen
query: Query: receptors , chimeric antigen [SEP] Chimeric antigen receptors is synthetic cellular receptors that reprogram t-lymphocytes to selectively bind antigens.

name: receptors , collagen
query: Query: receptors , collagen [SEP] Collagen receptors is cell surface receptors that modulate signal transduction between cells and the extracellular matrix. They are found in many cell types and are involved in the maintenance and regulation of cell shape and behavior, including platelet activation and aggregation, through many different signaling pathways and differences in their affinities for collagen isoforms. Collagen receptors include discoidin domain receptors; integrins; and gp6, one of the platelet membrane glycoproteins.

name: receptors , cxcr
query: Query: receptors , cxcr [SEP] Cxcr receptors is chemokine receptors that are specific for cxc chemokines.

name: receptors , estradiol
query: Query: receptors , estradiol [SEP] Estradiol receptors is cytoplasmic proteins that bind estradiol, migrate to the nucleus, and regulate dna transcription.

name: receptors , gaba
query: Query: receptors , gaba [SEP] Gaba receptors is cell-surface proteins that bind gamma-aminobutyric acid with high affinity and trigger changes that influence the behavior of cells. gaba-a receptors control chloride channels formed by the receptor complex itself. They are blocked by bicuculline and usually have modulatory sites sensitive to benzodiazepines and barbiturates. gaba-b receptors act through G-proteins on several effector systems, are insensitive to bicuculline, and have a high affinity for L-baclofen.

name: receptors , glucagon
query: Query: receptors , glucagon [SEP] Glucagon receptors is cell surface receptors that bind glucagon with high affinity and trigger intracellular changes which influence the behavior of cells. Activation of glucagon receptors causes a variety of effects; the best understood is the initiation of a complex enzymatic cascade in the liver which ultimately increases the availability of glucose to body organs.

name: receptors , hiv
query: Query: receptors , hiv [SEP] Hiv receptors is cellular receptors that bind the human immunodeficiency virus that causes aids. Included are cd4 antigens, found on t4 lymphocytes, and monocytes/macrophages, which bind to the hiv envelope protein gp120.

name: receptors , ige
query: Query: receptors , ige [SEP] Ige receptors is specific molecular sites on the surface of b- and T-lymphocytes which combine with IgEs. Two subclasses exist: low affinity receptors (Fc epsilon rii) and high affinity receptors (Fc epsilon ri).

name: receptors , interferon
query: Query: receptors , interferon [SEP] Interferon receptors is specific molecular sites or structures on or in cells with which interferons react or to which they bind in order to modify the function of the cells. Interferons exert their pleiotropic effects through two different receptors. alpha- and beta-interferon crossreact with common receptors, while gamma-interferon initiates its biological effects through its own specific receptor system.

name: receptors , interleukin
query: Query: receptors , interleukin [SEP] Interleukin receptors is cell surface proteins that bind interleukins and trigger intracellular changes influencing the behavior of cells.

name: receptors , kir
query: Query: receptors , kir [SEP] Kir receptors is a family of receptors found on nk cells that have specificity for a variety of hla antigens. kir receptors contain up to three different extracellular immunoglobulin-like domains referred to as d0, d1, and d2 and play an important role in blocking nk cell activation against cells expressing the appropriate hla antigens thus preventing cell lysis. Although they are often referred to as being inhibitory receptors, a subset of kir receptors may also play an activating role in nk cells.

name: receptors , mating factor
query: Query: receptors , mating factor [SEP] Mating factor receptors is a family of pheromone receptors that were initially discovered in saccharomyces cerevisiae as proteins necessary for fungal conjugation. Each mating factor receptor is expressed in haploid cells of a single mating type.

name: receptors , melatonin
query: Query: receptors , melatonin [SEP] Melatonin receptors is a family of G-protein-coupled receptors that are specific for and mediate the effects of melatonin. Activation of melatonin receptors has been associated with decreased intracellular cyclic amp and increased hydrolysis of phosphoinositides.

name: receptors , opioid , kappa
query: Query: receptors , opioid , kappa [SEP] Kappa opioid receptors is a class of opioid receptors recognized by its pharmacological profile. Kappa opioid receptors bind dynorphins with a higher affinity than endorphins which are themselves preferred to enkephalins.

name: receptors , opioid , mu
query: Query: receptors , opioid , mu [SEP] Mu opioid receptors is a class of opioid receptors recognized by its pharmacological profile. Mu opioid receptors bind, in decreasing order of affinity, endorphins, dynorphins, met-enkephalin, and leu-enkephalin. They have also been shown to be molecular receptors for [MASK].

name: receptors , oxytocin
query: Query: receptors , oxytocin [SEP] Oxytocin receptors is cell surface proteins that bind oxytocin with high affinity and trigger intracellular changes which influence the behavior of cells. Oxytocin receptors in the uterus and the mammary glands mediate the hormone's stimulation of contraction and milk ejection. The presence of oxytocin and oxytocin receptors in neurons of the brain probably reflects an additional role as a neurotransmitter.

name: receptors , polymeric immunoglobulin
query: Query: receptors , polymeric immunoglobulin [SEP] Polymeric immunoglobulin receptors is specialized Fc receptors (receptors, fc) for polymeric immunoglobulins, which mediate transcytosis of polymeric immunoglobulin a and immunoglobulin m into external secretions. They are found on the surfaces of epithelial cells and [MASK]. After binding to immunoglobulin a, the receptor-ligand complex undergoes endocytosis, transport by vesicle, and secretion into the lumen by exocytosis. Before release, the part of the receptor ([MASK]) that is bound to immunoglobulin a is proteolytically cleaved from its transmembrane tail. (From Rosen et al., The Dictionary of [MASK], 1989)

name: receptors , progesterone
query: Query: receptors , progesterone [SEP] Progesterone receptors is specific proteins found in or on cells of progesterone target tissues that specifically combine with progesterone. The [MASK] progesterone-receptor complex then associates with the nucleic acids to initiate protein synthesis. There are two kinds of progesterone receptors, a and b. Both are induced by estrogen and have short half-lives.

name: receptors , sigma
query: Query: receptors , sigma [SEP] Sigma receptors is a class of cell surface receptors recognized by its pharmacological profile. Sigma receptors were originally considered to be opioid receptors because they bind certain synthetic opioids. However they also interact with a variety of other psychoactive drugs, and their endogenous ligand is not known (although they can react to certain endogenous steroids). Sigma receptors are found in the immune, endocrine, and nervous systems, and in some peripheral tissues.

name: receptors , thrombin
query: Query: receptors , thrombin [SEP] Thrombin receptors is a family of proteinase-activated receptors that are specific for thrombin. They are found primarily on platelets and on endothelial cells. Activation of thrombin receptors occurs through the proteolytic action of thrombin, which cleaves the N-terminal peptide from the receptor to reveal a new N-terminal peptide that is a cryptic ligand for the receptor. The receptors signal through heterotrimeric gtp-binding proteins. Small synthetic peptides that contain the unmasked N-terminal peptide sequence can also activate the receptor in the absence of proteolytic activity.

name: receptors , transforming growth factor beta
query: Query: receptors , transforming growth factor beta [SEP] Transforming growth factor beta receptors is cell-surface proteins that bind transforming growth factor beta and trigger changes influencing the behavior of cells. Two types of transforming growth factor receptors have been recognized. They differ in affinity for different members of the transforming growth factor beta family and in cellular mechanisms of action.

name: receptors , tumor necrosis factor , member 14
query: Query: receptors , tumor necrosis factor , member 14 [SEP] Member 14 tumor necrosis factor receptors is a novel member of the tumor-necrosis factor receptor family that can also mediate herpes simplex virus type 1 entry into cells. It has specificity for [MASK] and the homotrimeric form of lymphotoxin-alpha. The receptor is abundantly expressed on t-lymphocytes and may play a role in regulating [MASK]. Signaling by the activated receptor occurs through its association with tnf receptor-associated factors.

name: receptors , tumor necrosis factor , member 25
query: Query: receptors , tumor necrosis factor , member 25 [SEP] Member 25 tumor necrosis factor receptors is a tumor necrosis factor receptor subtype with specificity for tumor necrosis factor ligand superfamily member 15. It is found in tissues containing lymphocytes and may play a role in regulating lymphocyte homeostasis and apoptosis. The activated receptor signals via a conserved death domain that associates with specific tnf receptor-associated factors in the cytoplasm.

name: receptors , tumor necrosis factor , type i
