query: Query: receptors , tumor necrosis factor , type i [SEP] Type i tumor necrosis factor receptors is a tumor necrosis factor receptor subtype that has specificity for tumor necrosis factor alpha and lymphotoxin alpha. It is constitutively expressed in most tissues and is a key mediator of tumor necrosis factor signaling in the vast majority of cells. The activated receptor signals via a conserved death domain that associates with specific tnf receptor-associated factors in the cytoplasm.

name: receptors , tumor necrosis factor , type ii
query: Query: receptors , tumor necrosis factor , type ii [SEP] Type ii tumor necrosis factor receptors is a tumor necrosis factor receptor subtype that is expressed primarily in immune system cells. It has specificity for membrane-bound form of tumor necrosis factors and mediates intracellular-signaling through tnf receptor associated factors.

name: receptors , vascular endothelial growth factor
query: Query: receptors , vascular endothelial growth factor [SEP] Vascular endothelial growth factor receptors is a family of closely related receptor protein-tyrosine kinases that bind vascular endothelial growth factors. They share a cluster of seven extracellular ig-like domains which are important for ligand binding. They are highly expressed in vascular endothelial cells and are critical for the physiological and pathological growth, development and maintenance of blood and lymphatic vessels.

name: receptors , wnt
query: Query: receptors , wnt [SEP] Wnt receptors is cell-surface receptors that specifically bind to [MASK] and activate the wnt signaling pathway.

name: recombinant fusion proteins
query: Query: recombinant fusion proteins [SEP] Recombinant fusion proteins is recombinant proteins produced by the genetic translation of fused genes formed by the combination of nucleic acid regulatory sequences of one or more genes with the protein coding sequences of one or more genes.

name: recovery of function
query: Query: recovery of function [SEP] Recovery of function is a partial or complete return to the normal or proper physiologic activity of an organ or part following disease or trauma.

name: rectal fistula
query: Query: rectal fistula [SEP] Rectal fistula is an abnormal anatomical passage connecting the rectum to the outside, with an orifice at the site of drainage.

name: rectal neoplasms
query: Query: rectal neoplasms [SEP] Rectal neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the rectum.

name: rectum
query: Query: rectum [SEP] Rectum is the distal segment of the large intestine, between the sigmoid colon and the anal canal.

name: recurrence
query: Query: recurrence [SEP] Recurrence is the return of a sign, symptom, or disease after a remission.

name: recurrent laryngeal nerve
query: Query: recurrent laryngeal nerve [SEP] Recurrent laryngeal nerve is branches of the vagus (tenth cranial) nerve. The recurrent laryngeal nerves originate more caudally than the superior laryngeal nerves and follow different paths on the right and left sides. They carry efferents to all muscles of the larynx except the cricothyroid and carry sensory and autonomic fibers to the laryngeal, pharyngeal, tracheal, and cardiac regions.

name: red cross
query: Query: red cross [SEP] Red cross is international collective of humanitarian organizations led by volunteers and guided by its Congressional Charter and the Fundamental Principles of the International Red Cross Movement, to provide relief to victims of disaster and help people prevent, prepare for, and respond to emergencies.

name: red meat
query: Query: red meat [SEP] Red meat is meat such as beef, goat, pork, or lamb which contains more myoglobin than poultry or seafood.

name: reduced folate carrier protein
query: Query: reduced folate carrier protein [SEP] Reduced folate carrier protein is a ubiquitously expressed folic acid transporter that functions via an antiporter mechanism which is coupled to the transport of organic phosphates.

name: reducing agents
query: Query: reducing agents [SEP] Reducing agents is materials that add an [MASK] to an element or compound, that is, decrease the positiveness of its valence. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 5th ed)

name: reference books , medical
query: Query: reference books , medical [SEP] Medical reference books is books in the field of medicine intended primarily for consultation.

name: reference values
query: Query: reference values [SEP] Reference values is the range or frequency distribution of a measurement in a population (of organisms, organs or things) that has not been selected for the presence of disease or abnormality.

name: reflex , abdominal
query: Query: reflex , abdominal [SEP] Abdominal reflex is contractions of the abdominal muscles upon stimulation of the skin (superficial abdominal reflex) or tapping neighboring bony structures (deep abdominal reflex). The superficial reflex may be weak or absent, for example, after a stroke, a sign of upper (suprasegmental) motor neuron lesions. (Stedman, 25th ed & Best & Taylor's Physiological Basis of Medical Practice, 12th ed, p1073)

name: reflex , abnormal
query: Query: reflex , abnormal [SEP] Abnormal reflex is an abnormal response to a stimulus applied to the sensory components of the nervous system. This may take the form of increased, decreased, or absent reflexes.

name: reflex , acoustic
query: Query: reflex , acoustic [SEP] Acoustic reflex is intra-aural contraction of tensor tympani and stapedius in response to sound.

name: reflex sympathetic dystrophy
query: Query: reflex sympathetic dystrophy [SEP] Reflex sympathetic dystrophy is a syndrome characterized by severe burning pain in an extremity accompanied by sudomotor, vasomotor, and trophic changes in bone without an associated specific nerve injury. This condition is most often precipitated by trauma to soft tissue or nerve complexes. The skin over the affected region is usually erythematous and demonstrates hypersensitivity to tactile stimuli and erythema. (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1360; Pain 1995 Oct;63(1):127-33)

name: refraction , ocular
query: Query: refraction , ocular [SEP] Ocular refraction is refraction of light effected by the media of the eye.

name: refractory period , psychological
query: Query: refractory period , psychological [SEP] Psychological refractory period is a delayed response interval occurring when two stimuli are presented in close succession.

name: regenerative medicine
query: Query: regenerative medicine [SEP] Regenerative medicine is a field of medicine concerned with developing and using strategies aimed at repair or replacement of damaged, diseased, or metabolically deficient organs, tissues, and cells via tissue engineering; cell transplantation; and artificial organs and bioartificial organs and tissues.

name: regional blood flow
query: Query: regional blood flow [SEP] Regional blood flow is the flow of blood through or around an organ or region of the body.

name: regional medical programs
query: Query: regional medical programs [SEP] Regional medical programs is coordination of activities and programs among health care institutions within defined geographic areas for the purpose of improving delivery and quality of medical care to the patients. These programs are mandated under u.s. Public Law 89-239.

name: registries
query: Query: registries [SEP] Registries is the systems and processes involved in the establishment, support, management, and operation of registers, e.g., disease registers.

name: regression , psychology
query: Query: regression , psychology [SEP] Psychology regression is a return to earlier, especially to infantile, patterns of thought or behavior, or stage of functioning, e.g., feelings of helplessness and dependency in a patient with a serious physical illness. (From apa, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 1994).

name: regulation or law
query: Query: regulation or law [SEP] Regulation or law is the science or philosophy of law. Also, the application of the principles of law and justice to health and medicine.

name: rehabilitation nursing
query: Query: rehabilitation nursing [SEP] Rehabilitation nursing is a nursing specialty involved in the diagnosis and treatment of human responses of individuals and groups to actual or potential health problems with the characteristics of altered functional ability and altered life-style.

name: rehabilitation research
query: Query: rehabilitation research [SEP] Rehabilitation research is studies and research concerning the psychological, educational, social, vocational, industrial, and economic aspects of rehabilitation.

name: reinforcement , social
query: Query: reinforcement , social [SEP] Social reinforcement is the strengthening of a response with a social reward such as a nod of approval, a parent's love or attention.

name: reinforcement , verbal
query: Query: reinforcement , verbal [SEP] Verbal reinforcement is use of word stimulus to strengthen a response during learning.

name: relative biological effectiveness
query: Query: relative biological effectiveness [SEP] Relative biological effectiveness is the ratio of radiation dosages required to produce identical change based on a formula comparing other types of radiation with that of gamma or roentgen rays.

name: relative value scales
query: Query: relative value scales [SEP] Relative value scales is coded listings of physician or other professional services using units that indicate the relative value of the various services they perform. They take into account time, skill, and overhead cost required for each service, but generally do not consider the relative cost-effectiveness. Appropriate conversion factors can be used to translate the [MASK] units of the relative value scales into dollar fees for each service based on work expended, practice costs, and training costs.

name: relaxation therapy
query: Query: relaxation therapy [SEP] Relaxation therapy is treatment to improve one's health condition by using techniques that can reduce physiological stress; psychological stress; or both.

name: religion and psychology
query: Query: religion and psychology [SEP] Religion and psychology is the interrelationship of psychology and religion.

name: religious missions
query: Query: religious missions [SEP] Religious missions is programs or projects established by religious groups or institution to support and provide missionary activities, including sharing faith or providing educational, medical, or other assistance.

name: religious personnel
query: Query: religious personnel [SEP] Religious personnel is persons that live and work according to a religious vocation, or calling, to a consecrated or ordained life.

name: renal artery obstruction
query: Query: renal artery obstruction [SEP] [MASK] obstruction is narrowing or occlusion of the [MASK] or arteries. It is due usually to atherosclerosis; fibromuscular dysplasia; thrombosis; embolism, or external pressure. The reduced renal perfusion can lead to renovascular hypertension (hypertension, renovascular).

name: renal elimination
query: Query: renal elimination [SEP] Renal elimination is the discharge of substances from the blood supply via the urinary tract.

name: renal plasma flow
query: Query: renal plasma flow [SEP] Renal plasma flow is the amount of plasma that perfuses the kidneys per unit time, approximately 10% greater than effective renal plasma flow (renal plasma flow, effective). It should be differentiated from the renal blood flow; (rbf), which refers to the total volume of blood flowing through the renal vasculature, while the renal plasma flow refers to the rate of plasma flow (rpf).

name: renal plasma flow , effective
query: Query: renal plasma flow , effective [SEP] Effective renal plasma flow is the amount of plasma flowing to the parts of the kidney that function in the production of urine. It is the amount of plasma perfusing the kidney tubules per unit time, generally measured by p-aminohippurate clearance. It should be differentiated from renal plasma flow which is approximately 10% greater than the effective renal plasma flow.

name: renal veins
query: Query: renal veins [SEP] Renal veins is short thick veins which return blood from the kidneys to the vena cava.

name: repetitive sequences , amino acid
query: Query: repetitive sequences , amino acid [SEP] Amino acid repetitive sequences is a sequential pattern of amino acids occurring more than once in the same protein sequence. There often is some sequence variation between the repeated segments. Many protein domains are constituted from repeats.

name: repression , psychology
query: Query: repression , psychology [SEP] Psychology repression is the active mental process of keeping out and ejecting, banishing from consciousness, ideas or impulses that are unacceptable to it.

name: reproductive health
query: Query: reproductive health [SEP] Reproductive health is the state of the reproductive system when functioning optimally without evidence of disease, disorders, or deficiencies.

name: reproductive isolation
query: Query: reproductive isolation [SEP] Reproductive isolation is mechanisms that prevent different populations from exchanging genes (gene flow), resulting in or maintaining [MASK]. It can either prevent mating to take place or ensure that any offspring produced is either inviable or sterile, thereby preventing further reproduction.

name: reproductive rights
query: Query: reproductive rights [SEP] Reproductive rights is reproductive rights rest on the recognition of the basic right of all couples and individuals to decide freely and responsibly the number, spacing and timing of their children and to have the information and means to do so, and the right to attain the highest standard of sexual and reproductive health. They also include the right of all to make decisions concerning reproduction free of discrimination, coercion and violence.

name: reproductive tract infections
query: Query: reproductive tract infections [SEP] Reproductive tract infections is infections of the genital tract in females or males. They can be caused by endogenous, iatrogenic, or sexually transmitted organisms.

name: rescue work
query: Query: rescue work [SEP] Rescue work is activities devoted to freeing persons or animals from danger to life or well-being in accidents, fires, bombings, floods, earthquakes, other disasters and life-threatening conditions. While usually performed by team efforts, rescue work is not restricted to organized services.

name: research device
query: Query: research device [SEP] Research device is device for research.

name: research embryo creation
query: Query: research embryo creation [SEP] Research embryo creation is the creation of embryos specifically for research purposes.

name: research personnel
query: Query: research personnel [SEP] Research personnel is those individuals engaged in research.

name: research report
query: Query: research report [SEP] Research report is detailed account or statement or formal record of data resulting from empirical inquiry.

name: residual volume
query: Query: residual volume [SEP] Residual volume is the volume of air remaining in the lungs at the end of a maximal expiration. Common abbreviation is rv.

name: resilience , psychological
query: Query: resilience , psychological [SEP] Psychological resilience is the human ability to adapt in the face of tragedy, trauma, adversity, hardship, and ongoing significant life stressors.

name: resistance training
query: Query: resistance training [SEP] Resistance training is a type of strength-building exercise program that requires the body muscle to exert a force against some form of resistance, such as weight, stretch bands, water, or immovable objects. Resistance exercise is a combination of static and dynamic contractions involving shortening and lengthening of skeletal muscles.

name: respect
query: Query: respect [SEP] Respect is a feeling of deep admiration for someone or something elicited by their abilities, qualities, or achievements and regard for the feelings, wishes, or rights of others.

name: respiratory aspiration of gastric contents
query: Query: respiratory aspiration of gastric contents [SEP] Respiratory aspiration of gastric contents is [MASK] refluxed gastric or duodenal contents.

name: respiratory care units
query: Query: respiratory care units [SEP] Respiratory care units is the hospital unit in which patients with respiratory conditions requiring special attention receive intensive medical care and surveillance.

name: respiratory dead space
query: Query: respiratory dead space [SEP] Respiratory dead space is that part of the respiratory tract or the air within the respiratory tract that does not exchange oxygen and carbon dioxide with pulmonary capillary blood.

name: respiratory distress syndrome , newborn
query: Query: respiratory distress syndrome , newborn [SEP] Newborn [MASK] is a condition of the newborn marked by dyspnea with cyanosis, heralded by such prodromal signs as dilatation of the alae nasi, expiratory grunt, and retraction of the suprasternal notch or costal margins, mostly frequently occurring in premature infants, children of diabetic mothers, and infants delivered by cesarean section, and sometimes with no apparent predisposing cause.

name: respiratory paralysis
query: Query: respiratory paralysis [SEP] Respiratory paralysis is complete or severe weakness of the muscles of respiration. This condition may be associated with motor neuron diseases; peripheral nerve diseases; neuromuscular junction diseases; spinal cord diseases; injury to the phrenic nerve; and other disorders.

name: respiratory protective devices
query: Query: respiratory protective devices [SEP] Respiratory protective devices is respirators to protect individuals from breathing air contaminated with harmful dusts, fogs, fumes, mists, gases, smokes, sprays, or vapors.

name: respiratory rate
query: Query: respiratory rate [SEP] Respiratory rate is the number of times an organism breathes with the lungs (respiration) per unit time, usually per minute.

name: respiratory sinus arrhythmia
query: Query: respiratory sinus arrhythmia [SEP] Respiratory sinus arrhythmia is a naturally occurring variation in heart rate that occurs during a breathing cycle, where the time between heartbeats is shortened during inspiration and prolonged during expiration. It is not the same as sinus arrhythmia, the disorder.

name: respiratory sounds
query: Query: respiratory sounds [SEP] Respiratory sounds is noises, normal and abnormal, heard on auscultation over any part of the respiratory tract.

name: respiratory system abnormalities
query: Query: respiratory system abnormalities [SEP] Respiratory system abnormalities is congenital structural abnormalities of the respiratory system.

name: respiratory therapy department , hospital
query: Query: respiratory therapy department , hospital [SEP] Hospital respiratory therapy department is hospital department which is responsible for the administration of diagnostic pulmonary function tests and of procedures to restore optimum pulmonary ventilation.

name: rest
query: Query: rest [SEP] Rest is freedom from activity.

name: restraint , physical
query: Query: restraint , physical [SEP] Physical restraint is use of a device for the purpose of controlling movement of all or part of the body. Splinting and casting are fracture fixation.

name: resuscitation orders
query: Query: resuscitation orders [SEP] Resuscitation orders is instructions issued by a physician pertaining to the institution, continuation, or withdrawal of life support measures. The concept includes policies, laws, statutes, decisions, guidelines, and discussions that may affect the issuance of such orders.

name: retention , psychology
query: Query: retention , psychology [SEP] Psychology retention is the persistence to perform a learned behavior (facts or experiences) after an interval has elapsed in which there has been no performance or practice of the behavior.

name: retention in care
query: Query: retention in care [SEP] Retention in care is patient's regular engagement with medical care after initial entry into the system.

name: retinal bipolar cells
query: Query: retinal bipolar cells [SEP] Retinal bipolar cells is interneurons of the vertebrate retina containing two processes. They receive inputs from the retinal photoreceptor cells and send outputs to the [MASK]. The bipolar cells also make lateral connections in the retina with the retinal horizontal cells and with the amacrine cells.

name: retinal dehydrogenase
query: Query: retinal dehydrogenase [SEP] Retinal dehydrogenase is a metalloflavoprotein enzyme involved the metabolism of vitamin a, this enzyme catalyzes the oxidation of retinal to retinoic acid, using both nad+ and fad coenzymes. It also acts on both the 11-trans- and 13-cis-forms of retinal.

name: retinal detachment
query: Query: retinal detachment [SEP] Retinal detachment is separation of the inner layers of the retina (neural retina) from the pigment epithelium. Retinal detachment occurs more commonly in men than in women, in eyes with degenerative myopia, in aging and in aphakia. It may occur after an uncomplicated [MASK] extraction, but it is seen more often if [MASK] has been lost during surgery. (Dorland, 27th ed; Newell, Ophthalmology: Principles and Concepts, 7th ed, p310-12).

name: retinal dysplasia
query: Query: retinal dysplasia [SEP] Retinal dysplasia is congenital, often bilateral, retinal abnormality characterized by the arrangement of outer nuclear retinal cells in a palisading or radiating pattern surrounding a central ocular space. This disorder is sometimes hereditary.

name: retinal hemorrhage
query: Query: retinal hemorrhage [SEP] Retinal hemorrhage is bleeding from the vessels of the retina.

name: retinal horizontal cells
query: Query: retinal horizontal cells [SEP] Retinal horizontal cells is neurons in the inner nuclear layer of the retina that synapse with both the retinal photoreceptor cells and the retinal bipolar cells, as well as other horizontal cells. The horizontal cells modulate the sensory signal.

name: retinal neoplasms
query: Query: retinal neoplasms [SEP] Retinal neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the retina.

name: retinal photoreceptor cell inner segment
query: Query: retinal photoreceptor cell inner segment [SEP] Retinal photoreceptor cell inner segment is the inner portion of a retinal rod or a [MASK], situated between the photoreceptor connecting cilium and the synapse with the adjacent neurons (retinal bipolar cells; retinal horizontal cells). The inner segment contains the cell body, the nucleus, the mitochondria, and apparatus for protein synthesis.

name: retinal pigment epithelium
query: Query: retinal pigment epithelium [SEP] [MASK] epithelium is the single layer of pigment-containing epithelial cells in the retina, situated closely to the tips (outer segments) of the retinal photoreceptor cells. These epithelial cells are macroglia that perform essential functions for the photoreceptor cells, such as in nutrient transport, [MASK] of the shed photoreceptor membranes, and ensuring retinal attachment.

name: retinal vein
query: Query: retinal vein [SEP] Retinal vein is central retinal vein and its tributaries. It runs a short course within the optic nerve and then leaves and empties into the superior ophthalmic vein or cavernous sinus.

name: retinal vein occlusion
query: Query: retinal vein occlusion [SEP] Retinal vein occlusion is blockage of the retinal vein. Those at high risk for this condition include patients with hypertension; diabetes mellitus; atherosclerosis; and other cardiovascular diseases.

name: retinoic acid receptor alpha
query: Query: retinoic acid receptor alpha [SEP] Retinoic acid receptor alpha is a nuclear receptor protein which belongs to a family of transcription regulators of ligand-responsive regulatory proteins which include steroid hormone receptors. In addition to a C-terminal ligand-binding domain, these nuclear receptors contain a highly-conserved N-terminal zinc-finger domain that mediates binding ligand-responsive elements.

name: retrograde degeneration
query: Query: retrograde degeneration [SEP] Retrograde degeneration is pathologic changes that occur in the axon and cell body of a neuron proximal to an axonal lesion. The process is characterized by central chromatolysis which features flattening and displacement of the nucleus, loss of Nissl bodies, and cellular edema. Central chromatolysis primarily occurs in lower motor neurons.

name: return to sport
query: Query: return to sport [SEP] Return to sport is resumption of sporting activity following a hiatus or period of absence due to injury or other reasons.

name: return to work
query: Query: return to work [SEP] Return to work is resumption of normal work routine following a hiatus or period of absence due to injury, disability, or other reasons.

name: reverse genetics
query: Query: reverse genetics [SEP] Reverse genetics is the use of techniques that produce a functional mutation or an effect on gene expression of a specific gene of interest in order to identify the role or activity of the gene product of that gene.

name: reverse transcriptase inhibitors
query: Query: reverse transcriptase inhibitors [SEP] Reverse transcriptase inhibitors is inhibitors of reverse transcriptase (rna-directed dna polymerase), an enzyme that synthesizes dna on an rna template.

name: reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction
query: Query: reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction [SEP] Reverse transcriptase polymerase chain reaction is a variation of the pcr technique in which cDNA is made from rna via reverse transcription. The resultant cDNA is then amplified using standard pcr protocols.

name: reverse transcription
query: Query: reverse transcription [SEP] Reverse transcription is the biosynthesis of dna carried out on a template of rna.

name: r factors
query: Query: r factors [SEP] R factors is a class of plasmids that transfer antibiotic resistance from one bacterium to another by conjugation.

name: rheumatoid factor
query: Query: rheumatoid factor [SEP] Rheumatoid factor is antibodies found in adult rheumatoid arthritis patients that are directed against gamma-chain immunoglobulins.

name: rheumatoid nodule
query: Query: rheumatoid nodule [SEP] Rheumatoid nodule is subcutaneous nodules seen in 20-30% of rheumatoid arthritis patients. They may arise anywhere on the body, but are most frequently found over the bony prominences. The nodules are characterized histologically by dense areas of fibrinoid necrosis with basophilic streaks and granules, surrounded by a palisade of cells, mainly fibroblasts and histiocytes.

name: rheumatology
query: Query: rheumatology [SEP] Rheumatology is a subspecialty of internal medicine concerned with the study of inflammatory or degenerative processes and metabolic derangement of connective tissue structures which pertain to a variety of musculoskeletal disorders, such as arthritis.

name: rho guanine nucleotide exchange factors
query: Query: rho guanine nucleotide exchange factors [SEP] Rho guanine nucleotide exchange factors is signaling proteins which function as master molecular switches by activating Rho GTPases through conversion of guanine nucleotides. Rho GTPases in turn control many aspects of cell behavior through the regulation of multiple downstream signal transduction pathways.

name: rib cage
query: Query: rib cage [SEP] Rib cage is the bony thoracic enclosure consisting of the vertebral column; the ribs; the sternum; and the costal cartilage.

name: rib fractures
query: Query: rib fractures [SEP] Rib fractures is fractures of any of the ribs.

name: ribosome subunits , large , eukaryotic
query: Query: ribosome subunits , large , eukaryotic [SEP] Eukaryotic large ribosome subunits is the large subunit of the 80s ribosome of eukaryotes. It is composed of the 28s [MASK], the 5.8s [MASK], the 5s [MASK], and about 50 different ribosomal proteins.

name: ribosome subunits , small , bacterial
query: Query: ribosome subunits , small , bacterial [SEP] Bacterial small ribosome subunits is the small subunit of eubacterial ribosomes. It is composed of the 16s [MASK] and about 23 different ribosomal proteins.

name: ribosome subunits , small , eukaryotic
query: Query: ribosome subunits , small , eukaryotic [SEP] Eukaryotic small ribosome subunits is the small subunit of the 80s ribosome of eukaryotes. It is composed of the 18s [MASK] and 32 different ribosomal proteins.

name: rice bran oil
query: Query: rice bran oil [SEP] Rice bran oil is oil extracted from the hard outer brown layer of rice bran after the husk has been removed.

name: right to die
query: Query: right to die [SEP] Right to die is the right of the patient or the patient's representative to make decisions with regard to the patient's dying.

name: right to work
query: Query: right to work [SEP] Right to work is the right of individuals to work, to free choice of employment, to just and favorable conditions of work and to protection against [MASK].

name: ring chromosomes
query: Query: ring chromosomes [SEP] Ring chromosomes is aberrant chromosomes with no ends, i.e., circular.

name: ring finger domains
query: Query: ring finger domains [SEP] Ring finger domains is a zinc-binding domain defined by the sequence [MASK]-X2-[MASK]-X(9-39)-[MASK]-X(l-3)-His-X(2-3)-[MASK]-X2-[MASK] -X(4-48)-[MASK]-X2-[MASK], where x is any amino acid. The ring finger motif binds two atoms of zinc, with each zinc atom ligated tetrahedrally by either four cysteines or three cysteines and a histidine. The motif also forms into a unitary structure with a central cross-brace region and is found in many proteins that are involved in protein-protein interactions. The acronym ring stands for Really Interesting New Gene.

name: risk adjustment
query: Query: risk adjustment [SEP] Risk [MASK] is the use of severity-of-illness measures, such as age, to estimate the risk (measurable or predictable chance of loss, injury or death) to which a patient is subject before receiving some health care intervention. This [MASK] allows comparison of performance and quality across organizations, practitioners, and communities. (from jcaho, Lexikon, 1994)

name: risk evaluation and mitigation
query: Query: risk evaluation and mitigation [SEP] Risk evaluation and mitigation is strategies required by the us Food and Drug Administration (fda) Amendments Act of 2007 when a question exists as to whether the benefits of a drug outweigh its risks. These constitute a safety plan with several potential components, including a medication guide, a communication plan, elements to ensure safe use and an implementation system to help guide the prescribers, pharmacists and patients.

name: risk factors
query: Query: risk factors [SEP] Risk factors is an aspect of personal behavior or lifestyle, environmental exposure, inborn or inherited characteristic, which, on the basis of epidemiological evidence, is known to be associated with a health-related condition considered important to prevent.

name: risk reduction behavior
query: Query: risk reduction behavior [SEP] Risk reduction behavior is reduction of high-risk choices and adoption of low-risk quantity and frequency alternatives.

name: risk sharing , financial
query: Query: risk sharing , financial [SEP] Financial risk sharing is any system which allows payors to share some of the financial risk associated with a particular patient population with providers. Providers agree to adhere to fixed fee schedules in exchange for an increase in their payor base and a chance to benefit from cost containment measures. Common risk-sharing methods are prospective payment schedules (prospective payment system), capitation (capitation fees), diagnosis-related fees (diagnosis-related groups), and pre-negotiated fees.

name: rna , algal
query: Query: rna , algal [SEP] Algal rna is ribonucleic acid in algae having regulatory and catalytic roles as well as involvement in protein synthesis.

name: rna , bacterial
query: Query: rna , bacterial [SEP] Bacterial rna is ribonucleic acid in bacteria having regulatory and catalytic roles as well as involvement in protein synthesis.

name: rna , catalytic
query: Query: rna , catalytic [SEP] Catalytic rna is rna that has catalytic activity. The catalytic rna sequence folds to form a complex surface that can function as an enzyme in reactions with itself and other molecules. It may function even in the absence of protein. There are numerous examples of rna species that are acted upon by catalytic rna, however the scope of this enzyme class is not limited to a particular type of substrate.

name: rna , chloroplast
query: Query: rna , chloroplast [SEP] Chloroplast rna is ribonucleic acid in chloroplasts having regulatory and catalytic roles as well as involvement in protein synthesis.

name: rna , circular
query: Query: rna , circular [SEP] Circular rna is rna molecules in which the 3' and 5' ends are covalently joined to form a closed continuous loop. They are resistant to [MASK] by exoribonucleases.

name: rna , complementary
query: Query: rna , complementary [SEP] Complementary rna is synthetic transcripts of a specific dna molecule or fragment, made by an in vitro transcription system. This cRNA can be labeled with radioactive uracil and then used as a probe. (King & Stansfield, a Dictionary of Genetics, 4th ed)

name: rna , fungal
query: Query: rna , fungal [SEP] Fungal rna is ribonucleic acid in fungi having regulatory and catalytic roles as well as involvement in protein synthesis.

name: rna , heterogeneous nuclear
query: Query: rna , heterogeneous nuclear [SEP] Heterogeneous nuclear rna is nuclear nonribosomal rna larger than about 1000 nucleotides, the mass of which is rapidly synthesized and degraded within the cell nucleus. Some heterogeneous nuclear rna may be a precursor to mRNA. However, the great bulk of total hnRNA hybridizes with nuclear dna rather than with mRNA.

name: rna , messenger , stored
query: Query: rna , messenger , stored [SEP] Stored messenger rna is messenger rna that is stored in a masked state for translation at a later time. Distinguish from rna, untranslated which refers to non-messenger rna, i.e. rna that does not code for protein.

name: rna , mitochondrial
query: Query: rna , mitochondrial [SEP] Mitochondrial rna is rna molecules encoded by the [MASK].

name: rna , satellite
query: Query: rna , satellite [SEP] Satellite rna is small, linear single-stranded rna molecules functionally acting as molecular parasites of certain rna plant viruses. Satellite RNAs exhibit four characteristic traits: (1) they require helper viruses to replicate; (2) they are unnecessary for the replication of helper viruses; (3) they are encapsidated in the coat protein of the helper virus; (4) they have no extensive sequence homology to the helper virus. Thus they differ from satellite viruses which encode their own coat protein, and from the genomic rna; (=rna, viral); of satellite viruses. (From Maramorosch, Viroids and Satellites, 1991, p143)

name: rna , small interfering
query: Query: rna , small interfering [SEP] Small interfering rna is small double-stranded, non-protein coding RNAs (21-31 nucleotides) involved in gene silencing functions, especially rna interference (RNAi). Endogenously, siRNAs are generated from dsRNAs (rna, double-stranded) by the same ribonuclease, Dicer, that generates miRNAs (micrornas). The perfect match of the siRNAs' antisense strand to their target RNAs mediates RNAi by siRNA-guided rna cleavage. siRNAs fall into different classes including trans-acting siRNA (tasiRNA), repeat-associated rna (rasiRNA), small-scan rna (scnRNA), and Piwi protein-interacting rna (piRNA) and have different specific gene silencing functions.

name: rna , small nuclear
query: Query: rna , small nuclear [SEP] Small nuclear rna is short chains of rna (100-300 nucleotides long) that are abundant in the nucleus and usually complexed with proteins in snRNPs (ribonucleoproteins, small nuclear). Many function in the processing of messenger rna precursors. Others, the snoRNAs (rna, small nucleolar), are involved with the processing of [MASK] precursors.

name: rna , viral
query: Query: rna , viral [SEP] Viral rna is ribonucleic acid that makes up the genetic material of viruses.

name: rna cap analogs
query: Query: rna cap analogs [SEP] Rna cap analogs is analogs of rna cap compounds which do not have a positive charge. These compounds inhibit the initiation of translation of both capped and uncapped messenger rna.

name: rna cleavage
query: Query: rna cleavage [SEP] Rna cleavage is a reaction that severs one of the sugar-phosphate linkages of the phosphodiester backbone of rna. It is catalyzed enzymatically, chemically, or by radiation. Cleavage may be exonucleolytic, or endonucleolytic.

name: rna folding
query: Query: rna folding [SEP] Rna folding is the processes of rna tertiary structure formation.

name: rna interference
query: Query: rna interference [SEP] Rna interference is a gene silencing phenomenon whereby specific dsRNAs (rna, double-stranded) trigger the degradation of homologous mRNA (rna, messenger). The specific dsRNAs are processed into small interfering rna (siRNA) which serves as a guide for cleavage of the homologous mRNA in the rna-induced silencing complex. [MASK] may also be triggered during this process.

name: rna isoforms
query: Query: rna isoforms [SEP] Rna isoforms is the different gene transcripts generated from a single gene by rna editing or [MASK] of rna precursors.

name: rnai therapeutics
query: Query: rnai therapeutics [SEP] Rnai therapeutics is a form of disease treatment which involves the silencing of genes that are associated with a disease by the process of rna interference.

name: rna polymerase sigma 54
query: Query: rna polymerase sigma 54 [SEP] Rna polymerase sigma 54 is a DNA-directed rna polymerase found in bacteria. It is a holoenzyme that consists of multiple subunits including [MASK] 54.

name: rna precursors
query: Query: rna precursors [SEP] Rna precursors is rna transcripts of the dna that are in some unfinished stage of post-transcriptional processing (rna processing, post-transcriptional) required for function. rna precursors may undergo several steps of rna splicing during which the phosphodiester bonds at exon-intron boundaries are cleaved and the introns are excised. Consequently a new bond is formed between the ends of the exons. Resulting mature RNAs can then be used; for example, mature mRNA (rna, messenger) is used as a template for protein production.

name: rna splice sites
query: Query: rna splice sites [SEP] Rna splice sites is nucleotide sequences located at the ends of exons and recognized in pre-messenger rna by spliceosomes. They are joined during the rna splicing reaction, forming the junctions between exons.

name: rna stability
query: Query: rna stability [SEP] Rna stability is the extent to which an rna molecule retains its structural integrity and resists degradation by rnase, and base-catalyzed hydrolysis, under changing in vivo or in vitro conditions.

name: rna transport
query: Query: rna transport [SEP] Rna transport is the process of moving specific rna molecules from one cellular compartment or region to another by various sorting and transport mechanisms.

name: robotic surgical procedures
query: Query: robotic surgical procedures [SEP] Robotic surgical procedures is surgical procedures performed remotely using a computer that controls surgical instruments attached to mechanical [MASK] designed to perform the tasks of the surgeon.

name: roc curve
query: Query: roc curve [SEP] Roc curve is a graphic means for assessing the ability of a screening test to discriminate between healthy and diseased persons; may also be used in other studies, e.g., distinguishing stimuli responses as to a faint stimuli or nonstimuli.

name: rod cell outer segment
query: Query: rod cell outer segment [SEP] Rod cell outer segment is the portion of a retinal rod cell situated between the rod inner segment and the [MASK] epithelium. It contains a stack of photosensitive disk membranes laden with rhodopsin.

name: rodent diseases
query: Query: rodent diseases [SEP] Rodent diseases is diseases of rodents of the order rodentia. This term includes diseases of Sciuridae (squirrels), Geomyidae (gophers), Heteromyidae (pouched mice), Castoridae (beavers), Cricetidae (rats and mice), Muridae (Old World rats and mice), Erethizontidae (porcupines), and Caviidae ([MASK] pigs).

name: roman world
query: Query: roman world [SEP] Roman world is a historical and cultural entity dispersed across a wide geographical area under the political domination and influence of ancient Rome, bringing to the conquered people the Roman civilization and culture from 753 b.c. to the beginning of the imperial rule under Augustus in 27 b.c. The early city built on seven hills grew to conquer Sicily, Sardinia, Carthage, Gaul, [MASK], Britain, Greece, Asia Minor, etc., and extended ultimately from Mesopotamia to the Atlantic. Roman medicine was almost entirely in Greek hands, but Rome, with its superior water system, remains a model of sanitation and hygiene. (From a. Castiglioni, a [MASK], 2d ed pp196-99; from f. h. Garrison, An Introduction to the [MASK], 4th ed, pp107-120)

name: rome
query: Query: rome [SEP] Rome is the capital city of Italy.

name: root canal filling materials
query: Query: root canal filling materials [SEP] Root canal filling materials is materials placed inside a root canal for the purpose of obturating or sealing it. The materials may be gutta-percha, silver cones, paste mixtures, or other substances. (Dorland, 28th ed, p631 & Boucher's Clinical Dental Terminology, 4th ed, p187)

name: root canal preparation
query: Query: root canal preparation [SEP] Root canal preparation is preparatory activities in root canal therapy by partial or complete extirpation of diseased pulp, cleaning and sterilization of the empty canal, enlarging and shaping the canal to receive the sealing material. The cavity may be prepared by mechanical, sonic, chemical, or other means. (From Dorland, 28th ed, p1700)

name: root caries
query: Query: root caries [SEP] Root caries is dental caries involving the tooth root, cementum, or cervical area of the tooth.

name: root cause analysis
query: Query: root cause analysis [SEP] Root cause analysis is multi-step [MASK] process used for improving safety by investigation of incidents to find what happened, why it happened, and to determine what can be done to prevent it from happening again.

name: root nodules , plant
query: Query: root nodules , plant [SEP] Plant root nodules is knobbed structures formed from and attached to plant roots, especially of legumes, which result from symbiotic infection by nitrogen fixing bacteria such as rhizobium or frankia. Root nodules are structures related to mycorrhizae formed by symbiotic associations with fungi.

name: round ligament of femur
query: Query: round ligament of femur [SEP] Round ligament of femur is ligament that connects the fovea of the femur head and the acetabulum notch in the hip joint.

name: round ligament of liver
query: Query: round ligament of liver [SEP] Round ligament of liver is a cord-like remnant structure formed from the closed left fetal umbilical vein. It is located along the lower edge of the falciform ligament.

name: rrna operon
query: Query: rrna operon [SEP] Rrna operon is genetic loci which direct transcription of [MASK] in bacterial operons. They are designated rrnB, rrnC, rrnD, etc. according to the structural position of the transcription unit in the dna sequence.

name: rubber dams
query: Query: rubber dams [SEP] Rubber dams is sheets of latex rubber punched and placed over the teeth during dental procedures to isolate the field of operation from the rest of the oral cavity (Jablonski; Illustrated Dictionary of Dentistry, 1982). Rubber dams are useful in preventing the swallowing of instruments or restorations during dental work.

name: rupture , spontaneous
query: Query: rupture , spontaneous [SEP] Spontaneous rupture is tear or break of an organ, vessel or other soft part of the body, occurring in the absence of external force.

name: rural health
query: Query: rural health [SEP] Rural health is the status of health in rural populations.

name: rural population
query: Query: rural population [SEP] Rural population is the inhabitants of rural areas or of small towns classified as rural.

name: saccharomyces cerevisiae
query: Query: saccharomyces cerevisiae [SEP] Saccharomyces cerevisiae is a species of the genus saccharomyces, family Saccharomycetaceae, order Saccharomycetales, known as "baker's" or "brewer's" yeast. The dried form is used as a dietary supplement.

name: safe sex
query: Query: safe sex [SEP] Safe [MASK] is sexual behavior that prevents or reduces the spread of sexually transmitted diseases or pregnancy.

name: sagittal abdominal diameter
query: Query: sagittal abdominal diameter [SEP] Sagittal abdominal diameter is the height of the abdomen as measured in the [MASK].

name: sagittal sinus thrombosis
query: Query: sagittal sinus thrombosis [SEP] Sagittal sinus thrombosis is formation or presence of a blood clot (thrombus) in the superior sagittal sinus or the inferior sagittal sinus. Sagittal sinus thrombosis can result from infections, hematological disorders, craniocerebral trauma; and neurosurgical procedures. Clinical features are primarily related to the increased [MASK] causing headache; nausea; and vomiting. Severe cases can evolve to seizures or coma.

name: saliva
query: Query: saliva [SEP] Saliva is the clear, viscous fluid secreted by the salivary glands and mucous glands of the mouth. It contains mucins, water, organic [MASK], and ptylin.

name: salivary ducts
query: Query: salivary ducts [SEP] Salivary ducts is any of the ducts which transport saliva. Salivary ducts include the parotid duct, the major and minor sublingual ducts, and the submandibular duct.

name: salivary gland neoplasms
query: Query: salivary gland neoplasms [SEP] Salivary gland neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the salivary glands.

name: salmonella infections , animal
query: Query: salmonella infections , animal [SEP] Animal salmonella infections is infections in animals with bacteria of the genus salmonella.

name: salmonella vaccines
query: Query: salmonella vaccines [SEP] Salmonella vaccines is vaccines or candidate vaccines used to prevent infection with salmonella. This includes vaccines used to prevent typhoid fever or paratyphoid fever; (typhoid-paratyphoid vaccines), and vaccines used to prevent nontyphoid salmonellosis.

name: salt gland
query: Query: salt gland [SEP] [MASK] gland is a compound tubular gland, located around the eyes and nasal passages in marine animals and birds, the physiology of which figures in water-electrolyte balance. The Pekin duck serves as a common research animal in [MASK] gland studies. a rectal gland or rectal [MASK] gland in the dogfish shark is attached at the junction of the intestine and cloaca and aids the kidneys in removing excess [MASK] from the blood. (Storer, Usinger, Stebbins & Nybakken: General Zoology, 6th ed, p658)

name: salvage therapy
query: Query: salvage therapy [SEP] Salvage therapy is a therapeutic approach, involving chemotherapy, radiation therapy, or surgery, after initial regimens have failed to lead to improvement in a patient's condition. Salvage therapy is most often used for neoplastic diseases.

name: sand
query: Query: sand [SEP] Sand is a hard granular material that is a component of soil. It is composed of very small pieces (between 0.06 and 2.0 millimeters in diameter) of disintegrating rock.

name: san francisco
query: Query: san francisco [SEP] San francisco is a city in northern California.

name: sarcoma , alveolar soft part
query: Query: sarcoma , alveolar soft part [SEP] Alveolar soft part sarcoma is a variety of rare sarcoma having a reticulated fibrous stroma enclosing groups of sarcoma cells, which resemble epithelial cells and are enclosed in alveoli walled with connective tissue. It is a rare tumor, usually occurring between 15 and 35 years of age. It appears in the muscles of the extremities in adults and most commonly in the head and [MASK] regions of children. Though slow-growing, it commonly metastasizes to the lungs, brain, bones, and [MASK] nodes. (DeVita Jr et al., Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 3d ed, p1365)

name: sarcoma , endometrial stromal
query: Query: sarcoma , endometrial stromal [SEP] Endometrial stromal sarcoma is a highly malignant subset of neoplasms arising from the endometrial stroma. Tumors in this group infiltrate the stroma with a wide range of atypia cells and numerous [MASK]. They are capable of widespread metastases (neoplasm metastasis).

name: sarcoma , myeloid
query: Query: sarcoma , myeloid [SEP] Myeloid sarcoma is an extramedullary tumor of immature myeloid cells or myeloblasts. Granulocytic sarcoma usually occurs with or follows the onset of [MASK].

name: sarcoma , small cell
query: Query: sarcoma , small cell [SEP] Small cell sarcoma is a sarcoma characterized by the presence of small cells, cells measuring 9-14 micrometers with a faint or indistinct rim of cytoplasm and an oval-to-elongated nucleus with relatively dense chromatin. (From Segen, Dictionary of Modern Medicine, 1992)

name: sarcoma , synovial
query: Query: sarcoma , synovial [SEP] Synovial sarcoma is a malignant neoplasm arising from tenosynovial tissue of the joints and in synovial cells of tendons and bursae. The legs are the most common site, but the tumor can occur in the [MASK] and other trunk muscles. There are two recognized types: the monophasic (characterized by sheaths of monotonous spindle cells) and the biphasic (characterized by slit-like spaces or clefts within the tumor, lined by cuboidal or tall columnar epithelial cells). These sarcomas occur most commonly in the second and fourth decades of life. (From Dorland, 27th ed; DeVita Jr et al., Cancer: Principles & Practice of Oncology, 3d ed, p1363)

name: sarcoma 37
query: Query: sarcoma 37 [SEP] Sarcoma 37 is an experimental sarcoma of mice.

name: satellite imagery
query: Query: satellite imagery [SEP] Satellite [MASK] is composition of images of earth or other planets from data collected during space flight by remote sensing instruments onboard spacecraft. The satellite sensor systems measure and record absorbed, emitted, or reflected energy across the spectra, as well as global position and time.

name: scalp
query: Query: scalp [SEP] Scalp is the outer covering of the calvaria. It is composed of several layers: skin; subcutaneous connective tissue; the occipitofrontal muscle which includes the tendinous galea aponeurotica; loose connective tissue; and the pericranium (the periosteum of the skull).

name: schizophrenia
query: Query: schizophrenia [SEP] Schizophrenia is a severe emotional disorder of psychotic depth characteristically marked by a retreat from reality with delusion formation, hallucinations, emotional disharmony, and regressive behavior.

name: school mental health services
query: Query: school mental health services [SEP] School mental health services is services which focus on the mental well-being of pre-college and pre-university students that include counseling and therapy.

name: schools , dental
query: Query: schools , dental [SEP] Dental schools is educational institutions for individuals specializing in the field of dentistry.

name: schools , medical
query: Query: schools , medical [SEP] Medical schools is educational institutions for individuals specializing in the field of medicine.

name: schools , public health
query: Query: schools , public health [SEP] Public health schools is educational institutions for individuals specializing in the field of public health.

name: schools , veterinary
query: Query: schools , veterinary [SEP] Veterinary schools is educational institutions for individuals specializing in the field of veterinary medicine.

name: school teachers
query: Query: school teachers [SEP] School teachers is members of staff responsible for teaching students in a school from pre-kindergarten through twelfth grade.

name: science in literature
query: Query: science in literature [SEP] Science in literature is literary works whose subject matter is science or about the profession of science and related areas.

name: scope of practice
query: Query: scope of practice [SEP] Scope of practice is the services that licensed professionals are deemed competent to perform, and permitted to undertake in keeping with the terms of their professional license.

name: screen time
query: Query: screen time [SEP] Screen time is period of activities done in front of an electronic screen, such as watching tv, working on a computer, or playing [MASK].

name: search engine
query: Query: search engine [SEP] Search engine is software used to locate data or information stored in machine-readable form locally or at a distance such as an internet site.

name: seasonal affective disorder
query: Query: seasonal affective disorder [SEP] Seasonal affective disorder is a syndrome characterized by depressions that recur annually at the same time each year, usually during the winter months. Other symptoms include anxiety, irritability, decreased energy, increased appetite (carbohydrate cravings), increased duration of sleep, and weight gain. sad (seasonal affective disorder) can be treated by daily exposure to bright artificial lights (phototherapy), during the season of recurrence.

name: seasons
query: Query: seasons [SEP] Seasons is divisions of the year according to some regularly recurrent phenomena usually astronomical or climatic. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

name: seawater
query: Query: seawater [SEP] Seawater is the salinated water of oceans and seas that provides habitat for [MASK].

name: secondary care
query: Query: secondary care [SEP] Secondary care is specialized healthcare delivered as a follow-up or referral from a primary care provider.

name: secondary care centers
query: Query: secondary care centers [SEP] Secondary care centers is a healthcare facility equipped to provide all but the most specialized forms of care, surgery, and diagnostic techniques.

name: secondary metabolism
query: Query: secondary metabolism [SEP] Secondary metabolism is a physiochemical process which occurs in a wide range of organisms which unlike basal metabolism is not required for or essential to short-term survivability but to long-term general well-being of the organism.

name: secondary prevention
query: Query: secondary prevention [SEP] Secondary prevention is the prevention of recurrences or exacerbations of a disease or complications of its therapy.

name: second harmonic generation microscopy
query: Query: second harmonic generation microscopy [SEP] Second harmonic generation microscopy is a microscopic imaging technique that takes advantage of the process of harmonic generation that occurs when [MASK] interact to generate new [MASK] of a different wavelength. In second harmonic generation, two [MASK] of the same wavelength and frequency, such as from a laser, interact inside a medium and are converted to a photon of twice the frequency and half of the wavelength of the two incident [MASK]. The light signals captured are used to produce images that are dependent on the unique optical properties of the material.

name: secretory rate
query: Query: secretory rate [SEP] Secretory rate is the amount of a substance secreted by cells or by a specific organ or organism over a given period of time; usually applies to those substances which are formed by glandular tissues and are released by them into biological fluids, e.g., secretory rate of corticosteroids by the adrenal cortex, secretory rate of gastric acid by the gastric mucosa.

name: sec translocation channels
query: Query: sec translocation channels [SEP] Sec translocation channels is universally conserved multiprotein complexes that form the protein transport channel of the general secretory (sec) pathway. The sec translocase is present in all bacteria, archaea, and eukaryotes. It is in the endoplasmic reticulum membrane of eukaryotic cells, in the thylakoid membrane in chloroplasts and in some protozoa in the [MASK].

name: sedentary behavior
query: Query: sedentary behavior [SEP] Sedentary behavior is behaviors during waking hours that have low energy expenditure and are often performed in a sitting or reclining posture.

name: seed bank
query: Query: seed bank [SEP] [MASK] bank is a repository of [MASK] maintained under optimal conditions that ensure long term storage, intended for use as a source of replenishment of [MASK] stock or plant genetic material.

name: seed dispersal
query: Query: seed dispersal [SEP] [MASK] dispersal is the various physical methods which include [MASK], insects, animals, tension, and water, by which a plant scatters its [MASK] away from the parent plant.

name: seedlings
query: Query: seedlings [SEP] Seedlings is young plants produced at the completion of germination of [MASK].

name: seed storage proteins
query: Query: seed storage proteins [SEP] [MASK] storage proteins is one or more types of plant [MASK] proteins providing the large amounts of amino acids utilized in germination and seedling growth. As [MASK] are the major food source from agricultural crops, [MASK] storage proteins are a major source of dietary proteins.

name: seizures , febrile
query: Query: seizures , febrile [SEP] Febrile seizures is seizures that occur during a febrile episode. It is a common condition, affecting 2-5% of children aged 3 months to five years. An autosomal dominant pattern of inheritance has been identified in some families. The majority are simple febrile seizures (generally defined as generalized onset, single seizures with a duration of less than 30 minutes). Complex febrile seizures are characterized by focal onset, duration greater than 30 minutes, and/or more than one seizure in a 24 hour period. The likelihood of developing epilepsy (i.e., a nonfebrile seizure disorder) following simple febrile seizures is low. Complex febrile seizures are associated with a moderately increased incidence of epilepsy. (From Menkes, Textbook of Child Neurology, 5th ed, p784)

name: selection , genetic
query: Query: selection , genetic [SEP] Genetic selection is differential and non-random reproduction of different genotypes, operating to alter the gene frequencies within a population.

name: selection bias
query: Query: selection bias [SEP] Selection bias is the introduction of error due to systematic differences in the characteristics between those selected and those not selected for a given study. In sampling bias, error is the result of failure to ensure that all members of the reference population have a known chance of selection in the sample.

name: self administration
query: Query: self administration [SEP] Self administration is administration of a drug or chemical by the individual under the direction of a physician. It includes administration clinically or experimentally, by human or animal.

name: self efficacy
query: Query: self efficacy [SEP] Self efficacy is cognitive mechanism based on expectations or beliefs about one's ability to perform actions necessary to produce a given effect. It is also a theoretical component of behavior change in various therapeutic treatments. (apa, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 1994)

name: self report
query: Query: self report [SEP] Self report is method for obtaining information through verbal responses, written or oral, from subjects.

name: semantics
query: Query: semantics [SEP] Semantics is the relationships between symbols and their meanings.

name: semantic web
query: Query: semantic web [SEP] Semantic web is a framework for development and promotion of common data formats and exchange protocols linked in a way that can be read directly by computers. Semantic Web is a platform for sharing and reusing data across application, enterprise, and community boundaries, by linking concepts rather than just documents.

name: semen
query: Query: semen [SEP] Semen is the thick, yellowish-[MASK], viscid fluid secretion of male reproductive organs discharged upon ejaculation. In addition to reproductive organ secretions, it contains spermatozoa and their nutrient plasma.

name: seminal vesicle secretory proteins
query: Query: seminal vesicle secretory proteins [SEP] Seminal [MASK] proteins is the secretory proteins of the seminal vesicles are proteins and enzymes that are important in the rapid clotting of the ejaculate. The major clotting protein is seminal vesicle-specific antigen. Many of these seminal vesicle proteins are under androgen regulation, and are substrates for the prostatic enzymes, such as the prostate-specific antigen, a protease and an esterase.

name: senior centers
query: Query: senior centers [SEP] Senior centers is community centers for older adults and providers of resources for the community. In addition to providing services and activities for older adults that reflect the community's diversity, they link participants with resources offered by other agencies.

name: sense of coherence
query: Query: sense of coherence [SEP] Sense of coherence is a view of the world and the individual's environment as comprehensible, manageable, and meaningful, claiming that the way people view their life has a positive influence on their health.

name: sensitivity training groups
query: Query: sensitivity training groups [SEP] Sensitivity training groups is a group of people who meet in an unstructured setting to learn about themselves, interpersonal relationships, and group processes and about larger social systems.

name: sensory deprivation
query: Query: sensory deprivation [SEP] Sensory deprivation is the absence or restriction of the usual external sensory stimuli to which the individual responds.

name: sensory gating
query: Query: sensory gating [SEP] Sensory gating is the ability of the brain to suppress neuronal responses to external sensory inputs, such as auditory and visual stimuli. Sensory filtering (or gating) allows humans to block out irrelevant, meaningless, or redundant stimuli.

name: sensory system agents
query: Query: sensory system agents [SEP] Sensory system agents is drugs that act on neuronal sensory receptors resulting in an increase, decrease, or modification of afferent nerve activity. (From Smith and Reynard, Textbook of Pharmacology, 1991, p367)

name: sentinel lymph node
query: Query: sentinel lymph node [SEP] Sentinel [MASK] node is first [MASK] node to receive drainage from the primary tumor. sentinel [MASK] node biopsy is performed to determine early metastasis status because cancer cells may appear first in the sentinel node.

name: sentinel lymph node biopsy
query: Query: sentinel lymph node biopsy [SEP] Sentinel [MASK] node biopsy is a diagnostic procedure used to determine whether [MASK] has occurred. The sentinel [MASK] node is the first [MASK] node to receive drainage from a neoplasm.

name: sentinel species
query: Query: sentinel species [SEP] Sentinel species is organisms used to determine measurable environmental risks or hazards to human health and or well-being, thereby serving as advance or early warning signs of impending danger to humans. Examples of sentinel species are monkeys, [MASK] pigs, and the fabled canary in the coal mine.

name: sentinel surveillance
query: Query: sentinel surveillance [SEP] Sentinel surveillance is monitoring of rate of occurrence of specific conditions to assess the stability or change in health levels of a population. It is also the study of disease rates in a specific cohort such as in a geographic area or population subgroup to estimate trends in a larger population. (From Last, Dictionary of Epidemiology, 2d ed)

name: seoul
query: Query: seoul [SEP] Seoul is the capital of south korea.

name: septal nuclei
query: Query: septal nuclei [SEP] Septal nuclei is neural nuclei situated in the septal region. They have afferent and cholinergic efferent connections with a variety of forebrain and brain stem areas including the hippocampal formation, the lateral hypothalamus, the tegmentum, and the amygdala. Included are the dorsal, lateral, medial, and triangular septal nuclei, septofimbrial nucleus, nucleus of diagonal band, nucleus of anterior commissure, and the nucleus of stria terminalis.

name: sequence alignment
query: Query: sequence alignment [SEP] Sequence alignment is the arrangement of two or more amino acid or base sequences from an organism or organisms in such a way as to align areas of the sequences sharing common properties. The degree of relatedness or homology between the sequences is predicted computationally or statistically based on weights assigned to the elements aligned between the sequences. This in turn can serve as a potential indicator of the genetic relatedness between the organisms.

name: sequence analysis , rna
query: Query: sequence analysis , rna [SEP] Rna sequence analysis is a multistage process that includes cloning, physical mapping, subcloning, sequencing, and information analysis of an rna sequence.

name: sequence tagged sites
query: Query: sequence tagged sites [SEP] Sequence tagged sites is short tracts of dna sequence that are used as landmarks in genome mapping. In most instances, 200 to 500 [MASK] of sequence define a Sequence Tagged Site (sts) that is operationally unique in the human genome (i.e., can be specifically detected by the polymerase chain reaction in the presence of all other genomic sequences). The overwhelming advantage of STSs over mapping landmarks defined in other ways is that the means of testing for the presence of a particular sts can be completely described as information in a [MASK].

name: serial extraction
query: Query: serial extraction [SEP] Serial extraction is the selective extraction of deciduous teeth during the stage of mixed dentition in accordance with the shedding and eruption of the teeth. It is done over an extended period to allow autonomous [MASK] to relieve crowding of the dental arches during the eruption of the lateral incisors, canines, and premolars, eventually involving the extraction of the first premolar teeth. (Dorland, 28th ed)

name: serial learning
query: Query: serial learning [SEP] Serial learning is learning to make a series of responses in exact order.

name: serial passage
query: Query: serial passage [SEP] Serial passage is inoculation of a series of animals or in vitro tissue with an infectious bacterium or virus, as in virulence studies and the development of vaccines.

name: serial publications
query: Query: serial publications [SEP] Serial publications is publications in any medium issued in successive parts bearing numerical or chronological designations and intended to be continued indefinitely. (ala Glossary of Library and Information Science, 1983, p203)

name: serine
query: Query: serine [SEP] Serine is a non-essential amino acid occurring in natural form as the L-isomer. It is synthesized from glycine or threonine. It is involved in the biosynthesis of purines; pyrimidines; and other amino acids.

name: serotonin antagonists
query: Query: serotonin antagonists [SEP] Serotonin antagonists is drugs that bind to but do not activate serotonin receptors, thereby blocking the actions of serotonin or serotonin receptor agonists.

name: serotonin plasma membrane transport proteins
query: Query: serotonin plasma membrane transport proteins [SEP] Serotonin plasma membrane transport proteins is sodium chloride-dependent neurotransmitter symporters located primarily on the plasma membrane of serotonergic neurons. They are different than serotonin receptors, which signal cellular responses to serotonin. They remove serotonin from the extracellular space by high affinity reuptake into presynaptic terminals. Regulates signal amplitude and duration at serotonergic synapses and is the site of action of the serotonin uptake inhibitors.

name: serotonin receptor agonists
query: Query: serotonin receptor agonists [SEP] Serotonin receptor agonists is endogenous compounds and drugs that bind to and activate serotonin receptors. Many serotonin receptor agonists are used as antidepressants; anxiolytics; and in the treatment of [MASK].

name: serotonin uptake inhibitors
query: Query: serotonin uptake inhibitors [SEP] Serotonin uptake inhibitors is compounds that specifically inhibit the reuptake of serotonin in the brain.

name: serum albumin , bovine
query: Query: serum albumin , bovine [SEP] Bovine serum albumin is serum albumin from cows, commonly used in in vitro biological studies. (From Stedman, 25th ed)

name: serum albumin , human
query: Query: serum albumin , human [SEP] Human serum albumin is serum albumin from humans. It is an essential carrier of both endogenous substances, such as fatty acids and bilirubin, and of xenobitoics in the blood.

name: serum sickness
query: Query: serum sickness [SEP] Serum sickness is immune complex disease caused by the administration of foreign serum or serum proteins and characterized by fever, lymphadenopathy, arthralgia, and urticaria. When they are complexed to protein carriers, some drugs can also cause serum sickness when they act as haptens inducing antibody responses.

name: severe acute malnutrition
query: Query: severe acute malnutrition [SEP] Severe acute malnutrition is acute form of malnutrition which usually affects children, characterized by a very low weight for height (below -3z scores of the median [MASK] Organization standards), visible severe wasting, or occurrence of nutritional edema.  It can be a direct or indirect cause of fatality in children suffering from [MASK] and pneumonia. Do not confuse with [MASK], a condition in which the body is not getting enough food, usually for extended periods of time.

name: severe acute respiratory syndrome
query: Query: severe acute respiratory syndrome [SEP] Severe acute respiratory syndrome is a viral disorder characterized by high fever, dry [MASK], shortness of breath (dyspnea) or breathing difficulties, and atypical pneumonia. a virus in the genus coronavirus is the suspected agent.

name: severe dengue
query: Query: severe dengue [SEP] Severe dengue is a virulent form of dengue characterized by thrombocytopenia and an increase in vascular permeability (grades i and ii) and distinguished by a positive pain test (e.g., [MASK]). When accompanied by shock (grades iii and iv), it is called dengue shock syndrome.

name: sex characteristics
query: Query: sex characteristics [SEP] [MASK] characteristics is those characteristics that distinguish one [MASK] from the other. The primary [MASK] characteristics are the ovaries and testes and their related hormones. Secondary [MASK] characteristics are those which are masculine or feminine but not directly related to reproduction.

name: sex chromatin
query: Query: sex chromatin [SEP] [MASK] chromatin is in the interphase nucleus, a condensed mass of chromatin representing an inactivated x chromosome. Each x chromosome, in excess of one, forms [MASK] chromatin (Barr body) in the mammalian nucleus. (from King & Stansfield, a Dictionary of Genetics, 4th ed)

name: sex counseling
query: Query: sex counseling [SEP] [MASK] counseling is advice and support given to individuals to help them understand and resolve their sexual [MASK] problems. It excludes treatment for psychosexual disorders or psychosexual dysfunction.

name: sex determination by skeleton
query: Query: sex determination by skeleton [SEP] [MASK] determination by skeleton is validation of the [MASK] of an individual by means of the bones of the skeleton. It is most commonly based on the appearance of the pelvis; skull; sternum; and/or long bones.

name: sex determination processes
query: Query: sex determination processes [SEP] [MASK] determination processes is the mechanisms by which the [MASK] of an individual's gonads are fixed.

name: sex differentiation
query: Query: sex differentiation [SEP] [MASK] differentiation is the process in developing [MASK]- or gender-specific tissue, organ, or function after [MASK] determination processes have [MASK] the [MASK] of the gonads. Major areas of [MASK] differentiation occur in the reproductive tract (genitalia) and the brain.

name: sex factors
query: Query: sex factors [SEP] [MASK] factors is maleness or femaleness as a constituent element or influence contributing to the production of a result. It may be applicable to the cause or effect of a circumstance. It is used with human or animal concepts but should be differentiated from [MASK] characteristics, anatomical or physiological manifestations of [MASK], and from [MASK] distribution, the number of males and females in given circumstances.

name: sex ratio
query: Query: sex ratio [SEP] [MASK] ratio is the number of males per 100 females.

name: sexual dysfunction , physiological
query: Query: sexual dysfunction , physiological [SEP] Physiological sexual dysfunction is physiological disturbances in normal sexual performance in either the male or the female.

name: sexual health
query: Query: sexual health [SEP] Sexual health is a state of physical, emotional, mental and social well-being in relation to sexuality, according to the [MASK] Organization.

name: sexual maturation
query: Query: sexual maturation [SEP] Sexual maturation is achievement of full sexual capacity in animals and in humans.

name: sex work
query: Query: sex work [SEP] [MASK] work is the act or practice of engaging in sexual relations for money or other benefit.

name: sex workers
query: Query: sex workers [SEP] [MASK] workers is people who engage in occupational sexual behavior in exchange for economic rewards or other extrinsic considerations.

name: shape memory alloys
query: Query: shape memory alloys [SEP] Shape memory alloys is alloys designed to recover their original shape upon [MASK].

name: shared governance , nursing
query: Query: shared governance , nursing [SEP] Nursing shared governance is model of nursing practice with shared decision processes designed to integrate core values and beliefs that professional practice embraces, as a means of achieving quality care.

name: sheep , domestic
query: Query: sheep , domestic [SEP] Domestic sheep is a species of sheep, Ovis aries, descended from Near Eastern wild forms, especially mouflon.

name: shock , septic
query: Query: shock , septic [SEP] Septic shock is sepsis associated with hypotension or hypoperfusion despite adequate fluid resuscitation. Perfusion abnormalities may include, but are not limited to [MASK]; oliguria; or acute alteration in mental status.

name: shock , surgical
query: Query: shock , surgical [SEP] Surgical shock is a type of shock that occurs as a result of a surgical procedure.

name: shock , traumatic
query: Query: shock , traumatic [SEP] Traumatic shock is shock produced as a result of trauma.

name: short bowel syndrome
query: Query: short bowel syndrome [SEP] Short bowel syndrome is a malabsorption syndrome resulting from extensive operative resection of the small intestine, the absorptive region of the gastrointestinal tract.

name: shoulder dislocation
query: Query: shoulder dislocation [SEP] [MASK] dislocation is displacement of the humerus from the scapula.

name: shoulder fractures
query: Query: shoulder fractures [SEP] [MASK] fractures is fractures of the proximal humerus, including the head, anatomic and surgical [MASK], and tuberosities.

name: shoulder joint
query: Query: shoulder joint [SEP] [MASK] joint is the articulation between the head of the humerus and the glenoid cavity of the scapula.

name: shoulder prosthesis
query: Query: shoulder prosthesis [SEP] [MASK] prosthesis is replacement for a [MASK] joint.

name: sibling relations
query: Query: sibling relations [SEP] Sibling relations is interactions and relationships between sisters and/or brothers. The concept also applies to animal studies.

name: siblings
query: Query: siblings [SEP] Siblings is persons or animals having at least one parent in common. (American College Dictionary, 3d ed)

name: sigmoid neoplasms
query: Query: sigmoid neoplasms [SEP] Sigmoid neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the sigmoid colon.

name: signaling lymphocytic activation molecule family member 1
query: Query: signaling lymphocytic activation molecule family member 1 [SEP] Signaling lymphocytic activation molecule family member 1 is a 70-kDa slam family receptor that consists of an extracellular immunoglobulin-like domain and an immunoglobulin c2-[MASK] domain. It is expressed primarily by thymocytes and activated t-lymphocytes, as well as by macrophages and [MASK]. It binds slamf1 receptors on other cells to mediate T-cell maturation and proliferation. It is also a receptor for the measles virus.

name: sign language
query: Query: sign language [SEP] Sign language is a system of hand gestures used for communication by the deaf or by people speaking different languages.

name: sign or symptom
query: Query: sign or symptom [SEP] Sign or symptom is clinical manifestations that can be either objective when observed by a physician, or subjective when perceived by the patient.

name: silent information regulator proteins , saccharomyces cerevisiae
query: Query: silent information regulator proteins , saccharomyces cerevisiae [SEP] Saccharomyces cerevisiae silent information regulator proteins is a [MASK] of nuclear proteins in saccharomyces cerevisiae that are required for the transcriptional repression of the silent mating type loci. They mediate the formation of silenced chromatin and repress both transcription and recombination at other loci as well. They are comprised of 4 non-homologous, interacting proteins, Sir1p, Sir2p, Sir3p, and Sir4p. Sir2p, an NAD-dependent histone deacetylase, is the founding member of the family of sirtuins.

name: silent mutation
query: Query: silent mutation [SEP] Silent mutation is a change to a dna sequence that doesn't change the amino acid sequence of the protein made.

name: silver
query: Query: silver [SEP] Silver is an element with the atomic symbol Ag, atomic number 47, and atomic weight 107.87. It is a soft metal that is used medically in surgical instruments, dental prostheses, and alloys. Long-continued use of silver [MASK] can lead to a form of poisoning known as argyria.

name: silver nitrate
query: Query: silver nitrate [SEP] Silver nitrate is a silver [MASK] with powerful germicidal activity. It has been used topically to prevent ophthalmia neonatorum.

name: silver proteins
query: Query: silver proteins [SEP] Silver proteins is compounds of silver and proteins used as topical anti-infective agents.

name: silver staining
query: Query: silver staining [SEP] Silver staining is the use of silver, usually silver nitrate, as a reagent for producing contrast or coloration in tissue specimens.

name: simplified acute physiology score
query: Query: simplified acute physiology score [SEP] Simplified acute physiology score is a severity of disease classification system designed to measure the severity of disease for patients aged 15 and over admitted to intensive care units.

name: single molecule imaging
query: Query: single molecule imaging [SEP] Single molecule imaging is high resolution imaging techniques that allow visualization of individual molecules of proteins, lipids, or nucleic acids within cells or tissues.

name: single parent
