query: Query: single parent [SEP] Single parent is a natural, adoptive, or substitute parent of a dependent child, who lives with only one parent. The single parent may live with or visit the child. The concept includes the never-married, as well as the divorced and widowed.

name: single photon emission computed tomography computed tomography
query: Query: single photon emission computed tomography computed tomography [SEP] Single photon emission computed tomography computed tomography is an imaging technique using a device which combines tomography, emission-computed, single-photon and tomography, x-ray computed in the same session.

name: sinus arrest , cardiac
query: Query: sinus arrest , cardiac [SEP] Cardiac sinus arrest is the omission of atrial activation that is caused by transient cessation of impulse generation at the sinoatrial node. It is characterized by a prolonged pause without p wave in an electrocardiogram. Sinus arrest has been associated with sleep apnea (rem sleep-related sinus arrest).

name: sinus floor augmentation
query: Query: sinus floor augmentation [SEP] Sinus floor augmentation is guided bone transplantation of the maxillary sinus surface with a bone substitute grafting. It increases the bone volume at the site of the dental implant and helps stabilize it.

name: sitting position
query: Query: sitting position [SEP] Sitting position is a standard patient position in which the patient is seated in a semi-sitting position (45-60 degrees) and may have [MASK] either bent or straight.

name: size perception
query: Query: size perception [SEP] Size perception is the sensory interpretation of the dimensions of objects.

name: skilled nursing facilities
query: Query: skilled nursing facilities [SEP] Skilled nursing facilities is extended care facilities which provide skilled nursing care or rehabilitation services for inpatients on a daily basis.

name: skin , artificial
query: Query: skin , artificial [SEP] Artificial skin is synthetic material used for the treatment of burns and other conditions involving large-scale loss of skin. It often consists of an outer (epidermal) layer of silicone and an inner (dermal) layer of collagen and chondroitin 6-sulfate. The dermal layer elicits new growth and vascular invasion and the outer layer is later removed and replaced by a [MASK].

name: skin abnormalities
query: Query: skin abnormalities [SEP] Skin abnormalities is congenital structural abnormalities of the skin.

name: skin absorption
query: Query: skin absorption [SEP] Skin absorption is uptake of substances through the skin.

name: skin aging
query: Query: skin aging [SEP] Skin aging is the process of aging due to changes in the structure and elasticity of the skin over time. It may be a part of physiological aging or it may be due to the effects of ultraviolet radiation, usually through exposure to sunlight.

name: skin cream
query: Query: skin cream [SEP] Skin cream is a water-soluble medicinal preparation applied to the skin.

name: skin diseases , metabolic
query: Query: skin diseases , metabolic [SEP] Metabolic skin diseases is diseases of the skin associated with underlying metabolic disorders.

name: skin diseases , parasitic
query: Query: skin diseases , parasitic [SEP] Parasitic skin diseases is skin diseases caused by arthropods; helminths; or other parasites.

name: skin manifestations
query: Query: skin manifestations [SEP] Skin manifestations is dermatologic disorders attendant upon non-dermatologic disease or injury.

name: skin neoplasms
query: Query: skin neoplasms [SEP] Skin neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the skin.

name: skin temperature
query: Query: skin temperature [SEP] Skin temperature is the temperature at the outer surface of the body.

name: skin transplantation
query: Query: skin transplantation [SEP] Skin transplantation is the grafting of skin in humans or animals from one site to another to replace a lost portion of the body surface skin.

name: skull base neoplasms
query: Query: skull base neoplasms [SEP] Skull base neoplasms is neoplasms of the base of the skull specifically, differentiated from neoplasms of unspecified sites or bones of the skull (skull neoplasms).

name: skull fracture , depressed
query: Query: skull fracture , depressed [SEP] Depressed skull fracture is a skull fracture characterized by inward depression of a fragment or section of cranial bone, often compressing the underlying dura mater and brain. Depressed cranial fractures which feature open skin wounds that communicate with skull fragments are referred to as compound depressed skull fractures.

name: sleep , rem
query: Query: sleep , rem [SEP] Rem sleep is a stage of sleep characterized by rapid movements of the eye and low voltage fast pattern eeg. It is usually associated with dreaming.

name: sleep deprivation
query: Query: sleep deprivation [SEP] Sleep deprivation is the state of being deprived of sleep under experimental conditions, due to life events, or from a wide variety of pathophysiologic causes such as medication effect, chronic illness, psychiatric illness, or sleep disorder.

name: sleep hygiene
query: Query: sleep hygiene [SEP] Sleep hygiene is habits and practices conducive to getting the right amount and quality of sleep, and include  responding to environmental factors that may influence one's sleep.

name: sleep latency
query: Query: sleep latency [SEP] Sleep latency is the time it takes to reach rem sleep. It is typically measured by polysomnography or eeg as a part of various sleep pattern tests (e.g., multiple sleep latency test).

name: sleep medicine specialty
query: Query: sleep medicine specialty [SEP] Sleep medicine specialty is a medical specialty concerned with the diagnosis and treatment of sleep wake disorders and their causes.

name: sleep wake disorders
query: Query: sleep wake disorders [SEP] Sleep wake disorders is abnormal sleep-wake schedule or pattern associated with the circadian rhythm which affect the length, timing, and/or rigidity of the sleep-wake cycle relative to the day-night cycle.

name: slit ventricle syndrome
query: Query: slit ventricle syndrome [SEP] Slit ventricle syndrome is an intermittent and self-limiting headache disorder in individuals with cerebrospinal fluid shunts emplaced for the treatment of hydrocephalus. The symptoms of headache, vomiting, and cranial neuropathies are associated with intermittent obstruction of the shunt.

name: smad proteins , inhibitory
query: Query: smad proteins , inhibitory [SEP] Inhibitory smad proteins is a sub-family of smad proteins that inhibit cell signaling by receptor-regulated smad proteins. They form autoinhibitory [MASK] loops in the tgf-beta signaling pathway and mediate signaling cross-talk with other signaling pathways

name: small business
query: Query: small business [SEP] Small business is for-profit enterprise with relatively few to moderate number of employees and low to moderate volume of sales.

name: small fiber neuropathy
query: Query: small fiber neuropathy [SEP] Small fiber neuropathy is disorder of the peripheral nerves that primarily impair small nerve fibers. The affected small nerve fibers include myelinated A-delta fibers (see a fibers) and unmyelinated c fibers. Because these small fibers innervate skin and help control autonomic function, their neuropathy presents with neuropathic pain, reduced thermal and pain sensitivity, and autonomic dysfunction (e.g. abnormal sweating or facial flushing). Small fiber neuropathy can be idiopathic or associated with underlying diseases (e.g., amyloidosis; diabetes mellitus; sarcoidosis; or vasculitis).

name: smart glasses
query: Query: smart glasses [SEP] Smart glasses is computerized eyewear with multiple technological applications for advanced computing and interoperability. Smart glasses are optimized to facilitate information and data access, capture, display, transfer, and manipulation.

name: smear layer
query: Query: smear layer [SEP] Smear layer is adherent debris produced when cutting the enamel or dentin in cavity preparation. It is about 1 micron thick and its composition reflects the underlying dentin, although different quantities and qualities of smear layer can be produced by the various instrumentation techniques. Its function is presumed to be protective, as it lowers [MASK]. However, it masks the underlying dentin and interferes with attempts to bond dental material to the dentin.

name: smoke inhalation injury
query: Query: smoke inhalation injury [SEP] Smoke [MASK] injury is pulmonary injury following the breathing in of toxic smoke from burning materials such as plastics, synthetics, building materials, etc. This injury is the most frequent [MASK] in burn patients.

name: smokers
query: Query: smokers [SEP] Smokers is persons with a history or habit of smoking.

name: smoking cessation
query: Query: smoking cessation [SEP] Smoking cessation is discontinuing the habit of smoking.

name: smoking cessation agents
query: Query: smoking cessation agents [SEP] Smoking cessation agents is substances that facilitate the cessation of tobacco smoking.

name: smoking reduction
query: Query: smoking reduction [SEP] Smoking reduction is a decrease in the incidence and frequency of smoking. Smoking reduction differs from smoking cessation in that the smoker continues to smoke albeit at a lesser frequency without quitting.

name: smoking water pipes
query: Query: smoking water pipes [SEP] Smoking water pipes is pipes for smoking tobacco, cannabis, and other substances, in which smoke is drawn through water. Do not confuse with smoking pipes.

name: snow sports
query: Query: snow sports [SEP] [MASK] sports is sports activities in the [MASK].

name: social communication disorder
query: Query: social communication disorder [SEP] Social communication disorder is persistent difficulties in the social uses of verbal and nonverbal communications. ([MASK])

name: social conditions
query: Query: social conditions [SEP] Social conditions is the state of society as it exists or in flux. While it usually refers to society as a whole in a specified geographical or political region, it is applicable also to restricted strata of a society.

name: social determinants of health
query: Query: social determinants of health [SEP] Social determinants of health is the circumstances in which people are born, grow up, live, work, and age, as well as the systems put in place to deal with illness. These circumstances are in turn shaped by a wider [MASK] of forces: economics, social policies, and politics (http://www.cdc.gov/socialdeterminants/).

name: social discrimination
query: Query: social discrimination [SEP] Social discrimination is group behavior toward others by virtue of their group membership.

name: social dominance
query: Query: social dominance [SEP] Social dominance is social structure of a group as it relates to the relative social rank of dominance status of its members. (apa, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 8th ed.)

name: social facilitation
query: Query: social facilitation [SEP] Social facilitation is any enhancement of a motivated behavior in which individuals do the same thing with some degree of mutual stimulation and consequent coordination.

name: social identification
query: Query: social identification [SEP] Social identification is the process by which an aspect of self image is developed based on in-group preference or ethnocentrism and a perception of belonging to a social or cultural group. (From apa, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 8th ed.)

name: social justice
query: Query: social justice [SEP] Social justice is an interactive process whereby members of a community are concerned for the equality and rights of all.

name: social learning
query: Query: social learning [SEP] Social learning is the concept of new knowledge acquisition through [MASK] and interaction with others.

name: social marketing
query: Query: social marketing [SEP] Social marketing is use of marketing principles also used to sell products to consumers to promote ideas, attitudes and behaviors. Design and use of programs seeking to increase the acceptance of a social idea or practice by target groups, not for the benefit of the marketer, but to benefit the target audience and the general society.

name: social media
query: Query: social media [SEP] Social media is platforms that provide the ability and tools to create and publish information accessed via the internet. Generally these platforms have three characteristics with content user generated, high degree of interaction between creator and viewer, and easily integrated with other sites.

name: social mobility
query: Query: social mobility [SEP] Social mobility is the movement or shifting of membership between or within social classes by individuals or by groups.

name: social norms
query: Query: social norms [SEP] Social norms is customary standards that govern behavior in groups, cultures, or societies. They reflect what a group deems acceptable in a social context in terms of appropriate and inappropriate values, beliefs, attitudes, and behaviors.

name: social participation
query: Query: social participation [SEP] Social participation is involvement in community activities or programs.

name: social skills
query: Query: social skills [SEP] Social skills is the personal [MASK] of abilities required to successfully interact and communicate with others, both verbally and non-verbally through gestures, body language and personal appearance.

name: social theory
query: Query: social theory [SEP] Social theory is frameworks of empirical evidence used to study and interpret social phenomena.

name: social validity , research
query: Query: social validity , research [SEP] Research social validity is evaluation of the degree of acceptance for the immediate variables associated with a procedure or program designed to change behavior. This includes the social significance of the goals of treatment, the social appropriateness of the treatment procedures, and the social importance of the effects of treatments.

name: social values
query: Query: social values [SEP] Social values is [MASK] standards or empirical variables in social life which are believed to be important and/or desirable.

name: social work , psychiatric
query: Query: social work , psychiatric [SEP] Psychiatric social work is use of all social work processes in the treatment of patients in a psychiatric or mental health setting.

name: social work department , hospital
query: Query: social work department , hospital [SEP] Hospital social work department is hospital department responsible for administering and providing social services to patients and their families.

name: social workers
query: Query: social workers [SEP] Social workers is professionals who work with persons affected by social disadvantages such as poverty; mental and physical illness or disability, and social injustice.  Their focus is on both the individual and his or her environment, including violations of their civil liberties and human rights.

name: societies , veterinary
query: Query: societies , veterinary [SEP] Veterinary societies is organizations having institutional membership limited to veterinarians and veterinary institutions.

name: sodium acetate
query: Query: sodium acetate [SEP] Sodium acetate is the trihydrate sodium [MASK] of acetic acid, which is used as a source of sodium ions in solutions for dialysis and as a systemic and urinary alkalizer, diuretic, and expectorant.

name: sodium bicarbonate
query: Query: sodium bicarbonate [SEP] Sodium bicarbonate is a [MASK], crystalline powder that is commonly used as a pH buffering agent, an electrolyte replenisher, systemic alkalizer and in topical cleansing solutions.

name: sodium chloride , dietary
query: Query: sodium chloride , dietary [SEP] Dietary sodium chloride is sodium chloride used in foods.

name: sodium fluoride
query: Query: sodium fluoride [SEP] Sodium fluoride is a source of inorganic fluoride which is used topically to prevent dental caries.

name: sodium hydroxide
query: Query: sodium hydroxide [SEP] Sodium hydroxide is a highly caustic substance that is used to neutralize acids and make sodium [MASK]. (From Merck Index, 11th ed)

name: sodium iodide
query: Query: sodium iodide [SEP] Sodium iodide is a compound forming [MASK], odorless deliquescent crystals and used as iodine supplement, expectorant or in its radioactive (i-131) form as an diagnostic aid, particularly for thyroid function tests.

name: sodium isotopes
query: Query: sodium isotopes [SEP] Sodium isotopes is stable sodium atoms that have the same atomic number as the element sodium, but differ in atomic weight. Na-23 is a stable sodium isotope.

name: sodium nitrite
query: Query: sodium nitrite [SEP] Sodium nitrite is nitrous acid sodium [MASK]. Used in many industrial processes, in meat curing, coloring, and preserving, and as a reagent in analytical chemistry techniques. It is used therapeutically as an antidote in cyanide poisoning. The compound is toxic and mutagenic and will react in vivo with secondary or tertiary amines thereby producing highly carcinogenic nitrosamines.

name: soft tissue injuries
query: Query: soft tissue injuries [SEP] Soft tissue injuries is injuries of tissue other than bone. The concept is usually general and does not customarily refer to internal organs or viscera. It is meaningful with reference to regions or organs where soft tissue (muscle, fat, skin) should be differentiated from bones or bone tissue, as "soft tissue injuries of the hand".

name: software design
query: Query: software design [SEP] Software design is specifications and instructions applied to the software.

name: solid phase extraction
query: Query: solid phase extraction [SEP] Solid phase extraction is an extraction method that separates analytes using a solid phase and a liquid phase. It is used for preparative sample cleanup before analysis by chromatography and other analytical methods.

name: solid waste
query: Query: solid waste [SEP] Solid waste is garbage, refuse, or [MASK], or other discarded materials from a [MASK] plant, water supply treatment plant, and air pollution [MASK] that include solid, semi-solid, or contained material. It does not include materials dissolved in domestic [MASK], irrigation return flows, or industrial discharges.

name: solitary fibrous tumor , pleural
query: Query: solitary fibrous tumor , pleural [SEP] Pleural solitary fibrous tumor is a rare neoplasm, usually benign, derived from mesenchymal fibroblasts located in the submesothelial lining of the pleura. It spite of its various synonyms, it has no features of mesothelial cells and is not related to malignant mesothelioma or asbestos exposure.

name: solitary pulmonary nodule
query: Query: solitary pulmonary nodule [SEP] Solitary pulmonary nodule is a single lung lesion that is characterized by a small round mass of tissue, usually less than 1 cm in diameter, and can be detected by chest radiography. a solitary pulmonary nodule can be associated with neoplasm, tuberculosis, cyst, or other anomalies in the lung, the chest wall, or the pleura.

name: solubility
query: Query: solubility [SEP] Solubility is the ability of a substance to be dissolved, i.e. to form a solution with another substance. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

name: solute carrier family 22 member 5
query: Query: solute carrier family 22 member 5 [SEP] Solute carrier family 22 member 5 is a high-affinity, ATP-binding, co-transporter for carnitine that is highly expressed in kidney, skeletal muscle, heart, and placental tissues. It transports one sodium ion with one carnitine molecule. It has a lower affinity for other organic cations and transports them independently of sodium. Mutations in the slc22a5 gene are associated with systemic carnitine deficiency.

name: somatosensory cortex
query: Query: somatosensory cortex [SEP] Somatosensory cortex is area of the parietal lobe concerned with receiving sensations such as movement, pain, pressure, position, temperature, touch, and vibration. It lies posterior to the central sulcus.

name: somatosensory disorders
query: Query: somatosensory disorders [SEP] Somatosensory disorders is disorders of sensory information received from superficial and deep regions of the body. The somatosensory system conveys neural impulses which pertain to proprioception, tactile sensation, thermal sensation, pressure sensation, and pain. peripheral nervous system diseases; spinal cord diseases; and brain diseases may be associated with impaired or abnormal somatic sensation.

name: sos response , genetics
query: Query: sos response , genetics [SEP] Genetics sos response is an error-prone mechanism or [MASK] of functions for repairing damaged microbial dna. sos functions (a concept reputedly derived from the sos of the international distress signal) are involved in dna repair and mutagenesis, in cell division inhibition, in recovery of normal physiological conditions after dna repair, and possibly in cell death when dna damage is extensive.

name: south africa
query: Query: south africa [SEP] South africa is a republic in southern Africa, the southernmost part of Africa. It has three capitals: Pretoria (administrative), Cape Town (legislative), and Bloemfontein (judicial). Officially the Republic of South Africa since 1960, it was called the Union of South Africa 1910-1960.

name: south australia
query: Query: south australia [SEP] South australia is a state in south central Australia. Its capital is Adelaide. It was probably first visited by f. Thyssen in 1627. Later discoveries in 1802 and 1830 opened up the southern part. It became a British province in 1836 with this self-descriptive name and became a state in 1901. (From Webster's New Geographical Dictionary, 1988, p1135)

name: sox transcription factors
query: Query: sox transcription factors [SEP] Sox transcription factors is a large family of structurally-related transcription factors that were originally discovered based upon their close sequence homology to an HMG-box domain found in [MASK]-determining region y protein. Many sox transcription factors play important roles in regulating cell differentiation. The numerous members of this family are organized in several subgroups according to structural identities found within the proteins.

name: soy milk
query: Query: soy milk [SEP] Soy milk is a beverage prepared from soybeans.

name: spacecraft
query: Query: spacecraft [SEP] Spacecraft is devices, manned and unmanned, which are designed to be placed into an [MASK] about the Earth or into a trajectory to another celestial body. (nasa Thesaurus, 1988)

name: space motion sickness
query: Query: space motion sickness [SEP] Space motion sickness is disorder characterized by nausea, vomiting, and dizziness, possibly in response to vestibular disorientation or fluid shifts associated with space flight. (From Webster's New World Dictionary)

name: space research
query: Query: space research [SEP] Space research is studies of interactions between living organisms and characteristics of the extraterrestrial environment. These studies specifically address the structure and function of living organisms in an extraterrestrial environment and interdependent relationships of organisms with each other and/or the extraterrestrial environment while also touching on the origin, evolution and potential for extraterrestrial life. (From www.nasa.gov/audience/foreducators/spacelife/)

name: space simulation
query: Query: space simulation [SEP] Space simulation is an environment simulating one or more parameters of the space environment, applied in testing space systems or components. Often, a closed chamber is used, capable of approximating the vacuum and normal environments of space. (From nasa Thesaurus, 1988) This also includes simulated extravehicular activity studies in [MASK] or water tanks.

name: spatial processing
query: Query: spatial processing [SEP] Spatial processing is integration of spatial information perceived by visual and/or auditory cues.

name: spatial regression
query: Query: spatial regression [SEP] Spatial regression is methods used to take into account and incorporate spatial autocorrelation and regional variation into regression analysis models of data that has spatial dependency, and also to provide information on the spatial relationships among the variables.

name: specialization
query: Query: specialization [SEP] Specialization is an occupation limited in scope to a subsection of a broader field.

name: species specificity
query: Query: species specificity [SEP] Species specificity is the restriction of a characteristic behavior, anatomical structure or physical system, such as immune response; metabolic response, or gene or gene variant to the members of one species. It refers to that property which differentiates one species from another but it is also used for phylogenetic levels higher or lower than the species.

name: specific gravity
query: Query: specific gravity [SEP] Specific gravity is the ratio of the density of a material to the density of some standard material, such as water or air, at a specified temperature.

name: spectrometry , mass , secondary ion
query: Query: spectrometry , mass , secondary ion [SEP] Secondary ion mass spectrometry is a mass-spectrometric technique that is used for microscopic chemical analysis. a beam of primary ions with an energy of 5-20 kiloelectronvolts (keV) bombards a small spot on the surface of the sample under ultra-high vacuum conditions. Positive and negative secondary ions sputtered from the surface are analyzed in a mass spectrometer in regards to their mass-to-charge ratio. Digital imaging can be generated from the secondary ion beams and their intensity can be measured. Ionic images can be correlated with images from light or other microscopy providing useful tools in the study of molecular and drug actions.

name: spectrum analysis , raman
query: Query: spectrum analysis , raman [SEP] Raman spectrum analysis is analysis of the intensity of Raman scattering of monochromatic light as a function of frequency of the scattered light.

name: speech articulation tests
query: Query: speech articulation tests [SEP] [MASK] articulation tests is tests of accuracy in pronouncing [MASK] sounds, e.g., Iowa Pressure Articulation Test, Deep Test of Articulation, Templin-Darley Tests of Articulation, Goldman-Fristoe Test of Articulation, Screening [MASK] Articulation Test, Arizona Articulation Proficiency Scale.

name: speech perception
query: Query: speech perception [SEP] [MASK] perception is the process whereby an utterance is decoded into a representation in terms of linguistic units (sequences of phonetic segments which combine to form lexical and grammatical morphemes).

name: speech recognition software
query: Query: speech recognition software [SEP] [MASK] recognition software is software capable of recognizing dictation and transcribing the spoken words into written text.

name: speech therapy
query: Query: speech therapy [SEP] [MASK] therapy is treatment for individuals with [MASK] defects and disorders that involves counseling and use of various exercises and aids to help the development of new [MASK] habits.

name: sperm count
query: Query: sperm count [SEP] Sperm count is a count of sperm in the ejaculum, expressed as number per milliliter.

name: sperm head
query: Query: sperm head [SEP] Sperm head is the anterior portion of the spermatozoon (spermatozoa) that contains mainly the nucleus with highly compact chromatin material.

name: sperm motility
query: Query: sperm motility [SEP] Sperm motility is movement characteristics of spermatozoa in a fresh specimen. It is measured as the percentage of sperms that are moving, and as the percentage of sperms with productive flagellar motion such as rapid, linear, and forward progression.

name: sperm retrieval
query: Query: sperm retrieval [SEP] Sperm retrieval is procedures to obtain viable sperm from the male reproductive tract, including the testes, the epididymis, or the vas deferens.

name: sperm tail
query: Query: sperm tail [SEP] Sperm tail is the posterior filiform portion of the spermatozoon (spermatozoa) that provides sperm motility.

name: s phase
query: Query: s phase [SEP] S phase is phase of the cell cycle following g1 and preceding g2 when the entire dna content of the nucleus is replicated. It is achieved by bidirectional replication at multiple sites along each chromosome.

name: spinal cord regeneration
query: Query: spinal cord regeneration [SEP] Spinal cord regeneration is repair of the damaged neuron function after spinal cord injury or spinal cord diseases.

name: spinal cord stimulation
query: Query: spinal cord stimulation [SEP] Spinal cord stimulation is application of electric current to the spine for treatment of a variety of conditions involving innervation from the spinal cord.

name: spinal fractures
query: Query: spinal fractures [SEP] Spinal fractures is broken bones in the vertebral column.

name: spinal neoplasms
query: Query: spinal neoplasms [SEP] Spinal neoplasms is new abnormal growth of tissue in the spine.

name: spinal stenosis
query: Query: spinal stenosis [SEP] Spinal stenosis is narrowing of the spinal canal.

name: spindle pole bodies
query: Query: spindle pole bodies [SEP] Spindle pole bodies is [MASK] organizing centers of fungi and diatoms. They are embedded in the nuclear envelope and evolve into the spindle apparatus during cell division.

name: spin labels
query: Query: spin labels [SEP] Spin labels is molecules which contain an atom or a group of atoms exhibiting an unpaired [MASK] spin that can be detected by [MASK] and can be bonded to another molecule. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Chemical and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

name: spin trapping
query: Query: spin trapping [SEP] Spin trapping is a technique for detecting short-lived reactive free radicals in biological systems by providing a nitrone or nitrose compound for an addition reaction to occur which produces an [MASK]-detectable aminoxyl radical. In spin trapping, the compound trapping the radical is called the spin trap and the addition product of the radical is identified as the spin adduct. (Free Rad Res Comm 1990;9(3-6):163)

name: spiral ganglion
query: Query: spiral ganglion [SEP] Spiral ganglion is the sensory ganglion of the cochlear nerve. The cells of the spiral ganglion send fibers peripherally to the cochlear hair cells and centrally to the cochlear nuclei of the brain stem.

name: spirit possession
query: Query: spirit possession [SEP] Spirit possession is the idea that abnormal behavior or a medical condition is evidence that a person is under the control of a supernatural power or spirit. This belief was most commonly held in religion and medicine of the medieval period and is also held in many tribal cultures today.

name: spiro compounds
query: Query: spiro compounds [SEP] Spiro compounds is cyclic compounds that include two rings which share a single atom (usually a carbon). The simplest example of this type of compound is Spiro[2.2]pentane, which looks like a bow tie.

name: spleen
query: Query: spleen [SEP] Spleen is an encapsulated lymphatic organ through which venous blood filters.

name: splenic artery
query: Query: splenic artery [SEP] Splenic artery is the largest branch of the celiac trunk with distribution to the spleen, pancreas, stomach and greater omentum.

name: splenic infarction
query: Query: splenic infarction [SEP] Splenic infarction is insufficiency of arterial or venous blood supply to the spleen due to emboli, thrombi, vascular torsion, or pressure that produces a macroscopic area of necrosis. (From Stedman, 25th ed)

name: splenic neoplasms
query: Query: splenic neoplasms [SEP] Splenic neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the spleen.

name: splenic rupture
query: Query: splenic rupture [SEP] Splenic rupture is rupture of the spleen due to trauma or disease.

name: splenic vein
query: Query: splenic vein [SEP] Splenic vein is vein formed by the union (at the hilus of the spleen) of several small veins from the stomach, pancreas, spleen and mesentery.

name: spontaneous combustion
query: Query: spontaneous combustion [SEP] Spontaneous combustion is a circumstance where a substance or organism takes fire and burns without an exogenous source. Spontaneous human combustion differs from preternatural human combustibility in that in the latter, some spark or trivial flame sets the fire and the body tissues, which have a greatly enhanced inflammability, continue to undergo incineration without any external heat source or combustible materials. (Bergman na. Spontaneous human combustion: its role in literature and science. Pharos 1988;Fall;51(4):18-21)

name: spores , bacterial
query: Query: spores , bacterial [SEP] Bacterial spores is heat and stain resistant, metabolically inactive bodies formed within the vegetative cells of bacteria of the genera Bacillus and Clostridium.

name: spores , fungal
query: Query: spores , fungal [SEP] Fungal spores is reproductive bodies produced by fungi.

name: sports equipment
query: Query: sports equipment [SEP] Sports equipment is equipment required for engaging in a sport (such as balls, bats, rackets, skis, skates, ropes, weights) and devices for the protection of [MASK] during their performance (such as masks, gloves, mouth pieces).

name: sports nutritional physiological phenomena
query: Query: sports nutritional physiological phenomena [SEP] Sports nutritional physiological phenomena is nutritional physiology related to exercise or athletic performance.

name: sports nutritional sciences
query: Query: sports nutritional sciences [SEP] Sports nutritional sciences is the study of nutrition processes during exercise and athletic performance as well as specific [MASK] of [MASK] and the relationship between [MASK] and nutrition disorders in [MASK].

name: spouse abuse
query: Query: spouse abuse [SEP] Spouse abuse is deliberate severe and repeated injury to one domestic partner by the other.

name: sputum
query: Query: sputum [SEP] Sputum is material coughed up from the lungs and expectorated via the mouth. It contains mucus, cellular debris, and microorganisms. It may also contain blood or pus.

name: squamous cell carcinoma of head and neck
query: Query: squamous cell carcinoma of head and neck [SEP] Squamous cell carcinoma of head and [MASK] is the most common type of head and [MASK] carcinoma that originates from cells on the surface of the nasal cavity; mouth; paranasal sinuses, salivary glands, and larynx. Mutations in tnfrsf10b, pten, and ing1 genes are associated with this cancer.

name: src homology domains
query: Query: src homology domains [SEP] Src homology domains is regions of amino acid sequence similarity in the src-family tyrosine kinases that fold into specific functional tertiary structures. The sh1 domain is a [MASK]. sh2 and sh3 domains are protein interaction domains. sh2 usually binds PHOSPHOTYROSINE-containing proteins and sh3 interacts with cytoskeletal proteins.

name: staff development
query: Query: staff development [SEP] Staff development is the process by which the employer promotes staff performance and efficiency consistent with management goals and objectives.

name: stainless steel
query: Query: stainless steel [SEP] Stainless steel is stainless steel. a steel containing Ni, Cr, or both. It does not tarnish on exposure and is used in corrosive environments. (Grant & Hack's Chemical Dictionary, 5th ed)

name: standing orders
query: Query: standing orders [SEP] Standing orders is medical procedures and prescriptions regarding treatment of a patient that can be exercised by other health care personnel when predetermined conditions have been met.

name: standing position
query: Query: standing position [SEP] Standing position is human position in which the body is held in an upright orthostatic position and supported only by the [MASK].

name: staphylococcus aureus
query: Query: staphylococcus aureus [SEP] Staphylococcus aureus is potentially pathogenic bacteria found in nasal membranes, skin, hair follicles, and perineum of warm-blooded animals. They may cause a wide range of infections and intoxications.

name: state dentistry
query: Query: state dentistry [SEP] State dentistry is control, direction and financing of the total dental care of the population by a national government.

name: state health plans
query: Query: state health plans [SEP] State health plans is state plans prepared by the State Health Planning and Development Agencies which are made up from plans submitted by the Health Systems Agencies and subject to review and revision by the Statewide Health Coordinating Council.

name: state medicine
query: Query: state medicine [SEP] State medicine is a system of medical care regulated, controlled and financed by the government, in which the government assumes responsibility for the health needs of the population.

name: static electricity
query: Query: static electricity [SEP] Static electricity is the accumulation of an electric charge on a object

name: statistics
query: Query: statistics [SEP] Statistics is works consisting of presentations of numerical data on particular subjects.

name: statistics , nonparametric
query: Query: statistics , nonparametric [SEP] Nonparametric statistics is a class of statistical methods applicable to a large [MASK] of probability distributions used to test for correlation, location, independence, etc. In most nonparametric statistical tests, the original scores or observations are replaced by another variable containing less information. An important class of nonparametric tests employs the ordinal properties of the data. Another class of tests uses information about whether an [MASK] is above or below some fixed value such as the median, and a third class is based on the frequency of the occurrence of runs in the data. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed, p1284; Corsini, Concise Encyclopedia of Psychology, 1987, p764-5)

name: stat transcription factors
query: Query: stat transcription factors [SEP] Stat transcription factors is a family of transcription factors containing sh2 domains that are involved in CYTOKINE-mediated signal transduction. stat transcription factors are recruited to the cytoplasmic region of cell surface receptors and are activated via phosphorylation. Once activated they dimerize and translocate into the cell nucleus where they influence gene expression. They play a role in regulating cell growth processes and cell differentiation. stat transcription factors are inhibited by suppressor of cytokine signaling proteins and protein inhibitors of activated stat.

name: steam
query: Query: steam [SEP] Steam is water in its gaseous state. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

name: st elevation myocardial infarction
query: Query: st elevation myocardial infarction [SEP] St elevation myocardial infarction is a clinical syndrome defined by myocardial ischemia symptoms; persistent elevation in the st segments of the electrocardiogram; and release of biomarkers of myocardial necrosis (e.g., elevated troponin levels). st segment elevation in the ecg is often used in determining the treatment protocol (see also non-st elevation myocardial infarction).

name: stem cell factor
query: Query: stem cell factor [SEP] Stem cell factor is a hematopoietic growth factor and the ligand of the cell surface c-kit protein (proto-oncogene proteins c-kit). It is expressed during embryogenesis and is a growth factor for a number of cell types including the [MASK] and the melanocytes in addition to the hematopoietic stem cells.

name: sterile alpha motif
query: Query: sterile alpha motif [SEP] Sterile alpha motif is a putative protein interaction module, approximately 70 amino acids long, that forms a small five-helix bundle with two large interfaces which may homo- and hetero-oligomerize, or bind non-sterile-alpha motif targets. The sterile alpha motif is present in a wide variety of eukaryotic proteins that function in diverse biological processes.

name: steroid synthesis inhibitors
query: Query: steroid synthesis inhibitors [SEP] Steroid synthesis inhibitors is compounds that bind to and inhibit enzymes involved in the synthesis of steroids.

name: stimulation , chemical
query: Query: stimulation , chemical [SEP] Chemical stimulation is the increase in a measurable parameter of a physiological process, including cellular, microbial, and plant; immunological, cardiovascular, respiratory, reproductive, urinary, digestive, neural, musculoskeletal, ocular, and skin physiological processes; or metabolic process, including enzymatic and other pharmacological processes, by a drug or other chemical.

name: stimuli responsive polymers
query: Query: stimuli responsive polymers [SEP] Stimuli responsive polymers is polymeric materials designed to change properties in response to a stimulus.

name: stomach neoplasms
query: Query: stomach neoplasms [SEP] Stomach neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the stomach.

name: stomach rupture
query: Query: stomach rupture [SEP] Stomach rupture is bursting of the stomach.

name: streptavidin
query: Query: streptavidin [SEP] Streptavidin is a 60-kDa extracellular protein of Streptomyces avidinii with four high-affinity biotin binding sites. Unlike avidin, streptavidin has a near neutral isoelectric point and is free of carbohydrate side chains.

name: streptococcus pneumoniae
query: Query: streptococcus pneumoniae [SEP] Streptococcus pneumoniae is a gram-positive organism found in the upper respiratory tract, inflammatory exudates, and various body fluids of normal and/or diseased humans and, rarely, domestic animals.

name: stress , mechanical
query: Query: stress , mechanical [SEP] Mechanical stress is a purely physical condition which exists within any material because of strain or deformation by external forces or by non-uniform thermal expansion; expressed quantitatively in units of force per unit area.

name: stress disorders , traumatic , acute
query: Query: stress disorders , traumatic , acute [SEP] Acute traumatic stress disorders is a class of traumatic stress disorders that is characterized by the significant dissociative states seen immediately after overwhelming trauma. By definition it cannot last longer than 1 month, if it persists, a diagnosis of post-traumatic stress disorder (stress disorders, post-traumatic) is more appropriate.

name: stress fibers
query: Query: stress fibers [SEP] Stress fibers is bundles of actin filaments (actin cytoskeleton) and myosin-II that span across the cell attaching to the cell membrane at focal adhesions and to the network of [MASK] that surrounds the nucleus.

name: stromal interaction molecule 1
query: Query: stromal interaction molecule 1 [SEP] Stromal interaction molecule 1 is a stromal interaction molecule that functions in the regulation of calcium influx following depletion of intracellular calcium in the endoplasmic reticulum. It translocates to the plasma membrane upon calcium depletion where it activates the calcium release activated calcium channel orai1.

name: stromal interaction molecule 2
query: Query: stromal interaction molecule 2 [SEP] Stromal interaction molecule 2 is a stromal interaction molecule that functions as a highly sensitive calcium sensor in the endoplamsic reticulum and [MASK]. It can regulate calcium release activated calcium channels in response to minor variations in intracellular calcium.

name: structural homology , protein
query: Query: structural homology , protein [SEP] Protein structural homology is the degree of 3-dimensional shape similarity between proteins. It can be an indication of distant amino acid sequence homology and used for rational [MASK].

name: structure collapse
query: Query: structure collapse [SEP] Structure collapse is failure in built environment with loss of functional integrity.

name: student run clinic
query: Query: student run clinic [SEP] Student run clinic is healthcare setting managed by medical personnel in training.

name: students , medical
query: Query: students , medical [SEP] Medical students is individuals enrolled in a school of medicine or a formal educational program in medicine.

name: students , nursing
query: Query: students , nursing [SEP] Nursing students is individuals enrolled in a school of nursing or a formal educational program leading to a degree in nursing.

name: students , pharmacy
query: Query: students , pharmacy [SEP] Pharmacy students is individuals enrolled in a school of pharmacy or a formal educational program leading to a degree in pharmacy.

name: students , public health
query: Query: students , public health [SEP] Public health students is individuals enrolled in a school of public health or a formal educational program in public health.

name: study guide
query: Query: study guide [SEP] Study guide is tool used to help facilitate learning and comprehension of a topic or to help prepare for an examination.

name: subcutaneous absorption
query: Query: subcutaneous absorption [SEP] Subcutaneous absorption is the uptake of substances via the [MASK].

name: subcutaneous fat , abdominal
query: Query: subcutaneous fat , abdominal [SEP] Abdominal subcutaneous fat is fatty tissue under the skin in the region of the abdomen.

name: substance abuse detection
query: Query: substance abuse detection [SEP] Substance abuse detection is detection of drugs that have been abused, overused, or misused, including legal and illegal drugs. Urine screening is the usual method of detection.

name: substance abuse treatment centers
query: Query: substance abuse treatment centers [SEP] Substance abuse treatment centers is health facilities providing therapy and/or rehabilitation for substance-dependent individuals. Methadone distribution centers are included.

name: substrate cycling
query: Query: substrate cycling [SEP] Substrate cycling is a [MASK] of opposing, nonequilibrium reactions catalyzed by different enzymes which act simultaneously, with at least one of the reactions driven by atp hydrolysis. The results of the cycle are that atp energy is depleted, heat is produced and no net substrate-to-product conversion is achieved. Examples of substrate cycling are cycling of gluconeogenesis and glycolysis pathways and cycling of the triglycerides and fatty acid pathways. Rates of substrate cycling may be increased many-fold in association with hypermetabolic states resulting from severe burns, cold exposure, hyperthyroidism, or acute exercise.

name: substrate specificity
query: Query: substrate specificity [SEP] Substrate specificity is a characteristic feature of enzyme activity in relation to the kind of substrate on which the enzyme or catalytic molecule reacts.

name: sudden infant death
query: Query: sudden infant death [SEP] Sudden infant death is the abrupt and unexplained death of an apparently healthy infant under one year of age, remaining unexplained after a thorough case investigation, including performance of a complete autopsy, examination of the death scene, and review of the clinical history. (Pediatr Pathol 1991 Sep-Oct;11(5):677-84)

name: sudden unexpected death in epilepsy
query: Query: sudden unexpected death in epilepsy [SEP] Sudden unexpected death in epilepsy is sudden death in a patient with epilepsy associated with seizures and seizure-related symptoms (e.g., apnea; hypoxemia) without other identifiable accidental causes (e.g., drowning; wounds and injuries).

name: suicide , assisted
query: Query: suicide , assisted [SEP] Assisted suicide is provision (by a physician or other health professional, or by a family member or friend) of support and/or means that gives a patient the power to terminate his or her own life. (from apa, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 8th ed).

name: suicide , attempted
query: Query: suicide , attempted [SEP] Attempted suicide is the unsuccessful attempt to kill oneself.

name: suicide , completed
query: Query: suicide , completed [SEP] Completed suicide is the successful attempt to kill oneself.

name: sulfate transporters
query: Query: sulfate transporters [SEP] Sulfate transporters is highly conserved families of transmembrane anion transporters that occur in both prokaryotes and eukaryotes. In humans, they are expressed by epithelial cells in a variety of tissues and participate in diverse physiologic functions such as cell motility and regulating the composition and acidity of body fluids. Some Slc13 family proteins function as sodium ion-coupled co-transporters of sulfate and other anions.

name: sulfur acids
query: Query: sulfur acids [SEP] Sulfur acids is inorganic or organic acids that contain sulfur as an integral part of the molecule.

name: sulfur dioxide
query: Query: sulfur dioxide [SEP] Sulfur dioxide is a highly toxic, colorless, nonflammable gas. It is used as a pharmaceutical aid and antioxidant. It is also an environmental air pollutant.

name: sun protection factor
query: Query: sun protection factor [SEP] Sun protection factor is a measure of relative protection provided by sunscreening agents against burns due to ultraviolet (uv) radiation from a light source.

name: superior cervical ganglion
query: Query: superior cervical ganglion [SEP] Superior cervical ganglion is the largest and uppermost of the paravertebral sympathetic ganglia.

name: suppression , genetic
query: Query: suppression , genetic [SEP] Genetic suppression is mutation process that restores the wild-type phenotype in an organism possessing a mutationally altered genotype. The second "suppressor" mutation may be on a different gene, on the same gene but located at a distance from the site of the primary mutation, or in extrachromosomal genes (extrachromosomal inheritance).

name: suppressor of cytokine signaling 1 protein
query: Query: suppressor of cytokine signaling 1 protein [SEP] Suppressor of cytokine signaling 1 protein is a suppressor of cytokine signaling protein that consists of an N-terminal kinase-inhibitory region, a central sh2 domain, a characteristic C-terminal socs box (a 40-amino acid motif, which functions to recruit e3 ubiquitin-protein ligase complexes). socs1 functions as a negative regulator of cytokines that signal through the janus kinases-stat 3 transcription factor (jak/stat3) pathway by inhibiting the activity of janus kinases.

name: surface plasmon resonance
query: Query: surface plasmon resonance [SEP] Surface plasmon resonance is a biosensing technique in which biomolecules capable of binding to specific analytes or ligands are first immobilized on one side of a metallic film. Light is then focused on the opposite side of the film to excite the surface plasmons, that is, the oscillations of free [MASK] propagating along the film's surface. The refractive index of light reflecting off this surface is measured. When the immobilized biomolecules are bound by their ligands, an alteration in surface plasmons on the opposite side of the film is created which is directly proportional to the change in bound, or adsorbed, mass. Binding is measured by changes in the refractive index. The technique is used to study biomolecular interactions, such as antigen-antibody binding.

name: surge capacity
query: Query: surge capacity [SEP] Surge capacity is a health care system's ability to rapidly mobilize to meet an increased demand, to rapidly expand beyond normal services levels to meet the increased demand in the event of large-scale disasters or public health emergencies.

name: surgery , oral
query: Query: surgery , oral [SEP] Oral surgery is a dental specialty concerned with the diagnosis and surgical treatment of disease, injuries, and defects of the human oral and maxillofacial region.

name: surgery , veterinary
query: Query: surgery , veterinary [SEP] Veterinary surgery is a board-certified specialty of veterinary medicine, requiring at least four years of special education, training, and practice of veterinary surgery after graduation from veterinary school. In the written, oral, and practical examinations candidates may choose either large or small animal surgery. (From avma Directory, 43d ed, p278)

name: surgery department , hospital
query: Query: surgery department , hospital [SEP] Hospital surgery department is hospital department which administers all departmental functions and the provision of surgical diagnostic and therapeutic services.

name: surgical clearance
query: Query: surgical clearance [SEP] Surgical clearance is process of evaluating the health of a patient and determining if they are healthy enough for surgery.

name: surgical instruments
query: Query: surgical instruments [SEP] Surgical instruments is hand-held tools or implements used by health professionals for the performance of surgical tasks.

name: surgical mesh
query: Query: surgical mesh [SEP] Surgical mesh is any woven or knit material of open texture used in surgery for the repair, reconstruction, or substitution of tissue. The mesh is usually a synthetic fabric made of various polymers. It is occasionally made of metal.

name: surgical oncology
query: Query: surgical oncology [SEP] Surgical oncology is a surgical specialty concerned with management of cancer.

name: surgical tape
query: Query: surgical tape [SEP] Surgical tape is a flat, flexible strip of material used to cover or fasten together damaged tissue.

name: survival
query: Query: survival [SEP] Survival is continuance of life or existence especially under adverse conditions; includes methods and philosophy of survival.

name: survival rate
query: Query: survival rate [SEP] Survival rate is the proportion of survivors in a group, e.g., of patients, studied and followed over a period, or the proportion of persons in a specified group alive at the beginning of a time interval who survive to the end of the interval. It is often studied using [MASK].

name: sustainable development
query: Query: sustainable development [SEP] Sustainable development is a process of change in which the exploitation of resources, the direction of investments, the orientation of technological development; and institutional change are all in harmony and enhance both current and future potential to meet human needs and aspirations. (http://www.un-documents.net/ocf-02.htm#I)

name: sustainable growth
query: Query: sustainable growth [SEP] Sustainable growth is achievement of an economic system that can continue to grow for the foreseeable future.

name: sutures
query: Query: sutures [SEP] Sutures is materials used in closing a surgical or traumatic wound. (From Dorland, 28th ed)

name: swimming pools
query: Query: swimming pools [SEP] [MASK] pools is excavations or containment structures filled with water and used for [MASK].

name: swine vesicular disease
query: Query: swine vesicular disease [SEP] Swine vesicular disease is an enterovirus infection of swine clinically indistinguishable from [MASK]-and-mouth disease, vesicular stomatitis, and vesicular exanthema of swine. It is caused by a strain of human enterovirus b.

name: symptom assessment
query: Query: symptom assessment [SEP] Symptom assessment is evaluation of manifestations of disease.

name: synaptic membranes
query: Query: synaptic membranes [SEP] Synaptic membranes is cell membranes associated with synapses. Both presynaptic and postsynaptic membranes are included along with their integral or tightly associated specializations for the release or reception of transmitters.

name: synaptic vesicles
query: Query: synaptic vesicles [SEP] Synaptic vesicles is membrane-bound compartments which contain transmitter molecules. Synaptic vesicles are concentrated at presynaptic terminals. They actively sequester transmitter molecules from the cytoplasm. In at least some synapses, transmitter release occurs by fusion of these vesicles with the presynaptic membrane, followed by exocytosis of their contents.

name: syndrome
query: Query: syndrome [SEP] Syndrome is a characteristic symptom complex.

name: synovial cyst
query: Query: synovial cyst [SEP] Synovial cyst is non-neoplastic tumor-like lesions at joints, developed from the synovial membrane of a joint through the joint capsule into the periarticular tissues. They are filled with synovial fluid with a smooth and translucent appearance. a synovial cyst can develop from any joint, but most commonly at the back of the [MASK], where it is known as popliteal cyst.

name: synovial fluid
query: Query: synovial fluid [SEP] Synovial fluid is the clear, viscous fluid secreted by the synovial membrane. It contains mucin, albumin, fat, and mineral [MASK] and serves to lubricate joints.

name: synthetic biology
query: Query: synthetic biology [SEP] Synthetic biology is a field of biological research combining engineering in the formulation, design, and building (synthesis) of novel biological structures, functions, and systems.

name: synthetic lethal mutations
query: Query: synthetic lethal mutations [SEP] Synthetic lethal mutations is mutations in genes which lead to cell or organism death when occurring in combination with mutations in one or more other genes.

name: syphilis , cardiovascular
query: Query: syphilis , cardiovascular [SEP] Cardiovascular syphilis is cardiovascular manifestations of syphilis, an infection of treponema pallidum. In the late stage of syphilis, sometimes 20-30 years after the initial infection, damages are often seen in the blood vessels including the aorta and the aortic valve. Clinical signs include syphilitic aortitis, aortic insufficiency, or aortic aneurysm.

name: syphilis , congenital
query: Query: syphilis , congenital [SEP] Congenital syphilis is syphilis acquired in utero and manifested by any of several characteristic tooth (Hutchinson's teeth) or bone malformations and by active mucocutaneous syphilis at birth or shortly thereafter. Ocular and neurologic changes may also occur.

name: syphilis , latent
query: Query: syphilis , latent [SEP] Latent syphilis is the stage of syphilis that occurs following the primary (chancre) and secondary stages. The patient is asymptomatic at the latent stage but remains seropositive for the spirochete.

name: systematic reviews as topic
query: Query: systematic reviews as topic [SEP] Systematic reviews as topic is works about a review of primary literature in health and health policy that attempt to identify, appraise, and synthesize all the empirical evidence that meets specified eligibility criteria to answer a given research question. Its conduct uses explicit methods aimed at minimizing bias in order to produce more reliable findings regarding the effects of interventions for prevention, treatment, and rehabilitation that can be used to inform decision making.

name: systems biology
query: Query: systems biology [SEP] Systems biology is comprehensive, methodical analysis of complex biological systems by monitoring responses to perturbations of biological processes. Large scale, computerized collection and analysis of the data are used to develop and test models of biological systems.

name: systems integration
query: Query: systems integration [SEP] Systems integration is the procedures involved in combining separately developed modules, components, or subsystems so that they work together as a complete system. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

name: systems theory
query: Query: systems theory [SEP] Systems theory is principles, models, and laws that apply to complex interrelationships and interdependencies of sets of linked components which form a functioning whole, a system. Any system may be composed of components which are systems in their own right (sub-systems), such as several organs within an individual organism.

name: tablets
query: Query: tablets [SEP] Tablets is solid dosage forms, of varying weight, size, and shape, which may be molded or compressed, and which contain a medicinal substance in pure or diluted form. (Dorland, 28th ed)

name: tachycardia , ventricular
query: Query: tachycardia , ventricular [SEP] Ventricular tachycardia is an abnormally rapid ventricular rhythm usually in excess of 150 beats per minute. It is generated within the ventricle below the bundle of his, either as autonomic impulse formation or reentrant impulse conduction. Depending on the etiology, onset of ventricular tachycardia can be paroxysmal (sudden) or nonparoxysmal, its wide qrs complexes can be uniform or polymorphic, and the ventricular beating may be independent of the atrial beating (av dissociation).

name: tail
query: Query: tail [SEP] Tail is an extension of the posterior of an animal body beyond the torso.

name: tandem affinity purification
query: Query: tandem affinity purification [SEP] Tandem affinity purification is a technique used to isolate specific interacting partners of macromolecular complexes that have been assembled with a tagged component (bait) that interacts with other partners in the complex. The interacting bait component is labeled with a dual-affinity tag that allows for capture of the complex by immunoprecipitation, followed by purification of only the partners of the complex interacting with the bait by affinity chromatography.

name: tandem mass spectrometry
query: Query: tandem mass spectrometry [SEP] Tandem mass spectrometry is a mass spectrometry technique using two (ms/ms) or more mass analyzers. With two in tandem, the precursor ions are mass-selected by a first mass analyzer, and focused into a collision region where they are then fragmented into product ions which are then characterized by a second mass analyzer. a variety of techniques are used to separate the compounds, ionize them, and introduce them to the first mass analyzer. For example, for in gc-ms/ms, gas chromatography-mass spectrometry is involved in separating relatively small compounds by gas chromatography prior to injecting them into an ionization chamber for the mass selection.

name: tape recording
query: Query: tape recording [SEP] Tape recording is recording of information on magnetic or punched [MASK] tape.

name: targeted gene repair
query: Query: targeted gene repair [SEP] Targeted gene repair is a technique which uses synthetic oligonucleotides to direct the cell's inherent dna repair system to correct a mutation at a specific site in an episome or chromosome.

name: taste buds
query: Query: taste buds [SEP] Taste buds is small sensory organs which contain gustatory receptor cells, basal cells, and supporting cells. Taste buds in humans are found in the epithelia of the tongue, palate, and pharynx. They are innervated by the chorda tympani nerve (a branch of the facial nerve) and the glossopharyngeal nerve.

name: taste disorders
query: Query: taste disorders [SEP] Taste disorders is conditions characterized by an alteration in gustatory function or [MASK] disorders are frequently associated with olfaction disorders. Additional potential etiologies include metabolic diseases; drug toxicity; and taste pathway disorders (e.g., taste bud diseases; facial nerve diseases; glossopharyngeal nerve diseases; and brain stem diseases).

name: taste threshold
query: Query: taste threshold [SEP] Taste threshold is the minimum concentration at which taste sensitivity to a particular substance or food can be perceived.

name: tax equity and fiscal responsibility act
query: Query: tax equity and fiscal responsibility act [SEP] Tax equity and fiscal responsibility act is pl97-248. Title ii of the Act specifies "provisions relating to savings in health and income security programs." This includes changes in payment for services, benefits and premiums of Medicare as well as changes in provisions under Medicaid and other specific programs covered by Social Security. Title ii includes various revenue measures.

name: tea
query: Query: tea [SEP] Tea is the infusion of leaves of camellia sinensis (formerly Thea sinensis) as a beverage, the familiar Asian tea, which contains catechin (especially epigallocatechin gallate) and caffeine.

name: teaching materials
query: Query: teaching materials [SEP] Teaching materials is instructional materials used in teaching.

name: teaching rounds
query: Query: teaching rounds [SEP] Teaching rounds is systematic discussions and teaching conducted in hospitals and healthcare facilities related to patient care.

name: tear gases
query: Query: tear gases [SEP] Tear gases is gases that irritate the eyes, throat, or skin. Severe lacrimation develops upon irritation of the eyes.

name: tears
query: Query: tears [SEP] Tears is the fluid secreted by the lacrimal glands. This fluid moistens the conjunctiva and cornea.

name: tea tree oil
query: Query: tea tree oil [SEP] Tea tree oil is essential oil extracted from melaleuca alternifolia (tea tree). It is used as a topical antimicrobial due to the presence of terpineol.

name: technical report
query: Query: technical report [SEP] Technical report is work consisting of a formal report giving details of the investigation and results of a medical or other scientific problem. When issued by a government agency or comparable official body, its contents may be classified, unclassified, or declassified with regard to security clearance. This publication type may also cover a scientific [MASK] or article that records the current state or current position of scientific research and development. If so labeled by the editor or publisher, this publication type may be properly used for journal articles.

name: technology assessment , biomedical
query: Query: technology assessment , biomedical [SEP] Biomedical technology assessment is evaluation of biomedical technology in relation to cost, efficacy, utilization, etc., and its future impact on social, ethical, and legal systems.

name: technology transfer
query: Query: technology transfer [SEP] Technology transfer is spread and adoption of inventions and techniques from one geographic area to another, from one discipline to another, or from one sector of the economy to another. For example, improvements in medical equipment may be transferred from industrial countries to developing countries, advances arising from aerospace engineering may be applied to equipment for persons with disabilities, and innovations in science arising from government research are made available to private enterprise.

name: telomere
query: Query: telomere [SEP] Telomere is a terminal section of a chromosome which has a specialized structure and which is involved in chromosomal replication and stability. Its length is believed to be a few hundred [MASK].

name: telomere homeostasis
query: Query: telomere homeostasis [SEP] Telomere homeostasis is maintenance of telomere length. During dna replication, chromosome ends loose some of their telomere sequence ([MASK].) Various cellular mechanism are involved in repairing, extending, and recapping the telomere ends.

name: templates , genetic
query: Query: templates , genetic [SEP] Genetic templates is macromolecular molds for the synthesis of complementary macromolecules, as in dna replication; genetic transcription of dna to rna, and genetic translation of rna into polypeptides.

name: temporal arteries
query: Query: temporal arteries [SEP] Temporal arteries is arteries arising from the external carotid or the maxillary artery and distributing to the temporal region.

name: temporal concept
query: Query: temporal concept [SEP] Temporal concept is concepts relating to time.

name: tendon injuries
query: Query: tendon injuries [SEP] Tendon injuries is injuries to the fibrous cords of connective tissue which attach muscles to bones or other structures.

name: tendon transfer
query: Query: tendon transfer [SEP] Tendon transfer is surgical procedure by which a tendon is incised at its insertion and placed at an anatomical site distant from the original insertion. The tendon remains attached at the point of origin and takes over the function of a muscle inactivated by trauma or disease.

name: tensile strength
query: Query: tensile strength [SEP] Tensile strength is the maximum stress a material subjected to a stretching load can withstand without tearing. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 5th ed, p2001)

name: terminology
query: Query: terminology [SEP] Terminology is work consisting of lists of the technical terms or expressions used in a specific field. These lists may or may not be formally adopted or sanctioned by usage.

name: tertiary care centers
query: Query: tertiary care centers [SEP] Tertiary care centers is a medical facility which provides a high degree of subspecialty expertise for patients from centers where they received secondary care.

name: tertiary healthcare
query: Query: tertiary healthcare [SEP] Tertiary healthcare is care of a highly technical and specialized nature, provided in a medical center, usually one affiliated with a university, for patients with unusually severe, complex, or uncommon health problems.

name: tertiary lymphoid structures
query: Query: tertiary lymphoid structures [SEP] Tertiary lymphoid structures is aggregates of immune cells formed near the sites of chronically inflamed, infected, or tumorous tissues.

name: testicular neoplasms
query: Query: testicular neoplasms [SEP] Testicular neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the testis. Germ cell tumors (germinoma) of the testis constitute 95% of all testicular neoplasms.

name: test taking skills
query: Query: test taking skills [SEP] Test taking skills is skills and strategies, unrelated to the traits a test is intended to measure, that may increase test takers' scores -- may include the effects of coaching or experience in taking tests. (eric Thesaurus)

name: tetracycline resistance
query: Query: tetracycline resistance [SEP] Tetracycline resistance is nonsusceptibility of bacteria to the action of tetracycline which inhibits aminoacyl-tRNA binding to the 30s ribosomal subunit during protein synthesis.

name: text messaging
query: Query: text messaging [SEP] Text messaging is communication between cell phone users via the Short Message Service protocol which allows the interchange of short written messages.

name: thalamic diseases
query: Query: thalamic diseases [SEP] Thalamic diseases is disorders of the centrally located thalamus, which integrates a wide range of cortical and subcortical information. Manifestations include sensory loss, movement disorders; ataxia, pain syndromes, visual disorders, a variety of neuropsychological conditions, and coma. Relatively common etiologies include cerebrovascular disorders; craniocerebral trauma; brain neoplasms; brain hypoxia; intracranial hemorrhages; and infectious processes.

name: therapeutic community
query: Query: therapeutic community [SEP] Therapeutic community is psychotherapeutic technique which emphasizes socioenvironmental and interpersonal influences in the resocialization and rehabilitation of the patient. The setting is usually a hospital unit or ward in which professional and nonprofessional staff interact with the patients.

name: therapeutic index , drug
query: Query: therapeutic index , drug [SEP] Drug therapeutic index is the ratio of the dose that produces toxicity to the dose that produces a clinically desired or effective response.

name: therapeutic or preventive procedure
query: Query: therapeutic or preventive procedure [SEP] Therapeutic or preventive procedure is the surgical procedures done to prevent or reduce the risk of developing cancer or other disease conditions in persons who may be predisposed to such conditions.

name: therapeutic touch
query: Query: therapeutic touch [SEP] Therapeutic touch is placing of the hands of the healer upon the person to be cured with the intent of spiritual energetic healing.

name: therapy , soft tissue
query: Query: therapy , soft tissue [SEP] Soft tissue therapy is the assessment, treatment, and management of soft tissue injury or dysfunction. Therapy is designed to reduce tension and irritation in affected tissues and may include massage; muscle stretching, or direct pressure on muscles, connective tissue, and trigger points.

name: thermal diffusion
query: Query: thermal diffusion [SEP] Thermal diffusion is the movement of molecules from one location to another as effected by temperature changes.

name: theta rhythm
query: Query: theta rhythm [SEP] Theta rhythm is brain waves characterized by a frequency of 4-7 Hz, usually observed in the temporal lobes when the individual is awake, but relaxed and sleepy.

name: thoracic duct
query: Query: thoracic duct [SEP] Thoracic duct is the largest lymphatic vessel that passes through the chest and drains into the subclavian vein.

name: thoracic nerves
query: Query: thoracic nerves [SEP] Thoracic nerves is the twelve spinal nerves on each side of the thorax. They include eleven intercostal nerves and one subcostal nerve. Both sensory and motor, they supply the muscles and skin of the thoracic and abdominal walls.

name: thoracic wall
query: Query: thoracic wall [SEP] Thoracic wall is the outer margins of the thorax containing skin, deep fascia; thoracic vertebrae; ribs; sternum; and muscles.

name: thrombin
query: Query: thrombin [SEP] Thrombin is an enzyme formed from prothrombin that converts fibrinogen to fibrin.

name: thumb
query: Query: thumb [SEP] Thumb is the first digit on the radial side of the hand which in humans lies opposite the other four.

name: thymic factor , circulating
query: Query: thymic factor , circulating [SEP] Circulating thymic factor is a thymus-dependent nonapeptide found in normal blood. Stimulates the formation of e rosettes and is believed to be involved in T-cell differentiation.

name: thymocytes
query: Query: thymocytes [SEP] Thymocytes is hematopoietic progenitor cells that have migrated to the thymus where they differentiate into t-lymphocytes. Thymocytes are classified into maturational stages based on the expression of cell surface antigens.

name: thymus extracts
query: Query: thymus extracts [SEP] Thymus extracts is extracts of the thymus gland that contain specific factors, peptides, and proteins with specific biological activities.

name: thymus gland
query: Query: thymus gland [SEP] Thymus gland is a single, unpaired primary lymphoid organ situated in the mediastinum, extending superiorly into the [MASK] to the lower edge of the thyroid gland and inferiorly to the fourth costal cartilage. It is necessary for normal development of immunologic function early in life. By puberty, it begins to involute and much of the tissue is replaced by fat.

name: thymus neoplasms
query: Query: thymus neoplasms [SEP] Thymus neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the thymus gland.

name: thyroid ( usp )
query: Query: thyroid ( usp ) [SEP] Thyroid (usp) is a dehydrated extract of thyroid glands from domesticated animals. After the removal of fat and connective tissue, the extract is dried or lyophilized to yield a yellowish to buff-colored amorphous powder containing 0.17-0.23% of iodine.

name: thyroid cancer , papillary
query: Query: thyroid cancer , papillary [SEP] Papillary thyroid cancer is an adenocarcinoma that originates from follicular cells of the thyroid gland and accounts for the majority of thyroid cancer cases. Cells exhibit enlarged, oval, or elongated morphologies with clear, round, nuclei. Fusions of ret, ntrk1, tpm3, and pcm1 genes are associated with this cancer.

name: thyroid epithelial cells
query: Query: thyroid epithelial cells [SEP] Thyroid epithelial cells is epithelial cells of the thyroid gland that produce and secrete thyroxine and triiodothyronine.

name: thyroid function tests
query: Query: thyroid function tests [SEP] Thyroid function tests is blood tests used to evaluate the functioning of the thyroid gland.

name: thyroid gland
query: Query: thyroid gland [SEP] Thyroid gland is a highly vascularized endocrine gland consisting of two lobes joined by a thin band of tissue with one lobe on each side of the [MASK]. It secretes thyroid hormones from the follicular cells and calcitonin from the parafollicular cells thereby regulating metabolism and calcium level in blood, respectively.

name: thyroid hormone receptors beta
query: Query: thyroid hormone receptors beta [SEP] Thyroid hormone receptors beta is high affinity receptors for thyroid hormones, especially triiodothyronine. These receptors are usually found in the nucleus where they regulate dna transcription. They are encoded by the thrb gene (also known as nr1a2, thrb1, or erba2 gene) as several isoforms produced by [MASK]. Mutations in the thrb gene cause thyroid hormone resistance syndrome.

name: thyroid nodule
query: Query: thyroid nodule [SEP] Thyroid nodule is a small circumscribed mass in the thyroid gland that can be of neoplastic growth or non-neoplastic abnormality. It lacks a well-defined capsule or glandular architecture. Thyroid nodules are often benign but can be malignant. The growth of nodules can lead to a multinodular goiter (goiter, nodular).

name: thyroid nuclear factor 1
query: Query: thyroid nuclear factor 1 [SEP] Thyroid nuclear factor 1 is a homeobox protein and transcription factor that localizes to the cell nucleus where it activates expression of thyroid specific genes such as thyroglobulin and the thyrotropin receptor. It is critical for maintaining thyroid tissue in a differentiated state and also plays a role in lung development. Mutations in the nkx2-1 gene are associated with chorea, benign hereditary.

name: tibia
query: Query: tibia [SEP] Tibia is the second longest bone of the skeleton. It is located on the medial side of the lower leg, articulating with the fibula laterally, the talus distally, and the femur proximally.

name: tic disorders
query: Query: tic disorders [SEP] Tic disorders is disorders characterized by recurrent tics that may interfere with [MASK] and other activities. Tics are sudden, rapid, nonrhythmic, stereotyped motor movements or vocalizations which may be exacerbated by stress and are generally attenuated during absorbing activities. Tic disorders are distinguished from conditions which feature other types of abnormal movements that may accompany another another condition. (From [MASK], 1994)

name: tick control
query: Query: tick control [SEP] Tick control is chemical, biological, or medical measures designed to prevent the spread of ticks or the concomitant infestations which result in tick-borne diseases. It includes the veterinary as well as the public health aspects of tick and mite control.

name: tight junction proteins
query: Query: tight junction proteins [SEP] Tight junction proteins is proteins that take part in the formation or structure of tight junctions.

name: tight junctions
query: Query: tight junctions [SEP] Tight junctions is cell-cell junctions that seal adjacent epithelial cells together, preventing the passage of most dissolved molecules from one side of the epithelial sheet to the other. (Alberts et al., Molecular Biology of the Cell, 2nd ed, p22)

name: time and motion studies
query: Query: time and motion studies [SEP] Time and motion studies is the [MASK] and analysis of movements in a task with an emphasis on the amount of time required to perform the task.

name: time factors
query: Query: time factors [SEP] Time factors is elements of limited time intervals, contributing to particular results or situations.

name: time management
query: Query: time management [SEP] Time management is planning and control of time to improve efficiency and effectiveness.

name: time out , healthcare
