query: Query: time out , healthcare [SEP] Healthcare time out is a period of time away from normal [MASK] taken to ensure key procedural details have been reviewed for better patient safety and help prevent medical errors.

name: tin
query: Query: tin [SEP] Tin is a trace element that is required in bone formation. It has the atomic symbol Sn, atomic number 50, and atomic weight 118.71.

name: tin compounds
query: Query: tin compounds [SEP] Tin compounds is inorganic compounds that contain tin as an integral part of the molecule.

name: tinnitus
query: Query: tinnitus [SEP] Tinnitus is a nonspecific symptom of hearing disorder characterized by the sensation of buzzing, ringing, clicking, pulsations, and other noises in the ear. Objective tinnitus refers to noises generated from within the ear or adjacent structures that can be heard by other individuals. The term subjective tinnitus is used when the sound is audible only to the affected individual. Tinnitus may occur as a manifestation of cochlear diseases; vestibulocochlear nerve diseases; intracranial hypertension; craniocerebral trauma; and other conditions.

name: tissue
query: Query: tissue [SEP] Tissue is Collections of differentiated cells, such as epithelium, connective tissue, muscles, and nerve tissue. Tissues are cooperatively arranged to form organs with specialized functions such as respiration, [MASK], reproduction, movement, and others.

name: tissue array analysis
query: Query: tissue array analysis [SEP] Tissue array analysis is the simultaneous analysis of multiple samples of tissues or cells from biopsy or in vitro culture that have been arranged in an array format on slides or microchips.

name: tissue culture techniques
query: Query: tissue culture techniques [SEP] Tissue culture techniques is a technique for maintaining or growing tissue in vitro, usually by diffusion, perifusion, or perfusion. The tissue is cultured directly after removal from the host without being dispersed for cell culture.

name: tissue expansion devices
query: Query: tissue expansion devices [SEP] Tissue expansion devices is devices used to generate extra soft tissue in vivo to be used in surgical reconstructions. They exert stretching forces on the tissue and thus stimulate new growth and result in tissue expansion. They are commonly inflatable reservoirs, usually made of silicone, which are implanted under the tissue and gradually inflated. Other tissue expanders exert stretching forces by attaching to outside of the body, for example, vacuum tissue expanders. Once the tissue has grown, the expander is removed and the expanded tissue is used to cover the area being reconstructed.

name: tissue fixation
query: Query: tissue fixation [SEP] Tissue fixation is the technique of using fixatives in the preparation of cytologic, histologic, or pathologic specimens for the purpose of maintaining the existing form and structure of all the constituent elements.

name: tissue plasminogen activator
query: Query: tissue plasminogen activator [SEP] Tissue plasminogen activator is a proteolytic enzyme in the serine protease family found in many tissues which converts plasminogen to fibrinolysin. It has fibrin-binding activity and is immunologically different from urokinase-type plasminogen activator. The primary sequence, composed of 527 amino acids, is identical in both the naturally occurring and synthetic proteases.

name: tissue scaffolds
query: Query: tissue scaffolds [SEP] Tissue scaffolds is cell growth support structures composed of biocompatible materials. They are specially designed solid support matrices for cell attachment in tissue engineering and guided tissue regeneration uses.

name: tissue survival
query: Query: tissue survival [SEP] Tissue survival is the span of viability of a tissue or an organ.

name: tobacco mosaic satellite virus
query: Query: tobacco mosaic satellite virus [SEP] Tobacco mosaic satellite virus is a spherical rna satellite virus which requires an obligatory helper tobacco mosaic virus for replication.

name: tobacco smoke pollution
query: Query: tobacco smoke pollution [SEP] Tobacco smoke pollution is contamination of the air by tobacco smoke.

name: tobacco use cessation
query: Query: tobacco use cessation [SEP] Tobacco use cessation is ending the tobacco habits of smoking, chewing, or snuff use.

name: token economy
query: Query: token economy [SEP] Token economy is a practice whereby tokens representing money, toys, candy, etc., are given as secondary reinforcers contingent upon certain desired behaviors or performances.

name: tokyo
query: Query: tokyo [SEP] Tokyo is capital of the country of japan.

name: tomography , optical coherence
query: Query: tomography , optical coherence [SEP] Optical coherence tomography is an imaging method using lasers that is used for mapping subsurface structure. When a reflective site in the sample is at the same optical path length (coherence) as the reference mirror, the detector observes interference fringes.

name: tongue habits
query: Query: tongue habits [SEP] Tongue habits is acquired responses regularly manifested by tongue movement or positioning.

name: tonic pupil
query: Query: tonic pupil [SEP] Tonic pupil is a pupillary abnormality characterized by a poor pupillary light reaction, reduced accommodation, iris sector palsies, an enhanced pupillary response to near effort that results in a prolonged, "tonic" constriction, and slow pupillary redilation. This condition is associated with injury to the postganglionic parasympathetic innervation to the pupil. (From Miller et al., Clinical Neuro-Ophthalmology, 4th ed, pp492-500)

name: tool use behavior
query: Query: tool use behavior [SEP] Tool use behavior is modifying, carrying, or manipulating an item external to itself by an animal, before using it to effect a change on the environment or itself (from Beck, Animal Tool Behavior, 1980).

name: tooth , artificial
query: Query: tooth , artificial [SEP] Artificial tooth is a fabricated tooth substituting for a natural tooth in a prosthesis. It is usually made of porcelain or plastic.

name: tooth , impacted
query: Query: tooth , impacted [SEP] Impacted tooth is a tooth that is prevented from erupting by a physical barrier, usually other teeth. Impaction may also result from orientation of the tooth in an other than vertical position in the periodontal structures.

name: tooth attrition
query: Query: tooth attrition [SEP] Tooth attrition is the wearing away of a tooth as a result of tooth-to-tooth contact, as in mastication, occurring only on the occlusal, incisal, and proximal surfaces. It is chiefly associated with aging. It is differentiated from tooth abrasion (the pathologic wearing away of the tooth substance by friction, as brushing, bruxism, clenching, and other mechanical causes) and from tooth erosion (the loss of substance caused by chemical action without bacterial action). (Jablonski, Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992, p86)

name: tooth cervix
query: Query: tooth cervix [SEP] Tooth cervix is the constricted part of the tooth at the junction of the crown and root or roots. It is often referred to as the cementoenamel junction (cej), the line at which the cementum covering the root of a tooth and the enamel of the tooth meet. (Jablonski, Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992, p530, p433)

name: tooth erosion
query: Query: tooth erosion [SEP] Tooth erosion is progressive loss of the hard substance of a tooth by chemical processes that do not involve bacterial action. (Jablonski, Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992, p296)

name: tooth fractures
query: Query: tooth fractures [SEP] Tooth fractures is break or rupture of a tooth or tooth root.

name: tooth loss
query: Query: tooth loss [SEP] Tooth loss is the failure to retain teeth as a result of disease or injury.

name: tooth migration
query: Query: tooth migration [SEP] Tooth migration is the movement of teeth into altered positions in relationship to the basal bone of the alveolar process and to adjoining and opposing teeth as a result of loss of approximating or opposing teeth, occlusal interferences, habits, inflammatory and dystrophic disease of the attaching and supporting structures of the teeth. (From Boucher's Clinical Dental Terminology, 4th ed)

name: tooth mobility
query: Query: tooth mobility [SEP] Tooth mobility is horizontal and, to a lesser degree, axial movement of a tooth in response to normal forces, as in occlusion. It refers also to the movability of a tooth resulting from loss of all or a portion of its attachment and supportive apparatus, as seen in periodontitis, occlusal trauma, and periodontosis. (From Jablonski, Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992, p507 & Boucher's Clinical Dental Terminology, 4th ed, p313)

name: tooth socket
query: Query: tooth socket [SEP] Tooth socket is a hollow part of the alveolar process of the maxilla or mandible where each tooth fits and is attached via the periodontal ligament.

name: torsion abnormality
query: Query: torsion abnormality [SEP] Torsion abnormality is an abnormal twisting or [MASK] of a bodily part or member on its axis.

name: total quality management
query: Query: total quality management [SEP] Total quality management is the application of industrial management practice to systematically maintain and improve organization-wide performance. Effectiveness and success are determined and assessed by quantitative quality measures.

name: touch
query: Query: touch [SEP] Touch is sensation of making physical contact with objects, animate or inanimate. Tactile stimuli are detected by mechanoreceptors in the skin and mucous membranes.

name: touch perception
query: Query: touch perception [SEP] Touch perception is the process by which the nature and meaning of tactile stimuli are recognized and interpreted by the brain, such as realizing the characteristics or name of an object being touched.

name: toxic optic neuropathy
query: Query: toxic optic neuropathy [SEP] Toxic optic neuropathy is damage to the eye or its function (e.g., visual impairment) due to optic nerve damage secondary to toxic substances such as drugs used in chemotherapy; immunotherapy; or radiation.

name: trace elements
query: Query: trace elements [SEP] Trace elements is a group of chemical elements that are needed in minute quantities for the proper growth, development, and physiology of an organism. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed)

name: tracheal stenosis
query: Query: tracheal stenosis [SEP] Tracheal stenosis is a pathological narrowing of the [MASK].

name: track and field
query: Query: track and field [SEP] Track and field is sports performed on a track, field, or arena and including [MASK] events and other competitions, such as the pole vault, shot put, etc.

name: traction
query: Query: traction [SEP] Traction is the pull on a limb or a part thereof. Skin traction (indirect traction) is applied by using a bandage to pull on the skin and fascia where light traction is required. Skeletal traction (direct traction), however, uses pins or wires inserted through bone and is attached to weights, pulleys, and ropes. (From Blauvelt & Nelson, a Manual of Orthopaedic Terminology, 5th ed)

name: training support
query: Query: training support [SEP] Training support is financial support for training including both student stipends and loans and training grants to institutions.

name: transcription elongation , genetic
query: Query: transcription elongation , genetic [SEP] Genetic transcription elongation is the lengthening of a nascent rna molecule by rna polymerase during transcription.

name: transcription factors , general
query: Query: transcription factors , general [SEP] General transcription factors is transcription factors that form transcription initiation complexes on dna, bind to specific dna-directed rna polymerases and are required to initiate transcription. Although their binding may be localized to distinct sequence and structural motifs within the dna they are considered non-specific with regard to the specific gene being transcribed.

name: transcription initiation , genetic
query: Query: transcription initiation , genetic [SEP] Genetic transcription initiation is the process that starts the transcription of an rna molecule. It includes the assembly of the initiation complex and establishment of the start site.

name: transcription initiation site
query: Query: transcription initiation site [SEP] Transcription initiation site is the first nucleotide of a transcribed dna sequence where rna polymerase (dna-directed rna polymerase) begins synthesizing the rna transcript.

name: transcription termination , genetic
query: Query: transcription termination , genetic [SEP] Genetic transcription termination is the discontinuation of transcription at the end of a transcription unit, including the recognition of termination sites and release of the newly synthesized rna molecule.

name: transcriptome
query: Query: transcriptome [SEP] Transcriptome is the pattern of gene expression at the level of genetic transcription in a specific organism or under specific circumstances in specific cells.

name: transduction , genetic
query: Query: transduction , genetic [SEP] Genetic transduction is the transfer of [MASK] by phages from an infected bacterium to another bacterium. This also refers to the transfer of genes into eukaryotic cells by viruses. This naturally occurring process is routinely employed as a gene transfer technique.

name: trans fatty acids
query: Query: trans fatty acids [SEP] Trans fatty acids is unsaturated fatty acids that contain at least one double bond in the trans configuration, which results in a greater bond angle than the cis configuration. This results in a more extended fatty acid chain similar to saturated fatty acids, with closer packing and reduced fluidity. hydrogenation of unsaturated fatty acids increases the trans content.

name: transfer , psychology
query: Query: transfer , psychology [SEP] Psychology transfer is change in learning in one situation due to prior learning in another situation. The transfer can be positive (with second learning improved by first) or negative (where the reverse holds).

name: transfer agreement
query: Query: transfer agreement [SEP] Transfer agreement is a written agreement for the transfer of patients and their medical records from [MASK] care institution to another.

name: transforming growth factor alpha
query: Query: transforming growth factor alpha [SEP] Transforming growth factor alpha is an epidermal growth factor related protein that is found in a variety of tissues including epithelium, and maternal decidua. It is synthesized as a transmembrane protein which can be cleaved to release a soluble active form which binds to the [MASK].

name: transforming growth factor beta
query: Query: transforming growth factor beta [SEP] Transforming growth factor beta is a factor synthesized in a wide variety of tissues. It acts synergistically with TGF-alpha in inducing phenotypic transformation and can also act as a negative autocrine growth factor. TGF-beta has a potential role in embryonal development, cellular differentiation, hormone secretion, and immune function. TGF-beta is found mostly as homodimer forms of separate gene products TGF-beta1, TGF-beta2 or TGF-beta3. Heterodimers composed of TGF-beta1 and 2 (TGF-beta1.2) or of TGF-beta2 and 3 (TGF-beta2.3) have been isolated. The TGF-beta proteins are synthesized as precursor proteins.

name: transfusion medicine
query: Query: transfusion medicine [SEP] Transfusion medicine is the area of hematology that is concerned with the transfusion of blood and blood components, and in prevention and treatment of adverse effects from blood transfusion errors.

name: transfusion reaction
query: Query: transfusion reaction [SEP] Transfusion reaction is complications of blood transfusion. Included adverse reactions are common allergic and febrile reactions; hemolytic (delayed and acute) reactions; and other non-hemolytic adverse reactions such as infections and adverse immune reactions related to immunocompatibility.

name: transients and migrants
query: Query: transients and migrants [SEP] Transients and migrants is people who frequently change their place of residence.

name: transistors , electronic
query: Query: transistors , electronic [SEP] Electronic transistors is electrical devices that are composed of semiconductor material, with at least three connections to an external electronic circuit. They are used to amplify electrical signals, detect signals, or as switches.

name: transitional care
query: Query: transitional care [SEP] Transitional care is health care provided during a transition to a different mode of care (e.g., transition to adult care).

name: transition temperature
query: Query: transition temperature [SEP] Transition temperature is the temperature at which a substance changes from one state or conformation of matter to another.

name: transition to adult care
query: Query: transition to adult care [SEP] Transition to adult care is transfer from pediatric to adult care.

name: translating
query: Query: translating [SEP] Translating is conversion from one language to another language.

name: translational medical research
query: Query: translational medical research [SEP] Translational medical research is the application of discoveries generated by laboratory research and preclinical studies to the development of clinical trials and studies in humans. a second area of translational research concerns enhancing the adoption of [MASK].

name: translations
query: Query: translations [SEP] Translations is products resulting from the conversion of one language to another.

name: transplantation , autologous
query: Query: transplantation , autologous [SEP] Autologous transplantation is transplantation of an individual's own tissue from one site to another site.

name: transplantation , heterologous
query: Query: transplantation , heterologous [SEP] Heterologous transplantation is transplantation between animals of different species.

name: transplantation , homologous
query: Query: transplantation , homologous [SEP] Homologous transplantation is transplantation between individuals of the same species. Usually refers to genetically disparate individuals in contradistinction to isogeneic transplantation for genetically identical individuals.

name: transplantation tolerance
query: Query: transplantation tolerance [SEP] Transplantation tolerance is an induced state of non-reactivity to grafted tissue from a donor organism that would ordinarily trigger a cell-mediated or humoral immune response.

name: transplant donor site
query: Query: transplant donor site [SEP] [MASK] donor site is the body location or part from which tissue is taken for transplantation.

name: transplant recipients
query: Query: transplant recipients [SEP] [MASK] recipients is individuals receiving tissues or organs transferred from another individual of the same or different species, or from within the same individual.

name: transportation of patients
query: Query: transportation of patients [SEP] Transportation of patients is conveying ill or injured individuals from one place to another.

name: trauma centers
query: Query: trauma centers [SEP] Trauma centers is specialized hospital facilities which provide diagnostic and therapeutic services for trauma patients.

name: travel medicine
query: Query: travel medicine [SEP] Travel medicine is multidisciplinary field focusing on prevention of infectious diseases and patient safety during international travel. Key element of patient's pre-travel visit to the physician is a health risk assessment.

name: trees
query: Query: trees [SEP] Trees is woody, usually tall, perennial higher plants (Angiosperms, Gymnosperms, and some Pterophyta) having usually a main stem and numerous branches.

name: trial of labor
query: Query: trial of labor [SEP] Trial of labor is allowing a woman to be in labor, obstetric long enough to determine if vaginal birth may be anticipated.

name: trigger points
query: Query: trigger points [SEP] Trigger points is discrete spots in taut bands of muscle that produce local and [MASK] when muscle bands are compressed.

name: triple negative breast neoplasms
query: Query: triple negative breast neoplasms [SEP] Triple negative breast neoplasms is breast neoplasms that do not express estrogen receptors; progesterone receptors; and do not overexpress the neu receptor/her-2 proto-oncogene protein.

name: troponin c
query: Query: troponin c [SEP] Troponin c is a troponin complex subunit that binds calcium and help regulate calcium-dependent muscle contraction. There are two troponin c subtypes: troponin c1 and c2. Troponin c1 is skeletal and cardiac type whereas troponin c2 is skeletal type. Troponin c1 is a biomarker for damaged or injured [MASK] and mutations in troponin c1 gene are associated with [MASK].

name: troponin t
query: Query: troponin t [SEP] Troponin t is a troponin complex subunit that binds to tropomyosin. There are three troponin t subtypes: troponin t1, t2 and t3. Troponin t2 is cardiac-specific whereas troponin t2 and t3 are skeletal subtypes. Troponin t2 is a biomarker for damaged or injured [MASK] and mutations in troponin t2 gene are associated with [MASK].

name: trpv cation channels
query: Query: trpv cation channels [SEP] Trpv cation channels is a subgroup of trp cation channels named after the vanilloid receptor. They are very sensitive to temperature; hot spicy food, and capsaicin. They contain a trp domain (a five-turn amphipathic helix with an invariant tryptophan) and ankyrin repeats. Selectivity for calcium over sodium ranges from 3 to 100 fold.

name: trust
query: Query: trust [SEP] Trust is confidence in or reliance on a person or thing.

name: tryptophan
query: Query: tryptophan [SEP] Tryptophan is an essential amino acid that is necessary for normal growth in infants and for nitrogen balance in adults. It is a precursor of indole alkaloids in plants. It is a precursor of serotonin (hence its use as an antidepressant and sleep aid). It can be a precursor to niacin, albeit inefficiently, in mammals.

name: tuberculosis , avian
query: Query: tuberculosis , avian [SEP] Avian tuberculosis is a variety of tuberculosis affecting various birds, including [MASK] and ducks. It is caused by mycobacterium avium and characterized by tubercles consisting principally of epithelioid cells.

name: tuberculosis , cardiovascular
query: Query: tuberculosis , cardiovascular [SEP] Cardiovascular tuberculosis is pathological conditions of the cardiovascular system caused by infection of [MASK]. Tuberculosis involvement may include the heart; the blood vessels; or the pericardium.

name: tuberculosis , endocrine
query: Query: tuberculosis , endocrine [SEP] Endocrine tuberculosis is infection of the endocrine glands with species of mycobacterium, most often [MASK].

name: tuberculosis , hepatic
query: Query: tuberculosis , hepatic [SEP] Hepatic tuberculosis is infection of the liver with species of mycobacterium, most often [MASK]. It is characterized by localized small tuberculous miliary lesions or tumor-like mass (tuberculoma), and abnormalities in liver function tests.

name: tuberculosis , laryngeal
query: Query: tuberculosis , laryngeal [SEP] Laryngeal tuberculosis is tuberculosis involving the larynx, producing ulceration of the vocal cords and the [MASK].

name: tuberculosis , male genital
query: Query: tuberculosis , male genital [SEP] Male genital tuberculosis is mycobacterium infections of the male reproductive tract (genitalia, male).

name: tuberculosis , ocular
query: Query: tuberculosis , ocular [SEP] Ocular tuberculosis is tuberculous infection of the eye, primarily the iris, [MASK], and choroid.

name: tuberculosis , oral
query: Query: tuberculosis , oral [SEP] Oral tuberculosis is tuberculosis of the mouth, tongue, and salivary glands.

name: tuberculosis , pulmonary
query: Query: tuberculosis , pulmonary [SEP] Pulmonary tuberculosis is mycobacterium infections of the lung.

name: tuberculosis societies
query: Query: tuberculosis societies [SEP] Tuberculosis societies is voluntary agencies concerned with prevention and treatment of tuberculosis.

name: tubulin
query: Query: tubulin [SEP] Tubulin is a [MASK] subunit protein found in large quantities in mammalian brain. It has also been isolated from sperm flagellum; cilia; and other sources. Structurally, the protein is a dimer with a molecular weight of approximately 120,000 and a sedimentation coefficient of 5.8s. It binds to colchicine; vincristine; and vinblastine.

name: tumor burden
query: Query: tumor burden [SEP] Tumor burden is the total amount (cell number, weight, size or volume) of tumor cells or tissue in the body.

name: tumor necrosis factor ligand superfamily member 13
query: Query: tumor necrosis factor ligand superfamily member 13 [SEP] Tumor necrosis factor ligand superfamily member 13 is a member of tumor necrosis factor superfamily found on macrophages; [MASK] and t-lymphocytes. It occurs as transmembrane protein that can be cleaved to release a secreted form that specifically binds to transmembrane activator and caml interactor protein; and b cell maturation antigen.

name: tumor necrosis factor ligand superfamily member 15
query: Query: tumor necrosis factor ligand superfamily member 15 [SEP] Tumor necrosis factor ligand superfamily member 15 is a member of tumor necrosis factor superfamily found on endothelial cells that plays a role in the inhibition of endothelial cell growth and physiologic angiogenesis.

name: tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily , member 7
query: Query: tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily , member 7 [SEP] Member 7 tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily is a member of the tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily found on most t-lymphocytes. Activation of the receptor by cd70 antigen results in the increased proliferation of cd4-positive t-lymphocytes and cd8-positive t-lymphocytes. Signaling by the activated receptor occurs through its association with tnf receptor-associated factors.

name: tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily , member 9
query: Query: tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily , member 9 [SEP] Member 9 tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily is a member of the tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily that is specific for 4-1bb ligand. It is found in a variety of immune cell types including activated t-lymphocytes; natural killer cells; and [MASK]. Activation of the receptor on t-lymphocytes plays a role in their expansion, production of cytokines and survival. Signaling by the activated receptor occurs through its association with tnf receptor-associated factors.

name: tumor stem cell assay
query: Query: tumor stem cell assay [SEP] Tumor stem cell assay is a cytologic technique for measuring the functional capacity of tumor stem cells by assaying their activity. It is used primarily for the in vitro testing of antineoplastic agents.

name: turkey
query: Query: turkey [SEP] Turkey is country in Southeastern Europe and Southwestern Asia bordering the Black Sea, between Bulgaria and Georgia, and bordering the Aegean Sea and the Mediterranean Sea, between Greece and Syria. The capital is Ankara.

name: twins
query: Query: twins [SEP] Twins is two individuals derived from two fetuses that were fertilized at or about the same time, developed in the uterus simultaneously, and born to the same mother. Twins are either monozygotic (twins, monozygotic) or dizygotic (twins, dizygotic).

name: twin studies as topic
query: Query: twin studies as topic [SEP] Twin studies as topic is works about methods of detecting genetic etiology in human traits. The basic premise of twin studies is that monozygotic twins carry identical genes, while zygotic twins are genetically no more similar than two siblings born after separate pregnancies. (Last, j.m., a Dictionary of Epidemiology, 2d ed)

name: twin study
query: Query: twin study [SEP] Twin study is work consisting of reporting using a method of detecting genetic causes in human traits and genetic factors in behavior using sets of twins.

name: type a personality
query: Query: type a personality [SEP] Type a personality is established behavior pattern characterized by excessive drive and ambition, impatience, competitiveness, sense of time urgency, and poorly contained aggression.

name: type d personality
query: Query: type d personality [SEP] Type d personality is behavior pattern characterized by negative emotionality, an inability to express emotions, and [MASK], which has been linked to greater cardiovascular disease and increased mortality. (from International Encyclopedia of the Social Sciences, 2008, p. 217)

name: type iii secretion systems
query: Query: type iii secretion systems [SEP] Type iii secretion systems is multiprotein transmembrane complexes in gram-negative bacteria involved in either the secretion of effector proteins from the bacterial cytoplasm into host cells, or the secretion and assembly of flagellar components. The major component of the T3SSs is called the injectosome or needle complex.

name: type ii secretion systems
query: Query: type ii secretion systems [SEP] Type ii secretion systems is gram-negative bacterial secretion systems which carry out the secretion of folded proteins.T2SSs secrete folded proteins from the periplasmic space that have been exported there by sec translocase or tat secretion systems, or they secrete folded proteins directly from the cytoplasm. The T2SSs have four substructures, an ATPase, an inner membrane platform, a pseudopilin, and secretin, an outer membrane complex which is a channel for secretion. (This bacterial secretin is not the same as the mammalian hormone also named secretin.)

name: type i secretion systems
query: Query: type i secretion systems [SEP] Type i secretion systems is gram-negative bacterial secretion systems which translocate effectors in a single step across the inner and outer membranes. The one-step secretion is carried out by a channel that passes from the cytoplasm, through the inner membrane, periplasmic space, and outer membrane, to the extracellular space. The specificity of type i secretions systems are determined by the specificity of the three subcomponents forming the channel - an atp transporter (atp-binding cassette transporters); a [MASK] protein ([MASK] proteins); and an outer membrane protein ([MASK] proteins.)

name: type vi secretion systems
query: Query: type vi secretion systems [SEP] Type vi secretion systems is multiprotein complexes in gram negative bacteria that deliver effector proteins into eukaryotic or prokaryotic cells by a mechanism similar to the contractile tail of bacteriophages. They are composed of a cell envelope-spanning tube which is surrounded by a contractile sheath and tipped by a cell puncturing complex; a base plate structure that anchors the assembly to the cell envelope; and an ATPase involved in the sheath contraction and disassembly of the complex.

name: type v secretion systems
query: Query: type v secretion systems [SEP] Type v secretion systems is secretion systems of gram-negative bacteria (single membrane proteins or multiprotein complexes) that carry out secretion of proteins from the periplasmic space to the extracellular space via a beta-barrel transmembrane pore. There are several t5ss subtypes: T5aSS monomeric autotransporters, T5bSS two-partner secretions systems (tpss), T5cSS trimeric autotransporters, T5dSS fused two-partner secretion systems, and T5eSS autotransporters with inverted domains.

name: tyrosine
query: Query: tyrosine [SEP] Tyrosine is a non-essential amino acid. In animals it is synthesized from phenylalanine. It is also the precursor of epinephrine; thyroid hormones; and melanin.

name: ubiquitin c
query: Query: ubiquitin c [SEP] Ubiquitin c is a single protein comprised of tandem repeats of the ubiquitin 78-amino acid sequence. It is a product of the polyubiquitin gene which contains multiple copies of the ubiquitin coding sequence. Proteolytic processing of ubiquitin c results in the formation of individual ubiquitin molecules. This protein is distinct from polyubiquitin, which is a protein formed through isopeptide linkage of multiple ubiquitin species.

name: uganda
query: Query: uganda [SEP] Uganda is a republic in eastern Africa, south of sudan and west of kenya. Its capital is Kampala.

name: ultrasonic surgical procedures
query: Query: ultrasonic surgical procedures [SEP] Ultrasonic surgical procedures is the use of high-energy shock waves, in the frequency range of 20-60 kHz, to cut through or remove tissue. The tissue fragmentation by ultrasonic surgical instruments is caused by mechanical effects not heat as with high-intensity focused ultrasound ablation.

name: ultrasonography , doppler , color
query: Query: ultrasonography , doppler , color [SEP] [MASK] doppler ultrasonography is ultrasonography applying the Doppler effect, with the superposition of flow information as [MASK] on a gray scale in a real-time image. This type of ultrasonography is well-suited to identifying the location of high-velocity flow (such as in a stenosis) or of mapping the extent of flow in a certain region.

name: ultraviolet rays
query: Query: ultraviolet rays [SEP] Ultraviolet rays is that portion of the electromagnetic spectrum immediately below the visible range and extending into the x-ray frequencies. The longer wavelengths (near-UV or biotic or vital rays) are necessary for the endogenous synthesis of vitamin d and are also called antirachitic rays; the shorter, ionizing wavelengths (far-UV or abiotic or extravital rays) are viricidal, bactericidal, mutagenic, and carcinogenic and are used as disinfectants.

name: umbilical arteries
query: Query: umbilical arteries [SEP] Umbilical arteries is specialized arterial vessels in the umbilical cord. They carry waste and deoxygenated blood from the fetus to the mother via the placenta. In humans, there are usually two umbilical arteries but sometimes one.

name: umbilical veins
query: Query: umbilical veins [SEP] Umbilical veins is venous vessels in the umbilical cord. They carry oxygenated, nutrient-rich blood from the mother to the fetus via the placenta. In humans, there is normally one umbilical vein.

name: unilateral breast neoplasms
query: Query: unilateral breast neoplasms [SEP] Unilateral breast neoplasms is tumors or cancer found specifically in one human breast, but not in both.

name: union list
query: Query: union list [SEP] Union list is works consisting of records of the holdings or items owned by two or more libraries.

name: united states department of agriculture
query: Query: united states department of agriculture [SEP] United states department of agriculture is a cabinet department in the Executive Branch of the United States Government concerned with improving and maintaining farm income and developing and expanding markets for agricultural products. Through inspection and grading services it safeguards and insures standards of quality in food supply and production.

name: united states department of defense
query: Query: united states department of defense [SEP] United states department of defense is a cabinet department in the Executive Branch of the United States Government whose mission is to provide the military forces needed to deter warfare and to protect the security of our country.

name: united states department of veterans affairs
query: Query: united states department of veterans affairs [SEP] United states department of veterans affairs is a cabinet department in the Executive Branch of the United States Government concerned with overall planning, promoting, and administering programs pertaining to veterans. It was established March 15, 1989 as a Cabinet-level position.

name: united states environmental protection agency
query: Query: united states environmental protection agency [SEP] United states environmental protection agency is an agency in the Executive Branch of the Federal Government. It was created as an independent regulatory agency responsible for the implementation of federal laws designed to protect the environment. Its mission is to protect human health and the environment.

name: united states federal trade commission
query: Query: united states federal trade commission [SEP] United states federal trade commission is an independent administrative agency concerned with maintaining competitive free enterprise by prohibiting unfair methods of competition and unfair deceptive acts or practices.

name: united states food and drug administration
query: Query: united states food and drug administration [SEP] United states food and drug administration is an agency of the public health service concerned with the overall planning, promoting, and administering of programs pertaining to maintaining standards of quality of foods, drugs, therapeutic devices, etc.

name: united states indian health service
query: Query: united states indian health service [SEP] United states indian health service is a division of the united states public health service that is responsible for the public health and the provision of medical services to native americans in the United States, primarily those residing on reservation lands.

name: united states office of economic opportunity
query: Query: united states office of economic opportunity [SEP] United states office of economic opportunity is a division of the Executive Branch of the United States government concerned with overall planning, promoting, and administering programs relative to the provision of opportunities for economic advancement.

name: united states office of research integrity
query: Query: united states office of research integrity [SEP] United states office of research integrity is an office of the united states public health service organized in June 1992 to promote research integrity and investigate misconduct in research supported by the Public Health Service. It consolidates the Office of Scientific Integrity of the National Institutes of Health and the Office of [MASK] in the Office of the Assistant Secretary for Health.

name: united states office of technology assessment
query: Query: united states office of technology assessment [SEP] United states office of technology assessment is an office established to help Congress participate and plan for the consequences of uses of technology. It provided information on both the beneficial and adverse effects of technological applications. The Office of Technology Assessment closed on September 29, 1995.

name: united states social security administration
query: Query: united states social security administration [SEP] United states social security administration is an independent agency within the Executive Branch of the United States Government. It administers a national social insurance program whereby employees, employers, and the self-employed pay contributions into pooled trust funds. Part of the contributions go into a separate hospital insurance trust fund for workers at age 65 to provide help with medical expenses. Other programs include the supplemental social security income program for the aged, blind, and disabled and the Old Age Survivors and Disability Insurance Program. It became an independent agency March 31, 1995. It had previously been part of the Department of Health, Education, and Welfare, later the Department of Health and Human Services. (From United States Government Manual, 1994-95)

name: united states substance abuse and mental health services administration
query: Query: united states substance abuse and mental health services administration [SEP] United states substance abuse and mental health services administration is an agency of the public health service concerned with the overall planning, promoting, and administering of programs pertaining to substance abuse and mental health. It is commonly referred to by the acronym samhsa. On 1 October 1992, the United States Alcohol, Drug Abuse, and Mental Health Administration (adamha) became samhsa.

name: universal health care
query: Query: universal health care [SEP] Universal health care is access for all people to needed health services (including prevention, promotion, treatment, rehabilitation and palliation) of sufficient quality to be effective while also ensuring that the use of these services does not expose the user to financial hardship. (From https://www.who.int/healthsystems/universal_health_coverage/en/)

name: universities
query: Query: universities [SEP] Universities is educational institutions providing facilities for teaching and research and authorized to grant academic degrees.

name: unpublished work
query: Query: unpublished work [SEP] Unpublished work is work that has not been formally published.

name: unsupervised machine learning
query: Query: unsupervised machine learning [SEP] Unsupervised machine learning is a machine learning paradigm used to make predictions about future instances based on a given [MASK] of unlabeled paired input-output training (sample) data.

name: urban health
query: Query: urban health [SEP] Urban health is the status of health in urban populations.

name: urban population
query: Query: urban population [SEP] Urban population is the inhabitants of a city or town, including metropolitan areas and suburban areas.

name: urban renewal
query: Query: urban renewal [SEP] Urban renewal is the planned upgrading of a deteriorating urban area, involving rebuilding, renovation, or restoration. It frequently refers to programs of major demolition and rebuilding of blighted areas.

name: urea
query: Query: urea [SEP] Urea is a compound formed in the liver from [MASK] produced by the deamination of amino acids. It is the principal end product of protein catabolism and constitutes about one half of the total urinary solids.

name: ureter
query: Query: ureter [SEP] Ureter is one of a pair of thick-walled tubes that transports urine from the [MASK] to the [MASK].

name: urethral neoplasms
query: Query: urethral neoplasms [SEP] Urethral neoplasms is cancer or tumors of the urethra. Benign epithelial tumors of the urethra usually consist of squamous and transitional cells. Primary urethral carcinomas are rare and typically of squamous cells. Urethral carcinoma is the only urological malignancy that is more common in females than in males.

name: urinary bladder neck obstruction
query: Query: urinary bladder neck obstruction [SEP] [MASK] [MASK] obstruction is blocked urine flow through the [MASK] [MASK], the narrow internal urethral opening at the base of the [MASK]. Narrowing or strictures of the urethra can be congenital or acquired. It is often observed in males with enlarged prostate glands.

name: urinary bladder neoplasms
query: Query: urinary bladder neoplasms [SEP] [MASK] neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the [MASK].

name: urinary catheters
query: Query: urinary catheters [SEP] Urinary catheters is catheters inserted into the [MASK] or kidney for therapeutic or diagnostic purposes.

name: urinary incontinence , stress
query: Query: urinary incontinence , stress [SEP] Stress urinary incontinence is involuntary discharge of urine as a result of physical activities that increase abdominal pressure on the [MASK] without detrusor contraction or overdistended [MASK]. The subtypes are classified by the degree of leakage, descent and opening of the [MASK] [MASK] and urethra without [MASK] contraction, and sphincter deficiency.

name: urinary sphincter , artificial
query: Query: urinary sphincter , artificial [SEP] Artificial urinary sphincter is an artifical implanted device, usually in the form of an inflatable silicone cuff, inserted in or around the [MASK] [MASK] in the surgical treatment of urinary incontinence caused by sphincter weakness. Often it is placed around the bulbous urethra in adult males. The artificial urinary sphincter is considered an alternative to urinary diversion.

name: urinary tract infections
query: Query: urinary tract infections [SEP] Urinary tract infections is inflammatory responses of the epithelium of the urinary tract to microbial invasions. They are often bacterial infections with associated bacteriuria and pyuria.

name: urine
query: Query: urine [SEP] Urine is liquid by-product of excretion produced in the kidneys, temporarily stored in the [MASK] until discharge through the urethra.

name: urine specimen collection
query: Query: urine specimen collection [SEP] Urine specimen collection is methods or procedures used to obtain samples of urine.

name: uterine artery
query: Query: uterine artery [SEP] Uterine artery is a branch arising from the internal iliac artery in females, that supplies blood to the uterus.

name: uterine artery embolization
query: Query: uterine artery embolization [SEP] Uterine artery embolization is the use of embolizing agents to block the arterial blood supply to parts or all of the uterus. The procedures are done to control bleeding or to cause destruction of uterine tissues.

name: uterine cervical erosion
query: Query: uterine cervical erosion [SEP] Uterine cervical erosion is loss or destruction of the epithelial lining of the uterine cervix.

name: uterine cervical neoplasms
query: Query: uterine cervical neoplasms [SEP] Uterine cervical neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the uterine cervix.

name: uterine monitoring
query: Query: uterine monitoring [SEP] Uterine monitoring is measurement or recording of contraction activity of the uterine muscle. It is used to determine progress of labor, obstetric and assess status of pregnancy. It is also used in conjunction with [MASK] to determine fetal response to stress of maternal [MASK].

name: uterine perforation
query: Query: uterine perforation [SEP] Uterine perforation is a hole or break through the wall of the uterus, usually made by the placement of an instrument or [MASK].

name: v ( d ) j recombination
query: Query: v ( d ) j recombination [SEP] V (d) j recombination is The process by which the V (variable), D (diversity), and J (joining) segments of immunoglobulin genes or T-cell receptor genes are assembled during the development of lymphoid cells using nonhomologous DNA end-joining.

name: vaccines , attenuated
query: Query: vaccines , attenuated [SEP] Attenuated vaccines is live vaccines prepared from microorganisms which have undergone physical adaptation (e.g., by radiation or temperature conditioning) or serial passage in laboratory animal hosts or infected tissue/cell cultures, in order to produce avirulent mutant strains capable of inducing protective immunity.

name: vaccines , combined
query: Query: vaccines , combined [SEP] Combined vaccines is two or more vaccines in a single dosage form.

name: vaccines , conjugate
query: Query: vaccines , conjugate [SEP] Conjugate vaccines is semisynthetic vaccines consisting of polysaccharide antigens from microorganisms attached to protein carrier molecules. The carrier protein is recognized by macrophages and T-cells thus enhancing immunity. Conjugate vaccines induce antibody formation in people not responsive to polysaccharide alone, induce higher levels of antibody, and show a booster response on repeated injection.

name: vaccines , contraceptive
query: Query: vaccines , contraceptive [SEP] Contraceptive vaccines is vaccines or candidate vaccines used to prevent conception.

name: vaccines , dna
query: Query: vaccines , dna [SEP] Dna vaccines is [MASK] vectors encoding antigens administered for the prevention or treatment of disease. The host cells take up the dna, express the antigen, and present it to the immune system in a manner similar to that which would occur during natural infection. This induces humoral and cellular immune responses against the encoded antigens. The vector is called naked dna because there is no need for complex formulations or delivery agents; the plasmid is injected in saline or other [MASK].

name: vaccines , inactivated
query: Query: vaccines , inactivated [SEP] Inactivated vaccines is vaccines in which the infectious microbial nucleic acid components have been destroyed by chemical or physical treatment (e.g., formalin, beta-propiolactone, gamma radiation) without affecting the antigenicity or immunogenicity of the viral coat or [MASK] proteins.

name: vaccines , subunit
query: Query: vaccines , subunit [SEP] Subunit vaccines is vaccines consisting of one or more antigens that stimulate a strong immune response. They are purified from microorganisms or produced by [MASK] techniques, or they can be chemically synthesized peptides.

name: vacuum
query: Query: vacuum [SEP] Vacuum is a space in which the pressure is far below atmospheric pressure so that the remaining gases do not affect processes being carried on in the space.

name: vaginal birth after cesarean
query: Query: vaginal birth after cesarean [SEP] Vaginal birth after cesarean is delivery of an infant through the vagina in a female who has had a prior cesarean section.

name: vaginal neoplasms
query: Query: vaginal neoplasms [SEP] Vaginal neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the vagina.

name: validation studies as topic
query: Query: validation studies as topic [SEP] Validation studies as topic is works on research using processes by which the reliability and relevance of a procedure for a specific purpose are established.

name: validation study
query: Query: validation study [SEP] Validation study is works consisting of research using processes by which the reliability and relevance of a procedure for a specific purpose are established.

name: vascular endothelial growth factor a
query: Query: vascular endothelial growth factor a [SEP] Vascular endothelial growth factor a is the original member of the family of endothelial cell growth factors referred to as vascular endothelial growth factors. Vascular endothelial growth factor-A was originally isolated from tumor cells and referred to as "tumor angiogenesis factor" and "vascular permeability factor". Although expressed at high levels in certain tumor-derived cells it is produced by a wide variety of cell types. In addition to stimulating vascular growth and vascular permeability it may play a role in stimulating vasodilation via [MASK]-dependent pathways. [MASK] of the mRNA for vascular endothelial growth factor a results in several isoforms of the protein being produced.

name: vascular endothelial growth factor b
query: Query: vascular endothelial growth factor b [SEP] Vascular endothelial growth factor b is a vascular endothelial growth factor expressed in a variety of tissues. It binds with high specificity to vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-1 and neuropilin-1.

name: vascular endothelial growth factor d
query: Query: vascular endothelial growth factor d [SEP] Vascular endothelial growth factor d is a vascular endothelial growth factor that specifically binds to vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-2 and vascular endothelial growth factor receptor-3. In addition to being an angiogenic factor it can act on lymphatic vessels to stimulate lymphangiogenesis. It is similar in structure to [MASK] in that they both contain n- and C-terminal extensions that were not found in other vegf family members.

name: vascular fistula
query: Query: vascular fistula [SEP] Vascular fistula is an abnormal passage between two or more blood vessels, between arteries; veins; or between an artery and a vein.

name: vascular remodeling
query: Query: vascular remodeling [SEP] Vascular remodeling is the active alterations of vascular wall structures, often leading to elevated vascular resistance. It is associated with aging; atherosclerosis; diabetes mellitus; hypertension; pregnancy; pulmonary hypertension; and stroke, but is also a normal part of embryogenesis.

name: vascular ring
query: Query: vascular ring [SEP] Vascular ring is congenital vascular malformation in which the aorta arch and its branches encircle the [MASK] and esophagus. Signs and symptoms include dyspnea; respiratory sounds, especially with eating, dysphagia, persistent [MASK], and gastroesophageal reflux or may be asymptomatic. Two most common types are double aortic arch and right aortic arch. It may be associated with other anomalies (e.g., digeorge syndrome).

name: vascular stiffness
query: Query: vascular stiffness [SEP] Vascular stiffness is loss of vascular elasticity due to factors such as aging; and arteriosclerosis. Increased arterial stiffness is one of the risk factors for many cardiovascular diseases.

name: vascular system injuries
query: Query: vascular system injuries [SEP] Vascular system injuries is injuries to blood vessels caused by laceration, contusion, puncture, or crush and other types of injuries. Symptoms vary by site and mode of injuries and may include bleeding, bruising, swelling, pain, and numbness. It does not include injuries secondary to pathologic function or diseases such as atherosclerosis.

name: vehicle emissions
query: Query: vehicle emissions [SEP] Vehicle emissions is gases, fumes, vapors, and odorants escaping from the cylinders of a gasoline or diesel internal-combustion engine. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 4th ed & Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

name: venous insufficiency
query: Query: venous insufficiency [SEP] Venous insufficiency is impaired venous blood flow or venous return (venous stasis), usually caused by inadequate venous valves. Venous insufficiency often occurs in the legs, and is associated with edema and sometimes with venous stasis [MASK] at the ankle.

name: venous valves
query: Query: venous valves [SEP] Venous valves is flaps within the veins that allow the blood to flow only in one direction. They are usually in the medium size veins that carry blood to the heart against gravity.

name: ventilation
query: Query: ventilation [SEP] Ventilation is supplying a building or house, their rooms and corridors, with fresh air. The controlling of the environment thus may be in public or domestic sites and in medical or non-medical locales. (From Dorland, 28th ed)

name: ventral striatum
query: Query: ventral striatum [SEP] Ventral striatum is a composite structure of the telencephalon that is defined by connectivity. It includes the nucleus accumbens; the islands of calleja; and parts of the caudate nucleus; the putamen; and the substantia innominata.

name: ventricular dysfunction , left
query: Query: ventricular dysfunction , left [SEP] Left ventricular dysfunction is a condition in which the left ventricle of the heart was functionally impaired. This condition usually leads to heart failure; myocardial infarction; and other cardiovascular complications. Diagnosis is made by measuring the diminished ejection fraction and a depressed level of motility of the left ventricular wall.

name: ventricular dysfunction , right
query: Query: ventricular dysfunction , right [SEP] Right ventricular dysfunction is a condition in which the right ventricle of the heart was functionally impaired. This condition usually leads to heart failure or myocardial infarction, and other cardiovascular complications. Diagnosis is made by measuring the diminished ejection fraction and a depressed level of motility of the right ventricular wall.

name: ventricular fibrillation
query: Query: ventricular fibrillation [SEP] Ventricular fibrillation is a potentially lethal cardiac arrhythmia that is characterized by uncoordinated extremely rapid firing of electrical impulses (400-600/min) in heart ventricles. Such asynchronous ventricular quivering or fibrillation prevents any effective cardiac output and results in unconsciousness (syncope). It is one of the major electrocardiographic patterns seen with cardiac arrest.

name: ventricular function , left
query: Query: ventricular function , left [SEP] Left ventricular function is the hemodynamic and electrophysiological action of the left heart ventricle. Its measurement is an important aspect of the clinical evaluation of patients with heart disease to determine the effects of the disease on cardiac performance.

name: ventricular function , right
query: Query: ventricular function , right [SEP] Right ventricular function is the hemodynamic and electrophysiological action of the right heart ventricle.

name: ventricular premature complexes
query: Query: ventricular premature complexes [SEP] Ventricular premature complexes is a type of cardiac arrhythmia with premature contractions of the heart ventricles. It is characterized by the premature qrs complex on ecg that is of abnormal shape and great duration (generally >129 msec). It is the most common form of all cardiac arrhythmias. Premature ventricular complexes have no clinical significance except in concurrence with heart diseases.

name: ventricular pressure
query: Query: ventricular pressure [SEP] Ventricular pressure is the pressure within a cardiac ventricle. Ventricular pressure waveforms can be measured in the beating heart by catheterization or estimated using imaging techniques (e.g., doppler echocardiography). The information is useful in evaluating the function of the myocardium; cardiac valves; and pericardium, particularly with simultaneous measurement of other (e.g., aortic or atrial) pressures.

name: ventricular remodeling
query: Query: ventricular remodeling [SEP] Ventricular remodeling is the geometric and structural changes that the heart ventricles undergo, usually following myocardial infarction. It comprises expansion of the infarct and dilatation of the healthy ventricle segments. While most prevalent in the left ventricle, it can also occur in the right ventricle.

name: ventricular septum
query: Query: ventricular septum [SEP] Ventricular septum is the muscular structure separating the right and the left lower chambers (heart ventricles) of the heart. The ventricular septum consists of a very small membranous portion just beneath the aortic valve, and a large thick muscular portion consisting of three sections including the inlet septum, the trabecular septum, and the outlet septum.

name: version , fetal
query: Query: version , fetal [SEP] Fetal version is the artificial alteration of the fetal position to facilitate birth.

name: vertebral artery
query: Query: vertebral artery [SEP] Vertebral artery is the first branch of the subclavian artery with distribution to muscles of the [MASK]; vertebrae; spinal cord; cerebellum; and interior of the cerebrum.

name: vesicular glutamate transport protein 1
query: Query: vesicular glutamate transport protein 1 [SEP] Vesicular glutamate transport protein 1 is a vesicular glutamate transporter protein that is predominately expressed in telencephalon of the brain.

name: vesicular glutamate transport protein 2
query: Query: vesicular glutamate transport protein 2 [SEP] Vesicular glutamate transport protein 2 is a vesicular glutamate transporter protein that is predominately expressed in the diencephalon and lower brainstem regions of the central nervous system.

name: vestibular nucleus , lateral
query: Query: vestibular nucleus , lateral [SEP] Lateral vestibular nucleus is vestibular nucleus lying immediately superior to the inferior vestibular nucleus and composed of large multipolar nerve cells. Its upper end becomes continuous with the superior vestibular nucleus.

name: veterans
query: Query: veterans [SEP] Veterans is former members of the armed services.

name: veterans disability claims
query: Query: veterans disability claims [SEP] Veterans disability claims is disorders claimed as a result of military service.

name: veterinary drugs
query: Query: veterinary drugs [SEP] Veterinary drugs is drugs used by veterinarians in the treatment of animal diseases. The veterinarian's pharmacological armamentarium is the counterpart of drugs treating human diseases, with dosage and administration adjusted to the size, weight, disease, and idiosyncrasies of the species. In the United States most drugs are subject to federal regulations with special reference to the safety of drugs and residues in edible animal products.

name: veterinary service , military
query: Query: veterinary service , military [SEP] Military veterinary service is a corps of the armed services concerned with animal medicine, the chief interest of which is the care of government-owned working dogs (as in the military [MASK] units), working horses (as in state funerals), and working military dolphins (as in undersea exploration and other activities). In the United States Army Veterinary Corps animal medicine overlaps and interconnects with biomedical research using laboratory research animals. a related activity is laboratory animal care. The Corps provides limited care for privately owned animals of military personnel through non-appropriated funds. Military service veterinarians in the United States Army must be graduates of accredited veterinary schools and must have a state license. (Telephone communication with Lt. Col. William Inskeep ii, u.s. Army Veterinary Corps, October 4, 1994)

name: veterinary sports medicine
query: Query: veterinary sports medicine [SEP] Veterinary sports medicine is the field of veterinary medicine concerned with physical fitness of animals in sports (horse racing, dog racing, etc.) and the diagnosis and treatment of sports injuries in animals.

name: vibration
query: Query: vibration [SEP] Vibration is a continuing periodic change in displacement with respect to a fixed reference. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

name: victoria
query: Query: victoria [SEP] Victoria is a state in southeastern Australia, the southernmost state. Its capital is Melbourne. It was discovered in 1770 by Captain Cook and first settled by immigrants from Tasmania. In 1851 it was separated from New South Wales as a separate colony. Self-government was introduced in 1851; it became a state in 1901. It was named for Queen Victoria in 1851. (From Webster's New Geographical Dictionary, 1988, p1295 & Room, Brewer's Dictionary of Names, p574)

name: video recording
query: Query: video recording [SEP] Video recording is the storing or preserving of video signals to be played back later via a transmitter or receiver.

name: vietnam conflict
query: Query: vietnam conflict [SEP] Vietnam [MASK] is a [MASK] occurring from 1954 through 1975 within the Republic of Vietnam. It involved neighboring nations and the United States and other members of the Southeast Asia Treaty Organization.

name: vimentin
query: Query: vimentin [SEP] Vimentin is an [MASK] protein found in most differentiating cells, in cells grown in tissue culture, and in certain fully differentiated cells. Its insolubility suggests that it serves a structural function in the cytoplasm. mw 52,000.

name: viral interference
query: Query: viral interference [SEP] Viral interference is a phenomenon in which infection by a first virus results in resistance of cells or tissues to infection by a second, unrelated virus.

name: viral matrix proteins
query: Query: viral matrix proteins [SEP] Viral matrix proteins is proteins associated with the inner surface of the lipid bilayer of the viral envelope. These proteins have been implicated in control of viral transcription and may possibly serve as the "glue" that binds the nucleocapsid to the appropriate membrane site during viral budding from the host cell.

name: virtual reality
query: Query: virtual reality [SEP] Virtual reality is using computer technology to create and maintain an environment and project a user's physical presence in that environment allowing the user to interact with it.

name: virulence
query: Query: virulence [SEP] Virulence is the degree of pathogenicity within a group or species of microorganisms or viruses as indicated by case fatality rates and/or the ability of the organism to invade the tissues of the host. The pathogenic capacity of an organism is determined by its virulence factors.

name: virulence factors
query: Query: virulence factors [SEP] Virulence factors is those components of an organism that determine its capacity to cause disease but are not required for its viability per se. Two classes have been characterized: toxins, biological and surface adhesion molecules that effect the ability of the microorganism to invade and colonize a host. (From Davis et al., Microbiology, 4th ed. p486)

name: virus
query: Query: virus [SEP] Virus is minute infectious agents whose genomes are composed of DNA or RNA, but not both. They are characterized by a lack of independent metabolism and the inability to replicate outside living host cells.

name: virus assembly
query: Query: virus assembly [SEP] Virus assembly is the assembly of viral structural proteins and nucleic acid ([MASK] or viral rna) to form a virus particle.

name: virus attachment
query: Query: virus attachment [SEP] Virus attachment is the binding of virus particles to virus receptors on the host cell surface, facilitating virus entry into the cell.

name: virus inactivation
query: Query: virus inactivation [SEP] Virus inactivation is inactivation of viruses by non-immune related techniques. They include extremes of pH, heat treatment, ultraviolet radiation, ionizing radiation; desiccation; antiseptics; disinfectants; organic solvents, and detergents.

name: virus integration
query: Query: virus integration [SEP] Virus integration is insertion of [MASK] into host-cell dna. This includes integration of phage dna into [MASK]; (lysogeny); to form a prophage or integration of retroviral dna into cellular dna to form a provirus.

name: virus internalization
query: Query: virus internalization [SEP] Virus internalization is the entering of cells by viruses following virus attachment. This is achieved by endocytosis, by translocation of the whole virus across the cell membrane, by direct [MASK] of the viral membrane with the cell membrane, or by fusion of the membrane of infected cells with the membrane of non-infected cells causing syncytia to be formed.

name: virus latency
query: Query: virus latency [SEP] Virus latency is the ability of a pathogenic virus to lie dormant within a cell (latent infection). In eukaryotes, subsequent activation and viral replication is thought to be caused by extracellular stimulation of cellular transcription factors. Latency in bacteriophage is maintained by the expression of virally encoded repressors.

name: virus release
query: Query: virus release [SEP] Virus release is release of a virus from the host cell following virus assembly and maturation. Egress can occur by host cell lysis, exocytosis, or budding through the plasma membrane.

name: virus shedding
query: Query: virus shedding [SEP] Virus shedding is the expelling of virus particles from the body. Important routes include the respiratory tract, genital tract (important in infectious disease transmission, vertical), and intestinal tract.

name: vision , low
query: Query: vision , low [SEP] Low vision is vision considered to be inferior to normal vision as represented by accepted standards of acuity, field of vision, or motility. Low vision generally refers to visual disorders that are caused by diseases that cannot be corrected by refraction (e.g., macular degeneration; retinitis pigmentosa; diabetic retinopathy, etc.).

name: visitors to patients
query: Query: visitors to patients [SEP] Visitors to patients is patients' guests and rules for visiting.

name: visual cortex
query: Query: visual cortex [SEP] Visual cortex is area of the occipital lobe concerned with the processing of visual information relayed via visual pathways.

name: visual field tests
query: Query: visual field tests [SEP] [MASK] tests is method of measuring and mapping the scope of vision, from central to peripheral of each eye.

name: visually impaired persons
query: Query: visually impaired persons [SEP] Visually impaired persons is persons with loss of vision such that there is an impact on activities of daily living.

name: visual pathways
query: Query: visual pathways [SEP] Visual pathways is [MASK] of cell bodies and nerve fibers conducting impulses from the eyes to the cerebral cortex. It includes the retina; optic nerve; optic tract; and geniculocalcarine tract.

name: vitamin
query: Query: vitamin [SEP] Vitamin is organic substances that are required in small amounts for maintenance and growth, but which cannot be manufactured by the [MASK].

name: vitamin b 12 deficiency
query: Query: vitamin b 12 deficiency [SEP] Vitamin b 12 deficiency is a nutritional condition produced by a deficiency of vitamin b 12 in the diet, characterized by megaloblastic anemia. Since vitamin b 12 is not present in plants, humans have obtained their supply from animal products, from multivitamin supplements in the form of pills, and as additives to food preparations. a wide variety of neuropsychiatric abnormalities is also seen in vitamin b 12 deficiency and appears to be due to an undefined defect involving myelin synthesis. (From Cecil Textbook of Medicine, 19th ed, p848)

name: vitamin b 6 deficiency
query: Query: vitamin b 6 deficiency [SEP] Vitamin b 6 deficiency is a nutritional condition produced by a deficiency of vitamin b 6 in the diet, characterized by dermatitis, glossitis, cheilosis, and stomatitis. Marked deficiency causes irritability, weakness, depression, dizziness, peripheral neuropathy, and seizures. In infants and children typical manifestations are [MASK], anemia, and seizures. Deficiency can be caused by certain medications, such as isoniazid.

name: vitamin b complex
query: Query: vitamin b complex [SEP] Vitamin b complex is a group of water-soluble vitamins, some of which are coenzymes.

name: vitamin d response element
query: Query: vitamin d response element [SEP] Vitamin d response element is a dna sequence that is found in the promoter region of vitamin d regulated genes. Vitamin d receptor (receptor, calcitriol) binds to and regulates the activity of genes containing this element.

name: vitamin k 2
query: Query: vitamin k 2 [SEP] Vitamin k 2 is a group of substances similar to [MASK] which contains a ring of 2-methyl-1,4-naphthoquinione and an isoprenoid side chain of varying number of isoprene units. In vitamin k 2, each isoprene unit contains a double bond. They are produced by bacteria including the normal intestinal flora.

name: vitamin k deficiency bleeding
query: Query: vitamin k deficiency bleeding [SEP] Vitamin k deficiency bleeding is hemorrhage caused by vitamin k deficiency.

name: vitreous detachment
query: Query: vitreous detachment [SEP] Vitreous detachment is detachment of the corpus vitreum ([MASK]) from its normal attachments, especially the retina, due to shrinkage from degenerative or inflammatory conditions, trauma, myopia, or senility.

name: vitreous hemorrhage
query: Query: vitreous hemorrhage [SEP] Vitreous hemorrhage is hemorrhage into the [MASK].

name: vocabulary
query: Query: vocabulary [SEP] Vocabulary is the sum or the stock of words used by a language, a group, or an individual. (From Webster, 3d ed)

name: vocal cord paralysis
query: Query: vocal cord paralysis [SEP] Vocal cord paralysis is congenital or acquired paralysis of one or both vocal cords. This condition is caused by defects in the central nervous system, the vagus nerve and branches of laryngeal nerves. Common symptoms are [MASK] including hoarseness or aphonia.

name: vocational guidance
query: Query: vocational guidance [SEP] Vocational guidance is systematic efforts to assist individuals in selecting an occupation or suitable employment on the basis of aptitude, education, etc.

name: voice training
query: Query: voice training [SEP] Voice training is a variety of techniques used to help individuals utilize their voice for various purposes and with minimal use of muscle energy.

name: volatile organic compounds
query: Query: volatile organic compounds [SEP] Volatile organic compounds is organic compounds that have a relatively high [MASK] at room temperature.

name: vulnerable populations
query: Query: vulnerable populations [SEP] Vulnerable populations is groups of persons whose range of options is severely limited, who are frequently subjected to coercion in their decision making, or who may be compromised in their ability to give informed consent.

name: wales
query: Query: wales [SEP] Wales is a region of the United Kingdom, in the southwestern area of Great Britain.

name: walking speed
query: Query: walking speed [SEP] Walking speed is the rate at which steps are made while walking.

name: walk test
query: Query: walk test [SEP] Walk test is a measure of endurance tests that show how far and fast an individual can walk without stopping within a certain period of time.

name: war crimes
query: Query: war crimes [SEP] War crimes is criminal acts committed during, or in connection with, war, e.g., maltreatment of prisoners, willful killing of civilians, etc.

name: war exposure
query: Query: war exposure [SEP] War exposure is the health and other ramifications of military and civilian exposure to war.

name: water cycle
query: Query: water cycle [SEP] Water cycle is circulation of water among various ecological systems, in various states, on, above, and below the surface of the earth.

name: water microbiology
query: Query: water microbiology [SEP] Water microbiology is the presence of bacteria, viruses, and fungi in water. This term is not restricted to pathogenic organisms.

name: water pipe smoking
query: Query: water pipe smoking [SEP] Water pipe smoking is a process by which smoke produced from burning substance is mixed with flavor-altering substances and drawn through water or other liquid into the mouth.

name: water pollutants , chemical
query: Query: water pollutants , chemical [SEP] Chemical water pollutants is chemical compounds which pollute the water of [MASK], [MASK], [MASK], the sea, reservoirs, or other bodies of water.

name: water pollutants , radioactive

name: western australia
query: Query: western australia [SEP] Western australia is a state in western Australia. Its capital is Perth. It was first visited by the Dutch in 1616 but the English took possession in 1791 and permanent colonization began in 1829. It was a penal settlement 1850-1888, became part of the colonial government in 1886, and was granted self government in 1890. (From Webster's New Geographical Dictionary, 1988, p1329)

name: wet macular degeneration
query: Query: wet macular degeneration [SEP] Wet macular degeneration is a form of retinal degeneration in which abnormal choroidal neovascularization occurs under the retina and macula lutea, causing bleeding and leaking of fluid. This leads to bulging and or lifting of the macula and the distortion or destruction of central vision.

name: wnt signaling pathway
query: Query: wnt signaling pathway [SEP] Wnt signaling pathway is a complex signaling pathway whose name is derived from the drosophila Wg gene, and the vertebrate int gene. query: Query: work capacity evaluation [SEP] Work capacity evaluation is assessment of physiological capacities in relation to job requirements. name: work of breathing
query: Query: work of breathing [SEP] Work of breathing is respiratory muscle contraction during [MASK]. The work is accomplished in three phases: lung compliance work, that required to expand the lungs against its elastic forces; tissue resistance work, that required to overcome the [MASK] of the lung and chest wall structures; and airway resistance work, that required to overcome airway resistance during the movement of air into the lungs. Work of breathing does not refer to expiration, which is entirely a passive process caused by elastic recoil of the lung and chest cage. (Guyton, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 8th ed, p406)

name: ww domains
query: Query: ww domains [SEP] Ww domains is an approximately 40 amino acid protein domain that occurs in a variety of unrelated proteins and may be repeated up to four times in some proteins. It is characterized by two tryptophan residues (ww) about 20 amino acids apart and folds into a stable triple-stranded beta-sheet. It binds proline-rich protein domains and phosphoserine or PHOSPHOTHREONINE-containing protein domains that occur in many signal-transducing and cytoskeletal proteins such as dystrophin.

name: yellow fever vaccine
query: Query: yellow fever vaccine [SEP] Yellow fever vaccine is vaccine used to prevent yellow fever. It consists of a live attenuated 17d strain of the yellow fever virus.

name: yellow nail syndrome
query: Query: yellow nail syndrome [SEP] Yellow nail syndrome is a rare condition characterized by the presence of yellow nails, lymphedema, and/or pleural effusion with respiratory tract involvement. Abnormal lymphatic network may play a role in its etiology. Occasionally inherited, yellow nail syndrome mostly is sporadic without apparent family history.

name: zinc oxide
query: Query: zinc oxide [SEP] Zinc oxide is a mild astringent and topical protectant with some antiseptic action. It is also used in bandages, pastes, ointments, dental cements, and as a sunblock.

name: zinc transporter 8
query: Query: zinc transporter 8 [SEP] Zinc transporter 8 is a zinc efflux transporter highly expressed by islet cells of the pancreas. It functions in the accumulation of zinc in intracellular vesicles and may be involved in insulin maturation and storage processes. Variations in the slc30a8 gene are associated with susceptibility to diabetes mellitus, type 2.
